# Changelog

Hive did not historically maintain a complete changelog. This file starts a pragmatic, forward-looking record for operators and contributors. We are not reconstructing every old change retroactively; instead, maintainers should add notable user-facing changes as PRs land.

## How we maintain this file

- In your PR, add the entry as a fragment file `changelog.d/<category>-<pr-or-slug>.md` (category one of `added`/`changed`/`deprecated`/`fixed`/`security` — see [changelog.d/README.md](changelog.d/README.md)) for user-visible features, fixes, security changes, migrations, deprecations, and breaking changes. Do not append to `## Unreleased` directly: one shared heading edited by every PR made unrelated PRs merge-conflict with each other ([#5675](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5675)). The transition window for direct edits closed on 2026-09-09; fragments in `changelog.d/` are the accepted route for new PRs.
- Fragments are compiled into `Unreleased` and moved into a dated release section automatically when a release is cut (`src/scripts/compile-changelog.sh`, driven by `.github/workflows/tagged-release.yml`). If the repository has no release tag for the change, use the merge date rather than inventing a version.
- Link issues or PRs when useful, but keep entries readable for operators who are not following every PR.
- Do not include routine refactors, test-only changes, or dependency churn unless they affect users.

## Unreleased

## 2026-11-10 (v6.11.0)

### Added

- When one check fails on several open PRs in a repository (`shared_ci_issues.min_prs`, default 3) or trips the red-main breaker, the hive now files one `[shared-ci] <check> failing across <owner/repo>` tracking issue itself, naming the check, the PRs and a log excerpt, and keeps its own issue up to date; before, only an agent triaging one of the red PRs filed it, so a check red on every contributor and bot PR in a repo could go unreported for a day. An incident someone else filed is left alone; disable with `shared_ci_issues.enabled: false`.

### Fixed

- A "Let hive decide" job that a hive restart or upgrade cut short is now marked failed ("interrupted by a hive restart before it finished, and not resumed") with an audit entry, instead of staying "pending" forever, and the job status endpoint (and admin MCP `delegated_decision_status`) answers the item's last result from the operator-action ledger instead of a 404 once the job has left memory. Nothing is re-run after a restart.
- A fork PR the hive cannot finish because its base changed `.github/workflows/` now parks at `085` with the one action that unblocks it (a person runs **Update branch** or `gh pr update-branch`, or merges the base in locally on a conflict), instead of asking a maintainer to bring the change into the repository or close it; a fork without maintainer edits names the author's step (projectbluefin/common#1611).
- The 090 "Ready for a human merge" comment no longer says "Blocked only by" the author's trust tier when GitHub reports the head behind a base that requires up-to-date branches: it names the base merge as a second blocker and stops offering "(or merge)" (projectbluefin/common#1619).
- Activity Monitor: a new pull request on a repo whose auto-merge is off (or on any repo of a hive below ACMM L6) no longer reads "waiting for the stage-label pass (next pass due now)", since no merge lane runs there to stage it; the row says a person merges it, shows the merge verdict, and, when GitHub would take the merge, offers **Merge now as maintainer** as its lead action.
- Bot Dependency Dashboards and the Hive Advisory Report no longer count as "Waiting on you" (approve-needed) when a triage bot labels them `needs-human`: the badge, topbar pill and the MCP's `waiting_on_you` now match the activity monitor, which never draws those issues.

## 2026-11-10 (v6.10.0)

### Added

- **Sentinel's sensitive-path list and the contributor lane's workflow fence scope can be set per repository.** Two opt-in hive.yaml keys under `project.repo_policies`, `sentinel_sensitive_paths` and `workflow_fence_scope`, replace `sentinel.sensitive_paths` and `auto_merge.contributor_lane.workflow_fence_scope` for one repository, so an operator can loosen (or tighten) them where the maintainers agreed without changing repositories that belong to someone else. A repository without the key behaves exactly as before, and a later change to the hive-wide value does not reach a repository that has its own. An explicit empty sensitive-path list matches nothing, as the hive-wide key does; `human_merge_paths` scope still keeps the full fence for a repository with no `human_merge_paths` entry. An invalid override stops the config from loading, and the running hive treats one that gets through as unset. Settings → Security → Suspicious Activity and Settings → Features → Auto Merge list the overrides (read-only), `settings_read` returns them, and the admin MCP `sentinel.settings` preview names every repository with its own list, what that list leaves out, and refuses a stale confirm if an override changed. See [hive-merge.md](src/docs/hive-merge.md#contributor-lane-auto-merge).
- A red pull request that is behind its base, and whose every failing check has since gone green on the base tip, now gets the base merged in by the hive (the same merge "Update branch" makes), so its CI runs again against the fix instead of waiting for a person. It covers PRs the automerge adoption recovery does not, including repositories with auto-merge off; it skips drafts, held PRs, forks without maintainer edits, dependency-bot branches and PRs at stage 072 or 074, makes at most 2 updates per repository and 6 per pass every 5 minutes, tries each head and base tip once, and goes through the new `base_refresh` write-back kind (hive-authored PRs, else L6 with the opt-in label; `writeback.kinds.base_refresh.unlabeled_min_level: 6` reaches every PR). Seen on projectbluefin/actions#544, which sat red on `pytest` for six hours after main repaired the baseline.

## 2026-11-10 (v6.9.1)

### Fixed

- The hold guard now announces that it stopped keeping a held PR mergeable at INFO instead of WARN; several held fork PRs stopping in one pass no longer trips the `unclassified_error_repeated` self-report, and the person-facing note on the PR is unchanged (#17520).
- A resident agent's kick no longer lists PRs on repos with auto-merge switched off as MERGE-ELIGIBLE; they move to NEEDS MAINTAINER MERGE with the reason, so the scanner stops spending a kick on hive-merge requests the relay always refuses.

## 2026-11-10 (v6.9.0)

### Added

- **Admin MCP can change the issue filter and Sentinel settings.** Two new write operations, `project.issue_filter` (`require_labels`, the `hard_suppress_labels` buckets, and reporter trust: `enabled`, `trusted_associations`, `trusted_logins`, `untrusted_require_labels`) and `sentinel.settings` (`sensitive_paths`, `disabled_behaviors`, `exempt_logins`, `trusted_authors_block`), save through the same owner-only endpoints as Settings → Labels and Settings → Security. Lists are edited with `add`/`remove`/`clear`: the preview reads the current values, shows each list before and after, and sends the merged list, and `write_confirm` is refused if those settings changed since the preview. A change that admits more issues without triage, or makes Sentinel flag fewer pull requests, is disclosed as widening, and the Sentinel preview names the pull requests that would no longer be held. On a hub-managed hive the issue filter preview warns that the hub may overwrite the change. See [Admin MCP → Writes](src/docs/admin-mcp.md#writes).
- **"Let hive decide" settings can be changed from the dashboard and admin MCP.** The new owner-only `GET`/`PUT /api/config/decisions/delegate` reads and changes `decisions.delegate`: the hive-wide switch, per-repository overrides, the LLM step (`llm.enabled`, `llm.model`) and `effect_timeout`. Settings → Features gains a *Let hive decide* block with the switch, the LLM toggle and the model. The new admin MCP operation `decisions.delegate_settings` changes one repository at a time without dropping the others, shows each change before and after, says when turning on the LLM step sends item text to a model or when a repository opens to Let hive decide, and is refused if the settings changed after the preview. A key-like `llm.model` is refused and never returned. Changes apply without a restart; nothing here starts a decision or merges anything.

## 2026-11-10 (v6.8.0)

### Added

- **Admin MCP: change merge settings through preview and confirm.** The new `auto_merge.update` write operation wraps `PATCH /api/config/auto-merge`, so an owner can change `squash_only`, `require_current_base`, `human_merge_paths`, the native merge queue, trusted authors, the contributor lane and the other merge settings without opening the dashboard. Lists take `add`/`remove` and `human_merge_paths` takes one repository at a time; the preview reads the current settings and sends each changed list or map whole, so entries you did not name are kept, shows every change before and after, and says when a change lets the hive merge more on its own. `write_confirm` refuses if any of those settings changed after the preview. The operation never merges a pull request.
- **The pin-only exception can be set from the dashboard and admin MCP.** `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only`, which lets a pull request whose only change is a version or digest pin bump on a human-merge path merge without a hand merge, is now on `PUT`/`PATCH /api/config/auto-merge` (whole map, owner only), in **Settings → Features → Auto-merge** next to the human-merge paths, and in the admin MCP `auto_merge.update` operation one repository at a time. It is validated with the same rules `hive.yaml` loads under, refused for a repository with no `human_merge_paths`, saved like the other merge settings and applied without a restart, including to the merge-request relay. The MCP preview names what turning one on or widening it lets merge. What counts as a pin bump, and every other merge gate, is unchanged.

## 2026-11-10 (v6.7.0)

### Added

- **The contributor lane's workflow fence can be limited to release-critical workflows.** A new owner-only setting, `auto_merge.contributor_lane.workflow_fence_scope` (Settings → Features → Auto Merge → Contributor-lane auto-merge → **Workflow fence scope**), chooses which CI workflow / action edits wait for an owner's approval of the current head. `all`, the default, keeps today's behaviour: every edit under `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**` does. `human_merge_paths` fences only a file that also matches the repository's `auto_merge.human_merge_paths`, so routine edits such as pin bumps and permission tightening go through review, CI and soak instead of needing a fresh Approve after every push. It fails closed: a repository with no `human_merge_paths` entry keeps the full fence, a renamed workflow file always trips it, and a merge GitHub refuses for want of the App's Workflows permission parks the head for a person. The tests-removed fence, Sentinel, the human-merge hold, the guard that never approves held fork CI runs for a workflow edit, and adoption's refusal to publish workflow edits upstream are unchanged. The stage notes, the merge asks and `/hive approve` replies all read the same scoped fence as the lane. Sentinel's default `sensitive_path` list still labels these PRs `sentinel-alert`; see [hive-merge.md](src/docs/hive-merge.md#contributor-lane-auto-merge).

## 2026-11-09 (v6.6.0)

### Added

- **Owner switch for admin MCP writes.** Settings → Channels now has an **Allow admin MCP writes** switch (`admin_mcp.writes_enabled`), so a hive's owner can turn the `/api/admin/mcp` write tools on or off from the dashboard. Before this, a hosted hive's owner had to ask the hub operator to set `HIVE_ADMIN_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES` on the Deployment. The switch is owner-only, audited as `config_admin_mcp_writes` (actor, old and new value), takes effect on the next MCP call with no restart, and turning it off refuses pending confirmations at `write_confirm`. Once used it overrides `HIVE_ADMIN_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES` in both directions; until then that variable decides as before, so existing hives keep their behaviour. **Use environment default** clears the switch again, so the variable (or the default, off) decides. The stdio `hive-admin-mcp` binary is unchanged and still reads only its own environment.

### Fixed

- fix(dashboard): drain review-question autodecide sweep before WS test cleanup (#17452)

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.7)

### Fixed

- ci(scorecard): skip push runs on non-default branches (v6) (#17415)
- Contributor run records now keep their `duration_s` when the relay's connection drops and the task is resumed, including across a hub restart. A resumed task runs on a new connection that never saw the assignment, so the hub had no start time and booked the run with no duration; the runs view then showed nothing or `0s`. On projectbluefin on 2026-11-09, a task held across the 16:46Z restart failed at 17:16Z after about two and a half hours with no duration, and a task whose socket flapped two minutes in shipped about 14 minutes later with none either. The task lease now stores the original assignment time (`assigned_at` in `task-leases.json`, optional, so older registries still load), and the run log measures from it. When the start is unknown, for a lease written before this change, the field is left off rather than guessed, and a duration that would be negative or longer than seven days is never written. Only the run record and its audit row change: the fast-failure streak and other readers of the assignment time behave as before.
- ci: Scorecard `push` runs on non-default release branches are skipped instead of failing; `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` runs are unchanged ([#17392](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17392)).

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.6)

### Fixed

- The "stage labels: adoption refused, a person pushed this PR themselves; asking the author instead" line is now logged once per PR head (and per due reason and adoption request), not on every sweep. On projectbluefin it repeated about once a minute for the same two heads (utah-packages#925 and #928). Log only: the refusal still runs every sweep and records and consumes exactly what it did before, and a new push logs it again.
- The hub no longer logs a WARN every time a contributor relay finishes its own PR-review cycle. The relay builds that review task for itself with a `pr-review-` id the hub never assigns, and sends its `task_complete` on purpose; the hub correctly ignores it and leaves the real assignment alone, but logged each one as `[contribute-ws] task_complete for unassigned task ignored (assignment left intact)` at WARN, so the WARN feed filled with expected events (projectbluefin's hive logged 9 on 2026-11-09 alone, all `pr-review-` ids, across three contributors). That line now logs at DEBUG for `pr-review-` task ids, so it is still traceable. Nothing else changes: the assignment is still left intact, the decision is still recorded, and a completion for any other task the connection does not hold still logs at WARN.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.5)

### Fixed

- The contributor card on Operations no longer lists closed or merged PRs as "N PRs awaiting rework (not yet dispatched)" right after a hub restart. Stage records stay in the store for 14 days after a PR leaves the listings, and until a repo's open-PR listing was complete again the card counted every one of them as owed rework: on projectbluefin, after the 2026-11-09 upgrade, one contributor's card went from 1 to 7 PRs, all closed or merged by a maintainer 9-13 days earlier, and another's showed 17 with 14 closed. While a repo's listing cannot vouch, the card now counts a 072/074 record only if a stage pass saw the PR within the 072 stalled dwell (24h), so a freshly returned PR still shows; a record the store marks superseded never counts, and a complete listing still decides as before (hivecommons/hive#14708). Display only: nothing was dispatched.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.4)

### Fixed

- A contributor's relay is no longer sent to rework a PR that has already merged or closed, and one `fix-pr` task now runs once. On hivecommons/hive#17385 a stage-072 nudge queued a fix at 12:32Z, the PR merged at 13:13:58Z, and at about 14:25Z the hub still handed the relay `fix-pr hive#17385`, which the relay then ran twice: about 4.5 minutes lost, nothing pushed. Each link in that chain is fixed. The fix queue took the nudge's display name (`hive` on a hive whose repos are listed without the org), so the "left stage 072" resolve, which looks up `owner/name`, never found the entry, and the relay got a repo it could not match to its authorized list; queued fixes are now keyed and sent as `owner/name`. Right before a queued fix is handed out, the hub now checks the PR is still open (from the state cache when it holds the repo, else one PR read tagged `hive:contribute_fix_dispatch`); a merged or closed PR leaves the queue with a `fix queue: dropped a PR that is no longer open` log line, and if the state cannot be read the fix waits for the next tick while the relay takes ordinary work. A fix handed out at a task boundary was pushed to the relay twice (once by the dispatcher, once by the `ready` handler); it is now sent once, and the relay ignores a second `task_assign` for a `fix-pr` task it is already running (as its primary task, in a parallel session, preempting, or deferred) and logs where it runs. Progress reports from a boundary fix running as the relay's primary task are no longer answered with `task_revoke: no active lease for this task`, which killed the fix mid-run.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.3)

### Fixed

- A relay subscribed to several hives no longer refuses a `fix-pr` task for its contributor's own PR because it was polling another hive. On projectbluefin/utah-packages#972 (2026-11-09) the relay accepted a fix at 14:42:58Z, deferred it behind a headless task, and refused it with `Hub is not the active polling slot` the moment that task ended at 14:45:39Z; the hub booked a failed attempt and a five-minute retry. The relay now takes a `fix-pr` from any subscribed hub, makes that hub its active one and tells the other hives it is busy elsewhere, and the hub puts a fix refused for the polling slot back in its queue without counting an attempt. Ordinary work from a hive the relay is not polling is still refused.
- A fork PR whose only red check is a maintainer-run fork guard (such as a fork-gated Canary) is parked for a maintainer at `stage/085-needs-decision` on its first red head, instead of being sent back to its author first. On projectbluefin/utah-packages#972 (2026-11-09) the PR was opened from a fork at 14:41:50Z, its Canary refused it at 14:42:24Z with "This is expected, not something the author can fix", and at 14:45:32Z the hive nudged the author with `required-check-failing:Canary` and queued relay rework, because neither the fork-guard index (not yet read for that head) nor the stage record (never parked on a guard) knew about it; the PR reached 085 only at 14:50:57Z. The stage pass now reads such a head's own check annotations once, with the index's rule, and records the guard for later heads. A fork head with any other red check still goes to its author.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.2)

### Fixed

- Contributor-first lanes are no longer left unworked by a relay that is busy on another hive. A relay subscribed to several hives works one task at a time, and while that task belonged to another hive it still looked to this one like a connected relay holding its role, so the governor kept the resident agent's kicks withheld while nobody worked the lane (seen on 2026-11-09: a relay set "Acting as: scanner" on one hive worked another hive's tasks for seven minutes and sent the first hive no request for work). Relays now tell every other hive that advertises the new `busy_elsewhere_v1` capability when they start and finish another hive's task, and the hub leaves such a relay out of coverage until the task ends or the relay asks it for work again. The frame names no hive, repository or issue. Older relays and older hubs behave as before.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.1)

### Fixed

- An approval or recorded decision now carries over the hive's own merge of the base branch when the base also edited a file the PR changes, as long as the edit is away from the PR's hunks: every hunk is still byte-for-byte what was approved and only its line numbers moved, so the workflow-path fence no longer re-arms and the PR no longer parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` waiting for a fresh approval of the same change (projectbluefin/utah-packages#924). Files under `.github/` still have to read exactly as approved, and a base merge that touched the PR's own hunks or their context lines still needs a new approval.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.5.0)

### Added

- The API proxy's per-agent GitHub API hourly cap can now be changed without editing `hive.yaml`, so an operator on a hub-managed spoke can give one agent more room. Settings → Forge App sets the fleet default (`agents.github_api_hourly_cap`: a number, `0` for no cap, blank for the default of 300) next to the agent reserve floor, and each agent's General tab sets its own value (`agents.<name>.github_api_hourly_cap`: a number, `0` for no cap, blank to inherit). The admin MCP gets the same two writes, `agent.github_api_hourly_cap` and `github.agent_api_hourly_cap`, whose preview discloses a raised or removed cap as widening. A save applies to the proxy at once, is saved to the dashboard overlay and audited; replicas and review heads follow their base agent, and the agent reserve floor still applies. Debug → GitHub API budget now lists each agent's cap and its calls in the current hour, and `config_effective_read` shows both values and each agent's effective cap. See [Changing the agent caps](src/docs/operator-reference/runtime-and-quota.md#changing-the-agent-caps).

### Fixed

- **A replica takes its base agent's GitHub API hourly cap even before the next reload.** A replica or review head (`reviewer-2`, …) with no `agents.<name>.github_api_hourly_cap` of its own now takes its base agent's override directly, so an override set on the base applies to its replicas at once instead of after the config is next reloaded. The lookup order is the agent's own value, then the base agent's, then `agents.github_api_hourly_cap`, then the default of 300; `0` means no cap at either level. See [Runtime and quota](src/docs/operator-reference/runtime-and-quota.md).
- **A session recycle no longer leaves Copilot agents on a bare `copilot` that asks approval for every command.** When a restart replaced a Copilot agent's session, a pane-poll tick still running for the old session could read the new, still-empty pane against the old start time, call it hung for hours, and start the hang diagnostic. The diagnostic killed the freshly relaunched session, typed `copilot` with no `--allow-all`, `--model` or deny flags, and returned at once because its context was already cancelled, so the agent ran that CLI until the next restart. On a hosted hive this happened to every Copilot agent at each 6-hour recycle; the architect then sat 4h50m at "Do you want to run this command?". The hang detector now skips a poller whose launch was cancelled, and the diagnostic re-checks under the manager lock before each step that touches the session.
- The hive no longer merges `main` into a fork PR parked at 085 on a maintainer-run fork-guarded check (such as a fork Canary) after a restart or a rate-limited pass. The branch-update guard read only an in-memory index that has no entry for the head in those windows, so on projectbluefin/utah-packages#917 the App merged `main` five times in 22 hours and each merge discarded the run the PR was waiting for. When the index has nothing, the guard now falls back to the PR's stage record: it holds the update while a recorded guard check is red on the exact head (or while the head's checks cannot be read), and lets it through once every guarded check is green.
- **An agent refused because the hive's shared GitHub API budget is low is now told so, with the reset time, and keeps working.** When the App installation's remaining core budget fell under `github.agent_reserve_floor`, the proxy's 429 and pane nudge said "hourly cap reached" and "stop all GitHub reads for this session", the wording for an agent's own `agents.github_api_hourly_cap`. On knuckle (2026-11-08) sec-check was refused at 379/400 and abandoned its whole audit. The reserve refusal now says the shared budget is low (not the agent's cap), gives the reset time and `Retry-After`, and tells the agent to pause GitHub reads until then and carry on with local work. The cap refusal's wording is unchanged.
- A `requires_human` from a review whose GitHub reads the hive proxy refused (the reviewer hit `agents.github_api_hourly_cap`, or the shared bucket fell below `github.agent_reserve_floor`) is no longer recorded as a verdict, whatever words the reviewer used. The proxy now remembers when it last refused each agent, and the review relay sets aside a `requires_human` with no in-scope finding, no high-risk marker and no already-landed PR when its agent was refused after the perspective was dispatched. The perspective is asked again after `review.pending_ttl`, the same path as the rate-limited "could not read" case. Before, summaries such as "GitHub reads stopped at the user's request after the hourly cap; … could not be verified" or "not assessed: GitHub API cap prevented reading" were not recognised, and projectbluefin/utah-packages#959, projectbluefin/utah#1161 and projectbluefin/finpilot#659 parked at `stage/085-needs-decision` on 2026-11-09. The expiry that follows such a set-aside, or any expiry whose every row went to an agent the proxy refused after the row was sent, no longer spends `review.max_redispatch`: the planner waits for the refusal's `Retry-After` (at most an hour past `pending_ttl`), re-asks, and counts it in the dispatch state's `cap_redispatches[]`, bounded separately at 8 before the usual `review-dispatch-exhausted` hold. Before, a reviewer capped for about 2h15m on one head still ended in that hold and a person was asked.
- **A sec-check turn that audits nothing is now recorded as blocked, not as a finished audit.** When sec-check had no checkout and its GitHub reads were refused, it wrote "security posture remains unassessed" and the hive counted the turn as an ordinary ended kick (seen on a hosted hive, 2026-11-08: 13 AIC, nothing audited). Both sec-check templates now tell the agent to end such a turn on `STAND DOWN — no repository audited: <reason>`. The kick-outcome classifier records that line as a stand-down, so the dashboard shows the turn as blocked, with the reason.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.4.6)

### Fixed

- **An issue the issue filter keeps off the agent queue no longer asks you to ADMIT it while an open pull request closes it.** The your-turn inbox listed projectbluefin/actions#733, a sec-check finding, as `agent_finding_not_admitted` ("add `triage/accepted`") while sec-check's own fix PR projectbluefin/actions#734, which closes it on merge, was open: the filter's rows carry no linked PRs, so the covered-by-PR rule never saw it. The dashboard now reads the closing references of the repository's open and held PRs it already has (no extra GitHub call) and shows such an issue as waiting on that PR ("Waits on PR #N, which closes it"); the ADMIT ask comes back if the PR closes unmerged.
- The 085 comment on a fork PR parked on a fork-guarded check (such as a fork Canary) now follows the head. On projectbluefin/utah-packages#917 a maintainer's Canary passed on `8d7a655`, the author then rebased the same patch onto a newer `main` (`82ef790`), and the PR stayed at 085 while its comment still asked for a run on an earlier head. The comment is now rewritten in place for each new head while the PR stays parked, and it says that a run on an earlier head does not cover the new one, because a rebase or a merge of the base changes the code the check runs.
- **The red-main sweep stops asking for classic branch protection the App cannot read.** `ReadBranchRules`, which the red-main sweep, the merge lane and the dashboard's merge-lane and ACMM views use for required checks, called `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{branch}/protection/required_status_checks` on every read. An App without Administration permission gets a 403 there every time, so on a live hive `hive:red_main` spent about 330 REST calls an hour on failures (it sweeps every active repo every 10 minutes). The answer was already being taken from the rulesets endpoint, which stays read every pass. A 403, or a 404 other than "Branch not protected", from classic protection is now remembered per repo and branch for `HIVE_REQUIRED_CHECKS_FORBIDDEN_TTL` (default 1h, the same knob the auto-merge required-checks cache uses) and replayed with the same result, so each repo costs one classic call an hour instead of six. "Branch not protected", 5xx and rate-limit errors are not remembered.

## 2026-11-09 (v6.4.5)

### Fixed

- **A PR whose description mentions `— hive:` in its text is signed now.** The PR-request watcher skipped the `— hive: agent=… backend=… model=…` line whenever the body contained `— hive:` anywhere, so a PR that described the repositories' monthly agent audit (Danathar/arch-bootc#473, Danathar/atomic-image-builder#640 and #678) was opened unsigned, and that audit, which reads only a line beginning with `— hive:`, then failed. The watcher, `ReconcilePRAttribution`, the issue and review relays that use the same trailer, and the `gh` wrapper's body-edit guard now treat only a line that starts with `— hive:` as a signature. See [hive-open-pr](src/docs/hive-open-pr.md).

## 2026-11-09 (v6.4.4)

### Fixed

- **A contributor container now puts the hive's knowledge where its CLI starts, so Codex reads it.** The container linked the knowledge export (`~/agent.md`) as `~/AGENTS.md` and `~/CLAUDE.md`, but it launches the interactive CLI in `~/.local/state/hive/agent-cwd`, an empty directory that is not a git repository. Codex reads `AGENTS.md` only from the git root down to its working directory, plus its own `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`, so a Codex contributor ran every task without the export (a `projectbluefin/utah-packages#879` session carried the user's own `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and none of the hive's). Claude worked only because it also reads `CLAUDE.md` from parent directories. The container now links into `HIVE_AGENT_CWD`, the way `just contribute-hive local` already did. It keeps each backend's global files in its own `$HOME` (`~/.bob/AGENTS.md`, the goose config seed, `~/.copilot`), never writes `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`, and removes its old `$HOME` links (only those that point at the export) so a CLI that reads parent directories does not load the export twice. Headless mode, whose CLI runs in the workspace, keeps the `$HOME` links. See [Where each backend reads its instructions](src/docs/contributor-relay.md#where-each-backend-reads-its-instructions).
- **The hive log now says where a contributor's role guidance got its Relevant Knowledge.** The guidance render logged only the shared `knowledge: injected` line, which names the role and reads like a resident kick, so an off-topic `# Relevant Knowledge` section (for `projectbluefin/utah-packages#879`, entries about other repositories' PRs) could not be traced to its cause. Each guidance render now logs one `role guidance knowledge:` line: `primed from issue <repo>#<n>` with the search query and the number of matching entries, or `nothing primed` with the reason (no title or labels to search on, or nothing matched). There is no fallback to general entries, and the line says so. See [The knowledge share of a kick](src/docs/operator-reference/sweeps-and-operations.md).

## 2026-11-09 (v6.4.3)

### Fixed

- **A contributor acting as an agent role now gets the assigned repository's `AGENTS.md` and the issue's relevant knowledge.** The role guidance from the previous fix took `AGENTS.md` and skills from the role's primary repository, so a contributor acting as scanner on `projectbluefin/common#1614` got the primary repository's instructions instead of `common`'s. It also left out the `# Relevant Knowledge` section entirely. The guidance is now built for the one assigned task (`Scheduler.BuildAgentGuidanceForTask`). Knowledge is primed from that issue's title and labels, and `AGENTS.md` and skills come from its repository. If the task names no repository, the primary repository is used, as before. Priming for a contributor records no kick summary or primed facts for the resident agent. Resident kicks are byte-identical. Standby dispatch gets the same guidance. See [What a contributor receives in a role](src/docs/contributor-trust-and-roles.md#what-a-contributor-receives-in-a-role).

## 2026-11-09 (v6.4.2)

### Fixed

- The "agent pane · N lines" disclosure on an Operations contributor card now stays open until you close it. The fleet list redraws every card every 4 seconds, and the pane's open state was meant to survive that, but the row key it was stored under was declared further down the function, so it was always empty and the pane snapped shut on the next poll ([#7317](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7317) added the pane). While you have text selected inside a pane, the cards now wait to redraw until you let go of the selection, and an open pane keeps its scroll position across redraws.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.4.1)

### Fixed

- **A contributor acting as an agent role now gets that role's guidance and their one assigned task, not the resident agent's whole kick.** A role-delegated task (and donated standby work) used to carry the resident agent's full manual kick: the hive's work list, the merge-eligible and CI-failing lists, the merge-sweep and sub-agent dispatch steps, the App-token instructions, the red-main notice and "Begin now: pick the authorized repo …". The assigned issue sat at the very bottom. On the projectbluefin hive, a contributor acting as scanner followed that template on one issue for over 100 minutes and 1.1M input tokens: it named its branch `scanner/fix-1614`, force-pushed, and polled CI for 30 minutes instead of reporting. The new `Scheduler.BuildAgentGuidance` renders the same templates through the same chain, but drops the resident session's sections and work lists. The prompt now says the assigned task is the whole job. Building the guidance also no longer runs a classification sweep over the cached queue on every assignment. Resident agents' kicks are byte-identical, and new golden tests pin them. See [What a contributor receives in a role](src/docs/contributor-trust-and-roles.md#what-a-contributor-receives-in-a-role).

## 2026-11-08 (v6.4.0)

### Added

- crux: saved run results complete, the seventh work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S7). A finished run can now be re-run with `POST /v1/runs/{id}/restart` (`crux --server … runs restart`): the server re-validates the request the run was accepted with as its original owner against the current configuration, links the two records (`restarted_from` / `restarted_by`), audits the restart with its reason, and refuses with `409 conflict` while the old run is still live so two drivers never resume one task. `GET /v1/runs` lists the caller's runs newest first (the operator's view is every run; `?status=` and `?limit=` narrow it), `GET /v1/runs/{id}/history` is the record's status transitions, and a `crux serve` restart now settles the `running` steps of an unfinished session to `unfinished` alongside the run. `crux runs list|restart|history` round out the CLI.
- The GitHub conditional-request (ETag / 304) response cache is now sized by `github.etag_cache_max_mb` and `github.etag_cache_max_entries` (env `HIVE_GITHUB_ETAG_CACHE_MAX_MB` / `HIVE_GITHUB_ETAG_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`), editable under Settings → Forge App and applied without a restart. The built-in default rises from 64 MiB / 4096 entries to 128 MiB / 8192 entries, cached bodies are stored gzip-compressed so the cap holds several times as many responses, and `/api/gh-rate-limits` plus the Debug → GitHub API budget panel show the cache's fill level (`bytes` / `max_bytes` / `max_entries`) so an operator can see eviction pressure before the hit rate slides.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.3.1)

### Fixed

- Contributor-first lanes are no longer left unworked by a relay the hub will not hand work to, or has no work for. A relay whose trust tier is in `hub.disabled_tiers` (or whose access is revoked) is refused every task, and a relay whose requests keep being answered `no_matching_work` (or `repo_unmintable`) is connected and idle, but both still counted as covering their role, so the governor kept the resident agent's kicks withheld while nobody worked the lane. Seen on hive-wild-mole on 2026-11-08: a relay covered the scanner lane while every request for work it sent, about every 30 seconds, was answered `no_matching_work`. The hub now leaves a revoked or disabled-tier relay out of coverage, using the same check that refuses it work, and leaves out a relay with no task that has been answered "no work for you" for two minutes. A task or fix-pr task handed to the relay counts it again at once.
- GitHub API budget: the dashboard's GitHub API card and the API budget mode now follow the core rate-limit window the hive's own responses are spending, not the first `GET /rate_limit` reading after a restart and not a stray reading from another window. After the 2026-11-08 18:30:53Z restart on a projectbluefin hive, the first reading (6945, reset 19:21:44Z) held the card at `observed_at` 18:30:55Z for most of an hour while the installation window (reset 18:56:25Z) was at 3195. Earlier that day, responses from the two windows alternated and the budget mode flipped between `normal` and `conserve` every few seconds. Readings are now kept per window (`X-RateLimit-Reset`): the snapshot takes the lowest `remaining` among windows reported in the last five minutes, the card and mode adopt that window, and `observed_at` keeps moving with each response. App-JWT responses (token mints, installation discovery) no longer move the snapshot. Conserve and critical thresholds, and what conserve sheds, are unchanged.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.3.0)

### Added

- crux: agent step service, the sixth work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S6). `POST /v1/runs` with `"profile": "agent"` now opens a step session — a contained run that provisions its checkout and waits — and `POST /v1/runs/{id}/steps` runs one agent step inside it: a `claude`, `codex` or `process` backend reads the prompt in the sandbox and its JSON answer is checked against the request's `output_schema`, with bounded re-asks on a mismatch, a per-attempt timeout, tool and turn limits where the backend can enforce them, and a recorded `unsupported` refusal where it cannot. Each step is logged in the S4 command log, announced as a `step` turn signal, and read back with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/steps[/{n}]` or `crux --server … step run|list|show`.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.2.0)

### Added

- crux: turn signals, the fifth work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S5). Every contained run now keeps an append-only `<workdir>/runs/<id>/signals.jsonl` of where its turn is and how it ended — `started` and `done` from the runner (`done` on every terminal path, with status, exit code and timed-out), `needs-input`, `input` and `blocked` from a gate opened with the new `run` field (`crux gate open --run`), and `thinking`, `tool`, `blocked`, `needs-input` or `input` posted by the run's owner. Read it with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/signals?since_seq=&limit=` or `crux --server … signal list`, post with `POST /v1/runs/{id}/signals` or `crux --server … signal emit`; each signal is also published as `run.signal` on `/v1/events`. The last kick outcome of every agent is saved under `<workdir>/signals/agents/` before `agent.kick_outcome` is published, and `GET /v1/agents/{name}/kick-outcome` answers it with `settled_for_last_kick`, so a driver that missed the event learns from the record whether its turn ended.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.1.2)

### Fixed

- Contributor-first lanes are no longer left unworked by a relay that has used up its hourly or daily task allowance. A relay at its tier's `max_per_hour` or `max_per_day` is refused work until the window rolls, but it still counted as covering its role, so the governor kept the resident agent's kicks withheld while nobody worked the lane (for the daily cap, that can be most of a day). The hub now leaves such a relay out of coverage, using the same limit check that refuses it work.
- The contributor quota guard's `continue-until-reset` and `pause-until-reset` overrides no longer drop out when a provider restates the same reset time a little differently. They were pinned to the exact reset epoch, so when a Claude reading reported the weekly window resetting at 06:59:59.634Z instead of the 07:00:00.373Z the override had recorded, the override stopped applying and the relay stayed held for 14 minutes. Two reset times within five minutes of each other now count as the same reset; a real roll to the next window (an hour later at the shortest) still ends the override. The "Contributor quota guard released" log line also now names what released the hold (a recovered reading, or the continue-once / continue-until-reset / disable-session override with the window still below its reserve) instead of always saying a fresh reading cleared every reserve.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.1.1)

### Fixed

- A bad operator model id no longer restart-loops an agent silently. On the `claude` backend, a dotted `claude-…` id such as `claude-sonnet-5.5` (the Anthropic id is `claude-sonnet-5-5`) is now refused with a `400` that suggests the dashed spelling, on every path that sets a model: `PUT /api/config/agent/{name}/models`, the settings dialog, `POST /api/model` (card dropdown, `hivectl agent model-set`, admin MCP `agent.model`) and adding an agent. A well-formed id that hive's model list does not know is still saved, with a `warning` in the `PUT .../models` response, because it may be newer than the list. When Claude Code refuses a model anyway ("There's an issue with the selected model (…)"), the agent card now shows `blocked: inference (model_rejected): model <id> rejected by the CLI` instead of a healthy, logged-in agent; kicks and automatic restarts back off (2 minutes, doubling), and after 3 refusals of the same id the agent is paused with trigger `model-rejected` and a reason that names the model. Before, one hive's `guide` agent restarted 502 times in 24 hours with no warning. See [agent-configuration.md](src/docs/agent-configuration.md#model-ids-are-checked-when-you-save-them) and [troubleshooting.md](src/docs/troubleshooting.md#an-agent-shows-model--rejected-by-the-cli).
- A Claude token refresh no longer cuts an agent off from the fleet's shared login, and a dashboard Claude sign-in now actually recovers the agents it was meant to (refs [#17031](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17031), [#17039](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/17039)). Each per-UID claude agent reaches the one shared login through a symlink, `~/.claude/.credentials.json` -> `/data/home/.claude/.credentials.json`. Claude Code refreshes its token about every 8 hours by writing a temp file and renaming it over that path, which replaces the symlink with a private `0600` copy. From then on the agent ran on its own token: a dashboard sign-in rewrote the shared file and never reached it, and once the private token was revoked the agent answered every kick with `Login expired · Please run /login` or `OAuth token revoked`, was re-paused by the login detector or restart-looped, and nothing told the owner that signing in again could not help. On one hive seven agents sat in that state through two sign-ins until the links were fixed by hand. Hive now checks every agent's link at launch, on every credential-watchdog cycle and right after a dashboard sign-in. When a regular file has replaced it, hive moves the file aside as `.credentials.json.stale-<UTC time>` (never deleting it), keeps whichever credential is newer and still usable in the shared file (so one agent's fresh refresh becomes the fleet's login instead of stranding the rest), restores the symlink, and records a `claude_credential_rebridged` Audit Log entry. A successful dashboard Claude sign-in also resumes the claude agents the login detector paused, and only those: operator, fleet-breaker, hook and other pauses stay. On the dashboard, an affected agent's card now says **credential bridge broken (private stale file)** instead of a generic "needs login", and the agent card's Claude button reads **Sign in Claude for all agents**, with a tooltip saying it is the fleet-wide sign-in rather than a per-agent login.
- Signing in to Claude from the dashboard now stores the plan behind the token. After the token exchange hive reads `GET /api/oauth/profile`, the same call Claude Code makes after its own login, and writes `subscriptionType` (`max`, `pro`, `team` or `enterprise`) and `rateLimitTier` into `/data/home/.claude/.credentials.json`. Before this, sessions on a dashboard-signed-in subscription token showed "Claude API" / "API Usage Billing" in the Claude Code banner, which operators read as API billing. If the profile read fails, the sign-in still succeeds: the token is written without the two fields and a `WARN` is logged. The plan already on file is carried over only when hive recorded it for the same account and organization, so a different account never inherits a stale plan. See [agent-configuration.md](src/docs/agent-configuration.md).

## 2026-11-08 (v6.1.0)

### Added

- Added an opt-in code scanning sweep (`code_scanning`, off by default, per repo): it files a repository's open GitHub code scanning alerts (CodeQL, OSSF Scorecard, Trivy, …) at or above `min_severity` (default `high`) as grouped `[governor] Code scanning: …` issues sized for one PR, at most five new issues per repo per hourly pass, updates them as alerts are added, fixed or dismissed, and closes them when every alert is gone. OSSF Scorecard's repo-posture checks are left out by default. It needs the GitHub App permission "Code scanning alerts: Read-only"; without it the dashboard shows a notice for the repo. See `src/docs/code-scanning.md`.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.6)

### Fixed

- `just contribute-hive` now passes `HIVE_AGENT_ROLE` into the contributor container in the default container mode and in krun mode. Before, the role was dropped at the container boundary (whether it was exported in the shell or set in `contributor.env`), so the relay connected with no role and a contributor-first agent lane was never covered. Local mode already worked.
- `just contribute-hive` now passes the quota-guard switches into the contributor container in the default container mode and in krun mode. `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_GUARD` is forwarded, so `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_GUARD=off` at launch (the opt-out the guard banner names) takes effect. `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_POOL_DIR` is mounted into the container and the relay is pointed at the mount, so `just contribute-quota continue-once` and the other scoped controls reach a container relay (the container's entrypoint keeps that mount path even when `contributor.env` names the host path). `just contribute-quota` now exports what it reads from `contributor.env`, so it uses the same pool directory and pool key as the relay. Before, both switches did nothing for a container relay unless `contributor.env` held `export` lines.
- A contributor relay that is stopped just after its agent finished a task now reports that task before it exits. Before, a `docker stop` (or Ctrl-C) a second or two after the agent's `HIVE_VERDICT` lost the `task_complete`: the relay exited with the frame still queued, and the container entrypoint ended the container without waiting for the relay. The hub then recorded the run as "abandoned: connection lost with the task still held" and offered the issue again. Now the relay waits up to 5 seconds (`HIVE_RELAY_SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_MS`) for a finished task's `task_complete` or `task_failed` to be written, sends no `ready` and hands back any offer while it waits, and exits at once on a second signal or when nothing is pending. The entrypoint waits for the relay before it stops tmux and exits. See [contributor-relay.md](src/docs/contributor-relay.md).

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.5)

### Fixed

- Contributor-first lanes are no longer left unworked by a relay that is connected but not taking work. A relay in standby mode, or one whose quota guard or provider quota hold is holding all work, used to count as covering its role, so the governor withheld the resident agent's kicks while nobody worked the lane (seen on 2026-11-08: a scanner relay held at 15% of its weekly window kept scanner "covered"). The hub now skips standby relays, and relays tell a hub that advertises the new `quota_hold_v1` capability when a quota hold starts and ends; older relays and older hubs behave as before.
- Switching `contributor_first` on for a lane a relay already covers now logs "contributor relay covering a contributor-first lane — withholding the resident agent's kicks" once. The line was written only when the governor first saw the cover, and it records cover for every role whether or not the flag is set, so the usual order (relay connected, then the owner flips the General-tab toggle) left no log line at all.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.4)

### Fixed

- automerge: the lanes' "once per PR head" memory now lasts for the life of the hive process instead of one sweep. The queued, trusted-author and contributor lanes run every minute on a fresh engine, and the memory lived on that engine, so it was empty on every tick. A refused `update-branch` (a fork head behind a base that changed workflow files) was sent again every sweep: projectbluefin `fsdk-containers#508` logged "update-branch refused" about every 75 s. A merge GitHub refused for want of an approving review was sent again every minute instead of every 30 minutes. The trusted-author merge-forward was tried every sweep instead of once per head. "Logged once per head" holds, such as "merge train: PR left out of every train", were logged on every sweep (about 15 PRs every 80 s). The memory now lives on the long-lived GitHub client and is shared by every lane's engine. A read-only integration-eligibility check keeps its own memory, so a check that makes no write never marks a head as tried.
- A spoke that rejects webhook deliveries now says why. `/api/status.webhooks` (and `/api/gh-rate-limits`) gain `mode_reason_code` — `no_secret` when `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, `signature_failed` or `deliveries_rejected` when deliveries arrive but fail, `no_deliveries` when the secret is set but nothing verified has arrived — plus `rejected_1h` and `last_rejected_at`; `mode_reason` gives the same cause in plain words. The 503 a spoke without a secret returns is now counted like any other rejected delivery (the log stays at one WARN per process), and `/api/health/deep` plus the dashboard health tooltip carry a `webhooks` warning such as "polling — no GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET on this spoke; relayed deliveries are rejected with 503". Before this, a hosted spoke whose hub never provisioned the secret read `healthy:false, mode:polling` with no reason, the same as "GitHub isn't sending". Only whether the secret is set is reported, never its value. See [webhooks.md](src/docs/webhooks.md).

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.3)

### Fixed

- automerge: the contributor lane's held-run approval now tries each PR head once per process instead of once per sweep. The once-per-head mark lived on the one-shot engine each sweep builds, so a head GitHub refused with 403 (the App lacks `actions: write`) was re-POSTed every ~80 s; on projectbluefin two PRs spent ~270 charged calls an hour on `POST actions/runs/{id}/approve` that could never succeed. The refusal stands, with the existing `hive:unauthorized` note and label, until the head changes or the App gains `actions: write`. Held runs GitHub's approve endpoint never accepts (anything but a fork `pull_request` run or an Actions-bot run) are no longer sent.
- The dashboard metrics collector reads each repo's GitHub metadata at most once an hour instead of on every five-minute collect. It read the primary repo for the outreach card's stars and forks, and every watched repo for the Issues-disabled banner, every collect: 189 `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` calls in an hour on a hosted hive with 20 repos (2026-11-08), 177 of them charged, for numbers that change a few times a day. One read per repo now serves both, a failed read is retried on the next collect, and the banner reflects a changed Issues setting within the hour. The advisory issue's create path still checks `has_issues` fresh before it creates.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.2)

### Fixed

- The GitHub ETag cache now keeps the hive's repeat reads, so they come back as free `304`s instead of being charged in full. The cache held 64 MiB of raw response bodies, and one closed-pull-request list page is about 2 MiB: on a hosted hive with 20 repos (2026-11-08) one variant of that list was 36 MiB across the repos, and the hive reads several variants every cycle. Each sweep pushed the rest of the working set out, so the cache sat at about 500 entries and, for example, the metrics collector's repo reads, which were unchanged, came back `304` only 12 times in 189. Bodies of 1 KiB or more are now held gzip-compressed (about 7x smaller), the entry bound is 16384, and `HIVE_GITHUB_ETAG_CACHE_MAX_MB` sets the byte bound for a hive that needs more. `etag_cache` in `/api/gh-rate-limits` and the status payload now also reports `bytes`, `max_bytes` and `evictions`.
- github: the issue un-park sweep reuses an item's comment list and label timeline while the item's `updated_at` in the issue list has not moved, instead of re-reading both for every parked issue and waiting PR on every pass. The seven-day command window, repo-permission and label-trust checks still run on every pass against the reused data; an item is read again when it changes, when the read was taken within two minutes of its last update, after the sweep writes to it, and at least every six hours. On the knuckle hive these reads were the largest REST consumer (`hive:issue_unpark`: 878 comment and 363 timeline reads charged in 50 minutes).

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.1)

### Fixed

- release: cap GitHub Release notes at `RELEASE_NOTES_MAX_CHARS` (120000) before the SBOM/NOTICE trailer, cutting the changelog section at a bullet boundary and linking the tag's full `CHANGELOG.md` section, so a first-on-the-line release such as v6.0.0 no longer fails `gh release create` with HTTP 422 "body is too long" after the tag and image retags have landed.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.204.1)

### Fixed

- Fleet report: repeated `copilot sniff: upstream dial failed` ERRORs — the proxy could not reach a `*.githubcopilot.com` host it was usage-sniffing, such as a dial timeout to `telemetry.enterprise.githubcopilot.com` — are now classified as `proxy_connect_dial_failed` (medium, component `github-proxy`, remedy "restore the spoke's outbound proxy or network path") alongside `proxy: CONNECT dial failed`, instead of surfacing as `unclassified_error_repeated` ([#17262](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17262)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.204.0)

### Added

- crux: agent step service, the sixth work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S6). `POST /v1/runs` with `"profile": "agent"` now opens a step session — a contained run that provisions its checkout and waits — and `POST /v1/runs/{id}/steps` runs one agent step inside it: a `claude`, `codex` or `process` backend reads the prompt in the sandbox and its JSON answer is checked against the request's `output_schema`, with bounded re-asks on a mismatch, a per-attempt timeout, tool and turn limits where the backend can enforce them, and a recorded `unsupported` refusal where it cannot. Each step is logged in the S4 command log, announced as a `step` turn signal, and read back with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/steps[/{n}]` or `crux --server … step run|list|show`.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.203.0)

### Added

- crux: checkout requests are bounded by a server ceiling (`--checkout-max-bytes`, `CRUX_CHECKOUT_MAX_BYTES`), private repositories clone with `CRUX_CHECKOUT_TOKEN` through a credential helper that never logs the token, and the `job` run backend isolates each Job with a deny-all NetworkPolicy by default (`job_network: none|host|default`)
- **Maintainer notes on the Activity Monitor.** With more than one maintainer running a hive, there was nowhere on the dashboard to leave a colleague a word about an item short of a GitHub comment everyone else could read. Each row now carries a 🗒 button with a count badge: click it for the item's maintainer notes — who wrote what, when — and a one-line composer (⌘/Ctrl+Enter). Notes are stored on the spoke in the append-only `/data/maintainer-notes.jsonl` and are never written to GitHub; every signed-in maintainer sees them, adding one takes write on the repo, deleting is author-or-owner, and the `maintainer-notes` SSE frame keeps the other browsers live. The scheduler types an item's notes into the agent's kick under `# Maintainer notes` (1 KB cap), so what a maintainer wrote on the row reaches whoever picks it up. `GET`/`POST /api/notes`, `DELETE /api/notes/{id}`; audited as `maintainer_note_add` / `maintainer_note_delete`.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.202.0)

### Added

- crux: turn signals, the fifth work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S5). Every contained run now keeps an append-only `<workdir>/runs/<id>/signals.jsonl` of where its turn is and how it ended — `started` and `done` from the runner (`done` on every terminal path, with status, exit code and timed-out), `needs-input`, `input` and `blocked` from a gate opened with the new `run` field (`crux gate open --run`), and `thinking`, `tool`, `blocked`, `needs-input` or `input` posted by the run's owner. Read it with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/signals?since_seq=&limit=` or `crux --server … signal list`, post with `POST /v1/runs/{id}/signals` or `crux --server … signal emit`; each signal is also published as `run.signal` on `/v1/events`. The last kick outcome of every agent is saved under `<workdir>/signals/agents/` before `agent.kick_outcome` is published, and `GET /v1/agents/{name}/kick-outcome` answers it with `settled_for_last_kick`, so a driver that missed the event learns from the record whether its turn ended.

### Security

- The CLI-memory drain now reaches each memory store by opening its directories one component at a time from the filesystem root, refusing any component that is a symlink and requiring each opened directory to be the inode `Lstat` saw. `cliMemoryDrainSources` already resolved stores with `EvalSymlinks` and kept only those under the agent's own home, but the drain still opened the store root by path, so an agent that swapped `.claude`, `projects` or a project slug for a symlink after that listing could have had another agent's store (or any hive-readable `memory/*.md` tree) drained under its own name and, with `truncate`, emptied. Such a store is now reported in `kept` and the drain error, never followed ([#17256](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17256)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.201.1)

### Security

- The CLI-memory drain opens every agent memory file through an `os.Root` anchored at its store and truncates it through the descriptor it read, instead of reading and `os.Truncate`-ing by path after the listing. The store belongs to the agent and the drain runs with the hive's privileges, so an agent that swapped a listed `.md` (or the store directory) for a symlink between the listing and the open could have had the hive copy any file it can read into the knowledge vault, or empty any file it can write — `TruncateDrained` counts a file with no parseable fact as "fully stored". Such a path is now reported in `kept` and the drain error, never followed ([#17251](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17251)).
- The drain also refuses a memory-file symlink whose target stays inside the store root (for a single-file store such as `GEMINI.md` that root is its parent, e.g. `~/.gemini/`), by `Lstat`ing each entry through the root and requiring the opened file to be the same inode, and `cliMemoryDrainSources` now resolves each store with `EvalSymlinks` and drops any that leaves the agent's own home — so a `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` pointed at another agent's store is never drained or truncated under this agent's name ([#17251](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17251)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.201.0)

### Added

- crux: per-run command log, the fourth work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S4). A contained run now records the command the runner hands to the sandbox — argv, cwd, start and end times, exit code, status (`completed`, `failed`, `unfinished` or `cancelled`), total stdout/stderr byte counts and a scrubbed head and tail of each — to `<workdir>/runs/<id>/commands.jsonl`, append-only. Read it with `GET /v1/runs/{id}/cmdlog?since_seq=&limit=` (paged by `next_seq`/`more`, visible only to the run's owner) or `crux --server … cmdlog list|show <run>`. Each record carries `capture: "runner"`: commands the run's process spawns itself (shell pipelines, `make` recipes, an agent's own tool calls) are not counted, and the work-services design note says so explicitly; `capture: "hook"` is reserved for an in-sandbox shim in a later slice.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.200.0)

### Added

- crux: human gates, the third work service of the Crux work-services RFC ([hivecommons/crux#114](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/114) S3). A driver opens a gate with `POST /v1/gates` (or `crux --server … gate open`) and a person answers it with `crux gate answer <id> --choice approve` or `POST /v1/gates/{id}/answer`. Answers must be one of the offered choices, and any free text goes in a separate note. The record keeps both who opened the gate and who answered it. An opener answering its own gate needs the explicit, audited `--as-operator` override. Gates are stored under `<workdir>/gates` (`pending/`, `resolved/` and a `gates.jsonl` journal), so they survive a `crux serve` restart. Re-opening the same gate returns the same id and the recorded answer. A gate that times out is marked `expired`, which is neither approval nor denial. `GET /v1/gates/{id}/wait` and `crux gate wait` block until the gate is answered or expires, and `gate.opened`, `gate.answered` and `gate.expired` events appear on `/v1/events`.

### Changed

- **dashboard:** the sidebar **Overview** pill now reads `BP = 19/4` instead of a bare `19/4`, naming the pair *board pressure* (BP) — the open issues and PRs the configured repos put on this hive's board, total open issues over total open PRs, before any of them is sorted into actionable, held, blocked or outside. The tooltip opens with "Board pressure (BP): 19 open issues / 4 open PRs — …" ahead of the existing equation; the Governor, Contributors and Knowledge pills are unchanged, and the term is defined in the dashboard glossary (#17240).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.199.3)

### Fixed

- **automerge:** the contributor lane's hive-wide auto-promotion search no longer drops every other repository when GitHub refuses to search one of them (`422 Validation Failed` for a renamed, deleted or invisible repo, or an unsearchable author): the chunk is re-asked one repository at a time, and each refused (author, repository) pair warns once and is left out of the search for an hour instead of repeating the 422 and the `repo search failed` warning on every sweep (#17148).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.199.2)

### Fixed

- The crux pushbroker pre-push secret gate now runs `git diff`/`git show` with `--text --no-textconv`, so a file git classifies as binary (a NUL byte in its first bytes, or a path marked `-diff`/`binary` in a committed `.gitattributes`) is scanned for token-shaped secrets instead of being hidden behind "Binary files differ" ([crux#128](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/128)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.199.1)

### Fixed

- An open issue labelled `proposal` or `kind/design` that nobody has claimed now derives the new `stage/018-open-for-discussion` and reads **Open for discussion** in the activity monitor instead of sitting at `stage/010-actionable` as agent work no lane will usefully pick up — including a proposal whose `Refs` RFC PR merged and left it `hive/partially-addressed`, a `040 → 018` fall booked as progress, not a regression. The stage reason names the label (`open for discussion: proposal`). The issue stays claimable: the claim gate is unchanged, a `/claim`, relay or agent claim stages it 020 / 030 as before, and removing the label returns it to 010 ([#17150](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17150)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.199.0)

### Added

- The model-ranked knowledge advisor now persists one compact record per decision (agent, kick id, the kick's primed issue/PR refs, mode, arm `shadow|deliver|holdout`, outcome, slug; never the model's reason or pane text) to `/data/knowledge-advisor-decisions.jsonl`, and the retro lane reads that store in production, so beads get their real `AdvisorArm` instead of always `none` and the `holdout_percent` comparison can be read from `Lane.AdvisorArmSummary()` ([#17211](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17211), part of [#17054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17054)).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.198.0)

### Added

- **cli memory:** with `agents.cli_memory.drain_to_knowledge` on, Hive now seeds a Claude Code `SessionEnd` hook running the new `hive memory-drain --cli claude --agent "$HIVE_AGENT"` command, so a session's memory becomes draft knowledge (and the stored files are emptied) when the session ends; the new `agents.cli_memory.drain_on_write` key (default off, fleet-wide or per agent) adds a `PostToolUse` hook that does the same as soon as a memory file is written. Operator `hooks` entries are kept, and turning the keys off removes only Hive's entry (#17209, #17210).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.197.0)

### Added

- The retro lane now records each bead's knowledge-advisor arm (`none|shadow|deliver|holdout|mixed`) with decision, delivered and held-out counters on `RetroRecord`, passes only those counters to the analysis model, and can summarize mean fix attempts, CI failures and kicks per arm with no model call, so the `holdout_percent` comparison needs no new instrumentation ([#17156](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17156), part of [#17054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17054)).

### Security

- crux contained runs: the ad-hoc `worktree {repo, commit}` form now refuses a non-canonical repository URL (`.`/`..`/empty segments, percent-encoding, credentials, query or fragment) and matches `repo_allowlist` on a segment boundary, the same rules the pinned-checkout service applies (#17102). A bare string-prefix check let `https://github.com/org/../other/repo` and `https://github.com/org-evil/…` pass an allowlist of `https://github.com/org`, and git resolved the `..` into a clone off the allowlist. Non-canonical `repo_allowlist` entries are now a configuration error (#17213).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.196.0)

### Added

- The Activity monitor lists rows that need you first on phones, with a sticky "waiting on you" count line that toggles the Waiting on you filter.
- **cli memory:** an agent can now ask the hive to drain its own Claude memory into the knowledge store on demand, by dropping a request into `/var/run/hive-metrics/memory-drain-requests`; the hive resolves the stores from the agent's own home (optionally narrowed to the hook's project `cwd`), refuses a request naming any other agent, audits each call as `cli_memory_drain_requested`, empties with `truncate` only the files whose every fact is in the vault, and answers a no-op when `agents.cli_memory.drain_to_knowledge` is off for that agent (#17208).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.195.0)

### Added

- **crux serve:** every API request now gets a span and `crux.serve.requests` / `crux.serve.request.duration` metrics, labelled only by method, route pattern (for example `GET /v1/agents/{name}`) and status class; no-op unless an OTel provider is configured (hivecommons/crux#126).
- **knowledge advisor:** with `knowledge.advisor_llm` set, a small model now ranks the mid-task advisor's candidates and picks one stored entry or nothing; it never writes advice. `shadow` delivers the matcher's top entry and logs the model's pick, `rank` delivers the pick with an optional `holdout_percent` control arm, budgets (6 calls per agent-hour, 300 per UTC day) and timeouts fail closed or to the matcher per `on_error`, and every decision writes one `knowledge advisor: decision` log line (#17155).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.194.0)

### Added

- CLI memory drain, phase 1 completion (#17056): a fact already in the vault now gains the draining agent's `agent:<name>` tag instead of being ignored, and keeps whatever state an operator gave it, so a deprecated memory is never revived. A memory file whose facts did not all reach the vault (vault unwritable, 200-facts-per-drain cap) is copied to `/data/knowledge/auto-memory-spool/<agent>/` before `clear_on_kick` wipes the store and retried on the agent's next drain; the drain log line now reports `spooled S`. `POST /api/knowledge/create` takes `state` (`approved` default, or `draft`, which is written into the local channel named by `layer` and never overwrites an existing entry) and accepts a `cli-memory`-tagged fact only as a draft carrying the drain's own tags. `bd create --type knowledge [--state] [--tag]… [--layer]` creates a fact through that endpoint.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.193.2)

### Changed

- Activity monitor text now has a 12px floor on phones, so the chips, timestamps and column headers stay readable at 390px wide.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.193.1)

### Changed

- Dashboard: on phones each Activity monitor row is a ~90px card — ☐/⋯ in the top-right corner, a clamped head (repo chip, #ref, two-line title, PR line, chips), the progress pill, one line of caption, no "no linked issue" placeholder — the pill sheet carries the full title and note, and the phone ergonomics probe counts the padded hit areas the pill and inline chips grow to 44px with; the 1280 layout is unchanged (hivecommons/hive#17161).
- **knowledge advisor:** the runtime now calls the knowledge adviser off the agent's poll goroutine with at most one call in flight per agent, so a slow adviser no longer stalls the tick; results are held until the delivery gates pass and dropped if the kick changed. Each observed scope carries an `Action` (`read`/`edit`/`run`) and is re-advised at most once, on its first edit or next `gh` command. An adviser can request a token-scrubbed pane tail, which the built-in matcher never does (#17153).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.193.0)

### Added

- Dashboard: on phones the Activity monitor Merged and merge-queue lists now open as full-width modal sheets with tap-sized rows, closable with ✕, Esc or backdrop, instead of clipped popovers; desktop popovers are unchanged (#17165).

### Fixed

## 2026-11-08 (v5.192.0)

### Added

- The Hive activity monitor on a landscape phone (≤500px tall, coarse pointer) uses the compact filter bar, hides the column header so the sticky stack is a single bar, and shows at most one merge banner, so rows are visible instead of chrome; portrait and desktop are unchanged (#17166, part of #17158).
- Activity monitor on a phone: every control meets the 44px coarse-pointer floor (`--tap-target-touch`), the per-row select / ⋯ controls move from the hidden left gutter into the row header, and the ⋯ menu opens as a full-screen sheet with tap-sized items.

Config only; the ranking pass lands separately (hivecommons/hive#17154).
