## 2026-11-08 (v5.191.1)

### Fixed

- Activity Monitor no longer draws a "Preparation train · 0 confirmed PRs" header over a single base-preparation ticket; one owner is the refresh lock holder, not a train, and its row comment already carries its state.

## 2026-11-08 (v5.191.0)

### Added

- Drained CLI-memory drafts (`cli-memory` tag) never reach an agent while they are drafts: not through the kick primer or knowledge advisor, not through any `?agent=` TOC or entry read, and not through curator auto-promotion, even when `include_states` admits drafts. The dashboard's knowledge view gains an **Auto-memory drafts** filter that shows each draft's `agent:` tags with owner-only Approve and Discard actions. A new owner-only command, `hivectl knowledge drain-memory --legacy [--truncate]`, drains the shared `/data/home/.claude/projects/*/memory` store into drafts tagged `agent:shared` (#17058).
- The Hive activity monitor on a phone replaces its 13-control toolbar and label chips with a sticky compact filter bar (All / PRs / Issues, Needs attention, Waiting on you, ⋯ Filters) that opens the full toolbar in a modal sheet, so the first row is visible without scrolling; desktop is unchanged (#17159, part of #17158).

### Fixed

- **fleetreport:** the stage engine's `stage flap suppressed` warning no longer files an `unclassified_error_repeated` fleet selfreport; refusing a same-head reversal is the flap guard working as designed and stays in local logs (#17142).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.190.0)

### Added

- Crux contained runs (`POST /v1/runs`, `crux runs start --checkout`) can execute in an S1 pinned checkout: the checkout's owner (or the operator) names its id, the run record carries it, and the checkout refuses deletion with 409 while the run is live. `/v1/runs` now admits lane project principals, with runs owned by and readable/cancellable only to their creator or the operator (hivecommons/crux#114 S1+S2).
- Hives with no `knowledge.git_sources` now index their primary repo's knowledge dir (`bead_synthesizer.publish.path`, else `docs/knowledge/` or `src/docs/knowledge/`) as a seeded `<repo>-knowledge` project-layer git source, and `knowledge.primer.max_bytes` defaults to 8192 instead of 4096.

### Fixed

- fix(crux): move pane-analysis helpers out of agent/manager_kick.go to stay under the file-size ratchet

## 2026-11-08 (v5.189.3)

### Fixed

- **fleetreport:** the stage dampener's `stage transition suppressed by dampener` warning no longer files an `unclassified_error_repeated` fleet selfreport; the suppression is the stage engine working as designed and stays in local logs (#17103).
- Closing-claim parsing no longer treats a parenthetical citation after a closing word (`fix in that section (#333)`) or the passive `closed by #N` as a claim, so the supersession sweep no longer closes changelog/docs follow-ups that cite the merged fixes they record (#17134).

## 2026-11-08 (v5.189.2)

### Fixed

- release: cap GitHub Release notes at `RELEASE_NOTES_MAX_CHARS` (120000) before the SBOM/NOTICE trailer, cutting the changelog section at a bullet boundary and linking the tag's full `CHANGELOG.md` section, so a first-on-the-line release such as v6.0.0 no longer fails `gh release create` with HTTP 422 "body is too long" after the tag and image retags have landed.

## 2026-11-08 (v6.0.0)

### Added

- Admin MCP can now set governor mode thresholds and the threshold-scaling curve through the preview-and-confirm write contract, with the `thresholds_source` reset and cadence effects disclosed before confirmation.
- dashboard: sidebar nav peeks collapsed sections open and restores them on the next jump (#10199)
- admin MCP: review_queue and governor_setup_proposal read tools (#10231)
- Added fake-engine conformance tests for the planning-engine boundary, covering the lease invariants an engine never sees, every row of the ADR-0021 failure-mapping table, and a second registered engine surfacing on the stage receipt and the run plan import ([#10358](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10358)).
- spektacular: smoke-test the pinned real CLI (#10351)
- worksource: add external HTTP/JSON work source behind work_source.type (#10363)
- planengine: neutral planning-engine types, Engine interface and Register/Lookup (#10369)
- dashboard: external work-source type picker, display-name badge and dropped-item counter (#10377)
- feat(config): runs.engine selector with fail-closed validation (#10387)
- feat: runs.engine selector docs and a Writing a planning engine guide (#10452)
- feat(dashboard): in-place Spek recheck on v6 (revision bump, single lease) (#10807)
- config: per-repo `project.repo_policies[].merge_strategy` (`direct` | `hive-serialized`) with validation, asymmetric permission and a read/write API; unset means `direct`. After a downgrade to a Hive without this feature the key is silently ignored and repos go back to `direct` (#10886)
- github: add lane-only branch-rules reader for ruleset required checks, up-to-date enforcement and merge_queue rule detection (#10887)
- The self-merge sweep, the lgtm queue sweep and the `hive-merge` relay now route through the serialized lane for repos with `merge_strategy: hive-serialized` ([#10889](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10889)). Every existing gate still applies (auto-merge switch, pause, ACMM level, holds, CI, approvals); the lane only adds to them. Only the PR at the front of the lane merges, after a final re-check that the path's own authorization still holds for the exact head. Other PRs are deferred with "not at the front of the lane", which is expected, not an error, and one sweep pass never merges two PRs into the same lane branch. A target branch with GitHub's native merge queue gets no direct merge from Hive, and the refusal says why. `direct` repos (the default) behave exactly as before.
- Admin MCP gains a read-only `version_read` tool that returns the running build from `/api/version` (`currentCommit`, `branch`, `channel`, `commitsBehind`, `behind`), and launched agents now default `HIVE_SHA` to the binary's own short commit so their identity footers stop reading `unknown`.
- The watchdog's "alive but not producing" dashboard warning now names what is queued ([#11223](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11223)). The existing text stays as the prefix, followed by "hive-wide" (the count is the governor's hive-wide queue, not that agent's own) and up to three queued items as `owner/repo#N` links to the forge, with "+N more" for the rest — so an operator can open the waiting issue or PR straight from the banner instead of hunting for it across repos.
- Upstream watch: a fork's first pass now starts at the fork's last commit in common with its upstream, or at a new optional per-repo `upstream_watch.repos.<repo>.start_from: YYYY-MM-DD`, instead of scanning the whole upstream history; and a merged-PR or release listing cut short by its page cap is reported with a warning and never advances the watermark, so older items are no longer skipped silently.
- The status snapshot now lists `hold_sources` on every held issue and pull request (level gate, outreach, reporter trust, self-authorization, SHA hold, holdguard, human-merge path, donated standby, dashboard pause, person or unknown), detected read-only and cached per PR so an unchanged refresh makes no extra GitHub API calls (#11564).
- The admin MCP `review_queue` tool and the weekly owner advice now read the server's "your turn" decision (hivecommons/hive#11507, part D2). `review_queue` returns exactly the your-turn items (the Projects inbox's N plus M, parked issues included), each with its `verb`, `reason_code`, `reason` and `inbox_rank`, in `inbox_rank` order, with `counts.your_turn` and `counts.to_close` matching the inbox header; the Overview export rows carry `inbox_rank`. The `clear-human-gate-prs` and `unblock-human-issues` advice rules count the your-turn PRs and issues from the same stored decision (`counts.yourTurn` and `counts.toClose` on `GET /api/hive-advice`) instead of re-reading `needs-human` and band labels, and the advice's open-issue count now includes parked and other non-actionable issues. The dashboard documentation describes the inbox, the marker, the verbs, reason codes, the ownership-by-level table, precedence, hold sources, the adjudicator wait rule, the safety net and the Parked and Gated band titles, and an automated agreement check verifies that card markers, inbox rows, the Overview Your turn term and chart slices, the review queue, the owner advice and the Projects counter describe the same set over the level table and a mixed fixture.
- The Overview JSON exports (`GET /api/overview/issues.json` and `prs.json`) now carry `snapshot_instance`, `snapshot_seq` and `snapshot_at`, naming the status snapshot their rows came from. `review_queue` compares the two exports it merges, re-reads both once when a status refresh landed between them, and otherwise fails asking the caller to retry rather than mixing `inbox_rank`s from two snapshots (hivecommons/hive#11507, part D2).
- A fork PR that fails because its upstream project is broken is no longer re-queued as "fix before new" on every kick ([#11609](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11609)). `hive-baseline-check.sh` now also reads the failing check on the upstream repository's default branch (the GitHub fork parent, or `--upstream OWNER/REPO`). When the check is red there and this repository's own default branch has no fresh green for it, the helper returns `DEFER_EXTERNAL` with an `external_marker` pinned to the PR head, the check and its failing check run. The agent ends its one triage comment with that marker. While every failing check run at the current head carries one, the governor sets `deferred_external` on the PR's `ci-failing.json` row, and FIX-BEFORE-NEW and CI_FAILING name the PR only as deferred. A push, a newly failing check, or a re-run of the check (a new run id, e.g. after it went green and failed again at the same head) brings it back. Batched GraphQL enrichment now carries each check run's real id (`databaseId`) instead of a positional stand-in, which the marker needs and which the CI failure-excerpt annotation lookup also uses.
- Try Hive on kind: a new `src/deploy/kustomize/overlays/kind/` overlay (core `k8s` base without the inference component, kind's `standard` StorageClass, agents on an external OpenAI-compatible endpoint), a [`try-hive-on-kind.md`](src/docs/try-hive-on-kind.md) walkthrough with kind-specific gotchas, and a `src/deploy/test_kind_quickstart.sh` smoke test ([#11657](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11657)).
- Nous (Strategy Lab) state is now durable: the governor ledger, learned principles, baseline snapshots and the dashboard panel configuration (mode, scope, goals, output, fast-fail, schedule, controllables) all live under `/data/nous` on the PVC — configurable with `data.nous_dir` / `HIVE_NOUS_DATA_DIR` — and survive pod restarts. Legacy `/var/run/nous/governor` files are migrated forward at boot, and the owner spoke backup/restore now carries `nous/` (snapshots excluded). RFC [#11585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11585) part 1/8 ([#11694](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11694)).
- The Experiment Lab now reads the Nous ledger and principles live instead of a snapshot taken at boot: every `GET /api/nous/status`, `/ledger` and `/principles` re-checks `<nous_dir>/governor/ledger.json` and `principles.json` (one stat per file; re-parsed only when changed), so a round the experimentation agent finishes shows up on the next panel poll without a restart. The `type`/`status` mismatch between what Nous writes and what the panel grouped on is resolved with one shared schema (`pkg/nousstore`): every ledger entry served carries `type` (`baseline`, `experiment`, `dry_run`, `analysis`, `shadow_analysis`) and `status` (`pending`, `active`, `completed`, `aborted`), plus `outcome` from Nous's `h_main_result`; every principle carries `type` (`domain`/`meta`, from Nous's `category`) and `status` (`active`/`updated`/`pruned`). Files written without the fields load with defaults; explicit unknown values are logged and defaulted rather than hiding the row; a half-written file keeps the last good copy. The panel shows type and status chips on each principle and on a new recent-rounds list, and the history timeline is keyed by status. `/api/nous/*` paths and `NousState` are unchanged. RFC [#11585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11585) part 4/8 ([#11697](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11697)).
- Nous: `experimenter` agent role with a Go engine contract (`pkg/nousengine`), `agents.<name>.engine` (default `nous`), and `nous.dispatcher` / `HIVE_NOUS_DISPATCHER` making Nous run `inline` by default while `sdk` stays selectable (RFC #11585 part 5, #11698)
- Experiment Lab campaigns can declare pinned dependencies — repos by full commit, files by URL plus sha256 — and `hive nous-setup` (run by `bin/nous-runner.sh` before the engine starts) fetches them from allowlisted hosts only, verifies every pin, caches them and records the resolved versions plus toolchain versions in `<nous_dir>/<run-id>/dependencies.json`. The allowlist is `nous.fetch_allowlist` / `HIVE_NOUS_FETCH_ALLOWLIST` (default `github.com`, exact hostnames, deny-by-default) and is reported by `GET /api/nous/status`; a fetch outside it, an unpinned declaration or a hash/commit mismatch refuses to start the campaign. Supply-chain guards now fail CI if the Nous pins drift or the runner grows a fetch of its own. RFC [#11585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11585) part 7/8 ([#11700](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11700)).
- Nous (Experiment Lab) can now mirror finished campaign folders to an optional, opt-in GitHub artifact repository (`nous.artifact_repo` / `HIVE_NOUS_ARTIFACT_REPO`) as per-campaign PRs pushed by the hive's own App identity, with secret scrubbing, a filename denylist, size caps, API-budget-aware backoff, status under `GET /api/nous/status.artifact_repo` and an owner-only `POST /api/nous/artifacts/sync` (RFC #11585 part 8).
- v6] Nous: verdict card and manual Promote (RFC 11585 part 6/8) (#11746)
- **Hive Chat phone sweep enforces message-list height minimums and boots its own hive** (#11870): the sweep now fails when `#hiveChatMessages` drops below `MIN_MESSAGES_HEIGHT_412x839` (410px) or `MIN_MESSAGES_HEIGHT_412x480_KEYBOARD` (160px), writes measured vs minimum to the job summary, and by default runs against a throwaway CI-booted hive in the token-less open/dev dashboard mode (a token-secured hive serves the sign-in page on `/`, which the headless browser cannot get past); the live-hive mode stays available as a manual `workflow_dispatch` input.
- Admin MCP gains read-only `log_read` and `log_sources` tools (and `GET /api/logs/read`, `GET /api/logs/sources`) that read the hive's own log and its rotated, compressed history without shell access: bounded lines and bytes, RFC 3339 windows, level and text filters, backwards cursor paging across rotation, read-time scrubbing of credentials and the hive's own secret values with counted redactions, and a read-write role check in the handler. `pkg/logscrub` gains a `basic-auth` category; `governor.logging.read_scan_max_mb` lowers the per-read scan bound (#11942).
- Admin MCP gains read-only diagnostic tools for an agent's live terminal log and archived kick logs, a run's stage log and detail, the deep health check, prompt history and the effective configuration with its provenance. They work the same in-hive and over stdio, are scrubbed, stay under 128 KiB and disclose any truncation ([#11943](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11943)). Configuration values are shown only for documented non-secret keys, and only to an owner the hive itself verified.
- Admin MCP `log_read` and `log_sources` gain the `proxy`, `hive-output`, `litellm` and `requests` sources: the dashboard auth proxy's output and the hive's pre-log output (both still on the container's stdout/stderr), the local litellm proxy's output (kept, not added to container output), and a dashboard request log (method, query-free path, status, `duration_ms`, auth `public`/`ok`/`failed`/`none`; auth-proxy terminal traffic and gateway-refused requests excluded). Files are 0600 in a 0700 `HIVE_OUTPUT_LOG_DIR` (default `/data/.hive/logs`), at most 5 × 10 MiB and 7 days per source; on a deployment where a process does not run (hub image, litellm local proxy off) the source is not available with a reason (#11944).
- Admin MCP can now tell whether the hive crashed, was killed or ran out of memory, without host access ([#11945](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11945)). Each start is recorded with how the previous run ended (`clean`, `not-closed`, `self-upgrade-failed` or `unknown`), its last-seen-alive time and its last memory reading, and can be read through the new `starts` log source. Every hive log line carries the short start identifier. The Go runtime's fatal-error trace is kept per start as the `crash` source (last 10, at most 1 MiB each; SIGKILL and out-of-memory kills leave none). `fleet_status` reports the container's memory limit (`memLimit`, `unlimited` when none) and out-of-memory kill count (`oomKillCount`). The admin MCP docs now list the evidence that still needs a host shell, with its in-container substitute.
- The stdio `hive-admin-mcp` binary now warns when it is out of step with the hub ([#12317](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12317), part of [#12316](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12316)). At startup and on `select_hive` it reads the active hive's `/api/version`; when the short SHAs differ it sends a one-line notice naming both builds and the update steps in `src/docs/admin-mcp.md` as the `initialize` instructions, and appends it to `unsupported admin MCP read tool`, `unknown tool` and hub 404 errors. Previously a stale binary failed new tools with no hint that it needed re-extracting or rebuilding. Nothing changes when the builds match or either SHA is unknown. The binary also identifies itself with `User-Agent: hive-admin-mcp/<version>+<short sha>`, and hivectl's client User-Agent is now configurable.
- Hub records the last-seen stdio `hive-admin-mcp` build and timestamp from a validated `hive-admin-mcp/<version>+<short>` `User-Agent` on `/api/version`, `/api/status`, `/api/status/summary` and admin MCP read calls, exposes them on `/api/version` and `version_read` next to `hub_build`, and flags build skew on the dashboard; other User-Agents (including `hivectl/0.1`) are never recorded (#12318).
- hivestate: new `mode-stuck` observation fires when the governor sits in `surge` or `idle` for 7 days, backed by a per-mode sample count on hourly buckets ([#12341](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12341)).
- `hive-open-issue` can record a typed release-only owner step with a tag and immutable target SHA while keeping the issue parked for its owner; this metadata does not yet authorize Hive to publish releases ([#12483](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12483)).
- Added the repo-policy opt-in `project.repo_policies[].release_on_approve` (default off); config only, no behaviour change yet (#12631).
- Opted-in repositories can have the hub create a typed release exactly once after an eligible maintainer replies `/hive approve`, with live target, tag, CI, and optional version-source checks ([#12634](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12634)).
- Scanner release-only owner steps now name the exact release tag and target in opt-in your-turn notices, and the dashboard Your-turn menu can run the same guarded release action.
- hivestate: pure observation detectors over the snapshot series (queue growth, hold growth, SLA, idle/thrashing agents, token efficiency) (#12652)
- Nous hive-state observations can be filed upstream when `nous.observations.enabled` is set (default off), capped by a restart-safe rolling weekly budget `nous.observations.max_per_week` (default 5) and never during a self-upgrade drain ([#12654](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12654)).
- `governor.labels.stage.engine.mode` (`off` / `shadow` / `enforce`, default `shadow`; Settings → Labels) switches the ADR-0025 central stage engine at runtime ([#13010](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13010), part of [#12999](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12999)): one reconciler is shared by the issue and PR sweeps, `off` is legacy pass-through, `shadow` counts every legacy/engine disagreement, `enforce` lets the engine write. `/api/status.stageEngine`, the activity tracker's status strip and the `hive_stage_*` series on `/metrics` report mode, derivations, mismatches and anomalies; the shadow → enforce rollout runbook is in `operator-reference.md`.
- Sidebar x/y count pills for Overview and Governor (#13148)
- `hivectl hives`, the TUI's Hives pane and the Commons web UI (`hivectl hives web`) now commit `profiles.yml` under a shared cross-process lock (`profiles.yml.lock`, mode 0600) and only if the file is still the revision they loaded. An edit made from one surface while another changed the hives is refused with nothing written — the CLI/TUI ask you to re-run, the web UI returns 409 "requires renewed review" — instead of one writer silently overwriting the other. ([#13179](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13179))
- Contributor relays now publish local scope adoption, subscription readiness, and draining task status for truthful contribution UI acknowledgements ([#13290](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13290)).
- `hivectl hives activity` shows per-repository completed tasks, outcomes and last activity from a new bounded, owner-only local relay history (`relay-activity.jsonl`), with `--clear` to forget it without touching profiles or consent.
- A `blocked` issue whose body carries `<!-- hive:recheck-after <RFC3339> -->` (and no blocked-on PR) is now listed as `blocked until <t>`, the activity monitor's blocked chip shows `re-check at <t>`, and once the deadline passes the blocked sweep lifts `blocked` with one `deadline <t> passed; re-triaging` note so the scanner re-triages it; issues that also carry `<!-- hive:ops-tracking -->` stay blocked (#13310).
- `crux/api` gains a Go client (`api.NewClient`) for `crux serve`: every verb, SSE log following and the runtime event stream, over a unix socket or TCP with a bearer token (#13536).
- The `crux` CLI gains a remote mode: `--server ADDR` (or `CRUX_SERVER`) with `--token` (or `CRUX_TOKEN`) makes `run`, `ps`, `logs`, `kick` and `stop` drive a `crux serve` over the API instead of an in-process runtime; `logs -f` follows the agent's output (#13536).
- `crux serve` exposes the agent runtime over a local HTTP+JSON API (Crux Stage 3, [#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536)): a unix socket (`$CRUX_SOCKET`, default `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/crux/crux.sock`, created 0600) and optionally TCP with `--listen`, which is refused without a bearer token (`--token` / `$CRUX_TOKEN`). The routes under `/v1` mirror the CLI verbs — list, get, run from a definition, logs (pane, buffer, full, or followed as SSE), kick, stop — plus an SSE event stream of starts, stops, kicks and observed state changes. The wire contract is the stdlib-only `crux/api`; the server is `crux/serve`.
- Review heads now end in one agreed verdict ([#13542](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13542), part 2). Once every head has answered every perspective, the base reviewer gets one decision kick per PR carrying every head's full report. It checks each head finding against the code, gives it a disposition (confirmed, not reproducible or out of scope) with a reason, sets the final severity of each confirmed finding, records one decided verdict per perspective, and posts the PR's only review comment, tagging findings with the heads that raised them. Routing (`severity.block_at`, backlog filing, fix kicks, human holds) runs on the decided reports; the heads' raw reports never route on their own. When every head approved with no findings, no decision session runs and, with `acknowledge_no_findings` on, the hive posts a single acknowledgement. `review.head_max_retries` is now enforced per head: a head that never answers is named in the decision and the comment instead of stalling the PR, unless no head answered, where `max_redispatch` applies as before. `/api/reviewer/accuracy` adds `review_heads`, scoring each review model's head reports against the decision.
- `agents.<name>.review_heads` lets the review swarm judge every perspective with several models independently ([#13542](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13542), part 1). Each head (`{backend, model, alias, replicas}`) is materialized like `replicas` as `<base>-<alias>-<n>` agents that copy the base reviewer with their own backend and model, are stripped on save and provisioned at boot by the entrypoint; `review.reviewer_agents` naming the base admits them. With `combined_perspectives: false` each perspective is dispatched once per head to that head's least-loaded replica, as a blind, record-only kick (`hive-review --record-verdict`, nothing posted on the PR), and the relay keeps one verdict per perspective per head. A decision step reconciles the heads into one verdict per perspective (see the part 2 entry); `review.head_max_retries` (Settings → Review gate) bounds per-head re-dispatch. Hives without `review_heads` dispatch exactly as before.
- The ACMM L2 pack now includes the `reviewer` agent in COMMENT-only mode (no fixer, no auto-merge) as the review-first entry point; review is part of L2 proper and no L2.5 level was added. L5/L6 reviewer behaviour is unchanged (#13574).
- Triage can now comment once on new RFC/feature issues with the existing settings that may already cover the request, each linked to Settings with the search pre-filled (`issues.rfc_existing_check.enabled`, default off; never labels or closes). Settings also accepts `#config/governor/<tab>/<query>` deep links that open with the search box filled in.
- `runs.triage.clarity_gate` (default off; `enabled`, `threshold` 0-100, default 60; Settings → Features → Incoming issue triage) scores each human-filed, unclaimed issue for goal, acceptance criteria, scope and detail before an agent is kicked on it. An issue under the threshold gets one `<!-- hive:clarity-gate -->` comment with concise questions for its author and the `needs-spec` label (stage/045) instead of a claim, and a park label write that failed is retried on the next kick even across a hive restart; removing `needs-spec` resumes the normal pipeline ([#13577](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13577)).
- The clarity gate (`runs.triage.clarity_gate`) now resumes a parked issue on its own: while the gate is on, a periodic sweep removes the hive's own `needs-spec` once the issue author, or a non-hive commenter with write/maintain/admin, replies after the gate's `<!-- hive:clarity-gate -->` question, and records the un-park so the issue re-derives `stage/010-actionable`; a `needs-spec` a person added is never lifted ([#13588](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13588)).
- Extend the FedRAMP Moderate and ISO 27001 Annex A profiles with more baseline controls (listed `not_covered` where Hive cannot evidence them) and rename the non-NIST `AC-2.ELIG` row to `ELIG-1` ([#13585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13585)).
- Show rolling 30-day issue reopen rates per repository and clarity-gate cohort in Evidence and Prometheus, with captured closure counts and explicit unknown/empty-cohort handling ([#13589](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13589)).
- At ACMM L5, a repo listed under the new per-repo opt-in `auto_merge.queue_on_approve_and_unhold` (off by default) queues an agent PR for auto-merge on green CI once one trusted merger has both approved its current head and removed its level `hold`, using the same path as the dashboard's queue button; nothing else counts as consent, and the L6 self-merge floor, head-SHA re-check, hold guard and Sentinel blocking are unchanged (#13629).
- Automerge can require a PR head to contain the current base before merging: repos listed in `auto_merge.require_current_base` get a green-but-stale head updated and re-tested instead of merged untested against newer base commits.
- Automerge can merge the base forward into a trusted human PR that only conflicts because the base moved: repos listed in `auto_merge.merge_forward_trusted_human` get one App-authored, signed-off merge commit on the PR branch (no human commit rewritten); a real conflict pushes nothing and posts one note naming the files both sides changed ([#13636](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13636))
- Per-repo opt-in `project.repo_policies[].max_open_held_prs` caps how many open PRs the hive App authored may still be waiting on a human in one repo (#13645, part of #13617). Only hive-opened PRs that still carry a hold count; human PRs never do, and a test-only or docs-only PR stops counting once it is auto-released. At the cap `hive-open-pr` refuses new PRs in that repo and PR-opening agents are told "repo at capacity: review or close existing PRs first" in their kick; issue filing, trust levels, the trusted-merger definition and the self-merge floor are unchanged. `0` means the default of 12; unset means no cap.
- **Your-turn critical path on the dashboard** ([#13646](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13646), part of [#13617](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13617)). Every your-turn issue and PR now shows what it waits on, how many other your-turn items it unblocks, and the one action that moves it (merge, release hold, rebase, rerun or approve). An explicit `Depends-on: #N` line in a PR body sets the order and agents now write it when they know the order. An issue waits on the PR that closes it, and a PR whose check is red on its base waits on that check and on the red-main fix. Overlapping PRs get only a soft "may conflict with #N" hint. Rows sort by what they unblock, dependents fold under their blocker as one expandable row ("8 PRs waiting on #255 (dakota-iso)"), the red-main banner says when the fix is waiting on you, and the phone widget's YOUR TURN counts show root causes rather than every waiting item. `/api/status` exposes the new fields per row and per repository (`waits_on`, `unblocks`, `may_conflict_with`, `action`, `repos[].yourTurn`, `yourTurn`).
- Add a reusable offline index for tracked code identifiers, config keys, flags and documentation across registered checkouts, with bounded input, deterministic results and per-repository coverage errors; prior-art gate and issue-filing integration remain follow-up work after #13773 lands.
- The review swarm's outcome now shows on the PR, and its follow-up work is tied to the PR it came from ([#13833](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13833)). The new `review.verdict_labels` block maps the current head's review state to one label each: `reviewing`, `approve`, `changes_requested`, `requires_human` (`reject` counts as `requires_human`). It works independently of the auto-merge engine's stage labels, so a hive with auto-merge off still shows "in progress / approved / changes requested / needs human" on every PR. Like `human_decision_label`, the labels are never created and never block. With `review_heads`, backlog items are now filed only from the decision step's reconciled findings, never from each head's raw report. That had produced near-duplicate items whose wording defeated the fingerprint check and spent the PR's daily cap. The items are also listed in a "Follow-ups filed" section of the decided review itself, on every head, rather than in a once-per-PR summary comment. Every review-backlog item, in every destination including Linear, is now parked on the PR it was filed from with the `blocked` label and the blocked-on marker, not only when the cited file is missing on the base branch. A new sweep lifts the block with a one-line note when the PR merges. When the PR closes unmerged it also lifts the block and comments "source PR #N closed unmerged — re-triage against current base", leaving the item open for normal triage: a closed PR is often superseded by one that lands the same lines, so backlog items are never closed or cancelled automatically.
- The semantic prompt-injection classifier can now run through a subscription CLI backend (`ioscan.CLIChatClient`) instead of an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. The CLI is launched with every tool disabled, in an empty temporary working directory, with an environment stripped of hive tokens, and its reply must contain exactly one valid JSON verdict; `ioscan.SupportsToolless` reports which backends qualify (currently `claude`).
- v5: the semantic prompt-injection classifier can run through the Claude CLI, launched with no tools, no MCP servers, no GitHub token and an empty working directory, on hives without a model endpoint: set `ioscan.classifier.backend: claude` (or pick it in Settings → Security → Input Defense). A CLI backend makes at most `ioscan.classifier.cli_budget_per_eval` calls per scheduler pass (default 8) and `ioscan.classifier.cli_daily_quota` calls per UTC day (default 500); backends that cannot run without tools (copilot, codex, gemini) are refused at boot. Port of [#14060](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14060) and [#14070](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14070) from v6 ([#14059](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14059), part of [#14037](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14037)).
- The semantic prompt-injection classifier can run through the Claude CLI, launched with no tools, on hives without a model endpoint: set `ioscan.classifier.backend: claude` (or pick it in Settings → Security → Input Defense). A CLI backend makes at most `ioscan.classifier.cli_budget_per_eval` calls per scheduler pass (default 8) and `ioscan.classifier.cli_daily_quota` calls per UTC day (default 500); backends that cannot run without tools (copilot, codex, gemini) are refused at boot.
- **`omnigent` contributor backend (T3 experimental).** Registered the Omnigent meta-harness CLI ([omnigent-ai/omnigent](https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent), Apache-2.0) across `KNOWN_BACKENDS`, `CLIBackends`, local confinement matrix tests, and contributor preflights. Omnigent orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agent harnesses; on the local CLI path it exposes no OS-level sandbox wired by Hive and requires explicit opt-in via `HIVE_OMNIGENT_DANGEROUSLY_RUN_UNCONFINED=1`. Every launch is `omnigent run --server local [--model <id>]` (`run` opens the agent REPL; `--server local` pins a local Omnigent server, so remote-server mode is unsupported), and container mode stages only `auth_tokens.json` and `config.yaml` from `~/.omnigent`, never session history. Omnigent's internal policy engine and sandboxing compose additively, while Hive's proxy remains strictly authoritative for all GitHub writes and push operations.
- The GitHub forge adapter implements `forge.Merger` and passes the shared merge contract (#14107): the hold gate refuses with `ErrHoldActive` and a head that is not the pinned commit with `ErrConflict`, both before the merge call; an already-merged change reports `ErrAlreadyMerged`, GitHub's 405/422 map to `ErrNotMergeable`, and `MergeOptions.DeleteBranch` removes the merged head branch. The merge delegates to `pkg/github.MergePR`, so it keeps the mutation boundary, forward-merge guard and merge audit.
- forge(gitlab): implement `Forge.Merge` for GitLab with strategy mapping, head-SHA guard, hold label enforcement, and 405/406/409 error mapping, verified by shared contract tests.
- Gitea and Forgejo merge implementation on the forge adapter (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/merge`), with merge style mapping, head commit guard, and shared merge contract test coverage ([#14110](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14110)).
- `project.repo_policies[].forge` and `forge_url` put one repo on GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo while the rest of the project stays on `project.forge` ([#14112](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14112), part of [#14096](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14096)). Both keys are validated at load. The governor's escalation writes go to each repo's own forge, and a repo-scoped kick carries the forge kind and names a non-GitHub forge in its text. Unset keys behave exactly as before.
- A merge requested through the hive-merge relay for a repo on GitLab or Gitea/Forgejo (`project.repo_policies[].forge`) now lands through that forge's merge API, after the same merge-eligible check pinned to the reviewed head. GitHub repos merge exactly as before. Authorship detection also recognises GitLab access-token bots and Gitea/Forgejo Actions as bots ([#14113](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14113), part of [#14096](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14096)).
- Projects cards on the dashboard now name their forge: each repo in `/api/status` carries `forge` (`github`, `gitlab` or `gitea`) and, for GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo, `forgeUrl`, so a hive with `project.forge: gitlab` or `gitea` shows its own host (for example `🦊 GitLab · gitlab.example.com`) and links to it instead of claiming github.com. A repo moved to another forge by `project.repo_policies[].forge` gets its own card label and links ([#14115](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14115)). The new [Forges](src/docs/integrations/forges.md) page documents what the GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo adapters support today.
- Nightly Forgejo smoke workflow (`.github/workflows/forgejo-smoke.yml`) that starts a digest-pinned Forgejo container, seeds a repo, issue and pull request, and runs the minimal governor loop (read issue → kick → merge via `forge.Merger`) against it; also runs on pushes and PRs touching `src/pkg/forge/**` or `src/pkg/apiproxy/**` ([#14116](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14116)).
- The Crux module ships its own `crux` binary, `src/crux/cmd/crux`, buildable from the nested module alone (`cd src/crux && make build`, or `GOWORK=off go build ./cmd/crux`) with the same `run`, `ps`, `logs`, `kick`, `stop` and `serve` verbs, `--server` / `CRUX_SERVER` remote mode and a `--version` flag. It loads agent definitions from plain YAML files with the new `crux/defs` package (`--defs <dir|file>` / `CRUX_DEFS`: portable `kind: AgentDefinition` documents or bare per-agent overlays); the root `cmd/crux` stays as a thin host that reads `hive.yaml`. `src/crux/Makefile` adds `build`, `test`, `vet` and `smoke` (starts `crux serve` on a private socket and drives it over the API), which CI runs; `src/crux/README.md` documents the module ([#14138](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14138)).
- `src/crux` is now published to `hivecommons/crux` as module `github.com/hivecommons/crux`: `.github/workflows/crux-sync.yml` runs `src/scripts/crux-publish.sh` on every v5 push touching `src/crux/**`, rewrites the module path, refuses to publish a tree that does not build with `GOWORK=off`, commits fast-forward on `hivecommons/crux` `main`, and turns a hive tag `crux/vX.Y.Z` into tag `vX.Y.Z` there so releases are cut from hive (#14138).
- **Dashboard activity monitor: blocked rows show their age in the since column too.** A blocked issue without `stage_since` now falls back to `created_at` there, matching the Open chevron (#14316).
- Hive Chat `/prs` now lists the actual open pull requests instead of a per-repo count: one row per PR under each repo (`owner/repo#N — title (@author · stage labels · age · ✅/❌/⏳ CI · approved/changes requested · needs decision · hold · mergeable)`), read from the status snapshot's cached PR rows — no extra GitHub call — and capped at 25 with an "… and N more" footer. The command remainder is now honoured as filters: `waiting on review`, `needs decision`, `hold`, `failing ci`, `mine` / `by <login>`, `repo <owner/repo>`, `stale` / `older than Nd`; unrecognised words are reported and the hint lists the filters. `/prs waiting on review` used to answer only "hivecommons/hive: 12 open PR(s)" (hivecommons/hive#14408).
- The ioscan semantic classifier can now run through Copilot CLI tool-less (`ioscan.classifier.backend: copilot`), alongside `claude`: copilot is launched with `--available-tools` set to a sentinel that names no tool, `--disable-builtin-mcps`, `--no-custom-instructions` and `--no-ask-user`, in an empty working directory with no hive token in its environment, and the prompt is passed as the `-p` value since copilot does not read stdin. When `classifier.backend` is empty and no model endpoint is configured, boot now falls back to the tool-less CLI the hive's own agents run on, so a Copilot-only hive at ACMM L5–L6 gets a classifier without extra configuration instead of silently withholding every kick that carries untrusted text. When the classifier is required at the current level but still cannot run, the dashboard shows a persistent `ioscan-classifier-blocked` alert saying kicks are being blocked and how to fix it (set an endpoint, set `ioscan.classifier.backend`, or `ioscan.classifier.fail_mode: open`); the fail-closed default is unchanged. `codex` and `gemini` remain refused (hivecommons/hive#14499).
- Retro lessons derived from human review feedback are now stored as drafts tagged `review-feedback` in the hive's local knowledge store, hidden from agents until the owner approves them; repeats of an approved or draft lesson are counted without changing its state (#14551).
- Owners can now find retro lessons learned from human review that are waiting for approval: the dashboard Knowledge section shows "N lessons awaiting approval", and `hivectl knowledge list --state draft --tag review-feedback` lists them. `GET /api/knowledge` gains `state` and `tag` filters, and asking for unapproved states without the owner role is refused.
- Repeat-failure check: with `repeat_failure.enabled` on, fresh-bash backends (claude, codex, goose, pi, gemini, bob, opencode, kilo and the inference backends) launch with a Hive-owned `BASH_ENV` script that records each agent command and its exit status once, chaining any existing `BASH_ENV`, and with `SHELL=/bin/bash` (bob moves from dash to bash while the check is on). Turning the check off removes the script at the next launch (#14554).
- Repeat-failure check: with `repeat_failure.enabled` on, each agent's dashboard row shows the check state (on, "not available for this backend", or "not receiving data" after `no_data_after_s` of shell activity without command records) and a "Repeating failure: `<command>` failed N times in M min (exit S)" note when a command keeps failing the same way; nothing is shown while the check is off and the agent is never paused. A code coverage table, mirrored in the backend support docs and checked in CI, lists every backend; none is marked covered yet, pending real-run evidence (#14559) (#14558).
- Every kick now opens with a **house style** section, identical across agents and backends: a managed repo's root `HIVE_STYLE.md` overrides the hive-wide `project.style` / `project.style_file`, which overrides the built-in text. Candidates are capped at `project.style_max_bytes` (4096); the repo file is untrusted and refused whole on an ioscan block with a `house_style_skip` audit line. Agent card and detail pane show a **style** field naming the source; `/api/status` exposes `agents[].styleSource` (#14582)
- The GitHub client can now return trusted human review feedback (including resolved and outdated review threads) and a rework summary for a reworked hive PR, as an injectable source for the retro lane; the live review follow-up path is unchanged.
- **Weekly competitor and SWOT report to Discord `#related-research`.** A new GitHub Agentic Workflow, `.github/workflows/weekly-competitor-report.md` (compiled to `.lock.yml` with the pinned gh-aw `v0.89.21`, Copilot engine, `copilot-requests: write`), runs every Monday at 13:00 UTC and on manual dispatch. It researches projects adjacent to Hive (OpenHands, SWE-agent, Devin, Copilot coding agent, Codex, Claude Code, Sweep, Factory, Jules, Gastown, Dagger, Kilo, Cline/Roo, Mentat, Aider, GPT-Engineer, Potpie, Agentless, public fleet-orchestrator write-ups) with read-only GitHub tools and proxy-aware `curl` inside a network allowlist, then writes a 600-900 word plain-language report with "What changed this week", a "Who does what" table, a cited SWOT for Hive, and "One thing to watch". The report is appended as a comment to tracking issue [#14613](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14613) and posted to Discord in 2000-character chunks through a custom safe-output job that reads the `DISCORD_RELATED_RESEARCH_WEBHOOK` repository secret. The workflow commits nothing and has no repository write permission ([#14612](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14612)).
- **Docs: Hive trust levels vs GitHub Copilot assisted permissions.** New page `src/docs/copilot-permissions-comparison.md` explains Copilot's assisted permissions (GA 2026-10-26, from GitHub's changelog and docs) next to Hive's ACMM levels, lanes, policy proxy with measured refusal counts from the hosted hives, review gates, hold flow and record-only shadow gates, with a dimension table and what each does that the other does not. Linked from the docs index and documentation map (#14613).
- RFC lifecycle notices to Discord: with `notifications.discord.rfc_channel_id` set (env `HIVE_DISCORD_RFC_CHANNEL_ID`; default empty, off) and a bot token, the hive posts one line to that channel when an RFC issue in a managed repo is opened (`RFC opened: #N <title> - <url> (by @author)`), closed (`RFC closed (completed|not planned): ...`), or taken off hold so it can be implemented (`RFC ready to implement (hold removed): ...`, on `hold` coming off an open RFC or a held RFC reaching `stage/010-actionable`, once per hold episode). An RFC is an issue with the `rfc` label or an `RFC`-prefixed title. The detector (`pkg/rfcnotify`) polls issues updated since its last pass and keeps per-issue records in `/data/rfc-notify.json`, so restarts never re-post and the first pass only records the baseline. Operators see each post in the audit log as `rfc-notify` (#14616).
- `review.delta_rereview` (default on), `review.delta_trivial_lines` (default 20) and `review.delta_max_age` (default 72h): a PR already judged at an earlier head is re-reviewed by its diff since that head, with the previous verdict and findings in the kick; an empty or trivial delta in files the previous verdict passed re-stamps that verdict onto the new head without a model call. Aggregates record `delta.previous_head` / `delta.trivial` so the cost dashboard can split delta reviews from full ones ([#14621](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14621)).
- `review.bot_author_model` (default empty = off), `review.bot_authors` (default `dependabot[bot]`, `renovate[bot]`, `github-actions[bot]`, `*[bot]`; the hive's own App never matches) and `review.bot_author_full_review_paths` (default `.github/workflows/**`, `Dockerfile*`): reviews of PRs opened by other bots run on a configured cheaper model unless the PR touches a full-review path or its files could not be listed ([#14625](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14625)).
- New `pkg/search` core for portfolio search (#14634, part of #14491): a `Backend` interface (`Index`, `Delete`, `Query` with hits and facets, `Stats`) and a dependency-free embedded inverted-index backend modelled on `pkg/codeindex`. Every document carries `repo`, `kind`, `at`, `url` and `visibility`; queries return ranked hits with highlight spans and facet counts by `kind`, `repo` and any keyword field. Per-repo snapshots are immutable, persisted to `/data/search/<owner>/<repo>.idx` via temp file and atomic rename, capped at 32 MiB per repo (exceeding it is a per-repo coverage error that keeps the previous snapshot), and held in memory under a 256 MiB budget with least-recently-queried eviction. Corrupt index files are ignored and rebuilt on the next update. Nothing uses the package yet, so operators see no change; ingest, APIs and the `search.*` settings land in follow-up issues.
- Opt-in portfolio search indexer (`search.enabled`, default off): every 30 minutes it incrementally indexes review evidence bundles, verdict findings, sentinel hits, complexity snapshots, beads and knowledge facts into `/data/search`, scrubbing secrets first, with `search.max_index_bytes_per_repo`, `search.max_memory_bytes` and `search.retention` (months, default 24).
- `GET /api/search` on the spoke ([#14637](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14637), part of [#14491](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14491)): owners and maintainers can search the local portfolio index by text, `kind`, `repo` and date range, and get highlighted hits plus facets by kind, repo, verdict and sentinel rule. It answers `404` unless `search.enabled` is set, rejects the reserved `semantic=true`, withholds injected text behind visible ioscan redaction markers, and audits each query string with actor and role but never the results.
- Report-only per-repo health score on spokes with `search.enabled`: each search index rebuild scores CI pass rate (90d), median time-to-merge, revert/follow-up rate and review verdict mix from local review evidence, and `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/health` returns the 0–100 weighted score with every component's inputs and `n` so it can be disputed. Components with fewer than 10 samples or no local data are `not_reported`, never zero; the stale-issue ratio, sign-off rate, dependency freshness and security-doc rot components are always `not_reported` in this release because no local signal source feeds them yet (`search.health.stale_after` and `security_doc_max_age` are accepted but have no effect until one is wired). Weights are tunable under `search.health.weights`. The score is never an ACMM input and is not read by merge decisions or Governor priority ([#14638](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14638)).
- **Prior-art gate searches past reviews (#14639).** With `search.enabled: true`, the Governor prior-art gate adds a lexical `search` source over the portfolio search index, so past review verdicts, findings, sentinel hits and beads that already cover an issue are ranked alongside merged PRs, closed issues, docs and code. Gate thresholds and parking are unchanged, re-surfaced text passes through ioscan, and an index error or timeout only drops that source's candidates. With search disabled the gate behaves exactly as before.
- `hivectl search <query>` and `hivectl repo health <owner/repo>` ([#14641](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14641), part of [#14491](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14491)): operator commands over the spoke's `GET /api/search` and `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/health`. `search` takes `--kind`, `--repo`, `--from`, `--to` and `--limit`, prints kind, repo, date, title and link per hit (or the full response with `-o json`) and warns about repos whose index is unreadable; `repo health` prints the report-only score with each component's weight, n and contribution. When the hive runs with `search.enabled` off, both say so plainly instead of returning a bare 404/503. New `docs/search.md` documents `search.enabled` and every `search.*` config key.
- `python3 src/scripts/check-docs-citations.py --fix` now repairs drifted `src/docs` line-range citations into `.go` files instead of only delegating to the `api-reference.md` route fixer: it resolves the first backticked symbol anchor on the citing line to a single top-level Go declaration (`func X(`, `func (recv) X(`, `type X`, `const X`, `var X`) and rewrites the range to start at that declaration and end at the first line that covers every anchor. It fails closed — zero or several matching declarations, an anchor outside the declaration, a non-`.go` target, or a line without anchors leaves the citation untouched and still reported as `DRIFT` with a non-zero exit — and a second `--fix` run is a no-op. This ends the hand-typed docs PRs for moved functions (#14713).
- **The repeated-failure check now sees commands run by copilot, omp and headless agy agents** ([#14746](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14746), [#14747](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14747), [#14750](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14750), part of [#14550](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14550)). These backends run shell commands where the neutral `BASH_ENV` route never reaches them, so an agent retrying the same failing command went unnoticed. With `repeat_failure.enabled` on, Hive now reads Copilot's `events.jsonl` session log (one record per shell `tool.execution_complete`, with the real exit code), loads a Hive-owned omp extension via its own `--extension` flag (one record per bash `tool_result`, fail-open), and has `hive agy-turn` record each finished `run_command` step. Nothing is written into the backends' own settings; with the check off Hive passes no flag and removes the omp extension at the next launch. copilot and omp are marked covered in the "Repeated-failure check" table of `docs/backend-support-tiers.md` with committed, re-runnable harness evidence; agy stays "not covered" there until a real-run harness can log in.
- The repeated-failure check now has a record route for `aider` agents ([#14752](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14752)): aider runs each command in an interactive `$SHELL -i -c`, which ignores `BASH_ENV`, so while `repeat_failure.enabled` is on Hive replaces the agent's `~/.bashrc` link (Hive-managed per-agent homes only, never contributor local mode) with a per-agent file that sources the shared rc file plus a guarded line loading the route script, and exports `SHELL=/bin/bash`; turning the check off restores the link at the next launch. The coverage table now records why `openhands` ([#14748](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14748)) and `muse` ([#14749](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14749)) stay not covered: Hive has no launch or hook wiring for either and writes none of their settings files.
- `GET /api/launch-cost/history` returns a persisted daily per-ref rollup (`share_usd`, `launches` per UTC day) of launch attribution, so cost per merged PR can be measured over 14+ days instead of the ~1-day `/api/launch-cost` window ([#14762](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14762)).
- crux: detect Copilot assisted-approval denials as a blocked/approval_denied state with the judge's feedback (#14796)
- The dashboard's **▶ terminal** now works for agents with `sandbox.runtime: job` ([#14798](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14798)). Those kicks run as a Kubernetes Job in another pod, so there was no tmux session to attach and the pane waited forever. For a job-runtime agent the link now opens a read-only viewer at `/terminal/job/<agent>` that streams the newest Job pod's log through the launcher's existing in-cluster client and `pods/log` RBAC: it follows the pod while the kick runs (waiting while it is `Pending`), prints the container exit code when it ends, and between kicks shows the last run's persisted sandbox transcript — which now ends with an `exit code: N` line — or a clear "no sandbox run yet" state. Podman-sandboxed and tmux agents are unchanged.
- A sandboxed reviewer can now post reviews ([#14986](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14986)). Every sandbox kick (Podman or `sandbox.runtime: job`) gets a review spool at `.hive/review-requests` in its workspace, and `hive-review` inside the sandbox writes there via `HIVE_REVIEW_REQUEST_DIR`. The review relay picks spooled requests up through the same policy path as the pod-local drop box, attributing each one to the kick's agent from a hive-owned manifest under `<work_dir>/sandbox-review-spools`, never from the file's contents. Because the spool is group-writable, each kick also gets its own random spool key (`HIVE_REVIEW_SPOOL_KEY`, passed only through the sandbox environment), and the relay accepts only requests that carry a valid HMAC under that key and haven't been accepted before, so another agent can't post a review as the sandboxed reviewer by dropping a file into its spool. A reviewer on an accelerator spoke can now run the change on the card node and post its verdict from there.
- A contributor blocked verdict that names its blocker (`owner/repo#N`, `#N`, or an issue/PR URL) now records it on the task issue — a native GitHub "blocked by" link for an open issue, a `hive:blocked-on` marker for an open PR — so the hive lifts `blocked` itself once the blocker closes.
- Activity Monitor: the waiting-on pill carries a presence indicator for the person the hive waits on ([#15051](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15051)) — a filled dot when their clanker is online (the hive waits), a filled square when it is offline (adoption is next; the tooltip says when: "@hanthor's clanker: offline 26h — hive will adopt at 15:10 (in 38m)"), a hollow ring when no clanker is registered ("waiting for a human reply"). Every PR row waiting on a named person (071 / 072 / 017) now carries `presence{login, state, kind, since, last_seen, next, adopt_at}` from the same hub lookup and clock adoption uses; the Needs-human popover and per-PR sub-rows show the same indicator. Shape, not colour alone, carries the state; nothing moves under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Review heads (`agents.<name>.review_heads`) now work with `review.combined_perspectives: true`: each head reviews every perspective in one record-only kick per PR head instead of one kick per perspective. A combined-mode reviewer set mixing lanes with and without heads still loads, with a boot warning that the plain lanes receive no combined perspectives.
- The hub's per-hive dropdown menu now has a **⏸ Pause hive** / **▶ Resume hive** item for the hive's owner (or a hub admin) ([#15092](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15092)). It drives the same fleet breaker as the spoke's own top-bar ⏸ button: `POST /api/saas/hives/{id}/breaker` queues the request and the spoke applies it on its next heartbeat, so a spoke can be paused without opening its dashboard.
- Activity Monitor: **Accept triage** now heads the "⋯" row menu of every issue waiting on a maintainer's triage — stage 015, the `needs-triage` pill, and the label-less 000-new row the reporter-trust gate holds before the first stage pass (previously only Hold / Re-evaluate / Mark needs-human were offered there). The hint reads *"adds `triage/accepted` as @you; the hive takes it on its next pass (≈N min)"*, the result toast carries the governor's next scanner pass, and the row reads accepted at once (015 → 010 actionable; a 000-new row flips to *triage ✓ → actionable (next)*), which the server narrates the same way once the label is on. Same audited, permission-gated write path as before ([#15215](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15215)).
- Hive PRs that touch `src/crux/**` now run crux's Go file-size ratchet (the `crux-file-size-ratchet` check), using the script and baseline fetched from crux `main` at run time. A PR that grows a grandfathered `src/crux` file past its baseline now fails in hive with crux's own `::error::` annotation instead of breaking crux `main` on the next sync. (#15331)
- An opt-in Kustomize component `src/deploy/kustomize/components/monitoring/` adds a Prometheus Operator `ServiceMonitor` targeting `/metrics` and patches the Deployment for `HIVE_METRICS_ENABLED` and `HIVE_METRICS_TOKEN` ([#15437](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15437)).
- The opt-in `monitoring` Kustomize component now ships a `PrometheusRule` with `HiveMetricsDown`, `HiveCostBurnHigh` (operator-patchable threshold) and `HiveStageTransitionAnomalies` alerts, each with a summary, description and runbook link, validated in CI with `promtool check rules` and unit tests ([#15438](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15438)).
- The opt-in `monitoring` Kustomize component now ships a Grafana dashboard (`hive-grafana-dashboard` ConfigMap labelled `grafana_dashboard: "1"`) covering estimated cost, tokens, PRs, reviews, rework, PR follow-ups and stage-engine anomalies, with the Prometheus data source as a variable ([#15439](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15439)).
- The dashboard's RUNNING tile now rotates its fleet spend through `$X this hour` → `$Y today` → `$Z this week` → `$W this month` (~4 s each, a quiet vertical crossfade of just the amount and window, agent count fixed, width reserved so the tile never wraps; pauses on hover and while the tab is hidden, instant under reduced motion, hover lists all four), and `/api/status.fleetRun` gains `dayUSD`, `weekUSD`, `monthUSD`, `windowsPriced` summed from the cost ledger over the UTC day, ISO week and calendar month (#15614).
- The activity monitor shows push progress on every PR row in the CI / Review column ([#15784](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15784)): the stage record keeps `waiting_push_since` / `last_push_at` / `last_push_sha`, booked from the `pull_request` synchronize / `push` webhook re-read with the enumerate head change as fallback. A 071 / 072 pill ends with the wait's age ("waiting on 👤 @user to push · 38m", muted-amber past `dashboard.stage_tracker.waiting_push_stale_h`, default 4); once a push lands the chevron returns to the column's own word (the 👤 clears — the ball is back with the hive) and the gray pill names the push ("@user pushed abc1234 · 2m" linking to the commit, "adopted from @x's #N · pushed 2m ago" on adopted rows, "pushed abc1234 · 2m" on plain CI / Review rows) while CI / the re-review for that head still run; the hive line reads "push seen 2m ago → CI/re-review queued".
- The dashboard's upgrade animation now plays for every pod roll, not only self-upgrades ([#15788](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15788)): the hub announces hub-managed rolls through the heartbeat (`upgrade_announce`), operators can announce theirs with `POST /api/upgrade/announce` (owner-only; one-liner in `dashboard-standalone-upgrades.md`), and a SIGTERM with no announce still publishes an SSE `upgrading` event with `phase: restarting` before the stream drops. The banner survives the reconnect, shows the new pod's boot phase from `/api/version.startupPhase`, and reads **Upgraded to `<sha>` ✓** or **Restarted ✓** by comparing build hash and process `startedAt`. Preview it any time with `?demo=upgrade` or Settings → Diagnostics → *Preview upgrade animation*.
- Stage tracker: the "pushed" pill on a CI / Review row now drops once the PR head moves past the pushed commit (hivecommons/hive#15797).
- The activity monitor's stage tracker names, on the PR sub-row drawn under an issue, the other listed open issues that PR also closes ([#15806](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15806)): a gray "also closes #15503" pill beside the PR link (comma-separated, three numbers then "+N", every number linking to its issue; the hover names each issue's title) — the reciprocal of the "↳ #N · under #M" chip the other issues already show. The issue's `linked_prs[]` entry drawn here (`drawn_under` == the issue) gains `also_closes` (number, title, url).
- The Activity Monitor's ⚙ settings gain a "Toasts & timing" section: info and error toast durations (`dashboard.stage_tracker.toast_info_s` / `toast_error_s`, 3–120 s, saved per hive through `PUT /api/config/dashboard` and served in the `/api/stage-tracker` payload, with a localStorage fallback only when the write is refused) and the contributor lane's pre-merge soak (`auto_merge.contributor_lane.soak_minutes`), live without a restart ([#15813](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15813)).
- The Hive activity monitor can now be popped out into its own browser window (⧉ on the card header, `?popout=1`, same sign-in, tracker-only layout for a second monitor, ⤶ Return to dashboard) or taken full screen (⛶ / the `f` key, Esc exits) ([#15829](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15829)).
- Add experimental, opt-in Matrix Rain and Cascade displays at `?kiosk=1&view=matrix`, with pause, reduced-motion paging, source and freshness labels, and authorized line fetching; the normal tracker is unchanged (#15936, RFC #15862).
- Serve Matrix lines via authorized `GET /api/matrix/lines` and a content-free `code-lines` SSE nudge on `/api/events` (experimental, default off; [#15935](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15935)).
- `ioscan.classifier.backend` now accepts `omp`, running the prompt-injection classifier through a tool-less omp CLI that authenticates via the omp auth broker.
- RFC notices in rich mode (`rfc_format: card` or `rfc_threads: true`) now announce open-decision count changes (at most one per RFC per 30 minutes), target and status changes, and an added `stage/045-needs-decision` or `needs-human` label into the RFC's thread. A retitle edits the card and renames the thread instead of posting. A same-author RFC with the same title within an hour gets no card, only one note in the first RFC's thread. Line mode is unchanged.
- Spokes can attach a bounded, read-only activity digest to their hub heartbeat, and the hub serves it per user and per hive on `GET /api/hub/activity` with ETag polling: 100 items by default under a hard 250-item server-side ceiling, private-repository items excluded unless the spoke opts in (always counted in totals), truncation and stale, not-reporting or missing hives disclosed, and digests kept in hub memory only. Nothing populates the digest yet and no rollout or participation setting changes ([#15951](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15951), RFC [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)).
- Spokes now publish the bounded activity digest to the hub: each heartbeat carries it, built in process from the stage tracker, with up to `hub.activity.max_items` items (default 100, hub ceiling 250). When the cap applies, the most urgent items are kept and `truncated` reports how many were left out. Private-repository items are left out unless `hub.activity.share_private` is set, but totals still count them. Once the hub acknowledges an etag, later beats send only that etag. A tracker change sends an activity-only update on the heartbeat endpoint at most once every 15 seconds, and changes that arrive meanwhile are merged into it. `hub.activity.enabled` defaults on for hosted spokes and stays opt-in for self-hosted ones ([#15963](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15963), RFC [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)).
- The heartbeat `activity` block now carries the stage hops, opens and merges a spoke saw since the hub last acknowledged them (at most 200, oldest dropped first, drops disclosed as `events_dropped`), and `GET /api/hub/activity` serves them as `events` from a fleet-wide, memory-only ring of the last 1,000 events, filtered per user and per hive like items, so the hub board can animate movement and show merge toasts ([#15964](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15964), RFC [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)).
- The streamer can now run a second, independent broadcast for the hub-wide monitor on `twitch.tv/hivecommonsfleet` ([#15966](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15966), part of [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)): `src/deploy/stream/fleet/` is its own namespace, Deployment, stream-key Secret name and NetworkPolicy, ships disabled (`replicas: 0`, `STREAM_ENABLED: "false"`), and its `STREAM_PROFILE=public-safe` refuses to start the encoder without the owner's enable, the public-safe policy acknowledgement, a real public source and an installed key. It renders the hub anonymously — the auth proxy accepts no token and strips cookies — because Twitch output is public whatever the dashboard's authentication. The existing `twitch.tv/hivecommons` stream config is unchanged and pinned by a test; no broadcast is activated.
- The hub serves an anonymous **public-safe Fleet activity view** at `/activity/public`, backed by `GET /api/hub/activity/public` ([#15966](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15966), part of [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)). It is the source of the `twitch.tv/hivecommonsfleet` broadcast, and `src/deploy/stream/fleet` now points `DASHBOARD_PATH` at it. The view shows only public-repository items and events from hives the registry lists as public on github.com. It leaves out private or unknown-visibility rows, totals and drop counts that can include private items, hive owners and every per-user grant. It never reads a session or token, so a signed-in viewer's own Fleet access cannot leak onto a public stream. The signed-in `/activity` page is unchanged, and no broadcast is activated.
- Add the Ghost coder (`mx.effect=ghost`) and Terminal (`mx.effect=terminal`) effects to the opt-in Matrix display, plus an `mx.captions=off` toggle; both render only lines already served by `/api/matrix/lines` (#16041, RFC #15862).
- Add a Matrix tab to the Activity Monitor header, shown only when `dashboard.matrix.enabled` is set; the status payload gains an additive `matrixEnabled` boolean (#16042, RFC #15862).
- The hub has a read-only **Fleet activity** page at `/activity`, linked as **📡 Fleet activity** next to **🔬 Evidence**. It shows the open issues and PRs of the hives you can see, from `GET /api/hub/activity`, which scopes every hive to you server-side. It polls every 15 s with `If-None-Match` and redraws only when the ETag changes. A **Hive** column carries a colour chip that opens the hive's own tracker; rows link to GitHub, titles render as text, and there are no action menus. Group-by-hive draws a header per hive with its item count and freshness (`stale` after two missed heartbeats, "upgrade to report activity" for hives that send no activity, missing hives). A list above the board always names truncated items, dropped events and stale or missing hives. Rows use the shared tracker row asset, and the page is served with its own Content-Security-Policy (no inline scripts, handlers or styles). Display mode follows separately ([#16063](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16063), part of [#15965](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15965), RFC [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)).
- The hub **Fleet activity** page (`/activity`) takes the spoke Activity Monitor's display parameters, read by the spoke's own code: `?kiosk=1` hides the chrome and cursor for an unattended screen, `?display=1` gives an attended chrome-less wall view that **Esc** or **d** leaves, `am.*` describes the board's view with the spoke's keys (kind, repo, q, author, sort, dir and `am.group=none`), and in display mode `am.view` + `interval` rotate `hub-activity` views with the spoke's wall-clock dwell. `am.*` keys the activity digest has no data for stay in the URL and are named on the board as not applied. A copy of the spoke's URL-view and playlist helpers is served byte-identical from `/activity/assets/` (`pkg/webassets/trackerview`), and a compatibility test fails if it drifts. The spoke tracker's display mode is unchanged ([#16064](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16064), part of [#15965](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15965), RFC [#15861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15861)).
- Every `?kiosk=1` view — the spoke Activity Monitor, the Matrix view and the hub's public Fleet activity page, i.e. the three Twitch streams — shows a small "Request a Hive" call-to-action pill bottom-right with `hive.hivecommons.dev/get-started` and a QR code of it ([#16236](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16236)). It never appears in the operator dashboard, `&cta=off` removes it, and the text is `dashboard.kiosk_cta_url` / `dashboard.kiosk_cta_text` on a spoke or `HIVE_HUB_KIOSK_CTA_URL` / `HIVE_HUB_KIOSK_CTA_TEXT` on the hub. `src/scripts/twitch-channel-cta.sh` sets the matching title, category and tags on the channels (`--dry-run`, idempotent, per-channel `channel:manage:broadcast` token).
- The *Let hive decide* dialog, the tracker payload (`sentinel_details`), `/api/sentinel` (`findings`) and the hive's "reviewed, intended" decision comment now name the files and the sentinel rule that fired — bounded to 10 paths per finding with a "+N more" count — instead of only "changes N sensitive path(s)" ([#16237](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16237)).
- The Hive activity monitor's header now carries its own live item count pill next to the title — the sidebar badge's twin, written by the same render call with the same ↑ +N / ↓ −N cue and `prefers-reduced-motion` handling — so kiosk (`?kiosk=1`), pop-out (`?popout=1`), display mode (`?display=1`) and browser full screen, which all hide the sidebar, still show how many items the monitor is tracking. The pill is enlarged in the chrome-less views so it reads at 1920×1080 ([#16243](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16243)).
- Added `github.notifications.shadow` (default off): would-notify instrumentation that classifies every notification-capable GitHub write by producer and class, counts repeats it would suppress, exports the counters on `/metrics`, and documents the write-site inventory — measurement only, no write changes (#16264).
- Per-recipient attention budget (`github.attention.recipient_budget`, `0` = off) with shadow would-overflow counting and an opt-in, edited-in-place digest (`github.attention.digest_recipients`); security, required-review, protocol-command and hold notices are never budgeted ([#16271](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16271)).
- Neutralise incidental `@user` mentions in copied text inside hive-authored status comments, so copying a title or quote no longer re-notifies the person named.
- With `github.notifications.attention_pilot` on, each item's `hive:status` card gains an **Attention** section (who owes what, since when, snoozed until), each repository gets one `Hive attention queue` tracking issue that is created once and then edited in place, and unresolved attention episodes get at most one reminder per `github.attention.reminder_interval` (default 24h), skipped while acknowledged or snoozed and after the recipient comments, reviews or changes a label; closing an item resolves its episodes and clears it from both.
- Add an opt-in code activity reader at `?kiosk=1&view=reader`. It shows pushed changes from `/api/matrix/lines` as readable, wrapping paragraph cards with green `+` additions and red `−` removals, with the repository, PR link, file, stage and observed time. It supports pause with P, Space or the button, pauses while you scroll, uses a static layout for reduced motion and stops in hidden tabs. The Matrix view is unchanged (#16475).
- Feed the Code activity reader whole pushed PR diff regions, including removals, through the existing authorized sentinel observer, with whole-region secret filtering, bounded memory-only history, policy reset, visible freshness, buffered-snapshot labels and explicit replay; stop restoring or writing the legacy Matrix code-history file.
- `/api/matrix/lines` now returns `more`, true only while another line the caller may see remains past the page, so clients paging a filtered backlog can stop without an empty follow-up request ([#16530](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16530)).
- The hive re-authors its own fixer-exhausted PRs by itself instead of parking them for a person ([#16582](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16582)): the exhausted hive PR is closed as superseded with a note, the issue is labelled `hive/re-authored` and requeued so the next kick opens a fresh PR from the current base (the kick asks for `Supersedes #<old>`). One automatic re-author per issue; a second exhaustion parks at 085 with Give direction / Hand it to a person / Close as not planned. The Activity Monitor words the issue `Re-authoring · superseding #N` (remediation evidence `kick`) and the fresh PR's chip `re-authored from #N`. `decide:re-author` is gone from the decision vocabulary: a person's rewrite of a contributor PR (unsigned DCO, exhausted) is `decide:adopt` — "Adopt as hive PR"; historical `re-author` ledger entries still read.
- Activity Monitor chevrons follow the canonical spec ([#16599](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16599)): a row always has 1–2 **active** chevrons (amber fill + counted caption) — the item's stage column, plus a CI/Review track only while it genuinely runs on the current head; every other chevron is an **icon only** (neutral not-yet-run, red failed/changes requested, green passed/approved) with its counts and the backend sentence in the tooltip. CI and Review icons are a tiny ring segmented into `checks_total` / `perspectives_total` steps that fills clockwise (pass green, fail red, newest step pulsing while running). When nothing moves the blocker column is filled in a still stalled style, e.g. `CI 1/11 · waiting on workflow approval` for heads whose workflow runs are `action_required` on GitHub (new `PRCIActivity.WorkflowApproval`, blocker `workflow-approval-required:N`). Review-pending rows never read `Review unknown` / a default `5/5`: with no verdict bundle on the head they are `Review N/5 · in progress` (N = verdicts actually posted) or `· adjudicating`.
- Expose conflict-aware merge train, rebase-attempt and stall-warning controls under Settings → Auto-merge → Merge train, including disabling stall warnings with zero seconds ([#16677](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16677)).
