- Publish standby pause reasons and per-lane queue depths on dashboard and terminal governor surfaces. (#8053)
- Hive now accepts and validates the standby-contributor configuration surface from [RFC #7629](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7629) — a per-lane `standby:` block (`enabled`, `min_model_capability`, `daily_cap_per_contributor`) plus the hive-wide `hub.standby_contributors` approved list, `hub.standby_model_tiers` mapping and `hub.standby_allow_private_repos` opt-in ([#8054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8054)). Nothing reads the block yet: it is the configuration half of a feature whose pause signal, relay mode, matching and dispatch land in later phases, so a hive that writes no `standby:` block is unaffected. What it does do is fail the load on the misconfigurations that would otherwise be silent — a lane switched on with nobody approved, a floor spelled `unknown` (the absence of a capability tier, not a weak one, and a floor anything would clear), a negative daily cap, an approval entry that is not a GitHub login, or two tier-map rows disagreeing about one model configuration. An omitted floor defaults to `T1`, the strongest, and an omitted daily cap to `0`, which dispatches nothing — so adopting the block early is safe. The floor stays readable-only on every surface, with a test that scans every route and client file to keep it that way: lowering it is an edit to `hive.yaml`, never a control, and no surface suggests it. See [the standby design record](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/design/standby-contributors.md) and [agent configuration](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/agent-configuration.md).
- Add standby_v1 relay declarations and hub-side per-connection standby state. (#8055)
- Hive now has the standby-contributor matching rules from [RFC #7629](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7629) as a pure package, `pkg/standby` ([#8056](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8056)): the `T1 > T2 > T3 > unknown` capability ordering, the whole-configuration tier map behind `hub.standby_model_tiers`, the per-lane floor comparison, and the rolling-day cap accounting that decides whether an approved contributor has a donated slot left. Nothing calls it yet — no lane counts anybody and nothing dispatches — so behaviour on every hive is unchanged; what lands is the decision itself, in one place, testable as a table. Three rules it is built to hold: a configuration the owner never mapped resolves to `unknown` and clears no floor, refused by its own explicit guard so the reason reads `configuration_unknown` rather than `below_floor`; a lane policy carrying no legal floor admits nobody rather than everybody; and a refusal states its class and never the delta, with the tier ordering unexported so no surface can render "you would qualify one tier down". The daily cap is a trailing 24-hour window rather than a calendar day, matching `tier_limits.max_per_day`, so a burst cannot straddle a reset, and it decrements at dispatch, so an abandoned donated task still costs a slot. See [the standby design record](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/design/standby-contributors.md).
- Count qualified standby contributors per paused lane and show the qualifying total on the dashboard tile. (#8056)
- `hivectl hives use` now switches a running contributor relay to the newly active hive without a restart by signaling the relay to reload its generated `contributor.env`; the relay records non-secret hub last-seen timestamps for `hives list` and lets any in-flight task finish on its original hive before soliciting from the new one (#8126).
- Added manual standby dispatch for paused lanes, including donated task markers, cap accounting, hold-gated completion, dashboard/chat controls, and attribution trailer fields. (#8135)
- Added standby S6 outcome ledger wiring with suspend-after-N declaration rejection and owner clear controls. (#8136)
- The standby-contributor suspend rule from [RFC #7629](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7629) now exists as a pure function over a donated-PR outcome ledger, `pkg/standby/suspend.go` ([#8136](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8136)): N consecutive closed-unmerged donated PRs (default 2) suspend that contributor-plus-configuration tuple on that hive until the owner clears it, a merge in between breaks the streak, and the owner's clear is appended as a `cleared` row so the ledger stays an audit record rather than being edited. A merge that only happened because somebody other than the donor pushed to the PR is recorded as `merged_after_rework` and counts as evidence in neither direction — it neither resets the streak nor advances it — classified from the author set `holdguard` already snapshots at hold time, rather than from a second answer to "who touched this after we recorded it". Nothing calls it yet: no outcome is recorded, nothing is suspended, and behaviour on every hive is unchanged; the dispatch path that writes the ledger arrives with [#8135](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8135). Every ambiguity in the rule resolves toward *not* suspending — an unrecognized ledger row is skipped rather than counted, an empty ledger is not suspended, and a threshold nobody configured means the documented default of 2 rather than the zero that would suspend every donor on sight. See [the standby design record](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/design/standby-contributors.md#suspend-rule).
- Standby matching now weighs the WORK as well as the worker ([#8137](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8137), step S7 of [RFC #7629](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7629)): a new owner-authored `hub.standby_item_tiers` list says which classes of item may be offered to a standby contributor and at what capability tier, and `standby.Qualifies` requires a donated configuration to clear both the lane's floor and the item's tier — a T1 configuration may take a T3 item, a T3 configuration may not take a T1 item. The list **ships empty, and empty means it is not in force at all**: the lane floor decides alone and every hive's answer is byte for byte what it was before. Entries are keyed on `(repo, label)` with duplicates a load error, an item matching no entry of a non-empty list is `unknown` and not standby-eligible, and a `T3` entry **must name the automated signal that makes it cheap to review** — the design's verifiability test for T3 eligibility, enforced at load rather than written down. The list is authoritative: Hive's classifier can propose a tier for an item from its labels, and that proposal is carried for logging and decides nothing — an item absent from the list does not become donatable because something proposed T3 for it. No surface writes the list or even names its key, held by the same scan that keeps the model floor read-only, and no surface proposes adding an item to it. See [the standby design record](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/design/standby-contributors.md) and [agent configuration](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/blob/v6/src/docs/agent-configuration.md#standby-contributors-standby).

Spektacular runs can now also be driven from chat and the Runs card: `POST /api/runs/spec` plus new `!runs spec`, `!runs status`, and `!runs list` chat verbs, with Spektacular artifact/status/step attribution shown on run cards.

- Added a contributor reasoning-effort floor: `hub.contribute_min_reasoning_effort` (with `hub.contribute_reject_unknown_effort` to control how an empty/unrecognised effort is treated) rejects relays whose reported reasoning effort ranks below the configured floor on a normalised, per-backend ladder (`minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max`). The floor is exposed on `GET/PUT /api/config/governor` next to `contribute_allow_models`, on the contribute policy (`min_reasoning_effort`/`reject_unknown_effort`) so relays can pre-check before submitting work, as an **Effort floor** control in Governor → Hub → Model Filter, and in `docs/contributor-relay.md` ([#9197](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9197)).
- The dashboard NPS prompt gains three operator options, all defaulting to today's behavior: `hub.nps_timing` overrides the eligibility timing (validated, handed to the dashboard in the status response); `HIVE_NPS_GA4_MEASUREMENT_ID` (unset = off) sends `hive_nps_survey_shown` / `hive_nps_response` / `hive_nps_dismissed` GA4 events carrying score, category and feedback length but never the text, widening the CSP only while set and honoring a per-browser opt-out, Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track; and `hub.nps_detractor_issues` (off by default) lets a score-1 user tick a consent box to have the hive's App open a public issue from 20+ characters of feedback, with mentions neutralized and 1-per-user / 3-per-hive daily limits (`POST /api/feedback/nps/issue`); see `src/docs/nps.md` (#9610).
- The dashboard can show signed-in users an occasional 4-point NPS feedback prompt (console-identical timing and backoff); responses are forwarded to the hub over the spoke's per-hive heartbeat bearer without the user's identity, stored in a rolling window, and readable only by hub admins at `GET /api/admin/nps` and on a new hub admin NPS card. On by default for hosted spokes, off for every other install (`hub.nps_enabled` / `HIVE_NPS_ENABLED`); see `src/docs/nps.md` (#9610).
- Standalone hives (no hub link) can send dashboard NPS responses to the hivecommons relay when the operator opts in (`HIVE_NPS_ENABLED=true`) and sets `hub.nps_relay_url` / `HIVE_NPS_RELAY_URL`; the hive generates and self-registers an Ed25519 install key (stored 0600 under `/data/secrets`) and signs every submission, so no per-install token is issued or configured. A hub with a pull secret (`hub.nps_relay_pull_secret` / `HIVE_NPS_RELAY_PULL_SECRET`) periodically pulls, deduplicates and acks those entries, which appear in `GET /api/admin/nps` tagged `source: relay` with their `install_id` and are labeled "unverified install" in the admin card. Everything defaults off; see `src/docs/nps.md` (#9619).
- escalation: successful email/push deliveries are now audited as `escalation_delivered` (sink, severity, title, `attempts=N` after retries) and logged at info, so operators have hive-side evidence for pages and decision mails, not only for failures (#9701)
- Carry contributor abandoned PR counts through spoke heartbeats and task-status pushes into the hub's merged leaderboard, treating older spokes as zero ([#15799](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15799)).
- Show abandoned PR counts in the dashboard and contribute landing leaderboards without changing contributor rankings ([#15796](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15796)).
- **Activity Monitor display controls.** In display mode (`?display=1`), moving the pointer or tabbing reveals an overlay with separate **Exit display**, **Copy link**, **Full screen** and **Keep awake** controls that hides after 3 s idle. Full screen and the screen wake lock are requested only when you click their control, never on load; unsupported and denied states render disabled or with the browser's reason and are never retried automatically. The copied link carries only `display=1`, the `am.*` view and `theme` — never a token. Nothing is persisted, and kiosk mode is unchanged ([#15929](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15929)).
- **Activity Monitor display playlists.** A display-mode URL can rotate between views: repeat `am.view=<url-encoded am.* query>` and set `interval=Ns|Nm` (10 s–1 h, default 60 s), e.g. `?display=1&am.view=am.needsHuman%3D1&am.view=am.kind%3Dpr&interval=2m`. Invalid views are skipped and fewer than two means no rotation. The current view follows the wall clock, so it survives reloads and reconnects; rotation is in memory only (no navigation, refetch or local storage), with a thin progress bar or a static "next in Ns" label under reduced motion. Playlists live only in the URL — no `hive.yaml` presets — and kiosk mode is unchanged ([#15932](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15932)).
- Activity Monitor display mode (`?display=1`) now says when its data is stale ([#15930](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15930), part of [#15860](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15860)). A wall screen used to keep showing its last payload as if it were live after the event stream or the spoke went quiet. Now the display header shows the hive id, a clock and a live dot. When the stream has been silent for more than two poll intervals, or the payload is older than two cache TTLs, the dot turns amber, the board dims and a banner reads *Stale: last update N ago*. The display recovers by itself when updates resume. After five failed reconnects it reloads on a 30 s → 10 min backoff, and it reloads once after an upgrade finishes. The URL, and so the view, survives the reload. The ordinary Activity Monitor and headless `?kiosk=1` output are unchanged.
- Activity Monitor display mode (`?display=1`) gains wall-screen options ([#15931](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15931), part of [#15860](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15860)). `density=tv` uses larger type and shows only each row's stage, title and actor. It shows only the rows that fit the screen, with a "+N more" footer instead of the pager. `shift=1` moves the board 1–2 px every 4 minutes to protect OLED screens from burn-in. With *reduce motion* on, a display plays no row movement and no shift. Both options are ignored without `display=1`, so the ordinary Activity Monitor and `?kiosk=1` render exactly as before. The TV layout adds nothing that changes state.
- The Hive activity monitor shows which rows Hive can finish on its own. A row that needs a person, now or at a gate further on such as an approving review branch protection requires or a hand merge, carries a **🧑 needs a person** chip whose hover text gives the reason, even while the lit step is still Hive's move. *Sort* gains **Hive end to end first** (Hive's rows, then rows waiting on someone else, then rows that need a person); the direction arrow puts the rows that need a person first. `/api/stage-tracker` items and their `linked_prs` add `finisher`, `finisher_verb` and `finisher_reason`, read from the same your-turn decision as the Overview.
- Hive activity monitor label chips are ordered `stage/NNN-*` by number then every other label alphabetically, every label is reachable — the **+N more** indicator is now a button that opens an in-app *All labels* dialog (same order, counts, type-to-filter, the chips' own toggles and *Clear*; labels picked there join the visible row) — and a **🙋 Needs human** facet leads the row, counting distinct items carrying any label of the server's needs-human set (`/api/stage-tracker.needs_human_labels`, the same list as the Projects *Needs human* preset, which now also includes `stage/071-needs-author` and the reporter-trust `needs-triage` label).
- **The Hive activity monitor can play a short "bug zapper" when a pull request merges while the page is open** ([#13275](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13275)). A speaker chip at the right end of the monitor's toolbar (🔇/🔊, off by default, remembered per browser under `hive.tracker.sound`) opts in; turning it on plays the zap once. The sound is synthesised in the browser with the Web Audio API — a third of a second of crackling noise swept down through a bandpass filter over a low thunk, peak gain 0.3 — so there is no audio asset and no request the dashboard's CSP would have to allow. It fires when a PR the tab was already showing turns merged between two tracker refreshes, once per PR, never on first load, never for issues or already-merged rows, at most two zaps per refresh, and never while the tab is hidden. To make "merged" distinguishable from "closed" (the tracker lists open work only), `GET /api/stage-tracker` now also carries `recently_merged` — the PRs whose `pr_merged` audit entry (sweep, queue, relay, or a human merge the PR poller observed) is under 30 minutes old.
- Activity Monitor: every row action now reports what actually happened in a result toast that stays until the row changes state (shared `result` payload on the decision, delegated-decision, accept-triage, hold, send-to-human and rescan endpoints), rows show an in-flight "acting…" cue from click to state change, each confirm dialog has a "Don't ask again for this action" box (reset from ⚙ → Confirmations) with the sentinel ⚠ line carried into the toast, the lit chevron turns while a hive agent is on the item and a one-line event line says what just happened, and a merge pins the row for a moment while an amber token rises into a new "Merged today" counter (toggle "Celebrate merges"). Requested by @clubanderson.
- `src/deploy/stream/`: a headless Twitch streamer image (Xvfb + Chromium + ffmpeg, published as `ghcr.io/hivecommons/hive-stream`) with Kustomize manifests that put the dashboard's Activity Monitor on an unattended 24/7 stream, plus a dashboard `?kiosk=1` display mode that hides the chrome, dialogs and every other section ([#15594](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15594)). Guide: `src/docs/streaming-the-activity-monitor.md`.
- **Activity Monitor URL views and display mode.** Every Activity Monitor filter can now be described in `am.*` URL parameters (`am.kind`, `am.repo`, `am.q`, `am.labels`, `am.group`, …), so a link reproduces the same view in a fresh browser profile; a tab opened with `am.*` keeps its filter to itself and never overwrites the saved one. A new 📺 header button (or `?display=1`) turns the monitor into an attended wall view with no row actions, left with Esc or `d`; it never requests full screen or a wake lock, grants nothing, and `?kiosk=1` is unchanged ([#15924](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15924), [#15925](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15925)).
- Admin MCP reads and acts on the Activity monitor: `stage_tracker_read` returns the board (stages, what each item waits on, decision options, linked items, blockers) with the monitor's filters and search, `delegated_decision_status` reads a "Let hive decide" job, and the `repository.rescan` and `repository.item_*` write operations are the monitor's row actions (accept triage, needs-human, blocker re-check / hand-off / partial close, Decide answers, Let hive decide) — never the merge answers, and a delegated decision sent through admin MCP never queues an auto-merge. On the HTTP endpoint a confirmed write now runs as the caller the hive verified (session or hub proxy), bound to whoever previewed it, so hub-proxied callers can write and their writes are attributed to them.
- Activity Monitor: a PR waiting on a contributor's clanker (stage 072/071) now offers **Adopt now — hive takes it over** (decision API `adopt` + `force: true`: forced supersede adoption bypassing presence, grace and `maintainer_policy`, marker `hive:adopted reason=operator-forced by=@login`) and **Reroute to another clanker** (decision API `reroute` + `to`: the follow-up work is dispatched to an online clanker's fix queue as a `fix-pr` interrupt, `hive:rerouted` note, `rerouted → @X` pill; falls back to Adopt now after `governor.reroute.pickup_timeout`, default 30m), in the row menu, the Needs-human popover and the delegated "Let hive decide" rules (hivecommons/hive#15038).
- `governor.labels.stage.adoption.maintainer_policy: adopt | ask | never` (default **adopt**) replaces the hard-coded "author maintains the repository; not adopting" rule: clanker PRs are adoptable on disconnect regardless of the owner's repo role (owner decision on [#14524](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14524), a maintainer's `author/clanker` PR left 26h at 072 with its hive offline). `ask` parks a maintainer's PR for an owner — the activity monitor row reads "waiting on @author (maintainer, offline 26h) — adopt?" and offers **Adopt** (`decide:adopt` → decision API `adopt`, which sets `adoption/supersede`); `never` is the previous behaviour. Every nudged 072 PR row now carries `adoption{due, blocked_by, since, nudges, author_online, …}` and a plain-words caption/pill; Settings → Labels gets the three-way selector.
- ADR-0025 and implementation plan for a central stage engine: one `pkg/stageengine` reconciler derives every `stage/*` label for issues and PRs from GitHub truth each cycle, a single `StageWriter` performs all stage writes, relay/claim paths submit facts instead of labels, and unexpected transitions are asserted as anomalies rather than rejected. Docs only; rollout gated by `governor.labels.stage.engine.mode: shadow | enforce`.
- Add the advisor lane's Copilot CLI (`agentStop`) and Codex CLI (`Stop`) adapters: hook files in hive-owned per-agent homes, `COPILOT_HOME` and `-c features.hooks=true` at launch, with no edits to operator config files (#9724).
- Added phase 1 of the advisor lane (#9722, epic #9638): a `model_roles` map and an opt-in `advisor` block (fleet default plus per-agent override), an evaluator that rides the trajectory lane's reviewer endpoint resolution with a fail-open posture, advisor records listed over `GET /api/advisor/records` and on the agent's dashboard card, and the `hive advisor-hook` Claude Code `Stop` hook adapter projected into the settings argument at launch — never an edit of the agent's own configuration.
- Advisor lane phase 2: OMP agents get the advisor through a hive-owned `session_stop` extension and a `--config` roles overlay, both projected at launch without touching the operator's OMP config.
- Added advisor-lane operator surfaces: Settings editing of the advisor block, per-agent overrides and model roles with the in-force value per agent; advisor spend beside agent spend (`GET /api/advisor/spend`, `advisor_by_agent` on `/api/cost`); time-window filters on `GET /api/advisor/records`; the read-only `advisor_records` admin MCP tool; and the advisor entry in the backend support tiers doc (#9725).
- Agents: idle CLI sessions over an RSS (`agents.session_recycle.max_rss_mb`, default 1536 MiB) or age (`max_age`, default 6h) budget are recycled through the normal restart path, bounding the V8 heap growth that was OOM-killing the pod; the dashboard shows each agent's session RSS and age (#14842).
- Added a repo-root `AGENTS.md` (and `CLAUDE.md` alias) telling agents that CI runs the tests: no local `go test`/build/lint, and never run this repo's suite inside an agent pane (#9416).
- **`/hive ack` and `/hive snooze <duration>` for attention episodes, plus the attention action contract** ([#16359](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16359), part of [#16270](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16270)). On a repository whose `github.attention.admitter` is this hive, the episode's responsible person or a maintainer (`write`/`maintain`/`admin`) can acknowledge an attention episode or pause its reminders (1m–30d) from a comment; the un-park sweep records who and when on the episode (`acked_by`, `snoozed_by`, `snoozed_until`), refreshes the attention status section and replies once. Anyone else is ignored and nothing is recorded. Acknowledgement is not approval: neither command changes a label, releases a security/merge/review hold or opens a merge gate. `attention.Event` / `attention.NewObservation` define the contract every attention event must satisfy — who, what changed and why now, requested action, evidence, what Hive tried, what happens next, and how to ack, snooze or resolve — and refuse incomplete events. See `src/docs/maintainer-commands.md` and `src/docs/notifications.md`.
- `github.notifications.attention_pilot` (default off) opts a hive in to the attention pilot ([#16358](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16358), part of [#16270](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16270)): routine issue notes — partial work, close/auto-close narration (merged fix, decomposed parent), reopened-after-merge, stage regressions, the covering-PR note and the blocker-settled note — fold into the issue's single `hive:status` card through the shared status writer, and a newly required action (confirming a merged fix) is still announced by exactly one notifying write. With the flag off nothing changes.
- The hive approves workflow runs GitHub holds behind "Approve and run workflows" once per PR head for trusted bots (`governor.ci.auto_approve_workflow_actors`, default dependabot and renovate), its own App and heads a person admitted from the dashboard (`governor.ci.auto_approve_workflows`, default on; needs App **Actions: Read and write**, or set it `false` to keep Actions: Read); counts are in `/api/status` `workflow_approvals`, and a missing `actions: write` permission shows `CI waiting · needs workflow approval on GitHub`.
- The contribution list now shows an **Auto** state for repositories that were turned on because you follow their Hive. Ticking "Accept all new repositories" (or pressing "Refresh membership") stages the new repositories as Auto for review, `hivectl hives preset refresh` marks them in `profiles.yml` (`auto:`), and turning one off under a followed Hive also excludes it so following does not add it back.
- Settings → Features → Auto-merge gains a "Merge only on current base" switch (`auto_merge.require_current_base_default`, **off** by default) and each row on the Repos tab a per-repo inherit / on / off override (`auto_merge.require_current_base` / `auto_merge.skip_current_base`); the repo card shows a `current-base` chip when the gate is on. A gated repo only merges a head that contains the current base tip — a green head whose base has moved is updated with GitHub update-branch and merges once CI is green on the new head, which would have stopped the stale-green merge that broke `v5` for every open PR for 20 minutes. Explicitly listed repos are strict; repos gated only by the default merge a head the App cannot update (fork without maintainer edits, branch protection) as tested, with one WARN per PR. The fleet default stays off while the gate soaks on hive's own hive ([#15335](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15335)).
- Conflict-aware merge train in every automerge lane ([#15117](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15117)): approved PRs to one base with overlapping changed files are grouped per sweep, one front merges at a time, siblings wait at stage/080 as `merge_gate.state=queued-behind` ("In merge train · 3rd of 4", never a human stage), and after the front merges the lane updates `behind` branches and asks the rebase-resolve hook for `dirty` ones (`auto_merge.merge_train.max_rebase_attempts`, default 2; past it: stage/085 "Needs human decision · rebase failed twice" with "Rebase, then merge as maintainer"). The Activity Monitor renders a train contiguously with a left rail and a `⛓ merge train · N PRs · front #X` header chip, and `/api/stage-tracker` items carry `merge_train{id,state,front,position,size,overlap_files,ahead}`. `auto_merge.merge_train.enabled` (default on) turns it off.
- Owners can set `auto_merge.require_current_base`, `auto_merge.squash_only` and `auto_merge.human_merge_paths` from Settings → Features → Auto-merge → Per-repository merge policy, so a hosted hive no longer needs a hand-edited config overlay for them.
- Added Campaign run detail panels with source issue/PR links, stage transcripts, and raw chronological logs.
- chat: `!runs reject <key> <reason>` now sends the reason to the dashboard (audit log), and the run checkpoint prompt tells users to reply with the `!runs approve|reject <key>` form that dashboard chat forwards (#10093, #10123)
- A failed `check_run`, `check_suite` or `status` webhook now reacts within seconds instead of waiting for the next governor sweep: the head SHA is resolved to its open PR from the PR detail cache, recorded as a CI failure signal (`/api/status.ci_failure_signals`), and a hive-authored PR's owning agent is kicked at once with the check name and log URL while a contributor PR gets a targeted automerge/contributor-lane pass — gated by `governor.ci_failure_webhook_kick` (default on), repo/agent pauses and a per-head cooldown (`governor.ci_failure_kick_cooldown_s`, default 600). Agents still never watch or poll CI themselves.
- ClankeR contributors can select Apple MLX on `/contribute` and use dedicated `just` setup/serve/launch recipes for user-managed MLX-LM inference through Pi on supported Apple Silicon Macs, with loopback-only configuration, explicit streaming tool-call verification, fail-closed checks, and public integration/setup documentation.
- Add opt-in Cline CLI coding workers to Crux, Hive and the ClankeR contributor relay, with explicit provider/model selection, isolated API-key credentials, bounded turns, streaming results and cancellation; disposable Jobs use dedicated provider Secret references and Podman uses a scoped read-only selected-provider mount with per-run cleanup; unsupported tool policies and OAuth refresh sharing fail closed.
- An agent finding that the issue filter keeps off the queues is now `CLOSE` when every permalink it cites is gone from the default branch (`cited_lines_gone`), instead of waiting to be admitted or triaged. The enumeration reads the cited lines at the pinned commit and the same file on the default branch. It checks at most 3 findings per repository per pass, trusts a result for 6 hours, and treats a read failure as unknown. A file that is gone from the default branch counts as unknown too, because a rename keeps the lines. projectbluefin/testsuite#1085, for example, cited `SKILL.md:163` for a fallback the guide no longer described.
- Add an opt-in, per-repo single-admitter attention primitive with durable condition episodes, quiet recovery, and uncertain-POST reconciliation; existing quiet-mode writers and review/hold behavior remain unchanged.
- Add `just contribute-watch` / `hivectl tui --watch` to mirror a running contributor's session and relay log, attach interactively, control quota and confirm Stop without changing the Hives configuration screen; krun contributors show a console-only state and attach with `podman attach`; local relays also keep a private, size-capped live-tail log buffer ([#13236](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13236)).
- Add a shared contribution-tree staging layer with reviewed membership and exclusion diffs, shared-Hive effects, guarded Apply retries, and separate persistence, relay notification, and pending-adoption receipts.
- Add a credential-free shared contribution tree read model and read-only `hivectl hives tree` inspection of saved consent, with explicit legacy, exclusion, and incomplete-discovery status; persisted hub discovery integration follows separately.
- Each contributor profile now records the PRs the hive had to adopt from that contributor: `abandoned` (one per PR, deduped) plus `abandoned_prs` records `{repo, pr, adopted_into_pr, reason, at}` on `/api/contributors`, counted at in-place adoption, supersession onto `hive/adopt-<n>` and operator takeovers (Adopt now / `adoption/supersede`, reason `operator_takeover`); automatic adoptions carry `offline` or `unresponsive` ([#15782](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15782)).
- Show abandoned PR counts and recent-adoption tooltips on Contributors cards, and expose historical totals and per-login counts in `/api/status.contributorPool`.
- Contributor-first lanes: `agents.<name>.contributor_first: true` makes a connected contributor relay acting as that agent's role the lane's primary worker. While such a relay is connected (and not stale or failure-paused) the governor withholds the resident agent's kicks, so the hive's own inference budget is not spent on work a contributor is already covering; the resident agent resumes on its normal cadence once no relay has covered the role for `contributor_first_grace` (default 10m). The Governor section shows which lanes are covered and by whom (`covered_lanes` on `/api/status`). Budget pause and standby dispatch are unchanged: a covered lane is never reported as paused for budget.
- Settings: the agent's General tab now has **Contributor-first** and **Contributor-first grace** controls for `agents.<name>.contributor_first` and `contributor_first_grace`, so a hive owner (including on a hub-hosted spoke) can switch a lane to contributor-first without editing `hive.yaml`. The toggle is disabled, with the fix named, for a role contributors may not act as; a save is refused with the same message the load would give, and takes effect on the next governor evaluation without a restart.
- Contributors can opt in to running the contributor container inside a krun microVM with `HIVE_CONTAINER_OCI_RUNTIME=krun` (environment or `contributor.env`): rootless podman and headless only, with a `/dev/kvm` and guest-kernel preflight, VM sizing from `HIVE_CONTAINER_MEMORY`/`HIVE_CONTAINER_CPUS`, an `Isolation: microVM (krun)` banner line, krun-aware `just contribute-stop` and `hivectl` relay controls, and no fallback to a plain container; unset leaves the launch unchanged (#12199).
- Contributor lane approves `action_required` workflow runs once per head for a PR author the contributor registry admitted at a `require_tiers` tier when the lane stops at `required-check-missing:<ctx>` (fork heads included), posting one `hive:contributor-held-runs-approved` audit comment; toggle `auto_merge.contributor_lane.approve_held_runs_for_registry_trusted` (default on). Claim-marker, auto-promoted and association admissions, sentinel/exclude-labelled PRs and `.github/workflows/**` diffs are never approved for (#14519).
- Show online ClankeR contributor IDs vertically in the Contributors sidebar count pill's hover and keyboard-focus tooltip.
- The sidebar **Contributors** item now reads **online/total** (for example `3/12`), the same two-part pill Governor and Overview use, with the tooltip *N online · M registered (heartbeat within 15m)* ([#15651](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15651)). *Online* is the stage tracker's own presence test — a registered contributor whose relay heartbeat landed within `governor.labels.stage.presence_window` — so the pill and *waiting on @name (offline 13m)* always agree. `/api/status.contributorPool` gains `online` and `presence_window`; `/api/contributors` rows gain `online`; the Contributors header shows the same figure and the card list sorts online contributors first with a green/grey presence dot.
- Cost section: the spend-over-time chart's default windows are wider and adjustable — hourly 24 h, daily 14 d (month/day labels once there are more than 7 bars), weekly 5 wk (one bar per week), monthly 5 mo (one bar per month) — with a −/+ stepper beside the range chips (hourly 6–72 by 6, daily 7–60 by 7, weekly 2–26, monthly 2–24; remembered per range). Spend-in-range and run-rate follow the stepped window. Each completed UTC day of cost snapshots is now folded into a per-day rollup kept ~2 years (`/api/cost` `daily_rollup`, `/data/cost-daily-rollup.json`) so weekly/monthly windows reach past the 30-day snapshot ring; bars with no recorded history draw hatched and the summary notes where history starts.
- Surface verified covered-by-PR and likely-done issue claims as labels and linked PR badges without hiding issues on comment evidence alone.
- The `crux` binary now exports its OpenTelemetry spans and new kick duration/outcome metrics (`crux.agent.kick.duration`, `crux.agent.kick.outcomes`, labelled only by agent role and outcome) over OTLP/HTTP when the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` environment names an endpoint; with none set nothing changes ([hivecommons/crux#19](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/19)).
- `crux agy-turn`: the headless agy turn subprocess is a `crux` subcommand, so a manager running under `crux serve` (which types its own executable into the pane) can drive agy agents the same way `hive agy-turn` does in-process.
- The crux callback API now records `crux.callback.request.duration` and `crux.callback.requests` metrics and a span per request, labelled by capability, status class and refusal code only; nothing is exported unless an OTel exporter is configured.
- crux: `serve` attaches a caller principal to every authenticated request (`serve.CallerFrom`): the control token is the operator (named by `--operator-name`/`CRUX_OPERATOR_NAME`), and lane project credentials are accepted as project principals on work-services routes only — agent RPCs still refuse them. Groundwork for the crux work services (hivecommons/crux#114 S0).
- crux: pinned checkout service (hivecommons/crux#114 S1): `POST/GET/DELETE /v1/checkouts` on `crux serve` (enabled by `--checkout-allow`/`CRUX_CHECKOUT_ALLOWLIST`) and `crux checkout add|rm|list` provision a git worktree pinned at a full 40-hex SHA from an allowlisted repository, owned by the caller principal, with a recorded TTL and a post-hoc size cap. Records live under `<workdir>/checkouts`; design notes in `docs/design/crux-work-services.md`.
- `crux` CLI (`src/cmd/crux`: `run`, `ps`, `logs`, `kick`, `stop`) that drives an agent through the `crux.Runtime` interface from a hive `AgentDefinition` or overlay file, with a control socket served by `crux run` so the observer commands act on the live runtime; shipped in the image and documented in `src/docs/crux-cli.md` ([#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536))
- Design record `src/docs/design/crux.md` for the Crux agent-runtime boundary (RFC #13536) and an architecture ratchet test that fails when any package outside `pkg/agent/...` references more distinct `agent.<Symbol>` identifiers or invokes tmux from more files than its recorded baseline.
- Add opt-in, forge-neutral Crux durable event/work lanes backed by NATS JetStream, project-scoped API credentials, verified publish generations, replay, fenced leases, authorized audited expiration recovery, persistent fair retry rotation and reusable reserved delivery slots, with Hive participating through a read-only governor adapter.
- Crux stage 2 (#14138): `crux/api/callback` is the stdlib-only wire contract a sidecar runtime uses to call back into hive for scoped GitHub tokens, REST accounting, usage, canary/text scans, conditions, the Linear credential and PR creation (HTTP+JSON over a hive-served 0600 Unix socket, fail closed when hive is unreachable); `crux/hivecap` adapts it onto the ring's existing seams and `pkg/cruxhost` is the hive-side mount over hive's existing implementations. The runtime never holds the App private key.
- `crux serve --hive-callback ADDR` (default `$CRUX_HIVE_SOCKET`, token from `$CRUX_HIVE_TOKEN`) dials hive's capability endpoint and feeds the runtime's seams from it (Crux sidecar plan, stage 3): the manager's condition reporter, sandbox pull-request creator, Linear credential resolver and push-token minter, and the process-wide tool-approve text scanner, all through `crux/hivecap` so each fails closed when hive is unreachable. The endpoint's reachability is reported as `hive_callback` on `GET /v1/health` and as the `hive_callback_unavailable` condition on `GET /v1/events` (`hivecap.Watch`, `serve.Server.Conditions`).
- `crux serve` now exposes every `crux.Runtime` family over its API (Crux sidecar plan, stage 3): per-agent start/restart/pause/resume/restart-count, full `crux.Process` snapshots, async kick + validate + dispatch state, kick-log listing and reads, verbatim definitions (add/update/remove/reconcile), overrides and pins, mode sync/clear, fleet breaker/ACMM/relaunch/startup-queue/crash-restart/token-refresh/kick-log archive, Copilot and Claude credentials, the Resumer session routes (`409 resume_busy`, `410 resume_session_gone`, `422 resume_unsupported`), one supervision read per agent, backend auth, nudges, audit, trajectory views, restore seeds, a synchronous `POST /v1/authorize` (204 / 403, unknown action 400 — clients treat anything but 204 as a denial), and the watchdog seam (`/v1/watchdog/agents`, per-agent observe and conditions; `501 not_supported` on a runtime without one). `GET /v1/events` carries the `crux.Host` observer events (kick outcome, pause transition, relaunch, pause persist, prompt, sandbox audit, audit, condition) with typed `data` payloads, and the server can run the Background loops in-process (`Server.Background`; `GET /v1/health` lists them). `crux/api.RuntimeRoutes` is the method→route table the parity tests hold the interface to; `crux/cruxtest.Recorder` is a recording `crux.Runtime`/`crux.Host` fake for anything that drives a runtime without running one.
- `crux/api/client.Runtime` implements every `crux.Runtime` family over the `crux serve` API (Crux sidecar plan, stage 3): `crux/runtime.New` returns it in `CRUX_MODE=sidecar` (connecting to `$CRUX_SERVER` or the serve socket) instead of `ErrModeUnavailable`, and `NewWatchdogFleet` composes a watchdog fleet for it from the wire watchdog source plus the runtime's Lifecycle. Kick and Host observer events ride one reconnecting `/v1/events` stream; the Resumer sentinels (`ErrResumeBusy`, `ErrResumeSessionGone`, `ErrResumeUnsupported`) round-trip from the server's status codes; Authorizer refusals and transport failures fail closed. A parity test holds `crux.Runtime` and `api.RuntimeRoutes` to each other in both directions so a method cannot be added without a route.
- crux: the proxy lets an in-hive Spek publish its RFC and children — GitHub `POST …/issues/{n}/sub_issues` and `POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by` and Linear `issueRelationCreate`/`projectCreate`/`projectUpdate` are allowed at ISSUES_ONLY; a new `crux/spekmarker` package parses the `<!-- spek:publish … -->` marker and `issueshape.SpekPublished` exposes it as the "already specified" clarity-gate signal (spektacular#114).
- Crux stage 4: sidecar agents now get the same credentials as in-process ones. The hive callback gains `agent_mint` (`POST /v1/tokens/mint`) and `bob` (`GET /v1/bob/credential`) families; `crux serve` installs callback-backed `SetAppAuth` (tier-scoped App installation tokens minted by hive over `POST /v1/tokens` and written in place to the per-agent cache), `SetAgentMint`, and the Bob key resolvers, all failing closed (no credential) when hive is unreachable; `sidecarHost` carries every remaining credential setter. Tokens are never logged.
- Crux stage 4 failure semantics (#14138): hive supervises `crux serve` as a child (`CRUX_SUPERVISE=child|external`, `CRUX_BINARY`) with readiness checks and restart backoff; a lost runtime socket refuses kicks with `crux.ErrRuntimeUnavailable` (no replay), raises the `crux_runtime_unavailable` fleet-report condition, and surfaces as `crux_runtime` in hive's `/api/health`; `crux serve` `/v1/health` reports `started_at`/`uptime_seconds`.
- Crux sidecar runtimes (`CRUX_MODE=sidecar`, [#14138](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14138) stage 4) now reach two more `crux.Host` setters over the hive callback endpoint: the manager's inference routes go to hive's proxy over `PUT`/`DELETE /v1/inference/routes/{agent}` (pushed by a non-blocking worker with retry and a one-minute resync, so a restarted hive relearns them) and sandbox branch pushes run through hive's journaling mutation boundary two-phase over `POST /v1/effects` / `POST /v1/effects/{id}/end` (an unreachable hive refuses the push; a denial is `effects.ErrDenied`; a sidecar that dies mid-push is journaled as abandoned after 15 minutes). `SetSpanStarter` is documented in-process-only. `api.HostSetters` is the disposition table (callback | event | route | config | in-process-only) for every `Host` setter and `crux/api/client`'s parity test fails when a setter is added without a row. In-process mode is unchanged.
- A sidecar Crux runtime now receives hive's host policy over the hive callback endpoint ([#14138](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14138), stage 4): `GET /v1/policy` and `POST /v1/policy/repo-auto-merge` carry build info, the explain-mode default, the kick log source, configured gateway backends, per-repo auto-merge, dead-session recovery ownership and the `agent_sandbox` config, which `crux serve --hive-callback` polls and installs on the manager. In-process mode is unchanged; inference routes, the sandbox mutation boundary and the span starter are not carried yet.
- Crux stage 4: hive now serves the inference usage ledger to a sidecar runtime over the hive callback's `usage` capability (it was `not_configured`), so a proxy whose `Accounting`/`Usage`/`Canary` seams are the callback adapters records usage and REST traffic into hive's ledgers, refuses GitHub writes while hive is unreachable and resumes when it returns.
- Added ADR-0018 and the dashboard design-system reference so the spoke, contributor portal, and hub can converge on shared tokens and theme overrides for #8536.
- Add opt-in, default-off `dashboard.matrix` config block with an explicit `owner/name` repo allowlist (#15928, part of #15862)
- The v6 dashboard has a **Search** section over the portfolio search index (`GET /api/search`): a query box, kind/repo/verdict/sentinel-rule facet chips, results linking to the PR, issue or bead, a visible marker on redacted hits and a note naming repos the index could not read. Each Projects card also shows a report-only health badge (score and status, components in the tooltip) from `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/health`. Both stay hidden while `search.enabled` is off, and the Search section is hidden from viewers who are not an owner or maintainer ([#14888](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14888)).
- "Let hive decide" on a parked issue now judges the way the owner would: a fleet self-report whose remedy is the spoke operator's (expired provider login, credentials, disk, network, App setup) gets one direction comment to the spoke owner — no `approved-direction`, no implementer, the park kept, and never the same direction twice; a hive-filed proposal is approved when it cites an incident or a fixed-one-at-a-time recurrence and declined for now (closed as not planned) when it cites neither; a hive-policy item's recommendation is a real sentence instead of "no special rule applies".
- *Let hive decide* now shows what the decision rests on. Under **Details**, the preview lists **What hive saw**: every fact the decision rules read (author, whether the contributor is connected, CI, conflicts, sign-off, review, Sentinel and the rest), each marked as fine, holding the item back, or steering the decision. Then come the rule that decided, with its whole reason, and each option that was ruled out, with the fact that ruled it out. The visible part of the dialog is unchanged.
- **"Let hive decide": LLM step for non-mechanical cases.** With the new `decisions.delegate.llm.enabled` (default false), an item the owner-delegate rules leave at the reversible default is decided by one model turn that sees the item, its thread, sentinel findings, linked items and the owner's policy; its structured verdict is validated against the delegate's closed action set and goes through the same safety rails, and any error or invalid reply keeps the reversible default.
- Add `hivectl hives repos <hive> --deselect-current` to clear current repository consent while retaining exclusions, provenance, and future-follow policy, and `--follow-new-repos=false` to stop following without removing accepted repositories.
- Add v6 Spektacular-backed design mode linking `hive-design`, dashboard approval, and `!runs design` to Spec/Plan run checkpoints with work-source design signal adapters.
- Complete v6 Spektacular design-mode work-source coverage with non-GitHub run admission, source-native artifact comments, and optional Jira/Linear status transitions.
- The admin MCP effective-configuration read (`config_effective_read`) now shows the values of the per-repository merge policy: the repositories on `auto_merge.squash_only` and `auto_merge.require_current_base`, and the path globs under each `auto_merge.human_merge_paths` repository, instead of only reporting them as set.
- Added hover help marks to the dashboard's GitHub API budget panel: "ETag hit rate" now explains that it is the share of cacheable REST GETs answered 304 Not Modified via a remembered ETag (free against the core rate limit, counted since process start), and "Core remaining" explains the hourly core limit, the bar's warn/critical colours, and the governor's conserve/critical behaviour when the budget runs low.
- Evidence cards: every panel now carries a server-computed letter grade (A+ … C-, or — for not enough data) and a one-sentence plain-English summary; dense stats and "what this does not show" move behind the ⓘ popover, and the CI gate card no longer breaks the type scale (#13204)
- Evidence "Outcome by author kind" card now records change failures per author kind: reverts (`reverted_14d`, from `reverted_by` links written when a merged PR's title or body names the original PR or commit — `Reverts #N`, `Revert "… (#N)"`, `This reverts commit <sha>` — via webhook, PR state or merged-PR backfill, with no new GitHub calls) and issue re-opens (`issue_reopened_14d`, stamped on the closing PR's bundle as `issue_reopens` when the claim ledger sees an issue it closed reopened within 14 days). `/api/evidence/summary` additively exposes `change_failures` and `change_failure_rate` = (reverts + re-opens) ÷ merged; the Outcome grade and plain summary include re-opens (#13241).
- Evidence outcome cards support explicit on/off control-window assignments with within-repository metrics and deltas withheld below 20 usable observations per arm; unassigned records remain separate. This is reporting groundwork only: dispatch scheduling and control collection are not yet enabled ([#13532](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13532)).
- The hub Evidence card gains an **Issue opens : PR merges** panel: hive-filed issues (audit-log `agent_issue_created` / `hive_issue_created`) ÷ hive-merged PRs (merged by this hive, or agent-authored — the Outcome by author kind set) per repository and fleet-wide over the selected window, read against the governor's cadence band instead of a flat 1:1 — surge/busy expects ≤ 1 (drain), quiet/idle expects 1–2 (bounded scouting), unknown expects parity ±25% — with a trailing-7-day sparkline over a rolling 30 days that should regress toward 1:1. Shipped as `issue_opens_pr_merges` on `/api/evidence/summary` and `cards["opens-merges"]`; thresholds are named constants in `pkg/evidence/opens_merges.go` (`src/docs/review-evidence.md`).
- Experiment Lab: the configuration dialog now ends with a **Data** section (snapshot / principle / experiment counts) and owner-only **Reset baseline**, **Clear knowledge** and **Reset everything** buttons backed by the new audited `POST /api/nous/reset` endpoint; deletions move data to `<nous_dir>/.trash/` first so a crash cannot half-delete the store (#12029).
- List Flue and Crustify / Wavefront in the public integration surfaces.
- New `pkg/forgestate` per-repo GitHub state cache (Phase 1 of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373), [#13374](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13374)): one in-process snapshot of open issues and PRs per repo, kept current by an ETag-conditional slow reconcile (a failed reconcile, such as a 403, keeps the last good snapshot and marks it stale instead of showing zero counts), webhook patches that re-fetch only the named item and upsert monotonically by `updated_at`/head SHA (closed and merged items leave at once, out-of-order deliveries settle correctly, delivery ids are kept for audit), and write-through of the hive's own label, comment, merge, close and claim mutations. It also adds a `forgestate_drift` metric, a startup gate that waits for every repo's first reconcile, freshness-bounded read-through for irreversible actions, and a per-minute `search` bucket budget. It is configured under a new `forgestate:` block (`enabled: false` by default) and is not wired to any reader yet, so enabling it changes no behaviour until the follow-up migrations land.
- forgestate: the governor's reconcile cadence now falls back from `eval_interval_webhook_s` to `eval_interval_s` automatically when webhooks degrade (no deliveries while GitHub activity continued, or deliveries failing verification) and returns only after two consecutive healthy windows; one INFO line each way (`webhooks degraded; polling cadence restored` / `webhooks healthy; webhook cadence engaged`), `/api/status.webhooks.mode` (`webhook` | `polling`) with `since`, `mode_reason` and `healthy_windows`. New `src/docs/webhooks.md` documents polling cadence vs webhook patch vs reconcile, the #13373 accuracy guarantees, every cadence key with its default, and the fallback (#13381).
- Add an opt-in, fail-closed GitHub `viewerCanUpdateBranch` lookup as groundwork for serialized-lane fork handling; existing merge and branch-update behavior is unchanged (#10890).
- OpenTelemetry spans and metrics for GitHub API spend and cache freshness ([#13380](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13380), Phase 3 of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)): every GitHub REST/GraphQL call gets a `github.request` span (`github.endpoint`, `github.repo`, `hive.caller`, `hive.pacing_class`, `github.cache_hit`, `github.ratelimit.remaining`/`bucket`, `github.shed`), the governor eval cycle gains `governor.stage_labels`, `governor.kick` and `governor.automerge` spans, and an OTLP/HTTP metrics pipeline exports `github.requests{caller,endpoint,status}`, `github.ratelimit.remaining{bucket}`, `github.secondary_limit_hits`, `forgestate.staleness_s{repo}`, `forgestate.drift{repo,kind}` and `webhook.event_to_patch_ms`. ForgeState reconcile now stretches its interval (2×/4×/8× below 20%/10%/5% core quota). Everything rides the existing `otel.enabled` + `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` switch and is off by default; see `operator-reference.md` § OpenTelemetry.
- `cmd/hive` boots against a sidecar `crux serve` when `CRUX_MODE=sidecar`: the sidecar client is wrapped so the Host observers (kick outcomes, pause transitions, relaunches, prompts, audits, conditions) are fed from the runtime's event stream, and hive serves its capabilities to the runtime over the hive callback endpoint (`$CRUX_HIVE_SOCKET`). The in-process path is unchanged and still the default.
- `hivectl hives hub add|list|show|remove` tracks hubs in a new optional `hubs:` key of `profiles.yml` and reads each hub's federation registry (`GET /api/hives`) to list its advertised Hives. `hub adopt` confirms and bulk-registers only missing Hives through the existing `hives add` path, `hub follow` stores a future-enrollment policy without changing current membership, and `hub refresh` reports additions/removals while retaining successful partial progress. No credentials are stored on hubs; redirects, error statuses and malformed registries report unavailability instead of empty results (#13174, #13175).
- Add the opt-in Claude Managed Agents self-hosted external backend prototype with relay capability gating, durable session reconciliation, and USD 25/day ledger metering.
- Hub My Hives: a dismissible "Your hive <name> is ready → Open your hive ↗" callout for owners explains that the hub only lists hives (the Guide, settings and GitHub App install live inside the hive), names any attention item that must be fixed there, and points at the row ⋯ menu; the hive-name link gains an ↗ glyph and tooltip and the ⋮ button a "Manage: permissions, pause, funding, delete…" hint. Dismissal is per user and hive in localStorage and re-arms when a new attention item appears.
- Auto-merge never merges a breaking-titled (`⚠️`/`⚠`) or `needs-owner-merge`-labelled PR: one shared `RequiresHumanMerge` predicate skips it in every lane and the merge train, the tracker parks it at 090 *Ready for human merge · human merge* ("breaking change — owner merges") with **Approve & merge as maintainer** as the lead action, and hive posts one writeback-gated comment saying it waits for a human. Configurable via `auto_merge.human_merge_title_prefixes` and `auto_merge.human_merge_labels`.
- Trusted integration candidates now compose real required CI jobs and bind read-only member-governance verification to signed exact-job receipts; execution remains opt-in and OFF by default, with protected-promotion qualification still required.
- Add independent default-OFF integration execution enrollment, versioned private candidate provenance and actual runner accounting, designated-executor authority, bounded preparation admission, and exact protected-prefix promotion guards without replacing normal review, trust, CI, hold, or native-queue authority.
- Add a default-disabled trusted integration-candidate materializer, create-only initial-dispatch ownership and isolated job-bound CI receipt workflows derived from read-only validation profiles; no execution controller, runtime activation or required CI/review replacement is enabled.
- Add default-off, explicitly scoped integration orchestration with durable change intents, separate candidate observations, workflow-job accounting, and bounded admission above the existing preparation and GitHub queue authorities.
- Add an isolated Integration-aware promotion protocol foundation with exact tested commit/tree and ordered-parent verification, journaled destination compare-and-swap, live-guard fencing and conservative ambiguous-result reconciliation; execution remains unwired and disabled, with producer, permissions and protection prerequisites documented.
- Add dashboard Settings controls and readiness/status reporting for the optional Jev smart classifier.
- Add an optional Jev typed-decision classifier backend for issue lane, tier, and run triage decisions, with keyword fallback and shadow-mode stats.
- Document the v6 Jev smart classifier prerequisites, settings/YAML enablement, cost, rollout, stats API, and troubleshooting.
- krun mode (`HIVE_CONTAINER_OCI_RUNTIME=krun`) now accepts interactive launches, so interactive-only backends such as `omp` can run in the microVM: the contributor container gets a TTY, the session is shown on the VM console, and the recipe prints `podman attach <container>` and the detach keys (Ctrl-P Ctrl-Q) instead of an `exec` command or tmux hint, because the krun handler refuses `podman exec`. Headless krun launches are unchanged, and krun still never falls back to a plain container, docker or local mode (#12202).
- Contributors running in krun mode (`HIVE_CONTAINER_OCI_RUNTIME=krun`) now report the display-only capability `isolation_class: microvm-krun` to the hub, shown on the Operations tab and never used for task selection or admission, and keep reporting the host's kernel in team metadata.
- **Tracker: "Let hive decide" for items parked at *Needs human decision*.** The *Decide…* submenu on a parked issue or PR row (and the selection bar's *Decide…* for a bulk run) now opens with **Let hive decide**: the hive makes the decision itself as the owner's delegate, under the owner's standing operating rules (`pkg/delegatedecision.PolicyText` — decisive, reversible, keep work moving; prefer contributor PRs over hive duplicates; approve small low-risk changes and trusted-author sentinel alerts with a "reviewed, intended" line; supersede offline contributors now; dedupe aggressively; secrets/PAT/org-permission items are owner-only; quarantine flaky tests; accept CI hygiene gates as ratchets and design proposals with explicit defaults; never auto-close review-backlog items), and records it exactly as a human decision is recorded — `/hive decision <text>` comment, park labels lifted, `triage/accepted`, queue approval on a released PR head — so the item leaves 085/045 without the owner. Every delegated comment carries `<!-- hive:delegated-decision by=<hive-id> policy=owner-delegate -->` and the Decisions log marks the row *delegated*, so delegated and human decisions can be told apart and counted. Rails: the delegate never merges, refuses items wearing `hold`, never grants membership/secrets/permissions (`needs-owner` + `hold` with the exact owner action instead), and only *recommends* on policy or scope changes to the hive itself (keeps 085). New endpoint `POST`/`GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/items/{number}/decide-delegated`; new setting `decisions.delegate.enabled` (default true) with a per-repo override. This release's decider is rules-first (the mechanically decidable rules above; the reversible default otherwise) — the LLM-backed decider for the rest is a follow-up.
- Inline the linked Linear issue (title, state, description, recent comments; capped and marked untrusted) into review kicks whose scope contract is a Linear issue, read hive-side so reviewers need no Linear token.
- Recognise configured Linear issue identifiers as review scope contracts.
- **Activity Monitor Matrix: bounded, scrub-drop line source behind `dashboard.matrix`** (#15934, part of #15862). When `dashboard.matrix` is enabled with an allowlist, the sentinel's existing patch fetch now feeds an in-memory source of pushed lines — no new GitHub calls, nothing written to disk. Only hive-identified authors on public, allowlisted repos are admitted; secret-shaped and generated paths are skipped before parsing; any line that `logscrub` would change, that already carries a redaction marker, that looks high-entropy or exceeds 160 runes is dropped rather than masked. Ingest is non-blocking (a full 64-slot channel drops and counts), with dedup per PR, 200 lines per head, a 2,000-line backlog and a per-minute rate cap. Default off: with the flag off no observer is registered and nothing is retained. No HTTP surface yet; the endpoint follows in #15935.
- Document Matrix's separate `hivecommonsmatrix` channel and add an inactive, silent streamer overlay with isolated deployment identity and zero replicas (#15937).
- Merge-hotspot advisor (`governor.hotspot_*`): the merge train's own PR file lists and rebase conflicts now feed a per-file score of how often concurrent PRs collide on the same file. Files above `hotspot_min_prs` / `hotspot_min_overlaps` in a `hotspot_window_days` window are reported on `GET /api/hotspots` (`hivectl governor hotspots`, `/api/status.hotspots`); a code file of at least `hotspot_min_lines` with two or more top-level symbol groups gets one `refactor: <path> is a merge hotspot — split into <N> units` issue (labels `agent/ci-maintainer`, `kind/cleanup`) through the writeback gate, deduped by `<!-- hive:hotspot file=<path> -->` and refiled no sooner than `hotspot_refile_days` after close. Docs are only ever recommended for a by-section split, generated files point at their source, and the ci-maintainer prompt gains a "Merge Hotspots" section describing the mechanical, no-behaviour-change split.
- Add merge-lane fork PR handling that gates branch updates on GitHub capability plus contributor base-sync and leaves one durable author comment when the author must update.
- Activity Monitor: a merge-train member's chip reads its place in the queue in ordinal words — "Merge queued · 1st", "Merge queued · 2nd · ~4m" (never the `front` / `queued-behind` slugs; hover "2nd of 6 in the merge queue · behind #15253 · ETA ~4m") — with a countdown to its estimated auto-merge turn that survives poll re-renders, the same words whether or not a merge sweep is evaluating it (the sweep is the spinning glyph and a "Checking now…" hover line), a hover that names what the head waits on (soak left, CI, a maintainer) and the estimate's basis, a Merge queue popover listing every train in merge order, a readable inline-SVG train icon on the train header chip ("merge train · 2 PRs · 1st: #15400"), the Merge queue column header and the 080 chevron, and a stall warning ("Merge queue stalled · head #15253 waiting for CI 3h", one activity-log line per train per hour) past `governor.merge_train_stall_warn_s` (default 3600). `/api/stage-tracker` `merge_train` gains `length`, `head_number`, `head_state`, `head_reason`, `head_since`, `eta_s`, `eta_at`, `eta_basis`, `late`, `stalled`, `stalled_s` (#15395).
- Merge queue: one PR per issue — when two open PRs declare the same `Fixes #N`, the sweep keeps one (a green head first, then the earlier-opened) and holds the other out of every train with gate state `duplicate-of:<n>` (chip "Duplicate of #15402 · needs a pick", `merge_gate.duplicate_of` / `duplicate_issue`, `needs-decision`); "Let hive decide" on either PR takes the existing supersede path (rule `one-pr-per-issue`: the held one closes as superseded with credit, the kept one is released) (#15395).
- Activity Monitor: the "Merge gate" column is now "Merge queue" everywhere a person reads it (header, hovers, legend, decision copy; ids, classes and JSON keys unchanged), and every merge-train state — the 1st in line included — lights that column even while the lane holds the head at 050/070 (hive's own #15400 lit CI / Review beside its 2nd-place sibling) (#15395).
- Automerge merge train: approved PRs whose changed files overlap are grouped per repo and base branch, and only one front per group (mergeable first, then oldest) merges per sweep pass, so parallel approvals no longer dirty each other; `auto_merge.merge_train.enabled` (default `true`) turns it off (#15141).
- mergelane: core of the serialized merge lane for `hive-serialized` repositories ([#10888](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10888), part of [#10884](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10884)). A new `pkg/mergelane` keeps a durable, fenced front record per (repo, target branch) under `/data/mergelane/`, orders pull requests oldest-eligible first, times out a stuck front (60 minutes by default, per-repo override, restarted on every update) and drives the front pull request through compare-based staleness detection, a merge update pinned to the evaluated head, required checks on the exact head (unknown or empty set means no merge), a live final re-check, a head-pinned merge and a post-merge parent check that alerts when the merge did not land on the validated tip. Every front entry and exit, update, merge and refusal is audited. The lane is not yet called by any merge path, so nothing changes for `direct` repositories.
- Added an operator page, `src/docs/monitoring.md`, covering Prometheus and Grafana monitoring of a hive: enabling the fail-closed `/metrics` endpoint with `HIVE_METRICS_ENABLED` and `HIVE_METRICS_TOKEN`, the metric families, alert runbook anchors, and a plain `scrape_config` without Prometheus Operator ([#15440](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15440)).
- Add a fail-closed monthly outcomes publication wrapper and reviewed-PR cadence for owner-supplied, sanitized evidence aggregates; deployment source access and monthly input remain explicit operator prerequisites.
- Automerge sweeps can enqueue eligible PRs into GitHub's native merge queue with the validated head pinned, report queue position and state, and withdraw Hive-enqueued entries only when the PR loses merge eligibility (a hold, a withdrawn or stale approval, changes requested, a paused or disabled repo, or a draft or closed PR) while preserving entries queued by people. The hand-off is opt-in per repo through `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.enabled` and `.repos` (default off; hives without queues see no change). On a queue-enabled base a `blocked` or `behind` PR is enqueued rather than reported `not-mergeable`; the `require_current_base` gate and the `behind` update-branch stay in force unless `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.skip_current_base_gate` is set. The `isMergeQueueEnabled` probe is cached per base branch for `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.probe_ttl` (default 30m) and the entry reconciliation runs only on opted-in repos. A mixed-authorship PR whose queue uses `SQUASH` parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` with the `merge-method` explanation, and the refusal is remembered per head for 30 minutes.
- Add native merge-group CI and an owned PR-evidence gate, opt-in external freshness-writer suppression, default-off scoped owner Settings controls, and a distinct Activity Tracker rail backed by bounded provider-neutral observations of actual GitHub queue entries, exact candidate CI, proven-or-unknown members and lifecycle receipts.
- Tracker, online-contributor and Knowledge sidebar count pills briefly show the actual signed increase or decrease on live updates, with directional amber feedback and a static reduced-motion alternative.
- Activity Monitor: hovering or focusing the *Needs human decision* chevron word or a lead *needs-human* / *triage needed* pill opens an in-app popover that says what the row is waiting on (the reviewer's own question when the hive has one, else the park reason in plain words, plus the blocker — "A reviewer requested changes on b0f5f80 — needs a new commit. Approving cannot override that."), offers the applicable actions as buttons (*Let hive decide* first, then Approve / Give direction / Close as superseded / Close as won't fix / Hold or Release; disabled ones grey with their reason) down the row context menu's code path, and names who asked and when; `GET /api/stage-tracker` rows carry the new `decision_needed` (`question`, `asked_by`, `since`, `blocker`, `blocker_reason`, `options[]`). Requested by @clubanderson ([#14994](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14994)).
- Settings → Features gains a "Nous / Experiment Lab" section exposing nous.dispatcher, nous.gate_poll_seconds, nous.fetch_allowlist and nous.artifact_repo.{repo,branch,path,sync_interval_seconds}, and the agent dialog exposes agents.<name>.engine; all are validated with the config package rules and found by the settings search (#12026).
- Add the reusable Hive `/ok-to-test` workflow and caller template so trusted same-repo bot/App workflow runs can be approved by a repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` without granting the Hive App Actions write.
- Onboarding problems the dashboard shows — GitHub App not installed / wrong installation / insufficient permissions / undelivered credentials, GHES base URL, project target, no projects, no agents — now carry a *New hive? Open the 🧭 Guide → step …* link that opens the Getting Started guide at the matching step; the Guide chip stays visible while any such problem is active, the guide's GitHub App step prints the concrete install URL for the configured GitHub host, and `GET /api/status` exposes the classification as `onboardingIssues[]` (plus `onboarding`/`guideStep` on system alerts and deep-health checks) (#15772).
- Activity monitor: a ✓ decision badge on every row you acted on from the dashboard — green once recorded, amber when the item is still at the same stage past the stuck window, red when the action failed — with a plain-words tooltip (what it is waiting on → what you chose, when → what the hive did next) and a **Decisions** filter (Awaiting my decision / I acted / Acted, still stuck). Actions are kept in a server-side ledger (`/data/operator-actions.json`), surface as `last_operator_action` on tracker rows and via `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/items/{number}`. Requested by @clubanderson.
- `hivectl evidence benchmark` and `src/scripts/outcome-benchmark.sh` compute a reproducible mediated-vs-unmediated outcome report (revert rate, change-failure, median time-to-merge, CI at merged head, changes-requested-before-merge, cost per merged PR; Wilson intervals, n < 10 not reported) with generated SVG charts under `src/docs/benchmarks/` and a `--readme` flag that rewrites the README's `<!-- outcomes:start/end -->` block, guarded by a drift test
- Hive now keeps each issue and PR's last your-turn ownership identity in its local record and writes an `ownership_transition` audit entry when it changes, from the status refresh only; a restart or the first refresh after deployment records nothing. An item that leaves the open list while it was your turn is recorded with the neutral reason "no longer in the open list (closed/merged/draft/exempt)".
- Human-merge-path holds now record their exact head without claiming pre-existing holds; a shared fail-closed release API validates App ownership and complete label history for later pin-only admission integration, with operator rollout prerequisites documented (#16269).
- Add validated per-repository `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` schema, changed-file patch evidence and a fail-closed pin-replacement syntax classifier as building blocks for #16242; merge-path exceptions are not yet enabled and existing human-merge protections remain unchanged.
- The `hive-merge` relay now honours the `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception, with the same checks as the automerge sweep plus an exact requested-head match; anything short of a proven pin-only change by a trusted author stays held (#16265).
- Enforce the `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception in the automerge sweep lanes and `/hive approve` (#16266): a PR by a listed trusted author whose complete diff is pin replacements on guarded paths is no longer held for a person. Any other changed file, including an unguarded changelog or doc, keeps the hold (#16326). Repos without an enabled entry are unchanged; the `hive-merge` relay enforces the same exception as of #16265.
- A pull request that waits on you now says how to answer it. While a PR at `stage/085-needs-decision` or `stage/070-fixing` is parked for your decision, or held by the review for a person, the hive status comment at the top of the PR carries a **Your move** section. It lists the `/hive` replies that answer it (`/hive approve`, `/hive decision approve <why>`, `/hive decision <what to change>`) and the GitHub review that does the same. The section is edited in place, so it sends no notification, and it is removed once the wait ends. Before this, such a PR only said "review and approve it" in prose.
- Show preparation owners and FIFO waiting positions in a visible train-style Activity Monitor rail, removing redundant preparation pills and the zero-train header summary while preserving real ready trains, PR stages, row sorting, pagination, and issue trees.
- `hivectl hives preset adopt --onboard` reviews and enrolls missing Hives and preset hub snapshots in one confirmed flow, reusing existing credentials and retaining successful enrollments on partial failure.
- Added an automated list-price refresh for the Cost panel: `go run ./internal/tools/pricetable` reconciles `src/pkg/tokens/pricing.go` with OpenRouter's public model catalogue (no vendor HTML scraped), rewrites only the rates that moved, bumps `priceTableDate`, and reports every change and every row it could not verify; the weekly `price-table-refresh` workflow turns a non-empty diff into a single `needs-human` PR on `bot/price-table-refresh`, and CI now fails when the table is more than 60 days old so a stalled refresh is noticed. See the "Price table refresh" section of `src/docs/token-tracking.md`.
- Once its `hive:recheck-after` deadline passes, a `blocked` ops-tracking soak checklist on the hive's own project gets one soak-evidence comment (stable-channel hives' heartbeat, restart loops and candidate digest/SHA, read from the hub or the spoke's own `/api/version`), the checklist lines that evidence proves are ticked, and `<!-- hive:recheck-done -->` stops repeats; the issue stays open and `blocked` for a maintainer to close (#13311).
- Red-main circuit breaker (#13630): when a required check has been red on a repo's default branch for longer than `red_main_threshold` (default `6h`, configurable per repo under `project.repo_policies`), PRs that fix main (the `fixes-main` label, `Fixes` on the `[shared-ci]` tracking issue, or files overlapping the failing check) rank first in the review queue, `hive-open-pr` refuses new PRs in that repo with a message naming the check and the fix PR (existing PRs and issue filing are unaffected), and the repo card shows "main red since <time> on <check>; fix: #N waiting on <who>". A check counts as green only once a run on the tip completes green, so pushes to a red branch do not restart the clock, and a PR naming a just-filed `[shared-ci]` tracking issue opens without waiting for the next sweep. Everything lifts automatically once main is green.
- The hub accepts a contributor's **opt-in** relay audit attestation: an `audit_share` on `task_complete` / `task_failed` (rows up to the shared level, clamped to the relay's capture level) writes a `relay_task_attested` audit row cross-referencing the contributor's local record. At `commands`+ the hub stores the shared command rows in `/data/contrib-audit/<login>/<task>.jsonl` (0600, 90-day retention) rather than the 500-entry audit ring. The new `hub.contribute_audit_share_request` (default empty) lets a hive *request* a level, advertised on `auth_ok` (`audit_share_requested`) and on `/contribute` before setup. Admission never depends on it ([#13458](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13458), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- `GET /api/audit?contributor=<login>` narrows the Audit Log to one contributor's rows (same 200-entry cap and role gate; combines with `?sensitive=1`), the Audit Log gains a `relay_` quick-filter chip beside the sensitive toggle, and the contribute page's Operations tab gains a read-only "Your assignments" card listing the caller's own `relay_*` audit rows ([#13454](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13454), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- The hub now records the contributor relay's lifecycle in the existing `/data/audit.jsonl` as `relay_*` rows — `relay_connected`, `relay_rejected`, `relay_disconnected`, `relay_task_assigned`, `relay_task_accepted`, `relay_task_declined`, `relay_token_minted`, `relay_task_completed`, `relay_task_failed`, `relay_task_revoked` and `relay_task_abandoned` (plus the reserved `relay_mcp_lease_issued` / `relay_mcp_lease_revoked`) — attributed to the contributor's GitHub login and session, with the task's repository and issue/PR number. Rows are written from frames the hub already receives, so an unmodified relay needs no change; progress and heartbeat frames are not audited and no token is ever written. `relay_token_minted` (which carries the `installation` id) and `relay_task_revoked` are sensitive actions and raise `sensitive_24h` on hives with active contributors; `relay_connected` is not sensitive and omits the remote address. Documented in `audit-log.md` and `contributor-relay.md` ([#13453](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13453), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- Delegated relay work is now covered by the audit substrate: a new `relay_audit_coverage` compliance posture check passes when the hub wrote at least one `relay_*` audit row in the last 24h or no relay connected, fails when relays connected without any row, and is mapped to SOC 2 CC7.2 (with notes on ISO A.8.15 and FedRAMP AU-2) ([#13455](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13455)).
- The contributor relay now keeps a leveled local audit stream (`off`, `lifecycle` by default, `commands`, `reasoning`) in `relay-activity.jsonl`: lifecycle events, GitHub-touching `gh`/`git` commands captured by a pane-only `PATH` shim, and the assistant turn behind each command, all redacted before they are written and never uploaded. `hivectl hives set <name> --audit-level` chooses the level per hive and `hivectl hives audit` reads it, with `--clear --level reasoning` removing only the stored reasons.
