Every remaining report (`acmm-shortfall` included) now carries the hive name, spoke link, owners, repos and `Affected hives` block and uses the self-report label set; an ACMM shortfall about a component this hive already has an open self-report for posts a short roll-up comment on that issue instead of filing its own. The hub relay's label-rejection retry falls back to the core self-report labels, never to none.
- The advisory issue lookup reads the ForgeState cache when a store is bound (`forgestate.enabled`): a memoized advisory issue costs zero GitHub calls on a healthy cycle, a cache miss one targeted GET, and the search/list path runs only when the cache cannot answer. The review-request watcher is event-driven: request-dir notifications and `issue_comment`/`pull_request_review`/`pull_request_review_comment`/`issues` label deliveries wake it, the unprompted scan is a 5-minute reconcile while webhooks are healthy, and the 10 s poll returns only when webhooks are degraded. A `--revise` request for a repo outside `review.revise_repos` is denied once instead of retried every tick (#13252).
- The automerge sweep lanes (self-authored, trusted-author, contributor lane) share one cached open-PR set from the ForgeState cache and run event-driven when `forgestate.enabled` is on ([#13377](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13377), part of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)): no `/pulls` list per 10 s tick, a `check_suite`/`check_run`/`status`/`pull_request_review`/`pull_request` webhook triggers a pass for the affected PR only, a 5-minute floor pass covers the no-events case, and every merge first re-reads the PR through the cache with a 60 s freshness bound; a stale snapshot never merges. Review gate, required checks and hold labels are unchanged, and the legacy listing ticker remains the default.
- Overview open issue / PR totals are read from the ForgeState cache (`pkg/forgestate`) when it is ready, and the merged-PR / closed-issue counts behind cost-per-PR and cost-per-issue are incremented from `pull_request closed` (merged) and `issues closed` webhook events and reconciled against GitHub search once an hour (`forgestate.CountsReconcileInterval`) instead of on every 5-minute collection ([#13376](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13376), Phase 2b of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)). A rate-limited or failed reconcile keeps the last good counts: `/api/status` carries `staleSince` and per-repo `countsStale` / `countsStaleSince`, `/api/cost` carries `count_stale_since` / `count_source`, and the Overview tiles and cost labels show "stale since <t>" rather than zeros.
- With `forgestate.enabled: true` the governor work source reads each repo's open issues and PRs from the per-repo ForgeState cache instead of listing GitHub every cycle ([#13375](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13375), Phase 2a of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)): the cache's reconcile is the only full list, webhook wakes decide from the cached snapshot without a list call, the first decision pass waits for the first successful reconcile of every repo, a repo whose reconcile failed is served last-good and marked stale, every kick ref is held to the same 60 s freshness bound as close/merge (one targeted `GET` when older, withheld when stale), and the hive's own label, close and merge writes plus webhook/confirmation single-item reads are fed straight into the cache.
- The sentinel now evaluates a PR as soon as a `pull_request` opened/synchronize/reopened webhook names it (reading only that PR and its files), and its full sweep is a 15-minute reconcile cadence that enumerates open PRs from the ForgeState cache instead of listing each repo. The GitHub Projects v2 work source lists its board on the same reconcile cadence rather than every eval cycle and applies `projects_v2_item` webhook deliveries as targeted patches; the spoke webhook receiver accepts and routes that event (#13379).
- hive-hosted-matrix stream overlay opens the dashboard with `view=reader` instead of the deprecated `view=matrix` alias (#16612).
- Changed the dashboard's Hive vs human trend to show counts per bucket by default, with axes and a hover title per bucket. A View dropdown also offers the hive share over a trailing window and the original 100% share area.
- Activity Monitor: the muted pill a PR wears while the hive's GitHub App is missing a permission now reads "hive bot lacks permission" instead of "unauthorized", and its tooltip, the row hover line, the Needs-attention chip title, the needs-human tip, the human-merge gate word and the decision popover say the same — nobody did anything illegitimate, the App installation lacks one permission (hivecommons/hive#16639). The `hive:unauthorized` label, comment marker and API fields are unchanged.
- Hive-authored superseding PRs (`Supersedes #N`, opened by the hive App) now auto-merge with no operator decision: a reviewer `requires_human` — security-sensitive included — is routed to the fixer instead of parking at `stage/085`, and only an unacknowledged sentinel finding, a hold, exhausted fix attempts, red CI after fixes or an unresolvable base conflict park it, each named in the 085 caption. New knob `auto_merge.hive_superseding.auto_merge` (default `true`).
- The hub's GitHub webhook relay now fans out to every enrolled hive that tracks the delivery's repository (and has a dashboard URL) instead of only the first match, so additional hives on the same repo no longer fall back to polling. One log line is emitted per relay target; hives without a dashboard URL are skipped and counted. (#13202)
- Hive activity monitor: every `090 Ready for human merge` row and its tooltip now say why a person must merge (`· workflow files`, `· untrusted author`, `· branch protection`, `· auto-merge off`, `· unauthorized`, … falling back to `· policy`), derived from the stage record's lane reason; nested PR sub-rows and the needs-attention headline carry the same (#14658)
- Refreshed the CA trust bundle in the spoke, contributor, hub, CI-runner and OSS-scanner images: two Mozilla roots withdrawn by the root programs (emSign ECC Root CA - G3, Comodo AAA Services root) are now distrusted at build time, and Node-based CLIs in the spoke and contributor images verify against the system store via `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca`. The image build now asserts the test chains are rejected.
- Label the dashboard Inception entry as Inception (spektacular) and clarify its Spektacular-powered L1 flow.
- Issue-side comment churn is cut by editing in place instead of re-posting ([#16433](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16433)): `hive:claim` / `hive:release` transitions now maintain one per-issue claim-ledger comment (`<!-- hive:issue-claim-ledger -->`, current state plus the last 8 transitions; `github.notifications.claim_ledger`, default on, `false` restores one comment per transition) that every existing claim reader still parses; a PR re-entering a needs-decision stage has its entry comment rewritten with an `Updated <ts>` line; a new push rewrites the hive's existing `hive-sentinel` comment for the new head; and in quiet mode a reviewer-lane review that narrates "no findings" with an approving, finding-free verdict is recorded and folded into the `hive:status` comment instead of being submitted as a review.
- Keep the optional Jev smart classifier advisory-only, with disagreement tracking and human-approved deterministic rule suggestions instead of model-enforced routing.
- ACMM L6 is now labelled **Autonomous** rather than "Fully Autonomous" everywhere operators see it — the dashboard header pill (`L6 · Autonomous`), the maturity-level dialog, the hub's level picker and ACMM pages, the `level-6` pack name, advisor criteria text, the tool-approval desk rationale, and the docs. L6 still parks items for human decisions, honours `hold`, cannot grant secrets, org membership, or workflow pushes, and keeps an owner in the loop, so "fully" overstated what the level does. The ladder is otherwise unchanged (L1 Inception → L5 Semi-Autonomous → L6 Autonomous); the numeric `acmm_level: 6` config value and the pack filename `level-6.yaml` are untouched, so no configuration changes are needed.
- Added an authoritative operator reference for Hive labels and control signals, replacing the short issue-label page and documenting how holds, approvals, contributor skips, planning labels, and dashboard bands affect work selection.
- `src/docs/landscape.md` is refreshed against the compared projects' current public docs (dated 2026-10-23), gains **New since August 2026**, **Agent isolation** and **Work sources** sections, and joins the fixed file list of `src/scripts/check-security-docs-readability.sh`, so the positioning page must also stay at Flesch-Kincaid grade 11 or below.
- Lane policies now check for an existing gate or written policy before filing a finding class, and propose the missing gate instead of filing a third same-class finding ([#13427](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13427), [#13428](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13428)).
- Tracker 090 *Ready for human merge*: the lead action is now **Approve and let hive merge** (`queue-merge`) — hive merges on its next tick once CI is green, soak and self-merge ban apply; **Merge now as maintainer** (`merge-now`, and its *Rebase, then merge as maintainer* variant) is secondary. The automerge sweep now honours an operator's recorded queue-merge approval on an untrusted-author PR and attributes the merge to that operator. On the hive's own PR the App no longer tries to review itself (GitHub 422 "Can not approve your own pull request"): the queue note is a comment, the operator's approval is recorded in the hive's store as the plain Approve records it, and the self-authored lane merges on it; the review-request watcher downgrades such a refused review to a COMMENT instead of retrying.
- logscrub: `ScrubString` and the contributor relay now mask the same api-key, Slack/Discord webhook, Slack token and Basic-auth shapes on v5 as on v6 ([#16470](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/16470)).
- Activity Monitor: the "Merged" ledger pill now rolls its numbers like a mileage odometer when they rise (per digit, ≈0.9 s ease-out; the total and the today / this week figures alike), sets them outright on the first draw, on a fall such as the midnight reset or under reduced motion, and keeps its width while rolling; the merge glyph's flight slowed from 0.9 s to 2 s on an ease-out, with the merged row pinned 3.5 s so it outlasts the landing.
- The dashboard's 🙋 Needs human facet now matches by pattern (`needs-human*`, `*needs-decision`, `*needs-author`) as well as by name, so new stages and labels no longer silently fall out of it; the *All labels* dialog shows a "Needs human covers N labels" group listing exactly which labels the facet selects. ([#13780](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13780))
- Replace browser-native hub and spoke dialogs with in-app modals/toasts and add ratchet tests to keep them out.
- Make the `/ok-to-test` workflow template (and `hivectl ok-to-test-template`, now with `--app-login` defaulting to the hive's App login) fully self-contained with the approval logic inlined — no `uses: hivecommons/hive/...` reference — so it works under restrictive Actions policies and on GHES; the 085 stage entry now embeds that rendered workflow when held runs outlive the `/ok-to-test` grace.
- Contributor-lane auto-merge: a hive owner / trusted merger's explicit approval on the current head — a GitHub `APPROVED` review on that commit, or a dashboard `/hive decision approve` bound to it — now releases the `contributor-lane:workflow-path` fence, so the hive merges an approved PR editing `.github/workflows/**` / `.github/actions/**` itself instead of parking it at `stage/090-ready-for-human-merge` (`auto_merge.contributor_lane.owner_approval_releases_workflow_fence`, default on). Approval on an older head does not count; a merge refused for want of the App's `workflows: write` marks the PR `hive:unauthorized` (`merge-workflow-path`) and parks the approved head at 090 as before. The 085 note for an unapproved workflow-path PR now reads "awaiting owner approval" (#14664).
- Hive activity monitor: `sentinel`, `needs human`, `needs human decision` and merge-time `unauthorized` pills are held back (payload `deferred_modifiers`) until the pull request reaches the merge gate (stage/080+), and do not count under *Needs attention* before then; `hold`, `draft`, `stalled`, `regressed` and an `unauthorized` on held workflow runs always show.
- Activity Monitor: a lit "PR in progress" chevron names who works the PR with their kind icon — `PR in progress · @login` plus the hive / clanker / person glyph, the way "Waiting for @login" does (hivecommons/hive#16770); the name truncates with the copy, the tooltip holds the full text, and nobody known keeps the bare word.
- Refreshed the model list-price table from OpenRouter (29 rows moved; list prices as of 2026-10-22): GPT-5.2/5.4/5.4-mini/5.5, the GPT-5.6 sol/terra/luna codex variants and GPT-5.3-codex now carry OpenAI's current per-family rates instead of a flat $1.25/$10; Claude Opus 4.1 ($15/$75), Sonnet 5 ($2/$10) and the Fable 5.1 / Sonnet 5.5 cache-read rates follow Anthropic's published figures; Gemini 2.5/3.5/3.6/3.7 Flash, Grok 4.5, Kimi K3 / K2.7-code, Llama 3.3 70B and DeepSeek chat follow their providers' current list prices. The Cost panel estimate uses the new rates from this release on.
- Refreshed the model list-price table from OpenRouter (2 rows moved; list prices as of 2026-10-26); the Cost panel estimate now uses the new rates.
- Refreshed the Kimi K3 and K2.7 Code list-price estimates from Kimi's direct API pricing as of 2026-11-02, using K3's default 5-minute cache-write rate; all other model rates remain unchanged.
- **Prior-art gate searches docs and code locally across every registered repo** — the `docs` and `code` prior-art sources now query a `pkg/codeindex` snapshot of each `project.repos` checkout under `checkouts_dir` instead of GitHub code search, so findings cover all repos without spending the code-search quota, and a missing, dirty or partly indexed checkout is called out in the gate comment when a comment is posted ("checkout missing/partial for <repo>", repo slug only, no host paths), and recorded in the audit log (`prior-art-gate-coverage-gap`) otherwise, rather than read as no prior art; coverage is as of the local checkout, not origin (#13878). Reports built while the index is still building are not cached, and the first index build starts at startup.
- Issues filed through `hive-open-issue` now follow the prior-art filing verdict: a high-confidence match is refused (naming the existing item) and recorded as a knowledge bead, and a medium match must carry a "Gap vs existing" section and gets the findings attached; each refusal is audited as `agent_issue_prior_art_refused`; off with `runs.triage.prior_art.enabled: false` ([#13879](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13879)).
- Show the dashboard shell before downloading its cacheable application script, prioritize the selected and visible panels, limit background refresh concurrency, and progressively render the latest live data without waiting for every panel before restoring navigation.
- `prompt_source` kick templates fetched from GitHub are now capped at 96 KiB by default (`promptsrc.DefaultMaxPromptBytes`, was 64 KiB; `HIVE_PROMPT_SOURCE_MAX_BYTES` still overrides it). The largest shipped policy, `src/policies/scanner-automerge.md`, grew past 32 KiB with the v5 forward-merge (#12832), which left the old cap with less than the 2x headroom `TestShippedTemplatesFitUnderCap` pins. Over-cap bodies are still rejected whole, never truncated.
- Activity Monitor: every PR whose only remaining step is the merge itself now reads one chevron word, **Queued for merge**, with a short qualifier after the dot saying why it has not merged yet — *· next pass in 42s*, *· checking now*, *· soak 12m left*, *· 2nd of 3* (merge train), *· next pass* (Approve / Let hive decide), *· after CI* (Approve and let hive merge while checks run, or a merge call refused for unreported checks), *· needs rebase* (head moved under the merge call), *· branch protection pending*. Three adjacent approved rows on hive's own tracker read *Ready for auto merge …*, *Approved · hive will…* and *Approved · merge queu…*; the tooltip keeps the full explanation. *Soaking*, *Merging*, *Rebasing*, *Needs human decision* and a *Merge failed* a person must fix stay their own words (hivecommons/hive#16653).
- The weekly owner advice "Clear the human gate on PRs" and "Unblock the human queue" are readable. They no longer say only "59 of 94 open PRs are your turn (1 INSPECT, 24 DECIDE, 34 REVIEW)" followed by five items whose notes could run to a paragraph. Each now gives the count waiting on a person, **why they wait** (grouped by reason in plain words, with where they sit, such as "24 parked until a maintainer decides (20 in utah-packages, 3 in utah, 1 in testsuite)"), a **How to help** line for the largest groups, and one short line per listed item. The raw signals moved to the end of the digest entry and fold away on the dashboard card. The API adds `why` and `help` to those recommendations.
- `hivectl evidence benchmark` now also draws the README outcome cards as 2× PNGs with an embedded font (flat colours, no glow), gains `--from-json` to re-render committed assets without the evidence tree, and the README embeds the PNGs so the cards look the same in every browser.
- The README and its outcome cards are written as short full sentences in plain speech, with the numbers inside the sentences. A test now rejects semicolons and label lines in the README prose and card text.
- README rewritten around plain-language evidence cards: `hivectl evidence benchmark` now also renders dark/light full-width SVG cards (accuracy, a before/after scenario from one real pull request, prompt injection, cost, "also" strip, how-it-works ladder) gated by `--readme-min-base` (default 200), takes `--stories` and `--red-team` inputs, and the generated README block lists Accuracy / Security / Cost / Also with no statistical vocabulary; the detailed charts and intervals stay in `src/docs/benchmarks/`, and the former README overview moved to `src/docs/what-is-hive.md`.
- Refresh the README around trust, productivity, efficiency, governance and auditability, with sourced charts and supported work tools. Benchmark regeneration no longer rewrites the root README; redraw its graphics with `node docs/readme/render-charts.mjs`.
- The review swarm now reviews **every open PR regardless of author** — hive agent, human, clanker at either trust tier, dependabot and any other bot — whenever PR review is on (`review.require_approval` + `review.fan_out`); the only switch is the review feature itself. `review.all_authors` is a deprecated no-op (still accepted, logged once). The automerge review gate now also covers the `trusted-bot` and `trusted-author` lanes, so a human's PR waits for the swarm verdict the same way the App's own does; previously human PRs merged through the trusted-author tier with zero swarm reviews ([#12974](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12974)).
- A reviewer's scope / follow-up question on a hive-authored PR with CI green and no unresolved finding no longer parks the PR at 085 "Needs human decision": the dashboard classifies the ask and runs the existing *Let hive decide* pipeline itself (approve → merge queue plus a `follow-up:` issue; direction → fixer; owner-only → park with the recommendation), once per head, while policy sign-off asks (workflow edits from forks, OWNERS / secrets / permissions, auto-merge config, sentinel) stay a person's. Off switch `governor.review.auto_decide_questions`; counter `review_questions_autodecided_1h` on `/api/status`.
- The RFC notice poll now remembers pull requests found not to be RFCs by head SHA, so unrelated busy PRs no longer have their files listed on every poll ([#15960](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15960)).
- Scanner policies now forbid running tests, builds or linters locally in any language (`go test`, `npm run build`, `pytest`, …), not just the npm/tsc commands; CI validates and agents read `gh pr checks` (#9416).
- Security docs rot pass: stale "tracked in" citations to closed issues (#2804, #6685, #9586) now say what landed or point at the live successor, every page in the set carries a `Last reviewed:` date, and a new CI guard `src/scripts/check-security-docs-rot.sh` (in the Docs Link Check workflow) fails when that date is older than 120 days or a tracking sentence cites a closed issue.
- The security documentation set (`security-model.md`, `security-threat-model.md`, `security-response.md`, `securing-your-hive.md`, `ioscan.md`, `ioscan-red-team.md`, `security-self-assessment.md`) is rewritten in plain language for a non-expert reader: 60% shorter overall, every page at Flesch-Kincaid grade 11 or below, process notes and `path:line` citations dropped, and factual drift fixed (responder roster, escalation path, SBOM statement, stale v4 header). A new CI guard, `src/scripts/check-security-docs-readability.sh`, runs in the Docs Link Check workflow and fails any of these pages, or `SECURITY.md`, that drifts above grade 11.
- Self-authored (Hive-authored) PR decision questions now escalate to `stage/085-needs-decision` only when they match a named risk class (`review.DecisionRiskClasses`: permissions/credentials, security, sensitive paths, data loss/irreversible, merge/trust policy, external side effects, licensing/legal, unverifiable) or the reviewer marks `<!-- hive-decision-risk: high -->`; every other question is resolved by policy and recorded as an advisory reason, replacing the narrow non-risk allowlist that parked green agent PRs (#13020) whose linked issue had already answered the question. The reviewer template now tells the swarm to cite the linked issue/spec (`per #<issue>: …`) instead of re-asking.
- The dashboard sidebar now reads "Experiment Lab (nous)" and "Inception (spektacular)" so the engine behind each section is visible from the left menu; the section card titles follow the same wording.
- The stage engine now treats a covering PR closing (040→010/030/020) and claim/start-marker reshuffles (030→020) as expected issue transitions instead of anomalies.
- Stage labels now flow through a single `StageWriter` (`pkg/github/stage_writer.go`): the automerge `ApplyStageLabels` sweep and the issue `SyncIssueStageLabels` sweep build `stageengine.Facts` and reconcile through `stageengine.Reconciler.ReconcileBatch` (default shadow mode, byte-identical labels). An AST admission test forbids direct `stage/*` add/remove calls outside the writer, with a temporary allow-list for the relay/claim/ledger paths. Part of #12999.
- Out-of-cycle stage writers (claim relay and release, in-progress start mark, PR-claim sync, decision parking and `/hive approve`/`/hive decision` un-park, dashboard contributor claims and verdict settle) now submit facts to the central stage engine (`stageengine.FactSink`) instead of writing `stage/*` labels directly; the resulting labels are unchanged, and a lapsed claim, lifted park or closed PR re-stages the issue immediately rather than a cycle later ([#13009](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13009), part of [#12999](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12999)).
- Task MCP reads the dashboard token from the Authorization header only and no longer writes launch connections into operator config; comment-relay markers and Actions dispatch IDs are checked against GitHub; standby dispatch honours `standby.enabled` and the private-repo setting; refs-only prompts keep policy checks and PR annotations; run detail events and Admin MCP output and pending confirmations are scrubbed and bounded.
- Hive activity monitor: rows order attention-first within each column — rows a person must act on now (a shown pill or a human-gated stage) first, plain rows next, `hold` / `draft` / closed-issue-anchored rows last — for the *Furthest along* and *Longest waiting* sorts and for the PR sub-rows under an issue; the direction arrow flips the age order but never the tier, and the `GET /api/stage-tracker` payload is pre-sorted the same way so chat `/prs` and the hub agree.
- Hive activity monitor: hover text in a tracker row now appears only on the `#N` link (which carries the row tooltip), the covering-PR link, the title and the lit chevron (stage plus whose move it is); passed and upcoming chevrons, the kind, author and mover icons, chips and the `since` column no longer show tooltips.
- Stage Tracker: soaking rows now say what the reader cares about — **Soaking · 4m left**, **Soaking · complete** once the window has run out, **Mergeable · merging now** when the lane's pass is on the soaked head — instead of the lane's internal "merge sweep" name, and the 095 caption ages the soak clock from the lane's last read instead of pinning "0s left at the last sweep" on a row still called soaking. (hivecommons/hive#15575)
- Hive activity monitor: every movement animation now runs flash → move → land — the chevron an item is leaving pulses twice before the chosen effect travels and the new chevron lands lit (one soft flash then a crossfade under `prefers-reduced-motion`); flash timing is tokenised as `--ham-move-flash-*`.
- Activity Monitor: a PR nested under its issue now draws its header on one line — connector, author icon, number, title, lineage chip and base-branch pill side by side with the title ellipsizing (full title on hover) — instead of stacking the connector, the title and the pill on three lines; issue titles and the top-level PR header ellipsize the same way.
- Activity Monitor merge zap re-voiced as a real bug-zapper arc: a high-voltage snap followed by a sputtering 120 Hz mains sizzle that dies out over ~0.45 s, high-passed at 700 Hz, replacing the swept-bandpass crackle and thunk.
- Forward-merge the latest v5 fixes and operator controls into v6 while preserving its Crux runtime boundary and split configuration layout.
- Forward-merge the latest v5 controller, Matrix, integration-orchestration, notification, and CI improvements into v6 while retaining its split configuration, Crux runtime boundary, serialized merge lanes, and dashboard controls.
- Documented three known gaps ahead of v6 promotion directly in the roadmap: the missing v6 release/GA workflow path (#9154), the un-triaged shipped-surface bug backlog (#9227, #9245), and the resulting PR merge-conflict pileup (#9319), so the published roadmap no longer reads as more finished than the branch is.
- The Activity Monitor's "waiting on" chip now draws who a row waits on instead of spelling it out: a human owner reads `waiting on [person] @login` with the stage chevrons' person glyph and no "(human · no clanker)" qualifier; a contributor's hive reads `waiting on [robot ●] @login` with the clanker's robot head and the online / offline / unknown dot beside it. The hover title says the rest — `Waiting on @zoe (human) — waiting for a human reply` / `Waiting on @hanthor's hive (clanker · offline 26h) — hive will adopt at …` ([#15227](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15227)).
- Getting Started checklist: plain-language "what Hive is" intro matching the docs, current method list (codex, goose, agy, omp, bob; openrouter, watsonx gateways), ACMM spelled out, Inception and Experiment Lab added to "More to explore", and docs links moved from the legacy docs.kubestellar.io domain and the v4 branch to docs.hivecommons.dev / v5.
- Boot and live-rewire wiring of the Project Inception stage observer now goes through the planning-engine registry selected by `runs.engine` ([#10356](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10356), part of [#10293](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10293)). With `runs.engine` unset and `runs.spektacular.enabled: true` the probe, status card, stage runner and hub executor install are unchanged; `/api/status`'s `spektacular` block additionally reports the selected `engine` name. If a dashboard edit live-rewires to an unknown engine, Hive logs the error and removes the stage runner instead of falling back to another engine.
- Adoption close-first now asks the write-back gate before it closes, labels or reopens a contributor's original PR ([#15272](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15272)). These writes land on a PR the hive did not author, but they were only counted in the direct-write ratchet baseline, so they ignored a repo pause, the per-repo mode and the `contributor_adopt` kind policy (default L6 + opt-in label). When the gate refuses, the original stays open and closes when the hive's copy merges, and the refusal shows up in the write-back drill-down. A reopen that is due waits for the next poll, for example until an operator lifts a pause; a refusal for any other reason (the kind policy changed after the hive closed the PR) is logged at warn, because it leaves a hive-closed PR shut until a person reopens it. The ratchet baseline drops `automerge_adoption_close_first.go` (7 → 0).

### Fixed

- A 045 park now offers `/hive approve` when its options are written as plain list items (`- A: …`), and lane policies ask every 045 park to name a recommended option. Before, the ci-maintainer parked a governance A/B/C on Danathar/goodreads-mcp#432 with `- A:` lines and no recommendation. The "What to reply" notice read no options there (it knew only `Option A:` and `**A.**`), so it took the `--needs-decision` comment for an owner-only step and offered `/hive done` and `/hive decision` but no `/hive approve`. The notice now reads options on `-`, `*` and `+` list items and headings (a prose `A: yes` line still is not one), so a marked park that lists options is a choice again. The 045 rule in all 20 lane policies asks for `Option A:` lines and a `Recommended: <letter>, because <reason>` line, or `Recommended (owner confirms): …` where governance rules forbid the hive choosing.
- `stage/085-needs-decision` notes no longer contradict each other on a PR that edits CI workflow files (projectbluefin/testsuite#1037): when a trusted merger's approval releases the `contributor-lane:workflow-path` fence ([#14664](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14664)), the entry comment's **What to do** asks for that GitHub **Approve** review instead of saying no approval helps, and still lists the sentinel alert and hold labels to clear; when the lane never merges the head unattended (tests removed, human-merge path, or a workflow fence the approval cannot release), the sign-off attribution and adoption-stalled notes offer only the by-hand merge with a merge commit and name the rule, and an open sentinel alert is named in them too.
- **A PR parked at `stage/085-needs-decision` for a stalled adoption is no longer left without its note.** The escalation marked the head noted before posting, so when GitHub answered the `<!-- hive:adoption-stalled … -->` (or workflow-path refusal, or unadoptable-fork) note with a 500 the PR sat at 085 with no comment on that head ever (projectbluefin/utah-packages#650, #652). The note is now recorded only once posted and is retried on later sweeps; it posts once per head and reason, so a different blocker on the same head (a check failure, then the hive's own sign-off attribution) gets its own note while the same one flapping back stays silent. A lane that errored on an approved head (080 at role rank) no longer drops an active escalation for a pass, which flipped projectbluefin/utah#919 085 → 080 → 085 on one head. Stage records from the previous build are read as already noted for their head, so the upgrade reposts nothing.
- Fix the stdio `hive-admin-mcp` server returning "unsupported admin MCP read tool" for every `issues_by_band` / `prs_by_band` call by sharing the dashboard's band-read path and result post-processing through `pkg/adminmcp`.
- Fix admin MCP `issues_by_band`/`prs_by_band` `band` argument always returning zero rows because rows carried the Overview display label instead of the band key (#10018).
- fix(dashboard): cap baseline_pct and make by_agent cost additive with total_usd (#10047)
- Campaign Release now returns an explicit conflict for run-backed Spektacular campaigns instead of revoking the contributor's stage lease and making the run disappear; Inception campaign leases can still be released.
- campaigns: release no longer 409s against a Spektacular run's synthetic stage-lease identity (#10059)
- Preserve exact Spektacular run IDs when revising campaigns, preventing phantom rows and slug collisions while keeping artifact-name translation confined to CLI resume commands; releasing a revise lease now leaves the live stage lease intact. Existing archives retain their stored IDs, so historical slug-based revisions may appear as separate campaign rows rather than merging into the live run.
- Owners can restart an escalated run's current stage or terminally abandon a run; persisted retirement prevents automatic design and run triage from recreating it after a restart, and `triage_fix` retirement now also suppresses automatic design admission.
- spektacular: the real-CLI smoke against the pinned Spektacular binary now also runs on pull requests that touch `src/pkg/spektacular/`, the contributor Dockerfile's pinned version, or the workflow itself, so a change that only the in-tree fake CLI agrees with can no longer merge green ([#10074](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10074)).
- Spektacular test stubs no longer emit `artifact_id`, matching the pinned 0.22.0 CLI (#10074).
- spektacular: hub-executor infrastructure failures before the agent launches (claim, token mint, clone/fetch/worktree, `spektacular init`) now back off and retry the same generation instead of spending the stage budget and escalating every queued run during a short outage; the post-exit `status` check gets its own bound after the stage deadline so a final document written at the timeout is not failed; a settlement that fails to persist is retried each tick instead of leaving the run held until restart; finished runs' `.executor.lock` and empty run directories are swept; and run admission and the executor reject a `repo` with `..`, empty or absolute segments that would escape the workspace (#10077, #10110, #10108, #10111, #10080)
- Make the shared Jam store (`campaign-jam.json`) write crash-durable: the temp file is now fsynced before it is renamed over the store, and the directory after, so a power loss can no longer leave a zero-length store that fails every campaign's Jam. Each write uses a unique temp file that is removed on any failure, instead of a fixed `campaign-jam.json.tmp` that a failed write could leave behind (#10083).
- Fix the shared Jam store (`campaign-jam.json`): writes for a campaign id the hive does not know now return `404` instead of adding an entry, so read-write users can no longer grow the file with made-up ids; a zero-length store is reported as a `500` store error instead of being read as empty and overwritten (which silently dropped every campaign's threads, polls and decisions); and with no `data.metrics_dir`/`logs_dir`/`agents_dir` configured Jam fails loudly instead of writing into the process working directory (#10083).
- The run-detail interview history for Spektacular spec/plan stages no longer attempts a status-derived tier: `interviewFromStatusHistory` and the `Instruction()` accessor read `instruction`/`question`/`prompt`/`description` keys the pinned 0.22.0 per-artifact `status` verb never emits, so that tier was always a no-op; the panel still fills from the answer-file/transcript parsing tier and the one-row-per-`completed_steps` fallback, unchanged ([#10099](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10099)).
- agent: Claude agents no longer crash-loop at launch on v6 — MCP connections (including the injected task MCP) are passed as `--mcp-config` JSON instead of the nonexistent `--mcp-server` flag; the bare-shell crash log now carries the CLI's `exit_code` and a token-scrubbed `pane_tail` so the cause is visible without attaching to tmux (#10161)
- spektacular: hub executor exit status vs pipe EOF, lazy clone auth (#10162)
- spektacular: use ID-prefixed artifact names in hub prompts and resolve counter ids (#10163)
- runs: fix spec checkpoint panic and re-import design/regenerated Spektacular plans (#10164)
- runs: keep run re-admission and design start idempotent (#10165)
- spektacular: migrate existing projects, sanitize init name, accept 0.23+ CLI shapes (#10166)
- runs: make Spec/plan checkpoint reject re-mint the held generation (#10167)
- spektacular: hub executor launches the configured backend CLI (#10168)
- Align terminal run-key abandonment documentation and OpenAPI registration, and cover explicit owner admission/reset refusal after retirement.
- dashboard: keep sidebar version upgrade action visible and clear stale progress (#10183)
- cmd/hive: rewireSpektacular keep path no longer stops the kept executor (#10189)
- dashboard: check Spektacular spec readiness before approving design (#10190)
- jam: scan agent-invite prompt fields and tighten Projects sync token binding (#10191)
- jam: conflict-check REST spec edits, bound the live socket, write Jam state atomically (#10193)
- campaigns: derive stable ids for inception restarts and Spek runs (#10194)
- cost: attribute claude sessions from recorded cwd, not dir-name guess (#10195)
- nous: correct baseline_pct docs (#10226)
- runs: retry the reviewed plan lease on checkpoint reject (#10228)
- spektacular: accept CLI document statuses, park failed plan imports, drop gh from hub prompt (#10230)
- jam: publish Project sync through the real GitHub Projects v2 API (#10235)
- dashboard: fix spektacular config rollback, admin MCP fields, hub backend/model card, plan run link (#10236)
- runs: clear stale_plan on approval, gate fan-out on approval, keep run-wait latch, ungate Spek resume (#10240)
- fix(spektacular): make fake CLI answer --version and omit artifact_id like 0.22.0 (#10269)
- agent: derive hub-launched task MCP URL from the host this spoke is served on (#10284)
- build: fail the image build when the Spektacular install fails (#10286)
- campaigns: don't report plan document status under implement-stage runs (#10288)
- inception: admit the run before completing approve and report its run key (#10296)
- runs: verify reported PR before completing implement stage (#10298)
- spektacular: validate runs.spektacular.interview in YAML config (#10300)
- runs: make Spektacular Run approve idempotent and serialize plan checkpoint approvals (#10301)
- runs: mark retried stage_completed events; design artifact comment best-effort (#10302)
- mcp: forward held filter in issues_by_band/prs_by_band ahead of limit cap (#10310)
- runs: supersede rejected run plans and design artifacts at checkpoint reject (#10311)
- jam: report Jam store 5xx in project-sync and validate Projects v2 node ids (#10312)
- spektacular: headless launch denylist parity and a version-accurate fake CLI (#10313)
- spektacular: back off instead of spending a generation on missing credentials/colliding run worktrees (#10314)
- fix(hub): stop installing unused Spektacular binary in Dockerfile.hub (#10326)
- mcp: page issues_by_band/prs_by_band rows past the limit cap with offset (#10330)
- jam: serialize the shared Jam store across processes and publish GHES project syncs (#10331)
- runs: re-mint held plans filed under run_key, reset-to-spec design artifacts, surface dropped artifact comments (#10333)
- nous: bound baseline_pct in /api/nous/status after snapshot rollover (#10340)
- spektacular: make the fake CLI version-faithful for stale status and plan export (#10375)
- fix(spektacular): align fake CLI with pinned contract and add real-binary conformance job (#10388)
- fix(dashboard): port v5 proxy-only outward discovery to v6 Spek recheck (#10809)
- **Dashboard: the repo card's merge-strategy button no longer overlaps the `🐝 swarm` chip on v6.** The card header (`.repo-name`) and its badge/action groups now wrap, so the merge-strategy button, swarm chip, pause chip and auto-merge toggle each keep their own space on narrow cards instead of being drawn on top of one another, and the `direct` ⇄ `hive-serialized` switch stays readable and clickable. Fixes #10980.
- The `hive-serialized` merge lane and the ACMM `acmm:merge-queue` credit no longer treat a ruleset-only branch's required checks as unknown when the GitHub App lacks the Administration permission ([#10984](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10984)). A 403 from classic branch protection now falls back to the rulesets' required checks (GitHub still enforces classic rules at merge time), and a lane repo that earns no ACMM credit shows the reason on its row.
- A `hive-serialized` lane no longer keeps a red front pull request for the whole front timeout ([#11023](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11023)). When the self-merge or `lgtm` queue sweep rejected the front before the lane (for example as not mergeable once its required check failed after the lane's branch update), the lane was never consulted again, so every pull request behind it — including the fix for a red target branch — waited 60 minutes. The sweeps now hand a rejected front to the lane, which re-evaluates it without merging and lets it leave at once with the real reason (`required check "test" finished as failure on head …`), so the next pull request starts on the same tick. The front timeout stays the fallback for checks that never finish, and its reason now says what the lane last knew instead of always claiming the checks did not finish.
- The reviewer lane (`role: reviewer`, the L5/L6 pack `adjudicator`) is no longer kicked when it has nothing to do ([#11046](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11046)). The governor used to kick it every 30-minute cadence tick even when the lane was dormant below ACMM 5 or no escalated PR awaited adjudication, costing a full model turn just to reply "stand down" and leaving the dashboard showing the idle lane as **BLOCKED — policy stand-down**. The scheduler now applies the same two Go-side gates the kick already used and skips the kick, logging `nothing to adjudicate` or `dormant below ACMM 5`; the next tick checks again. A stand-down that is still rendered (a forced or manual kick) no longer ends with the `Begin now: pick the authorized repo …` closing line that contradicted it ([#11045](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11045)).
- Agents on every backend now bypass the hive proxy for loopback addresses (`NO_PROXY`), and plain-HTTP forward failures name the calling agent in the log.
- feedback: author issues as the submitter, never the operator PAT (#11051)
- Fix the watchdog flagging advisory pack agents (e.g. `supervisor`) as "alive but not producing": the advisory-only exemption now resolves the effective mode (explicit mode, else the ACMM level default) the same way `SyncModeFiles` does (#11167)
- Fixed: `label_driven: true` now reaches the un-park sweep on v6 so Hive steps aside on label-driven repositories (#11312)
- Agents now read an issue together with its comments ([#11443](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11443)). The scanner policy, the governor work-source rule and the five quality policies, the reviewer's linked-issue read, the scanner kick in `bin/kick-agents.sh`, and the contributor assignment prompt (GitHub issues only) now say `gh issue view <n> --comments`, the form the planning prompts already used. Previously these reads printed the issue body alone, so decisions and corrections posted as comments were missed.
- fix(config): drop duplicate coverage-target declarations after v5v6 merge (#11485)
- The `NOTICE matches the module graph` check no longer reports a timed-out go-licenses source lookup as NOTICE drift. go-licenses resolves `gopkg.in/*` source URLs with a live HTTP `?go-get=1` fetch and, on timeout, silently renders `Source:   Unknown`; the byte-exact drift gate then failed unrelated PRs and told contributors to commit the degraded file. `generate-notice.sh` now retries the walk when any source is unresolved, `validate-generated-notice.sh` refuses such a file so notice-autofix never commits it, and `check-notice-drift.sh` names the failure as a generator problem to re-run rather than drift to commit (#11486).
- **Automerge no longer merges PRs with failing CI into unprotected bases** ([#11489](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11489)). When GitHub reports a known-empty required-check set (unprotected base, or protection with no required checks), the sweep treated it like an unreadable set and deferred completed failures to the merge endpoint — which enforces nothing there, so #11471 merged into `v6` with 27 failing checks. Only a genuinely unknown required set (protection lookup failed) now defers to server-side enforcement; with a known-empty set, completed non-meta, non-ignorable CI failures block locally with `check-failure` / `status-failure`, while the metadata carve-out (#11456) and the positive-evidence and fresh-head guards (#11424) are unchanged.
- Repo cards no longer show issues parked with `needs-decision`, `needs-direction`, `needs-spec` or `needs-reporter-confirmation` as grey FILTERED; they now show an orange chip naming the person being waited on, and the first three count toward the "need human review" header total (#11490, #11494).
- fix(config): restore coverage-target declarations dropped by racing de-dup fixes (#11493)
- Repo cards on the dashboard no longer render their header row twice; the single header keeps the fork pill and the merge-strategy button (#11502).
- fix(dashboard): name repo-card chips by label instead of NEEDS HUMAN (#11506)
- Upstream-sync PRs on `upstream_watch` forks (labelled `upstream-sync`, on an `upstream-sync/` branch, or titled `chore: sync upstream …`) now land as merge commits instead of squashes, so the fork keeps upstream's ancestry and the next sync no longer re-conflicts; forward-merge heads with dotted versions (`sync/v1.7.11-to-v1.9.1`) are recognised too ([#11508](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11508)).
- Stamped the stdio `hive-admin-mcp` binary with its git build, so `initialize` reports `<version>+<sha>`, `version_read` shows `stdio_build` and `skew` against the hub, and the `limit` schema now documents its 1-50 cap ([#11513](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11513)).
- issues: the un-park sweep now replies and logs when a `/hive approve`/`/hive decision` comes from the account named in `project.ai_author` instead of ignoring it; boot warns when `ai_author` is a user login on an App-authenticated hive (#11512)
- Hub agents on `backend: omp` are no longer treated as crashed, interrupted mid-turn, or kicked into the sign-in wizard. The hub's pane detectors now recognise omp's status line (`▶─` / `π >`) as a running CLI, so the crash detector, kick pre-check and startup wait stop restarting a healthy omp ([#11516](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11516)); a mid-turn omp 18.2+ pane (the ` ⎋ <intent>` activity row or `⠧ 4m` spinner+elapsed) now reads as working, so a kick no longer sends Ctrl+C into a running turn or declares it ended early ([#11517](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11517)); and omp's first-run setup wizard and auth-code prompt now raise login-needed instead of reading as a ready prompt, with the onboarding auto-dismiss matching the splash's real `press ⏎ to skip` text ([#11518](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11518)).
- The close-on-merge ledger sweep now lists each claimed repository's open issues once per pass and only reads the PR and issue for claims whose issue is still open, instead of re-reading every merged claim kept in the 30-day ledger (closed issues included). This stops the post-restart quota spike where cold ETag/PR caches let the sweep exhaust the GitHub App's 5,000/hour core quota ([#11538](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11538)). If listing a repository's open issues fails, that repository is skipped for the pass with one warning and retried on the next.
- The merge-lane panel no longer tells operators to turn on GitHub's up-to-date rule when Hive simply could not read the branch rules (for example while rate limited); it now says the rules could not be read, shows the reason and omits the recommendation. Fixes #11540.
- Issue comments and label adds/removes refused by GitHub before anything was applied (403 `Resource not accessible by integration`, 404, 410, 422, rate limits) are now journaled NotApplied instead of Unknown, so the same write retries once the cause is fixed — e.g. after a repo is added to the GitHub App installation ([#11556](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11556)). Writes already stuck as Unknown (from a timeout, 5xx, or the old behaviour) are now reconciled against the issue's comments/labels on the next attempt instead of failing with `needs reconciliation before retry` forever, so no hand-editing of `journal.json` is needed.
- A conflicting Renovate PR in a repo whose Renovate config sets `rebaseWhen: never` is no longer stuck with nothing showing a person must act: a new per-pass sweep posts one plain-words comment (once per head SHA, recorded durably in `/data/metrics/dependency-bot-conflicts.json`) telling the reader to tick Renovate's rebase/retry checkbox, adds `needs-human`, and removes that label again once the PR stops conflicting or closes — only when the sweep added it. The hive still never pushes to, rebases or closes bot branches ([#11558](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11558)).
- Fix hold-source detection so a pull request whose latest hold label was applied by a non-App bot lists `unknown` alongside its Hive-notice sources, and no longer offers Release hold.
- Dashboard "your turn" ownership: an issue with an open linked PR is never a `CLOSE` item, even if it still carries `hive/covered-by-pr`; non-actionable issue rows now keep human acknowledgement and use the ordered parking-label check; escalation first-seen times are pruned only for repositories enumerated in the snapshot; a reviewer-lane agent on a pause/off cadence counts as unavailable; the optimistic hold toggle no longer attaches a stale decision to the moved item; the self-authorization hold shown on the governor page uses the hive-wide level like the decision does ([#11565](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11565), [#11507](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11507)).
- The "your turn" safety net and likely-done rule now use the routed lane's real push rights, live claims and task leases, and the reporter-confirmation gate, so ordinary backlog no longer shows a stale-issue review marker and likely-done issues routed to a lane that cannot push show a "to close" marker for the operator ([#11592](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11592)).
- `hive-baseline-check.sh` can reach a shared-CI verdict again from inside an agent session ([#11608](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11608)). Its sibling-PR lookup used `gh pr list`, which the agent `gh` wrapper refuses for staff agents, so every run ended in "could not read open PR checks", every failing PR landed in the unknown bucket, and `DEFER_TO_INCIDENT` / `RERUN_BASELINE` were never reached — shared CI breakage was handed out as one repair target per PR. The helper now lists open PRs with a read-only REST `GET repos/<repo>/pulls` and reads the exact named check per PR head (check runs first, commit statuses only when no check run carries the name); an unreadable sibling still makes the verdict unknown rather than PR-local.
- An agent mode you change in the dashboard now survives a restart: mode is marked operator-owned like model and backend, a same-level pack re-apply leaves it alone, and an explicit ACMM level change hands it back to the pack. The level-6 architect description now matches its `ISSUES_AND_PRS` mode instead of claiming it auto-merges ([#11650](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11650)).
- The contributor relay now answers Claude Code's folder trust prompt by selecting "Yes, I trust this folder" instead of a bare Enter that picked "No, exit". It also relaunches the CLI once if it exited during onboarding, and stops after a bounded number of dismiss attempts with an error naming the manual-trust workaround, rather than looping forever (#11658).
- Fixed the `/api/events` SSE stream being buffered by the Compose/Quadlet nginx gateway: the dashboard now sends `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and nginx disables proxy buffering for it (#11659).
- Dashboard hold add/remove no longer edits the published per-repo work breakdown in place while `/api/status` encodes it, which was a data race under `-race`; the counts are now copied before they are adjusted, matching the Ownership map fix ([#11675](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11675)).
- Nous (Experiment Lab) gates now reach the owner and the answer reaches the agent. The agent-side bridge (`bin/nous-hive-gate.py`) used to *PUT* its question to the owner-only `/api/nous/gate-decision` endpoint, which always failed, so nothing ever showed in `GET /api/nous/gate-pending` and every design/findings gate silently timed out as a reject. The bridge now publishes `<nous_dir>/gates/pending.json`; the hive mirrors it into the Experiment Lab (polling every `nous.gate_poll_seconds` / `HIVE_NOUS_GATE_POLL_INTERVAL`, default 15s, and on every `gate-pending` read), pings the owner once per gate, and `PUT /api/nous/gate-decision {"decision":"approve|reject|abort","reason":"…"}` records `gates/decision.json` + `gates/history.jsonl` for the agent to pick up. Decisions are validated (`400` for an unknown value, `409` when nothing is pending or `gate_id` is stale) and audited with the gate id. RFC [#11585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11585) part 3/8 ([#11696](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11696)).
- The `kind` and `standalone` Kubernetes overlays now wire the GitHub PAT into `hive.yaml` with `github.token: ${HIVE_GITHUB_TOKEN}`, matching `src/hive.yaml.example`. Before this, a pod set up by following `try-hive-on-kind.md` crash-looped with `github.token, github.app_id or github.forge is required` even though `hive-secrets` held the token. The kind smoke test (`src/deploy/test_kind_quickstart.sh`) now creates `hive-secrets` with placeholder tokens so the rollout can succeed, and the kind guide explains that fixing the config after a failed first boot also means deleting the `hive-data` PVC or `/data/hive.yaml.runtime` ([#11775](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11775)).
- Running `kubectl apply -k` again on the Kubernetes base or any overlay no longer deletes the keys in `hive-secrets`. The base used to ship an empty `hive-secrets` Secret, so each re-apply's three-way merge removed the keys an operator had added with `kubectl apply`, and the next restart refused to start without `HIVE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN`. `src/deploy/k8s/secret.yaml` is now only a commented template outside the kustomization, and operators create the Secret themselves, as the docs already describe. The Deployment already treats every `hive-secrets` reference as optional ([#11776](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11776)).
- dashboard chat: `!kick`, `!pause` and `!resume` with no agent name now reply with their usage instead of an empty unknown-agent error (#11828).
- Dashboard chat `!kick` now replies that the kick is queued until the first governor scan when the dashboard defers it, instead of claiming it was kicked (#11829).
- Open Hive Chat as a full-height sheet on phones (≤600px): hide the 💬 launcher and lock page scroll while open, show suggestion chips only on an empty conversation, and keep the input row above the keyboard (#11836).
- Hive Chat suggestion chips now only send text the chat can answer: the "Search docs for …" and "What changed in …" chips search the knowledge base, a bad `!runs spec`/`!runs design` target replies with the usage line instead of raw HTTP JSON, and the inception relay state reply no longer ends with a double period. (#11837)
- chat: `!inception start`/scan refuse to start when the hive has no enabled brainstorm agent, and a failed brainstorm kick is surfaced in `!inception state` instead of a silent capture phase (#11851)
- docs: admin MCP design doc now lists all 13 log-scrubber categories, matching pkg/logscrub (#11946)
- `log_read` (and `GET /api/logs/read`) now answers `status: "incomplete"` with a `next_cursor` when a read stops on its per-call scan bound, so an empty first page of an older window no longer reads as "no matches", and `lines` is always an array (`[]` when nothing matched) instead of `null` (#11984).
- Admin MCP reads through the in-hive `/api/admin/mcp` endpoint now report the hive's error reason (for example "until must not be before since") instead of a bare HTTP status, matching the standalone `hive-admin-mcp` binary.
- dashboard: show upgrade animation when upgrade is hub-initiated (v6) (#12074)
- dashboard: the Experiment Lab toggle now shows the "Experiment Lab (nous)" sidebar entry and section at ACMM L3+ (was L4), reactively on the next status refresh, and the toggle names the L3 requirement (#12076)
- Fix owner-only hand-offs never reaching the "Your turn" inbox ([#12329](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12329)). A pull request not written by Hive whose review verdict on the current head is `requires_human` is now your turn (`REVIEW`, reason code `review_requires_human`), matching the `human_hold` stage `/api/review/pipeline` already showed; a newer push with no verdict yet clears it, and Hive-authored PRs keep their `needs-human` / adjudicator rules. Agents can now park an existing issue whose remaining step only the owner can take with `hive-open-issue comment --needs-decision`, which applies the configured needs-decision label before posting the comment, and every scanner policy tells them to do so instead of leaving the issue unlabelled for its claim to lapse.
- `hive-open-issue comment --needs-decision` now requires the lane's write allowlist to include `label` as well as `comment`, and refuses a pull-request target, so the configured needs-decision label can only be applied to an issue by a lane allowed to label ([#12334](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/12334)).
- Fix the parked-issue "What to reply" menu: it now reads lettered options and recommendations from the hive's own comments, stops claiming a recommendation that was never stated, offers a new `/hive done` reply for owner-only steps parked or filed with `--needs-decision` (its reply is the hand-off that tells the next lane to re-check the step and close the issue, and `/hive help` no longer dismisses the step), names the labels it actually cleared, follows renamed `hard_suppress_labels` in the un-park sweep, and no longer copies `/hive approve` / `/hive decision` on label-driven repos that refuse them (#12372).
- Stop the App's self-merge sweep merging its own or a trusted bot's PR after a `requires_human` or `reject` review verdict, whatever `review.require_approval` says and across fix pushes, until a fresh approving review or a person releases it, and show every review-swarm `human_hold` reason (requires_human or reject for any author, dispatch exhausted, fix cap, no fixer, loop cap) as "Your turn", with the exhausted-retries hold now sending the same escalation event and label as the other holds (#12374, #12377).
- Teach every lane that can hand an item to a person (ci-maintainer, sec-check, quality, architect, outreach, strategist, guide, scanner), the ADR-0019 `needs-direction` escalation and the workflow-push overlay to park it with `hive-open-issue comment … --needs-decision` instead of posting prose with no park label.
- Your turn: an issue labelled `blocked` now waits elsewhere when a GitHub blocked-by link names what it waits on and becomes your turn (`blocked_unexplained`) once stale with none recorded; pull requests waiting on a required or changes-requested review, a Gated-band decision label (`needs-decision`, `needs-direction`, `needs-spec`, `2-discussing`) or a hand merge no Hive lane will make are now your turn with a verb (#12376, #12378).
- An issue labelled `blocked` now reaches the person who can lift it (#12376). `blocked` is a default dashboard waiting label (server and browser), so a blocked issue shows in the Parked band and a PR labelled `blocked` is Gated. The un-park sweep treats `blocked` as a parking label: it keeps the "What to reply" notice on the issue, `/hive approve` lifts the label and re-offers the issue, `/hive decision <text>` lifts it with instructions, and label approval removes it only when the App bot applied it. A contributor's blocked verdict whose reason says a person must act (an admin, maintainer, owner or operator, with no other item, upstream or release named) is now labelled `needs-human` instead of `blocked`, so it is that person's turn in the inbox.
- Dependency-bot PRs (Renovate, Dependabot, mergeraptor) whose required check is held or never started, whose required CI stays red, or that conflict with their base past a grace period now get one comment naming the action and `needs-human`, so they show as your turn instead of sitting blocked (#12379).
- Fix runs waiting on a person (plan/spec/implement checkpoints, design review, stale plans, exhausted stage retries) and approval-desk items such as a parked self-merge never reaching the Your-turn inbox: they now become your turn with the new reason codes `run_checkpoint`, `run_stale_plan`, `run_stage_exhausted` and `approval_pending`, even when the run's issue carries a claim or lease and with no escalation sink configured, and link to the Runs tab or the Approvals card ([#12380](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12380)).
- Close-on-merge no longer closes an issue as fixed when the merged PR only says `Refs #N` or says part is left open, and `needs-decision`/`needs-direction` issues now wait for confirmation instead of closing. (#12381)
- A self-upgrade that is deferred while agent kicks drain (`hub.upgrade_drain_timeout_s`) is no longer shown as a stuck upgrade: the spoke reports its drain deadline in the heartbeat and the hub holds the stuck-upgrade alert, drift signal, orphan sweep, stale-upgrade re-arm loop and the dashboard's red elapsed counter until it passes. The honoured deadline is capped relative to the upgrade's start, so a spoke cannot renew it indefinitely. Spokes that do not report it behave as before.
- Recheck GitHub label state before accepting a cached mutation-journal success, so repeated label toggles and claim expirations remove stale `claimed` labels while retries still deduplicate ([#12482](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12482)).
- Unanswered typed release owner steps remain parked in “Your turn” instead of being re-offered to agents as merged-PR remainder work ([#12632](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12632)).
- The Nous observations weekly budget ledger is now guarded by a process-level lock and written atomically through a unique temp file, so overlapping eval cycles can no longer exceed `max_per_week` or file the same fingerprint twice.
- The settings parity test no longer treats a help-text mention as Settings UI coverage for `data.nous_dir`, and its `# TODO #11854` allowlist entry is restored until an editable control exists.
- The admin MCP `agent.resume` preview now discloses that resuming claims operator ownership of the agent's pause state when the agent is paused (`pause_owner: operator`, which exempts it from the ACMM pack visibility sweep) unless the agent already owns it, so `agent.pause` followed by `agent.resume` is no longer a silent config change; `/api/agents` reports `pauseOwner` for this. The admin MCP docs and v6 readiness runbook now also state that token-authenticated writes are audited as the configured owner's login (or `owner`), not `local`, and note the `pause_owner` side effect of resume. ([#12797](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12797), [#12796](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12796))
- Failed pane writes and rejected kick deliveries now reach the governor and kick-status error paths without recording success; repeated write failures use the existing undeliverable reporting, a failed insurance Enter after the first was accepted still counts as delivered, and idle reviewer lanes and first-scan-deferred targets appear as skipped in governor evaluation logs ([#12846](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12846)).
- Manual Kick on an agent no longer runs the ioscan over the whole server-rendered prompt, so reviewer-queue.md's own `curl | sh` line no longer replaces every manual reviewer kick with the withheld marker; only operator-supplied prompt text is scanned, and a withheld operator prompt now logs a warning naming the rules ([#12936](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12936)).
- Serialized merge lanes promptly release a blocked front whose head is up to date and whose required checks pass, confirming the block with a fresh PR read before recording it and promoting the next pull request instead of waiting for the front timeout ([#12955](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12955)).
- Fix a review-swarm `requires_human` (or `reject`) hold staying in the owner's "your turn" inbox and in `/api/review/pipeline` `human_hold` after the owner approved the PR or replied `/hive approve`. The self-merge sweep now records the person's release it accepts in `review-hold-releases.json`, and the pipeline and inbox read it through the same `github.ReleasesReviewHold` rule; a newer blocking verdict holds the PR again.
- The `hive` composite action and `hive-action-smoke` workflow on v6 gain a `mention_login` input (default `hivecommons-hive`) for the relay comment `@<login> status …`; `app_handle` remains as a deprecated alias, and the runbook precondition is updated (#12964)
- The `hive-action-smoke` workflow is now registered on the default branch so it can be dispatched, and its relay comment @-mentions a configurable `app_handle` (default `hivecommons-hive`) that the hive's mention parser recognises (#12964).
- With `agent_issue_decision_policy: resolve`, Hive-authored needs-decision requests are now downgraded only when they positively classify as engineering questions; requests the classifier cannot place stay parked for the owner (#12969, #12972)
- The dependency-bot red-CI hand-off no longer blames the bump for a failure Hive already triaged as transient ([#12977](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12977)). An agent that diagnoses a red check as transient or infrastructure-related, not caused by the diff, now ends its triage comment with `<!-- hive-ci-transient head=<sha> check=<encoded name> run=<check run id> -->`, pinned to the head and failing run like `hive-ci-external`. While every failing run at the current head carries one, the hand-off comment says the failure was not caused by the bump and asks for a re-run of the failed check. Without a marker, the comment now lists re-running a transient failure as an option before fixing, pinning or closing the bump. A push or a re-run (a new run id) makes the marker stale.
- Fix the GitHub Actions trigger always declining relay comments with `agent_mention_declined … guard=repo` when the project's `repos:` list uses bare names: the mention/action kick path now matches the event repository (`owner/name`) against configured entries through one normalising helper that accepts `owner/name`, bare `name`, and `https://github.com/owner/name` forms case-insensitively, qualifying bare entries with the config's `org`.
- An @-mention that arrives while its target agent is still starting up is now queued and delivered once the agent is up, instead of being silently discarded when a governor cadence kick lands in the same startup window. Mention and action kicks go into a small per-agent FIFO (deduped by source, capped at 8) that a later cadence kick can no longer evict; the oldest queued mention is typed at startup and any leftovers replace later governor cadence kicks only — one-shot kicks from other callers (planning, dashboard, hooks, restart-with-message) are always delivered as sent. A queued mention is dropped only on FIFO overflow or when the agent is stopped; both are audited and report `kick-dropped`, so the mention store no longer keeps a stale pending entry and 👀 ack (#12982, #13055).
- Fix the governor run loop stalling during a GitHub rate-limit caution window: the issue stage-label sync is now deadline-bounded and legacy label housekeeping is deferred until the window lapses, so config reloads and heartbeat stats no longer starve.
- Saving an agent's prompt template from the dashboard no longer fails with "permission denied" when the shipped template in `/data/policies` is read-only (e.g. on hosted hives). The edit is saved as a user override in `/data/policy-overrides`, which the editor and the next agent run read ahead of the shipped default; the editor now flags a read-only shipped template and shows where the override is saved (#13005).
- Audit entries written by the outgoing pod during a hosted-spoke rolling update are no longer lost on NFS-backed `/data` ([#13046](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13046)). With `maxSurge: 1` both pods appended to the shared `/data/audit.jsonl`, and NFSv3's client-side `O_APPEND` let the new pod's writes overwrite the old pod's — a successful-but-clobbered write that never surfaced as an error. Only the holder of a small `/data/audit-writer.lease` now appends to `audit.jsonl`; the other pod writes to its own `/data/audit-spill-<pod>-<start>.jsonl`, the outgoing pod releases the lease on shutdown, and the new holder merges spill files back into `audit.jsonl`, which stays the canonical file. The lease is stale after 90s, above the NFS client's default 60s attribute cache ([#13072](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13072)); see `docs/audit-log.md` for the mount-option assumption. The first rollout onto this release still has an unleased old pod, so the fix takes effect from the following rollout.
- Claim label is generic hive/claimed-by-human, not per-user (#13051)
- Pull requests are never claimed as issues: review-swarm review/fix kicks (whose refs are PRs) are no longer listed in the issue-claims ledger, and the claim admission gate refuses a number that names a pull request. A PR author's comment on its own PR no longer records an issue claim that staged the PR `stage/030-pr-in-progress` — an issue-only stage — until the PR sweep healed it (hivecommons/hive#13061, seen on #12994).
- The issue relay no longer reports `ok:true` for a `stage/045-needs-decision` (or `needs-human`) park the stage engine did not apply: if the issue still wears another stage afterwards, the result is `ok:false` with the reason and the request is retried (#13069).
- Owner advice no longer counts on-demand agents (those with no schedule by design) as missing a cadence; only agents that should have a cadence but don't are flagged ([#13083](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13083)).
- An owner's `/hive approve` reply (or a trusted merger's approving review) posted after the review swarm's `requires_human` verdict now releases a contributor-lane PR, including one the owner opened under their own login, the same way it already did on the self-authored lane. The release is written to the same `review-hold-releases.json` ledger, so the PR leaves the dashboard's "your turn" inbox and `stage/085-needs-decision` instead of sitting there with no command able to clear it. Only a trusted merger's release counts on that lane. The merge-request relay agents use to land PRs now also refuses a PR whose latest decisive review verdict is `requires_human` or `reject` until a trusted merger has released it, so an agent can no longer merge a PR past a verdict that says it will not merge unattended ([#13085](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13085)).
- A person's release of a review verdict hold (an **Approve** review or a `/hive approve` reply) now survives clean `Merge branch 'main'` updates: merges that leave the PR's own non-merge commits and its patch against the merge-base (compared like a patch-id) unchanged. Each such merge moved the head and drew a fresh `requires_human` verdict, which re-held the PR even though its diff had not changed; the hold now counts from the first blocking verdict on the same non-merge content, in the self-merge sweep, the contributor lane, the merge-request relay and the review pipeline's your-turn decision alike. A new commit, a merge that carries conflict resolution (or whose cleanliness cannot be read), or a rewritten history still starts a new hold ([#13086](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13086)).
- Hive now acknowledges `/hive approve` on pull requests once per command and explains what the merge lane will and will not do with it — naming the GitHub **Approve** review that releases a `requires_human` hold — without clearing hold labels. The `stage/085-needs-decision` comment names the lane's release action, including when a maintainer must merge manually ([#13087](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13087)).
- Stop a review-verdict hold with no recorded time (an unreadable `review-verdicts.json`) from being released by any earlier trusted-merger approval on the merge relay and the self-authored automerge sweep.
- Review-backlog findings whose evidence file exists only on the reviewed PR (absent on its base branch) are filed `blocked` with a `<!-- hive:blocked-on pr=owner/repo#N -->` marker and without `help wanted`; a `blocked` issue derives no stage label and refuses every automated claim, and a sweep lifts the label once the PR merges or closes. `hive-open-issue comment --blocked-on-pr <n>` posts the same neutral note with `@`-mentions stripped, so the scanner no longer pings a fork's author to do the hive's work. The contributor relay keeps a session off an issue it just failed or abandoned for `governor.claims.reclaim_cooldown_s` (default 6h) instead of handing it back every ten minutes.
- Exclude stall nudges that the harness "continue" nudge recovered from the fleet-report `agent stall` evidence so self-recovery no longer files hive defects (#13098).
- The release comments the hub posts when it lifts a relay-applied `blocked` or decision label now treat the relay-supplied verdict reason as untrusted text (#13106): it is flattened onto one line, capped on a rune boundary, stripped of HTML comment delimiters so it cannot forge the hub's own idempotency markers, and @mentions in it are neutralised, so a contributor relay can no longer make the App identity notify arbitrary users or inject extra lines into an issue comment. The verified reporter handle still reads as a mention.
- Preserve UTF-8 rune boundaries when truncating contributor verdict reasons in the persisted ledger, preventing replacement characters in long multilingual reasons ([#13110](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13110)).
- Show superseded contributor PRs with close / keep-open actions in the Review Queue even when automatic closure is disabled; the sweep audits every detection and the queue shows no countdown while `supersession_sweep.close_contributor_prs` is off ([#13114](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13114)).
- Fixed a `requires_human` verdict on an untrusted contributor PR routing to `stage/050-review-pending` (and picking up `stage/stalled`) instead of `stage/085-needs-decision` when the contributor lane's author-association admission reason applied or nothing had reported on the head yet (#13115, #13112).
- Superseded contributor PR threads now lead with the close/keep-open decision: review comments render the `hive-decision-question` as visible text, reviews marked `<!-- hive-redundant-of: #N -->` (now documented in the reviewer policy) show a `no-op merge: duplicate of #N` headline instead of a 0/5 score, and the supersession sweep notice addresses the repo operator with the recommendation and choices, staying neutral when an operator already chose keep-open (#13116).
- The entrypoint's agent token-cache re-own step now matches only the agent's own `gh-token-<agent>.cache` files (and `.cache.*` / `-<n>.cache` siblings) instead of any file containing the agent name, so `reviewer` no longer steals `code-reviewer`'s token cache ([#13123](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13123)).
- The review-fix kick no longer pushes hive-signed commits onto PRs whose login author is a person, even when the PR is hive-attributed; the fix is proposed in the review instead (#13124).
- Review-fix commits are no longer pushed to PRs opened under a plain user login, even when it is the configured `github.ai_author`; the fix is proposed in the review instead, since the squash would fail the sign-off check.
- The dashboard now shows the release semver the hive is running ([#13130](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13130)). `/api/version` returned only a hard-coded legacy `version` constant and the commit, so the build-stamped semver (`hive --version`, already sent to the hub) never reached the UI. It now exposes it as `release` (omitted when the build has no version), and the sidebar version chip and menu show it next to the commit.
- The dashboard header's feedback, theme and other right-hand buttons no longer overlap the project title or ACMM badge at window widths between 769px and 900px; those widths now show icon-only Settings, Health and Guide chips ([#13135](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13135)).
- 085 entry comment follows the decision cause; flag @maintainer placeholder questions (#13139)
- Moves within 070/071/072 re-attribute the fix, not a regression (#13140)
- Contributor dispatch now honors `[vN]` title prefixes and `Target: vN` issue-body declarations, while a validated `wrong_base` verdict re-routes the next offer instead of applying `hive/already-done` or closing the issue ([#13146](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13146)).
- A `replicas:` copy of an agent (`<agent>-2` .. `<agent>-N`) can now read its own GitHub token on per-UID deployments ([#13166](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13166)). Replicas exist only in memory, so the entrypoint never gave them a `hive-<agent>-N` user, private token group or pre-created token cache. The manager ran each replica as a bare `uid:node` and its cache was written `dev:node 0600`, so every `gh` call in the replica was blocked with `token_cache_unavailable` and a restart did not help. The entrypoint now derives replica names from each agent's `replicas:` setting and provisions them at boot like declared agents. Raising `replicas` on a running hive still needs a restart before the new copies can read their tokens.
- The adjudicator can now hand an escalated pull request to a maintainer ([#13183](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13183)). Previously its contract offered only REPAIR, DE-ESCALATE and RECOMMEND-CLOSE, so when a PR was fine but needed a maintainer-only action (for example dispatching a workflow with `rebuild_akmods=true`) the agent improvised an unrecorded "HOLD", and the dashboard kept the PR in "waiting on someone else" with an empty reason for four hours before blaming the adjudicator for not acting. The reviewer lane now has a fourth verdict, HAND-OFF: the audited comment starts with a single `**Next step for a maintainer:**` line and the PR gets the `reviewer-handoff` label (needs-human stays).
