- The chat spine (dashchat, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Matrix, MS Teams) now authenticates to the local dashboard API with the server-to-server `X-Hive-Internal` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer` ([#9134](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9134)). On a standalone or heartbeat-only spoke with an `authorized_users` allowlist (a direct-route spoke) the bearer path is deliberately disabled, so every `!runs`, `!status`, `!kick`, checkpoint fetch and the `/api/events` SSE stream answered 401 and the spine logged `SSE disconnected … SSE status 401` at capped backoff forever; the earlier `chatDashboardToken` fix only helped hub-proxied hives. Wrong-token requests are still refused on both deployment shapes. Command-triggered requests keep their `X-Hive-Chat-Actor` audit attribution (#9125): the dashboard now honors that header on the `X-Hive-Internal` path too, only when no session identity exists and without changing the granted role.
- Dashboard chat now keeps its poll cursor honest across reloads, hive restarts and busy channels ([#9135](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9135)). `GET /api/chat/messages` returns `{messages, next, epoch, gap, viewer}` instead of a bare list; the browser persists `{epoch, seq}` with the transcript, so a reload no longer replays every retained reply with fresh unread badges, a restart (new `epoch`, or `next` below the cursor) resets the cursor and re-polls instead of silently dropping the next N replies, and a ring eviction (`gap`) renders a marker instead of pretending the tail is complete. Polling runs every 2 s while the panel is open, 10 s while closed, pauses in hidden tabs, and backs off exponentially (60 s cap) on non-2xx or network errors instead of hammering a 401. The panel is documented as one shared channel: another operator's input is rendered as a labelled peer line and kept out of the viewer's own `history`, so it no longer appears as if the viewer typed it.
- Dashboard chat no longer answers `!runs spec …` locally with a run listing; like every other `!` command it is submitted to the shared chat spine, so the owner-only `!runs spec <owner/repo#n>` start-run command reaches the allowlist and role checks instead of being short-circuited by a dashboard intent. A dashboard chat command the spine refuses (author outside the allowlist, or an empty allowlist) now shows a visible `❌ … refused` reply in the panel instead of silently never answering; Discord, Slack and the other channel transports keep their silent refusal. The v6 conformance suites for Discord, Slack and dashboard chat now drive the real surface (`Listen` against a fake Discord/Slack API, a started dashboard chat bot) so they fail when ioscan or the shared authorization path is bypassed ([#9136](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9136)).
- Slack `missing_scope` / `not_allowed_token_type` errors from socket setup and message sends are no longer reported as "chat topic updates unsupported": only `conversations.setTopic` maps them to the topic-capability error, every other call now surfaces the actual Slack error code with token/scope guidance, and config validation now rejects an enabled `notifications.slack` block whose `app_token` does not start with `xapp-` or whose `bot_token` does not start with `xoxb-` — the swapped-token mistake that produced the misleading message ([#9137](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9137)).
- Slack Socket Mode no longer drops commands during routine socket refreshes: on a `disconnect` envelope (including the early `warning`) the bot opens the replacement socket before closing the old one and switches without the 5 s reconnect sleep. A socket silent for 90 s (the bot pings every 30 s) is now treated as dead instead of hanging on a path that died without a FIN, and reconnect backoff is jittered by ±20% ([#9138](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9138)).
- The Slack single-user message route (`POST /api/saas/slack/user/{username}`) now enforces its self-only rule for non-admins with `canonicalEqual` instead of a flat `strings.EqualFold` ([#9139](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9139)). Previously, on a hub using a custom/OIDC provider that issues subjects differing only by case, a non-admin `custom:AbC` could DM the distinct user `custom:abc` through the hub — the spam-relay floor the handler exists to enforce. OIDC subjects now compare exactly, as every other owner check has since the F17 audit; GitHub logins still match case-insensitively.
- Removed the legacy standalone Node.js Discord bot (`discord/`, `systemd/hive-discord.service`) on `v6`: it had been crash-looping on a `SyntaxError` since May and predated the v6 command spine's allowlist/ioscan/outbound-scrub guards. The Go bot (`src/pkg/discord`, `notifications.discord.{bot_token,channel_id,allowed_users}`) is the only Discord bot going forward — hosts still running the old unit should run `systemctl disable --now hive-discord.service` ([#9140](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9140)).
- Documented that the Discord bot's application requires the **MESSAGE_CONTENT** privileged gateway intent (and View Channel/Read Message History/Send Messages permissions), since without it the REST poller silently receives empty message content and commands are ignored with no error logged ([#9141](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9141)).
- The Discord poll loop now backs off exponentially (capped, jittered) on repeated fetch errors instead of retrying at a fixed 5s cadence forever, logs 401/403 once instead of on every tick, and honors a 429's `retry_after` on both polling and outbound sends ([#9142](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9142)).
- Spektacular's `runs.max_stage_retries` now takes effect for hub-executed spec and plan stages. Before, the lease keepalive re-armed the hub executor's lease on every cleanup tick, so a stage whose agent exited with the document still draft, or failed, was never retried or escalated. The hub executor now owns the budget: each spent generation mints a retry generation until the budget runs out, then raises a `decision` escalation. The escalated run stays in `/api/runs` as `waiting_on=human` (`waiting_reason=stage_budget_exhausted`), and both the escalation and the generations spent survive a restart ([#9143](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9143)).
- Bound Spektacular CLI calls and stage polling, and run stage polling independently so a hung CLI cannot stall contributor lease and websocket cleanup ([#9144](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9144)).
- Honor `runs.spektacular.binary` in hub executor initialization, status probes, and spec/plan agent prompts ([#9145](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9145)).
- Spektacular interview answers now pass through the input scanner, identical submissions are idempotent, and consumed request/answer files are cleared without letting reused question IDs inherit stale answers ([#9146](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9146)).
- Inviting an agent into a campaign Jam thread now actually invokes a model ([#9147](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9147)). Previously `POST /api/campaigns/{id}/jam/agents` recorded caller-supplied `reply`/`proposed_text` (or a canned echo of the maintainer's prompt) under agent/model attribution without calling anything. The invite now sends the thread context — ioscan-gated — to the hive reviewer endpoint using the agent's configured model (reviewer model for Spektacular), records only the model's reply and proposed spec text, attributes them to the model actually called, and rejects caller-supplied `reply`, `proposed_text` and `model` with `400`. With no reviewer/LiteLLM endpoint configured the invite fails with `503` instead of posting placeholder text.
- Cancel revoked Spektacular hub stages, join workers and status polling on shutdown, protect active worktrees across hub restarts, and bound retained executor output and bookkeeping ([#9148](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9148)).
- `tagged-release.yml` and `promote-stable.yml` on `v6` no longer carry `v5` by literal ([#9154](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9154)). Both now serve the branch they were started from (`github.ref_name`) and refuse unless it is under `release_lines` in `.github/release-lines.yml`, via the new `src/scripts/check-release-lines.sh --is-release-line <branch>`. Previously a `workflow_dispatch` from `v6` checked out `v5`'s tip, derived with `RELEASE_LINE: v5`, and merged a release PR into `v5`, or promoted `v5`'s `candidate` to `stable`. It now fails at its first step. Nothing could ever mint `v6.0.0` either; adding `v6` to `release_lines` now enables that with no workflow edit. The rest of the release-line cut (the `docker.yml` channel rows on both branches, the default branch, and docs) is now a checklist in `src/docs/release-line-guard.md`. `release-channels.md` again says `edge` is published from `v6`, not `v5`. `tagged-release.yml` runs the release-line check from its own ref before checking out the commit it considers, and admits a `docker.yml` run only when that run was a `push`: `docker.yml` also runs on fork `pull_request`s, whose `head_branch` a fork can name `v5`.
- Telegram no longer loses notifications or replays commands ([#9158](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9158)). An unmatched backtick or code fence, common in LLM-written summaries, used to leave `<code>`/`<pre>` open so Telegram rejected the whole message; the HTML translation now always closes its tags, never nests code spans, and drops the fence language tag, and a message Telegram still refuses to parse is resent as plain text. A rate-limited (429) request is now re-sent once after the `retry_after` wait instead of being dropped after it. On start the bot now skips updates queued while it was down, so a restart no longer re-runs a `!kick` that was in flight or executes hours-old commands, and an update is never delivered twice within a run.
- fix(matrix): backfill dropped events via `/rooms/{id}/messages` when a sync's timeline is `limited`, instead of only logging a warning (#9159)
- fix(matrix): honor `limited`/`prev_batch` on sync so gappy timelines are backfilled instead of silently dropped (#9159)
- `hive-admin-mcp` (stdio) capped list tools (`agents_list`, `runs_list`, `leases_list`, `claims_list`, `plans_list`, `contributors_list`) now send `limit` as a query parameter instead of a percent-encoded path segment, so they no longer answer `HTTP 404` against a real hive ([#9160](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9160)).
- Admin MCP output no longer masks token counts and hive identifiers as credentials: `budget.update` previews, `settings_read` and `fleet_status` now show `totalTokens`, `max_tokens`, the `tokens` usage block and `hive_*` names, while credential keys and `hive_mcp_v1.` lease tokens stay masked ([#9161](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9161)).
- The admin MCP pending-confirmation store (`/data/admin-mcp-pending-confirmations.json` on the dashboard, `~/.config/hive/…` for stdio) no longer grows without bound or wedges admin writes ([#9162](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9162)). It now keeps at most 64 unconfirmed previews (oldest evicted first), persists only the request `write_confirm` executes instead of the whole human-facing preview, and replaces the file through a synced temp file + rename so a crash mid-write can no longer leave truncated JSON. A file that is already unreadable is moved aside as `<file>.corrupt-<timestamp>` and the store starts empty, so a torn write costs at most a re-issued `write_preview` instead of disabling every admin write until an operator deletes it.
- Fixed the admin MCP: `refuse_operation` now matches recorded exclusions exactly instead of by substring, writes report themselves unavailable up front when a confirmed write could not authenticate, results over 256 KiB are truncated with disclosure on both transports instead of failing, and the stdio binary's `HIVE_ADMIN_MCP_HIVES`/`HIVE_ADMIN_MCP_ACTIVE` configuration is documented.
- GitHub `@hive` mentions: a follow-up mention on an issue or PR is no longer silently declined after the hive's own reply ([#9164](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9164)). The per-thread cap aliased `classification.review_bots.max_attempts_per_thread` (default 1) and counted every App-authored comment on the conversation, so one completion reply — or any stage comment, review summary or escalation the hive had ever posted there — declined every later mention as `guard=rate-limited`. Mentions now have their own key, `github.mentions.per_thread_max` (default 3); only the App's own mention completion replies, which now carry a hidden `<!-- hive:mention-reply -->` marker, count toward it; and a mention past the cap is audited as `guard=thread-cap, detail=count=N max=M`. Completion replies posted before this change carry no marker and are not counted.
- One GitHub mention that cannot be delivered no longer stalls every later mention in its repo or spends its summoner's hourly budget ([#9165](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9165)). The poller used to stop at the first mention whose thread count or kick failed (an agent that cannot be kicked, a provider backoff), and each retry used up another per-user and per-repo rate-limit token. On the third retry the mention was declined as `rate-limited`, even though the human had already seen 👀 on it. The poller now continues past a failed mention and holds the watermark at it, and the failed attempt returns its tokens. After three failed attempts the mention is declined as `kick-failed` or `thread-count-failed`. The 👀 reaction is now added only after the kick is delivered, so it no longer appears on a summon that produced no run. A reaction that fails on a locked issue is recorded as `ack=failed` and does not block delivery. Marking a mention as seen, including an Actions OIDC dispatch, no longer moves the repo's polling watermark forward past mentions that have not been polled yet.
- GitHub mention triggers (v6): the mention store (`/data/github-mention-triggers.json`) is now written atomically, so a pod killed mid-save no longer leaves a torn file. A store that still fails to parse is moved aside to `*.corrupt-<unix-nanos>` and replaced with an empty one, logged at Error, instead of silently disabling mentions, the poller, the webhook and the responder at boot. The seen-key set now ages entries out after 45 days instead of growing forever, and existing stores migrate on first load. Actions OIDC dispatch (`POST /api/contribute/actions/dispatch`) now refuses with 503 when the store is not loaded, instead of deduping `run_id`/`run_attempt` against a throwaway in-memory store that accepted every retry ([#9166](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9166)).
- Escalation email no longer loses the daily digest or queued escalations ([#9167](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9167)). A digest the SMTP relay rejects is now kept for the next send and audited as `escalation_digest_failed` instead of vanishing without a log line. A hive.yaml reload that does not touch the escalation settings — e.g. flipping any dashboard Settings toggle — keeps the running dispatcher, so queued pages and the pending digest survive it; a reload that does change them carries the digest over to the new email sink and gives the old dispatcher up to 30s to deliver what it had queued. A push retry backoff never waits past that 30s: the event gets its final attempt at once instead. Anything it still cannot deliver is audited as `escalation_dropped_on_stop`.
- GitHub Actions-triggered mentions now check the trusted-comment-author allowlist against the live `github.actions` config instead of a stale boot-time snapshot, so a `trusted_comment_authors` override no longer gets silently ignored (mentions were declined with `guard=action-author` even when the actor was actually trusted) ([#9169](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9169)).
- GitHub mentions blocked by ioscan content filtering are now properly declined without triggering a kick or acknowledgment reaction ([#9169](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9169)).
- GitHub mention detection now requires a word boundary before `@hive` (or `@hive[bot]`), so an unrelated e-mail address like `ops@hive.example.com` no longer triggers a mention kick ([#9169](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9169)).
- GitHub mention triggers now live-reload mention, Actions and review-bot settings, including starting and stopping the mention poller when mentions are toggled ([#9169](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9169)).
- Push and on-call escalations no longer lose pages to provider limits or throttling ([#9170](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9170)). Pushover titles/messages are truncated to 250/1024 characters (an oversize link is left off), the PagerDuty summary to 1024, and the ntfy body to 4096 bytes with the link kept intact — previously an oversize `Governor budget exhausted` page drew a 400, was re-sent unchanged, and was dropped. A 429, 408, 5xx, or transport failure is now re-attempted twice with a short backoff that honours `Retry-After` (capped at 30s), while any other 4xx is final on the first answer instead of burning an identical retry. The ntfy `Title` header is RFC 2047-encoded so titles carrying `—` or other non-ASCII text arrive intact, `escalation_drop_oldest` now names the event actually evicted from the full queue, and `escalation_delivery_failed` no longer embeds the request URL — an ntfy topic URL is the topic's only credential.
- Inception no longer advances to scaffold on unconfirmed transcript proposals: `proposed=true` beads are excluded from the fact thresholds and from `RecordFacts`, pending proposals survive the advance instead of being wiped, and transcript uploads report the real import error (and a 400 when a zip imports nothing) instead of a misleading format error ([#9171](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9171)).
- **Dashboard → Extensions → Spektacular settings now apply without a restart** (#9172). Enabling, disabling or retuning Spektacular or its hub executor re-probes the binary and rewires the stage runner and executor in the running hub; a hub executor mid-stage keeps running and picks up the change once that stage finishes. The save response carries `spektacularApply` (`live` / `deferred` / `restart`) and the dashboard warns when the change is not yet live. `PUT /api/config/governor/features` now returns 500 when the config cannot be persisted instead of reporting success.
- fix(scheduler,cmd/hive): kick planning no longer compacts actionable issues away and kick rendering fixes (#9174, #9177)
- Chat personas now survive a restart ([#9175](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9175)). `!persona setup` answers, learning signals, pending suggestions and accepted-adjustment history used to live in a per-transport in-memory map, so every spoke restart silently reset run summaries to the defaults. The spoke now keeps them in `/data/chat-personas.json`, one file shared by the dashboard, Discord, Slack, Telegram, Matrix and Microsoft Teams transports and keyed by transport and author ID. If the file cannot be read at startup the spoke logs `chat persona store unavailable`, leaves the file untouched and keeps personas in memory until the next restart. The hub **Persona profile** section and `GET /api/persona/profile` are removed: nothing ever wrote a persona to a hub user record, so the section never had anything to show, and the docs no longer say personas are stored on the hub.
- The optional Jev smart classifier (`classifier.backend: jev`) can no longer stall scheduler sweeps when its provider is down, rate-limiting, or slow ([#9178](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9178)). Previously every uncached issue paid the full `classifier.jev.timeout` serially — twice per sweep, once for classification and again for run triage — so a 150-issue queue against an unreachable endpoint delayed kicks by about 10 minutes every eval cycle. Failed issue revisions are now not retried for 5 minutes, 3 consecutive failures open a 5-minute circuit breaker that recovers through a single probe call (logged as `classify: jev: … skipping Jev until …` with only the failure class, never provider response text), and each sweep or manual kick runs classification and run triage under one `max(10s, timeout)` deadline; skipped calls count as `fallback`. The Jev guide now also documents that each request sends the issue's title, full body, labels, author, repository, number, and `updated_at` to the configured provider, including for private repositories.
- Listing campaigns now groups legacy revisions without rewriting archive state or deleting revision directories and wiki snapshots; campaign actions use the newest snapshot's existing ID ([#9179](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9179)).
- The hub health verdict no longer lets a run waiting on a human mask a real red: "advisory posting failing", "advisory stale", and stale create/merge output now stay the headline instead of reading amber "run waiting on human", and the stale-output red can again be re-explained by the model-error-streak detector. `HIVE_FLEET_RUN_WAIT_AMBER_SECONDS=0` now means "use the default" like `fleet.run_wait_amber_seconds: 0` instead of ambering every waiting run, and the "since" time is anchored to the heartbeat that reported the wait so it no longer drifts between beats. The Gitea forge's `RemoveLabel`/`SetHold(false)` now resolves the label from the labels on the PR itself, so an organisation-level hold label is actually removed instead of silently left in place ([#9180](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9180)).
- Run checkpoint approve/reject (`POST /api/runs/{key}/checkpoint`, and the chat and mobile surfaces that use it) now acts on the checkpoint's stage instead of guessing from the epic's design metadata ([#9181](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9181)). Previously, a design-mode run that skipped the Spec checkpoint (`runs.checkpoints.spec: false`) reached the plan checkpoint with its design still pending. Approving it returned `{"ok":true}` but left the plan in `draft` and the lease at `plan`, and rejecting it re-queued the design without touching the plan. Now a disabled Spec checkpoint auto-approves the design, and an approval that cannot move the held lease answers `409`. Spec approval moves the lease before it writes the design approval, so a GitHub error on the approved label no longer returns `502` and leaves the run stuck at `spec` where no retry could move it. The failed signal is logged, audited, and recorded on the run's timeline instead.
- Spec runs admitted without a design epic (triage `spec` verdict, `POST /api/runs/spec` outside design mode, nous, inception) no longer wedge at the default-blocking spec checkpoint: the held spec now shows `waiting_on=human` and can be approved or rejected through `/api/runs/{key}/checkpoint` and the dashboard ([#9182](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9182)).
- Standby suspension checks no longer make synchronous GitHub requests during status builds or WebSocket handling. A background worker reconciles PR outcomes every five minutes, and legacy issue-numbered rows that return 404 are retired without penalizing contributors ([#9183](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9183)).
- One closed donated standby PR can no longer suspend a contributor configuration on its own: concurrent reconciles no longer record the same closure twice, the suspend rule counts each PR once, and the standby outcome ledger is saved crash- and concurrency-safely with unreadable ledgers reported instead of silently dropped ([#9184](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9184)).
- Preserve lease's `workItem` and MCP token fields in `reofferOrphanedStageLocked`, so when a relay lease expires and its stage is re-offered, the next adopter receives the Jira/Linear context. This fixes silent failure of `postCompletionPRComment` and the run title falling back to the bare run key in `/api/runs`.
- Chat spine SSE consumer now honours `event:` names — partial `agent-status` frames diff agents against the last full snapshot instead of being parsed as full state — runs ioscan once per outbound message with the blocked-drop path audited, and tears down silent SSE streams via an idle watchdog so a dead dashboard connection reconnects instead of hanging forever.
- Restore the tokenized `padding: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2)` on `.overview-carousel-arrow` that the v5→v6 forward-merge regressed to a raw `2px`, keeping the dashboard styling ratchet baseline intact.
- Fix v6 readiness runbook Discord step to reference the correct SSE disconnect log line (`chat: dashboard SSE disconnected` not `discord SSE disconnected`); refs #9699 live exercise.
- The `hivecommons/hive/.github/actions/hive` comment relay (and the `hive-action-smoke` workflow) now @-mentions the hive's actual GitHub App handle instead of a hard-coded `@hive`, so relayed commands are recognised when the App is named something else (for example `@hivecommons-hive`). Set it with the new `app_handle` input or the `HIVE_APP_HANDLE` repository/organization variable; the default stays `hive`, and `@` and `[bot]` spellings are accepted (#9707)
- Made TestConsumeSocketAckFailureSkipsDelivery deterministic by injecting a wrapped net.Conn that fails the socket ack write once it has observed the envelope on the wire, instead of racing a real TCP teardown (#9935)
- Activity Monitor "Accept triage" now moves the issue to 010 Actionable in the same request: the handler writes `stage/010-actionable` alongside `triage/accepted` when the issue has no stage label or wears `stage/015-triage-needed` (never regressing a later stage, never on a held issue), and the tracker no longer reads an issue carrying `triage/accepted` with no stage label as 000-new while waiting for the engine's next pass.
- Recognize install, boot, and explicitly named E2E GitHub Actions workflows in the ACMM E2E prerequisite, retaining web/configuration and directory alternatives without treating unrelated CI workflows as E2E coverage.
- Activity monitor: stage chevrons are again only as tall as their caption (one line of text → a one-line chevron, two lines → two, never more) with the caption centred instead of flush-left in a fixed two-line box, and the CI / Review lanes are notched chevrons like the other stages (state shown by fill and text colour) rather than bordered boxes.
- Hive activity monitor: a PR whose closing reference names an already-closed issue (a superseded PR whose body still says `Fixes #N`) no longer shows a bare `#N` in its issue slot. The issue's title is rendered struck through with a `closed` chip — `(closed issue)` when no title is available — and a number-only reference is completed by the eval cycle from the forgestate cache or one issue read per issue, memoised for 24 hours, never once per cycle.
- The hub activity event ring now also drops any event held longer than 24 hours, so a low-volume hive that keeps heartbeating no longer keeps old events in hub memory indefinitely after the fair-share eviction change ([#16072](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16072)).
- The fleet-wide activity event ring now evicts the oldest event of the hive holding the most events, so one spoke can no longer evict every other hive's events ([#16050](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16050)).
- Restore activity issue/PR header spans and far-right action controls; keep truthful current-phase highlights across parallel CI/Review, wrap all chevrons within two lines with complete hover/keyboard details, show unknown track states as icons rather than verbose panels, and label observed PR remediation “Remediating” without renaming native states or implying work during waits.
- Activity Monitor: the "Needs human decision" popover now opens on an issue row whose one covering PR is parked for a decision (stage 085); the trigger was keyed on the issue instead of the PR, so clicking or hovering did nothing.
- **Activity monitor: a row that needs a person says so once.** A row the your-turn decision hands to a person carries the "🧑 needs a person" chip, and a PR with the `needs-human` label or parked on a human decision also drew a "needs human" or "needs human decision" pill beside it, so the row said the same thing two or three times (with the "Needs human decision" chevron). When the chip is shown, those two pills now fold into its hover ("also flagged: needs human"); every other pill (hold, blocked, draft and the rest) still shows, and a row without the chip keeps its needs-human pill.
- The Hive activity monitor no longer draws bot Dependency Dashboards or the Hive Advisory Report as rows. #13261 took them off, but the v5 → v6 top-up that brought in the single open-items set (#13434) dropped that filter, so projectbluefin/bluefin-report#52 (mergeraptor[bot]'s Dependency Dashboard) sat on the monitor as "Open · since 4d". They stay in the `/api/stage-tracker` payload, so `open_issues` still equals the Overview tile; the monitor leaves them out of its rows, label chips and needs-attention counts, and the header's sum names them (`· 2 bot dashboards or advisory reports not listed`).
- Activity monitor: "Needs human: …", "Current blocker", "Next move", "Claimed by" and optional-delegation lines under an item are hive notes again — they open, tuck left into the ⬡ icon after the same 30 s as other hive notes, re-open on click, and a re-render never re-opens a line the tab already showed. The row's Let hive decide / Sentinel alert controls still carry the decision state. #16011 had drawn these as static rows that never left.
- Activity monitor: the pills on a row's title line (`train · joins behind #N`, `stage ↓`, the base-branch pill) no longer draw on top of the PR title. The chevron-strip grid rule added with the parallel CI/Review lanes (`.ham-strip:not(.ham-head-cols)`) also matched the title line, because `ham-head-cols` sits on the strip's row, not on the strip. That squeezed the issue, PR title and pills into the first three chevron-wide columns, and pills wider than one column spilled left over the title. The rule now excludes the title line by its row, so the issue spans Open..Claimed again, the PR starts at PR in progress, and the pills sit at the right.
- Admin MCP: `budget.reset`, `backup.create`, `circuit_breaker.engage` and `circuit_breaker.release` can be previewed and confirmed again. Since the unpersistable-preview check landed, `write_preview` refused all four with "contains a confirmation value that cannot be stored; update that field outside admin MCP", so the fleet circuit breaker, a budget-window reset and a backup could not be run through MCP on either transport. These operations take no arguments and report no details, and the pending-confirmation scrub turned their empty (nil) details into `{}`, which the check read as a masked value. The scrub now leaves nil maps and lists as they are; credential-bearing values are refused exactly as before.
- Admin MCP: the `version_read` tool description and the operator guide name the fields the hive really returns for the running commit, `hash` and `short`. They named `currentCommit`, which `GET /api/version` does not return, so a model asked for the running commit looked for a field that was never there. The guide (`src/docs/admin-mcp.md`) also lists the `triggers` settings section, which `settings_read` has always offered, and no longer says the write tools appear only when writes are on: `write_preview` and `write_confirm` are always listed, marked disabled with the reason.
- Admin MCP HTTP endpoint (`POST /api/admin/mcp`): `ping` is answered with an empty result, as MCP requires, instead of "method not found", so a client that pings to check the server is alive no longer reads the hive as gone. Notifications other than `notifications/initialized` (for example `notifications/cancelled`, which a client sends after it gives up on a tool call) are acknowledged the same way `notifications/initialized` always was, instead of being answered with a "method not found" error. Unknown request methods are still refused with `-32601`. The stdio binary was not affected.
- Admin MCP: `issues_by_band` accepts `band: "outside"`. The issues Overview export has a sixth band, `outside`, for open issues the scanner kept off the agent queues, and the tool returned it in `bands[]` with its count and on the rows themselves. Asking for it was refused as `unknown band "outside"`, because the tool's own list of band names had only the five donut bands, so those issues could be read only by paging through every row. `prs_by_band` is unchanged; pull requests have no such band.
- Admin MCP: `plan.propose` names the issue it is about. A proposal given by repo and number (no title) showed its target as `<nil>` in the preview summary and in the confirmation message, so the operator was asked to confirm "proposing a draft plan for <nil>". It now shows `owner/repo#N`. A proposal given by issue url alone is accepted too, as the endpoint already resolves it; before, `write_preview` refused it although `url` is in the operation's schema. A number below 1 is refused at preview instead of after confirmation.
- Admin MCP reads no longer mask values that cannot hold a credential. A read masked everything under a key containing `token`, `secret`, `password`, `credential` or `authorization` (booleans and `*tokens` counts excepted), so `settings_read` returned `[masked:token]` for a numeric rate (`tokens_per_coin`); `[masked:authorization]` for the whole per-repository self-authorization hold policy (`repoSelfAuthorizationHold`); and a mask for a secret that is not set at all, which read the same as one that is. `contributors_list` hid `token_expires_at`, `token_issued_at` and `token_last_used_at`. These are now shown: an empty value or `null`, an empty list or object, a timestamp, a token count or rate, and the self-authorization hold settings. Everything else under those keys is masked as before, kept values are still scrubbed by shape, and the stricter rule that decides what a write preview may store is unchanged.
- Admin MCP: `settings_read` returns a Settings section whole. It went through the list tools' row cap, which keeps the first 20 entries of a list by default, although `settings_read` has no `limit` argument to raise it. On a hive with more than 20 agents the governor settings came back with 20 agents (`agents_truncated: true`), and a section that is itself a list, such as `backends`, was cut to 20 entries, with no way to read the rest. A section is now bounded only by the 256 KiB text cap. The list tools (`agents_list`, `runs_list` and the others) keep their cap.
- Stdio admin MCP (`hive-admin-mcp`): a hub 404 on a diagnostic read (`agent_log_read`, `agent_kicks_list`, `agent_kick_read`, `run_log_read`, `run_detail_read`, `health_deep_read`, `prompt_history_read`, `config_effective_read`) now carries the build-skew notice, as a hub 404 on every other read tool already did. When the binary and the hub are different builds and the hub does not serve the route, the error names both builds and says to update the binary, instead of only "the hive answered HTTP 404". The hub's response body is still never included.
- Admin MCP: a result over the 256 KiB text cap now loses entries only from the lists that are actually large. The cap halved the list with the most entries first, whatever its size, so on a 15-agent, 12-repo hive `fleet_status` (350 KB) came back with `acmmPackAgents`, `cadenceMatrix` and `configuredAgents` cut from 15 entries to 7 for a saving of a few KB, on top of the cuts to `agents` and `repos` that were needed. Lists are now ranked by encoded size, so small lists stay whole, and lists of equal size are cut in name order instead of at random, so the same result is truncated the same way on every call.
- Issues that the issue filter (`project.issue_filter.require_labels`) keeps off every agent queue now reach the inbox as `ADMIT` when someone has to let them in. That covers an issue carrying `approved-direction`: `/hive decision` and `/hive approve` apply that label, not the filter's. It also covers an agent's finding where agents self-authorize and no `TRIAGE` row applies (by default at L6), and an undecided issue a person filed. The reason names the labels that admit the issue. Before, on projectbluefin, testsuite#1091, server#622, dakota-iso#294 and others got an un-park reply saying "still outside the agent queue", while sitting in band "outside" with no verb. Agent findings such as testsuite#1085 and documentation#1630 had no inbox row either.
- The merge sweep now re-runs cancelled or failed workflow jobs (or refreshes the branch) on an operator-approved contributor PR whose only blocker is a red check that is green on the base, instead of standing down from adoption and nudging the fork author to push a new head for a shared-CI flake they cannot re-run; cancelled runs now count as re-runnable in the adopted-PR recovery too.
- A hold added after Adopt now no longer leaves the row captioned as queued; it reads 'release the hold first' (#15665)
- An operator's Adopt now takes over any PR, a hive owner's or maintainer's included: the stage engine honours the forced adoption instead of refusing it as person-authored on every sweep, which left the row at "adopting… (queued)" forever. The hive still never adopts a person's own PR on its own initiative; the audit names the author taken over from.
- Approve no longer deadlocks a contributor PR the hive cannot merge as-is: when the approved head is on a fork the App cannot update and sits behind the base (`fork-not-editable`), conflicts, or lacks a sign-off, the admission no longer records `not adopted: a maintainer approved this head; the hive merges it as-is` — the hive adopts and carries the approval to its copy. Adopt now always wins over an earlier Approve: recording it clears the admission blocker at once, the row immediately reads *adopting… (queued)* with the Adopt now action gone from the menu and popover, and the decision response says `adoption-queued` instead of promising the running pass when the copy has not opened yet.
- A delegated `adopt-supersede` decision no longer reports "done" when only the request label landed: the Activity Monitor ✓ now reads "decided: adopt-supersede · executing…" until the adoption engine records the copy ("adopted as #N") or definitively cannot ("could not adopt: <reason>", with what a person can do). A PR that edits `.github/workflows` is decided as a capability gap and routed to the `capability:workflows-permission` blocker instead of flipping back to a bare Needs human decision; re-adoption after a closed copy surviving the mutation journal landed in [#15209](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15209) ([#15188](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15188)).
- Adoption: an adopted red PR is routed to the fixer once per red episode (its head plus its failing checks) instead of being re-announced on every eligibility pass, and a PR the hive already parked at `stage/085` (`adoption-stalled:<reason>`) on its current head leaves `ci-failing.json`, so the scanner is no longer kicked to re-triage a red it cannot fix until the head moves or the escalation is released
- Keep adopted contributor PRs with review-requested changes in the fixer's work list until a new head lands, and surface exhausted fix attempts instead of silently idling.
- "Let hive decide" no longer hands an adopted PR to the hive's fixer when the hive cannot push its branch. projectbluefin/utah#919 (a fork the hive had recorded fork-rehome-refused on) and projectbluefin/testsuite#1037 (a fork changing `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, whose fixer pushes GitHub refused three times) were decided "hive's fixer: … then it merges" and read "the hive is fixing it" for days. The delegate now checks push-ability first (same-repo, or a fork with maintainer edits and no workflow-file diff, with no fork-rehome-refused, workflow-path escalation or capability blocker recorded): a connected author gets the fix list back, otherwise the park stays with the person who asked (`adopted-push-refused`). An answer already recorded on such a PR's head shows as your turn (`adopted_push_refused`) instead of "the hive is fixing it".
- The hive no longer merges an adopted PR after its own fixer undid the PR's change. On projectbluefin/utah#1091 the adopted fixer made CI pass by re-adding the 25 `baselines/triage.toml` entries the PR removed, leaving a docs-only diff, then announced "sweep will merge when green". Each hive push on an in-place adoption is now checked against the PR's diff at the contributor's head the adoption started from: if fewer than half of those changed lines remain, the push is refused (so is any push on top of it, and stale-red recovery never releases it), the PR goes to `stage/085-needs-decision` (`adoption-fixer-reverts-pr`) with a "Fixing CI would undo this PR's change" note, and the contributor lane will not merge that head. Until the check passes, the lane holds the head (`contributor-lane:adoption-intent-pending`), and an agent's "sweep will merge when green" note on a hive push is rewritten to say the check comes first. The scanner policy tells the fixer to park instead of pushing such a commit.
- Fix adopted contributor PRs so review changes-requested verdicts route to Hive-owned fixer retries instead of sitting behind stale no-verdict or maintainer-approval waits.
- Adopted contributor PRs no longer dead-end at `stage/074-adopted-by-hive`: an in-place adoption whose hive fix the squash sign-off gate strips, or whose head sits past the 074 dwell with a blocking review-swarm finding and CI idle, converts to a superseding `hive/adopt-<n>` App PR (`reason=signoff-rehome` / `in-place-stalled`) carrying the contributor's commits and the open finding; an adoption nobody is working (unchanged head past the dwell, or a failed re-home) moves to `stage/085-needs-decision` as `adoption-stalled:<lane reason>` with one comment naming the exact blocker. Existing 074 store records are re-evaluated every sweep. Red-PR fix kicks for adopted PRs now say green CI is not done while a finding is open and never report "only tide / maintainer lgtm remains" below stage 080.
- Adoption: a contributor PR the hive adopted in place (stage 074) is the hive's to finish — a merge conflict or red check on it reaches the fixer like a hive-authored PR's (the sentinel alert now blocks only the merge, not the repair, so an adopted PR no longer sits red for hours with nobody kicked), the fixer is told to leave the sentinel label for a maintainer, external review-bot threads on it are repaired rather than answered with suggestions, and the tracker caption says whether the hive is rebasing, fixing CI or addressing review findings
- An adopted PR whose hive fix does what its review asked is no longer stuck at `stage/085-needs-decision` as "Fixing CI would undo this PR's change". On projectbluefin/utah-packages#943 the review asked that the PR's two wontfix entries stay pending; the hive adopted the PR for those asks and pushed a commit that did exactly that, and the undo guard parked it because the push kept only 2 of the PR's 20 changed lines. The park held until the head moved, so a later approve could not release it. When the hive adopts a PR for the review swarm's requested changes (CI not red), a push the guard refuses is now taken once the reviewer approves that exact head, whether the approve comes before or after the push is checked; the park is released with no second note. A fix for red CI that undoes the PR (projectbluefin/utah#1091) stays refused even if the reviewer approves it, and any verdict other than approve keeps the park.
- Stalled contributor PRs whose diff trips the contributor lane's diff fences (tests removed, CI workflow / action files edited) are adopted instead of being refused on every sweep (`adoption due but refused by diff fence`, hivecommons/hive#13212): adoption is not a merge. The fence is carried forward — recorded on the stage record (`adopt_diff_fence`), named in the adoption comment, and stamped into a superseding App PR's body as `<!-- hive:carried-fence reason=… -->` — so the fix lane repairs CI while every merge lane (contributor, self-authored, trusted-author, queued) still routes the green head to `stage/085-needs-decision` for a manual merge. The dco-rehome second takeover carries the fence too instead of releasing the adoption back to 072. Only a head that moved since evaluation or an unreadable / incomplete file list still defers adoption to the next sweep.
- Stage-074 adoption escalation: a red optional check alone no longer escalates an adopted PR to 085; records written before the adopted-head clock existed start their dwell at first sight instead of reading back to the original adoption; the escalation releases back to 074 when its reason clears (comment still once per head); the stalled note reports the head's real dwell (hivecommons/hive#13040).
- The hive no longer parks an adopted `role/trusted` PR at `stage/085-needs-decision` as `adoption-stalled:hive-signoff-attribution` because of its own self-signed fix commit: when the head mixes the contributor's commits with App-signed ones, every commit self-signed and the repo not in the new `auto_merge.squash_only` list, the lane elects a merge commit (`merge-method/merge` label, one `<!-- hive:merge-commit -->` note, `Sign-off survives the squash` honours the label, merge sweeps use `merge_method=merge` and record the reason on the claim). A PR already parked on that reason is released on the next sweep; a refused election stalls with the refusal named. ([#13800](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13800))
- When the hive adopts a contributor PR that was returned for the review swarm's requested changes (or another review ask) with CI green, the adoption note now says what the nudge asked for. It used to say "CI stayed red for 2h after the nudge" whatever the nudge was for, the superseding PR body said "adopted after CI went red", and the in-place note promised to "fix CI here". The note now reads the nudge's own diagnosis: red checks, review asks, or both. An in-place adoption held by a blocking review verdict also says that the in-place fix repairs CI only, and that a finding still open after the stage dwell moves to a superseding PR.
- Adoption: when the hive's superseding copy of an adopted PR is closed without merging, the stage-label pass now re-adopts (fresh copy from the same head, new `hive:adopted` marker), reverts the adoption with a `hive:adoption-reverted` note when the head moved or the copy cannot be opened, and parks the PR as `adoption-child-closed-twice` if copies are closed twice within an hour; "Let hive decide" re-adopts instead of answering "no change", and the tracker shows "Adopted → #N (closed) · recovering" instead of "Needs human decision" (hivecommons/hive#15052).
- Activity monitor: an issue whose only PRs are a contributor's original and the hive's adoption copy of it no longer offers "Let hive decide — all 2 PRs" or reads "fell back to Covered by pr — Covered by PR #N — …; PR #M — … changes requested". The pair is one logical PR: the caption reads "Covered by #N (adopted from @author's #M) — in CI / review", the superseded original's verdict never gates the issue, the feed says "moved to" when an issue stops mirroring its PR, and the copy's body carries the original's annotated `Refs #N` lines so it keeps the issue link. (hivecommons/hive#15549)
- When a person merges a contributor PR the hive adopted, the hive now closes its own `hive/adopt-<n>` PR (one note) if the original merged at the same head, instead of leaving a redundant copy open that flips between stages as the base moves.
- Adopted contributor PRs now supersede automatically when confirmed push-access loss or squash sign-off attribution prevents in-place repair (not on API errors or unrelated base workflow drift), and idle rebase work falls through to a hive-owned branch instead of parking for a human; fixer instructions preserve contributor authorship and sign-offs (#13975).
- Adopted fork PRs are now closed (with a note linking the superseding PR) when the superseder merges, regardless of which stage the original has since moved to; when hive cannot close the original it is marked superseded so the activity monitor drops the row (#14471).
- Contributor adoption (stage `074` and its re-home / DCO re-home) no longer takes over a PR whose author has admin or maintain permission on the repository (backport of [#14305](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14305), [#14301](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14301)). The permission is read once per repository and author per 10 minutes; a failed read is not cached and defers, neither adopting nor releasing; an existing adoption of such an author is released, closing a still-open hive superseder with a note first.
- An adopted PR waiting unattempted in the fixer queue no longer runs the stage/074 stall clock toward a needs-decision park; the wait is capped at four dwells and does not apply when the fixer is unavailable (#15036).
- A PR superseded by a hive adoption now closes promptly and reads as one muted line in the Activity Monitor (hivecommons/hive#15511 listed hive's #15574 *Merge queued* and, under it, the still-open original #15526 whose greyed note "· Adopted → #15574 · superseded (hive re-authored with sign-off)" wrapped to two lines; the close-first close had been refused by the write-back gate with `needs-opt-in-label`). New `governor.labels.stage.adoption.close_superseded: on_adopt|on_merge` (default `on_adopt`): a clanker- or hive-authored original closes in the adopting pass by policy — the gate admits the close as `superseded-agent-pr` without the `contributor_adopt` opt-in label once the copy carries its commits and sign-off; a human-authored original still needs the label, else it closes when the copy merges. The tracker marks the original `superseded_by: M` (cleared when the copy dies, omitted for in-place adoptions) and the copy's `adopted_from.state` / `lineage.from_state`; the muted sub-row's note is now "superseded · hive adopted → #M" ("superseded · closed · hive adopted → #M" once closed) on one line — the title ellipsizes first, the hover carries "re-authored with the same commits and sign-off" and whether it closes when #M merges or is already closed — and the line stays only while #M is open and listed.
- Fixed the dashboard applying advisor settings when the `hive.yaml` save failed: the fleet, model-roles and per-agent advisor edits now roll back on a failed save, so the live config and `GET /api/config/advisor` stay unchanged ([#13371](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13371)).
- Advisor reviews now report a dollar cost, `daily_budget_tokens` survives restarts, applies when the endpoint reports no usage and holds under overlapping reviews, and a `concern` verdict no longer keeps an agent from ending its turn repeatedly.
- Advisory digest posts to archived (read-only) repositories are no longer retried every cycle or self-reported as failures (#13570)
- Hive advisory checklists (the dedupe agent's `<!-- hive:dedupe-checklist -->` issues) are now worked by the hive itself: the close-on-merge sweep ticks each `- [ ] #N …` item as #N closes or merges and closes the advisory as completed once every item is resolved (`dedupe.advisory_autoclose`, default on); the Activity Monitor never parks an advisory at 045 (chip *Advisory · hive is working the items (k/N resolved)*, optional **Close now** lead); and the delegated-decision plan for issues says *Approve the direction of #N and let the hive pick it up* (or, for an advisory, *Close the advisory* / *Keep open; hive is working k/N items*) instead of the PR merge-queue wording (#15754)
- Governor: the advisory digest no longer re-resolves every long-closed advisory bead against GitHub on every eval cycle; closed beads with a persisted `resolved_at` outside the recently-resolved window skip the lookup, and the remaining lookups share one memoized, budgeted resolver per build. This stops the digest from draining the installation rate-limit quota and from pinning the governor loop (stale `/api/status`) under post-reset slow-start pacing.
- Advisory digest: when the newest digest comment on the advisory issue is not App-authored, re-pin to the App's own digest comment (or create one) and persist that anchor; log the foreign-comment warning once per issue per process (Debug thereafter) with the action taken, and skip the edit when the digest's material content is unchanged for the anchor.
- Repo pause now silences every hive-originated write to the paused repo, not only agent-requested ones: the advisory digest comment is neither edited nor re-created while the repo is paused (logged once per update interval as `advisory digest skipped: repo paused` with the pause's `by`/`reason`, and never counted as a post), the write-back containment gate refuses every kind — own items included — with reason `repo-paused`, and the duplicate-PR, closed-issue stage-label and hard-suppress sweeps skip paused repos. A paused `torch-spyre` spoke had kept editing its pinned `## 🐝 Advisory Digest` on every restart while the auto-merge sweeps correctly stood down.
- The hive no longer reopens an advisory issue a person closed. projectbluefin/common#639 was closed by a maintainer ("no longer used") and reopened by the hive the next day. A person's close now stands: the hive files a new advisory issue saying which one it replaces and why, and naming `advisory.target`. A close by a bot or the hive, or one GitHub does not attribute, is reused as before (#4167).
- Dedupe advisories with nothing to act on are no longer filed as issues, and advisory issues no longer look like stalled work ([#15381](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15381)): the dedupe lane's prompt files a new checklist only for an action-required row, and the issue-request relay refuses an `issue-create` whose dedupe-checklist body has zero near-duplicate pairs, zero resolved candidates, zero missing PR↔issue links and no task lines (audited as `agent_issue_empty_advisory_refused`, summarised in a knowledge bead). In the Activity Monitor an issue wearing `triage/advisory`, carrying the dedupe-checklist marker or a `Decision required: no` line is an advisory: the Open chevron reads **Advisory · read & close** (or **Advisory · nothing found · safe to close** when its own counts are all zero) with no "· since Nh" or stale tint, the caption is *Advisory for maintainers · read, then close*, it is excluded from Needs human / Needs attention, and the row menu leads with **Close (read)**, which closes the issue as completed through the existing decision path (`close-read`).
- The agent channels list now escapes repository names before rendering them, matching the other channel fields ([#15907](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15907)).
- Agent Channels now offers only supported kick channels, explains GitHub issue triggering through CEL rules and signed webhooks, and shows actionable save errors without retaining rejected edits; signed issue-opened deliveries now wake the existing governor/CEL evaluation path.
- Every issue the hive files now starts with its `[<agent>]` tag, with no producer left out: one `issueshape.AgentIssueTitle` function is the choke point for every issue-creation path — `CreateIssue`, the review-backlog, dedupe, hotspot (`[ci-maintainer]`, matching its `agent/ci-maintainer` label), self-report, upstream-watch, advisory and recommendations filers, and the proxy's `gh issue create` — puts the tag first (ahead of any emoji), never doubles it, and a guard test fails any new raw create that skips it. The Activity Monitor draws the tag as a chip ahead of the title instead of repeating it. Existing issue titles are left as they are; dedupe ignores the tag so they still match their tagged successors.
- Dashboard agent "Now:" line tests report when their JavaScript fixture cannot run because Node.js is missing from PATH, instead of failing the test run ([#12924](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12924)).
- Explain how to resume a paused agent in its dashboard pause details and keep the tooltip within the viewport.
- `go test ./pkg/agent/...` no longer orphans its per-run tmux server (with `-zsh` panes spinning on deleted cwds and `sh -c … pluk watch` pipe-pane children): TestMain now kills every server under the run's `TMUX_TMPDIR` before removing the socket dir, a detached reaper covers panic/`-timeout` exits, and a post-run guard fails the run if any of its tmux or pluk processes survive.
- `GET /api/agents` returns agents in name order. It walked the agents map, so the order changed on every call. The admin MCP `agents_list` tool keeps only the first `limit` entries (20 by default, 50 at most), so on a hive with more agents than the limit each call returned a different, random subset and no call could be relied on to show a given agent; `agent.resume` previews, which look an agent up in that list, were affected the same way. `hivectl agent list` output is now stable too.
- Linkify GitHub repo issue and PR references in dashboard alert banners so stalled-plan alerts open in a new tab.
- A contributor's "already done" verdict that cites no PR or commit, or whose citation fails verification, no longer adds `hive/already-done` or posts "Hive: already resolved by …". The issue gets a comment saying the contributor reports it may already be resolved, and keeps the `contribute_already_done_hold_days` offer hold; verified merged-PR evidence still labels and closes as before.
- The hive closes its own already-landed PRs as superseded instead of asking a person: a hive-authored PR (an adoption included) whose reviewer verdict says the change is already on the base — by the `hive-redundant-of` marker or by naming the landing PR in words — is closed with the superseded comment, its adopted originals are settled and closed too, and the parent issue gets the usual closing; the empty-diff freshness guard no longer reads the hive's own label bumps as a fresh head. Logged as `self-authored:already-landed` ([#15647](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15647)).
- A PR whose `requires_human` review verdict a person has answered no longer stays in the owner's your-turn queue, and the answer now reaches the author agent on hives without review approval ([Danathar/dns-failover#155](https://github.com/Danathar/dns-failover/pull/155)). After the owner's `/hive decision <instruction>`, the hive recorded the decision for the head and moved the PR to `stage/070-fixing`, but the dashboard kept the row as "Hive's review needs a human decision" for over an hour, and no fix was ever dispatched: the review planner returned before reading any answer whenever `review.require_approval` or `review.fan_out` was off. Ownership now reads the recorded answer for the current head (the decision ledger the stage engine already reads), so an answered `requires_human` or `reject` verdict reads "@who answered Hive's review on this head …; the hive is fixing it" until a new head or a newer verdict; a dispatcher hold or the fix-loop cap stays the owner's. With review dispatch off, the planner now plans only answered heads, handing each instruction to the author agent once per head exactly as with review on, and leaves every other PR's dispatch state alone.
- Agent GitHub API hourly cap now warns once per agent per window instead of on every rejected request (#14118)
- **Trusted-author tier hands App-authored PRs off under its own reason** — the sweep logged `reason=contributor-lane:app-authored tier=trusted-author` and recorded a trusted-author stage observation carrying the contributor lane's reason, which read as if the contributor lane had routed the App's own PRs. The tier now skips them as `trusted-author:app-authored`; `contributor-lane:app-authored` is emitted by the contributor lane only. Stage derivation treats both as no-opinion hand-offs, so the self-authored lane's `review-gate:no-review-bundle` keeps owning the stage; merge gating is unchanged ([#14482](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14482)).
- An approval no longer carries onto a later head on a pusher-chosen commit date alone (follow-up to hivecommons/hive#16817). The date fallback now also requires that the hive had listed that commit as the PR's head by the time of the review; the first listing of each head is kept in a new persisted record, `pr-head-sightings.json` in the stage state directory. A commit with no listing on record (for example one from before the upgrade) carries nothing by date, so a backdated content push under a later base merge cannot inherit an approval. A review on a non-merge head, and the walk over diff-preserving base merges to the approved commit, are unchanged.
- `/hive approve` on a hive-authored or trusted-author-lane PR is now acknowledged only for trusted mergers; anyone else gets the same "not a trusted merger" reply the contributor lane gives instead of a false acknowledgement (#13093).
- **`/hive approve` no longer promises a merge for a workflow-file head that also removes tests.** Its reply keyed the "a trusted merger's Approve review lets the lane merge" caption on the workflow-path fence alone; since the contributor lane checks removed tests before the owner-approval release ([#15027](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15027)), such a head stops at `contributor-lane:tests-removed`, so the reply now gives the manual-merge wording instead ([#15034](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15034)).
- The dashboard's Approve result toast now leads with the outcome in plain words ("Approved #510 as @user · sentinel alert cleared by your review"), names the concrete next step and who merges (hive's merge sweep with the soak figure, or "merge it on GitHub yourself" on the human-merge lane), repeats the ⚠ sentinel paragraph only while the alert is still open after the action, lists what was posted on a muted secondary line, and on Prow-managed repos says the approval is recorded in hive while Prow approval still needs an OWNERS reviewer — instead of "`/lgtm` + `/approve` posted (released: …) … the merge gate takes it from here; the dashboard merges nothing" ([#15212](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15212)).
- Adoption of a stuck contributor-clanker PR is automatic: the predicate that makes the activity monitor offer Adopt (`automerge.AutoAdoption`) is the sweep's trigger, so a PR at 072 whose author is offline past the grace (one heartbeat buys one window, `mode=queued` nudges count as offline) is adopted by hive on that sweep for conflicts, requested changes, failing required or optional checks and `fork-not-editable` forks; the row says when (`hive adopts it in 3m unless a new head lands`), names the fork blocker, and the log carries the trigger. Adopt now stays as the override.
- Superseded hive PRs no longer park on a person. A **hive-authored** PR whose closing targets are all closed, one of them by a different merged PR, and whose head conflicts with the base (or whose files that PR already covers) is closed by the hive itself as `hive/superseded` with a notice naming the superseding PR — in the self-authored auto-merge lane before any review is dispatched, in the supersession sweep when GitHub refuses the rebase for a conflict, and in close-on-merge of the superseding PR — under the new `governor.auto_close_superseded` knob (default on; human-authored PRs are never auto-closed). A contributor PR adopted in supersede mode (stage 074) now leaves `stage/085-needs-decision` in the adopting pass when the park was only the review swarm's `requires_human`: the original renders in the CI/Review column with an "Adopted → #N" pill instead of "Needs human decision", and the duplicate-fix sweep no longer closes the superseding App PR as a duplicate of the PR it supersedes. Evidence: #14965 (closed by #14957 for #14952, parked >1h), #14975 → #14980, #14947 → #14977.
- The fleet selfreport feed no longer files the automerge sweep lanes' (queued, trusted-author, contributor) `base-refresh:merge-guard` skip ("destination merge already in progress") as an `unclassified_error_repeated` issue; it is an expected, self-limiting outcome and stays in local logs (#16520).
- Fixed self-authored and trusted-author automerge to gate on required branch-protection checks instead of GitHub's aggregate merge state, with per-PR skip reasons.
- Activity Monitor: a PR parked on a person who must act on the PR itself (rerun CI, approve workflow runs, resolve a GitHub permission, answer open review findings) now lights the PR in progress chevron — "Waiting for @who · rerun shared ci on GitHub" — and leaves the Merge queue column empty; only rows actually queued / merging, or a merge-ready PR parked on a merge decision, sit in Merge queue.
- The dashboard backend switch (`POST /api/switch/{agent}/{backend}`, `PUT /api/config/agent/{name}/models`, and ACMM pack backend moves) now clears a `launch_cmd` that launches the previous CLI instead of persisting `backend: codex` next to `launch_cmd: /usr/bin/bob …`; `hive.yaml` and per-agent overlay saves refuse that contradiction with a 400 and a dashboard alert; and when a hive boots with the contradiction already in its base config the loader drops the stale `launch_cmd`, keeps the backend, logs an ERROR and raises a per-agent dashboard alert instead of exiting — a stale `launch_cmd` used to crash-loop the hive until someone hand-edited the PVC.
- The Merge-eligible band ("nothing needed; it merges on its own") holds only pull requests Hive will merge. The auto-merge label used to put a PR there whatever its verdict, so projectbluefin/server#583 (a red check) and #613 (GitHub refusing the merge) sat there. Now the label counts only before the sweep has a verdict and only when nothing blocks the PR; the sweep's own eligible verdict still decides. In a repo whose auto-merge is off, a PR held only by a Hive-side gate (a contributor-lane refusal, a red check nobody declared required) is a hand merge in the your-turn inbox, its reason naming both. projectbluefin/documentation#1668 and projectbluefin/actions#697 had shown no reason at all.
- The reviewer now carries a person's recorded decision across up to five consecutive hive base refreshes, not just one, so two App merge-from-base commits landing before any gate reads the PR no longer force a re-decision; every hop must still be an App-authored merge of the base that leaves the diff unchanged ([#15766](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15766)).
- Stage engine / fix loop: a PR whose every failing check is also red on the base branch tip (and whose diff does not touch workflows, Dockerfiles or go.mod) stays at 050/060 with reason `base-branch-red:<checks>` instead of 070/071/072, consumes no fix-loop attempts, posts one hold comment per head, and a hive-raised `needs-human` over such a head is removed automatically; kick builders list these PRs separately from repair targets.
- Fix a data race in the beads store: `Update` (and so `SetMetadata`, `Claim`, `Close`, `AddDependency`) now edits a private copy of the bead and swaps it in, so readers holding a bead from `Get`/`List` — e.g. the run checkpoint plan tree during a concurrent plan approval — see a stable snapshot instead of a map being written under them.
- Blocked sweep: a contributor relay's `blocked` verdict is no longer lifted every few minutes. The relay labels with its hub-minted task token, so GitHub records the hive's own App bot as the actor, and the marker-less lift added for review-backlog twins ([#13364](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13364)) took it for a hive defect: the issue went back to the ready band, the next agent hit the same blocker and the relay re-applied the label, daily. The marker-less lift now applies only to review-backlog items (body carries `filed by Hive review backlog`) that GitHub reports no open "blocked by" link on; every other marker-less `blocked` stays for a person to lift (`/hive approve`, [#7924](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7924)).
- A `blocked` label that names nothing is no longer a dead end. A contributor relay's blocked verdict that named no issue or PR used to leave `blocked` with no marker: before 10-28 the sweep lifted it and the next relay re-blocked it (projectbluefin/utah#771 cycled 19 times); since then it stuck and the issue showed in no inbox ("labelled blocked — the label records no reason"). The blocked sweep now turns such a hive-applied block into a `needs-human` ask with one note, a verdict whose reason is empty or only the relay footer is booked idle with its label released (projectbluefin/utah#1002), and a blocked-on marker in a comment (projectbluefin/finpilot#624, #390) now names the blocker in the row reason and the band signal.
- Dashboard: a blocked issue waiting on another issue now names it in the stage tracker caption
- **Blocked on an issue, not only a PR.** The blocked-on marker now has an issue form, `<!-- hive:blocked-on issue=owner/repo#N -->`, read from the issue body or its newest marker comment: the blocked sweep keeps `blocked` while that issue is open (stripping only `help wanted`), lifts it with one `<!-- hive:unblocked -->` note once it closes, and never lifts it as marker-less; a malformed issue marker counts as no marker and PR markers behave as before. The contributor prompt asks an agent that prints `blocked` on a GitHub issue to put that marker on its comment. Before, a hive-applied `blocked` for an issue dependency was lifted as marker-less, so projectbluefin/utah#10 and #855 went back to triage and were re-verified "still blocked" again and again.
- bob 2.x's busy indicator ("⠇ Processing… (Enter to steer, Tab to queue)") is now recognised as an in-progress turn. Previously a kicked bob turn was classified as ended ~30s after delivery while bob was still working, so the kick outcome settled early and the turn-end kick log archive under 🕘 past kicks was a mid-run snapshot rather than the full run.
- Fixed the GitHub enumerator's closed-PR attribution scan so it is bounded by recent updates, capped at five pages, cached across ticks, and no longer fails repo enumeration when the closed-PR scan encounters a transient GitHub error.
- Report boundary enforcement as demonstrated when observed writes were blocked, not a refusal-rate grade; keep zero, Sentinel detections, and coverage limitations informational.
- Keep historical terminal-PR accounting off current-work claim evaluation with cancellable bounded review batches, retained retries, and idempotent timeline persistence; preserve synchronous fail-closed claim safety and durable first observations.
- The image CA-distrust check parses only the probe's stdout, so the arm64 lane built under QEMU no longer fails on docker's platform warning; unexpected docker errors are now printed.
- The hive's routine "everything since a time" GitHub reads can now be answered with free `304`s. The un-park sweep's comment reads, the closed-issue stage sweep, the review backlog split, the shared-CI rerun sweep and the same-component check built their `since=` from the current clock, so the URL changed on every pass and the ETag cache (keyed on the full URL) never matched. On a hosted hive with 20 repos on 2026-11-07, untagged issue-comment lists were answered `304` only 51% of the time and issue lists only 28%, against 83% to 91% for the pull-request lists, while the hive needed about 8,250 calls an hour against a 7,000 limit. The `since` sent to GitHub is now rounded down to the hour; each sweep still filters on its exact cutoff, so nothing is missed. The calls the periodic sweeps, the governor cycle, the state cache, the metrics collector, the request watchers, the mention poller and dashboard requests make are now named in `/api/gh-rate-limits` (`hive:<sweep>`) instead of all reading as `hive`.
- Cadence matrix no longer shows a green working dot for an agent that is paused or has no cadence in the current mode; the active-mode cell reads "no cadence" to match the row badge.
- Clarify that campaign release only releases Inception pickup leases and preserves both contributor-held and pending Spektacular stage leases.
- Fix inception Campaigns Revise/Continue actions to update the stable campaign in place and collapse duplicate revision archives on load.
- "Let hive decide" on an issue parked because the GitHub App lacks a permission (the scanner's "cannot push `.github/workflows/*` (no `workflows` permission); needs a human") no longer un-parks it only for the next sweep to re-park it: the report is recorded as a structured blocker (`<!-- hive:blocker kind=capability:workflows-permission -->`, inferred from the prose when the marker is missing), the delegated decision returns no-effect with the plain-words reason and the ways out (grant the permission with a link to the App settings, re-check permissions, mark partially addressed and close, keep waiting), a loop guard disables the delegate once the same reason comes back after a delegated un-park, `stage/045-needs-decision` and `approved-direction` no longer coexist, the tracker row reads "Blocked · App lacks workflows permission", and ⚙ → Security plus `/api/status.capabilities` name the missing permissions and how many items wait on them ([#15099](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15099)).
- Activity Monitor: the merge celebration (✓ glow, token to "Merged today") now plays for a PR drawn inline on its issue's row — before, only the counter ticked because such rows carried no sub-row key; rows stamp the PR keys they draw and ⚙ → Merges gains a **Test celebration** button. Reported by @clubanderson.
- Dashboard Channel card: when the last spoke-side upgrade was superseded by an external roll (`kubectl rollout restart`, image bump, floating-tag pull), the `↷ Running <sha>` headline now ages the running build (`releaseStatus.attempt.runningSince`, flagged `rolledExternally`) instead of the day-old superseded upgrade; the superseded note moves to a secondary line with its own timestamp, and the version menu's "Last upgrade" says "superseded (rolled externally, now <sha>)" rather than a bare "succeeded".
- Fixed Hive Chat and Discord agent lifecycle messages so completed/working notices show useful summaries and links instead of captured CLI TUI footer chrome.
- Dashboard chat now authenticates to the local dashboard with the resolved dashboard auth token (file or DASHBOARD_AUTH_TOKEN), not only HIVE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN; fixes HTTP 401 on `!runs`, heartbeat and `!runs spec` on hosted spokes.
- Hive Chat now answers the question it was asked instead of a canned dump. The server used to tokenise every message into a bag of words and match on keywords alone, so `/agents stuck`, `/agents scanner status` and "Which agent completed last?" all returned the full agent roster and `/prs waiting on review` returned per-repo PR counts, with the arguments silently discarded. A new router keeps the arguments: a bare `/agents`, `/prs`, `/beads` or `/status` still prints its summary, while a command with arguments or a plain-words question is answered by one read-only model turn over a compact, scoped snapshot of the hive state the dashboard already holds (agents with blockers, last kick and last completed action; open PRs with stage labels, review state, CI and age; actionable issues; items awaiting a decision; governor; alerts; version and last upgrade), instructed to say "I don't have that data" rather than guess and to cite the items it used. The turn runs on the governor reviewer endpoint with a timeout and in-flight cap, writes one `chat_grounded_answer` audit line, and can never trigger an action. When grounding is unavailable a scoped question gets the command's usage, never the bare dump. New setting `chat.grounded_answers.enabled` (default on) and `chat.grounded_answers.model`.
- Fixed Hive Chat free-text inputs so common questions get local answers and unavailable responders return a visible message instead of appearing silent.
- The action-pins CI gate (`src/scripts/check-action-pins.sh`) no longer reports `action pin check FAILED` with no finding when a workflow directory contains no SHA-pinned `uses:` lines (pipefail turned grep's empty match into a failure), and its `NOT-PINNED` message now names the workflow file rather than the line number where the file name belonged. The resolver reports every missing SHA instead of stopping at the first, and the gate now has a hermetic self-test, `src/scripts/test-check-action-pins.sh`, covering each of its failure branches.
- Hive activity monitor: the stage-chevron pulse and needs-human breathe now animate only the opacity of an overlay (compositor thread) instead of `filter` / `background` on the chevron, so an idle dashboard tab no longer restyles the page every frame.
- Hive activity monitor: stage chevrons no longer pulse for Open, Open · hold, Claimed or any other waiting step; only a step the hive is acting on (gentle pulse) or one waiting on a person (slower amber→red breathe) animates, and `prefers-reduced-motion` silences both.
- Activity Monitor stage tracker: a PR head whose checks are still reporting now reads `CI running · 4 checks pending` (chevron `CI 7/11 · 4 running`, or the last one or two unfinished names) instead of `CI activity unknown · last observed missing` / `CI unknown · no check results observed` / `no verdict yet`; a required check with no run while others still execute is one sentence in the tooltip rather than the "missing" verdict; the "no check results observed" wording is reserved for a head with zero check runs; and the chevron tooltip states each fact once (count word, detail sentence, head, source, observation time) instead of repeating the unreported check four times (#16630). Check names embedded in captions and chevron text are wrapped in single quotes.
- A red check run another PR produced on a shared head no longer counts against a PR. projectbluefin/utah-packages#890, an in-repo copy of the fork PR #878 at the same SHA, went to `stage/072-returned-to-contributor` for "Failing checks: Canary" on #878's fork Canary run, 41 seconds after it opened and before its own Canary had started. Check runs are now attributed by PR: a run naming other PRs, or a run naming none whose workflow run had a different head repository or branch (the branch alone for another app's suite), is not this PR's. Failed lookups keep the run.
- CI_FAILING repair queue keeps non-adopted fork PRs comment-only even when the fork allows maintainer edits; only stage-074 adopted fork PRs are listed as push-repairable, and those name the contributor branch.
- Retry CI-failure webhook kicks with bounded backoff when the owning agent is busy, then drain a bounded per-PR/check pending queue on governor evaluations; discard resolved signals when checks pass or PRs close.
- `TestBootDashboardWithClassifier` no longer races: `bootDashboardWith` starts the merged-PR lifecycle backfill in a goroutine that logs through the boot logger, so the test's log sink is now the goroutine-safe `syncLogBuffer` instead of a bare `strings.Builder` ([#13168](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13168), [#13169](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13169), [#13170](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13170)).
