- `TestCampaignDeleteRemovesArchiveOnly` is order-independent again: it now resets the process-wide lifecycle timeline store before listing campaigns, so completed-run journeys recorded by earlier tests in a shuffled run no longer appear as a third campaign ([#13167](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13167)).
- `TestGFISweepReleaseAndConvertWiring` no longer flakes: it now waits for the release goroutine's final state transition (labelled key cleared, `Released` stat bumped) instead of only the forge side effects, which could be observed before the stats were updated ([#13048](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13048)).
- The goose ACP probe seam (`runGooseACPProbe`) is now guarded by an RWMutex, mirroring the copilot SDK helper seam, so a background CLI-model refresh started by one test can no longer race with the next test swapping the probe (`TestQueryCLIModels_GooseUsesProvider` data race) ([#13047](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13047)).
- `TestKickHitsTheEscapedEndpointExactlyOnceAndRendersTheQueuedStatus` now gates the fixture's kick response while the three `K` presses are delivered, so the `kickPending` bound is asserted inside the in-flight window instead of racing the first response ([#13191](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13191)).
- CI flake coverage for dashboard workspace cleanup, sandbox state transitions, and fixture startup now uses race-safe workspace root access and deterministic readiness/completion signals instead of short polling windows.
- Activity Monitor: a CI ring that is not yet full now renders the CI chevron active ("CI 13/19 · running") beside a running Review instead of a silent part-green glyph; check-run motion on the head leads red, unreported or ambiguous neighbours, and icon-only green is reserved for a complete ring (hivecommons/hive#16631).
- Prevent repeated scanner sweeps from being reported as CI polling by counting repeated reads within each kick, excluding earlier kicks' reads ([#14061](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14061)).
- CI failure log reads (`gh run view --log` and `--log-failed`) no longer trigger stop-polling nudges or fleet reports while agents diagnose failed jobs.
- The CI-poll stop nudge and `ci_poll_nudge` self-report now also skip replica and variant names of the exempt `ci-maintainer` and `quality` lanes (e.g. `ci-maintainer-2`), not only the exact lane name (#14719).
- The `ci_poll_nudge` fleet self-report now fires only when an agent polled CI more than once since the kick; a single post-push check still gets the in-session nudge but no longer files a report.
- Stop the CI-poll wall-clock nudge from interrupting a long scanner sweep that reads each PR once; a lone poll or a repeated read past the wall clock is still nudged ([#14066](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14066)).
- Detect verified current-head GitHub Actions workflow/check reporting stalls after bounded consistency observations, expose exact run/attempt provenance and owner action without changing CI gates or automatically rerunning workflows.
- Bound ARC runner pod ephemeral storage and documented the node-spread patch so self-hosted CI no longer overpacks node-local disks before jobs start.
- CI runner image: bumped the pinned `gh` to 2.103.3 (the apt repo only serves the latest), and the daily CLI pin bump now keeps that pin current, including `gh` patch releases.
- A PR hive opens now records its issue claims in the duplicate-PR claim ledger immediately, so a contributor can no longer be admitted to an issue that PR already covers in the window before the next claim scan (#14472).
- The duplicate-PR guard no longer drops a PR claim the webhook recorded after the claim scan's listing began; the issue stayed covered until the next scan re-listed the PR instead of being re-offered and getting a second PR ([#15559](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15559) saw #15561 and #15567).
- Issue stage records no longer regress to `010-actionable` on a claim release while the duplicate-PR claim ledger holds an open PR that covers the issue: the out-of-cycle stage facts consult the ledger (not only the store's memory) and re-derive `040-covered-by-pr`; a merged `pull_request` webhook now runs close-on-merge for that PR's issues at once instead of waiting for the next reconcile pass; and every eval cycle (cached ones included) backfills store records that sit below 040 under an open ledger claim, so the scanner stops being re-offered issues an open PR already fixes.
- Claim-hook retry settings are now read under a lock, fixing a data race between a lingering claim-effect goroutine and a test swapping them ([#14839](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14839)).
- Activity Monitor: a clanker-authored PR that a trusted human sends back with a CHANGES_REQUESTED review now shows **Returned to contributor** (072, actor the owning contributor, caption `Returned to @thatguywob's hive — @clubanderson requested changes`) instead of `Sentinel alert · needs human` — the human's review on the current head is the human the sentinel, hold and workflow-path parks were waiting for, so the sentinel pass no longer re-asserts 085 over 072 until a new head re-arms it (per head, like the dashboard Approve release). The same holds for a return placed by hand: when a trusted maintainer removes `stage/085` and adds `stage/071`/`stage/072` themselves, the reconciler reads the label event, records it against the head and keeps the stage instead of logging `added=[stage/085] removed=[stage/072-returned-to-contributor]`. "Needs author" (071) stays a person's PR. The dashboard **Give direction** decision is accepted on clanker PRs too: the direction is posted to the contributor's hive as a change request and the row moves to 072; the 409 "the hive did not open this pull request" is kept only for a person's PR, which no hive can carry direction to. The 071/072 chevron keeps its routing word with any sentinel finding as a ` · sentinel` suffix ([#15159](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15159)).
- Stage labels: `needs-triage` is now removed in the same label write that moves an issue to 020-claimed or later (including a direct claim from 015), open issues already claimed and still wearing it are reconciled on the next sweep, and the Hive activity monitor no longer reads a stale `needs-triage` as "Triage needed" on a claimed row — it shows the stage and lists the leftover label as `stale_labels` in a muted tooltip line (#14644).
- The dashboard CLI-model last-good tests no longer expire 24 hours after their fixture date: the cache constructor now takes its clock before loading persisted catalogs (#12036).
- Hive and contributor image builds retry Cline installation with fresh npm metadata up to four times to tolerate transient registry propagation failures ([#16666](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16666)).
- Agents on the `cline` backend are no longer refused for a connection Hive added itself. Hive adds a `hive-task` connection for its own task MCP endpoint to every agent, and the Cline policy check counted it as operator configuration, so a `backend: cline` agent with no `tools` or `connections` of its own was refused in its pane and on sandbox kicks with "Cline cannot enforce Hive tools/connections configuration". That connection no longer counts. An agent with its own `tools` or connections, or a `hive-task` connection that points anywhere else or carries its own `auth`, `env_name` or `options`, is refused as before.
- Close-on-merge backfill now reads a pull request that cross-references an issue from another repo in that PR's own repo, instead of looking up the same number in the issue's repo and logging a 404 warning every pass.
- close-on-merge no longer closes a pull request as a "fixed issue" when a merged sibling-repo PR mentions it (#14744).
- Close-on-merge no longer closes an issue a merged PR only references. The backfill sweep passed the configured short repository name (`utah-packages`) into the close path, and the `Refs` guard compared it with the parsed `owner/repo`, so `Refs #490` on projectbluefin/utah-packages#860 looked like no reference and #490 was closed with "Fixed by #860". References now compare as `owner/repo`. The close path reads the same non-closing decision as the coverage comment (`Refs`/`Part of`, or "#N stays open"). An issue carrying `hive/verified-open` or `hive/partially-addressed` is closed only by a PR whose own text closes it. `GET /api/close-on-merge/wrong-closes?days=N` lists issues closed the wrong way for maintainers to reopen.
- A merged pull request from another repository listed under `closedByPullRequestsReferences` is no longer reported as a same-repo closer, so tracker chips cannot link an issue to an unrelated PR ([#15494](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15494)).
- Automerge no longer caches a 404'd closing-keyword target as not-a-PR for the process lifetime; it is re-read after 10 minutes (#15120).
- Stop calling a PR merge-eligible while GitHub holds it for a code owner's review. A ruleset `pull_request` rule with `require_code_owner_review: true` and `required_approving_review_count: 0` (or classic protection's `require_code_owner_reviews`) makes GitHub report `reviewDecision: null` on a `blocked` PR, so Hive read it as "required checks green; ignoring non-required GitHub blockers" and the serialized lane cycled such PRs through the front for the full front timeout without ever surfacing them. The protection facts now record the code-owner rule for a blocked PR with no review decision, and `HumanReviewBlocksMerge` reports `code-owner review required by ruleset "<name>"`: the merge verdict skips the PR and the your-turn inbox shows it as a review for a person, as for `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (hivecommons/hive#12953).
- Fix hub-launched Codex agents so they run unattended with approvals/sandbox bypassed, classify Codex approval/update prompts, and seed CODEX_HOME to disable startup update checks.
- Kicks are no longer silently lost when a Codex agent's TUI is sitting in a menu or modal ([#13765](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13765)). Codex menus such as `/hooks` keep a `›` selection caret that the readiness check mistook for the input prompt, so the manager typed kick after kick into the menu, each turn "ended" with no output, and the review swarm spent every retry on a pane that never received them. Before typing a kick the manager now recognises known Codex menu footers (`esc back`, `esc close`, `enter details`), sends `Escape` (up to three times, re-checking after each) and only types once the prompt is back. If the menu does not close, the kick is marked undeliverable with the reason `prompt-not-ready: menu footer "…"` — shown in the logs and the dashboard busy reason — and is not recorded as delivered. Backends without known menu footers behave exactly as before.
- With `review.combined_perspectives: true`, review kicks are now spread across every eligible reviewer instead of always going to the first one in name order. Each combined kick goes to the reviewer with the fewest PR heads still pending on it, counting kicks planned in the same cycle. Before this, every combined review queued on one agent, so additional reviewers and `replicas:` copies sat idle and raising `review.max_parallel_reviews` only lengthened that agent's queue.
- `hivectl hives web` and `hivectl tui --hives` contribution tree, from a first-time / power-user / keyboard-and-screen-reader sweep: membership is discovered on load, errors show beside Apply instead of far down the page, repeated buttons carry their target in their accessible name (roving Tab stop, skip links, `<main>`), unrestricted Hives read "can receive all N" instead of "0/N selected" and no longer mask restricted siblings in a hub headline, Collapse/Expand all, `/` to search with a result count, "Select N matching repositories", plain-language receipt and diff, a glossary, readable contrast in light and dark mode, and no horizontal scroll at 320 px.
- `hivectl hives web`: the page embedded its session token double-quoted, so every API call sent `X-Hive-Commons-Token` with literal quote characters and was rejected with 401 — the contribution tree and profile table never loaded, showing only "unauthorized". The token is now embedded as a single JS string literal.
- Ground weekly competitor reports in revision-pinned upstream source and dated evidence, and block publication or automatic work when provenance or existing-work checks fail.
- Editing a disabled or ACMM-gated agent's configuration no longer reports a missing runtime process as a repeated sync failure ([#16798](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16798)).
- Restart an agent on a non-inference backend whose live CLI pane stays on a consent or blocking-prompt menu after repeated undeliverable kicks, instead of leaving it wedged with every kick failing as "CLI did not reach input prompt" and never reported (#12921).
- Continuous-mode agents no longer idle forever when the manager misses a turn-end signal: the governor presumes a kicked turn over after `continuous_turn_ceiling` (default 45m) and re-arms the next kick, so a stuck reviewer resumes instead of leaving PRs at `stage/050-review-pending` until a pod restart.
- Local-mode contributors no longer start with a sandbox that cannot run anything, and `just contribute-stop` now stops local relays. `just contribute-hive claude local` (and `litellm`) runs a sandboxed `true` through bubblewrap before the relay connects; on Ubuntu, where the `bwrap-userns-restrict` AppArmor profile or `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1` makes every agent command fail, it stops with that cause and points to container mode. A `HIVE_VERDICT` whose reason says the agent's own environment is broken (for example "environment failure", "Bash tool broken", `apply-seccomp`) is classified `blocked` and handed back as an `environment` task failure instead of being booked as a completed task. `just contribute-stop` also stops the relay named in `~/.config/hive/contributor-relay.pid` and its tmux session, and a local start refuses to run beside a live local relay instead of starting a second one under the same contributor ID ([#14832](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14832), [#14833](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14833)).
- Improved the contributor Management tab layout so admin controls read as grouped settings sections on desktop and mobile.
- Fix the contribute queue holding an issue as "already claimed by a PR" after a PR that only said `Refs #N` merged. Such a PR landed part of the work and left the issue open for the rest, so the issue now goes back to contributors, as it already did for agents (#7061). A merged `Refs #N` also ranks below every open PR in the claim ledger, so it never hides someone's open PR on the same issue. The contribute-ws `skip:` admission lines are now logged when an item is first withheld or its reason changes, not on every pass.
- Dashboard: the no-OAuth `/contribute/register` page now HTML-escapes the request host when rendering the example curl command (#13353).
- A contributor relay PR reported for a dispatched issue now gets `Fixes #N` appended (when its body neither closes the issue nor says it stays open) and the GitHub sidebar link, so the PR-claim ledger and the issue list see the issue as covered instead of leaving it Actionable while the PR waits in review as "no linked issue" ([#14763](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14763)).
- `contribute-hive` / the contributor relay no longer point a clanker at the retired `*.hive.kubestellar.io` hosted-hive domain: a `contributor.env` saved before the move is relocated to `*.hive.hivecommons.dev` in memory with a one-time warning naming the file, and a TLS "does not match certificate's altnames" error now parks the hub with a single remediation line (re-resolving a hosted hive once via the hub registry) instead of reconnecting every 16 s forever ([#14609](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14609)).
- Contributor dispatch now reads every spelling the scanner uses for an issue's release-line declaration — `**Target branch:** \`v6\``, `Target-branch: v6` and an inline `… Target: v6 (open the PR with --base v6)` — so the task prompt names the declared base instead of the hub branch and the contributor no longer has to answer `wrong_base` ([#14764](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14764)).
- The Commons contribution editor reports partial staging failures honestly, prevents overlapping batch actions, and explains runtime uncertainty, offering status, selection provenance and exclusion recovery.
- Keep TUI contribution reviews within terminal height, with wrapped target identities, keyboard scrolling, persistent Apply/Back hints, and Apply paused when the terminal is too small to review.
- Contributor images now select Bob 1.x/2.x launch flags at runtime and accept both `BOB_API_KEY` and legacy `BOBSHELL_API_KEY` credentials, matching hub-side agents (#14334).
- Contributor drop cool-off is scoped per contributor: a relay that repeatedly drops an issue is cooled off from that issue for the cool-off period, while other contributors are still offered it. The resume cool-off refusal and the resume claim re-assert paths now have test coverage (#13763, #13767).
- Contributor-lane PRs no longer park at `stage/085-needs-decision` on a reviewer decision marker or bare `requires_human` while they are in CI/Review. The only early exit is a concrete security / trust finding (`review.IsSecuritySensitiveFinding`: reviewer high-risk marker, security perspective hold, security-class question, finding on a sensitive path — `sentinel.sensitive_paths` plus the new `security.sensitive_paths` — or insecure behaviour flagged), recorded as `decision_finding` and printed by the 085 comment and tracker as `the review found: …`. Everything else goes back to the clanker or is advisory and the PR moves on to the merge gate, where an untrusted author's PR parks at `stage/090-ready-for-human-merge` for the operator's merge — never auto-merged (#15640).
- Review swarm verdicts recorded with an abbreviated `head_sha` (e.g. `98489e7`) are now widened to the full head at the relay and matched by prefix everywhere the lanes look them up (contributor-lane verdict gate, merge-eligibility aggregate, dispatch planning, review queue), so contributor PRs whose current head the swarm already judged get that verdict instead of sitting at `contributor-lane:no-verdict`; the CI-snapshot evidence bundle is keyed by `owner/name` and carries `base_sha` from the GraphQL batch, so it no longer fails validation as `repo "hive" must be owner/name` / `base_sha is required`; and the stage tracker caption names the head it awaits ("awaiting review of head <sha7>").
- A contributor-lane PR on a hive whose review swarm is off no longer waits at `050-review-pending` forever. `auto_merge.contributor_lane.require_reviewer_verdict` (default on) wanted a reviewer verdict whenever a reviewer agent existed, but the review planner only asks reviewers when `review.require_approval` and `review.fan_out` are both on. On a self-hosted spoke with the swarm off, twelve green docs PRs sat at "Review swarm requested; waiting for a verdict" with the Review track reading "0/5 · in progress" and nothing dispatched. Such a head now skips as `contributor-lane:review-off` and parks at `085-needs-decision` with that cause, and the Activity Monitor's Review track says a person must review instead of "in progress".
- Kept the Contributors sidebar count and cards on one roster snapshot, and replaced relay IDs in its online tooltip with GitHub usernames without repeated ClankeR labels.
- Avoid filing repeated-error reports for contributor-lane sweeps deferred by GitHub combined-status HTTP 500 responses; the sweep still fails closed and retries.
- Every contributor trust-tier change (operator trust/revoke, newcomer→contributor auto-promotion, registration) now appends `{tier, prev, at, by, reason, source}` to the contributor's `tier_history`, writes a `contributor-tier-changed` audit event, and is shown as "tier since … · by … · reason" on the Contributors view and in `GET /api/contributors`; same-tier writes are no-ops. The stage lane re-reads the author's registry tier every sweep — including for PRs parked on needs-rebase/hold/excluded labels — so a promotion or demotion reaches parked PRs on the next pass instead of sticking to the stale `role/*` label ([#15177](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15177)).
- Expected contributor concurrency, hourly, and daily tier-limit refusals no longer generate repeated runtime-error self-reports; the warnings and task limits remain intact (#14414).
- Repeated copilot sniff upstream read timeouts now log one WARN per window instead of one per request, so transient network timeouts no longer trip fleet self-reports ([#15356](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15356)).
- Cost chart and daily rollup keep large session-flush steps that reach a new high instead of discarding them at the $500 discontinuity floor; only restores of already-reached ground are dropped (#13497)
- The dashboard Cost panel's cost / PR and cost / issue tiles no longer show "—" (or fall back to the merged-by-hive counter, which is 0 at ACMM L5) on hives with many repos: the hive-attributed count reconciled every configured repo in one burst — 38–76 Search API calls for 19 repos against GitHub's 30/minute limit — so it failed every hour and never produced a baseline. The reconcile now asks about a budgeted slice of repos per paced pass, direct search counts batch `repo:` qualifiers into a few queries, partial progress is served and labelled (`count_partial`) instead of discarded, a refusal keeps the last attributed count stale, and the reason is surfaced as `count_error` in `/api/cost` and the tile tooltip.
- Cost chart: an increment is now spread back only over the stretch its own model's counter sat flat, never past that counter's previous rise, so a model recorded in real time (the proxy's Copilot capture) no longer smears each 5‑minute step across the previous 24 h — the first day of live recording had drawn ~$860 on the day before it (whose own record was $1.19) and left the earlier ~$1 days under a pixel; bars with any spend now keep a visible minimum height beside a much taller day, and the hourly view places spend in the hour it was recorded.
- Fix dashboard cost-per-PR and cost-per-issue divisors for App-authored multi-repo hives, preserving persisted counts instead of showing false zeroes when GitHub counts are unavailable.
- cost: price `claude-fable-5.1` at the Fable 5 list rate and prune per-agent `/data/home/agents/<agent>/.copilot/session-state` trees with the same retention as the shared tree (#13488, #13491)
- Cost section: the bar chart, "spend in selected range" and the run-rate now all derive from the one window the range selector names — hourly = 24 one-hour bars, daily = the last 7 calendar days as weekday bars, weekly = the current Mon→Sun week as weekday bars, monthly = the current calendar month as one bar per day, custom = hour bars up to 2 days and day bars beyond. The run-rate is the window's spend over its elapsed length (per hour for hourly bars, per day otherwise) instead of a fixed trailing 6 h, so switching the selector updates the chart and both summary figures together. Previously weekly/monthly drew 12 multi-week bars across 84/360 days.
- The Cost card now warns when the running agents' models have recorded no usage for over 24 hours and marks the run-rate "(recording incomplete)", backed by a new `recording` block on `/api/cost` ([#13485](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13485)).
- CI coverage job now allows 30 minutes for two sequential `go test` passes, up from 20 minutes, to prevent cancellations on green runs (#15266).
- crux `logs -f` / `run` streaming and the server `follow=1` log endpoint now stream by ring-buffer offset, so repeated lines and bursts are no longer dropped or duplicated.
- `crux` `agentsmd.ParseNearest` now resolves and confines the starting directory to the repository root before its first `os.Stat`, so a relative path escaping the root (or a sibling such as `repo-other` next to `repo`, which the old separator-less prefix check admitted) falls back to the root `AGENTS.md` instead of parsing a foreign file as the repository's own ([crux#50](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/50)).
- crux: `governor.bob.api_key_file` is now resolved through the same managed-secrets-directory check as the LiteLLM, gateway and inference key files.
- `crux serve` now honours `n` on `GET /v1/agents/{name}/logs?follow=1`, replaying only the last `n` buffered lines (none for `n=0`) before streaming, and `crux --server ADDR logs -n N -f` sends it, so the follow no longer prints the whole 200-line window regardless of `-n`; without `n` the replay is unchanged ([hivecommons/crux#70](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/70)).
- crux proxy: `topLevelMutationFields` now reads block strings and `#` comments inside GraphQL argument lists the same way it does in selection sets, so a `"""..."""` holding a lone quote (or a commented quote) in a mutation's arguments can no longer desynchronise the scan and hide later top-level fields from the capability check (hivecommons/crux#54)
- Crux guardrail path matching now normalises redundant separators and `.`/`..` components before matching protected paths
- Distinguish durable lane broker initialization conflicts from unavailability without exposing backend details, and expose stable lane error-code constants while preserving existing HTTP responses.
- `crux logs` now rejects a negative `-n` with a usage error instead of panicking (hivecommons/crux#59).
- crux: the permissions watcher now chowns and chmods each walked entry through the descriptor it opened, mirroring fixModeFile, so the entry it reported is the entry it changes.
- The crux proxy's canary scan of GitHub write bodies now refuses a request whose body could not be fully read, matching the Linear gate and the oversized-body path. Before, a read error consumed the body and still let the request through, so it reached GitHub empty and unscanned.
- The Crux publish script no longer deletes `runbooks/` in `hivecommons/crux` on every sync
- `crux-publish.sh` now rewrites relative `../docs/` links in the published `docs/MODULE.md` to absolute hive URLs pinned to the synced hive commit, fixing dead links in hivecommons/crux.
- crux/pushbroker: successful pushes now record `finished_at` in the audit result (previously only failures did) ([#14529](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14529)).
- The `crux` module README (published as `docs/MODULE.md` in hivecommons/crux) now shows `crux logs -n 50 scout` instead of `crux logs scout -n 50`; `crux logs` parses flags with a standard `flag.FlagSet`, which stops at the first positional argument, so the documented order exited with the usage error instead of printing output ([hivecommons/crux#72](https://github.com/hivecommons/crux/issues/72)).
- `crux serve --listen` now refuses a non-loopback bind (`0.0.0.0`, `::`, `:port`, or a remote address) even when a bearer token is set, and `crux/api.ParseAddress` refuses `http://` or bare `host:port` for a non-loopback host: the TCP listener is plain http, so the token would otherwise cross the network in cleartext. Expose the API remotely through a TLS-terminating proxy that dials the loopback listener, or reach it with `https://`. The shared rule is `api.LoopbackHost`.
- Collect review outputs for open PRs without rereading every historical report, request only missing current-body perspectives, settle reviewer slots only from fresh report receipts, preserve newer verdicts against late collection/restamps, and log collection lag plus pending versus delivery-confirmed occupancy.
- Hub dashboard: the Hives table's "Showing N of M assigned hives · K filter(s) active" summary now lists each active selection as a removable chip (`Alert: Stale advisory ×`, `Search: kalantar ×`, `Location: cluster-a ×`, …) beside the count, so a table narrowed by a filter set from outside the collapsed FILTERS drawer — an alert-type chip in Attention needed, a usage-rollup row writing the search box, or a saved default view restored on load — is never a one-row mystery; clicking a chip removes just that filter. The Fleet quadrant card above the table no longer claims "N hives in view": its median is computed server-side over the whole fleet and never followed the table's filters, so it now reads "all N hives" and, while the table is narrowed, adds "(table filters not applied)" (#13079).
- Dashboard chat and Spektacular hub-executor tests are now isolated from shuffled CI state, so local status answers and synthetic cleanup ticks no longer depend on unrelated run projections or wall-clock cleanup scheduling.
- Dashboard: the infinite "pulse" indicators (working-agent dots, status dots, stale agent cards; the activity monitor chevrons are handled separately) now animate only `opacity` on an overlay instead of `filter`, `box-shadow` or `border-color`, so they run on the compositor thread. An idle dashboard tab with the activity monitor open was spending ~70% of a CPU core re-styling, painting and layerizing the whole page every frame; measured with ~70k DOM nodes and 113 running animations, animations accounted for the bulk of main-thread time. Knowledge-base fact cards also use `content-visibility: auto`, so the thousands of cards scrolled out of the 500px list no longer get laid out and painted.
- The dashboard header bug button now opens the feedback form directly (the form tab is labelled "New report" instead of "Submit"; "My reports" stays one click away), and a failed feedback submission now shows the HTTP status and the server's error message (or the trimmed response body) in the toast, with every rejected report also logged server-side, instead of an uninformative error ([#13144](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13144), [#13145](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13145)).
- Dashboard header: the feedback and theme buttons no longer overlap the ACMM level badge on ~900-1400px viewports ([#13135](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13135)).
- Dashboard history APIs now bound chart responses, accept timestamp cutoffs, and support conditional requests; cost polling transfers only new full-resolution samples, launch-cost detail is bounded without changing totals, and status snapshots support ETag revalidation ([#13789](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13789)).
- Dashboard idle-CPU remainder (#13764): `stage-tracker` SSE nudges from status publishes and webhook invalidations are now coalesced to at most one frame per ~2s (a burst collapses into one trailing frame with the newest seq), and `/api/stage-tracker`'s ETag no longer hashes `generated_at`, so an unchanged tracker revalidates as a 304 instead of a full 200 on every rebuild. Open tabs stop refetching and re-rendering the tracker once per webhook. The 304 carries `X-Hive-Stage-Tracker-Generated-At`, `Last-Modified` and the source header so the "updated" chip stays truthful on a quiet hive.
- Dashboard tabs pause registered refresh timers while hidden, reuse date formatters, and release finished sparkline animation effects to reduce idle CPU and retained rendering work.
- Saved dashboard layouts no longer sink the Runs and Overview sections to the bottom of the page ([#10397](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10397)). A one-character regression in `dashboardLayoutNormalize` inserted missing sections after the anchor instead of before it; it was hidden because the dashboard shuffle and rest CI jobs ran without Node, silently skipping 39 node-backed tests ([#10398](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10398)). Those jobs now set up Node 22 so the tests run.
- dashboard: "PRs by model" rank now uses a confidence-weighted score (Wilson 95% lower bound of first-pass merge rate × (1 − fail) × (1 − no ship)) instead of raw first-pass %, folds model-id spellings (provider prefix, `:variant`, `5-5`→`5.5`) into one row with the raw ids in the tooltip, lists unattributed rows unranked at the bottom, renders the metric column labels once in a sticky header with `?` tooltips, and explains the formula and each column in the help text (#15618).
- Fix dashboard clipping and overflow on desktop and phones: wrap complete navigation, repository, issue/PR, model and knowledge labels; adapt activity pipelines, agent cards, overview legends and readiness rows to their actual width; keep settings tabs and wide tables locally scrollable; and fit chat panels, pressure/timeline labels plus cost, audit and diagnostics controls inside their available space.
- dashboard: a long-open tab no longer freezes on an old snapshot (wrong Overview pill/card and activity-monitor counts beside a fresh tab that is right) when its `/api/events` stream dies silently. The server now sends a `keepalive` event every 20s on idle streams and drops clients whose socket is dead; the page reconnects and refetches `/api/status` after 90s of silence and whenever the tab becomes visible again.
- Hive activity monitor sounds no longer go silent after a reload: when the browser's autoplay policy holds the audio engine back (every reload — including the dashboard's automatic reload on a new hive version — starts without user activation), the 🔊 chip turns amber and a one-time toast with an **Enable sounds** action says a click or key press on the page is needed, instead of each zap/buzz being dropped silently. Gesture plays (▶ Play, turning sound on) now start their voices inside the click itself so Safari unlocks the engine, a `resume()` that settles before the state flips waits for `statechange` rather than counting as blocked, and priming also listens for click/touchend.
- DCO checks now treat commits linked to `project.ai_author` as the hive's in both the unsigned split and the squash-unsafe count, and a split cached before hive identities counted is read again once, so an in-flight hive-authored PR is re-signed instead of waiting for a person ([#16701](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16701), [#16703](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16703)). The docs now state that this login linkage comes from the commit email and is trusted only because the in-place path needs base-repo push access ([#16702](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16702)).
- The post-merge DCO trailer check (`src/scripts/check-dco-trailers.sh`) no longer fails a squash commit whose author is a GitHub noreply address (`<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com`) signed off under the same contributor's real email, when the branch's own history shows the two identities belong to one person; such commits are reported as informational `same-person-noreply` lines naming the evidence commit, with no GitHub API call. The v5 squash of #15315 (`687c3cb0`) is waived until that evidence exists on v5 ([#15401](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15401)).
- Adopted contributor PRs whose unsigned commits are the hive's own no longer hold at stage 074 with `dco-missing`: the stage engine re-signs them itself (in place on base-repo heads, re-homed onto `hive/adopt-<n>` on forks) and the replay now carries merge commits from a base sync instead of refusing to re-sign (#14666)
- Waive the post-merge DCO trailer check for `fb153585e` (squash of #13548 dropped the author sign-off that both branch commits carried); maintainer disposition recorded in #13607.
- "Let hive decide" no longer calls a PR's CI red when only a non-required context (tide) is pending: the plan reads the head's own checks, derives its WHY from the recorded stage-entry reasons (reviewer requires_human / high-risk), and on a PR the hive adopted in place hands the finding to the hive's fixer instead of "sending it back to its author".
- "Let hive decide" no longer fails with a bare "hive unavailable": the preview retries transient GitHub failures (an intermittent 500 on check-runs failed it outright), answers a merged/closed item or an unrecoverable GitHub read as 409/424 with the reason instead of a 502 the hosted Ingress replaced with its generic outage page, and the dialog now names the hive, says why it could not preview (merged since the row loaded, GitHub failed after N attempts, no GitHub client, gateway 502) and that "Let hive do that" stays off until a preview loads (hivecommons/hive#16776).
- Dashboard: the *Let hive decide* preview is one clear decision instead of a wall of text — one verb-first sentence (no doubled "Hive would:"), one short why, at most two "then" items, the sentinel finding / rails / ruled-out rungs under a collapsed Details, and **Approve & merge as-is** offered only when the head is mergeable as it is.
- Activity Monitor: a row the operator sent to *Let hive decide* now follows one post-decision state machine instead of showing a green ✓, a *Hive is deciding…* spinner and the stale striped *Ready for human merge · untrusted author* pill at once. The ✓ is the decision badge (tooltip names who chose, what hive decided, when and what comes next — never a merge celebration); the pill and chevron move to where hive actually is (*Adopted · opening hive copy…* at the merge gate, *Fixing · hive is addressing @reviewer's review* at 070), progress text names the recorded decision (*Approving…* only for an approve); toasts lead with the outcome in one line. *Let hive decide* previews first (`POST …/decide-delegated/plan`, no side effects) with **Let hive do that** / **Approve & merge as-is** / **Cancel**, and the chosen button is recorded. Adoption pairs render explicitly (dimmed *Adopted → #N · superseded* original, *↳ adopted from #N* chip on the copy; a closed original is one dimmed cached-title line, never a blank numbered row). Any recorded decision lifts `needs-human` and the 045/085 stage labels in the same write and the projection never leaves a decided row in 085. All operator-facing strings use the chevron's stage vocabulary through one shared mapping (no raw `060 reviewed` / `stage/…`); 060 *reviewed* is drawn in the CI / Review column as *Review passed · CI in progress* (the lane's recorded reason) — the merge gate column starts at 080. "The author's hive" is now "the author's clanker" everywhere; no-effect popover times are local relative times and *Merge as maintainer* is the in-tracker action when available.
- A recorded `/hive decision` (or trusted CHANGES_REQUESTED review) on a PR head is now folded into the reviewer verdict for that head as a durable, head-scoped answer, so the stage-label reconciler's verdict route treats the `requires_human` / decision-requested verdict as **answered** on every tick and after a restart: instructions route to `070-fixing` with reason `contributor-lane:decision-answered`, a bare approve clears the hold, and only a new head with a fresh `requires_human` verdict asks again. Ends the 070↔085 flap seen on hive#14628, where the fix planner or a maintainer moved the PR to 070 and the next reconcile tick put it back ([#14679](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14679)).
- A maintainer's `/hive approve` / `/hive decision <text>` on an issue the hive itself parked with `needs-human` now lifts that source label along with `stage/045-needs-decision`, so the stage engine derives `stage/010-actionable` instead of re-deriving 045 from the surviving `needs-human` two minutes later and silently undoing the un-park (seen on [#12984](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12984)). The rule is one function, `stageengine.DecisionLiftsNeedsHuman`: the un-park sweep reads the label timeline and lifts `needs-human` only when the last account to add it was one of the hive's own — the maintainer's decision is the human input the hive asked for; a `needs-human` added by a person, or one whose timeline cannot be read, stays exactly as before ([#12680](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12680)), and `hold` is never touched. The accepted reply now says which happened and, when the label stays, who added it. Same rule on label-driven repos' `/hive approve` ([#13075](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13075)).
- Dashboard: approving a PR from the activity monitor no longer answers "Hive's merge sweep merges it…" — the decision `Next` sentences, the *Approve and let hive merge* consequence and the GitHub approval note now say "Hive merges it on its next merge pass once CI is green and the head has soaked", the user-facing wording from #15575; a ratchet test keeps "sweep" out of decision text (#16767).
- Preserve maintainer decision intent through PR decision paths: `/hive decision approve <rationale>` stays an approval (`yes, but …` stays an instruction), `/hive decision` is read at 070 as well as 085, a later same-head trusted APPROVED review releases a standing metadata-only request (and is dropped again if dismissed), edited non-closing issue references stay non-closing, and trusted contributor change requests return to the author (#14816).
- Dashboard: the Activity Monitor decision pills ("Let hive decide", "Approve and let hive merge", "Merge now as maintainer") no longer flash grey and unclickable on a page reload while the viewer's role is still loading; the tracker treats an unknown viewer as pending rather than read-only and repaints once auth resolves.
- "Let hive decide" no longer reports an item as "decided, but it hasn't taken effect" when a scanner parked it again (`needs-human`, `stage/045-needs-decision`, `stage/085-needs-decision`) after the recorded decision; a park applied after the decision is a new ask and is decided anew instead of posting the decision-stalled comment ([#15276](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15276)).
- **Let-hive-decide toast: an issue decision no longer reads as "approved for merge".** On hive's own spoke, issue #15021 (`approved-direction` applied, `stage/045-needs-decision` never removed) produced the toast "Hive decided on hivecommons/hive#15021: decided, but it hasn't taken effect … Hive decided **approved for merge** at 2026-10-28T20:41:22Z". Nothing merges on an issue. The decision glossary (`pkg/delegatedecision`) now carries issue words beside the PR words for every decision kind that differs — `approve` → PR "approved for merge" / issue "approved to proceed — an agent may claim it"; `direction`, `close-superseded` and the `hold` reason likewise — and `ActionPlainOn` / `PlainOn` / `DetailOn` select by item kind in the toast, the `/hive decision` comment and the stalled follow-up (the SPA mirror `stageTrackerPlainWords(slug, detail, itemKind)` does the same). The headline no longer says "decided … decided" ("no effect yet"), and the SPA rewrites the server's RFC3339 stamps into the operator's clock ("2h ago (4:41 PM)") through the shared timezone helper. When the hive can see the real cause — the 045 park label still on an issue that already carries `approved-direction` — the toast says so ("stage/045-needs-decision is still on the issue; the scanner skips it until that label clears") and offers the fix first: **Lift the park (remove stage/045-needs-decision)** runs the audited issue-decision path that removes the label and tells the stage engine the park lifted, followed by Re-evaluate now, Re-run decision and Give direction.
- A trusted merger's `/hive decision` on a hive-authored PR parked at `stage/085-needs-decision` now moves the PR: the whole comment (not just its first line) is recorded as the instruction and quoted verbatim in the fix kick, a decision on the current head supersedes the swarm's decision-requested verdict so the PR derives `stage/070-fixing` in the same pass as the acknowledgement, a bare `/hive decision approve` is recorded as an approval that releases requires_human instead of kicking a fix that says "approve", and an acknowledged decision whose record did not survive a restart is rebuilt from the comment thread ([#14679](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14679)).
- A dedupe-agent checklist is no longer folded into an existing finding that shares a path with it. projectbluefin/actions#543, a data-loss bug, received the repository's whole checklist as a "Folded finding"; checklists now skip the path folds like DAG children do. The review backlog's "Same file as #N" cross-link also names the path the two items share: on projectbluefin/utah-packages#868 it named the finding's own `config/factory-build-backlog.toml`, which #852 never cited (the shared file was `docs/skills/factory-build-backlog.md`).
- A parked issue that only defers to another parked issue's decision no longer counts as its own owner ask. Danathar/tududi#512 (the upstream v2.0.0-rc.1 tag) was parked with "Answer on #511; the same choice applies here" and sat in the your-turn inbox beside #511 as a second decision. Lane policies now tell a deferring park to add `--blocked-by <N>`, and `hive-open-issue comment` accepts that flag and links the existing issue "blocked by #N". The enumeration carries the open-blocker count on parked rows, and the dashboard reads a decision park whose open blocker is itself a decision park as waiting on that decision, not as your turn; a decision blocked by ordinary work stays your turn. The relay now also does this on its own: a `--needs-decision` park with no `--blocked-by` whose text defers to an earlier open decision park ("answer on #N", "the same choice ... #N", "parking this with #N", "#N settles it") or cites the same Actions run as one is linked "blocked by" that issue, with a note saying where to answer, so one decision asked by several lanes (Danathar/tududi#511, #512, #528) reaches the owner once. Only lower-numbered issues are targets, so two asks never wait on each other.
- "Let hive decide" no longer refuses a workflow fix the hive can land. An agent writing "the hive's token cannot change workflow files" (true of its own contributor-tier lane) made the delegate answer recommend-only `capability-gap`, even when the App installation granted `workflows: write` and a merge-tier lane served the repository. The delegate now checks both before calling it a gap. The unpark notice also ignores the delegate's own `hive recommends: …` comment, so `/hive approve` keeps meaning the issue's recommended option, and hold-gated agents are told to name their lane's token, not the hive's, as the limit.
- "Let hive decide" no longer approves a bare "direction" on an issue that asks its owner to choose between options. Before, projectbluefin/utah#920 (carry debugging tools in the image, a `ujust` recipe, or a `-dx` flavor) planned *Approve the direction of #920 and let the hive pick it up* under `default-approve`, recording no choice, so the claiming agent would pick one itself. The delegate now reads the issue's options (the lettered options the "What to reply" notice reads, or a numbered list a `Pick one:` / "competing" / "options" lead-in introduces, from the body or the newest hive park comment). When the same text recommends one, it goes with that option and names it in the plan and in the recorded `/hive decision` (rule `recommended-option`). When it recommends none, it writes nothing and leaves the choice to a person, offering Give direction (rule `competing-options`).
- The "What hive saw" facts for a delegated decision now list the options an issue offered and the recommended option, so the competing-options verdict can be checked against its inputs.
- "Let hive decide" no longer approves a PR "as it is" over a standing change request. On projectbluefin/testsuite#1057 the delegate's mergeable-as-is rung approved a green, conflict-free fork PR while a maintainer's CHANGES_REQUESTED review stood on its head, confirming the review swarm's High finding. The delegate now reads each maintainer's latest opinionated review (what keeps GitHub's reviewDecision at CHANGES_REQUESTED) and the swarm's verdict on the exact head. A standing change request rules the rung out and becomes the fix the decision names (return to the contributor, or fix-then-merge when they are offline); a requires_human verdict on the head rules the rung out too, and the reviewer's question is answered by the release rule that says so. The ruled-out reason is recorded in the decision's ladder.
- "Let hive decide" now says why a preview failed instead of "hive unavailable". While the hive's GitHub App was out of quota, every preview failed with "Could not preview owner/repo#N (hive unavailable)": the server answered 502, and the hosted Ingress replaces every 502 with its own "hive is restarting" body. The preview now answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header and reads "GitHub API rate limit for this hive is exhausted; resets at 17:32Z" (or the secondary limit's retry time); other GitHub refusals (a 404, a permission 403), a closed item or a missing dashboard snapshot answer 424 with the real message. 502 is left for a GitHub that could not be reached at all.
- Delegated issue decisions now use the blocker ledger's shared capability inference, keeping repository-write, branch-protection, secret, and workflow permission gaps parked instead of approving ineffective directions, while retaining the park for other missing App permissions (#15217).
- Delegated decisions to supersede an offline contributor PR now queue the existing adoption engine immediately, preserving contributor commits, sign-off, credit, and issue closing references.
- Delegated decisions keep hive-authored superseding PRs parked when a reviewer policy sign-off question is recorded, showing the exact question for confirmation while scope and follow-up questions remain eligible for automatic approval. Scope and follow-up questions still auto-decide under the superseder rule.
- Contribute `hub.disabled_repos` now matches a plain entry against the exact repository name (full or bare, case-insensitive), so disabling `owner/dakota` no longer also disables `owner/dakota-iso`; `*` globs and `/regex/` entries work as before, and the **Repos for contribute** toggles in the dashboard follow the same rule.
- Dispatch never opens a second PR for an issue that already has one
  ([#15469](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15469)): an open PR's
  webhook that covers an issue now preempts a contributor task already in
  flight on it (the author's own PR excepted); the duplicate-fix sweep tells
  a registered relay contributor's PR from a person's, so its one superseded
  notice passes the write-back gate instead of being suppressed; and a PR
  the merge train holds as `duplicate-of#<winner>` is parked with its author
  (072/071/070, "Duplicate of #winner") without nudge or adoption, never
  "Approved; waiting its turn".
- Image builds now fall back from `mirror.gcr.io` to `docker.io` (via the new `BASE_REGISTRY` build-arg) when the mirror throttles with 429, and the docker freshness guard no longer rejects fresh images when git lengthens the 7-char short hash (#13208, #13226).
- Dashboard stage tracker: a PR whose drawn_under issue is filtered out or on another page is now drawn under a listed issue instead of disappearing (#15116).
- Removed the v6 dashboard Platform top-level section so platform details stay in Diagnostics, matching v5.
- Label mutations left `Unknown` or `Planned` in the effect ledger no longer fence retries forever when the reconciling label read keeps failing; after an hour the operation expires and the idempotent label write replays.
- Branch updates and review submissions left `Unknown` in the mutation journal no longer refuse retries indefinitely: the next attempt reconciles the operation from GitHub (the PR head for `branch_update`, the PR's reviews for `review_submit`) and, when GitHub cannot be read, expires it after one hour so the retry can run ([#13870](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13870), [#13873](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13873)).
- `LoggingBoundary` now forwards `LookupApplied` to its wrapped boundary, so idempotency lookups through a logging wrapper see the journal.
- The dashboard no longer shows a pull request as "merge-eligible — merges on its own" when its repository's auto-merge is off (an owner setting, or a hive below ACMM L6); it shows as waiting on a person to merge it by hand.
- A hive-authored PR whose diff against its base is empty (an adoption whose fix already landed through another PR) is now closed by the hive as superseded by the PR the reviewer named, through the writeback gate, instead of parking at "needs decision"; a person's empty PR still gets the prompt. Adoptions' dispatch records now carry `hive_authored`, so their decisions route through the self lane rather than the contributor lane. A reviewer decision question re-asked on a new head (including a merge-from-base, which no longer triggers a review round for an empty PR) is identified by its `hive-redundant-of` PR or normalised wording and refreshes the standing review in place with no second 085 comment. The tracker's decision popover quotes the reviewer's question from the newest verdict on any head, shows a "redundant of #N" chip and leads with "Close as superseded" ([#15499](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15499)).
- Activity Monitor: a stalled merge train's chevron no longer renders as an empty amber chevron — the stall words were painted ochre on amber; they now inherit the chevron colour and read `Merge queue · stalled — waiting on #<head> (needs maintainer merge) · 1h21m`, every `merge_train.state`/`head_state` maps to words, and an unmapped state falls back to its humanised name plus place instead of `''`
- Evidence CI-gate panel: bundle snapshots are now judged against the required checks the merge gate would use for that repo (`auto_merge.repos.<repo>.required_checks`, else the global default) instead of the global list alone, and green merges missing a config-required check are queued for GitHub confirmation so branch protection can clear or confirm them; on a multi-repo hive the primary repo's gate check no longer produces spurious `missing_required` suspicions for repos that never had it (#13225).
- The Evidence card's "Outcome by author kind" no longer reports a PR this hive reviewed but did not merge as "outcome unknown": the governor's review-outcome ledger pass now stamps the PR's newest evidence bundle with the forge outcome it already fetched (`outcome` block: merged by someone else, with an `unrecorded` merge naming the merger, or closed without merge), and `GET /api/evidence/summary` applies the ledger's rows at read time for PRs whose bundle has no stamp. The summary adds `merged_elsewhere` per author kind and `missing.prs_outcome_from_ledger`; `missing.prs_outcome_unknown` now means truly unresolved. No extra GitHub calls. (#13186)
- Evidence: the "Issue reopen rate · rolling 30 days" card now uses the shared panel chrome (collapse toggle, ⓘ explainer, n= chip of distinct issues closed, grade pill) and a compact, overflow-contained table instead of unstyled browser defaults that bled into the next card.
- Experiment Lab's Observe/Suggest/Evolve and Governor/Repo/Both buttons now take effect immediately: `PUT /api/nous/mode` and `/scope` mirror the new value into `GET /api/nous/status` instead of only persisting it for the next restart. The config dialog's Trust Ladder is now a working control sharing the same handler, both surfaces are disabled with an "Owner access required" tooltip for non-owners, and any server rejection is shown as an error toast instead of being swallowed (#12039).
- An owner's approval of a contributor PR that edits `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**` now survives the hive's own base refresh: when the only commits since the approved head are App-authored merges of the base branch and the PR's diff is unchanged, the workflow-path fence stays released instead of re-arming, so a strict up-to-date branch rule no longer needs a fresh approval every time the base moves. Any contributor push still re-arms it.
- `/hive approve` (and the dashboard decision) on an issue `project.issue_filter.require_labels` refuses no longer writes a `stage/010-actionable` or `015-triage-needed` that the next sweep strips ("outside the pipeline: filtered"): out-of-cycle stage facts are checked against the filter, so the issue keeps no stage, and the reply says it is still outside the agent queue and names the required label(s) that would admit it instead of promising the queue. The blocked sweep's unblocked notes say "re-triaging" instead of "This issue is actionable again".
- **The fix loop no longer treats a failing non-required check as red.** `HasFailingRequiredCheck()` was true for any failing non-meta check run, so a PR whose only red check was advisory (a `continue-on-error` job the branch ruleset does not require, which GitHub reports as unstable but mergeable) drew FIX-BEFORE-NEW re-dispatches with nothing to fix, spent the whole budget, and was parked with `needs-human` and `reviewer-handoff` (Danathar/tududi#467: 6 kicks on one head). It now consults the required set `EnrichCIStatus` already resolves for the blocked-PR pill: when that set is known and non-empty, every required check reported as a check run, and none of them failed, the PR is not red. The stuck-red reaper, the escalation ledger, the claim-suppression release and the dependency-bot red-CI handoff all follow it; the ledger treats such a PR as pending, so it keeps its history and an existing `needs-human` label stays put. An unknown or empty required set, or a required check that has not reported as a check run, still fails closed. The open-PR recommendation report keeps listing any red PR under "Failing CI" through the new `HasFailingCheck()`.
- The Hive activity monitor's chevron column now follows a PR's current state, never the highest stage it once reached: a PR under repair (070 fixing, 071 needs-author, 072 returned-to-contributor, 074 adopted-by-hive, or a red required check) lights CI / Review even while a stale `merge-failed` gate or planner-ordered merge train still rides on its record — hive's own #15574 read "Fixing · conflicting" under Merge queue. One predicate decides both the column and train membership (`stageTrackerItemColumn` / `stageTrackerUnderRepair`), `left_train` is mirrored onto `linked_prs[]`, and ratchet tests pin every stage × gate × train state to its column A covered issue's list place now follows the same live work its strip draws — an open covering PR with no stage yet counts as 040 covered-by-PR for sorting too, so a just-filed issue with an open PR no longer sinks to the bottom among the New rows (hive's own #15654) ([#15656](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15656)).
- Hub dashboard Fleet quadrant: the median now runs over active hives only (assigned and online — the table's own predicates), unassigned placeholders and offline hives are counted as excluded rather than as zeros, "Finds its own work" no longer scores Productivity for a hive that has reported no activity, each fleet axis tile says "n of N measured", every scored axis gets its own summary line (a 0 names the criterion behind it), and the header reads "N active hives · M offline or unassigned excluded" instead of "all N hives".
- Standalone `Fleet report:` issues are fully retired: an ACMM shortfall now opens or rolls up onto the hive's `[selfreport]` tracker (with owners, spoke link and diagnostics), the hub relay folds a legacy standalone payload from an old spoke onto that tracker or answers `410 Gone`, and the hive watching the report repo closes any bot-filed `Fleet report:` issue that still lands with a pointer to the self-report design.
- Governor section shows the fleet `running N · $X this hour` figure as a visible stat; it previously rendered only inside the hidden compact governor strip
- A fork PR waiting on a check only a maintainer can run (a fork-guarded check such as a fork Canary) stays with the maintainer across new heads. On projectbluefin/utah-packages#869 and #862 each new head (a merge of the base, or the author's push) read as an ordinary red check until the next enumeration read its annotation, so the PR dropped to 072 and the author was nudged to fix a check they cannot fix. #862 got 13 hive merge-of-main commits, each discarding the exact-head run it waited for. The recorded `fork-guard:` reason now carries onto a new head while the same check is red, the hive no longer updates the branch of a fork head waiting on a fork-guarded check, and the 085 ask names the head the maintainer must run the check for.
- A fork pull request red only on a fork-guard check (such as a required `Canary` that cannot run on forks) is no longer nudged ("Failing checks: Canary") or adopted on each new head before it is parked: the guard's checks are remembered on the PR, a later head red on nothing else goes straight to `stage/085-needs-decision`, the nudge never lists a fork-guard check, and automatic adoption refuses a head whose only blocker is the guard (projectbluefin/utah-packages#862, #869).
- **Contributor PRs from forks the hive cannot push to are no longer adopted and parked within minutes.** The hive never moves a fork's commits into the base repository, so adopting a fork PR whose branch it cannot push to only parked it at `stage/085-needs-decision` on the next pass, 15 minutes after the author's relay went offline. Such a PR now stays at `stage/072-returned-to-contributor` with its nudge and the relay's queued `fix-pr` task, and is parked at 085 with the same maintainer ask only after the 072 dwell (24h) since the nudge on that head. In-place adoption on forks that allow maintainer edits, same-repository adoption, and explicit owner-delegated adoption are unchanged.
- A fork pull request whose only failing checks refuse forks (for example "a fork pull request cannot publish…; a maintainer must push this branch to the repository") is now parked at `stage/085-needs-decision` with the check named, instead of being returned to its contributor or adopted, since only a maintainer can clear it ([#14273](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14273)).
- A fork PR whose update-branch GitHub refuses because the base changed `.github/workflows/` now parks at 085 as `fork-workflow-update`, telling the author or a maintainer to run `gh pr update-branch` or merge the base in, instead of `workflow-permission` asking for an App permission it may already hold; after a workflow-file refusal the sweep no longer calls update-branch again until the head or the base moves.
- Serialize automatic final base refreshes per repository/base across merge lanes, preserve pending preparation outside ready train seats, and allow already-current, CI-green, reviewed successors to merge without waiting for a preparing front.
- knowledge: `FullFact` only takes a vault page body from a vault page of the fact's own layer, so the reported layer matches the store that supplied the body (#16926)
- Fixed Model Gateway/LiteLLM key rotation so saved keys immediately refresh live agent proxy routes, surface the effective key SHA-256 in APIs/UI, and log only the hash for operator correlation.
- Good-first-issue curation no longer advertises blocked, time-gated or operations-tracking issues: the sweep re-reads live labels before labelling, skips issues carrying `<!-- hive:ops-tracking -->` / `<!-- hive:recheck-after … -->` or soak-checklist phrasing, withdraws `good first issue` + `help wanted` with a correction comment when a labelled issue turns out to be blocked, held, parked or ops tracking, the blocked sweep strips `help wanted` from blocked issues with no tracked PR, and `promote-stable.yml` stamps its emergency follow-up issue with both markers (#13304)
- **A good-first-issue invite the hive posted is withdrawn when the issue parks afterwards.** The sweep skipped every issue it had advertised in the current process as `already-selected` before scoring it, so an issue parked at `stage/045-needs-decision` (or blocked, held, or found to be an ops checklist) after the invite kept inviting newcomers until the hive restarted (projectbluefin/utah-packages#527). Such an issue is now re-scored and withdrawn like any other labelled issue.
- **The `gh` wrapper no longer posts empty or blanked bodies for contributor agents.** A `gh pr create -F -` whose body already closed the task issue, or that targeted a non-default base, opened the PR with the hive footer alone: the auto-close step read stdin and did not hand the body on. The labeled try of `gh issue edit -F -` consumed stdin, so its unlabeled retry blanked the issue. Both now read the body once. The wrapper also refuses a create or comment whose body is empty (`empty_body`), a body that is only an `@path` (`body_file_reference`, gh posts it literally) and an edit that would blank the body (`blanking_edit`), and the auto-close step no longer appends `Closes #N` to a body that says the issue stays open (`Refs #N — partial … remains open`).
- The `bin/gh-wrapper.sh` wrapper now passes `gh issue comment --delete-last` and `gh pr comment --delete-last` through without a body: the missing body is no longer refused and the hive footer is no longer injected as `--body`, which gh rejects alongside `--delete-last` ([#15031](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15031)).
- Raised golangci-lint run timeout from 5m to 10m so clean cold-cache runs (~4m50s) no longer flake at the ceiling (#9263)
- Governor eval cycles no longer take 10-20 minutes on hives with several due agents: kicks are now delivered to different agents concurrently (still in order per agent), so the tick waits for the slowest agent's input prompt instead of the sum of every agent's wait, and a webhook wake reaches the activity tracker within one short cycle.
- Fork PRs that allow edits by maintainers no longer read as forks the hive cannot push to. The GraphQL PR batch (`graphql_pr_batch`, on by default) stored each PR's detail without `maintainerCanModify`, and the scan reused that detail in place of a REST read, so every fork PR came out "not editable". The hold guard then stopped keeping held fork PRs current without asking GitHub, and posted "a fork the Hive app cannot push to" on projectbluefin/gutenprint-printer-app#196 and projectbluefin/hplip-printer-app#199, whose forks both allow maintainer edits. The repair queue's push-or-comment-only choice and the dashboard's adopted-PR push check read the same field. The batch query now asks for `maintainerCanModify` and carries it into the stored detail.
- Preserve review opinions, trusted human review state, and comment and thread counts in GraphQL PR batches.
- The contributor rule's hands-free approve now needs every perspective the head is owed. A bare non-security `requires_human` (or decision question) on a contributor PR resolved to `approve` and merge-eligible even when another perspective had never reported. Since the relay stopped recording rate-limited "could not read" reviews (#16994), that included a head whose security review was dropped: correctness asked a product question, nothing backed a security finding, and the head became merge-eligible with no security review. With a perspective missing the head now reads `incomplete` (`review coverage incomplete: missing security`), and the planner asks for the missing perspective on the normal `pending_ttl` / `max_redispatch` path. A fully reviewed head still resolves hands-free to approve, and the fixer-lane, fix-cycle-cap and security-finding outcomes are unchanged.
- The hard-suppress reconcile no longer lifts a hive-applied `hold` or `blocked` because any merged PR mentioned the issue: only a PR in one of the hive's repos authored by the App bot or `project.ai_author` counts (a person's intake PR listing ~65 issues had lifted `blocked` from issues waiting on outside dependencies).
- A host with no codex account no longer warns "provider headroom probe failed" and gets flagged as a repeated unclassified error: the codex app-server's "account authentication required to read rate limits" refusal is now classified as `no_credentials` (headroom stays unknown/fail-open) and logged at info. Fixes #16078.
- Hub heartbeat: the evidence-bundle summary (a walk of every review-evidence JSON under /data — ~22k entries, ~27 s on the hosted hive's NFS) no longer runs inside the 10 s collect budget; it is refreshed in the background and read from cache, so the spoke sends a full beat instead of an identity-only MINIMAL one every cycle. A collect that still overruns now logs its slowest sub-collectors and, once it finishes, is cached as last-good for the next beat. The heartbeat-delivered App key is skipped when unchanged and otherwise written atomically (temp file + rename), fixing the per-beat "failed to write github app key from heartbeat: permission denied" on root_squash NFS.
- Hub heartbeat collect no longer times out on hives with many accumulated Copilot sessions: `AllStatuses()` used to walk every `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl` under the agent manager (one stat per session, ~16k sessions on NFS = 8–12 s cold), which starved the 10 s collect budget, so the hub saw only MINIMAL/LAST-GOOD stale beats and reported the hive unhealthy for stable-promotion soak. The transcript-liveness walk now runs on its own refresher goroutine with hot/cold session caching, and status snapshots read only the cached result.
- Stop filing duplicate unclassified self-reports for the hub heartbeat collect-timeout outcome notices (minimal liveness beat, skipped beat before identity is known, and stale stats without fresh agent overlay); retain local warnings and fleet reporting of collector timeouts, slow collectors, panics, and heartbeat failures ([#16516](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16516)).
- Historical PR accounting (the merged- and closed-PR enrichment worker that reads each settled PR's merger and reviews) now pauses while the GitHub API budget is in `conserve` or `critical` mode, keeps its queue, and catches up once the budget is back to `normal`; the pause and the resume are each logged once. Before this it kept running a batch every ten seconds whatever the budget said. After a restart the 72-hour settle replay re-queues every recent merged or closed PR, about two REST calls each, and on a hosted hive with 20 repos on 2026-11-07 that replay spent about 400 calls in five minutes while the hourly budget was already under the conserve threshold, helping push it to `critical` and then to an exhausted bucket. Nothing plans, claims or dispatches from this accounting, so delaying it is safe.
- A PR whose sign-off attribution problem comes from the hive's own commits (the contributor's self-signed commits beside the hive's App-signed fix commit, or a head the hive pushed) is no longer returned to the contributor at 071/072 with instructions to re-sign commits they never made. It parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` with one maintainer note per head naming what clears it, and when a trusted merger approves the current head the lane elects a merge commit (`merge-method/merge`) as it already did for `role/trusted` PRs. A head made only of the author's own App-signed commits still goes back to its author.
- Fix Hive Chat so forwarded commands and unsupported free-text always produce a visible assistant response, and empty Completed payload fences no longer render copy-only blocks.
- Hive Chat command hints now return data-backed answers or concrete diagnostics instead of silent dashboard-bot fallbacks.
- Fixed the stage tracker and the governor's cached actionable snapshot keeping a pull request the hive had merged or closed itself listed as open until GitHub's `closed` webhook came back round through the hub, the closed-row sweep ran on the next status publish, or the next full enumeration replaced the snapshot. On a hosted hive in webhook cadence hivecommons/docs#469 was merged by the automerge sweep at 18:25 and still read "Sentinel alert - needs human" an hour later, with the governor re-evaluating it as merge-eligible seven more times from the cached snapshot while the hub relay was dropping deliveries. Every hive merge path records a `pr_merged` / `pr_closed` audit event; that record now applies the same closed snapshot a webhook delivery would, so the row leaves both stores the moment the hive performs the write, with no GitHub call and no dependence on the webhook round-trip (hivecommons/hive#14420).
- A hive-authored PR whose issue a different merged PR closed — or that a merged PR's body declares it `Supersedes` — is now closed as superseded (ledger reason `superseded-by-merge`) instead of parked at `stage/085-needs-decision` on the reviewer's `requires_human`, sent to 070 to rebase a conflicting head, or left wearing `needs-rebase`; the self-authored sweep asks the superseded rule before the needs-rebase label block, and a closing claim closed as not planned with no merged closer also closes the PR ([#15276](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15276)).
- `hivectl` and the stdio admin MCP (`hive-admin-mcp`): a name that needs percent-encoding in a request path now reaches the hive as named. Callers escape each path segment, and the shared client then escaped the whole path a second time, so `/` went out as `%252F` and the hive read a literal `%2F` in the name. Over stdio the `agent.model` write with a model id such as `kiro-api-key/claude-opus-5:high` asked the hive for the model `kiro-api-key%2Fclaude-opus-5:high`; `hivectl` commands that take a name with a `/`, a space, `#`, `%` or a non-ASCII letter had the same fault. Names without such characters were never affected, and run keys only worked because the run endpoints decode twice. The HTTP admin MCP endpoint was not affected.
- `hives web` no longer stalls other requests while page-load auto-discovery waits on an unreachable hub ([#13708](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13708)); discovery now runs outside the server lock.
- Fixed the hold guard retrying a held PR's branch update every pass without ever reaching GitHub after its first update. Each update is now one attempt per head and base. An accepted update is waited on, and a refusal or an update that never lands stops until the head or base moves, with a note telling a person to update the branch. PRs returned to their contributor (072) are no longer updated.
- The hold guard no longer re-applies `hold` over a dashboard Approve: when a trusted merger approved the PR's current head through the hive's own decision record and the hive removed the sentinel/hold gate label on their behalf, the guard accepts that head instead of reading the hive's lift as unreviewed drift ([#15644](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15644)).
- Fix dashboard repository hold pills so toggles immediately update the cached status snapshot, return a status-sequence floor, and render distinct Hold/Release controls.
- A `hold` the hive set for a human-merge path is no longer described as a reporter-trust hold. projectbluefin/utah#1097 and projectbluefin/finpilot#627 were told to "Release it … and the lane merges on its next pass, or keep it until a maintainer has reviewed the issue's reporter", while the hive's own notice said it will not merge them. The hold's provenance now records `human-merge-path` when the App's human-merge-path notice is on the PR, and the 085 comment and the decision popover say a maintainer merges it by hand; a hold the hive can only attribute to its label event points at the hive's notice instead of naming the reporter gate.
- Held PRs stopped by an older build's workflows-refusal record are retried once when the base branch moves, instead of being skipped until the next head push.
- Hold guard no longer merges the base branch into held Renovate/dependency-bot PRs (a `renovate/*` head branch or a `renovate[bot]`, `dependabot[bot]` or `mergeraptor[bot]` author); the bot keeps those branches current itself, and a hive commit made Renovate stop rebasing them.
- The closing-keyword and reference parsers no longer read the `#8203` inside Renovate's `&#8203;` (zero-width space) as an issue reference. On projectbluefin/gutenprint-printer-app#169, "fixed and prefixed label handlers by [@&#8203;…" became a claim on #8203, and the review filed projectbluefin/gutenprint-printer-app#170 about the artifact. The review backlog also no longer files an info-severity finding that says "no action needed": it opens an item with nothing to do.
- The hub's SaaS auth-check now waves `/api/webhook/github` through to hosted spokes, so relayed GitHub App webhooks reach the spoke's HMAC-verified receiver instead of being answered by nginx with a login redirect; hosted hives no longer report `webhooks.healthy=false` / `events_1h=0` while the hub relays events ([#13231](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13231)).
- Fix Spek hub executor stage ownership so relays are not offered hub-owned spec/plan work, duplicate run rows are collapsed, and placeholder leases hand off by run key.
- Fixed the hub and hive image builds failing once Alpine's `ca-certificates-20261020-r0` and Debian trixie's `20250419+deb13u1` dropped the withdrawn emSign ECC Root CA - G3 / Comodo AAA Services entries: the distrust step now rewrites each entry only when it is still shipped and keeps asserting the roots are absent from the regenerated bundle. The contributor (bookworm) and OSS-scanner (trixie) images received the same tolerance pre-emptively.
- Search engines no longer crawl or index the hub's auth-gated and API routes. Google Search Console had been reporting hub pages as "Blocked due to unauthorized request (401)" / "access forbidden (403)" because `robots.txt` said `Allow: /` and hosted hives' `/robots.txt` 302'd to the hub login. `GET /robots.txt` on the public hub now disallows every gated route group (`/api/`, `/login`, `/dashboard`, `/metrics`, `/openapi.json`, …) while keeping the landing pages and sitemap crawlable, any other host gets `Disallow: /`, every 401/403/login-redirect and every `/api/*` response carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, the login pages carry a `noindex` meta tag, and hosted spoke dashboards serve `/robots.txt` (`Disallow: /`) ahead of the auth gate and mark all their responses `noindex`.
- hub: the Assigned hives table's Version column is now width-bounded and wraps as a two-line block (channel · SHA · behind · drift / status · actions · auto-upgrade select); the "why not now", drain-agents and missed-window explanations moved to hover titles, the Repos "as:" line wraps, and cell side padding tightened, so the table fits a 1600px viewport without horizontal scroll.
- Automerge review gate: a trusted human's APPROVED review on the exact head now clears every non-approved swarm outcome, `changes-requested:<perspectives>` and the new `requires-human` included, and the `review_evaluated` audit line records `human_approver=<login> overrode=<outcome>`; the gate classifies the head from the same normalized aggregate verdict the contributor lane and `stage/085-needs-decision` read, so a `requires_human` head no longer shows as `changes-requested:style` to the merge gate (rationguard#296). Review-plan fix kicks — a maintainer's changes-requested review or `/hive decision` text — are delivered ahead of the governor kick for the same agent instead of timing out behind it every cycle, and an undelivered review/fix kick is logged and audited by PR (`review_kick_undelivered`) (hive#13100).
- A PR a person pushed themselves — an owner or maintainer in `dashboard.authorized_users`, or any `author/human` PR — is never adopted by the hive ([#15202](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15202)).
