The contributor-lane "contributor offline" rule now applies only to clanker and registered-contributor PRs; a `requires_human` or changes-requested verdict on a human-authored PR routes to 071 Needs author and tells the author what the reviewer asked (or that the branch conflicts and needs their rebase) instead of parking at 085; and "Let hive decide" on such a PR can only approve-admit a reviewed, green head, return it to its author with the reviewer's question or the fix, or hold. The adoption path itself — the engine's `adoption/supersede` label handler, the delegate executor and the 090 "ready for human merge" decider from #15181 — refuses a person's PR with a logged reason that the stage tracker row shows as "not adopted: the hive asks them, not adopts". Folded from #15191: a DCO-less clanker head at 090 adopts in supersede mode rather than waiting on a person.
- A PR whose App-linked commits are signed off as the hive App while the author is a person or a clanker now goes back to its author by kind (`stage/071-needs-author` / `072-returned-to-contributor`, reason `hive-signoff-attribution`) with one comment per head giving the exact `git commit --amend --reset-author -s` fix, instead of parking at `stage/070-fixing` where no hive lane can rewrite a contributor's branch; and a trusted-author PR the enforcing review gate holds (`review-gate:no-review-bundle` / `awaiting-review-approval`) reads `stage/050-review-pending` at once rather than carrying no stage until the swarm's verdict lands.
- Inception ignores echoed clarification-question placeholders, including kick-template instructions, and waits for real questions before advancing to clarification ([#15153](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15153)).
- The brainstorm watcher's pluk subscriber now reads `data.to` from `state_change` events and keeps tailing the log past end-of-file, so idle transitions and appended events are no longer missed.
- Run governor maintenance sweeps on independent, non-overlapping timers using immutable configuration snapshots; report sweep cadence in `/api/health` and governor tick stage durations so slow maintenance no longer delays unrelated sweeps or evaluation ([#16286](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16286)).
- A watchdog "agent not producing" stall caused by the inference provider refusing requests (`blocked: inference (...)`, e.g. a 429 `budget_exceeded` hard cap) is no longer filed as an `unclassified_error_repeated` self-report; the cause is upstream and already shown as a blocked agent, so the fleet issue tracker stops collecting it as a hive defect (#15986).
- proxy: inference forward paths tolerate endpoints that already end in /v1 instead of calling /v1/v1/chat/completions (#13219)
- Serialize inference and live Copilot token updates through atomic file publication so concurrent responses cannot race over the shared temporary usage file or overwrite newer cumulative totals with an older snapshot.
- **Settings can now switch the ioscan semantic classifier off, and "open" fail mode sticks at L5–L6.** On an L5–L6 hive with no model endpoint (any hive whose agents all run on a subscription CLI such as Copilot), the classifier that became default-on in #13858 fails closed and withholds every piece of untrusted issue and comment text. The fixes the boot log names (`ioscan.classifier.enabled: false` or `ioscan.classifier.fail_mode: open`) had no dashboard control, and choosing **ioscan fail mode → open** silently saved as unset, which reads back as closed at L5–L6. Settings → Security → Input Defense now has **Semantic classifier** (level default / on / off) and **Classifier fail mode** (follow ioscan fail mode / open / closed), "open" is stored as written, and switching the classifier off takes effect on the next scheduler pass without a restart ([#14025](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14025), [#14027](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14027), [#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- Input Defense settings saved from the dashboard now actually unblock kicks at ACMM L5+ ([#16973](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16973)). Saving ioscan fail mode "open" was stored as unset, which at L5+ falls back to the ACMM pack's fail-closed default, so the setting snapped back to "closed" and kicks carrying untrusted text stayed withheld. "open" is now stored as given, and every ioscan save in Settings → Security → Input Defense rebuilds the semantic classifier from the new backend and fail mode immediately, clearing the blocked-kick alert when it no longer applies. A runtime ACMM level change (for example L4 → L5 in the dashboard) rebuilds the classifier the same way, so the level's classifier requirement and fail mode apply without a restart. The alert and the Classifier backend help text no longer tell operators to restart for changes the dashboard now applies live, and the alert names the `ioscan.fail_mode` key the Security tab actually exposes.
- An agent whose held-PR coordination kick is blocked by ioscan fail-closed now logs the WARN once per agent and demotes repeats to Debug, matching the main fail-closed kick path, instead of warning on every tick and tripping an `unclassified_error_repeated` runtime self-report ([#14442](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14442)).
- An ioscan classifier that could not be constructed (no model endpoint for the hive's CLI, e.g. a Copilot-only hive at ACMM L5+) no longer consumes the per-eval classifier budget ([#14629](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14629)). Previously the first 64 strings per governor eval were withheld under fail-closed and every later string passed on unclassified as `budget_exhausted`, so whether an agent's kick survived depended on its render position. The fail-open path now also logs the classifier error once per distinct error instead of once per string, which stopped a hosted hive from self-reporting 64 "ioscan classifier failed open" warnings every eval.
- An unconfigured ioscan classifier (no model endpoint) now logs a one-time "not configured" warning instead of the fleet-reported "failed open" runtime error; genuine backend errors still warn as before ([#16748](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16748)).
- Overview issue bands agree with the labels: a held issue is Parked (chip `hold`), not Unclaimed (projectbluefin/utah#551); a parked issue whose only done label is `hive/likely-done` stays Parked instead of Confirm & close (projectbluefin/common#1328); and an issue at `stage/040-covered-by-pr` with no done label says an open PR covers it rather than "already done" (projectbluefin/utah#12, #1075).
- Issue-claim side effects on GitHub (the `stage/020-claimed` write, the claimed-by / preempted labels and their removal on release) now retry transient failures — timeouts behind the per-repo label writer, network errors, rate limits, 5xx, or a journaled attempt whose outcome was uncertain — up to four times with a doubling pause, instead of giving up after one 15s attempt and leaving an issue an agent is already working at `stage/010-actionable`. Claim, takeover and release comments are still posted once, so a timed-out comment is never duplicated (hivecommons/hive#14766).
- Stage tracker: an open issue carrying a hold-class label (`hold`, `do-not-merge*`, `hive-pause/<id>`) now shows as "Open · on hold" instead of 045 "Needs a human decision", even beside `needs-human`; the issue stage reconciler walks the Hold list, removes a stale `stage/045-needs-decision` and forgets the store record, and `needs-human` / `needs-decision` / `needs-spec` without a hold still park at 045. PR holds are unchanged (#13012)
- Issue-stage lane marks its merged-full-fix close comment with `<!-- hive:closed-by-merged-pr pr=N -->` and checks for it first, so a failed close is retried without posting the note again.
- **A PR that names an issue in its title, body or a comment now counts as linked to it** ([#14859](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14859)). The contribute view's issue→PR resolver checked only the PR title and body, so it dropped any search hit that mentioned the issue elsewhere. The same title/body-only view let a scanner note claim that a PR "does not reference" an issue when two of its commits said `Fixes #N`. The resolver now also reads the issue's timeline `cross-referenced` events (up to five pages of 100, under the existing 4s lookup timeout), which cover title, body and comment references (a commit-message-only reference is a `referenced` event and is not matched). The scanner and dedupe policies now tell agents to check that timeline and the PR's commits and comments before saying a PR does not reference an issue, and to say "no closing keyword in the PR body" when only the body lacks one. The added policy section grows the largest shipped policy past the 2x headroom the prompt-size cap requires, so `promptsrc.DefaultMaxPromptBytes` rises from 64 KiB to 96 KiB; `HIVE_PROMPT_SOURCE_MAX_BYTES` still overrides it.
- `hive-open-issue --no-consolidate <reason>` lets a caller file a separate issue instead of being folded into an open one; the watcher records the reason as `consolidation_skipped_reason` (#14360)
- `hive-open-issue` relay: a placeholder or made-up `--repo` can no longer put the hive into a retry loop. The script now validates `--repo` before writing anything (must be `owner/name`, not a documentation placeholder such as `owner/repo`, and inside `$HIVE_REPOS`) and exits 2 with the reason, including under `--dry-run`; the watcher classifies failures as permanent (invalid/placeholder/unconfigured repo, GitHub 404/410/422/401, non-rate-limit 403 → quarantined `.failed` on the first tick with one `ERROR` naming the path) or transient (5xx, network, rate limit, ledger *Unknown* → backoff), reconciles an *Unknown* effect-ledger entry against the repo's open issues and expires it after 1h if the lookup keeps failing, and gives up a `kind: issue` create after 3 consecutive reconciliation failures or 8 identical errors instead of 24h. Eleven identical `owner/repo` smoke-test requests from three agents, all sharing one content-derived idempotency key stuck in *Unknown*, had retried for 3+ hours on the hive's hive.
- Every issue the hive files now carries the filing agent in its title (`[reviewer] Review backlog (security): …`, `[governor] refactor: … is a merge hotspot …`): one shared `issueshape.TitleFor` helper tags titles idempotently at `CreateIssue`, in the review-backlog, hotspot and upstream-watch title builders, and in the egress proxy for an agent's raw `gh issue create`; open-issue title dedupe ignores the tag so items filed before it still match instead of being refiled.
- Record validated operator approvals before optional GitHub reporting, bound reporting waits, and keep mutation-journal readers responsive during ordered durable writes without weakening merge gates.
- The mutation journal now clamps the timestamp used for retention pruning to its own clock, so a skewed or forged future timestamp on a commit can no longer age out other journal entries early (#14830).
- Replace flat 60% knowledge confidence defaults with signal-based scores and show unscored facts honestly.
- Kick freshness self-reports include counts by refusal category, making repeated withheld kicks diagnosable without exposing refs or raw errors.
- A kick's log is now archived to `/data/logs/kicks/<agent>/` as soon as its turn ends, not only when the next kick, a restart or a graceful shutdown rotates the scrollback out. A daily-cadence agent whose container crashed hours after its turn finished (exit code 17, OOM — no SIGTERM, so the shutdown snapshot never ran) used to lose the run entirely and show nothing under 🕘 past kicks. The later rotation snapshot of the same kick replaces the `turn-end` archive, so each kick still has exactly one file and retention still counts kicks.
- Kick-refusal detection no longer fires on echoed kick content. Security-review and scan kicks legitimately list issues titled "prompt injection …"; when the CLI echoed those bullets, the agent was marked as having refused the kick (scanner and reviewer on one spoke), hiding the turn's real output. Structured markdown lines — bullets, table rows, headings, numbered items, bold spans, `#123` references — are now skipped; first-person refusal prose still registers.
- Kiosk mode (`?kiosk=1`) always renders the dark theme unless `&theme=light` is given, so a fresh headless streamer profile no longer broadcasts light mode.
- Dashboard knowledge: `GET /api/knowledge/toc?types=general` now returns the facts the table of contents lists as `general`. A fact with no type of its own (a wiki page without one, or the conventions entry derived for a git source) is listed as `general`, but the filter compared that word with the empty type and returned none of them. The entry read and the effective-knowledge view take the same filter. Other type filters and agent scopes are unchanged.
- Completed Kubernetes Jobs are now immediately deleted even if the caller's context expires during pod log collection, preventing them from lingering for the full TTL ([#16547](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16547)).
- The issue stage reconciler now removes this hive's `hive/claimed-by-<agent>` label from any issue it sees with no live claim (no live `hive:claim` marker or assignee and no live ledger claim), parked, blocked and held issues included. A label written without a ledger claim — a `claim` request on an issue no kick listed, `governor.claims` off, a failed release write — had no other remover, so parked issues kept a lapsed agent's label indefinitely (projectbluefin/utah#10, #855; projectbluefin/utah-packages#882). Human labels and other hives' agent labels are never touched, an unreadable claim keeps the label, and nothing is kicked.
- The launch-cost collector now caches each settled day's sorted per-ref list for its persisted store, rebuilding only days that changed instead of re-listing the whole retained rollup every tick (#14834).
- Activity Monitor: a row parked on a human decision now shows "Let hive decide" inline beside the server's lead (e.g. "Re-author") instead of hiding it under ⋯ → Decide…, and inline action pills are filled buttons with a ▸ glyph and a consequence tooltip so they no longer pass for record pills like "adopted from #N".
- Issue claims: the enumeration-time claim read and the in-progress sweep now fall back to the hub's own claim ledger when the forge carries no live `hive:claim` marker, so a claim whose 🔒 comment was suppressed by the per-issue comment budget no longer has `stage/020-claimed` stripped and the issue flipped back to `stage/010-actionable` ("waiting for the scanner") while the ledger still withholds it from kicks.
- "Let hive decide" now walks a decision ladder for contributor PRs — already fixed by a merged PR → mergeable as-is → rebase-then-merge → return to a connected contributor → adopt-supersede as the last resort — so a PR whose issue was already fixed and merged is closed as superseded with a note naming the merging PR instead of being adopted (#15219 / #15240). The decision names the author's tooling truthfully ("the author's clanker" vs "the author's hive"), the toast and PR comment say why, and the decide API exposes `decision.ladder {decision, reason, ruled_out}`.
- "Let hive decide" no longer un-parks an item whose blocker is a missing GitHub App permission (such as `workflows`); it recommends granting the permission and keeps the item parked, so the needs-human is not re-applied in a loop (#15099).
- dashboard: Lifecycle Timeline axis labels no longer stretch and journey rows no longer collapse to stripes (#10956, #10977)
- Add a left-sidebar link and empty state for the dashboard Lifecycle Timeline.
- Merge lanes no longer merge a PR whose linked issue is on hold or parked for a decision. The self-authored, trusted-author, queued and contributor lanes read every open same-repo issue the PR body closes once the head is otherwise ready to merge, and refuse with `linked-issue:hold:#N:<label>` (hold labels, `hive-pause/<id>`, `do-not-merge*`) or `linked-issue:needs-decision:#N:<label>` (`stage/045-needs-decision`, `needs-human`, retired decision labels). The PR stages `085-needs-decision` with an entry comment naming the issue and the label to remove; removing it lets the next sweep merge. A failed issue read withholds the merge for that tick (`linked-issue-check`). Prompted by projectbluefin/utah#874, which merged while the maintainer was still waiting on #551; a `hold` on #551 would now have stopped it.
- The `agent_login_required` selfreport now names the backend that lost its login: the login scanner's `login required detected` record carries `backend`, `login_hint` (the CLI's login command) and `credential_valid`, so the operator knows which provider to re-authenticate on which agent instead of being told only the agent name; `codex` gets a login hint (`codex login`) ([#16953](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16953)).
- `log_read` (admin MCP) and `GET /api/logs/read`: a log file whose first line is longer than 64 KiB can be paged. Paging identifies a file by a digest of its first line. The digest was taken over the whole line when a page was returned but over at most 64 KiB when the cursor was looked up, so the two never matched: following `next_cursor` into such a file always answered `cursor_expired` ("no longer retained"), and only the newest page of that file could be read. This hit `hive.log` and its rotated history when a file opened with a very long record, and the `proxy`, `litellm` and `hive-output` sources whenever a file opened with a runaway line, since those are stored in 64 KiB pieces that are each longer than 64 KiB once wrapped. The digest now covers at most the first 64 KiB of the line on both sides.
- A new head on an in-place-adopted PR pushed by someone other than the author with write or higher on the repository, or by another App, no longer hands the PR back to the offline author or nudges them: the hive keeps the adoption. A push by the author, or by a read-only third party, still yields as before (projectbluefin/utah#919, projectbluefin/utah-packages#804, #812, #822).
- A contributor PR that edits workflow / action files (or removes tests) and is also parked for a sentinel alert, a hold label or a `requires_human` verdict now gets a `stage/085-needs-decision` comment that says from the start that a maintainer must merge it by hand, and why. The lane stops at the first thing that blocks a PR and reaches those blocks before its diff fence, so the comment used to ask a trusted merger to approve the head "and the hive re-evaluates". No approval can merge such a PR, and the manual-merge rule only appeared once the first block was cleared. Human routing now reads the head's diff fence itself (once per head) and names it alongside the other blocks. A clean diff, or one that cannot be read, leaves the comment unchanged.
- Matrix kiosk no longer goes stale for the length of a governor tick: an incremental sentinel pass now reads only new PR heads in the allowlisted repos every two minutes, independently of the full 15-minute sweep, and `/api/matrix/lines` reports `last_ingest_at` / `next_ingest_in_s` so the footer can tell "nothing pushed" from "nothing ingested". The set of already-evaluated PR heads now persists under `/data/sentinel-heads.json` and is restored at boot, so a hub-triggered restart no longer re-diffs every open PR; the first ingest also runs at boot instead of waiting for the reconcile timer ([#16276](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16276)).
- Matrix kiosk: the freshness HUD and get-started CTA now stay pinned above the canvas in every effect, including `mx.effect=terminal`, and typed rows stop above the HUD band.
- Stopped the unbounded memory, thread and connection growth in the hive process that OOM-killed hosted hives ([#14681](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14681)): `/api/stage-tracker` held its cache mutex across the whole tracker build (one review-evidence lookup per open PR, each a glob of the repo's evidence directory on NFS — tens of seconds), and every webhook delivery and every status publish invalidated that cache through the same mutex, so webhook handlers, the governor's publish and every dashboard poll queued behind back-to-back rebuilds that never drained. Invalidation is now a flag flip that never waits, at most one rebuild runs at a time outside the lock, concurrent polls get the previous body as `source: stale`, a poll whose client went away stops waiting, and the evidence-directory sibling listing is memoised per repo directory for 60 s instead of re-read per PR.
- Dashboard "Merge blocked" alerts now clear on their own once the blocked PR closes or its fork workflow runs are approved / the approval setting is relaxed, instead of waiting for an unrelated App merge or a restart (#9391).
- Dashboard: the merge celebration bee is drawn at `--fs-3xl` (≈32 px, was ≈17 px) with a theme-aware halo so it reads on dark and light panels, and the Activity Monitor's Merged counter now rolls visibly like an odometer — the rightmost wheel (and any wheel right of the changed digit) spins a full turn on every increase, the day/week counts roll with the same mechanism, the day/week line no longer disappears mid-roll on the dark theme, and a reload rolls up from the values the tab showed before.
- Activity Monitor: a PR merged by anyone — a maintainer's `gh pr merge --admin` as much as the hive's own sweep — now leaves the board with the bee fly-off and a merge toast naming the merger (`#16644 merged by @clubanderson` / `merged by 🐝 hive`); `recently_merged` is the union of the audit log and the merged ledger with `merged_by`, an `issue_comment` on a just-merged PR no longer reads as "closed", and a closed-not-merged exit keeps its quiet toast (hivecommons/hive#16658).
- Activity Monitor: a merge outcome ("Merging", "Merge failed", "Waiting for CI") always renders in the Merge gate column, whatever stage the lane fell back to; the merge-failed chip is a fixed short phrase (GitHub's refusal translated to plain words — "4 required checks haven't finished", "branch protection blocks it", "needs rebase", "not allowed" — with the raw text only in the tooltip's Details line, clamped by CSS), "retrying" while the sweep is on it; pending CI reads "CI running", never "CI is red"; cues say "back to Reviewed" instead of a stage slug; and the automerge sweep remembers GitHub's "required status checks are expected" refusal per head so it stops re-PUTting /merge every pass while the PR is still blocked (hivecommons/docs#512).
- Activity Monitor: an issue row whose covering PR is at the merge gate no longer concatenates its lane reason ("open PR #15090 covers it (PR at 060-reviewed)") into the merge-gate pill as a two-line clipped label; the pill is the stage word plus a gate fact only, the issue row reads the gate from the nested PR so it agrees with the PR sub-row, and the cover reason leads the glyph tooltip as "Open PR #15090 covers it · at 060-reviewed" (#15101).
- Activity monitor: the Merge gate column now reads one word per state in pipeline order — Awaiting merge gate (what holds it) → Ready for auto merge (next sweep in Ns) → Soaking (time left) → Merging → Merged — instead of "Ready for auto merge" for 060/080/100 alike; every row at the gate carries a leading glyph (spinning while hive's sweep is on the PR, a clock while it waits) whose tooltip and aria-label say in plain words what is happening and when the next sweep is, and the agent-working spinner names the agent. New `merge_gate` field on `/api/stage-tracker` PR items and nested linked PRs. Legend in docs/dashboard-sections.md ([#15073](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15073)).
- A PR parked at 085 on a red check no longer flips to 080 whenever a contributor-lane pass is refused the destination-merge lock. The lane reports that refusal (`base-refresh:merge-guard`, "destination merge already in progress") together with its error, and the classifier's errored-lane branch ran first: an approved head read as a weak 080, which replaced the standing 085 and seated the red PR at the front of a merge train until the next evaluated pass put it back (projectbluefin/utah-packages#917, about 15 round trips on one head). The refusal is now no stage opinion, error or not.
- Serialized merge lane: a front pull request that is closed, merged outside the lane, turned into a draft or retargeted now leaves on the next automerge sweep pass, with a `front check: …` exit reason, and the next waiting pull request is promoted. The sweeps list open pull requests only, so no merge path ever called in for such a front again and it held every waiter until the front timeout (up to four timeouts when its checks were last seen pending). Each pass now reads every front of a `hive-serialized` repository once; open fronts are unchanged.
- Serialized merge lane: a pull request that only an automerge sweep lane would merge, and whose branch update and merge writeback containment refuses (for example an auto-promoted contributor PR without `hive-review` at L6), no longer takes the lane front. It used to reach the front and hold it for the full front timeout, refused every round with `writeback: unsolicited write suppressed`, while owner-queued pull requests waited behind it; with several such PRs the lane made no merges for hours. The lane now asks containment before the PR takes a place, so it is refused without being recorded (no front churn), and a front whose sweep writes become refused leaves on its path's next call. The lgtm queue, `/hive merge` relay and dashboard paths are not asked and behave as before.
- A human-gated (085) PR that is approved on its current head now stays in the Merge queue column while CI on that head is queued or re-running, instead of flipping to PR in progress and back as checks cycle; failing CI or an unapproved review still moves it out ([#16595](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16595)).
- The dashboard no longer lists a PR as Merge-eligible ("it merges on its own") when its base branch only accepts merges through GitHub's merge queue. Hive merges over REST and cannot enqueue, so the sweep skips such PRs with `merge-queue-required`; the merge classifier now reads the same memory of merge-queue bases the sweeps keep, gives the PR a hand-merge verdict naming `merge-queue-required`, and leaves it out of `merge-eligible.json`. The queued, trusted-author and contributor-lane sweeps now share that memory with the self-authored sweep instead of losing it every tick.
- Automerge: when GitHub refuses a merge for want of an approving review and a person's change request still stands on the PR, the `stage/085-needs-decision` comment now names the reviewer, the commit they reviewed and what the hive pushed since. It asks them to re-review, or a maintainer to dismiss the review, instead of asking anyone for an Approve over it (projectbluefin/utah-packages#633). PRs without a standing change request keep the same text. The self-authored sweep also re-reads `mergeable_state` right before the merge call and skips a head GitHub now calls conflicting, and a 405 "Pull Request has merge conflicts" from any lane is reported as `conflicting` instead of `merge-failed`.
- The merge-request relay (`hive-merge`) now evaluates the same contributor-lane policy as the auto-merge sweep before merging a contributor-authored PR: a verified claim tier outside `require_tiers`, an unfinished contributor soak, a head under `min_head_age`, a missing reviewer verdict, or a `hold`/sentinel/needs-decision label refuses the request terminally, surfaces the gate in the agent's result, and is audited as `merge_request_refused`. Previously an agent's merge request bypassed those gates, so an untrusted-tier contributor PR with green CI could be merged minutes after it was opened. Hive-authored PRs keep the relay's existing behaviour, and `merge-eligible.json` no longer lists PRs parked on a human decision.
- Show the tracker's existing repository chip on merge notifications, keeping same-number PRs in different repositories linked to their own merge and row.
- The Activity Monitor no longer draws a merge train over PRs that are still at CI / Review: the merge train is a merge-queue concept, so only PRs at 080 and beyond ride one and the header counts only them. A PR short of the queue whose files overlap another open PR's now shows a muted "overlaps #N" badge ("overlaps #15637 (sidebar.html, index.html) — will queue behind it") instead of a rail, ordinal or "1st:" header ([#15653](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15653)).

The train header no longer says "not in this view: 7 more" over PRs that were never in the merge queue: `size`/`members` count only the PRs riding in this payload, and when the page does not draw every member the header says why — `on another page: #N`, `hidden by the filter: #N`, `not in this payload: #N`. The header's hover explains the mechanics (members touch the same files, merge one at a time in order, each rebased onto the base only after the PR ahead merges) and a member's hover says its slot, `Position: 3rd of 4 · after #X merges`.
- Merge train: a PR GitHub reports conflicting on its own, or one at 072 returned-to-contributor (label or stage record), is no longer admitted to or counted in a merge train and draws no train idle comment — hive's own conflicting #15307 read `queued-behind#15424:4/6`; a conflicting PR rides only while the train itself is repairing it (#15395).
- Activity Monitor: the merge-train header now counts the rows actually drawn under it — members shown as sub-rows of their linked issue join the train run, and members a filter hides are named (`1 of 3 PRs here · not in this view: #…`) instead of the header claiming `3 PRs` over one row; a PR that needs a person's merge (untrusted author, no linked issue, human-merge rule) is no longer a merge-train member or head, so PRs behind it no longer wait on a merge that cannot happen.
- Merge trains now order their members by readiness first: PRs the lane knows are merge-ready (080 admitted, soaking, merge queue) lead, members it has not evaluated follow, and members still in CI/Review trail — re-sorted every pass, so a PR going green moves up and one going red moves back. A PR still in CI/Review renders in its real column with a "train · joins behind #N when green" chip instead of a Merge-queue chip, and a train with no ready member says its front is provisional ([#15761](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15761)).
- The Activity Monitor's merge count no longer resets on reload: a persistent merged ledger under `/data` records every pull request the hive tracked that reached merged (whoever merged it) and `/api/stage-tracker` carries `merged{today, total_7d, total_30d, all_time, recent}`; the chip, now **Merged** (all-time, with today / this week beneath), is pinned at the top of the tracker with the column header strip, opens a popover of recent merges, and a merge raises a bee (or "+1") from the row's ✓ cell to the chip or off the top of the screen plus a dismissible bottom-right banner with a *Show row* link ([#15147](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15147)).
- Dashboard: the Merged pill's odometer now rolls only after the celebration bee lands — the day/week line, a total the server had already raised, and merges over the flight cap no longer move the drum while a glyph is in the air; several merges in one flight are a single roll to the final value after the last landing, reduced motion sets both at once (#15568).
- Dashboard: the Activity Monitor's Merged counter is a mechanical odometer at rest, always (only the wheels that change roll) — #15409 had sized only the flying glyph and drawn the roll as a transient overlay over plain text.
- Dashboard: the Merged pill's odometer is drawn at the chip's own type size on one quiet inset track — no 18 px bevelled drum cells, no glow — so it sits level with the other topbar chips, and the pill's icon is the dashboard's bee glyph rather than a filled hexagon; the roll animation is unchanged (#15543).
- Activity Monitor: the bottom-right "merged" toast shows the PR number again ("#15122 merged" instead of a bare "# merged") — the number was a Number and the page's HTML escaper drops non-strings (the "All merges" list had the same blank numbers and counts); it now also falls back to the nested pr record or the GitHub URL and never renders a bare "#".
- The serialized merge lane no longer stops merging when CI is backlogged ([#12952](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12952)). Its front timeout was fixed at 60 minutes and a front whose required checks were only queued was rotated out, so the next pull request needed a new branch update and CI run; with a queue longer than an hour no pull request ever merged. The timeout is now configurable hive-wide (`project.merge_front_timeout`) and per repository (`project.repo_policies[].merge_front_timeout`), and a front whose required checks are all still queued or in progress gets its deadline extended, up to 4x the timeout, with a `front-extend` lane decision recorded for each extension.
- Merges the GitHub forge adapter performs are now audited as `path=forge` instead of being attributed to the merge relay (`path=relay`), and the dashboard's PR throughput counts them as hive merges.
- Activity Monitor: the Merge gate column now shows **Merging** (with `merging_since` and who is merging) for every merge path the moment the GitHub merge call starts, holds it for at least the merge toast's lifetime (30 s) before the row advances to ✓, and reads **Merge failed** with GitHub's reason when the call is refused — rows no longer jump from CI/Review straight to merged.
- Retire stale missing-required-check merge banners only after successful exact-current-head evidence, preserving required App identity and other PRs' unresolved blockers.
- On phones and tablets the dashboard menu button (☰) is no longer cut off at the left edge of the top bar. The button kept a `-10px` left margin from when it was a bare glyph; since it became a bordered navbar chip, the top bar's left zone (which hides overflow) clipped its left side.
- Dashboard: on phones, dialogs with long bodies (the **What changed** release notes after an upgrade, alerts, the export viewer, the Level 6 auto-merge notice, settings bodies) now open as full-screen sheets with a fixed title and ✕, a scrolling body and fixed buttons, honouring the safe-area insets; every long modal body shows a bottom fade while there is more to read (cleared at the end) and a thin always-visible scrollbar on desktop, so content no longer looks cut off
- Overview KPI tiles no longer overflow the phone viewport right after a restart: the "refreshing after restart" pill wraps inside the card instead of widening the headline grid, tile sublines and sparklines stay within the tile, and the `--fs-2xs`/`--fs-2xl`/`--fs-3xl` type tokens are now defined at `:root` so they no longer fall back to the 16px body size (hivecommons/hive#16601).
- Stop filing a fleet self-report when copilot model discovery fails only because the operator has not completed the dashboard Copilot Login; the condition is still written to the local audit log and warn line, now with `state=credential_missing` and a `recovery` field naming the Copilot Login, and any earlier real discovery failure is cleared from the tracker so it cannot file with stale text (#12947).
- The dashboard no longer WARNs on every poll when an inference backend returns no models (once per backend per hour); the fleet report names the flapping case `models_endpoint_empty` (#16369)
- Document the Teams five-post thread-reply polling limit and top-level checkpoint approval workaround in `MSTeamsConfig` and the v6 readiness runbook ([#12739](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12739)).
- Fix the Microsoft Teams chat backend (v6) so notifications, command replies, and checkpoint approvals keep working. Outbound messages now go to a Teams **Workflows** webhook as an Adaptive Card envelope, because Microsoft retired the Office 365 Incoming Webhook connectors the backend used to post to. Point `notifications.msteams.webhook_url` at a Workflows "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received" URL ([#9155](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9155)). An expired Graph delta token (HTTP 410 / `resyncRequired` / `syncStateNotFound`) now triggers a fresh delta baseline, with a WARN that shows the gap, instead of retrying the dead link forever and silently dropping all inbound commands ([#9156](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9156)). Thread replies under the bot's recent posts are now polled via `/messages/{id}/replies`, so replying `approve` to a checkpoint prompt works. The inbound dedupe set is capped at 1024 IDs, the same limit Matrix uses, so it no longer grows without bound ([#9157](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/9157)).
- Stage every issue a hive PR closes as `stage/040-covered-by-pr` the moment the PR opens, not just the one the hive-open-pr request declared: the relay now unions the request's issues with the body's `Closes #N` list, and the `pull_request` webhook emits the same CoveredBy fact for each hive-authored closing claim it records in the claim ledger. Scanner-filed sub-issues closed alongside their parent no longer sit at `010-actionable` with the scanner as their actor for the PR's whole CI run.
- Bound the convergence mutation journal: terminal (Applied/NotApplied) operations age out after 7 days and the oldest terminal entries are evicted past 20k entries, so `journal.json` — reloaded and fully rewritten on every label/comment/merge transition — stops growing without limit (53k entries / 56 MB on the hosted hive, ~60% of all Go allocations). Planned/Unknown entries are never pruned.
- native-queue-policy workflow checks out the base branch head instead of the PR's stale recorded base sha, so the policy test file is always present.
- The native queue policy check now passes as a no-op instead of failing when a `pull_request_target` run lands on a pull request that is already closed or merged ([#16128](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16128)).
- Native merge queue withdrawal now also triggers on a release in progress and on a human-merge path, so a Hive-enqueued PR no longer keeps merging through GitHub's queue during a release freeze or after `human_merge_paths` changes (#15517).
- Activity Monitor rows parked on a person now state why on the row itself: the hive-note line reads `#N — Needs human: <blocker> — <ask> · requested by … · lead: <first enabled option> ▸ · @author is pushing it in #PR`, the issue's decision column keeps `Blocked · App lacks workflows permission 👤` while a covering PR drives the strip, the `needs human` pill carries the full reason and reveals the line on click, the 085 chevron reads `Needs human · <short reason>` (e.g. "edits CI workflows"), an issue blocked only by its PR's pending decision reads `decision on #PR`, the first enabled blocker option leads when the server disables "Let hive decide" (shown muted with its reason), and the "owed — blocked:  …" caption double space is gone ([#16623](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16623)).
- With `auto_merge.require_current_base` on, the hive no longer merges the base into a PR whose base branch only accepts merges through GitHub's merge queue (projectbluefin/finpilot#599). The hive cannot enqueue and the queue tests base plus PR itself, so each `base-moved` update only moved the head off its review and the PR waited for a fresh one, three times in a day. The gate now skips the update for 24 hours after the last `merge-queue-required` refusal on that base, and the PR holds at `100-merge-queue`; the 30-minute merge-queue memory no longer has to stay fresh between refusals for that.
- An issue the hive answered without a pull request no longer sits at `stage/010-actionable` forever. When an agent explained why it could not open a PR but did not park the issue for the owner, the issue stayed "waiting for the scanner" while the scanner never came back, so it was missing from Your Turn and had no `/hive` replies. Once such an issue stalls at 010, and the hive's own comment is the newest word on it, the hive now posts a short note with the options (close it, or keep it open with instructions) and parks it at `stage/045-needs-decision` for you.
- Quiet notification mode (`github.notifications.mode: quiet`, the default) now folds the remaining per-event comments the hive posted into the single edited `<!-- hive:status -->` comment: the post-merge evidence pointer, the `hive:unblocked` note (now also idempotent per issue and settled PR in either mode, and skipped when the same merge closes the issue), the review backlog summary, the contribute hub's claim marker and an agent's relayed `hive/awaiting-ci`, `Parking on stage/045…` and `Already fixed` status notes. Closing an issue leaves one closing comment: the close-on-merge sweep and the issue-stage lane no longer both post `Fixed by #N`. The GitHub client logs `github notifications created=N edited=M suppressed=K` once an hour so the effect can be measured ([#15918](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15918)).
- Fixed a `-race` data race and intermittent assertion failure in `TestRunNousGateWatch`: the test now reads watcher logs through a mutex-guarded buffer and waits for each tick to be processed before asserting.
- The Activity Monitor's Merged odometer no longer rolls before the bee lands: a merge the merge-gate hold still masks as "Merging" is held back from the count like a flight to come, so the number waits through the hold and the flight and rolls once when the glyph reaches the chip. Successive merges queue their rolls and the display ends on the server's value; a reload still shows the server's number at once ([#15762](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15762)).
- Adoption now resolves merge conflicts for a returned-to-contributor PR whose clanker is offline instead of handing the PR back: when the supersede's replay of the base onto `hive/adopt-<n>` conflicts, the hive opens the copy anyway and the fixer's rebase-resolve episode (`requested_by: adoption`, two attempts) resolves it; after two failures the PR parks at `stage/085` with `rebase-failed-twice` (copy) / `adoption-stalled:rebase-failed-twice` (original) offering *Adopt into fresh branch* / *Close as superseded*. An attempt that opened nothing is re-admitted once the clanker has stayed offline for `governor.labels.stage.adoption.offline_grace` (default 30m), and its branch push is a fresh journal claim so the branch an earlier attempt deleted is recreated. Tracker row reads "Adopting · fixer resolving conflicts" while the fixer works.
- Activity monitor: a contributor PR whose `stage/*` labels the write-back gate kept off GitHub (fork PR, no opt-in label) no longer reads as an unclassified "PR in progress · @x's clanker" when the stage engine holds it at `stage/085`: the stage record carries `labels_suppressed` and the tracker trusts it instead of treating the missing park label as a lifted park. An unclassified clanker PR now carries its author's `presence`; when the clanker is offline the chevron reads `PR in progress · @x's clanker · ■ offline 3h` and the caption names the next automatic step (a green PR is reviewed and merged without its author; hive adopts only once it is returned and nothing is pushed for `adoption.after_offline`). Human-authored PRs are unchanged and never adopted.
- automerge: `/ok-to-test` is now posted at most once per head SHA (durable comment marker, survives restarts), is skipped entirely when Prow replies that the App is not a trusted commenter and the repo has no `hive-ok-to-test.yml` workflow, and such PRs park at `stage/085-needs-decision` with a single `needs-human` note instead of looping.
- omp agents now receive their bootstrap prompt at launch, and `HIVE_OMP_APPROVAL_MODE` and the reasoning effort are validated against omp's accepted values and shell-quoted instead of being passed through unchecked.
- A `model_roles` entry with `backend: omp` (or no backend) can now carry `reasoning_effort`; omp roles accept omp's thinking levels instead of being rejected at config load.
- **omp hub agents now get pluk classification** (#11525): the image's pinned pluk has no `omp` pattern set, so `pluk watch --cli=omp` recorded only `raw_output` while Hive logged a successful attach. Hive now ships `src/deploy/pluk-patterns/omp.patterns` (copied to `/opt/hive/pluk-patterns/`) and passes `--patterns-dir` for omp agents, logs a `WARN` for backends with no pattern set, and no longer discards `pipe-pane` failures. Upstream counterpart: hivecommons/pluk#223.
- The dashboard's omp model/effort picker now runs `omp models --json` under each omp agent's own HOME (where its sign-ins live) instead of `/data/home`, so signed-in agents list their real models rather than always the static fallback; the fallback is logged at `WARN` with the HOME probed, and its `gpt-5.6-*` (no `minimal`) and `gemini-3.7-flash` (adds `minimal`) effort rows match omp's catalog. Docs gain an omp hub-agent sign-in procedure, the advisor support table now lists omp/copilot/codex as supported (and the parity test requires `Yes` rows), and `env-vars.md` documents `HIVE_OMP_DANGEROUSLY_RUN_UNCONFINED` and `HIVE_OMP_BACKEND_SQLITE` (#11522, #11523).
- **omp contributor mode: plural advisor header, sync-back validation, stage disabled-row check.** The relay's post-verdict review now recognises the plural `Advisor N notes` header, so batched advisor notes under the verdict are no longer dropped. `--sync-back` validates the container's credential row before writing it to the host (timestamp not in the future, oauth rows only, JSON object with access/refresh tokens, identity fields unchanged) and reports each rejection. `--stage`/`--describe` treat a provider as usable when at least one of its rows is active, matching the relay's rule. Fixes #11526, #11527, #11528.
- **omp container mode now stages `models.yml`.** Custom providers (a self-hosted llama.cpp/vLLM/OpenAI-compatible server, a gateway) live in `~/.omp/agent/models.yml`, which `just contribute-hive omp` never copied, so a `modelRoles` default or advisor naming one did not exist in the container and omp fell back to another model. `bin/omp-backend.js --stage` now ships `models.yml`/`models.yaml` narrowed to the selected providers' blocks (another provider's literal `apiKey` or headers never travel), refuses a file it cannot narrow, and `--describe` no longer asks you to sign in to a provider that `models.yml` configures with `auth: none` or its own `apiKey`.
- A lifted block gets one "Unblocked" note, and it no longer calls an un-admitted issue actionable. On projectbluefin/website#987 the review-backlog reconciler posted "Unblocked: …#986 merged … This item is actionable now" and, 8 seconds later, the blocked sweep posted "Unblocked: …#986 is no longer open; re-triaging." The issue had no `triage/accepted`, so neither was true. Whichever path runs second now sees the first one's note for the same PR and stays quiet. On an issue `project.issue_filter` does not admit, the note says "Unblocked — waiting for a maintainer to admit it" and names the label that admits it.
- Dashboard: the Overview tile totals, the left-nav Overview `issues/PRs` pill and the Hive activity monitor list now all derive from one canonical server-side open-items set (`/api/status.openItems`), so the three can no longer disagree; the activity monitor's sidebar counter is now that total (needs-attention moved to the header suffix and the counter tooltip); totals count listed items (extra reported-but-unlisted items show as "+N not yet listed"), ForgeState cache items seed tracker rows, and a boot-restored snapshot is marked stale until the first fresh enumeration instead of being served as current.
- The hub orphan sweep no longer abandons an upgrade 20 minutes in when the spoke is alive, still on its old build and reports no drain: a spoke on a build that predates drain reporting drains in-flight kicks silently for the default 45-minute window, and clearing the latch there left the instruction only in memory, so the next merge-driven hub restart lost it and daily-window `:stable` hives missed every window. The latch is now held for the default drain window plus the usual grace, which keeps re-delivery alive across hub restarts ([#14856](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14856)).
- Log sources `proxy`, `litellm` and `hive-output` (read with `log_read`): a line that never ends is stored in records of at most 64 KiB, and the split no longer cuts a multi-byte character in half. Before, a character that straddled the 64 KiB mark was lost: its two halves were stored as replacement characters (`�`) in two records. The Go writer and the Node auth proxy's writer now both move the split back to the start of that character. ASCII output was never affected.
- Fix the create-PR duplicate guard refusing an agent's PR because a dependency-bot PR (Renovate, Dependabot, or a custom-named App such as `mergeraptor[bot]`) edits one of the same files: the overlapping-files check now counts only PRs this hive's agents opened (the App bot plus `github.additional_bot_logins`). When it does refuse a request, the issues the request was for get a note naming the branch and the blocking PR, are no longer staged under a PR that does not reference them, and the refusal is logged at WARN.
- The Overview's PR rows say what actually holds a PR, and drafts are counted. `hold_reason` told PRs held only by their sentinel alert (projectbluefin/homebrew-tap#60, testsuite#1108) to wait "until the hold label is removed" and called their absent `hold` "usually the ACMM level gate", and gave a holdguard hold (utah-packages#878) the same ACMM sentence. It now names a hold label only when the PR wears one, and keeps the ACMM sentence for a generic hold whose recorded sources are unknown or name the level gate; the repository card's tooltip uses the same rule. The Draft band read 0 hive-wide while projectbluefin/common#1532, #1626 and server#585 were open drafts, because the enumeration sidelines drafts; the bands and `/api/overview` now count them.
- Dashboard Overview: after a restart the stale badge reads "⟳ refreshing after restart (<n>m ago) · N/M repos scanned · showing snapshot from <t>" while the governor still serves the snapshot restored from disk, instead of "⚠ stale since <previous pod's time> (1h ago) · serving last-good". `/api/status` carries `restartRefresh` (restore time, snapshot read time, scan tally); it clears with the first completed enumeration.
- Dashboard: the left-nav Overview `issues/PRs` pill now mirrors the Overview tile's **Total open issues** / **Total open PRs** exactly — same `/api/status` snapshot, same render pass, same last-good figures when GitHub refuses an enumeration — instead of counting Hive activity monitor rows, which omitted items outside the tracker (e.g. `24/11` beside tiles reading `31/18`). The pill's tooltip now carries the tile equation.
- Dashboard: a repo whose issue list came back empty beside open pull requests is no longer published as "0 issues · N PRs". The enumeration verifies the empty list against the repository record and serves the last-good enumeration or reports the missing issues as an unlisted, stale remainder; the Overview marks such repos "issues syncing" instead of printing a confident zero.
- An owner's approving review counts for a PR head only when it approved that content. GitHub moves an existing review onto a later merge of the base, so on projectbluefin/utah#1078 a review submitted 2026-11-04 01:17Z was read as approval of 9d8ceab, a commit made the next day, and released the workflow-path fence. Now the review counts when it was submitted at or after the head commit's date, or when the head adds only base merges that leave the PR's diff unchanged; the fence comment then says the approval was carried over a base merge. The same rule lets an approval on the previous head answer `requires_human` after such a merge (it is no longer re-asked), and the 085 **What to do** no longer asks for an approval that is already recorded.
- Activity Monitor: an owner's Approve (either variant) on an untrusted-author PR is now a trust override for that head — the stage record carries `admitted_by: operator-approval:<login>`, the contributor lane merges the head as-is after checks and soak, and the adoption engine refuses to adopt or supersede it while the admission stands (before, the approval was reduced to a comment and the claim-tier rule adopt-superseded the PR). When the head cannot merge as-is (commits without a Signed-off-by) the popover and both Approve confirms say so before acting and offer "Re-author as hive PR" as a separate choice. Fixes #15136 (#15156).
- Dashboard *Decide… → Approve* on a parked pull request now records the person's approval against the PR head (the auto-merge lanes and the stage engine read it as the answer to a `requires_human` / decision-requested verdict, like a trusted merger's Approve review), lifts the hive's `needs-human` park, removes the `sentinel-alert` label and records a head-keyed `sentinel_acknowledged` action in the review evidence bundle so bundle-only sentinel alerts clear too, re-derives the stage and drops the tracker cache. Before, it only posted the `/lgtm` + `/approve` comments, which no lane read, so the row stayed at stage/085 *Needs human decision*; the delegated *Let hive decide* path is unchanged (comments only, never clears a sentinel alert). The activity monitor's lit chevron for a detour (085 on the Merge gate column) now names the parking stage in its hover instead of borrowing "Awaiting merge admission … Next move: human" from the column.
- Fix the "What to reply" notice on a re-parked owner step recommending `/hive approve` again after an accepted `/hive approve` did not do the step, which looped: it now recommends `/hive done` when the owner step asks for it or approve already answered that step, drops `/hive approve` on such a step, and a second `/hive approve` there gets a reply pointing at `/hive done`. Lane policies now ask for `-R <owner/repo>` on every `gh` command handed to the owner (Danathar/goodreads-mcp#443).
- A pack agent that an ACMM level adds to a hive whose operator moved their agents onto one inference gateway (e.g. the L2 `reviewer` on a LiteLLM hive) now joins that gateway with its default model instead of the pack's Copilot CLI, and a pack-owned agent that already exists on a CLI — or on a gateway the hive has since moved off — is moved there on the next restart. The gateway is the one every operator-picked backend names, provided the agents already on it are a majority of the other enabled agents; pack-owned CLI agents such as the L2 `supervisor`/`brainstorm` do not veto the move and follow it, and once moved they count toward that majority so the next level's agent (the L3 `ci-maintainer`) follows too. A hive with an operator-picked CLI agent, or with only a minority of agents on a gateway, is left as is, and an operator-owned or legacy unowned `backend:` is never moved (#14678).
- Applying a pack no longer seeds its model id onto a kept hand-set non-gateway backend such as `codex`; the agent keeps its own model ([#13288](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13288)).
- An issue parked at `stage/045-needs-decision` is re-checked when the work its park depends on moves: if a PR or issue the park text names merges or closes, or a PR that refers to the issue ("Refs #N", a closing keyword) merges, Hive posts one note listing what changed and keeps it current, so a maintainer does not decide from a premise that no longer holds. The note never un-parks the issue. `/hive approve` on a park that names no recommendation and no options now gets a reply saying so and leaves the issue parked, instead of un-parking it with the decision "go with the recommendation"; with options and no recommendation it records "go with option A: …", as the notice already offered.
- The park re-check note now says when the change a parked issue asks for has already landed, and the "What to reply" notice then recommends `/fixed`. Before, Danathar/arch-bootc#634 (ci-maintainer's retry for the build-cache delete loop in `.github/workflows/build.yml`) stayed in the owner's inbox after scanner's #635 merged the same retry in the same loop and closed #633. The note said only "#633 was closed". Now, when the park quotes its change in a fenced code block, the re-check reads the patch of each named PR that merged and of the merged PR that closed each named issue. If that patch removes a quoted line in a file the park names, the note says "#633 was closed on … by merged #635, which changed the lines this issue asks to change in `.github/workflows/build.yml`", and the notice's first bullet is **`/fixed` → the change this issue asks for already landed in #635; close it as completed (recommended)**.
- **The park re-check now follows a closed PR to the hive's adopted copy of it.** When a PR a parked issue waits on closed unmerged because the hive adopted it, the `<!-- hive:park-recheck -->` note now also lists the hive's copy (the App PR whose body says `Supersedes #N`) when it merged or closed unmerged, and when a person closed the copy it quotes the first paragraph of their closing comment (mentions defanged, at most 300 characters) with a link, then offers `/fixed` or `/hive decision <your instructions>`. The copy usually never mentions the parked issue, so a maintainer's answer to the park's question stayed invisible on the issue ([projectbluefin/utah#13](https://github.com/projectbluefin/utah/issues/13)). At most three closed PRs are followed per issue per pass; notes on issues without such a copy are unchanged.
- The park re-check no longer calls a decision park out of date because a PR its evidence merely lists merged. projectbluefin/server#614 parked on #583 (both options merge it) and listed #584 and #588 among the PRs its red check touched; the re-check reported those two merging as "the park reason names it" while #583 was still open. When a park's lettered options name references, only those count; a park without options, or with options that name none, keeps every named reference.
- A 045 park from a hosted contributor's needs-decision verdict now says why. The relay applies the decision label, and the agent was only asked to comment, so projectbluefin/common#1605 and projectbluefin/utah#1036 sat at 045 with no question. When nobody has commented since the task was assigned, the hub now posts the reported question once, marked `<!-- hive:contribute-park task=… -->`, with the recommendation when the reason names one. The task prompt now asks for `decision: <question>; recommended: <option, because why>`.
- fix(park-recheck): pre-park comments and issue bodies from untrusted authors no longer feed the park re-check landed-change match; only text from the hive's own accounts, known contributors (live relay claim or a contributor-registry profile above the self-registered newcomer tier and not revoked, so a relay-authored park still counts after its 30-minute claim expires) and trusted maintainers does, and each excluded pre-park comment or issue body is logged with its author (#16765)
- A parked issue no longer stays in the owner's your-turn queue after the hive has answered it ([Danathar/openaudible-autoupdate#177](https://github.com/Danathar/openaudible-autoupdate/issues/177)). A decision park (`stage/045-needs-decision`) that an open or held PR authored by the hive's App closes now reads "Waits on hive PR #N, which closes it" instead of `DECIDE`; the park label stays, so the ask returns if the PR closes unmerged, and a closing PR from anyone else leaves it your turn. The agent that parked an issue can also take the ask back with `hive-open-issue comment <n> --withdraw-decision`: the relay checks that the newest Hive park text is that agent's, that the park is a decision and not `needs-human`, then posts the comment with a `<!-- hive:park-withdrawn by=<agent> -->` marker, lifts the park through the stage engine (040 when an open PR covers the issue, else 010) and deletes the "What to reply" notice, which until now kept recommending the option the agent had withdrawn. All lane policies tell agents to withdraw a park whose question has gone away.
- Dashboard: an issue parked at stage/045-needs-decision (or the older stage/085 spelling) no longer shows "already done" or files under Confirm & close; only 040 covered-by-pr and the PR stages past it count as covered.
- Spek runs no longer vanish when a stage waits more than 30 minutes for a taker: run-stage leases held by the hub (admission, fan-out, hub executor) are kept alive across cleanup ticks and re-armed on restart instead of being pruned with the relay-task TTL. The contributor relay's multi-hub rotation now skips hubs whose socket is down instead of parking `ready` on a dead hub, and the pane classifier recognises the Copilot CLI 1.0.88 footer (`/ commands` without `for help`; `◉ Working … esc interrupt` as busy).
- Auto-merge sweeps no longer call merge on every pass when GitHub refuses it with a 405 that no retry cures: "At least N approving reviews are required" (`merge-refused:review-required`, retried when the head or the PR's mergeable state changes, or after 30 minutes) and "Merge commits / Squash merges / Rebase merges are not allowed on this repository" (`merge-refused:method-not-allowed`, per repository and method). Both park the PR at `stage/085-needs-decision` with a comment naming the rule instead of showing it as merge-imminent at 100, and the merge-queue-only base memory now applies to every sweep, not only the self-authored one.
- Keep the dashboard navigation button label visible on phone-sized screens.
- An agent's `gh pr edit --body` (or `--body-file`, or `-F -`) on a PR the hive opened no longer deletes the PR's `— hive: agent=… backend=… model=…` line. The PR-request watcher appends that line when it opens the PR, but gh replaces the whole body, so an agent that rewrote its description seconds later removed it (Danathar/arch-bootc#625, removed 28s after creation; Danathar/atomic-image-builder#795, where the only other change was "18 failures" → "16 failures"). Nothing put it back. The repos' monthly Agent audit trail then failed on those PRs as "opened by the Hive app with no `— hive:` signature line" (atomic-image-builder#834, arch-bootc#627). The `gh` wrapper now re-appends the PR's current line when the new body has none of its own, on the hive's own PRs only. PRs whose line is already gone are not repaired.
- Retrofit Hive-authored `Refs #N` pull requests from the claim-label sweep too, so existing open implementation PRs gain GitHub's issue-list link even after their issue has moved out of the in-progress stage lane.
- Retrofit Hive-authored default-branch PRs that used `Refs #N` so issue-stage sweeps add GitHub issue links, and unstick open issues whose claiming PR already merged.
- Ensure Hive-authored default-branch PRs that cover issues get closing-keyword links, while partial or non-default PRs leave issue-stage comments explaining GitHub link limitations.
- Hive PR notifications no longer spam authors and watchers: the stage stalled/regressed notes, the trusted-human 071 note and the duplicate-PR redirect share one `<!-- hive:status -->` comment per PR that is edited in place instead of appending a comment per event; "**Reviewed** — no findings" reviews are recorded as verdicts without a GitHub review and a head carries at most one hive review; the 071 note @-mentions the author once per cause instead of once per head; a check returning to pending after a push is no longer a regression and a merge-train queued/rebasing wait is never stalled. New knob `github.notifications.mode` (`quiet` default, `normal` restores the old behaviour) ([#15875](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15875)).
- The open PR overlap check now fetches the exact API-reported head when GitHub has not exposed a PR's pull ref, so an available sibling commit no longer blocks unrelated PR checks.
- Activity Monitor: the PR in progress chevron is the row's fallback — it defers (settled, icon only) whenever CI or Review runs, so CI + Review is the only pair ever active together — and its words are the PR's lifecycle (`Unassigned · next: scanner`, `Waiting for @author · fix owed`), never the CI / review verdict — and an active CI / Review chevron has exactly one fill: the stalled-blocker track no longer renders a darker amber, and running checks stay active whatever the poll's age (hivecommons/hive#16643).
- The pr-request watcher now reports an unpushed head branch once per request instead of once per retry, states the exact ref and repository it checked and what the push relay recorded for that branch (queued, pushed, failed, or no record) rather than asserting a push-authentication failure, and logs when the request later succeeds on retry; `hive-open-pr` warns at request time when the head is not on the remote, naming the branch, remote and push step; fleet-report fingerprints no longer treat a possessive apostrophe as an opening quote, which truncated this report's scope to "the agentQ" ([#16969](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16969)).
- Avoid duplicate unclassified fleet reports when a PR request head branch has not been pushed.
- Activity Monitor: every nested PR sub-row under an issue now has its own ⋯ menu and checkbox, so Let hive decide, Approve, Close as superseded (pre-filled with the one sibling), Won't fix, Give direction and Hold act on that PR rather than on "the issue's nested PR"; an issue with two or more open PRs offers "Let hive decide — all N PRs" and the delegated decision decides each PR on its own, listing every outcome (`items`) instead of silently picking one; the selection bar gains "Let hive decide (N selected)" with a "3 sent · 2 decided · 1 no-op" tally ([#15009](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15009), [#15017](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15017), [#15020](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/15020)).
- **The PR Throughput card no longer counts each hive merge twice.** The hive's merge paths audit a merge as `owner/repo` (`path=sweep`, `queue`, `relay` or `forge`), and the PR poller audits the same merge again as the repo is configured, bare in a single-org hive, with `path=hive`. The two entries had different PR keys, so both counted. On projectbluefin's 12-hour window the card showed 51 merged ("20 hive identity · 5 human · 6 other automation · 20 auto-merge sweep") where GitHub has 31, and a 78% hive share where the real share is 65%. The card now qualifies bare repos with the hive's org before counting, so both entries share one key. When both are present it counts the merge once, under the merge path that made it rather than the poller's `hive`, so `merged_by_path` sums to `merged`, and the hive-vs-human share, the hourly bars and the repo filter use the same de-duplicated count. Existing audit entries are read this way too, so past windows correct themselves. The poller now records `owner/repo` as well. The all-time counters stop double-counting new merges, but keep the double counts they already persisted.
- The PR Throughput card's "Top repos" list counted every in-window PR action (PRs opened, reviews, comments, claims, issues created and closed) while sitting beside "Merged by agent". It now counts merges only, de-duplicated like the rest of the card, and is labelled **Merged by repo**.
- `hive-open-pr` now corrects a PR-title emoji that contradicts the Conventional Commits type (`📝 docs: …` → `📖 docs: …`, `📖 fix: …` → `🐛 fix: …`) before the PR is opened, the agent instructions spell out the convention (✨ feature, 🐛 fix, 📖 docs, 📝 proposal, ⚠️ breaking, 🌱 chore) and the review-priority classifier names 📝 as the proposal emoji, so a hive-authored docs PR no longer fails the repository's required `PR Type` check on the emoji swap.
- Run the pinned ARM64-only PR verifier on native ARM64, preserve GitHub-hosted isolation for forks, and report incompatible or failed verification explicitly instead of leaving stale optional results unexplained.
- Group complete preparation issue/PR row units into a front-first FIFO block with an uninterrupted connector through captions and nested spacing; preserve unrelated rows and child associations, distinguish unverified recorded fronts, and validate geometry in Chrome with its required runtime dependencies.
- Restore the Activity Monitor's compact preparation train pill and side rail on actual tracker rows, retaining live pipeline comments without changing stages, sorting, linked trees, or ready/native queue membership.
- Fence preparation settlement against superseded head/base/review inputs and concurrent owner or attempt changes, preserving unresolved refresh ownership and fresh-review requirements without treating required-green as release authority.
- Give an active base-preparation owner's current CI-green head bounded reviewer-slot priority, yielding to aged review waits between confirmed handoffs without changing review, merge, or resource gates.
- Recognize an active preparation owner's own base refresh when the destination advances beyond its recorded base snapshot, including after restart, using the existing App-authored unchanged-content proof while preserving CI, review, ownership, and fairness gates.
- Show durable base preparation owners and FIFO tickets in the Activity Monitor without presenting pending CI or review work as a ready merge train.
- fleet report: the knowledge primer's byte-cap warning is an operator configuration signal, not a repeated runtime defect, and no longer files an `unclassified_error_repeated` self-report (#14173).
- A hive whose ID contains "hold" (e.g. `hosted-available-oke-11-placeholder-r05x`) no longer treats its own `hive/<id>` provenance label as a hold label. The substring hold rule was parking every issue and PR the hive had ever claimed — excluded from the actionable set, skipped by the automerge sweep, and counted as on hold (69 items on one spoke). Provenance labels are now exempt from hold matching; `hold`, `*hold*`, and `hive-pause/<id>` behave as before.
- Copilot live usage capture now records Claude completions that the Copilot CLI sends to the Anthropic `/v1/messages` endpoint (JSON and streamed, including prompt-cache tokens), and helper calls on another model no longer relabel the agent's model ([#13487](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13487)).
- Repeated blocked proxy requests (e.g. Copilot-internal endpoints) are now logged once at WARN instead of on every attempt, ending false-positive self-reports (#14204)
- The bundled proxy no longer rejects device-flow sign-in on direct-route spokes: `POST /api/gh-user-auth/start` and `/poll` (exact paths) are forwarded without the shared token, and mutating requests carrying a `hive_session` cookie reach the Go API, which authenticates the session itself. Neither gets `X-Hive-Internal`; all other unauthenticated mutations still return 401 ([#15872](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15872)).
- The crux proxy now treats hostnames case-insensitively and ignores a trailing dot when classifying hosts for inspection.
- Standalone deployments (Docker Compose, Podman Quadlet, LXC): the hive's two MCP endpoints now work through the bundled gateway on port 3001. The dashboard auth proxy answered `401 Unauthorized` to the task MCP (`POST /api/contribute/mcp`) before the hive could check the caller's own credential, so hub-launched agents and remote contributors could not use it whenever their task MCP URL went through the gateway (`dashboard.public_url` or a hub-assigned dashboard URL). It also answered 401 to anonymous calls to the public knowledge MCP (`POST /mcp/knowledge`) and had no route for that path at all, so the endpoint was unreachable even after the owner switched it on. The proxy now forwards exactly these two paths to the hive: the hive still verifies the task MCP caller's launch token or lease, and still serves public knowledge only while the owner's switch is on. A request let through this way gets no gateway credential (`X-Hive-Internal`), other methods on `/mcp/knowledge` are answered `405`, and every other unauthenticated write is refused as before. Kubernetes deployments and the default `http://localhost:3002` task MCP URL were not affected.
- The agent proxy now applies its plain-HTTP destination policy to uninspected CONNECT and transparent-TLS tunnels as well, so all three egress legs dial only globally routable addresses; `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD=true` lifts it for every leg at once
- Public knowledge MCP: `knowledge_search` and `knowledge_toc` accept a `limit` written as a whole float, such as `5.0` or `1e1`. Their schemas declare `limit` an integer, which a whole float is, and clients whose JSON stack writes every number as a float send that form; the endpoint refused the whole call with "invalid arguments". A fractional or quoted `limit` is still refused, and a whole number above the maximum is still clamped to it.
- Public knowledge MCP (`/mcp/knowledge`): on a running hive, a `GET` or `HEAD` is answered `405` with `Allow: POST`. The path was registered for `POST` only, and the dashboard's static file server takes every `GET` no other route claims, so a `GET` on the endpoint came back `404` from the file server. The MCP transport lets a client ask for an event stream with a `GET` and says a server with no stream answers `405`; a `404` reads as "no such endpoint". `POST` behaves as before, other methods were already answered `405`, and a switched-off endpoint still answers `404`.
- Public knowledge MCP: `knowledge_toc` with `type: "general"` now returns the facts the table of contents lists as `general`. A fact with no type of its own (a wiki page without one, or the conventions entry Hive derives for a git source) is shown with type `general`, but the filter compared that word with the empty type and returned nothing, so the type a client read off an entry could not be used to ask for it. The other type filters are unchanged.
- The public knowledge address shown to the owner under Settings → Knowledge is now one readers can reach. It uses `dashboard.public_url` when set, then `X-Forwarded-Host`, then the request host. A standalone hive reached through its built-in proxy used to show the internal `http://127.0.0.1:3002/mcp/knowledge`; it now shows the `/mcp/knowledge` path alone when the real address is not known.
- The push broker's trailing-blank-line normalisation now amends HEAD with `git commit --amend --only -- <files>`, so only the files it rewrote enter the amended commit; paths the agent had staged but not committed stay in the index instead of being folded into the push. The outgoing file list and protected-path check are re-evaluated against the amended commit, and the protected-path guard moved to `pushbroker/protected.go`.
- crux/pushbroker: trailing-blank-line normalisation no longer silently re-tracks a touched path the agent had staged for deletion (`git rm --cached`); the staged deletion is put back after the amend ([#16198](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16198)).
- Agents whose Copilot CLI start-up banner reports "API rate limit exceeded ... Use /login to re-authenticate" are no longer treated as stuck at a login prompt. That banner means GitHub rate-limited the token *validation* call, not that the token was rejected; classifying it as a login prompt burned the three token-restart attempts inside the same rate-limit window and latched the give-up flag, stranding otherwise-healthy agents (quality, reviewer) for hours. The spoke now recognises the banner, leaves the token store alone, and relaunches the agent on a slow (5 min) uncapped cadence until validation succeeds.
- Allow independently proven, CI-ready pull requests to prepare past a completed refresh awaiting CI, without displacing unresolved mutations or bypassing dependency, review, fresh-base, or serialized-merge gates.
- When hive closed its own copy of an adopted PR, re-adopting it now opens a fresh copy instead of being mistaken for the earlier adoption and undone, and a recorded copy that is still open is reused ([#15204](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15204)).
- Activity Monitor: a PR at *Ready for human merge* now offers **Approve & merge as maintainer** and **Approve — let hive merge** at the top of its ⋯ menu and needs-human popover (new `merge-now` / `queue-merge` decisions, merger/owner only, confirm + toast + decision badge), every needs-human state carries at least one matching action with a consequence line plus *Let hive decide* (on a 090 PR the hive answers at once in plain words why it won't merge, with the merge buttons), and the *untrusted author* pill explains why in plain words and how to trust the author (#15078).
- Stop filing fleet runtime self-reports for the expected handoff after rebase attempts are exhausted, while retaining the local warning and diagnostics ([#16510](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16510)).
- The Activity Monitor's "Approve & merge as maintainer" on a PR that needs a rebase (behind or conflicting with its base) becomes **Rebase, then merge as maintainer** instead of failing with a GitHub 405: the click records your approval first, has the hive rebase the PR, waits for CI, then merges it with your approval on record — the row reads *Rebasing → merge queued (approved by @you)*, the ledger's `followed[]` carries each step, and a conflict settles as *failed* with the conflicting files and the options *Adopt into fresh branch* / *Close as superseded*. The approval stays bound to the head you read: only a head the hive itself committed counts as the rebase, and a head anyone else pushes after your click settles the follow-through as *failed* (`foreign-head`) with nothing merged and *Approve the new head & merge* as the way out. The option is also offered at 085 *Needs human decision* when the row wears needs-rebase. The fixer router now classifies a conflicting PR before skipping rows parked at needs-decision and routes a PR with an armed follow-through as pushable, so a parked PR that falls behind is no longer owned by no lane; and the unpark sweep dismisses any recorded changes-requested whose source is the hive's own `/hive decision` comment ([#15103](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15103), [#14822](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14822)).
- No merge lane ever rebased a conflicting PR — the self and trusted-author lanes stopped at prow's `needs-rebase` label before their update-branch call, and the fixer router only listed hive-authored or adopted PRs as rebase work, so PRs the operator opened under their own identity through session agents sat `dirty` with nobody kicked.
