Now a `behind` PR gets update-branch from its lane despite the stale label, and a `dirty` PR by the hive or a trusted author is dispatched to the fixer as a rebase-resolve task (rebase onto the base, resolve, force-with-lease to the PR's own branch) with a loop guard of two attempts per conflict episode: the Activity Monitor pill reads **Rebasing · attempt n/2**, then **Rebase failed · 2/2 — needs a person**, and *Rebase, then merge as maintainer* rides the same task; the conflict-aware merge train's rebase hook ([#15117](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15117)) now opens that same episode (`requested_by: merge-train`), and its rebase-exhausted row offers *Rebase, then merge as maintainer* live instead of disabled ([#15103](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15103)).
- **Approve** on a PR that is behind or conflicting no longer says "the merge gate takes it from here" (the gate skips a conflicting PR for good): the approval is recorded, the fixer's rebase episode opens in the operator's name, the toast reads *Approved — #N conflicts with base; hive will rebase it next pass (attempt 1/2)* with a **Rebase, then merge as maintainer** button, and the row's *Approving…* cue clears as soon as the decision records instead of lingering beside the ✓ ([#15103](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15103)).
- **The red-PR fix kick asks for a DCO re-sign only where DCO is enforced.** `no-dco` is written on every managed repo but gates only where the repository enforces DCO ([#12544](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12544)); the FIX-BEFORE-NEW kick nonetheless told the fixer, whenever the label was present, to re-sign the PR's commits and `git push --force-with-lease` first — on a Renovate-style bot branch in a repo with no DCO gate, a rewrite nothing asked for. The re-sign is now the required first step only when a `DCO` check is among the failing checks; otherwise the kick carries one note to re-sign only if the repository asks for it.
- The stage tracker's `regressed` chip now fires only on a genuine fall: a lapsed claim (020 → 010/015), the claim's PR-evidence flicker (030 → 020), the agent returning to its covering PR (040 → 030) and a 040 → 010 after the covering PR merged partially are no longer booked as regressions; the marker clears on the first forward hop instead of waiting for the item to climb back to the stage it fell from; and on a hive-driven row with nothing waiting on a person it draws as a muted `stage ↓` pill (tooltip: the hive is handling it) outside **Needs attention**, keeping red for human-gated rows ([#14570](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14570)).
- The contributor relay's one-shot hub-registry relocation (after a certificate hostname mismatch) now follows only an `https://` entry under the hub's own spoke domain; registry entries naming any other host, a plain-http URL, or a spoke-domain lookalike are skipped and the hub stays parked with the existing remediation line.
- relay: a hub that acknowledged standby no longer stays trusted for standby_lane pushes after its socket closes (#16463)
- Claim release markers, including routine relay task completions, now share the per-issue automated comment budget with claim markers instead of posting without a cap; the local claim ledger remains authoritative when a release comment is suppressed ([#13766](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13766)).
- Tagged releases resume: a `release: none` HTML-comment marker that rode in a `changelog.d/` fragment (#12928, merged 2026-10-19) was compiled into `## Unreleased` on every merge and made the release workflow's decide job skip every commit since v5.186.4 as an "explicit human override" — the fragment could only be consumed by the very release it vetoed. The fragment is removed; `check-changelog-fragment.sh` and `compile-changelog.sh` now reject a `none` marker in a fragment (bump markers stay allowed); and a hand-placed `none` freeze in CHANGELOG.md is surfaced as a workflow warning annotation and fails the decide job once it has outlived `RELEASE_FREEZE_MAX_DAYS` (default 7) instead of silently skipping forever. Also fixed on the way out: with the resulting 1,369-fragment backlog the bump inference's `grep -q` died of SIGPIPE under `pipefail` and would have labelled the catch-up release a patch instead of the minor its `### Added` section calls for.
- New agent claims clear stale `hive/claimed-by-human` labels when trusted claim and release comments confirm the prior human claim was released ([#14231](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14231)).
- Activity Monitor: the PR in progress chevron on a red PR now reads the evidence-based remediation state — `Changes requested · unassigned · next: scanner` while nobody has picked it up, `Remediating · <actor> · 4m` only on a running fix kick, a clanker claim or a working agent on the PR, and a done-style `Fix pushed abc1234 · re-review pending` once a head lands after the red signal; a push that predates the changes-requested review no longer reads as a fix. The item carries `remediation: {actor, kind, since, source}` and the tooltip names the evidence (hivecommons/hive#16525).
- Auto-merge no longer merges the base branch into dependency-bot PRs (a `renovate/*` head branch or a `renovate[bot]`, `dependabot[bot]` or `mergeraptor[bot]` author) once they are out of hold: the lanes' update-branch, the current-base refresh, merge-forward, the merge train's sibling update and rebase requests, the trusted-author fixer rebase, adopted-PR recovery and `hive-merge --update-branch` all leave the rebase to the bot, and a behind bot branch holds as `behind` instead. A hive commit made Renovate stop rebasing the branch for good.
- Fix the repeat-failure Muse Code session reader walking its agent-writable session tree without a bound: each directory keeps only its newest-named entries, the logs followed and directories listed per scan are capped, a log a cap leaves out keeps its read offset instead of being replayed (a bounded number of them, newest first), and the tail reader is shared with the Copilot reader (#14877, #14878).
- Contributor and resident agents no longer park issues at `stage/045-needs-decision` for a target repository's own "offer a spec / confirm before implementing" instruction gate or a registered sibling checkout that is simply not cloned yet: prompts and policies state the hive dispatch satisfies such gates, the hub reclassifies a gate-citing verdict as idle and lifts the label once per issue, and a new `project.repo_policies[].companion_repos` key clones sibling repositories alongside the target.
- Fix repo-card issue and PR pills collapsing their title to one character per line. Since the your-turn critical path (#13731) added "waits on …" and "unblocks N" chips inside the pill, a row with several signals in a narrow card column gave every pixel to those chips. The title kept no width of its own and wrapped one letter at a time down a tall, empty pill. Seen on projectbluefin/common#1486 and other gated PRs. The title now keeps a 10rem floor, the signals and chips wrap onto a line under it, and a chip wider than the pill is cut off with an ellipsis. Its full text stays in the tooltip.
- The reporter-trust merge hold (#9665) no longer holds hive-authored PRs, judges only linked issues (closing-keyword and declared links; a link that resolves to a PR is skipped, hive self-reports count as trusted), and the stage-label pass releases a hive-set reporter-trust hold left on a hive-authored PR; the stage tracker pill now reads "Held by hive · reporter trust (issue #N by @X, contributor)" / "Held by @login" with a release/keep decision popover, and the needs-decision comment names who set the hold and why.
- The automerge sweep reads a branch's ruleset required checks when classic branch protection says nothing is required, so rulesets-only repositories no longer read as "no required checks" and stall at `ci-unverified`; the contributor lane also approves a registry-trusted author's held runs at `ci-unverified` when every `pull_request` run on the head is held.
- Activity Monitor: a pushed head with nothing against it now waits on `🐝 hive reviewer · re-review of <sha>` instead of the PR author (`rework.owed_by`), the Review chevron is the lit one once CI is green, and the GraphQL PR batch no longer caches a truncated `statusCheckRollup` page as the head's full check list — which had read `CI 7/11 · required check "test" hasn't reported` on an all-green head with 70+ contexts (#16635).
- After a restart, the periodic GitHub sweeps no longer all run in the first second. The merge sweep still starts at once. The others start one at a time over the first five minutes, so a restart no longer uses up much of the GitHub App's hourly request limit in a few minutes. After that first pass each sweep runs on its usual schedule.
- Activity Monitor: "Returned to" rows now name the clanker's owner (`@login's clanker`) even when an issue is drawn through its covering PR, instead of the issue author (the hive App bot); rows the supersession sweep found superseded say "Superseded by #N · decide" and the "Close as superseded by…" prompt is prefilled with that PR.
- review: one backlog issue per finding per PR across perspectives and heads — carried-over "previous/prior … still present" notes and `<!-- hive-refers-to: #N -->` citations are references that never refile (at most one "still present at <head>" comment per head); on merge the blocked sweep checks the base itself and closes items whose file or symbol is gone; the activity monitor folds blocked review notes under their source PR as one muted line and counts the group once; dedupe ignores a leading `[reviewer]` title prefix
- The review backlog no longer folds a finding into an open issue just because both cite the same file: it folds only when the category (review perspective) matches and the finding cites the same symbol or a nearby line; otherwise it files a new issue cross-linked with "Same file as #N" ([#13906](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13906)). The same check now applies to an open issue matched only by its "Review backlog (<perspective>)" title prefix, and scanner-filed issues without a "Review backlog (…)" title or "Perspective:" line no longer receive folded review findings (retiring the [#11578](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11578) behaviour).
- Review backlog: a finding filed `blocked` (evidence file absent on the base branch) that folded into an already-open twin issue with the same title no longer carries `blocked` onto the twin. The fold discards the filing's body and with it the `<!-- hive:blocked-on pr=… -->` marker, so the twin was parked with nothing to lift it, lost `help wanted` and refused every claim; now the twin's own state governs. The blocked sweep additionally lifts a hive-applied `blocked` that has no blocked-on marker, no `hive:recheck-after` deadline and no `hive:ops-tracking` marker (a human-applied one is left alone) ([#13364](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13364)).
- Activity Monitor: the Review and CI chevrons wear the amber in-progress fill only while perspectives or checks are actually running; a finished verdict is done-style (approved, changes requested, or a muted "awaiting human decision"). Back in PR in progress with the hive on the repair, a human-decision verdict reads "changes requested" instead of "awaiting human decision" (#16531).
- The review swarm is told that CI evidence, like code, counts only for the head it reviews. A review of projectbluefin/homebrew-tap#60 at 95440f7 said `cask-payload` "fails on this head (job 127519980309)"; that job ran on the previous head, d892290, which the new head had fixed. The read instructions now say a check run, job or log speaks for the head only when its `head_sha` matches, and give the one-line read that checks it.
- Reviewed row now counts reviews submitted after a PR's first read and reviews by deleted accounts (as unknown) (#16119, #16123)
- The contributor relay's PR review cycle no longer stalls waiting for a human to approve extra commands: its prompt no longer restricts the agent to the PR-listing commands, names the `gh` reads it needs to check review comments, reviews, checks and an UNKNOWN merge state, and tells the agent never to ask for permission. If a command is unavailable, the agent skips that check and names it in the `HIVE_VERDICT` ([#13787](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13787)).
- Fix review evidence CI snapshots being written under a short-name path (`evidence/<repo>/unknown`) and rejected as invalid; they now update the PR's bundle at `evidence/<owner>/<repo>/…`, which also stops the repeated "bundle invalid, not written" warnings (#12958).
- review evidence: upserts to a PR's evidence bundle now take a cross-process file lock so hub and agent writers no longer lose verdicts (#13911).
- The "review fix dispatch excluded" line for PRs the hive did not author (`not-hive-authored`) is now logged at INFO instead of WARN, so the expected policy skip is no longer filed as an `unclassified_error_repeated` fleet issue ([#14870](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14870)).
- review-fix: a `changes_requested` verdict whose report carries no `body_digest` is now treated as "digest unknown → body unchanged" instead of "PR body edited → re-review", so PRs at `stage/070-fixing` get a fix kick instead of being re-asked for review every cycle (#14665). Reports are now stamped with the PR body digest at collect time and when the relay records advisory verdicts; a starvation guard forces the fix path after 3 consecutive revisit-suppressed cycles, each suppressed cycle logs a WARN with its reason, and the planner summary line reports `fix_excluded` / `fix_excluded_reasons`.
- A person's release of a review verdict hold now sticks ([#12957](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12957)). Previously every refresh of `review-verdicts.json` re-stamped an unchanged verdict's `recorded_at`, and the self-merge sweep only counted an approving review or `/hive approve` posted after that time, so a `requires_human` PR was held again within minutes of its owner releasing it. Each verdict now carries a `first_recorded_at` that refreshes leave alone, and the hold is judged against it; `recorded_at` still drives retention. A new head, body digest, or outcome is still a new verdict that needs a new release.
- The review swarm no longer parks a Hive-authored PR at `stage/085-needs-decision` when its only workflow change is a strict `permissions:` reduction (hivecommons/hive#13068). hivecommons/pluk#305 narrowed a workflow-level `contents: write` to `contents: read` with green CI and still needed a human `/hive decision` because the `permissions-credentials` / `sensitive-paths` risk classes from #13043 keyed on the topic, not the direction. The relay now proves the direction structurally from the PR diff (`review.WorkflowPermissionsTighteningOnly`: only removed or lowered scopes, a block replaced by `permissions: {}`, no new job/step/trigger/`uses:`/`secrets.*`/`id-token: write`, no other sensitive path touched) and, only then, suppresses those two classes and the `permission`/`privilege` escalation terms; the suppression is recorded as a `permissions-tightening-only` reason on the aggregate. Any widening, any mixed diff, or anything the parser cannot prove still gates exactly as before, and the reviewer prompt now says the same thing. This is verdict classification only — no stage, transition or merge-gate change.
- A reviewer that could not read a PR because of a rate limit (HTTP 429, GitHub's rate limit, or the hive's own per-agent `agents.github_api_hourly_cap`) no longer produces a `requires_human` verdict. The relay drops that report, the perspective's dispatch expires after `review.pending_ttl`, and it is asked again. Before, five "could not read … HTTP 429 … not reviewed" reports parked projectbluefin/testsuite#1116 at `stage/085-needs-decision` and the owner's delegate asked a person about "the security review withheld approval". On a contributor PR without the security report, the same verdict would have resolved hands-free to approve on a head nobody read.
- Two review-aggregate paths no longer approve heads they should not. On a contributor PR, a perspective's `reject` next to another perspective's non-security decision question resolved hands-free to `approve` and merge-eligible (with a `changes_requested` too, to the fixer lane): the contributor rule made the question advisory and dropped the reject with it. The head now gets the verdict the reject alone gives it, `reject`, which holds the PR for a person; the question stays in the reasons. On a hive-authored PR, the advisory approves for a non-risk decision question and for a bare non-risk `requires_human` never checked review coverage, so a head whose security review never arrived (a dead kick, or since #16994 a rate-limited review the relay does not record) was merge-eligible. With a perspective missing the head now reads `incomplete` (`review coverage incomplete: missing security`), and the planner re-asks only that perspective under `pending_ttl` / `max_redispatch`. A fully reviewed hive PR's non-risk question is still advisory.
- Fix reviews stalled by removing a configured review perspective while heads are running.
- Review swarm: a re-review triggered by a PR body edit no longer asks the reviewer to revise its old review in place in repos outside `review.revise_repos`. The publish side refuses that request, so the finished review was discarded and the PR re-dispatched until it parked as review-dispatch-exhausted.
- The Activity Monitor's Review and CI chevrons never say "activity unknown": with no verdict and no reviewer in flight the tooltip states what the head waits on (closed, draft, waiting for CI, not started and who is next, or no data for the head yet · refreshing), a settled verdict names who decided, how long ago and each perspective's verdict with its first finding, and settled verdicts stay known as observations age.
- A `requires_human` verdict already stored from rate-limited "could not read … HTTP 429" reviews no longer keeps a PR parked. The verdict collect now sets those report files aside as missing, the way the relay already skips new ones, and withdraws a stored `requires_human` that only they produced. The head reads `incomplete`, and the planner asks the missing perspectives again under `review.pending_ttl` and `max_redispatch`. A head with a set-aside security review is never resolved hands-free to approve while that review is owed. A real hold still parks the PR: a diff too large to read, a security finding, a decision question or the high-risk marker. Before, the pre-upgrade files on projectbluefin/testsuite#1116 kept head `ae22434` at `stage/085-needs-decision` hours after the relay fix was live.
- Review dispatch now remembers heads it passed over for want of a free reviewer, promotes them ahead of webhook-prioritized PRs after three consecutive cycles, and the review queue plus Activity Monitor say how far the review got and how long the head has waited instead of a bare `stalled` pill (#15229).
- The self-report classifier no longer files `unclassified_error_repeated` issues for the review-request watcher warning that an abbreviated verdict head is not the PR's current head and was recorded as written (#14997).
- The activity monitor no longer tells an author who just force-pushed that they have given "no response" ([#16021](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16021)): a human PR whose new head was red again re-entered 071 within one sweep, which restarted the waiting-on-push state and re-nudged for the new head, so the rework chip read `requested · no response` and the row kept "Needs @author". The stage record now remembers the original ask and the head pushed after it (`rework_asked_at`, `rework_pushed_head`, `rework_pushed_at`) across that re-ask, the chip reads `pushed · re-review pending` dated from the push with `requested_at` on the original ask (a review verdict on the pushed head is a fresh ask), and a row whose `push` field says pushed drops the "Needs @author" decision and the needs-human count until CI / the re-review settle.
- A maintainer's PR keeps `role/trusted` when the hive merges main into it. A person's Approve (or the hive's in-place adoption) admits the PR's head, and that route returned before the clean-merged-PR auto-promotion check, so the role label fell back to the author's raw registry tier. On projectbluefin/utah#1132 the hive's merge commit carried hanthor's own approval onto the new head, and the PR went from `role/trusted` to `role/newcomer` three minutes later and stayed there; projectbluefin/utah-packages#893 flipped the same way and back once the approval no longer matched the head. The role now comes from the author's own standing on every admission route: the registry tier, or trusted when their clean merged history promotes them. Who pushed or approved the head no longer changes it.
- The rootless Podman qualification probe now keeps its temporary image store under `/var/tmp` to avoid quota-limited `/tmp` storage and preserves image-pull diagnostics when a prerequisite fails.
- Activity Monitor: the row menu's consequence hints ("merges #15118 into v5 now via hive's identity, attributed to you", "records your approval; the hive's merge sweep merges #15118 on its next pass…") no longer run past the menu border over the rows behind it — a menu with hints grows wider (capped to the viewport) and each hint wraps on its own line under its label, the rescan hint included (#15175).
- Keep ACMM plan auto-approval from bypassing held Spek run checkpoints, recording auto-approval provenance only when the run checkpoint is explicitly disabled.
- Run detail attaches the newest Spek stage transcript even after the lease generation advanced into the next stage, so spec/plan documents, interview Q&A and agent output no longer vanish once a stage completes.
- Runs: a relay adopting a run stage now replaces the hub executor's placeholder lease (not only the admission lease), so the run no longer appears twice in `/api/runs` with a never-expiring duplicate. When a relay's stage lease ages out, the stage is re-minted as an admission placeholder at the same stage and generation so the run returns to the offer pool instead of vanishing.
- Stop the LKE cache-prune DaemonSet from deleting live toolchain binaries by archive timestamp; operators must apply the updated manifest to protect runner tool caches (#13425).
- Show the Activity Monitor's running fleet cost and its rotating period on a separate, wrapping line below the running count so narrow tiles and zoom no longer truncate the amount or period.
- Runs: a checkpoint-held lease no longer reports `activity.lease_heartbeat_at` in the future (the derived heartbeat is clamped to now), and a normal stage advance no longer inherits the `reason`/`reset` attributes of an earlier owner reset on the lifecycle timeline. (#10120, #10117)
- Merge queue holds every open PR claiming an issue that another open PR in a different automerge lane also claims (the hive's own PR vs a trusted human's PR for one issue) until a decision is recorded — lane reason `merge-train:claim-conflict#<other>:<issue>`, log `same-issue claim conflict undecided: #A vs #B`, tracker chevron "held · duplicate of #B · needs decision", and a delegate plan that names the concrete PRs to keep and close instead of "all 2 PRs" (hivecommons/hive#15810).
- Sandboxed agents (`sandbox.enabled: true`, Podman or `runtime: job`) no longer 404 on the card's `📄 full log` / `📋 log text` buttons: hive archives the container's captured stdout/stderr as the kick log (`<kick_log_dir>/<agent>/<kick-start>-sandbox.log`, `source: sandbox-job`/`sandbox-podman`) when the run ends, serves the newest archive from `GET /api/agents/{name}/log`, lists every run in the 🕘 kick history, and names the archive in the last-run record (`logId`); before its first run the button explains that no archived run exists yet. The output used to live only in the Job pod (deleted on completion) and the sandbox workspace (swept after two hours). Reported-by: @joerunde (a1-vllm-spyre spoke).
- Sandboxed kicks no longer push a branch and open a PR just because commits exist: `.hive/agent-report.json` gained an optional `status` (`success`, `failed`, `blocked`), and when the report says `failed`/`blocked` or the sandbox exited non-zero hive keeps the commits local, records the run as failed with the reason (`prWithheld`, shown on the card as "no PR opened: …"), and writes a `sandbox_pr_withheld` audit line instead of a PR that can only fail CI. Reports without a `status` publish as before. Reported-by: @joerunde (a1-vllm-spyre spoke).
- Sandbox PRs now take their title/body from `.hive/pr-title.txt` / `.hive/pr-body.md` in the workspace (or the HEAD commit) instead of a fixed placeholder that referenced hive's own tracker
- Sandboxed agent run records are now written without holding the agent manager lock, so a slow data volume no longer stalls status and kick calls, and `sandbox-runs/runs.jsonl` is compacted to its newest 1000 records so the token collector's scan cost stays bounded.
- The review-request watcher no longer polls at its short cadence indefinitely when the sandbox review manifest directory is untrusted (#14993).
- Sandbox publish preflight (`publish.verify`) reads its commands from config only; a `<!-- hive:publish.verify … -->` block found in a kick message is logged and ignored instead of run.
- The scanner's governor (backlog) kick is no longer deferred indefinitely behind review-fix kicks: after an agent's governor kick has been displaced by a delivered fix kick on two consecutive cycles, the governor kick goes first for that cycle and the fix kick is re-planned, so actionable issues are offered to the agent again instead of sitting unclaimed for hours (#15166).
- Per-agent scoped-token mint with no GitHub App installation ID now logs one actionable warning per agent instead of every tick, and is reported as the `github_app_not_installed` fleet-report class rather than `unclassified_error_repeated` (#14186)
- The dashboard metrics collector now caches its GitHub Search-API count queries (hive-attributed merged PRs / closed issues per repo, outreach PR counts) for `HIVE_FORGE_COUNT_CACHE_TTL` (default `20m`) instead of re-asking on every collect, serves the last-good counts (marked stale) with a 10-minute retry backoff and a rate-limited warning when a refresh fails, and stands down while the GitHub slow-start caution window is engaged. Re-asking every cycle tripped GitHub's secondary rate limit on the hosted hive (2026-10-21) and darkened the automerge sweeps and advisory lookups behind it. Follow-up to the faster eval cycles from #13319.
- `EnumerateActionable` no longer publishes a repo as empty when GitHub refuses its fetch transiently (secondary/primary rate limit, 429, 5xx, pre-emptive refusal): the repo's last successful enumeration is substituted for up to two hours and listed in `ActionableResult.stale_repos`; the repo card carries `countsStale` and the Overview KPI snapshot is marked incomplete so history skips it. The dashboard previously showed TOTAL OPEN ISSUES 0 and a one-row activity monitor during such a refusal while the repo had 19 open issues. Webhook per-row tracker refreshes also skip their GET while the caution window is engaged.
- Webhook, review and continuous-agent wakes no longer re-list every tracked repository: the cadence tick (`eval_interval_webhook_s`, 900s while webhooks are healthy) is the authoritative reconcile pass, each webhook delivery's targeted re-read now upserts/moves/removes that one item in the governor's cached actionable snapshot (not just the activity-monitor row, so newly opened items no longer wait for a cycle), and wake cycles plan from that cached snapshot (`source=cached`, `/api/status.cachedCycles` / `webhookPatches`). A reconcile pass that fails outright keeps the previous snapshot published and marked stale instead of dropping to zero.
- The webhook patch path treats the delivery as a hint and re-reads the item before upserting, applies upserts monotonically by `updated_at` (recording the `X-GitHub-Delivery` id, fetch time and head SHA in `item_patches` for audit), removes closed/merged items and re-adds reopened ones after the confirming GET, and bounds irreversible actions: `CloseIssue`/`MergePR` planned from a snapshot refuse while the repo is stale and re-read an item older than 60s first. A reconcile that fails outright (or a cold start whose GitHub share failed) publishes the last-good figures with `staleSince` / `countsStaleSince` and an Overview "stale · as of" badge instead of zeros.
- The slow-start pacer now prioritises by caller: the governor's enumeration runs high priority, periodic housekeeping (automerge sweeps, review-request watcher, advisory lookups, metrics/fleet-stats collectors) is shed instead of queued when the caution-window queue is deeper than it could wait, the self-authored automerge sweep backs off to a 60s floor while cautious, and GitHub App installation-token mints bypass the pacer entirely — so a secondary-limit 403 no longer starves the eval cycle and token refresh behind housekeeping (`slot would miss request deadline`).
- One GitHub secondary-limit 403 no longer stalls merges for over an hour. A secondary 403 with no `Retry-After` used to assume a full hour, then add the 10-minute slow-start window. For those 70 minutes every low-priority call that would queue more than 5s was shed, including the automerge sweep's commit-status read. On the projectbluefin hive (2026-10-28) one search refusal after a restart meant no PR merged for over an hour, even an approved PR with 19/19 checks green, while the primary quota stood at 87%. Such a 403 now backs off for `Retry-After` when GitHub sends it, or until `X-RateLimit-Reset` when `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is `0`. Otherwise it waits one minute, GitHub's documented rule, and doubles on each repeat up to 15 minutes. Separately, once an automerge lane reaches a candidate PR, the PR's evaluation and merge run at normal pacing priority, so its status and check-run reads are never shed as housekeeping.
- The contributor security hold now reads scope-effective reports, the same ones the review gate decides from, so a security report whose raw `requires_human` verdict only rests on out-of-scope findings can no longer keep a contributor PR parked for a person when a sibling perspective supplies the effective `requires_human` ([#16865](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16865)).
- On a PR the hive did not author, the security review's `requires_human` now stays a hold for a person (`stage/085-needs-decision`, with the finding named) when another perspective also asks for changes. Before, the sibling `changes_requested` folded the security hold into the fix cycle and the PR went back to its author at `stage/072-returned-to-contributor`, although a security finding is the contributor rule's one early exit to a person ([#15640](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15640)). projectbluefin/utah-packages#890 was sent to its author for a PR-body edit while the security review's question about a new App credential waited on a maintainer.
- Activity Monitor bulk “Let hive decide” now works when a multi-PR parent issue is selected, confirming and deciding each open PR once even when its sub-rows are also selected ([#15061](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15061)).
- Review: on a hive-authored PR, a `requires_human` or decision-requested perspective whose in-scope finding sits on a sensitive path (for example `.github/workflows/`) now stays a person's decision under `self_authored_decision_policy: resolve`. It parks at `stage/085-needs-decision`, and the comment names the finding and the reviewer's ask. Before, an ask worded without a risk-class term, such as "apply the `pr-validate.yml` hunk from the PR body", was turned into `changes_requested`. The PR then sat at `stage/070-fixing`, with `stage/stalled` coming and going, through fix attempts that could not land the workflow edit, and nobody was asked. A recorded `decision_finding` also stops the read-time verdict normalizers from turning the hold back into `changes_requested`. Asks for changes, and asks off the sensitive paths, still go to the fixer.
- A spoke whose self-upgrade `PATCH` on its own Deployment is rejected or timed out by a cluster admission webhook (a failing Kyverno webhook on vllm-d blocked every patch) no longer reports the upgrade as **failed** when a plain restart will land it anyway. The patch deadline is raised from 10s to 45s (above the 10s webhook default, so the apiserver can return the real webhook error) and retried once; when the patch still fails and the Deployment tracks a floating tag that the kubelet re-pulls (`imagePullPolicy: Always` or unknown), the spoke exits immediately with a distinct exit code and reports **pending-restart**, so the hub keeps the in-flight latch instead of counting a failed attempt. The hub's stuck-upgrade alert and the orphan-sweep give-up message now carry the spoke's classified cause ("cluster admission webhook (e.g. Kyverno) is rejecting or timing out Deployment patches — a cluster admin must fix or exempt the webhook") instead of the misleading "Deployment tracks a floating tag" guess ([#14385](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14385)).
- The hub no longer re-requests a channel commit date from GitHub on every render after a failed lookup (e.g. HTTP 403 rate limit); it backs off for 10 minutes per commit, so rate-limited hubs stop repeating the "channel commit date: fetch failed" warning.
- The `ci_poll_nudge` self-report now lists the repeated CI-status commands (with counts) in its diagnostics, so the fleet issue is triageable instead of showing only an idle pane summary (#14289).
- Classify the login-required, ioscan classifier fail-closed and startup-kick-dropped WARNs as named fleet-report classes instead of `unclassified_error_repeated` (#14262, #14263, #14266)
- Classify transient GitHub-fetch, label-provisioning and agent-CLI restart-loop WARNs as named fleet-report classes (`github_fetch_transient`, `label_provisioning_failed`, `agent_cli_restart_loop`), report `ioscan_classifier_unavailable` on first observation, and tighten the `agent_pane_timeout` keywords (#14258, #14259, #14260, #14277, #14278, #14286)
- Recurring agent-runtime log lines no longer land in the self-report feed as "unclassified". Self-healing noise (cached GitHub 404s, rate-limited Copilot token validation, permissions repairs) is ignored, while tmux, proxy TLS handshake, per-agent directory setup and review-evidence write failures and feedback issue-refresh failures now report under their own named classes.
- The watchdog's `agent credential failure` log line is now reported under the existing `agent_login_required` selfreport class instead of `unclassified_error_repeated`, so owners are pointed at re-authenticating the agent backend rather than a generic defect report ([#16861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16861)).
- Repeated lane-gate and trusted-author sweep warnings caused by a transient GitHub 500 on the status read are no longer filed as selfreport issues (#15785, #15786); a hub heartbeat rejected with a restarting-hub 502/503/504 is likewise classified as transient (#15789)
- Fleet selfreports no longer file an unclassified-runtime-error issue when the request pacer refuses a request because its slot would miss the caller's deadline; the WARN stays in local logs (#15109).
- Fleet report: forward-port of #13932 to v6 — 'prompt timeout — dumping pane' and 'pane content at timeout' agent-readiness WARNs (plus 'startup kick dropped' / 'cli never reached input prompt') are now classified as agent_pane_timeout (low severity) instead of unclassified_error_repeated (#14264, #14265).
- Fleet selfreports no longer file an unclassified-runtime-error issue per caller when GitHub rate limiting or the hive's own request pacing makes many callers log the same transient failure; the WARNs stay in local logs (#15106).
- Self-reports no longer loop between a spoke and whoever closes them: a runtime-error fingerprint names the defect (class + normalised message) instead of the build, a fingerprint closed upstream is not re-filed by the same hive while it keeps observing the condition (the 7-day cooldown now runs from the last observation, on the direct path and through the hub relay), "Cleared on" comments are paced to once per hive per 24h and withheld under a closed issue, and the catch-all `unclassified_error_repeated` class joins only issues whose title matches the message rather than any open issue of that class.
- Hosted spokes that relay self-reports through the hub now honour the same per-hive new-filing cap and minimum gap as direct filers, so a restarting spoke can no longer file a burst of ten issues in one second; over-cap reports are deferred and retried on the next cycle.
- The fleet self-report no longer files an unclassified-error issue when the review-request watcher suppresses a duplicate review comment under the per-head cap (#15906).
- fix(fleetreport): forward-port the ioscan fail-closed classifier keywords and the copilot model-substitution skip to the v6 self-report feed so they no longer surface as `unclassified_error_repeated` (#14355, #14356)
- Fixed Sentinel posting an "author is trusted (hive agent)" notice instead of a blocking alert on a PR the hive opened to supersede an adopted contributor PR. Such a PR is now judged by the adopted PR's author, since its code is theirs; a maintainer's clearance of the same head on the adopted PR carries over.
- Sentinel `ci_gate_weakening` no longer counts removed `#` comment lines in YAML, Makefile and Justfile CI files, and matches its gate keywords as whole words, so a PR that only rewrites workflow comments (or mentions "hardcoded" or "gateway") is not flagged as weakening CI. `sensitive_path` still flags every workflow edit.
- Sentinel no longer re-flags a PR a maintainer already cleared when a later push leaves every flagged change exactly as reviewed, such as a merge of the base branch from the hive's keep-mergeable step or "Update branch". Each alert now records a digest of what it flagged (each finding's rule and paths, and every flagged file's status and patch against the merge base, read from GitHub's PR files API). A new head with the same digest, after a human (not a Hive account, not a bot) removed the label, counts as cleared: the label is not re-applied and the marker comment is rewritten for the new head. A push that changes a flagged file's patch, flags something new, or returns a flagged file without a patch still re-alerts, as does any alert written before digests existed. This extends the clearance-on-a-newer-head rule from [#13602](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13602) to removals made before the push.
- Avoid filing repeated-error fleet reports for sentinel skips caused by GitHub pacing, while retaining the local warnings and reporting other failures.
- Sentinel: a dashboard Approve on a flagged PR is now remembered as the release of that head — the sweep reads the hive's own `hive:pr-approval head=<sha>` comment instead of treating the hive-account `unlabeled` event as nobody's clearance, so it no longer re-posts the alert and re-applies `sentinel-alert` to the head the owner just approved (dibs#510, hivecommons/hive#15214); a new push still re-arms. On a Prow repo where the bot is not an approver, a later Approve records the decision without re-posting `/lgtm` + `/approve` and reports `commands_skipped`.
- Sentinel now treats trusted Hive authors as notice-only by default, remediates stale trusted-author alert labels, and offers `sentinel.trusted_authors_block` for operators who want the blocking label on trusted PRs too.
- Surface shared-CI recovery permission refusals as an actionable operator handoff, retry after the permission cooldown even on unchanged PRs, and align bot-PR squash attribution with the existing required check.
- A contributor PR whose only red check turns out to be a shared CI incident no longer keeps a nudge that says "the hive will not merge it until the head changes". The 072 nudge goes out as soon as the PR goes red, and the scanner's `[shared-ci]` incident marker can land minutes later: on hivecommons/hive, #16993, #16995, #17000 and #17001 were nudged for `native-queue-policy` about ten minutes before the scanner deferred them to incident #17003. The stage pass already moved such a PR out of 072, but the nudge stayed as posted. Now the nudge is edited in place to say it was withdrawn, for a shared incident or for checks that are red on the base branch, and the head's nudge count is reset. When the incident closes, the PR stays deferred until the shared-CI rerun sweep has re-run its failed jobs (at most 30 minutes), so it is not handed back in the gap before the re-run. The nudge also names the checks that are red on the head where it used to list the CI gate's bare `check-failure` token.
- Sidebar count pills (Overview `40/18`, Governor `4/12`, Projects, Hive activity monitor, Knowledge, Contributors) now share one right edge. The hover-revealed hide toggle (⊘) is appended after the pill on every hideable row and held an invisible 20px slot there, so those pills sat ~26px left of Overview's (the one row that cannot be hidden). The pill is now always the last flex child; the toggle fades in between label and pill on hover, so nothing shifts.
- Dashboard sidebar: the Overview counter (`33/13`, open issues / open PRs) and the Hive activity monitor counter (`37`, rows) count the same open set two ways — every open issue is a row, a PR is its own row only when not drawn under a listed issue. Both tooltips and the activity-monitor header now say so (`37 rows (33 issues + 4 PRs on their own row) · 9 PRs shown on their issue's row`), so the numbers read as one population, not a disagreement.
- Spoke dashboard: clicking a left-sidebar item now keeps the chosen section pinned at the top of the viewport while late renders (status poll/SSE repaints, lazy panels, collapsing sections) shift the layout above it, instead of scrolling away and needing a second click. The hold re-anchors on layout drift for 2.5 s and releases on any wheel/touch/key input; render-time scroll anchoring pins the navigated section rather than the neighbour peeking under the sticky navbar.
- A signed-commit reconciler compare that hits a 404 (missing head branch or invisible repository) is now classified as a persistent GitHub refusal, so it is counted, bounded and noted once instead of being retried uncounted every pass ([#16202](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16202)).
- Activity Monitor: a row parked on a policy sign-off ask (e.g. a fork's workflow change) now says "Review 5/5 · needs your sign-off" / "needs owner sign-off" instead of "awaiting human decision", leads with an inline "Approve ▸" when CI is green (then "Let hive decide ▸"), and no longer captions "Recommendation recorded" when hive kept the park without recording a recommendation.
- Hive no longer supersedes its own PRs for a missing sign-off: the automerge DCO stage treats commits on a PR by hive's `ai_author` or App login as self-squash (so an App-signed commit no longer counts as squash-unsafe), `signoff-rehome` keeps hive-authored and operator-approved heads in place instead of re-authoring them as a new PR, the App's signed re-author commit always carries a `Signed-off-by` trailer, and the push relay refuses a hive-identity commit that lacks one.
- The sign-off attribution notes on an adopted or hive-caused `stage/085` PR (`adoption-stalled:hive-signoff-attribution` and the maintainer sign-off note) no longer say the `Sign-off survives the squash` gate "stays red" on repositories that do not run `.github/workflows/dco-squash-attribution.yml`. They now say the hive will not squash-merge the head, and name that check only when the head's required or reported checks include it. The adopted-PR stall escalation ("adopted PR sits with nothing the hive can push") is logged at INFO instead of WARN, so designed escalations no longer add up to an `unclassified_error_repeated` fleet self-report ([#14466](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14466)).
- Activity Monitor: a tracker row (issue row or PR sub-row) now renders at most one hive note line. The needs-human / decision ask outranks the blocker, next-move and stage-transition notes; a lower note's facts ride the winning line as a trailing clause only when they say something the row does not already (a "moved to Needs human decision" note under a strip already lit at Needs human decision is dropped). The single line keeps its ⬡ icon, View link and one relative age ([#16627](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16627)).
- `skillreg.SpecServesRepo` no longer treats differently-owned org-qualified repo references as the same repo ([#16168](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16168)): a spec scoped to `laredo/cuga-agent` now correctly refuses to serve `acme/cuga-agent`, while bare↔qualified matching remains (bare `cuga-agent` still matches qualified `laredo/cuga-agent`).
- The scanner, issue-request watcher and `/contribute` relay lane no longer dispatch an issue an open pull request already fixes: a live open-PR check (`scanner.skip_issues_with_open_pr`, default on) skips the claim, labels the issue `has-open-pr` and logs `claim skipped: open PR already linked`; and a duplicate-fix sweep resolves two open PRs fixing one issue without an owner decision — the earlier green/pending PR stays, the later hive PR is closed as `duplicate-of:<keeper>` with one comment, a person's later PR is commented on and left open, and only an earlier red/stale PR facing a later green one is escalated to `stage/085` ([#14799](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14799)).
- The hub now keeps GitHub slow-start pacing productive after rate-limit bursts by rejecting hopeless paced requests before they consume slots, reclaiming cancelled slots, logging caution windows, and coalescing duplicate channel commit lookups so hosted hive auto-upgrades can keep resolving targets ([#11468](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/11468)).
- List all 61 SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria in the compliance profile, with explicit not-covered rationales and mappings for monitoring, protected credential movement, and encrypted backups. The A1.2 backup mapping reports the effective key source (governor key_file, default Secret/PVC mounts, or the HIVE_BACKUP_KEY fallback) rather than the raw key_file path.
- Enforce the Spektacular Spec checkpoint hold before runs advance to Plan.
- Fix Spek live activity so hub lease renewals no longer mask idle agent output; dashboard activity now reports agent log idle time and artifact-creation waits.
- Spektacular runs no longer stall after a final plan with `fallback failed: file "<slug>/plan.md" not found`: the plan task-list fallback and the spec postback read now use the timestamp-prefixed artifact id Spektacular actually reports instead of the run's bare slug ([#8737](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8737)).
- Fixed the Spektacular hub executor to resolve timestamped artifact IDs, preserve run worktrees across retry generations, restart stalled own leases, surface non-final CLI exits, and expose live progress/log tails.
- Spektacular hub executor: prune stale git worktree registrations before `worktree add`, keep a run's worktree alive while any lease on the run (including unclaimed retry generations) is active, and mark the executor workspace as a safe git directory so `dubious ownership` no longer blocks git after a uid change. Also fix a Tick race that relaunched a just-finished stage after the lease had already advanced, and kill the whole agent process group on timeout so orphaned CLI grandchildren cannot pin the executor slot, and stop relaunching the agent for a stage whose document is already final (e.g. a plan held for approval).
- The Spek interview form on run and campaign cards is now readable: numbered question blocks, selectable option rows, an optional note per question, and proper Submit/Refresh buttons.
- Spektacular runs no longer stall at "plan is final but task-list import failed; not advancing" on Spektacular 0.22, which has no `plan export` verb: the runner now recognises cobra's `unknown flag: --format` rejection as "export unavailable" and falls back to the on-disk plan artifact, and the plan.md fallback parses Spektacular's native `#### - [ ] Phase N.M: Title` headings (with `**Repo:**`) as the implement tasks in document order, instead of turning every component-breakdown and acceptance-criteria bullet into work ([#8737](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8737)).
- Fix Spektacular stage transcript capture so already-final probes no longer overwrite real session transcripts, status polls include raw step instructions, documents include content, and run stage generations advance once per stage attempt.
- Spektacular stage runner no longer parks a freshly admitted run with `missing_workdir` before any relay has claimed it. Admission leases owned by `hive-triage` are reported as unclaimed and wait for a run-stage-capable contributor; a refusal recorded against one owner's checkout is cleared when the same generation changes hands.
- Spektacular hub-executor workspace paths now consistently use the race-safe workspace-root accessor, preventing shuffled dashboard CI from reporting false data races while stages are being cleaned up.
- Harden the hub Spektacular executor's run/stage lifecycle: git on a shared clone (clone, fetch, worktree prune/add and the sweep's worktree remove) is now serialised per repository so concurrent runs no longer race ([#10107](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10107)); a reused run worktree is moved to the freshly fetched commit before each launch while keeping its untracked `.spektacular/` artifacts ([#10105](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10105)); the poll runner re-resolves the timestamped document on a new generation instead of polling the previous one ([#10096](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10096)); the already-final shortcut now clears the consumed interview round ([#10102](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10102)); an interview request left beside a final document is discarded instead of skipping capture and holding the next stage ([#10101](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10101)); and interview answers are refused while the agent CLI still runs, with request/answer files read bounded ([#10103](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10103)).
- **Spektacular hub executor hardening (#10104, #10095, #10100, #10130, #10098):** the per-generation CLI log is capped at 32 MiB and `/api/runs/{key}/log` reads only the last 4 MiB; run artifact slugs are capped at Spektacular's 64-character name limit so `spec new`/`plan new` no longer fail for long repo names; `file list` and workdir-resolution errors are surfaced instead of swallowed; and `PUT /api/config/governor/features` rejects `spektacularInterview` values other than `auto`/`human` instead of silently storing `human`. Docs now state that file mtime ranks artifacts sharing a slug.
- `auto_merge.squash_only` and per-repo `governor.labels.stage.dco.required` overrides keyed `owner/repo` now apply in a single-org hive: the stage pass matched them on the bare display name, so a squash-only repo could be labelled `merge-method/merge` and loop on GitHub's method-not-allowed refusal.
- `GET /api/hub/release/stable-promotion` no longer mixes a fresh stable SHA with the digest and commit date of the previous stable build, and reports the stable commit time as `built_at` (it was published as `promoted_at`, which misread a commit time as the tag's promotion time).
- The gh wrapper's refusal of `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` for staff agents now names the reads that still work: merged PRs through `gh search prs --repo <owner/repo> --merged --json …` or a GET of `repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls?state=closed`, any authorless `gh search`, and `gh pr view` / `gh issue view`. Agents read the old "listing is blocked" as "there is no way to look up merged PRs", so ci-maintainer parked red audit-trail checks for the owner instead of diagnosing them (Danathar/dns-failover#152, Danathar/openaudible-autoupdate#169). The gate itself is unchanged.
- `stage/030-pr-in-progress` now requires PR evidence. A hive-agent issue claim used to derive 030 on its own (claimswire `claimFactFor`, the `claim` issue request, and the live `hive:claim` marker on enumeration), so an issue the scanner claimed while triaging wore "PR in progress" with no PR or branch to show (hivecommons/hive#13069). Claims — agent, human, contributor, external — now derive `stage/020-claimed`; 030 is written only when the claim carries `PRStarted` (a `hive-open-pr --issues` request or a `<!-- hive:start branch=… -->` / `pr=…` marker), recorded on the ledger and the claim marker as `pr_started=true` so the sweep re-derives the same stage. Legacy `IssueStageFor` and the stage-engine adapter changed together (shadow mismatch gate stays 0); goldens regenerated with `pr_started` variants and three #13069 regression cases.
- The expected-transition table and pipeline diagram now draw `020-claimed → 010-actionable` and `030-pr-in-progress → 010-actionable` (claim released or expired) plus `020 → 040`, so claim expiry is no longer a `stage_transition_anomaly`.
- Stage engine (shadow): the PR deriver now reproduces the stage the automerge pass writes, not only `resolveStage`'s opinion — the pass hands it its post-step inputs (`PRPassFacts`: detected author kind, prior record, human-route evidence, DCO walk, adoption state) and `DerivePR` applies the same 07x split, normalized-fixing guard, `RouteHuman`, DCO override and 074 yield. Human hand-offs the route refined to 071/072 (red checks, conflicts) or 050 (no verdict for the head yet) were counted as `085` mismatches on every pass and kept the 48 h shadow gate from ever reading zero; a goldens parity test now derives all 8 231 fixtures through the engine.
- The stage pipeline diagram and the engine's expected-transition table now draw `071-needs-author ↔ 050-review-pending` (the human twin of the 072 edges), so a human author pushing a fresh head no longer counts as a `stage_transition_anomaly`.
- PR stage labels no longer flip between two stages on every pass with nothing changed. Two sweeps (the engine's ticker and the main loop's queued sweep) reconcile alternate passes from one tracker. A contributor lane that skipped a PR because another merge to its destination was in flight recorded `base-refresh:merge-guard`, which was written as an awaiting-admission stage over the stage the other sweep set a minute earlier (projectbluefin/utah-packages#869 080↔085, #873 080↔090); it is now no opinion. And a lower lane no longer overwrites the stage a higher lane set for the same head while that lane simply did not run this pass, for up to 30 minutes (projectbluefin/utah-packages#878 070↔072).
- The stage-label reconciler now warns once per PR head and refusal reason when the write-back gate refuses reopening a hive-closed superseded PR, instead of on every tick.
- A PR stage the write-back gate kept off GitHub now drives the Overview bands and the your-turn inbox, and the hive no longer announces a label it did not write. On projectbluefin the gate refused every 072/074/085 label on 24 contributor and fork PRs (opt-in label missing, or the backfill guard) from 10-30 on; the stage engine recorded the stage, but bands and ownership read labels, so a PR parked at 085 showed "blocked" with no reason and was in nobody's inbox, while its note said "Moving to `stage/085-needs-decision` so a person sees it" (projectbluefin/fsdk-containers#491, projectbluefin/utah-packages#812). The snapshot now carries the recorded stage beside GitHub's labels (`suppressed_stage`), band and ownership read it, the inbox reason says the label is not on GitHub, the Activity Monitor row's tooltip names the gate's reason (`labels_suppressed`), and escalation notes say the hive would move the PR and why it did not.
- Make review-verdict normalization independent of the previous PR stage and suppress same-head stage reversals for 15 minutes at the reconciler write boundary, preventing idle PRs from repeatedly restarting label-triggered CI ([#16880](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16880)).
- An issue with both a live agent claim and an open hive PR that fixes it now stays at stage/040-covered-by-pr: the eval sweep runs the duplicate-PR guard before the live-claim filter, so the claim no longer re-buckets the issue "claimed" (020) every cycle after its PR opens and the dashboard stage tracker no longer shows a spurious `regressed` chip on nearly every claimed issue.
- A contributor PR is no longer called "Ready for a human merge" while a required check has never reported on its head. projectbluefin/utah#1074, utah#1072 and utah-packages#873 read "N/N checks green … Ready for a human merge" because they were opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so the ruleset-required checks never ran and GitHub would refuse the merge. The stage pass now reads the base branch's required checks (cached per repo and branch), names the ones with nothing reported ("required not reported: contract"), and keeps the PR at `060-reviewed` until they report.
- The stage tracker now surfaces an Actionable issue the scheduler withholds for an open GitHub "blocked by" dependency: the row wears the `blocked` modifier, the chip and tooltip name the blocker(s), the payload carries `blocked_on`, and the caption reads "waiting on #N" instead of plain "waiting for the scanner" — sequenced RFC sub-issues no longer look like intake starvation (hivecommons/hive#14765).
- Stage tracker *Let hive decide* now opens its preview at once as a skeleton (Cancel enabled, the action disabled until the plan lands, errors inline with Retry, no double-fire), prefetches the plan when a row's decision options are revealed and serves it from a 45 s bounded server cache with a `Server-Timing` header; covered issue rows read "Covered by PR #N — waiting for a decision on the PR" with a chip that scrolls to the PR's row, and every 👤 next move carries a short `human_reason` after its chevron word ([#15773](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15773)).
- Stage tracker: Let hive decide now shows the hive is working at once, covered issues no longer repeat their PR's button, and a person's move says why (#15773)
- Activity tracker: the "updated … ago" chip now reports when its 30s poll is failing (`poll failing (HTTP 504)` / `(unreachable)`), goes amber at once and demotes `fresh` to `cache`, instead of counting up "updated 8m ago · fresh" from the last good payload while the server is unreachable (#14416).
- Dashboard: the Hive activity monitor's ▶ Play / ▶ Play both sound previews were silent in Safari and Chrome because the play checked `AudioContext.state` synchronously right after an un-awaited `resume()`; previews now create and resume the context inside the click, wait for it to come up (handling Safari's `interrupted` state), show "Playing…" on the button and toast when the browser blocks audio, while automatic merge/open plays resume briefly without bursting and re-arm gesture priming until a resume actually succeeds.
- Activity Monitor: the row event line no longer says "fell back to" for forward moves whose stage number happens to decrease — triage accepted (015 → 010), a decision made (085 → 080), the author resuming (072 → 070). The stage table now carries `falls_to` from the stage engine's regression rule, and only those hops read as a fall.
- Stage writer no longer removes Prow's `dco-signoff: yes|no` labels; it only reconciles its own `dco` / `no-dco` pair, ending the remove/re-add label war with Prow on every open PR (#13125).
- Issue stage sweep writes `stage/040-covered-by-pr` again for issues an open PR covers: the second in-cycle `annotateIssueWithClaim` pass no longer re-grades the hive's synthesised covered label as GitHub's, which had left issues with an open `Fixes #N` PR stuck at 010 (#14397).
- stagelabels: Owned and Plan now match existing stage labels case-insensitively, consistent with Current (#13909)
- Stage-label predicates `Current` and `IssueCoveredByPR` now consistently normalize labels (lowercase and trim whitespace) before matching, ensuring both functions agree on case handling.
- Issue claims held by a hive agent are released the moment that agent's CLI is relaunched (hive boot, restart), with a `hive:release` marker comment that claim readers now honour, so an issue no longer sits at `stage/020-claimed` for the full agent TTL after a rollout. Rate-limit relaunches of Copilot agents are also spaced across the fleet (one per 30s) instead of all agents re-validating the same exhausted token budget together.
- Parked issues no longer show "Needs human decision" after a maintainer has acted: the un-park sweep honours a maintainer's `/fixed` (alias `/close`) on a parked issue — closing it as completed, clearing `needs-human` and the stage labels, and posting one acknowledgement ([dibs#459](https://github.com/hivecommons/dibs/issues/459)); `/hive approve` and `/hive decision` lift `needs-human` whoever applied it, with the reply naming who had, while `hold` stays untouched ([docs#419](https://github.com/hivecommons/docs/issues/419)); a new closed-issue sweep strips `stage/*` and a Hive-added `needs-human` from issues that closed wearing them ([homebrew-hive#127](https://github.com/hivecommons/homebrew-hive/issues/127)); and the dashboard tracker drops closed issues and reads the needs-decision state from the issue's current labels rather than a stale store record.
- Demote the stale status snapshot drop to Info; warn only after repeated consecutive drops (#14117)
- relay: a multi-hub relay now accepts standby assignments from the hub that acknowledged its standby instead of rejecting them as not the active polling slot (#16422)
- Bot Dependency Dashboards and the Hive Advisory Report no longer get a stage label. A triage bot's `needs-human` on mergeraptor's Dependency Dashboards (projectbluefin/gutenprint-printer-app#45, ps-printer-app#50, hplip-printer-app#42) parked them at `stage/045-needs-decision`; the sweep and the out-of-cycle facts now derive no stage for standing meta issues, so the 045 comes off.
- Classify repeated startup kicks dropped during an agent restart or stop as `startup_kick_interrupted` instead of an unclassified runtime error.
- Agent status, triage, verification and gate-check comments and every relay `label` request no longer count as a start signal, so they no longer record an agent claim or stage the issue `stage/030-pr-in-progress`; a comment starts work only with `<!-- hive:start -->`, a "starting now"-style phrase or an opening "Starting …"/"Implementing …". Claim admission (every producer) now also refuses issues parked on a person (`stage/045-needs-decision`, `needs-spec`, …) and umbrella issues labelled `epic` (new `governor.claims.never_claim_labels`, default `[epic]`), and the stage engine never derives `stage/020`/`stage/030` from a claim on an epic. The Settings dialog (Features → Issue claims) gains a “Never-claim labels” control for `governor.claims.never_claim_labels`.
- The dashboard status snapshot is now published before the governor's serial kick dispatch as well as after it, so `/api/status` (and the stage tracker, agent states and `governor.nextKickAt` derived from it) reflects an evaluation within seconds instead of after every due kick has been delivered — a phase that took 10–15 minutes on hosted hives and, when a rolling upgrade landed mid-dispatch, meant the evaluation never reached the dashboard at all. Snapshots the stale-build guard refuses are now logged at Warn and counted in a new `statusStaleDrops` field on `/api/status`.
- The Twitch matrix streamer no longer drops frames on every encoder hiccup: `VIDEO_QUEUE_FRAMES` defaults to 256, the audio queue is configurable (`AUDIO_QUEUE`), x11grab uses wallclock timestamps with `aresample=async=1` so audio/video PTS cannot drift, and a stall watchdog restarts ffmpeg when frames stop for 30 s or `speed` stays below 0.90x for 60 s, publishing its samples to `/run/stream/health.json`; the README gains a "Why does the player buffer?" diagnosis recipe.
- Twitch streamer (`src/deploy/stream`): no longer OOMKilled in a loop when the x264 encoder falls behind — the x11grab input queue is bounded (`VIDEO_QUEUE_FRAMES`, 16 raw frames instead of 1024, which could pin 8.5 GiB of MIT-SHM frames shared with Xvfb), x264 threads follow the cgroup CPU quota instead of `nproc`, Chromium runs with `--disable-dev-shm-usage --renderer-process-limit=1 --disable-extensions --js-flags=--max-old-space-size=1024`, the supervisor reloads the tab when Chromium's RSS passes `CHROMIUM_RSS_RELOAD_MIB`, and the Deployment requests 1 CPU / 3 Gi and limits 3 CPU / 6 Gi
- Twitch streamer self-heals: a watchdog asks Twitch whether the channel is live and restarts ffmpeg (then the pod) when ingest drops silently; probes now follow the watchdog heartbeat and tolerate Twitch's post-drop key lock.
- "Let hive decide" now tells the owner when a recorded decision never took effect and what to do about it: past `decisions.delegate.effect_timeout` (default 30m) a repeat click answers "Hive decided <plain action> at <time>, but it hasn't taken effect: <plain why>" with Merge as maintainer / Re-run decision / Close as superseded / Send back for a new commit as buttons, and the hive posts one plain-words follow-up on the item; every rule, verdict and reason is rendered from one glossary (Go + dashboard mirror) so slugs like `contributor-offline` or "supersede" are never shown bare; the delegate's `/hive decision` comment carries "Hive decided / Why / What happens next / If it doesn't happen"; and a decision comment the hive itself posted is never parsed as a reviewer's change request — the self-blocking seen on [#14822](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14822).
- Delegated "supersede now" adoption decisions on trusted-bot PRs (`github-actions` and friends, observed on the self-authored lane) are executed instead of silently skipped every sweep with the `adoption/supersede` label left in place (hivecommons/docs#500 waited 15h); the supersede replays a conflicting head onto a fresh base first and, when that replay conflicts, posts one note naming the failure, consumes the request and keeps the PR on its fixing stage with reason `supersede-conflict`, and a request on the hive's own PR is refused once with a note rather than looping.
- Review aggregation no longer routes a hive-superseding PR to the fixer when every perspective's `requires_human` is a pure approver question with nothing above an informational finding. That route dispatched no-op fix kicks until the cycle was exhausted, then re-authored the same change (#16398 → #16456 → #16607) while the approver the reviewer asked never saw a decision. Such a head keeps its decision question, parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` with approve / request-changes actions, and the tracker's review chevron reads "waiting on a human approver · reviewer verified, needs sign-off".
- Task MCP: `ci_health` lists the checks required for the task's own repository. It always listed the global `auto_merge.required_checks`, even for a repository with its own `auto_merge.repos.<repo>.required_checks`, so a worker there was pointed at checks its repository does not require and never shown the ones it does. `ci_health` also no longer reports the primary repository's name as each check's `default_branch`: the hive keeps no default branch per repository, so the field is now left out instead of carrying a wrong value.
- Task MCP: the `dependencies` tool (and `context_bundle` when it includes `dependencies`) can no longer deadlock a bead store. For a task whose issue has a planned epic, it looked the epic's children up from inside a read of that same store. The store's lock is not reentrant, so if anything wrote a bead between the two reads (a claim, a status change, the planner creating children), the inner read waited for the writer and the writer waited for the outer read. From then on every read and write of that agent's bead store blocked until the hive restarted, and the contributor admission gate, which reads every bead store on each pass, hung with it. The children are now found in the single pass that already walks the store. A child created before its epic is also no longer listed twice in `suggested_plan`.
- Task MCP: the `knowledge` tool, which worker agents call to look up the hive's knowledge for their task, now finds facts for a query of several words and for a word that comes later in a page, and it returns each fact's complete body. Before, it kept a fact only when the whole query was one unbroken piece of the title, the first 200 characters or the tags, so most lookups came back empty although the knowledge store's own search had found the fact, and the body it served was that 200-character snippet with no tool to read the rest. A body longer than 16 KiB is cut and ends with a marker that says so. `repo_conventions` now also returns a fact typed `conventions` for the task's repository when the word is not in its text. Both tools now check the page they read for a body: when a page of the same name in another knowledge channel was a draft or belonged to another repository, `repo_conventions` could serve that page's text, and it now serves the listed fact instead.
- Fix the task MCP going dead 30 minutes into a remote contributor's task on hives with `task_mcp.remote_enabled`: the per-task MCP token expired with the first task-lease window even though the hub kept renewing the lease, so every task that ran longer got HTTP 403 from its task MCP for the rest of the task. The token now works for as long as the hub's lease on the task is alive, is still refused as soon as the task is released, completed, failed, yanked or its lease lapses, and has a hard cap of 24 hours after assignment.
- Task MCP endpoint (`POST /api/contribute/mcp`): `ping` is answered with an empty result, as MCP requires, instead of "method not found", so an agent's MCP client that pings to check the server is alive no longer reads the hive's task server as gone. Notifications other than `notifications/initialized` (for example `notifications/cancelled`, sent after a client gives up on a tool call) are acknowledged the same way `notifications/initialized` always was, instead of being answered with a "method not found" error. Unknown request methods are still refused with `-32601`. Authentication is unchanged: the endpoint still answers only a caller that presents a valid lease token, launch token or the dashboard token.
- Kicks: the "Task context MCP" pointer is now sent only to agents that have the `hive-task` MCP server. Every kick told its agent "The `hive-task` MCP server is connected for this launch. Call `context_bundle` first", but only a Claude Code launch is given that server, so agents on copilot, codex, gemini, goose, omp, pi, agy, bob, cline and the other non-Claude backends were told on every kick to call a tool they do not have. With `task_mcp.drop_stuffed_context: true` their issue and PR lists were also cut down to bare `repo#N` refs, leaving them with neither the lists nor the server. The pointer and the elision now apply only to an agent that launches as Claude Code (an inference backend or a model gateway counts, and an agent that provider rotation moved to another backend is judged by the backend it runs on) on a hive with a dashboard token; without that token no launch token is minted and the endpoint refuses every call, so no agent on such a hive is pointed at it. Every other agent gets the kick it had before the pointer existed.
- Task MCP: `related_work` and `history` judge citations of the task's issue correctly. An item counted as related when its title or body held `#N` followed by a boundary, whatever stood before it, so issue 42 of any other repository (`kubernetes/kubernetes#42`) and text such as `abc#42` counted as a citation of this repository's issue 42 and unrelated items were served as related work. A full link to the issue (`https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`) did not count at all. A bare `#N` now counts only at the start of the text or after a character that cannot end a repository name or a word; `owner/repo#N` must be this repository; and a link to the issue or pull request in this repository counts (including GitLab's `/-/issues/N`).
- Task MCP: `related_work` (and the `related_work` part of `context_bundle`, and `history`) works on hives that list their repositories by bare name. Most hives write `project.repos: [console]` with `project.org`, and every issue and pull request in the hive's snapshot is stamped with that spelling, while a task is always scoped to `owner/repo`. The tool compared the two spellings, matched nothing, and answered with an empty list for every task on such a hive. An item that carries its repository's bare name is now read as that repository's full name. An item that names a different repository is still left out.
- The task MCP endpoint now answers a notification-only POST (a request with no `id` and a `notifications/` method) with `202 Accepted` and no body, as MCP Streamable HTTP expects, instead of a `200` JSON-RPC result ([#16903](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16903)).
- The dashboard's `/terminal` proxy now presents ttyd's basic-auth credential (`HIVE_TTYD_CREDENTIAL`, else `hive:<HIVE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN>` — the entrypoint's precedence) on every forwarded request, including the websocket upgrade, and drops any browser-supplied `Authorization` instead of relaying it. On token-protected spokes the already-authenticated browser was re-challenged by ttyd with a native user/password dialog after the dashboard had admitted it; the Node proxy's `/terminal` route is fixed the same way (#14693).
- Deflaked `test-issue-confirm-fixed.sh`: the DRY_RUN assertion piped `printf` into `grep -q`, which raced SIGPIPE under `pipefail` and intermittently failed `build-and-test`. (#16151)
- Fixed the tool-approval scan lane skipping its guardrail-path check for write tools it did not recognise by name ([#16976](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16976)): `create`, `apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor`, `multi_edit`, `write_file` and any agent-specific editor tool writing `.github/workflows/**`, `OWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `hive.yaml`, `policies/**`, `proxy/rules*` or `gh-wrapper*` auto-approved at L5/L6 where `write`/`edit` were denied. The check now holds every tool not classified read-only that names a file — an unrecognised tool name fails closed on those paths, so a read tool `IsReadOnly` does not spell is denied there until it is added (Copilot CLI's `view` is now spelled). `IsLocalWrite` spells the Copilot CLI and Codex editor tools too.
- Dashboard topbar: the ≡ drawer toggle is no longer clipped off the left edge on phones, and on ≤360px-wide screens the 🐛/⚙ chips collapse into the account menu (which gains a Settings entry) instead of overflowing the row.
- The dashboard topbar no longer shows an empty outlined pill between Settings and the health badge when every AI provider is usable: the hidden providers chip (`#oc-providers`) was still painted because the shared `.nav-chip` display rule outranked the `hidden` attribute. The chip now also carries a title/aria-label describing its state.
- The Hive activity monitor now lists every open issue and pull request from its `opened` webhook (with replay and poll fallback) instead of waiting for the governor's next publish, and renders a not-yet-staged item as a `000-new` row in the Open column that says who moves it next — a maintainer's triage label or the hive's stage-label pass — and when the next pass is due (#15094).
- Activity Monitor: while a row action is in flight the lit chevron shows one readable progress caption ("Queuing for merge…") on an opaque plate instead of a faint label over the stripes next to the old stage word (hivecommons/hive#15412).
- Hive Activity Monitor: every lit stage pill now draws its actor icon from a server-derived `stage_actor` (hive ⬡, contributor clanker, human, bot cog, or none with a "no one is working on this right now — why" tooltip) instead of guessing from the author; a bot-authored or unowned red PR reads "Conflicting · bot PR" / "Red · nobody on it" instead of an active "Fixing"; a PR closing several open issues is drawn once (`drawn_under`) with a "↳ #N · under #M" chip on the other issues; and the "Merged today" counter sits directly above the Merge gate / ✓ column header so the merge token's flight ends above the gate.
- Activity monitor row actions now show progress and never fail silently (hivecommons/hive#15436). **Close (read)** on an advisory row did nothing — an advisory is not a decision park, so the `decide:*` target mapping came up empty and the click returned without a request, a dialog or a toast. It now acts on the advisory row itself and really closes the issue (acknowledgement comment, closed as completed); an empty target list toasts a warning instead of returning silently. Every mutating row action (close-read, close-superseded, won't-fix, hold, approve, merge, decide) puts the chevron into the striped busy state with the verb as caption from the first byte sent, shows *Closed · leaving list* / *Merged · leaving list* once the server answers, and the server drops an operator-closed item from the tracker for `HIVE_OPERATOR_CLOSED_GRACE` (default 15m) so the row cannot come back before GitHub's list catches up. A close on an operator-paused repo is refused with the reason and writes nothing; refused, failed and network-errored actions restore the chevron, toast the reason and put it on the row's history badge (red, hover's first line), and the ledger records refused answers as `failed` with the one-line why.
- Describe failing author-owned PRs with unknown work activity instead of inferring that nobody is working from an absent Hive stage actor, including inline and nested PRs while preserving known Hive and bot routing.
- Activity Monitor: no status symbol rotates on a chevron or pill any more — the working glyph, the merge gate's ⟳ sweep glyph and the acting caption's spinner are static icons; their tooltips still say what the hive is doing (#15187).
- Every open issue in the Activity Monitor now offers a permission-checked Close issue action with an in-app confirmation; only the selected issue closes, leaving linked pull requests and other issues unchanged.
- Activity tracker: a follow-up or duplicate PR opened against an issue an earlier merge already delivered now reads `closed by #N` (the merged PR GitHub records as the closer, never an open PR with `Fixes #N`), or `closed · this PR unmerged` when no merged closer is known, instead of a bare `closed` chip that read as if the issue had been closed before its fix merged; docs state the rule that the hive closes an issue only after its PR merges
- A PR or issue closed on GitHub no longer reappears on the Hive activity monitor for minutes after the webhook re-read had already removed it.
