The eval cycle in flight at the time of the close published its status snapshot from the enumeration it started with (listing the item open), overwriting the webhook patch until the next full enumeration re-listed the repo (pluk#313 came back 4 s after closing and left again ~5 min later; up to `governor.eval_interval_webhook_s` plus a cycle in the worst case). Webhook re-reads are now remembered for `dashboard.stage_tracker.webhook_refresh_replay_window_s` (default `1800`) and re-applied to every status snapshot published meanwhile, monotonic on GitHub's `updated_at` so a later reopen still wins; repo issue / PR totals follow the patched lists, and a closed PR also takes its issues-feed copy with it. Closed items now leave within one dashboard poll.
- A closed issue or PR no longer stays on the Hive activity monitor when the confirming re-read a webhook delivery queues is refused (critical API budget, rate-limit caution window) or fails: the tracker now applies the payload's own `state` on every `issues`, `issue_comment` and `pull_request*` delivery, so a closed or merged item leaves on whichever action arrives (`labeled`, `unlabeled`, a comment — not only `closed`), its eviction is handed to the governor and remembered for replay like a re-read, and an open re-read older than the listed copy can neither rewrite the row nor un-remember a close (hivecommons/hive#14159 and #14064 sat at "Triage needed" / "Needs human decision" twenty minutes after closing, through the close, a bot comment and the stage-label sweep's unlabel). As a backstop for deliveries that never arrived, on each status publish it lists each repo's items closed since its last look every `dashboard.stage_tracker.closed_sweep_interval_s` (default `300`, one list call per repo, negative disables) and evicts any still shown.
- Activity Monitor: a PR the hive closed when it opened its replacement (close-first supersession) no longer renders under its issue as a bare sub-row with an empty ladder; the live replacement PR carries a small "supersedes #N" chip (hover: when it was closed, link) as the only trace, and the issue's ladder follows the live PR alone.
- Tracker Copy link now copies the selected issue or PR's canonical URL, including PRs linked or nested under issues, instead of copying the parent issue link.
- Show verified external merges at Activity Monitor's existing terminal step on root, inline and nested PR rows, using retained models and the actual recorded merger without inventing queue membership, Hive ownership or a second merge event.
- Hive activity monitor: the per-row select checkbox and ⋯ actions gutter is now present on every issue and PR row after every render path and always visible — dimmed at rest, full emphasis on hover/focus, on selected rows, and on all rows while a selection or the context menu is open — instead of a hover-only reveal that left an unpredictable, shifting subset of rows with a visible gutter as the live refresh swapped nodes under a still pointer (follow-up to [#13535](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/13535)).
- Activity Monitor: the right-most tracker column no longer shows a ✓ — the column header, the unmerged cap chevron and the "did I act on this?" badge now wear a history mark (clock with a counter-clockwise arrow); the badge is a neutral pill, carries the count of recorded actions and an aria-label, and keeps its hover history. The green ✓ remains only once a PR has merged.
- Explain exact-head human requirements separately from optional delegation and neutral ownership without inferring human presence, preserve covering-PR reasons and genuine current actions, reconcile old-head push requests and observed same-head CI retries, and keep pending head validation and requested review changes in CI/Review rather than implying approval or preparation admits a ready merge-queue seat.
- Keep informational trusted-author security notices separate from actual sentinel gates in Activity Monitor, quoting the real reviewer question without assigning exclusive decision authority to either the PR author or a person the reviewer mentions.
- Activity Monitor issue messages now follow covering PR progress instead of stale New/scanner captions, including links discovered from the PR side.
- Activity Monitor merge zap fires again: `recently_merged` entries recorded by the PR poller under a repo's short name (`repo=hive`) are now qualified to the `owner/name` the tracker rows carry, so human and observed merges match; a PR that drops off the open list a poll before its `pr_merged` audit entry lands is remembered as open until the entry arrives instead of being missed; a context the autoplay policy still holds suspended re-arms the gesture priming rather than queueing stale voices. New: a short bee-like buzz when an issue or PR first appears on the list (same opt-in chip, once per item, capped per refresh, silent on hidden tabs); turning the chip on plays one zap then one buzz.
- Keep Activity tracker chevrons compact on mobile while preserving their caption and icon alignment.
- Hive activity monitor: stage moves now animate on the live refresh. The hosted hive refreshes the tracker about once a second and the panel was rebuilt wholesale each time, cutting every move off after its opening flash; rows are now reconciled by item key so an in-flight move keeps its node, and rows leaving the list collapse out (`--ham-move-exit-ms`) while new rows fade in (`--ham-move-enter-ms`), both off under None or reduced motion.
- Hive Activity settings: the Movement animation preview no longer stacks a second, mis-sized chevron strip under the sample row; each Preview rebuilds the one sample row in place so it matches live tracker rows.
- Activity Monitor tracker: a human-authored PR waiting on its own author no longer leads with the red "Close as superseded" inline button (a close leads only when the server marks it `lead`, i.e. the reviewer named the superseding PR) and its pill reads "waiting on @author to push"; an issue and its asking nested PR render "Let hive decide" once, on the PR sub-row, instead of twice.
- Hive activity monitor: the `since` age now sits in line with the chevron strip and the status pill (`hold`, `stalled`, `unauthorized`, …) hugs the last title line directly over its own strip, with a hairline between entries and a whole-row hover tint, so a tall row (wrapped title, `↳ #PR` line) no longer floats its pill and age into the gap between two rows (#14640).
- Hive activity monitor: every row that involves a PR now draws the issue on the left and the PR on the right. A PR with no open linked issue shows a muted "no linked issue" (or "linked issue #N closed") placeholder in the issue slot and names itself in the PR column instead of standing in the issue slot with the PR column blank; `/api/stage-tracker` PR items carry `linked_issues` (GitHub's closing references for the PR body's Fixes/Closes/Resolves keywords) and a PR whose open issue is listed is paired with it from the PR side too ([#13421](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13421)).
- Activity tracker ([#15589](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15589)): a merge-queue chevron reads "Merge queued · 1st of 2" (the place with the queue length) and, when more than one train is on the page, names its train — "· train main.go" (the first overlapping file's basename, else the head `#N`) with a hover leading "Train of 2 PRs overlapping main.go; merges after #15567." — so two trains no longer show two unexplained "1st"s; the provisional suffix reads "queued 1st of 2 once ready" the same way, and each train's header and member rows share one left-rail accent colour so trains tell apart at a glance.
- Activity monitor: a PR whose body says `Refs #N` (or `Related to`, `Part of`, `Towards`, `See` …), whose title ends in `(#N, part 1)`, or whose first paragraph mentions an open issue, now sits on that issue's row under a muted `refs` chip instead of showing "no linked issue"; closing links still win and are drawn unchanged.
- Activity Monitor: a PR or issue by a registered contributor-hub clanker owner now reads as a clanker (author_kind_source `registry`) instead of an inferred person, so the row icon, its tooltip and the stage pill's holder ("@login's clanker") agree with the stage engine that adopts such PRs.
- An issue an open PR already covers (040) no longer falls to 020/010 — and books a spurious **regressed** badge on the activity monitor — when a contributor claims it, the claim is released, or a start mark lands between sweeps: the out-of-cycle stage-fact path now re-reads the remembered covering PR and keeps 040 while it is open. The `regressed` pill also explains itself: its tooltip, the row tooltip and the current-stage caption read "regressed: <from> → <to> at <time> because <reason>".
- Dashboard activity tracker: a pull request whose `Fixes #N` issue has already closed while the PR is still open is now anchored on the PR — the PR's number, title, stage and age lead the row and the closed issue becomes a muted `closes #N · closed` chip (plus `issue closed (not planned)` when GitHub says so) — instead of drawing the dead issue struck through as the headline (hivecommons/hive#14655).
- Activity Monitor: a PR whose linked issue is already closed keeps that issue as the row head (struck through, `closed` chip) instead of promoting the PR into the issue slot; when another merged PR closed the issue the chip reads `closed by #N` and links to it (#15232).
- Activity monitor hovers, the merge-gate chip popover, the ⋯ menu hints and the server captions say each thing once in plain words: the 090 "Ready for human merge" popover is now one sentence of state, one primary action ("Merge it") plus "More ⋯", who asked and when, and a collapsed Details holding how to trust the author and the rails; the untrusted-author reason, caption, next-move line and menu consequences lost their config keys, stage numbers and internal nouns and no longer repeat each other ([#15394](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15394)).
- **The activity monitor no longer shows "Sentinel alert" on a PR whose `sentinel-alert` label a maintainer already removed.** The tracker also flagged any PR whose current head's review evidence recorded sentinel findings, which was meant for trusted authors' notice-only findings but also caught blocking alerts a maintainer had reviewed and cleared — so a cleared, unchanged PR kept its danger chip and "Sentinel alert · needs human" lane text indefinitely. Sentinel findings in the evidence bundle now record whether they were a `notice`, and a row without the label is flagged only by notice findings. Bundles written before this read as alerts, so an older notice-only row stops showing the chip until its next sentinel pass.
- **Hive activity monitor: open-since age and one row count.** A plain *Open* chevron (no stage label yet, not on hold) now reads "Open · since 3d" ("since 14h" under two days), taken from the same instant the row's `since` column draws, with the ISO time in the chevron tooltip and a subtle red tint past two days (`STAGE_TRACKER_OPEN_STALE_DAYS`); *Open · hold* is unchanged, and an Open item carrying the `blocked` label gets its own "Open · blocked" word (⛔, hold's tint) that keeps the age — "Open · blocked · since 7h" — with the blocker (or the label) named in the chevron tooltip; hold wins when both are present. The sidebar badge and the list header no longer disagree: both are the **row count** of the default view from one shared function (the badge used to count open issues + PRs while the "of N" line counted rows, so a PR drawn on its issue's row made the badge read higher). That gap is now a footnote on the "showing" line's tooltip and the badge — "2 PRs shown on their issue's row" — and each such PR is led by a ↳ glyph whose link tooltip explains the shared row (and names the other issue when two list the same PR). A PR whose issue a filter hides still renders as its own row.
- Activity Monitor sounds work for every repo the hive governs: the client-side short-name resolution for `recently_merged` now learns `owner/name` from every item of every repo (issues included), so a repo whose last open PR just merged still zaps; the multi-repo path (server-side qualification over all configured repos, merge/new-item detection over the union of all repos' items) is now pinned by tests.
- Activity Monitor: a PR under repair — being fixed, waiting on its author or contributor, parked on a human decision, or with a red required check — is no longer a merge-train member. The planner skips it, the tracker drops it from the train with a muted hover note ("left the merge train while being fixed; rejoins when green"), the remaining members close ranks (count, ordinals, front), and a train left with one PR renders no header and no ordinal. Hive's own #15405 led a header as "1st: #15405" while its chevron read "Fixing" ([#15615](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15615)).
- The shared tracker row asset now exports `trackerrow.RequiredGlobals`, the `STAGE_TRACKER_*` constants it reads from its host page pinned to the spoke's values, and tests fail if that list drifts from the asset or if the spoke declares a different value, so the hub cannot silently light different columns than the spoke. `dashboard-source-layout.md` also lists `tracker-human-attention` in manifest order (#16067, #16068).
- Activity Monitor: a PR queued in the base preparation train whose current head is already approved now reads "Approved N/M · queued for base refresh behind PR #<front>" instead of "waiting for a verdict on the current head" (hivecommons/hive#16756).
- A red hive pull request whose failure an agent triaged as infrastructure is now re-run instead of sent back to a fixer. On [projectbluefin/common#1647](https://github.com/projectbluefin/common/pull/1647) the agent said "infrastructure, not this change" four times, the fix loop still counted six fix re-dispatches on that one commit and escalated the PR to a person, and a lane then pushed an empty "retrigger CI" commit. When every failing check run on the head carries a `hive-ci-transient` marker, Hive now re-runs the failed jobs once for that head (`rerun-failed-jobs`, through the write-back gate as `ci_rerun`) and sends no fix kick while that re-run is owed. A head still red after the re-run goes back to the normal fix loop. The fix kick now tells the agent to stamp the marker and never push to retrigger CI, and the reviewer lane's DE-ESCALATE verdict no longer asks for a push when the branch is already current.
- Fix inference-gateway requests failing with `tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks` when a Claude Code user turn carries text alongside a tool result: the translator now emits the `tool` messages directly after the assistant `tool_calls`, before the text.
- Activity Monitor: an issue the reporter-trust gate holds for a maintainer now reads **Triage needed** in the Open column (chevron, hover and row headline) from the moment the gate holds it, with the `needs-triage` modifier and the inline **Accept triage** lead — instead of **New** with the ask only in the caption, as hivecommons/hive#15437–#15440 did before the awaiting label landed; the caption of every held row (000-new or 015) is now exactly *Triage needed — accept or close* instead of repeating *triage* three times.
- Stage engine: `stage/015-triage-needed` is now derived only for issues the reporter-trust gate is holding (`needs-triage` label or the `reporter_triage` bucket); issues filed by hive agents or trusted humans are triaged by construction and stay `010-actionable` instead of being demoted to 015.
- Refresh persisted triage acceptance into the work queue and activity monitor on first acceptance and idempotent retries, reporting handoff failures instead of showing an unconfirmed success.
- Trust-promotion announcement records in the stage-label store are no longer exempt from `Prune` forever: they are now dropped once unseen for 180 days (or the prune age if longer), so the store stops accumulating one record per contributor while an author is still not re-announced within that window (#15463).
- Contributor-lane auto-promotion is announced once per author per hive instead of on every open PR by the author at once: the first PR that earns it gets one shorter, author-wide comment ("@login is now trusted for contributor-lane merging in this hive …"), the author's other open and later PRs post nothing, the announced fact survives restarts in the stage store, and a demotion followed by re-promotion announces once more ([#15443](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15443)).
- Activity Monitor: a row never lights more than two chevrons, and a filled chevron now always means "this is where the item is / what is in motion". CI and Review are filled (amber) only while a check-run or a review perspective is actually running on the current head; passed / approved, findings, pending and decided verdicts are words in their colour on the muted field. Unreported checks and rows waiting on a person render as pending words, never amber. When both tracks run, the stage chevron is settled-current. A queued review swarm reads "Review 0/5 · swarm requested" instead of 5/5 (#16540).
- A trusted merger's typed `/hive decision approve` now answers the review swarm's `requires_human` question on the head, as the dashboard's approval already did, instead of releasing only the workflow-path fence. Before, an owner-authored PR that edits `.github/workflows/` released the fence on that comment, was told the hive "merges this PR itself once the usual gates … are clear", and then sat at `contributor-lane:no-verdict` for hours (Danathar/zfs-aurora-complex#254); GitHub refuses the owner's own Approve review, so nothing on the PR named the command that would clear the verdict. The contributor lane records the typed approval as the decision when it reads the comment for the fence (so it counts on a PR with no stage label), and the un-park sweep records a bare `/hive decision approve` on a PR the hive did not open instead of replying with review-only advice. A decision recorded on the head after the comment still stands. The fence-release comment says whether the approval answered the verdict or which command still does; the 085 comment, the `/hive approve` reply on a workflow-path PR and the docs name `/hive decision approve` (typed or from the dashboard) as clearing both gates.
- Fixed an accepted `/hive approve` / `/hive decision` leaving `stage/045-needs-decision` on an issue that `project.issue_filter` refuses, under a reply saying it was removed. The un-park now hands the stage writer the labels the issue really carries, and its replies name only the stage labels that are gone once the engine has run.
- The "What to reply" notice on a parked issue now stays the newest comment, in a green TIP box with the recommended reply in bold. Before, it was posted once and only edited in place, so a later comment buried it: on Danathar/exult#374 the notice went up at 10:03, the agent's new owner step re-parked the issue at 19:15, and the commands sat mid-thread above it. When a later comment pushes the notice up, the sweep now posts a fresh one at the bottom and deletes the old one; a maintainer's command and Hive's reply to it do not move it, and the move goes through the write-back gate. The notice and the `/hive help` reply list the commands in a GitHub `[!TIP]` alert, which GitHub themes green for light and dark, with the reply `/hive approve` accepts in bold and marked `(recommended)` when the park names one.
- `/hive approve` on a label-driven repo no longer replies that the hive removed `stage/045-needs-decision` when a kept `needs-human` (added by a person or a lifecycle bot) re-parks the issue there; the reply now says the stage stays until that label is removed.
- Refresh an issue's cached tracker snapshot after an accepted maintainer decision so its Actionable ribbon no longer retains stale needs-human badges and decision questions while waiting for a GitHub webhook.
- Show temporary upgrade holds as Delayed instead of missed windows, and clear resolved delay warnings after a successful upgrade on both dashboards, including older history entries.
- Accept verified merged PRs from a repo's enabled `upstream_watch` upstream for reporter-trust, without trusting upstream authors globally; cross-repo associations and acceptance labels no longer grant local reporter trust ([#13348](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13348)).
- Dashboard chat's bang-command defer guard now uses a byte comparison so the v6 chat conformance scan passes on the v6 base branch (#9136)
- Fix v6 dashboard forward-merge debris in OpenAPI coverage, diagnostics health rendering, run-plan import, and version provenance UI.
- Fixed the v6 build after the v5 forward-merge: restored `HubConfig.TaskStatusPush` and `StatsDisplayEntry.Icon` in the split config files and gave the planengine adapter a default engine name.
- Restore OMP splash detection after the pane-signal extraction: recognize both Unicode and plain Enter footers without requiring a welcome banner, while keeping matching scoped to the OMP backend.
- Apply writeback containment to incoming v6 automatic issue, pull-request, merge-lane, and work-source updates while preserving explicitly requested approvals, replies, and dashboard actions.
- `hive validate` now lists base-config `launch_cmd` entries dropped for contradicting their backend and exits non-zero instead of printing "config OK" (#15769)
- Fix the label relay for `hive/verified-open`: it now creates the label on repositories that lack it before adding it, the refusal for a request that also removes `hive/likely-done` or `hive/covered-by-pr` tells the agent to resend the add on its own, and the verify-once kick text says to add only `hive/verified-open` and report after the relay result is ok (#11679).
- `hive/verified-open` and `hive/already-done` no longer stand together. projectbluefin/testsuite#1023 got already-done, then verified-open two hours later, and the inbox offered it as "verified done but could not close". The label relay's verified-open now removes the done labels, a verified already-done removes verified-open, and the issue stage sweep settles issues already wearing both from their label events (the later verdict stands).
- `/api/version` now reports the Go version the hive was actually built with in its `go` field, instead of a fixed `1.25` that no longer matched the build.
- Activity Monitor CI chevron counts (`CI 7/11`) are now driven by `check_run`/`workflow_job`/`status` webhook deliveries applied straight into a per-head check set — no PR re-read per check fan-out — with one coalesced check-run listing only when the head has none yet, so rows no longer sit at `CI ?/?` after a push or for sidelined PRs until the next eval cycle; `/api/status.webhooks` gains `last_ci_event_at`, `ci_events_1h`, `ci_events_applied_1h`, `ci_refetches_1h` and the hub relays `workflow_run`/`workflow_job` (hivecommons/hive#16521)
- review: a not-hive-authored head whose fix is withheld is now reported in `FixExclusions` only on the cycle that first withholds it, matching `auditWithheldReviewFixes`' doc instead of repeating every eval cycle (#14882, #14883).
- A lane that cannot push `.github/workflows/**` now hands a workflow-only change to the lane that can, instead of parking it for the owner. ISSUES_AND_PRS lanes (ci-maintainer, quality and the rest) get a contributor-tier token with no Workflows permission, and the workflow ceiling told them to park such a fix with `--needs-decision`. So on Danathar/exult#374 the owner approved a direction, ci-maintainer was kicked again and re-parked it as an owner step ("Why there is no PR: ... no workflows permission"). Danathar/arch-bootc#634 and Danathar/zfs-aurora-complex#266 were filed the same way, while scanner (ISSUES_PRS_MERGE) was merging workflow fixes in the same hive. Now, when an enabled ISSUES_PRS_MERGE lane serves the repository (one scoped to other repositories is never chosen, since it would be refused there) and the park's text says the change is a workflow file the lane cannot push (and offers no lettered options), the relay does not park it. It adds `hive/workflows-lane` and a "Handed to `<lane>`" note, and the scheduler routes the issue to that lane. With no such lane, or when that lane itself could not push, the owner gets the park as before.
- The contributor lane now binds an unmarked owner approval (a typed `/hive decision approve`, or a dashboard `/approve` posted without a head marker) to the time GitHub first showed the PR's current head, never to the head commit's committer date. That date is written by the pusher's git, so a later push carrying a backdated commit could inherit an approval given on the head before it and release the workflow-path fence for a diff the approver never saw. An approval older than the observed head now leaves the fence armed, exactly like an APPROVED review on a stale commit; the approver re-approves the new head to release it. This is deliberately fail-closed and slightly narrower than before: the observed time is pinned on the hive's first sweep of the head, and any comment or label that lands between the push and that sweep moves it later, so an approval typed in that gap is also treated as stale and has to be typed again. A head with no pinned time yet binds nothing.
- Automerge: GitHub's 403 "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow … without `workflows` permission" on a branch update is now recognised as `workflow-permission` by the sweep, the trusted-human merge-forward and the hold guard. The PR parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` for a person, merge-forward no longer reports it as a conflict (070/071), and the hold guard stops retrying it until the head moves.
- Offer a workflows-capable lane for parked workflow changes instead of incorrectly asking operators to grant an existing App permission.
- An agent's "the App cannot push `.github/workflows/`" is checked before it parks anything. On projectbluefin/testsuite#1059 and #1073, scanner (ISSUES_PRS_MERGE, whose token asks for the Workflows permission) parked a workflow fix the same day the App pushed `e2e.yml` in #1089, and the issues showed "Blocked · App lacks workflows permission" for four days. Now the relay refuses that park when the parking lane's tier pushes workflows and the App installation grants `workflows: write` (read at most every five minutes), and hands a contributor-tier park to the workflows lane only when the installation is not known to lack the permission. The blocker ledger records a workflows blocker only when no lane can push workflow files on that repository or the item is a fork PR (a fork branch takes no workflow push from the App), and a re-check that runs with the un-park sweep releases existing ones and routes them to the workflows lane. Merger- and trusted-tier kicks now say their token can push `.github/workflows/**`. A park that quotes GitHub's own rejection of the push still stands, and that evidence is kept across later unquoted re-reports; a contributor-tier lane's quote is not treated as evidence about the App.
- Preserve durable write counter totals and retry pending counts after transient file read errors ([#14531](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14531)).
- Write-back containment: every unsolicited GitHub comment, label and review from platform sweeps (sentinel, hold-gate notices, stage labels, supersession, duplicate-fix, reporter-trust) now passes one central per-kind gate (`writeback.*`) that requires both an ACMM floor and the review opt-in label on foreign PRs, never back-fills onto PRs that predate hive's write access, and surfaces suppressed writes in the dashboard instead of on GitHub
- Restore the writeback direct-write ratchet on `v5`: the lapsed claimed-by label removal added in #16849 is annotated as gated, so `TestDirectWriteRatchet` passes again for every PR based on `v5`
- Fix the dashboard "Your turn" inbox telling the operator to `rebase` a PR GitHub reports as `blocked` (waiting on a required review or status) or `draft`: only `dirty` and `behind` now name `rebase`, and a blocked PR names `approve` (or `rerun` when CI is red) (#14175).
- Fix the "Your turn" inbox showing a superseded PR that still touches files the merged PR did not as `CLOSE`: the supersession sweep now records `reason=subset|extra-files` (and the extra files) in its audit detail, and such PRs show as `REVIEW` (`superseded_extra_files_review`) naming the extra files with keep open recommended (#14176).

### Security

- **The owner-step marker in an issue body now counts only when the hive authored the issue.** Previously anyone able to edit a hive-parked issue's body could add `<!-- hive:owner-step -->` (or a typed release step) and change what the "What to reply" notice offers; comments were already gated on hive authorship. Issues filed through `hive-open-issue` are unaffected. ([#12643](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12643))
- Stage-074 adoption now applies the contributor lane's diff fences before taking over a contributor PR: a PR that touches CI workflow/action definitions, deletes or guts tests, or whose file list cannot be read is no longer adopted in place or superseded by an App PR (including the `dco-rehome` takeover); it stays at stage 072 with a logged `contributor-lane:*` reason ([#12850](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12850)).
- `hivectl hives web` now rejects requests whose `Host` is not a loopback host on the listening port (DNS-rebinding protection) and cross-origin browser requests (`Origin` / `Sec-Fetch-Site`), sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response, and the page removes the launch token from the URL and browser history once loaded. Token auth is unchanged. ([#13178](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13178), part of [#13153](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13153))
- The local `hivectl hives web` API now accepts its access token only through the `X-Hive-Commons-Token` header, preventing API credentials from leaking through query strings ([#13245](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13245)).
- Image builds compile with Go 1.27.3: the `golang:1.27-alpine` builder digest in `src/Dockerfile`, `src/Dockerfile.hub`, `src/Dockerfile.contributor` and the base-registry probe now resolves to `1.27.3-alpine` instead of `1.27.2-alpine`, and the contributor image's standalone toolchain moves from Go 1.24.4 to 1.27.3, so the shipped `hive`, `hivectl`, `bd` and hub binaries carry the `crypto/x509` fix for GO-2026-6809 ([#13329](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13329)).
- Dashboard review-evidence downloads, listings, aggregates, tracker annotations, heartbeats, and evidence-derived metrics now verify bundle signatures against the configured Ed25519 key before using on-disk data; unsigned mode still verifies content hashes, while an unavailable configured key or tampered bundle fails closed ([#13900](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13900)).
- Keep the hive PR open and parked when a clean competing contributor PR references the same issue; delegated decisions now recommend a human adequacy comparison instead of automatically closing the hive's work ([#13998](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13998)).
- Refuse to publish contributor workflow/action edits into upstream adoption branches, and revalidate head evidence before every supersession. The refusal is recorded once per head: the PR gets one note and moves to needs-decision instead of being re-checked every sweep.
- Semantic classifier daily-quota exhaustion now writes an `ioscan_classifier_daily_quota_exhausted` audit event once per UTC day (text still passes on unclassified, as before).
- The proxy's plain-HTTP forward path now identifies its caller and refuses destinations that are not globally routable — loopback, link-local (cloud instance metadata), RFC 1918, CGNAT and multicast — checked at dial time so a hostname resolving inward is refused too; set `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD=true` to allow them (#14082)
- The proxy write-gate rule table mirrors GitHub posture for GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo: direct MR/PR creation and merge are hard-denied for every agent level (forcing the hive-open-pr and hive-merge request-file paths as the bot identity), reads and issues/comments/labels follow the ACMM ladder, and unknown routes fail closed ([#14114](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14114), part of [#14096](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14096)).
- "Let hive decide" (`POST …/items/{number}/decide-delegated`) no longer reads a pull request head as CI-green from `mergeable_state` alone. GitHub reports `blocked` both for a missing required review and for red required checks, and `unknown`/`behind` say nothing about the head, so the delegate could approve a PR whose required checks were failing or had never run and record it as a "green head" decision. The gatherer now settles those states from the head's combined status and check runs — no red, nothing pending, at least one green — the same way it already judged a competing PR, and such heads get the `fix-then-merge` direction instead of an approval ([#14167](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14167)).
- Limit GitHub claim-effect processing to one worker per active issue so claim/release churn no longer accumulates waiting goroutines; queued effects still run in order without dropping release cleanup.
- The hive capability endpoint (`callback.Listen`, bound from `$CRUX_HIVE_LISTEN`) now refuses a TCP address off loopback, the same fail-closed rule `crux serve --listen` has applied since #13967. The listener is plain http gated by `$CRUX_HIVE_TOKEN`, and it serves `POST /v1/tokens`, which mints GitHub App installation tokens — a routable bind would have carried both the bearer token and every minted token across the network in cleartext. The k8s sidecar-container option is unaffected: the containers share the pod's network namespace, so `127.0.0.1` reaches the sidecar. Remote access goes through a TLS-terminating proxy. (#14348)
- The inference translator on `127.0.0.1:18444` now names its caller from the socket owner's UID, the way the GitHub proxy path and the decision endpoint already do, instead of from the `x-api-key` header the caller chose. That header is `sk-hive-<agent name>` and the name is public inside the pod, so any local process could previously borrow a different agent's inference route — backend, model, upstream credential and usage attribution. A mapped agent UID is authoritative (a header naming someone else is logged and overridden), the hive's own control plane keeps the header name, and an unidentifiable caller is refused with 401 unless `HIVE_PROXY_ADVISORY_OK=true`. The translator server also gained a `ReadHeaderTimeout` ([#14439](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14439)).
- Refuse proxy-owned inference translator requests unless advisory identity is explicitly enabled, preventing forged agent identities through private plain-HTTP forwarding when `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD=true` (#14448).
- Stop draft, deprecated and superseded knowledge facts from reaching contributor agents: `GET /api/knowledge/export` (the startup knowledge contributor agents download) now carries approved facts only for every caller, the task MCP knowledge served to agents is approved-only, and the agent-reachable reads (`/api/knowledge` list, search, `/{layer}`, `/{layer}/{slug}`, vault facts, TOC and entry) return approved facts unless a verified owner asks for other states with `include_states`; for any other caller `include_states` is ignored. The dashboard's Knowledge browser asks for every state, so owners still see drafts to approve (#14546).
- The Hub's GitHub browser-login contract tests now cover PKCE end to end ([#14598](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14598)). The tests check that the authorize redirect carries the S256 challenge of the `hive_oauth_pkce` cookie and that the token exchange sends that exact `code_verifier` in the form body. A missing, expired, malformed or truncated verifier must fail with `400` before the code is redeemed. A verifier GitHub rejects must not create a session or user record. The verifier must never appear in a request URL or the logs. `src/docs/hub-login-token.md` now documents the PKCE step and the fail-closed behavior. Login behavior is unchanged.
- The Hub's GitHub browser login now binds the PKCE verifier to the login transaction and rejects a missing or substituted verifier locally, before the authorization code is ever sent to GitHub ([#14598](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14598)).
- The Hub's GitHub browser login now uses PKCE (S256) as defence-in-depth, binding the authorization code to the browser that started the login: the authorize redirect carries a `code_challenge`, the matching `code_verifier` lives in a short-lived single-use HttpOnly cookie and is sent in the token-exchange form body. A callback with a missing or malformed verifier is rejected with 400 before any code exchange or session is minted; logins started before the upgrade must be restarted (#14633).
- Keep raw IOScan classifier errors, including private endpoint URLs and DNS details, in local logs rather than public selfreport diagnostics.
- Prevent comment-only PR cross-references from moving issues to Reviewing or Closed in the dashboard; timeline PR links now require a closing keyword in the PR title or body ([#14985](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14985)).
- A rebase-then-merge follow-through no longer treats an unsigned head as the hive's own just because its author email is the App bot's noreply address: an author GitHub resolves to the App bot now counts only on a commit GitHub reports as verified, as GitHub's update-branch commits are ([#15421](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15421)).
- The hold guard no longer treats an approval carried from an adopted PR as proof that a trusted merger reviewed the copy's current head ([#15698](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15698)).
- Agent NO_PROXY only appends the OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL host when it is a concrete hostname or IP, so a wildcard or leading-dot host can no longer widen the proxy bypass (#15726)
- Fix tool approval's built-in destructive-command detection for root/home removal and fork bombs without relying on host text-scanner findings, and avoid matching removal of ordinary subpaths ([#15727](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15727)).
- Redact credentials from logged errors, Stringer, TextAppender and TextMarshaler values (including marshal errors), and resolved LogValuer attributes, including nested groups and bound logger attributes ([#15729](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15729)). Text-rendered attributes are now emitted as strings, including in JSON logs where a value implementing `json.Marshaler` may previously have emitted a number or object.
- The built-in destructive-command check now also matches equivalent root and home removal spellings such as `rm -rf //`, `rm -rf /.`, `rm -rf "/"`, `rm -r -f /` and `rm -rf ${HOME}`, instead of relying solely on the host text scanner ([#15740](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15740)).
- The built-in destructive-`rm` check in `crux/toolapprove` now reads a command the way bash would hand it to `rm`, without running anything, and judges what each target means rather than how it is spelled ([#16094](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16094)). Quoting and escapes, `$'…'` strings, brace expansion (`/{,}`, `{rm,-rf,/}`), `.`/`..` components (`/tmp/..`, `$PWD/../../..`), `$IFS` splitting, subshells, command substitutions and re-quoted commands (`bash -c '…'`, `eval`) now resolve to the same verdict as plain `rm -rf /`. A recursive `rm` of the root, the home directory, the working directory or any ancestor of one is flagged. That set now includes `rm -rf .`, `./*`, `..` and `"$PWD"`, matching the existing treatment of `rm -rf *`. A new spelling-equivalence test derives about 70,000 bash-equivalent commands from destructive and safe seeds and gates every detector change on them. The analysis has explicit limits: 1024 brace words per word, nesting 32 brace groups and 8 re-read levels deep, and a work budget proportional to the command. A command past them is reported as a separate `shell command exceeds destructive-command analysis bounds` violation instead of passing clean. The `rm` branch of the old regex is retired, so its false positives no longer fire: non-recursive `rm -f /`, literal `'$HOME'` and `"~"`, and `a=rm -rf /`. An `rm` that is the subcommand of a version-control tool (`git rm -r --cached .`, `hg rm`, `svn rm`) is not the binary and is not flagged.
- The contributor lane's workflow-path approval no longer accepts an edited comment as an approval: a `/hive decision approve` (or dashboard `/approve`) whose comment was modified after it was posted is ignored, the same rule the un-park sweep already applies, so rewriting a merger's earlier comment cannot be read as that merger's approval (#16127).
- The push broker's trailing-newline normaliser now resolves each changed file's parent directory and skips any path that escapes the workspace through a symlinked directory, as it already did for a committed symlink at the leaf. Since the normaliser began committing HEAD's blob rather than the working-tree bytes, an agent that committed `dir/file` and then swapped `dir/` for a symlink out of the sandbox workspace could have had that blob written briefly into a hive-owned file by the host-side broker before the restore put it back ([#16211](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16211)).
- Require human policy sign-off for reviewer questions on workflow and action edits, including same-repository PRs.
- Email escalations now pass every operator-visible field through the shared secret/canary scrubber at the surface boundary, instead of relying on each caller to remember to scrub first ([#8047](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8047)). A GitHub token, JWT, AWS key, private key, or `ioscan` canary that reached an escalation body used to be mailed out intact for any caller that dispatched unscrubbed text — the three call sites in `cmd/hive` scrubbed, and nothing made that a property of the surface. The digest path made the window longer still: `info` and `decision` events sat unscrubbed in the digest buffer until the configured send time, up to a day later. Scrubbing now happens on the way into `Deliver` (so the buffer holds scrubbed text) and again where every immediate and digest mail is composed. The `From`/`To` addressing and the provenance footer are untouched: they are operator configuration, not event text. A v6 guard-invariant conformance suite (`src/pkg/escalate/conformance_v6_email_test.go`) pins this across the whole SMTP session — envelope, headers, and body — and fails if the email surface grows the pieces of an inbound reply-to-act path (a mail-reading dependency, a poller or reply entry point, inbound `EmailConfig` fields, or a locally-invented sender allowlist) without the `ioscan`, `Converse`, role-floor, and mode-ladder guards that path requires.
- Push and on-call escalations (ntfy, Pushover, PagerDuty) now pass every operator-visible field through the shared secret/canary scrubber at the surface boundary, instead of relying on each caller to remember to scrub first ([#8048](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8048)). A GitHub token, JWT, AWS key, private key, or `ioscan` canary that reached an escalation body used to leave the trust boundary intact — into a third party's push pipeline and onto an on-call phone screen — for any caller that dispatched unscrubbed text; the three call sites in `cmd/hive` scrubbed, and nothing made that a property of the surface. Sink credentials are untouched: they are the authorization to deliver, not event text. A v6 guard-invariant conformance suite (`src/pkg/escalate/conformance_v6_test.go`) pins this for all three providers and fails if the push/on-call surface grows an inbound action path or a state-reaching dependency that would need the `ioscan`, `Converse`, role-floor, and mode-ladder guards it currently has no way to reach.
- Pass `github.ref_name`, the gate SHA and the run number to `docker.yml` publish steps through step `env:` and quote them in the shell, and compare `github.ref` instead of `github.ref_name` in `dco-post-merge.yml` guards, closing OpenSSF Baseline OSPS-BR-01.02 reported by LFX Insights (#8208).
- Hub-launched agents now receive a per-launch lease-scoped token in their task MCP URL instead of the dashboard auth token; the token is bound to the launch scope and stops working when the launch ends (#8348)
- Enforce ioscan input scanning on dashboard kick prompts, redacting or refusing unsafe prompts before they reach agents (#8698).
- Fixed a chat command allowlist bypass where any authenticated dashboard role — regardless of the specific chat author — could issue `!` commands even when `allowed_users` was explicitly configured, restoring per-author enforcement of the allowlist.
- Harden Activity Monitor source-work verification with credential-free, bounded, read-only Git inspection that cannot execute workspace hooks, filters or helpers; unsupported normalization and unstable repository evidence stay unknown.
- Admin MCP: a name of `.` or `..` can no longer steer a request to a different endpoint. Agent, run, repository, contributor and plan names go into the request path, and `.` and `..` survive URL escaping. The hive's router answers such a path with a redirect to the cleaned path, which is another route: `/api/kick/../status` is `/api/status`, and `/api/model/../<name>` is `/api/<name>`. The stdio binary (`hive-admin-mcp`) followed that redirect with the same method, body and token, so with writes enabled a registered operation such as `agent.model` could be previewed and confirmed into a `POST` the admin MCP does not offer, including ones its exclusion catalogue refuses, and a read tool could return another endpoint's data under the wrong name. Over the HTTP endpoint the redirect was not followed and the caller only saw "HTTP 307". Both transports now refuse a request path with an empty, `.` or `..` element before anything is sent, for every read and write, and `write_confirm` refuses a stored confirmation that carries one. Re-extract or rebuild `hive-admin-mcp` to get the fix on stdio.
- Base-preparation state files and directory are no longer created group-writable (0o644/0o755, matching the stage store). (#15844)
- A recorded decision, and the base-preparation proof, now follow a PR onto a new head only when the merge commit is one GitHub created and verified (signed, committed by `web-flow` or the App) rather than any commit whose author email resolves to the App bot, and a base...head compare that reaches GitHub's 300-file listing cap fails closed instead of being compared on a truncated file list ([#16860](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16860)).
- Contributor registration tokens expire after 90 days by default, support an optional inactivity cutoff, and can be inspected or revoked individually or in bulk from Management and `hivectl contribute tokens`; GitHub-authenticated `hivectl contribute login` rotates expired tokens, while legacy credentials receive persisted migration-time issuance dates (#13804).
- The pinned-checkout service's repository allowlist now matches on URL segment boundaries and refuses non-canonical repository paths. Previously `CRUX_CHECKOUT_ALLOWLIST` was compared as a plain string prefix against the URL the caller sent, so `https://host/allowed/../other/repo` (which git resolves to `other/repo`), `file:///allowed/../../elsewhere`, and `https://host/allowed-evil/repo` all passed for an entry of `https://host/allowed`. Requests whose path contains `.`, `..`, empty or percent-encoded segments are now rejected as bad requests before any clone, and a prefix that does not end in `/` must be followed by `/`, `.git` or the end of the URL.
- Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0 in src/crux to clear GO-2026-6617/6612/6611/6603 (govulncheck red on hivecommons/crux main).
- Dashboard directions for contributor PRs now require the sweep's classification label, honoring `governor.labels.author` names, instead of falling back directly to PR-body markers; the sweep's body-marker classification remains unchanged ([#15268](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15268)).
- Deleting a registry-only hive now requires being its owner or a hub admin; entries whose spoke never reported an owner are admin-only (#16134)
- Discord notifications and RFC notices no longer ping @everyone or roles from untrusted text such as issue titles
- Bumped the Go toolchain to 1.26.10 so the `govulncheck` gate stops flagging GO-2026-6809 (`crypto/x509` certificate verification), reachable from the dashboard's HTTP server. The gate was red on the default branch itself, blocking every open PR.
- Bumped the Go toolchain to 1.26.9 and `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 so the `govulncheck` gate stops flagging GO-2026-6599 through GO-2026-6611 (HTTP/2 framer, `crypto/tls`, `net/http`, `mime/multipart`, `html/template`). The vulnerable versions were reachable from the dashboard's HTTP server and the GitHub client, and the gate was red on the default branch itself, blocking every open PR.
- Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0 to clear GO-2026-6860 (govulncheck).
- The hold guard only advances a held PR's reviewed baseline after a merge-from-base when the new head is a two-parent merge of a base-branch commit into the head the hive asked to update, so a contributor push racing the update is no longer adopted as reviewed hygiene; the base parent is matched against the live base branch, so a base that moved before the update does not turn the hive's own merge into drift ([#14534](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14534)).
- Delegated issue decisions record reporter-authored option text only by option label: when the options come from the body of an issue a non-hive account filed, the owner-attributed `/hive decision go with option N` no longer quotes the reporter's summary, while the "Let hive decide" preview still shows that summary as a quoted excerpt of the issue's words; options from hive-authored text keep their summary (#16937).
- Jam REST writes and WebSocket presence/edits now use the authenticated user instead of caller-supplied agent/model attribution, preventing forged authorship and unlimited poll votes through changing agent names; server-generated agent replies retain their attribution (Refs #10056).
- **An owner's approval of a workflow-file change no longer merges a head that also deletes tests.** The contributor lane's diff check names only its first fence, and the owner-approval release ([#14664](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14664)) lifts the workflow-path fence alone, so a PR that edited `.github/workflows/**` and removed tests merged on that approval with the test removal never checked. Such a head now stops at `contributor-lane:tests-removed`, which no approval overrides, before any release is read.
- `log_read` (admin MCP) and `GET /api/logs/read`: one of the hive's own secret values is now redacted when it holds a quote, a backslash or a control character. The hive log, the request log and the output sources are stored as JSON, so such a value is on disk only in its JSON-escaped form (`pa\"ss\\word`). The read-time redaction looked for the plain, URL-encoded and base64 forms only, so it missed it and the value came back readable in the returned line. The JSON-escaped form, with and without HTML escaping, is now redacted as well. Values made only of letters, digits and ordinary punctuation were always redacted.
- Scrub `[]byte`, `[]string`, map, struct and other composite log attributes (and `TextMarshaler` values) so credential-shaped tokens no longer bypass the log scrubber ([#15735](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15735), [#15736](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15736)).
- A hive authenticated with a personal access token and no configured identity now learns its own login from `GET /user`, so a once-only marker (unpark reply, label-approval, sentinel) pasted by another commenter is no longer trusted; hives that cannot reach `/user` keep the previous behavior ([#13520](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13520)).
- **Security:** contributor adoption no longer moves a fork pull request's commits into a `hive/adopt-<n>` branch of the base repository (supersede, DCO re-home, or in-place-stalled re-home). The re-homed PR was a same-repository PR, so the fork's unreviewed code ran with the repository's trusted CI and skipped its fork-only guards; one such run published and signed a canary image. A fork PR the hive cannot finish on the fork's own branch now parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` (`adoption-stalled:fork-rehome-refused`) with a maintainer ask. PRs from branches of the base repository are re-homed as before.
- Bumped transitive `body-parser` to 2.4.0 and `qs` to 6.17.1 in `src/proxy/package-lock.json` (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw), matching what `dashboard/` already pins, and `undici` to 6.29.1 in `discord/package-lock.json` (GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx TLS option drop and four DoS advisories). `/discord` now has its own Dependabot npm entry so the directory gets the same weekly coverage as `/src/proxy` and `/dashboard`.
- The `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception now verifies the commits behind the head, not only the PR author login: every commit must be authored by a `trusted_authors` login, committed by GitHub itself (`web-flow`) or a `trusted_authors` login, and carry a GitHub-verified signature (which binds to the committer, not the author), and the list must end at the current head. Before, anyone with write access could push a pin-shaped commit onto a trusted author's branch (a `dependabot/...` branch keeps `dependabot[bot]` as PR author) and have the sweep or `/approve` waive the human-merge-path hold on it. Unsigned or foreign commits, an unreadable or empty commit list, or a list that does not end at the head now hold the PR as before; the commit list is read only once the diff already qualifies, so refused PRs cost no extra API call.
- The opt-in `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception now admits an `action-sha` pin only when the new SHA is anchored in its upstream action repository: with a `# vX[.Y[.Z]]` comment the upstream `tags/vX…` ref (annotated tags dereferenced) must point at exactly that SHA, otherwise the SHA must be an ancestor of the upstream default branch ([#16399](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16399)). GitHub resolves a `uses:` SHA across the whole fork network, so a pin-shaped line could otherwise point at a commit pushed to any fork. Any 404, mismatch, rate limit or API error keeps the human-merge-path hold; repos without the key are unaffected. The pin-only commit check now uses the shared PR commit lister ([#16401](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16401)).
- Pushbroker now checks both source and destination paths of renamed files, preventing protected workflows, policies, and other guarded files from being moved out of protected paths to bypass the push gate ([#15728](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15728)).
- RFC lifecycle notices no longer post RFCs from private repositories (titles and links) to `notifications.discord.rfc_channel_id` unless `notifications.discord.rfc_include_private: true` authorizes it. The gate applies in every mode, line mode included. Repo visibility is resolved once per repo and cached for an hour. A repo whose visibility cannot be resolved, or that is `internal`, counts as private (fail closed). Withheld RFCs still advance the detector state, so they never replay later (#15926, part of #15869).
- The sentinel no longer releases an alert on a dashboard-approval comment, nor writes its clearance record into an existing marker comment, unless one of the hive's own known accounts wrote it: a hive that cannot name its own accounts no longer falls back to trusting any author there, so a PR author cannot forge the release for their own head ([#15262](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15262)). Skipping the dashboard `/lgtm` + `/approve` commands after a Prow rejection now believes only the Prow bot (`kubestellar-prow[bot]`), not any installed bot quoting the rejection phrase ([#15263](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15263)).
- Spektacular hub executor hardening: the hub-launched agent CLI no longer inherits the hive process's inheritable/ambient capabilities (it is started through `setpriv`, and the stage is refused when that is not possible) ([#10054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10054)); it now receives the proxy CA paths `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`/`GIT_SSL_CAINFO` so proxied Copilot/Claude TLS works ([#10076](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10076)); clone credential files left behind by a hub that died during clone/fetch are removed by the executor sweep after an hour ([#10109](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10109)); and the prompt/log writes and stage transcript capture no longer follow symlinks in the worktree, with captured documents scrubbed like CLI output ([#10078](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10078)).
- Spektacular hub executor: when the hub-launched agent CLI runs as its own executor UID, it now gets the same egress proxy environment as regular agents — `HTTP(S)_PROXY` pointing at the local proxy (replacing any value forwarded from the hive process), `HIVE_PROXY_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and the proxy CA in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`/`GIT_SSL_CAINFO` — so traffic the `:443` redirect does not catch is still routed through, and attributed by, the per-agent proxy ([#10054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10054)).
- Spektacular hub executor: with per-agent UID isolation active, the hub-launched agent CLI now runs as its own `hive-<identity>` UID through `su-exec` instead of the hive uid, so it cannot read the GitHub App key or clone credentials and its HTTPS egress goes through the proxy redirect; the entrypoint provisions that UID when Spektacular is enabled, and the stage is refused when it is missing ([#10054](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/10054)).
- The Activity Monitor streamer's loopback `authproxy` (`src/deploy/stream`) now forwards only `GET`/`HEAD` to the dashboard and answers every other method `405` locally, before the bearer is attached. The token it injects is the spoke's shared dashboard token, which the dashboard treats as an unscoped owner; the kiosk only ever reads, so a compromised or misbehaving page in the `--no-sandbox` Chromium can no longer reach agent-control, config or settings mutations with that authority.
- With `task_mcp.remote_enabled` on, a hive that set neither `dashboard.public_url` nor `hub.dashboard_url` named the hub as its own task MCP: `task_assign` carried `mcp.url = <hub.url>/api/contribute/mcp` (`https://hive.hivecommons.dev`, the default on every hive) together with this hive's lease bearer, the relay wrote both into the contributor's `.mcp.json`, and the contributor's agent presented the bearer to the hub. A hive whose hub link is off but that still held a `hub.dashboard_url` handed that stale address out the same way. `mcp.url` is now only ever this hive's own address: `dashboard.public_url`, or `hub.dashboard_url` while `hub.enabled` is true. `hub.url` is never used. A hive with no such address sends no `mcp` block and mints no bearer, so its contributors work without the task MCP until the operator sets `dashboard.public_url`.
- Fixed the tool-approval guardrail-path check never seeing the target of a Copilot CLI `apply_patch` call ([#16979](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16979)). The tool carries its paths in the patch text (`*** Update File:`, `*** Add File:`, `*** Delete File:`, `*** Move to:`) instead of a path argument, so `ToolRequest.GetFilePath` returned an empty string and a patch touching `.github/workflows/**`, `OWNERS`, `hive.yaml` or `policies/**` auto-approved at L5/L6. `GetFilePath` now falls back to the first path in the patch body, and the guardrail check now iterates the new `GetFilePaths` over every path the request names, so a patch that lists a harmless file first and a guardrail path later is still caught.
## 2026-11-08 (v5.189.1)

### Changed

- docs(dashboard): review fallback doc comment describes the reviewer-lane branch (#17125)

### Fixed

- pr-request watcher: a closing reference to an issue that does not exist in the target repository (404) now rejects the request as a permanent claim error instead of retrying with backoff forever (#17124).

## 2026-11-07 (v5.190.0)

### Added

- `agents.cli_memory.drain_to_knowledge` (default off) converts each agent's CLI memory (Claude `MEMORY.md` + topic files, Codex `memories*`, Gemini `GEMINI.md`) into `state: draft` knowledge entries in the bead-synth vault before every kick and before `clear_on_kick` wipes the store — tagged `cli-memory`, `agent:<name>`, `cli:<name>`, `repo:` when derivable, deduplicated by content hash, never auto-approved; one `cli-memory: drained N facts …` log line per drain. Proposed by @gregoryhunt (#17033).
- `v6` is now an official release line: `.github/release-lines.yml` lists `[v4, v5, v6]`, so `tagged-release.yml` mints `v6.x.y` tags (starting at `v6.0.0`), GitHub Releases, SBOMs and immutable image retags from the `v6` branch exactly as `v5` does; the default-branch copy of the workflow relays a completed `v6` build to `v6`'s own copy, since GitHub only delivers `workflow_run` to the default branch. Channel ownership is unchanged — `stable`/`candidate`/`:latest` follow `v5`, `edge`/`v6-latest` follow `v6`.

### Changed

- Contributor nudges are now one comment per PR and reason class, edited in place for a new head or changed reason, with a single re-nudge after `auto_merge.nudge_repeat_after` (default 72h); an agent's free-text relay comments fold into the `hive:status` card in quiet mode or one `hive:origin-notes` comment per item otherwise; a marker ratchet test caps unmarked bot comment emitters (hivecommons/hive#17067).

### Fixed

- The "Review · waiting for CI" detail no longer says a reviewer will be requested when the repo has no hive reviewer lane; it now says a person must review (hivecommons/hive#17095).
- fix(crux): move buffer/output getters out of agent/manager.go to stay under the file-size ratchet (#17122)
- The bob startup preflight now checks that the per-agent `~/.bob` (where bob writes its installation ID and chat recordings since per-agent homes landed) is writable, instead of probing the shared `/data/home/.bob` that only holds the bridged settings, so an unwritable state directory is reported against the directory bob actually uses (#17062).
- Dashboard: on a phone (≤480px) merged banners and toasts span the viewport width with a two-line title, a mono lane/merger/time line, one links row, tap-anywhere dismiss and a "+N more" pill after the newest three; the Overview KPI label/subline no longer jump to a larger font under 720px (the #16613 override assumed `--fs-2xs` was undefined at `:root`).
- The native-queue workflow contract test asserted `native-queue-policy.yml`'s release-lines pin as the literal `[v6, -v4]`; with v6 a `release_lines` entry the pin reads `[-v4]`, so the test now resolves the pin against `release_lines` and checks that v5 and v6 are covered.

### Security

- The shared Claude Code user settings file (`/data/home/.claude/settings.json`, which every interactive claude agent reads through its per-agent `~/.claude/settings.json` bridge) is now hive-owned and kept read-only to agent UIDs. Before each claude launch the manager checks that the file is a regular file owned by the hive; a symlink or a file owned by another uid is moved aside to `settings.json.rejected` and the file is re-seeded, and group/other write is removed from a hive-owned copy. The entrypoint sweeps and the permissions watcher no longer widen this file to group write. Settings keys such as `hooks` and `apiKeyHelper` run commands in every agent's session, so one agent can no longer change them for the rest of the fleet; operators who keep extra keys there (for example `enabledPlugins`) and find the file moved aside after upgrading can re-apply them from the rejected copy as the hive user (#17059).
- The pinned-checkout service's repository allowlist now matches on URL segment boundaries and refuses non-canonical repository paths. Previously `CRUX_CHECKOUT_ALLOWLIST` was compared as a plain string prefix against the URL the caller sent, so `https://host/allowed/../other/repo` (which git resolves to `other/repo`), `file:///allowed/../../elsewhere`, and `https://host/allowed-evil/repo` all passed for an entry of `https://host/allowed`. Requests whose path contains `.`, `..`, empty or percent-encoded segments are now rejected as bad requests before any clone, and a prefix that does not end in `/` must be followed by `/`, `.git` or the end of the URL.

## 2026-11-07 (v5.189.0)

### Added

- An agent whose `knowledge.agent_scopes.<agent>.include_states` lists `draft` is now primed with the draft knowledge entries it authored (`author:`/`owner:` frontmatter matching the agent, its base agent or a hive owner login), each marked `(draft)` in the kick; every other kick stays approved-only ([#17076](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17076)).

### Fixed

- `docs/crux-serve.md` and `docs/env-vars.md` now document `crux serve --runs-config` / `CRUX_RUNS_CONFIG` and the `/v1/runs` routes, and the work-services design doc reflects that S2 and S7 shipped (#17027, #17028).
- A claim's GitHub side effect (label, stage or ledger write) that kept timing out after its bounded retries logged `issue-claims: GitHub side effect failed` with no matching class, so the hive filed it as `unclassified_error_repeated`. It now lands under its own `issue_claim_effect_failed` class, with the underlying error still in the log line (hivecommons/hive#17069).

## 2026-11-07 (v5.188.0)

### Added

- New `agents.cli_memory` block (per-agent `cli_memory:` override): `auto_memory` (default false) pins Claude Code / Codex / Copilot CLI auto-memory off via `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`, `[features] memories = false` and `"memory": false`; `clear_on_kick` wipes that agent's `~/.claude/projects/*/memory`, `$CODEX_HOME/memories*` and `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` before each non-resume kick (hivecommons/hive#17032).
- Mid-task knowledge advisor (opt-in `knowledge.advisor`, default off): when a running agent's work enters a scope that was not on screen at kick time, the matching knowledge entries the kick did not already carry are typed into its session as one `📚 Knowledge:` line each, capped per kick (`knowledge.advisor_max_per_kick`), never during a tool call, with per-agent opt-out (`knowledge.advisor_exclude_agents`) and a `knowledge-advisor` prompt-history trigger for measurement (#17052)
- Knowledge entries can carry a `scope:` frontmatter block (`paths`, `labels`, `lanes`); the kick primer surfaces a scoped entry only when the kick's lane, issue labels or known file paths match, so repository facts are injected on demand instead of on every kick (#17045).

### Changed

- Review backlog: findings below the new `review.backlog.min_severity` (default `P2`) are no longer filed as issues but collected in one upserted `hive:review-followups` comment on the PR; the issue cap `review.backlog.max_per_pr` (default 3) now applies over the PR's lifetime instead of per day (`max_per_pr_per_day` is a retired alias); and new findings sharing a perspective are filed as one checklist item. Set `min_severity: P3` to file every finding as before (hivecommons/hive#17065).

### Fixed

- Hosted spokes now inject the primary repo's `AGENTS.md` into kicks: when neither `project.checkouts_dir` nor a matching `policies.local_dir` names a local checkout, the scheduler fetches `AGENTS.md` from the repo's default branch through the hive's GitHub client (15-minute cache, last-known-good on API failure, same injection cap) and materialises it under `/data/agentsmd-cache/<owner>/<repo>/` so the log shows `agentsmd: injecting repo instructions into kick` with that root ([#17090](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/17090)).
- Tagged Release no longer stands down when `v5` advances past the commit `docker.yml` built. The version tag now names the release commit parented on that built SHA (the retagged images' exact tree plus the changelog), the release lands on `v5` as a merge commit even when the tip has moved, and the hourly backstop releases the newest built ancestor of the tip instead of requiring the tip itself; `docker.yml` push builds also get their own concurrency slot so a merge burst no longer cancels them. Under merges faster than a multi-arch build the old "defer to the successor" rule had no terminating condition and left `v5` untagged from `v5.186.4` (2026-10-18) onward.

## 2026-11-07 (v5.187.0)

### Added

- `governor.labels.stage.engine.mode` (`off` / `shadow` / `enforce`, default `shadow`; Settings → Labels) switches the ADR-0025 central stage engine at runtime ([#13010](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13010), part of [#12999](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12999)): one reconciler is shared by the issue and PR sweeps, `off` is legacy pass-through, `shadow` counts every legacy/engine disagreement, `enforce` lets the engine write. `/api/status.stageEngine`, the activity tracker's status strip and the `hive_stage_*` series on `/metrics` report mode, derivations, mismatches and anomalies; the shadow → enforce rollout runbook is in `operator-reference.md`.
- Sidebar x/y count pills for Overview and Governor (#13148)
- `hivectl hives`, the TUI's Hives pane and the Commons web UI (`hivectl hives web`) now commit `profiles.yml` under a shared cross-process lock (`profiles.yml.lock`, mode 0600) and only if the file is still the revision they loaded. An edit made from one surface while another changed the hives is refused with nothing written — the CLI/TUI ask you to re-run, the web UI returns 409 "requires renewed review" — instead of one writer silently overwriting the other. ([#13179](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13179))
- Contributor relays now publish local scope adoption, subscription readiness, and draining task status for truthful contribution UI acknowledgements ([#13290](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13290)).
- A `blocked` issue whose body carries `<!-- hive:recheck-after <RFC3339> -->` (and no blocked-on PR) is now listed as `blocked until <t>`, the activity monitor's blocked chip shows `re-check at <t>`, and once the deadline passes the blocked sweep lifts `blocked` with one `deadline <t> passed; re-triaging` note so the scanner re-triages it; issues that also carry `<!-- hive:ops-tracking -->` stay blocked (#13310).
- `crux/api` gains a Go client (`api.NewClient`) for `crux serve`: every verb, SSE log following and the runtime event stream, over a unix socket or TCP with a bearer token (#13536).
- The `crux` CLI gains a remote mode: `--server ADDR` (or `CRUX_SERVER`) with `--token` (or `CRUX_TOKEN`) makes `run`, `ps`, `logs`, `kick` and `stop` drive a `crux serve` over the API instead of an in-process runtime; `logs -f` follows the agent's output (#13536).
- `crux serve` exposes the agent runtime over a local HTTP+JSON API (Crux Stage 3, [#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536)): a unix socket (`$CRUX_SOCKET`, default `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/crux/crux.sock`, created 0600) and optionally TCP with `--listen`, which is refused without a bearer token (`--token` / `$CRUX_TOKEN`). The routes under `/v1` mirror the CLI verbs — list, get, run from a definition, logs (pane, buffer, full, or followed as SSE), kick, stop — plus an SSE event stream of starts, stops, kicks and observed state changes. The wire contract is the stdlib-only `crux/api`; the server is `crux/serve`.
- Review heads now end in one agreed verdict ([#13542](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13542), part 2). Once every head has answered every perspective, the base reviewer gets one decision kick per PR carrying every head's full report. It checks each head finding against the code, gives it a disposition (confirmed, not reproducible or out of scope) with a reason, sets the final severity of each confirmed finding, records one decided verdict per perspective, and posts the PR's only review comment, tagging findings with the heads that raised them. Routing (`severity.block_at`, backlog filing, fix kicks, human holds) runs on the decided reports; the heads' raw reports never route on their own. When every head approved with no findings, no decision session runs and, with `acknowledge_no_findings` on, the hive posts a single acknowledgement. `review.head_max_retries` is now enforced per head: a head that never answers is named in the decision and the comment instead of stalling the PR, unless no head answered, where `max_redispatch` applies as before. `/api/reviewer/accuracy` adds `review_heads`, scoring each review model's head reports against the decision.
- `agents.<name>.review_heads` lets the review swarm judge every perspective with several models independently ([#13542](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13542), part 1). Each head (`{backend, model, alias, replicas}`) is materialized like `replicas` as `<base>-<alias>-<n>` agents that copy the base reviewer with their own backend and model, are stripped on save and provisioned at boot by the entrypoint; `review.reviewer_agents` naming the base admits them. With `combined_perspectives: false` each perspective is dispatched once per head to that head's least-loaded replica, as a blind, record-only kick (`hive-review --record-verdict`, nothing posted on the PR), and the relay keeps one verdict per perspective per head. A decision step reconciles the heads into one verdict per perspective (see the part 2 entry); `review.head_max_retries` (Settings → Review gate) bounds per-head re-dispatch. Hives without `review_heads` dispatch exactly as before.
- The ACMM L2 pack now includes the `reviewer` agent in COMMENT-only mode (no fixer, no auto-merge) as the review-first entry point; review is part of L2 proper and no L2.5 level was added. L5/L6 reviewer behaviour is unchanged (#13574).
- Triage can now comment once on new RFC/feature issues with the existing settings that may already cover the request, each linked to Settings with the search pre-filled (`issues.rfc_existing_check.enabled`, default off; never labels or closes). Settings also accepts `#config/governor/<tab>/<query>` deep links that open with the search box filled in.
- `runs.triage.clarity_gate` (default off; `enabled`, `threshold` 0-100, default 60; Settings → Features → Incoming issue triage) scores each human-filed, unclaimed issue for goal, acceptance criteria, scope and detail before an agent is kicked on it. An issue under the threshold gets one `<!-- hive:clarity-gate -->` comment with concise questions for its author and the `needs-spec` label (stage/045) instead of a claim, and a park label write that failed is retried on the next kick even across a hive restart; removing `needs-spec` resumes the normal pipeline ([#13577](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13577)).
- The clarity gate (`runs.triage.clarity_gate`) now resumes a parked issue on its own: while the gate is on, a periodic sweep removes the hive's own `needs-spec` once the issue author, or a non-hive commenter with write/maintain/admin, replies after the gate's `<!-- hive:clarity-gate -->` question, and records the un-park so the issue re-derives `stage/010-actionable`; a `needs-spec` a person added is never lifted ([#13588](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13588)).
- Extend the FedRAMP Moderate and ISO 27001 Annex A profiles with more baseline controls (listed `not_covered` where Hive cannot evidence them) and rename the non-NIST `AC-2.ELIG` row to `ELIG-1` ([#13585](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13585)).
- Show rolling 30-day issue reopen rates per repository and clarity-gate cohort in Evidence and Prometheus, with captured closure counts and explicit unknown/empty-cohort handling ([#13589](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13589)).
- Automerge can require a PR head to contain the current base before merging: repos listed in `auto_merge.require_current_base` get a green-but-stale head updated and re-tested instead of merged untested against newer base commits.
- Automerge can merge the base forward into a trusted human PR that only conflicts because the base moved: repos listed in `auto_merge.merge_forward_trusted_human` get one App-authored, signed-off merge commit on the PR branch (no human commit rewritten); a real conflict pushes nothing and posts one note naming the files both sides changed ([#13636](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13636))
- Add a reusable offline index for tracked code identifiers, config keys, flags and documentation across registered checkouts, with bounded input, deterministic results and per-repository coverage errors; prior-art gate and issue-filing integration remain follow-up work after #13773 lands.
- The review swarm's outcome now shows on the PR, and its follow-up work is tied to the PR it came from ([#13833](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13833)). The new `review.verdict_labels` block maps the current head's review state to one label each: `reviewing`, `approve`, `changes_requested`, `requires_human` (`reject` counts as `requires_human`). It works independently of the auto-merge engine's stage labels, so a hive with auto-merge off still shows "in progress / approved / changes requested / needs human" on every PR. Like `human_decision_label`, the labels are never created and never block. With `review_heads`, backlog items are now filed only from the decision step's reconciled findings, never from each head's raw report. That had produced near-duplicate items whose wording defeated the fingerprint check and spent the PR's daily cap. The items are also listed in a "Follow-ups filed" section of the decided review itself, on every head, rather than in a once-per-PR summary comment. Every review-backlog item, in every destination including Linear, is now parked on the PR it was filed from with the `blocked` label and the blocked-on marker, not only when the cited file is missing on the base branch. A new sweep lifts the block with a one-line note when the PR merges. When the PR closes unmerged it also lifts the block and comments "source PR #N closed unmerged — re-triage against current base", leaving the item open for normal triage: a closed PR is often superseded by one that lands the same lines, so backlog items are never closed or cancelled automatically.
- v5: the semantic prompt-injection classifier can run through the Claude CLI, launched with no tools, no MCP servers, no GitHub token and an empty working directory, on hives without a model endpoint: set `ioscan.classifier.backend: claude` (or pick it in Settings → Security → Input Defense). A CLI backend makes at most `ioscan.classifier.cli_budget_per_eval` calls per scheduler pass (default 8) and `ioscan.classifier.cli_daily_quota` calls per UTC day (default 500); backends that cannot run without tools (copilot, codex, gemini) are refused at boot.
