- Automerge sweeps can enqueue eligible PRs into GitHub's native merge queue with the validated head pinned, report queue position and state, and withdraw Hive-enqueued entries only when the PR loses merge eligibility (a hold, a withdrawn or stale approval, changes requested, a paused or disabled repo, or a draft or closed PR) while preserving entries queued by people. The hand-off is opt-in per repo through `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.enabled` and `.repos` (default off; hives without queues see no change). On a queue-enabled base a `blocked` or `behind` PR is enqueued rather than reported `not-mergeable`; the `require_current_base` gate and the `behind` update-branch stay in force unless `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.skip_current_base_gate` is set. The `isMergeQueueEnabled` probe is cached per base branch for `auto_merge.native_merge_queue.probe_ttl` (default 30m) and the entry reconciliation runs only on opted-in repos. A mixed-authorship PR whose queue uses `SQUASH` parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` with the `merge-method` explanation, and the refusal is remembered per head for 30 minutes.
- Add native merge-group CI and an owned PR-evidence gate, opt-in external freshness-writer suppression, default-off scoped owner Settings controls, and a distinct Activity Tracker rail backed by bounded provider-neutral observations of actual GitHub queue entries, exact candidate CI, proven-or-unknown members and lifecycle receipts.
- Tracker, online-contributor and Knowledge sidebar count pills briefly show the actual signed increase or decrease on live updates, with directional amber feedback and a static reduced-motion alternative.
- Activity Monitor: hovering or focusing the *Needs human decision* chevron word or a lead *needs-human* / *triage needed* pill opens an in-app popover that says what the row is waiting on (the reviewer's own question when the hive has one, else the park reason in plain words, plus the blocker — "A reviewer requested changes on b0f5f80 — needs a new commit. Approving cannot override that."), offers the applicable actions as buttons (*Let hive decide* first, then Approve / Give direction / Close as superseded / Close as won't fix / Hold or Release; disabled ones grey with their reason) down the row context menu's code path, and names who asked and when; `GET /api/stage-tracker` rows carry the new `decision_needed` (`question`, `asked_by`, `since`, `blocker`, `blocker_reason`, `options[]`). Requested by @clubanderson ([#14994](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14994)).
- Add the reusable Hive `/ok-to-test` workflow and caller template so trusted same-repo bot/App workflow runs can be approved by a repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` without granting the Hive App Actions write.
- Onboarding problems the dashboard shows — GitHub App not installed / wrong installation / insufficient permissions / undelivered credentials, GHES base URL, project target, no projects, no agents — now carry a *New hive? Open the 🧭 Guide → step …* link that opens the Getting Started guide at the matching step; the Guide chip stays visible while any such problem is active, the guide's GitHub App step prints the concrete install URL for the configured GitHub host, and `GET /api/status` exposes the classification as `onboardingIssues[]` (plus `onboarding`/`guideStep` on system alerts and deep-health checks) (#15772).
- Activity monitor: a ✓ decision badge on every row you acted on from the dashboard — green once recorded, amber when the item is still at the same stage past the stuck window, red when the action failed — with a plain-words tooltip (what it is waiting on → what you chose, when → what the hive did next) and a **Decisions** filter (Awaiting my decision / I acted / Acted, still stuck). Actions are kept in a server-side ledger (`/data/operator-actions.json`), surface as `last_operator_action` on tracker rows and via `GET /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/items/{number}`. Requested by @clubanderson.
- `hivectl evidence benchmark` and `src/scripts/outcome-benchmark.sh` compute a reproducible mediated-vs-unmediated outcome report (revert rate, change-failure, median time-to-merge, CI at merged head, changes-requested-before-merge, cost per merged PR; Wilson intervals, n < 10 not reported) with generated SVG charts under `src/docs/benchmarks/` and a `--readme` flag that rewrites the README's `<!-- outcomes:start/end -->` block, guarded by a drift test
- Human-merge-path holds now record their exact head without claiming pre-existing holds; a shared fail-closed release API validates App ownership and complete label history for later pin-only admission integration, with operator rollout prerequisites documented (#16269).
- Add validated per-repository `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` schema, changed-file patch evidence and a fail-closed pin-replacement syntax classifier as building blocks for #16242; merge-path exceptions are not yet enabled and existing human-merge protections remain unchanged.
- The `hive-merge` relay now honours the `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception, with the same checks as the automerge sweep plus an exact requested-head match; anything short of a proven pin-only change by a trusted author stays held (#16265).
- Enforce the `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception in the automerge sweep lanes and `/hive approve` (#16266): a PR by a listed trusted author whose complete diff is pin replacements on guarded paths is no longer held for a person. Any other changed file, including an unguarded changelog or doc, keeps the hold (#16326). Repos without an enabled entry are unchanged; the `hive-merge` relay enforces the same exception as of #16265.
- Show preparation owners and FIFO waiting positions in a visible train-style Activity Monitor rail, removing redundant preparation pills and the zero-train header summary while preserving real ready trains, PR stages, row sorting, pagination, and issue trees.
- `hivectl hives preset adopt --onboard` reviews and enrolls missing Hives and preset hub snapshots in one confirmed flow, reusing existing credentials and retaining successful enrollments on partial failure.
- Added an automated list-price refresh for the Cost panel: `go run ./internal/tools/pricetable` reconciles `src/pkg/tokens/pricing.go` with OpenRouter's public model catalogue (no vendor HTML scraped), rewrites only the rates that moved, bumps `priceTableDate`, and reports every change and every row it could not verify; the weekly `price-table-refresh` workflow turns a non-empty diff into a single `needs-human` PR on `bot/price-table-refresh`, and CI now fails when the table is more than 60 days old so a stalled refresh is noticed. See the "Price table refresh" section of `src/docs/token-tracking.md`.
- Once its `hive:recheck-after` deadline passes, a `blocked` ops-tracking soak checklist on the hive's own project gets one soak-evidence comment (stable-channel hives' heartbeat, restart loops and candidate digest/SHA, read from the hub or the spoke's own `/api/version`), the checklist lines that evidence proves are ticked, and `<!-- hive:recheck-done -->` stops repeats; the issue stays open and `blocked` for a maintainer to close (#13311).
- The hub accepts a contributor's **opt-in** relay audit attestation: an `audit_share` on `task_complete` / `task_failed` (rows up to the shared level, clamped to the relay's capture level) writes a `relay_task_attested` audit row cross-referencing the contributor's local record. At `commands`+ the hub stores the shared command rows in `/data/contrib-audit/<login>/<task>.jsonl` (0600, 90-day retention) rather than the 500-entry audit ring. The new `hub.contribute_audit_share_request` (default empty) lets a hive *request* a level, advertised on `auth_ok` (`audit_share_requested`) and on `/contribute` before setup. Admission never depends on it ([#13458](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13458), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- `GET /api/audit?contributor=<login>` narrows the Audit Log to one contributor's rows (same 200-entry cap and role gate; combines with `?sensitive=1`), the Audit Log gains a `relay_` quick-filter chip beside the sensitive toggle, and the contribute page's Operations tab gains a read-only "Your assignments" card listing the caller's own `relay_*` audit rows ([#13454](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13454), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- The hub now records the contributor relay's lifecycle in the existing `/data/audit.jsonl` as `relay_*` rows — `relay_connected`, `relay_rejected`, `relay_disconnected`, `relay_task_assigned`, `relay_task_accepted`, `relay_task_declined`, `relay_token_minted`, `relay_task_completed`, `relay_task_failed`, `relay_task_revoked` and `relay_task_abandoned` (plus the reserved `relay_mcp_lease_issued` / `relay_mcp_lease_revoked`) — attributed to the contributor's GitHub login and session, with the task's repository and issue/PR number. Rows are written from frames the hub already receives, so an unmodified relay needs no change; progress and heartbeat frames are not audited and no token is ever written. `relay_token_minted` (which carries the `installation` id) and `relay_task_revoked` are sensitive actions and raise `sensitive_24h` on hives with active contributors; `relay_connected` is not sensitive and omits the remote address. Documented in `audit-log.md` and `contributor-relay.md` ([#13453](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13453), part of [#13441](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13441)).
- Delegated relay work is now covered by the audit substrate: a new `relay_audit_coverage` compliance posture check passes when the hub wrote at least one `relay_*` audit row in the last 24h or no relay connected, fails when relays connected without any row, and is mapped to SOC 2 CC7.2 (with notes on ISO A.8.15 and FedRAMP AU-2) ([#13455](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13455)).
- Dashboard: stage-tracker action-result toasts (adopted, posted, held, no-op) now close themselves after 15 s with the countdown bar and hover/focus pause; errors and toasts offering next actions stay until acknowledged.
- Settings → Features → Review Gate → Reviewers now picks `review.reviewer_agents` from the hive's configured agents, showing each agent's engine/model, the review-capable count, a warning when fan-out would run every review on a single engine, and a note when combined-perspective mode limits fan-out to the first reviewer; `GET /api/config/review` gains `reviewer_candidates`.
- `review.pending_fix_ttl` sets how long a dispatched review fix may go without a new head before the next bounded attempt is dispatched (default 2h; negative disables expiry). It was previously fixed at 2h even though the docs presented it as tunable (#14643).
- `review.require_labels` — a PR-side approval allow-list for reviews, the counterpart of `project.issue_filter.require_labels`: when set, the hive reviews only PRs carrying at least one of the labels. Enforced server-side in the cadence reviewer's PR list, the fan-out dispatch planner and the `hive-review` relay (which re-reads the PR's labels and refuses any review, thread reply or verdict on an unlabelled PR, audited as `review_label_gate_refused`), so a prompt cannot bypass it. New **Settings → Features → Review Gate → "Only review labelled PRs"** toggle with a label list, saved through `PUT /api/config/review`. Empty (the default) changes nothing. Reported-by: @joerunde (a1-vllm-spyre spoke: "the team wants reviews gated — run only when a label is added to a PR").
- `review.reviewers.autoscale` (off by default; Settings → Review Gate → Reviewers) sizes the reviewer lane to its backlog ([#14685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14685)): the planner now reports the PRs it left waiting for a free reviewer or a parallel slot, and a controller adds a `reviewer-N` replica after `scale_up_cycles` cycles behind `target_backlog_per_reviewer` (or a wait older than the review-pending stage dwell), drains the top replica after `scale_down_cycles` idle cycles and retires it only once its turn ends. Scale-ups are refused by named guards — `at-max`, `cooldown`, `saturated` (kicks not reaching the CLI prompt), `provider-budget`, `provider-headroom`, `max-parallel-reviews`, cgroup `cpu` / `memory`. Dynamic replicas go through the ordinary replica expansion (same role, prompt, token, pane and cadence as `reviewer-2`) and the entrypoint pre-creates their users up to `max`. Each decision logs as `reviewer autoscale: 2→3 reason=backlog=7 oldest=41m0s`; `/api/status.reviewerAutoscale` and an *auto* badge on the lane's agent cards show current/target/min/max and the last decision.
- Reviewer calibration now compares five-bin self-reported confidence with an evidence-derived score, preserves raw reports and legacy fallback, and shows series coverage and monotonic merge-share comparisons without changing review gating ([#13239](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13239)).
- Stage tracker: a PR row returned to its author (071 needs-author / 072 returned-to-contributor) now carries a `rework` pickup signal — requested / queued / acknowledged / working / re-review pending — on the waiting-on pill, its tooltip and the row event line, derived from the stage record, the PR list and the contributor fix queue with no extra GitHub calls.
- Render RFC lifecycle notices as Discord summary-card embeds alongside transition text when `rfc_format: card` is configured on the designated announcer.
- In rich mode (`rfc_format: card` or `rfc_threads: true`, on the designated `rfc_announcer`), RFC lifecycle notices now cover RFC documents proposed as pull requests: a PR titled `📝 proposal:` / `📝 RFC`, or one adding or changing `docs/rfc-*.md` / `src/docs/rfc-*.md`, is announced once when it opens (titled by the document's first heading when available) and once with `RFC doc accepted` when it merges, attributed to the RFC issue its body links. PRs already open at the baseline are not announced, the private-repository gate applies, and line mode stays issues-only (#15942, part of #15869).
- RFC lifecycle notices gain opt-in rich-mode keys under `notifications.discord`: `rfc_format` (`line`, the default, or `card`; an unknown value is a config error), `rfc_threads`, `rfc_announcer` and `rfc_backlink_comment`. All default off, so today's one-line posts are unchanged. Card and thread rendering land later. For now, rich mode switches on the designated-announcer gate: a hive set to `rfc_format: card` or `rfc_threads: true` without `rfc_announcer: true` posts nothing and logs `rfc notify: rich mode requires rfc_announcer; not posting` once. Its detector state still advances, so turning on the announcer later does not backfill. This stops several hives sharing a channel from racing to publish (#15926, part of #15869).
- With `rfc_threads: true` on the designated `rfc_announcer`, each RFC now gets one Discord thread under its opened card, with a durable per-RFC message/thread mapping in `/data/rfc-notify.json` (state version 2; version 1 files load unchanged), a write-ahead intent plus Discord `enforce_nonce` and a bounded 50-message history lookup so a crash or retry never posts a second card, later closed/ready/doc-accepted events posted into the thread (closed and ready also echoed once to the channel), and an opt-in `rfc_backlink_comment` that comments the thread link on the RFC once, only after the thread exists (#15939).
- Loopback-only `net/http/pprof` listener (`debug.pprof_addr`, default `127.0.0.1:6060`, `off` to disable), a `mem: runtime snapshot` INFO line every 60 s (heap in-use/live/objects, next GC, goroutines, OS threads, GOMEMLIMIT), the same counters under `runtime` in `GET /api/health`, and a cgroup-aware GOMEMLIMIT default (85% of the container memory limit when the env var is unset) ([#14681](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14681)).
- `agents.<name>.sandbox.job.scheduler_name` sets the Job pod's `schedulerName`, for clusters whose admission webhook requires a custom scheduler for device-requesting pods (e.g. `spyre-scheduler`)
- Sandboxed kicks gained a deterministic publish preflight that does not trust the agent's report: `sandbox.publish.verify` (per agent) or `agent_sandbox.publish.verify` (global) lists shell commands hive runs in the same sandbox image/workspace after the run (with `HIVE_CHANGED_FILES` / `HIVE_CHANGED_TESTS` exported), and the first non-zero exit withholds the push and the PR with the command's output tail on the card (`no PR opened: verify failed (1/2): uv run pytest --collect-only -q (exit 2) …`) and in the kick log. A whole-suite `pytest --collect-only` there would have stopped a test-gap PR whose new test file's basename clashed with an existing one and broke collection for every CI shard. Reported-by: @joerunde (a1-vllm-spyre spoke); hivecommons/hive#14999.
- `src/docs/security-model.md` is now the complete inventory of how hive keeps autonomous agents from doing damage: threat model, a control table (control → threat → file/ADR → how to verify), sections per layer from agent runtime isolation to human-in-the-loop, an honest gaps list, and an audit checklist for a running hive; linked from the docs index, documentation map and the root README security section (#13409).
- A trusted maintainer's **changes requested** review on a hive-authored PR, or a `/hive decision <what to change>` comment on one parked at `stage/085-needs-decision`, now moves the PR to `stage/070-fixing` and kicks the author agent once per head with the text verbatim plus the swarm's outstanding findings; the self-authored automerge lane no longer merges over such a review, `/hive decision` on a PR the hive did not open gets an explanatory reply instead of silence, and the 085 entry comment names both actions (hivecommons/hive#13041, live case hivecommons/hive#12968).
- Self-reports now notice clogged queues and repeated errors without a hand-placed hook: a `slog` tee (`pkg/fleetreport/slogfeed`) on the hive's root logger feeds every WARN/ERROR line into `unclassified_error_repeated` (5 identical normalised messages in 10 min; clears after 20 quiet minutes; benign i/o-timeout / context-cancel lines and messages already covered by an explicit class are skipped), and two new queue-health classes report work the hive is silently not doing — `issue_request_stuck` (an issue-request file that has failed ≥3 attempts or been retrying for ≥30 min; clears on completion/quarantine) and `effect_ledger_op_stuck` (a journaled external effect refused for reconciliation while Unknown/Planned for ≥30 min; clears when applied or reconciled). The dashboard's Fleet report card labels every runtime class in plain words. Motivated by eleven placeholder relay requests retried for six hours behind one Unknown ledger op that no self-report ever mentioned.
- Self-report (`[selfreport] …`) issues now name the reporting hive by its display name and link to its dashboard: the evidence table gains `hive name` and `spoke` rows and each `Affected hives (N)` line renders `name (hive id) … — open` as a link to the dashboard. Both travel as `hive_name` / `spoke_url` on the report and the hub relay, which overlays its own project name and vanity URL and fills them for older spokes; hub-less hives stay anonymous and render `—` (#13211).
- Sentinel sweep: optional bounded PatchObserver hook on the PR-patch fetch (#15933)
- Add owner-only Event triggers settings with scoped scanner first-seen issue presets, advanced CEL editing, validation, durable conflict-protected saves, and a direct link from agent Channels.
- Settings now expose the prior-art gate's kinds, max_findings, max_parks_per_cycle and bot_close_ttl with validation.
- Add an opt-in Hub-coordinated CLI session pool for spokes. Participating Hives keep separate workspaces, UIDs, credentials, and tmux sessions; the Hub leases a global live-session slot and idle sessions are terminated after a turn. Configure `HIVE_SHARED_AGENT_POOL_ENABLED` on spokes and `HIVE_SHARED_AGENT_POOL_MAX_SESSIONS` (optionally `HIVE_SHARED_AGENT_POOL_MAX_PER_HIVE` for a per-tenant cap) on the Hub.
- Activity Monitor: every soak-related pill — 095 "Soaking" and a trust-blocked head at 060/080 — now carries the lane's soak clock (`soak: {started_at, until, window_s, head_sha}`) and counts it down in place, says "ready — next sweep in Nm" once the window has passed and "Soak restarted · new head" when a push replaced the soaked head; hovering the soak chevron shows the live time left, when the soak ends and the rule, refreshed as the clock ticks. "merge sweep running" no longer hides the countdown ([#15218](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15218)).
- Hive honours the Spek publish marker `<!-- spek:publish name=… artifact_id=… target=… [task=…] [rfc=…] -->` (spektacular#109/#114): a Spek-published child stays on the direct-fix path under `runs.triage` (never a new `spec` run), skips the clarity score, and its kick line carries the RFC link and spek identity with the `Fixes #<child>` instruction; the RFC itself (marker without `task=`) is treated like `epic` for `governor.claims.never_claim_labels` and `IsTrackerIssue`, so Hive never claims it even in a repo without that label. Parser in `pkg/spekmarker`; documented in `docs/spektacular.md` → Publish hand-off.
- Stage engine: new issue-only stage `stage/015-triage-needed` ("Triage needed") for an actionable issue no maintainer has looked at yet — it carries `needs-triage` or the reporter-trust gate holds it in `reporter_triage`; issues filed by hive agents or trusted humans stay 010. The activity monitor's Actionable column now reads "Actionable", "Triage needed" or "Needs human decision"; the Open column is unchanged. 015 is a tracking state, not a gate: claiming and PR coverage move it on exactly like 010, and a maintainer triaging it (015 → 010) is never a regression.
- Stage tracker: new PR stage `stage/095-pre-merge-soak` between `090-ready-for-human-merge` and `100-merge-queue`. A PR the automerge lane has admitted but whose pre-merge soak window is still running now lands on 095 (dashboard word "Soaking", headline "Pre-merge soak — Xm left" from the new `soak_remaining_seconds` tracker field) instead of showing as "Admitted — merging"; 100 is reserved for soak-complete, merge-eligible PRs. 100 → 095 on re-evaluation is a reclassification, not a regression; a quiet 095 past its 45m dwell gets a stall note flagging a probable lane bug.
- Landed the central stage engine skeleton from ADR-0025 (hivecommons/hive#13007, part of hivecommons/hive#12999): the new `pkg/stageengine` package carries the shared `Facts`/`Decision` contract, the `Deriver` registry, the `StageWriter` and `FactSink` interfaces, a `Reconciler` with off/shadow/enforce modes, the `Expected` transition table generated from the stage diagram (a test proves table ⇔ diagram), and the ADR's counters; `pkg/github/automerge` and `pkg/github` gain adapters that derive PR and issue stages through today's `resolveStage` / `IssueStageFor` unchanged, so the sweeps keep their behaviour until PR-C switches them to the reconciler.
- Stage labels: golden fixture corpora freezing the current PR-side (`resolveStage`/`classifyStage`) and issue-side (`IssueStageFor`) stage derivation byte-for-byte, replayed by `stage_goldens_test.go` / `issue_stage_goldens_test.go` (regenerate with `-update`), plus `pkg/stagelabels/shadowdiff`, a pure recorder that counts legacy-vs-engine stage/reason mismatches with a bounded example ring for the ADR-0025 shadow rollout ([#13006](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13006)).
- The Activity Monitor Twitch streamer now carries the tracker's merge-zap and new-item-buzz sounds: Chromium plays into a PulseAudio null sink that ffmpeg captures (`STREAM_AUDIO=silent` restores the silent track), and kiosk mode (`?kiosk=1`) turns tracker sounds on by default without a gesture or localStorage write (`&sound=off` keeps it quiet).
- The review swarm now honours `agents.<reviewer>.review_models` ([#13243](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13243)): every `[review-perspective:…]` kick is planned against the PR's author model, carries the same `## Independent review — run this review with <backend>/<model>` section the queue kick uses, and respects `exclude_author_model` / `exclude_author_family` / `fallback` (`skip` withholds the kick, `requires_human` holds the PR). New `review.perspective_models` pins a model per perspective. Verdicts now carry `author_model` and `review_model` even without a pool (the reviewer-accuracy summary falls back to the reviewer's launch model), and the Evidence → Accuracy card and `/api/evidence/summary` add per-author-family and same-family vs cross-family buckets (`outcomes_by_author_family`, `by_author_family`, `by_family_match`, verdict `same_family`).
- **Dashboard toasts show a countdown bar timed to their auto-dismiss.** Every timed toast — success, info, warning, an error given an explicit deadline, and an in-flight toast resolved into its result — now draws a 2px bar along its bottom edge that drains from full to empty over exactly the toast's dismiss window, so it reaches zero at the moment the toast leaves. The bar takes the toast's severity colour at reduced opacity, never shifts layout, is hidden under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and is absent on sticky (error) and persistent (spinner) toasts that wait for a click.
- Dashboard toasts: the countdown bar now drains right-to-left over the toast's real lifetime (`--toast-ttl`), pauses with the dismiss timer while the pointer or keyboard focus is on the toast and resumes on leave, uses the severity colour at 40% so it reads in dark and light mode, and stays visible under reduced motion.
- Activity monitor: a multi-row selection offers **Accept triage (N selected)** — leading the selection bar and the bulk ⋯ menu when every selected row waits on a maintainer's triage, *Accept triage (k of N)* when some rows are skipped — accepting every selected issue through the existing per-item endpoint with one summary toast ("Accepted 4 issues").
- The activity monitor says who holds a claimed item, not just what kind of actor. `GET /api/stage-tracker` rows (and nested `linked_prs[]`) carry `claimant: {kind: hive-agent|clanker|person, login, agent, hive, since, source}` on claimed / in-progress issues and PRs under review or rework, derived from the worker-claim ledger, the `hive:claim` marker (with its hive fingerprint), an assignee or the agent the status payload says is on it. The lit chevron appends one token after its word — **Claimed · quality**, **Claimed · quality@alchemy** (another hive), **Claimed · @bob's clanker**, **Claimed · @alice** — and the chevron hover adds *Held by: <identity> since <ago> (<source>)*. Nothing is added when nobody is named.
- Hive activity monitor: draft PRs (forge draft bit or prow `do-not-merge/work-in-progress`) now wear a muted `draft` pill with a tooltip explaining the review and merge lanes skip them, and their Open cell reads "Draft · since …" without the stale tint, instead of a bare "Open · since …" that looked stuck (#14572).
- Activity Monitor: a row's "Hive: …" note shows for 30 s when it is new, then slides left into a small ⬡ info icon so the list stays quiet; the icon's tooltip keeps the note and its age, a click (or Enter / Space) opens it for another 30 s, a hidden tab pauses the clock, and ⚙ → Hive notes → *Auto-collapse hive notes* (default on) turns it off.
- The Activity Monitor renders a row's lead action inline — `[Accept triage]`, `[Let hive decide]`, `[Merge now]`, `[Adopt…]` — as a button beside the chips whenever the next move is the viewer's, the same entry the ⋯ menu leads with, with its hint as the hover and greyed with the reason when the viewer lacks write access; a sidelined issue (reporter triage, filtered) now keeps its author kind in the row payload ([#15456](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15456)).
- The activity monitor's tracker now says where an adopted PR came from: the hive's copy wears a compact `adopted from @author's #N · 6h` chip beside its number, linked to the original, with a plain-words hover on why the hive took it over (CI red and the contributor's agent silent, a maintainer's request, a DCO / rebase re-home); a still-open original reads `superseded by #M`. The `lineage` field behind it is also what the *Let hive decide* preview and the row hover use to add *(adopted from #N)* after the PR number, so an issue covered by an adopted PR no longer looks like the hive took a contributor's PR for no reason.
- Hive activity monitor: a **Movement animation** section in the card settings (⚙) with a subtle, user-selectable animation when an item's lit chevron moves to another column (six styles, default colour wash; respects `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- Activity Monitor: the **PR in progress** chevron names who is working the PR, exactly like **Claimed** — `PR in progress · scanner ⬡`, `PR in progress · @odttlnt's clanker 🤖`, `PR in progress · @clubanderson 👤` — resolved from a live worker-ledger claim on the PR, else the PR author (a hive PR names its attribution-trailer agent); the name ellipsizes before the one-line sub-row wraps and the hover carries the full identity and source (hivecommons/hive#15541).
- Dashboard: the Hive activity monitor now shows a per-repository chip before each issue/PR number (tinted per repo, muted for the primary repo, click to filter to that repo; "Show repo chip" setting in ⚙ defaults to only when multiple repos are listed) and gains a **Group** control (None / Repo) that groups rows under collapsible, sticky per-repo headers with row, needs-attention and per-column counts, remembered across reloads.
- Hive activity monitor rows have a right-click context menu (also the ⋯ gutter button, Shift+F10 and the context-menu key) with the actions that fit the row's state — Decide… (on a PR parked at 085 — or the issue row nesting it — Approve posts `/lgtm` + `/approve` as the operator, Close as superseded by… with a PR picker, Won't fix, Give direction as `/hive decision`; on an issue parked at 045 approve direction / send back to the hive / close; recorded exactly as the maintainer's comment would be; never merges), Hold / Release hold, Re-evaluate now, Mark needs-human, Open on GitHub, Copy link — and multi-select (gutter checkbox, Shift+click range, Cmd/Ctrl+click toggle, Space) with a selection bar whose bulk actions run per row under a progress toast and list failures by row. Selection survives the live re-render and is dropped for rows that leave. Backed by the existing hold, send-to-human and rescan endpoints plus a new audited `POST /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/items/{number}/decision`.
- Hive activity monitor: a ⚙ settings modal on the card lets you replace the merge zap and new-item buzz with your own WAV (or any browser-decodable audio) files, kept in the browser (IndexedDB, 4 MB cap, built-in fallback if a file fails to decode), with a Play-sounds master toggle, a 0–100 volume slider applied to built-in and uploaded sounds, per-sound preview and reset. Sounds fire for every repo the hive governs.
- Hive activity monitor: an Open issue still labelled `needs-triage` now shows a "triage needed" action chip (and "Open · triage needed" in its tooltip), alongside the existing hold chip.
- Triage prior-art gate (`runs.triage.prior_art`, default on): before any agent claims a feature / RFC / epic issue, the scheduler searches knowledge beads, the Settings index, merged PRs (12 months), closed issues, docs and code for the issue's key terms. A human-filed issue whose best finding reaches the threshold (default 70) is parked at the new `stage/017-possible-existing` ("Possibly exists · needs author") with one comment quoting the findings and two replies: `/hive decision proceed — <gap>` lifts the park and appends a *Scope vs existing* section to the body; `/hive decision exists` closes it `not_planned` with `already-exists`. A discoverability advisory bead is recorded so the docs can improve. Clanker-filed issues are parked the same way and auto-closed after `bot_close_ttl` (default 72h) with no reply; hive-filed issues are never parked (a findings note is attached and the agent prompts make the search a precondition to filing). The dashboard tracker shows the lane and a `possible dupe` chip (#13575).
- `hivectl tui --hives` now shows the shared Hub → Hive → Repository contribution tree (press `t` in the Hives overlay) with textual selection, badge, follow, readiness and activity columns, ancestry-preserving search, staged edits with affected counts for bulk actions, and review-then-Apply or Discard; it shows the same diff and Saved / Relay reload / Acknowledged receipt as `hivectl hives web`, writes nothing until Apply, and asks before discarding unapplied edits on leave or quit.
- Twitch live stream (https://www.twitch.tv/hivecommons) listed in every community-link cluster: README badge and Community section, CONTRIBUTING, community/getting-started docs, issue-template contact links, dashboard sidebar Help / FAQ / Getting Started modal, the `/contribute` portal and default `contribute.help_links`, and hub landing/status page navs and footers. (#15635, #15637)
- Mark lanes `unauthorized` when the hive's GitHub App lacks the permission for the next step: a `403 Resource not accessible by integration` on a prerequisite call (first: approving held workflow runs without `actions: write`) adds `hive:unauthorized`, posts one comment per head naming the permission and the human step, logs once per head, parks the PR at 085 as `Awaiting human: approve workflow runs`, shows a muted `unauthorized` pill in the activity monitor, and clears itself the tick the step is no longer needed ([#14589](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14589)).
- Both dashboards now show scheduled-upgrade progress ([#14950](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14950)). The hub hive card and the spoke's version menu render the upgrade state as a pill — `Draining · 2/5 agents in turn: reviewer 38m, scanner 12m · 14m left`, `Missed window · drain lapsed` — and list the hub's recent upgrade attempts so a missed window is visible on both sides. `/api/version` carries `upgradeProgress` and `upgradeHistory`. Owners get an **Upgrade now (interrupt turns)** action on the hub card while a hive is draining or missed; it is the normal upgrade request with `?interrupt=1`, audit-logged, delivered on the next heartbeat as `upgrade_interrupt`, and makes the spoke skip its drain and restart immediately.
- Scheduled upgrades now expose their progress as data on both dashboards ([#14950](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14950), motivated by [#14856](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14856)): the hub's `/api/saas/my-hives` carries `upgradeState` (`scheduled` → `draining` → `pulling` → `rolling` → `verifying` → `done` | `missed`, with the drain deadline/countdown and the agents whose turns are holding it — "2/5 agents in turn: reviewer 38m, scanner 12m") and `upgradeHistory`; the spoke's `/api/status.upgradeProgress` derives the same state locally and the heartbeat policy gains `next_window_at` (the hive's own window, even on `stable`) plus `upgrade_history`. The hub persists the last 14 attempts and held windows per hive (`HIVE_HUB_UPGRADE_HISTORY_MAX`) under `/data/saas/upgrade-history/`, so a missed window survives a hub restart and is never silent. The spoke's drain report now includes per-agent turn elapsed (`upgrade_drain.turns`).
- The dashboard now tells the operator when work is parked on a human: `/api/stage-tracker` carries `waiting_on_human` (`count`, `items[{repo, number, type, kind, since, who}]`; kinds `needs-decision`, `ready-for-human-merge`, `approve-needed`, `returned-to-contributor-offline`, `other-human-wait`) and each item `waiting_on_you` / `wait_kind`. A second, orange **Hive activity monitor** sidebar badge and a **Waiting on you · N** topbar pill (hidden at zero) show the count; both, `?filter=waiting-on-you` and the new **Waiting on you** toolbar chip narrow the activity monitor to those rows; a debounced in-app toast (one per ten minutes, none in kiosk mode) fires when the count rises. Hold, advisories, decided rows and contributors still inside their grace are not counted.
- `hivectl hives web` now renders the shared Hub → Hive → Repository contribution tree with keyboard navigation, mixed selection states, staged Apply/Discard, revision-checked review, and separate Saved / Relay reload / Acknowledged receipts; opening the page preserves legacy profiles without migration.
- **GitHub webhooks now move the Hive activity monitor row for just the PR or issue that changed, in seconds.** A verified `POST /api/webhook/github` delivery that names an item this hive tracks (`pull_request*`, `check_suite`/`check_run`, `status`, `push` to a PR branch, `issue_comment`, any `issues` action) drops the `/api/stage-tracker` cache at once and queues a targeted re-read of that one item — a single `GET`, debounced by `dashboard.stage_tracker.webhook_refresh_debounce_ms` (default `2000`) and coalesced per item so a check fan-out costs one request — then patches its row in the status snapshot (labels, title, draft flag, last activity; closed or merged items leave) and sends the `stage-tracker` SSE nudge. Before, a webhook only invalidated caches and the tracker waited for the next eval cycle (120 s today, up to `governor.eval_interval_webhook_s` = 900 s in webhook mode), so webhooks made the tracker slower rather than faster. No repository is re-enumerated; the read uses the paced REST transport and is skipped while the API budget is critical. `dashboard.stage_tracker.webhook_refresh: false` turns it off. `/api/status` and `/api/gh-rate-limits` `webhooks{}` additively gain `targeted_refreshes_1h` and `tracker_invalidations_1h`.
- **GitHub webhooks now wake the governor loop and refresh the stage tracker in seconds, with fewer GitHub calls.** A verified `POST /api/webhook/github` delivery that invalidates cached state — `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, `check_suite`/`check_run`, `push` to a PR branch, `issues` label/reopen — asks the loop for an early eval cycle, debounced by `governor.webhook_wake_debounce_s` (default `10`) and spaced at least `governor.webhook_wake_min_gap_s` (default `30`) apart; the wake cycle re-enriches only the PRs the webhooks marked dirty and serves every clean PR from cache, so `eval_interval_webhook_s` (default `900`) is now a safe base tick while webhooks are healthy. The loop re-checks webhook health when the `2 × eval_interval_s` window closes and drops back to `eval_interval_s` right away rather than at the next stretched tick, logging one line per transition (`github webhooks healthy; eval mode webhook` / `github webhooks went stale; eval mode poll`); `/api/status` reports `evalMode`, `evalIntervalS`, `lastWakeReason`, `lastWakeAt` and `webhookWakes`. Each status publish also invalidates the `/api/stage-tracker` cache and sends a `stage-tracker` SSE event the dashboard refetches on, instead of waiting out the cache TTL plus its 30 s poll. See the operator reference's "Webhook-driven PR cache invalidation" for the App event subscriptions and `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` setup.
- The write-back gate is content-aware: an identical comment on the same item within 24h, the same notice fanning out to several items within 60s, or more than 60 comments of one kind per repo per hour is suppressed (`writeback.dedupe`), persisted across restarts, counted on `/api/status` and shown in the Write-back containment drill-down as `duplicate`, `burst` or `rate-capped`.

### Changed

- Clarified the busy-no-activity stall documentation to cover live CLI panes without an input prompt ([#12922](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12922)).
- build(deps): bump golang.org/x/net from 0.60.0 to 0.61.0 in /src (#12941)
- build(deps): bump express from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0 in /src/proxy (#12942)
- `governor.labels.stage.engine.mode` now defaults to `enforce` (was `shadow`) after the ADR-0025 rollout gates held on hive's own spoke; an invalid value still falls back to `shadow`, and ADR-0025 is Accepted. Set `mode: shadow` or `off` to opt out. Part of #12999.
- Stage engine (ADR-0025, plan PR-F): the issue stage derivation now lives in `pkg/stageengine` (`DeriveIssue` over `IssueFacts` carrying the resolved hold / blocked / park / umbrella / triage label verdicts); `pkg/github.IssueStageFor` is a shim over it and the issue goldens replay unchanged. `cmd/hive/stageengine_wire.go` is gone (the issue deriver is built in; automerge registers the PR deriver at init) and the ADR's review-state open question is closed with the `ReviewFacts.State` fold table ([#13011](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13011)).
- Stage engine (ADR-0025, plan PR-F part 1): the legacy comparator is retired. `governor.labels.stage.engine.mode` accepts `enforce` (default) or `shadow`; `shadow` is now a pure pause (derive and count, write nothing) and the old rollback value `off` is rejected at config load. `stage_shadow_mismatch_total`, the `mismatches`/`lastMismatchExamples` fields of `/api/status.stageEngine` and the tracker strip's mismatch item are gone. Retiring the comparator exposed and fixes an enforce-mode gap: the PR sweep's engine decision dropped the dwell verdict and configured author-kind names, so `stage/stalled` was never written on a PR and a merged/closed PR kept its `role/*` label ([#13011](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13011), part of #12999).
- docs: say noWorkReasonMaxLen caps bytes, not runes (#13109)
- refactor: co-locate truncateReasonBytes with noWorkReasonMaxLen (#13121)
- Moved the contribution stage test fixture out of the shipped `hivectl` package into `hivectltest`, so its placeholder credentials are no longer compiled into the hivectl binary ([#13342](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13342)).
- images: bump claude 2.1.306 -> 2.1.308 (#13509)
- Crux: `cmd/crux` is a host composition root in the root module, like `cmd/hive`, and is no longer counted as a ring package by the outbound ratchet; with its `config`/`defsrc` rows gone the ring imports nothing from Hive in non-test code (Stage 2 prerequisite 3 complete).
- Crux design doc: Stage 1 marked shipped, measured outbound edge table and Stage 2 (nested module) prerequisites recorded, how to run the Crux package set alone (#13536).
- The Crux agent runtime (`pkg/agent`) no longer imports `pkg/github`, `pkg/agentaudit` or `pkg/tracing` (RFC #13536, Stage 2 prerequisite): the created-PR shape and the per-agent token-cache path moved into the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/types` leaf as `PRResult` and `AgentTokenCachePath` (with `github.CreatePRResult` now an alias, so `*github.Client` still satisfies the sandbox executor's `PRCreator`), the runtime-emitted audit vocabulary, `AuditSink` and `Fields` moved there too (`pkg/agentaudit` aliases them; `pkg/toolapprove` imports the leaf), and the `agent.send_kick` trace span is opened through a new `Manager.SetSpanStarter` seam that `cmd/hive` wires to `tracing.StartSpan`, so reach bookkeeping is unchanged for the hive binary while an embedding without `pkg/tracing` still gets OpenTelemetry spans on the global tracer. The review-prompt restart-trigger test moved from `pkg/agent` to `pkg/review` against the new `crux.FatalNetworkErrorPatterns()` accessor. A new fail-closed ratchet, `src/internal/testutil/crux_outbound_ratchet_test.go`, records every remaining import from the Crux package set to the rest of Hive (dominated by `pkg/config`) and only lets the list shrink. No user-visible behaviour change.
- The inference-gateway health store and the issue/comment shape validators moved into the Crux ring as the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/inferencehealth` and `pkg/crux/issueshape`; `pkg/inferencehealth` and `pkg/issueshape` alias every symbol, so hub, dashboard, github and classify callers are unchanged and the proxy no longer imports either Hive package (Stage 2 prerequisite 3, #13536)
- The GitHub proxy now takes its canary registry, inference usage sink and GitHub REST accounting through three narrow seams (`proxy.CanaryScanner`, `proxy.UsageSink`, `proxy.GitHubRESTAccounting`) that `cmd/hive` wires to `pkg/ioscan`, `pkg/tokens` and `pkg/github`; `ioscan.CanaryLeak` is now an alias of `pkg/crux/types.CanaryLeak`. No behaviour change for a running hive; the proxy no longer imports any Hive package outside the Crux ring (Stage 2 prerequisite 3, #13536)
- The Crux boundary ratchet (`src/internal/testutil/crux_boundary_ratchet_test.go`) now fails closed when a per-package `agent.<Symbol>` or tmux baseline is above the measured count, so removed coupling must be locked in by lowering the baseline in the same change (RFC #13536). Internal test change only; no user-visible behaviour change.

Labels and reasons are unchanged. Closes #13779.

Policy text and docs no longer call it "proposed".

- A combined review head kick (`review_heads` under `review.combined_perspectives: true`) now tells the head to read the PR once and judge each perspective in its own parallel sub-agent, then record the one verdict array itself, falling back to reviewing the perspectives in sequence when sub-agents are unavailable. Every sub-agent runs on the head's own model, so each head's verdicts still come from the model it is stamped with.

- The rebase-then-merge follow-through now counts a head as the hive's own by its committer: an email-domain-only match (no GitHub login resolved) needs GitHub to report the commit as verified, and the author counts only when GitHub resolves it to the App bot, since a signature never vouches for the author address ([#15182](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15182)).

The spoke dashboard serves byte-identical HTML; nothing changes for operators yet — this is groundwork for the hub Fleet activity page ([#16062](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16062), part of [#15965](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15965)).

Previously the flag help text and documentation did not mention this relationship.

- crux: the socket-directory ownership/mode check used by both `crux serve` and the callback listener is now one shared implementation (`crux/internal/privatedir`), so future hardening cannot drift between the two (#16213, #16214).
- **gh-aw compiler upgraded to v1.0.1, with the weekly competitor report regenerated in the same change.** The pinned compiler moves from `v0.89.21` to `v1.0.1` in the on-ramp compile CI and the gh-aw install docs, and `weekly-competitor-report.lock.yml` plus `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` are regenerated from the unchanged Markdown source rather than hand-edited ([#16226](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16226), replacing [#16190](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/16190)). The compiler itself now emits `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.2 and `actions/download-artifact` v8.0.2, so the `uses:` lines, the `# gh-aw-manifest` header and the "Custom actions used" list agree again (the manifest still listed v8.0.1/v7.0.1 after hand pin bumps). Runtime pieces move with the compiler: setup action v1.0.1, Copilot CLI 1.0.103 with a checksum pin, AWF firewall 0.29.0, MCP gateway v0.5.0, GitHub MCP server v2.0.3. Secrets, triggers, engine and the agent's permissions are unchanged; the generated `conclusion` job gains read-only `checks: read` for gh-aw's agent-failure diagnostics, and the `safe_outputs` job on `ubuntu-slim` is capped at 15 minutes (gh-aw v1.0.1's slim-runner limit). The "Firewall blocked N domains" false positive in the report comment, fixed upstream in gh-aw v0.89.22, no longer appears.
- The per-recipient attention budget (`github.attention.recipient_budget`, still `0` = off) and opt-in digest (`github.attention.digest_recipients`) now load from the `github.attention` block and gate the episode ledger's live first pings and reminders: over-budget asks stay open and listed (status card, attention queue, digest) instead of being posted, and security, required-review, protocol-command and hold asks are never budgeted ([#16271](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16271)).
- The post-merge refs sweep (`src/scripts/comment-merged-refs.sh`) no longer posts its "PR #N has merged and referenced this issue with a non-closing `Refs`" nudge when the issue's `hive:status` card already carries an `issue-partial:<pr>` section for that PR (#16363)
- chore(dashboard): fold the no-models warning branches into one if/else (#16382)
- chore(crux): format validateBounds range text lazily (#16406)
- Attention pilot (`github.notifications.attention_pilot: true`): the last two routine issue notes that still posted standalone comments now fold into the issue's single `hive:status` card — the relay's one-line state notes (awaiting CI, parking, already fixed) and the decision-downgrade note left when a label change walks back an earlier maintainer decision (section `issue-decision-downgrade`). Quiet mode without the pilot is unchanged. Section text is also neutralised so quoted issue-authored text can no longer open or close status-card sections ([#16270](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16270)).
- Code activity supersedes the Matrix code view: the Activity Monitor topbar has one **Code activity** entry (still `#oc-matrix-tab`) that opens the published-checkpoint reader at `?kiosk=1&view=reader` in a new tab. The decorative rain/cascade/ghost/terminal renderers and their `mx.*` settings are retired. Saved `?kiosk=1&view=matrix` URLs are a deprecated alias for the reader, and the internal `/api/matrix/lines` and `dashboard.matrix.*` names are deprecated but still supported. Capture and broadcasting stay off by default.
- build(deps): bump ws from 8.21.3 to 8.22.1 in /src/proxy (#16567)
- Fixer queue keys and deferred-fix reconciliation now use the same repository qualification as the review queue, including whitespace trimming and empty-repository handling ([#16571](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/16571)).
- Document why dashboard matrix authentication failures also receive `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- The stage tracker's row tooltip and current-stage line now share one relative-age formatter (#16668)
- `src/docs/env-vars.md` and `src/docs/security-model.md` now describe `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD` as it behaves since [#16785](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/16785): the destination guard covers plain-HTTP forwards, uninspected CONNECT tunnels and transparent-TLS passthrough, and the override lifts it for all three legs at once. The docs previously described the guard and its override as plain-HTTP-only.
- Dashboard: repository org-qualification in `buildReposWithForge` is now expressed once instead of in two duplicated blocks (#16929).
- docs: refresh Codex model snapshot provenance (#16965)
- images: bump claude 2.1.318 -> 2.1.319 (#16970)
- Stage transition dampener: document that `stagelabels.Store`'s dampener history is deliberately in-memory and not persisted with the record; given the short 30-minute window, a process restart only resets suppression, and a reconciler test now covers the suppressed early-return path ([#16978](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16978), [#16981](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16981)).
- The `ioscan` semantic classifier is now on by default at ACMM L4–L6 (off at L1–L3; `ioscan.classifier.enabled` overrides). A new `ioscan.classifier.fail_mode` says what happens when the classifier cannot answer: `open` passes the rule-cleaned text on, `closed` withholds it. Unset, it follows `ioscan.fail_mode`, so it is closed at L5–L6. At L5–L6 a hive with no model endpoint configured withholds untrusted text until one is set or the classifier is turned off; the boot log says so. Cost is one cached model call per untrusted text per pass, documented in `docs/ioscan.md` ([#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- `ioscan` peels more encodings before matching (base64 up to three layers, hex escapes, HTML entities, percent encoding, rot13, hyphen/underscore slugs; reported as `injection.obfuscated`), adds rules for paraphrased overrides, forged system turns, text addressed to the AI, claimed approvals, mass deletion via the API, workflow-secret echo, `authorized_keys` writes, fetch-then-run and force-push over `main`, and records a short quoted mention of an injection phrase at Low instead of withholding it. Red-team corpus grew by 20 attacks and 6 benign controls; block rate 67% → 97%, benign false positives 2 → 1 ([#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- `ioscan`'s red-team corpus now has a committed scorecard baseline (`src/pkg/ioscan/testdata/scorecard_baseline.json`) and a CI ratchet: the attack block rate may only go up and the benign false-positive count may only go down. `go test ./pkg/ioscan/ -run TestScorecardRatchet -v` prints the per-family table ([#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- `ioscan` now applies a per-surface block threshold (`ioscan.block_at`: `issue_body`, `comment`, `pr_body`, `review`). For text by an untrusted author the default moved from High to Medium, so any injection or dangerous-instruction rule that fires withholds the text instead of only recording it; text by the hive's own identities, repo owners and members keeps the High line. Red-team corpus block rate 51% → 67% with no new false positives ([#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- `ioscan` now scans an issue/PR conversation as one unit as well as comment by comment (`ioscan.ScanThread` / `EnforceThread`), so a prompt-injection payload split across two comments is withheld from both halves. The kick path uses it on each PR's review-bot threads, which were previously injected unscanned. A new `injection.bypass_review` rule blocks direct orders to merge or proceed without review. Red-team corpus block rate 42% → 51% with no new false positives ([#6685](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6685)).
- Activity monitor: once a CI or Review chevron reaches a settled verdict (all checks reported / review approved or changes requested) the chevron shows only its icon in green (pass) or red (fail); the former words ("CI 11/11 passed", "Review 5/5 · 1 changes requested", failing check names) move into the chevron tooltip and `aria-label`. In-progress and awaiting-human states keep their text; chevron geometry is unchanged.
- Activity Monitor rows now draw a PR's base-branch pill (`v5`, `main`) right after the repo chip at the head of the row, before the issue number, instead of in the right-hand modifier cluster; the pill names its PR on hover ("PR #N targets v5") and rows with no linked PR show none. ([#16620](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16620))
- Activity Monitor now shows independent CI and Review columns on each PR, preserving current-head required App/check identity, freshness and each reviewer's own completion receipt. Source repair returns visually to PR in progress only with verified successful source-edit evidence; assignments, administrative writes and owner/adoption waits stay explicit without changing native stages or merge authority.
- Contributor PRs the hive adopted in place (`stage/074-adopted-by-hive`) now merge under the hive's own authority: the contributor lane admits the adopted head (`contributor-lane:adopted-by-hive`) without the original author's registry tier, claim marker or GitHub association, once CI, reviewer verdict, DCO, diff fences and soak pass on exactly the head the hive adopted/pushed; a contributor push over it still yields back to 072 and the usual trust gates. Opt out with `governor.labels.stage.adoption.auto_merge: false`.
- Supersede adoption is close-first: the hive closes the contributor's original in the same pass that opens its copy (one note naming the copy and why, `hive/superseded`), so an issue never shows two active PRs; a copy that is closed unmerged or red at two heads reopens the original (`adoption-copy-failed`, at most once per 24h). `governor.labels.stage.adoption.supersede.close_first: false` keeps the original open until the copy merges (#15135).
- Agent-runtime configuration (`agents`, `backends`, `providers`, `tool_approval`, `agent_sandbox`, `turn` and the governor-nested watchdog / engine / gateway / trajectory / rotation blocks) is now grouped in Go under `config.AgentRuntimeConfig` and `config.AgentRuntimeGovernorConfig` (inlined, so `hive.yaml` is unchanged) as the first Crux boundary (#13536).
- `src/docs/api-reference.md` is now an index over per-area pages in `src/docs/api-reference/<area>.md` (health/status, snapshots, auth, configuration, agents and controls, packs and ACMM, cost, knowledge, contribute, nous, inception, beads, dashboard misc, hub SaaS, hub server), so a route change touches one small page instead of one 760-line table and PRs stop conflicting on it ([#15299](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15299)). `check-api-reference-citations.sh` walks the index and every area page by default (a file or directory may still be passed) and `--fix` rewrites only the page whose citations drifted; existing `api-reference.md#<section>` anchors still resolve.
- Docs: `github.app_signed_commits` now has an operator-reference row (default off, App-only, what it rewrites, fallbacks, Settings location) and the level-6 checklist and `github-app-setup.md` point at its dashboard switch (Settings → Forge App → "Re-author agent PRs as GitHub-signed commits") instead of calling it YAML-only.
- Raise the dedicated LKE CI runner ceiling to 140 to relieve queued checks while preserving existing runner resources and the four-runner minimum.
- Codex model fallback refreshed to the 0.165.0 catalog: `gpt-6.1-sol` (the CLI's current default) and the new `gpt-6.1-terra` appear in the dashboard's codex model picker when the live `codex app-server` probe cannot run, instead of the stale 0.159.0 snapshot that lacked both
- `hivectl hives web` now looks like the Hive dashboard (🐝 header, amber eyebrow, dashboard dark/light palette, amber primary button) and the contribution tree works like a file manager: `↑ ↓` move, `←`/`→` collapse/expand or jump to parent/child, `Space` selects, `Enter` expands, `*` expands everything below, typing jumps to a name, and an info panel in the sticky bar describes whatever row is focused or hovered. Each hub and Hive gains a tick-down "Accept all new repositories" box (a hub's box sets it on every restricted Hive under it, with a mixed state) and an "Accept N new" button for repositories already waiting.
- `hivectl hives web` is simpler: the "contribution tree" is now just "What you contribute to", a one-sentence intro (glossary and keys folded into "Help & keyboard"), short row text such as "3 of 12 on · 9 new" instead of three clauses of status, repositories as a plain checkbox with a "New"/"Excluded" badge, secondary actions (Pause, Deselect all, Exclude, Add) shown only on the active row, a one-line "Your changes" summary and a four-line plain-language save receipt, with "Manage Hives" collapsed. On a 6-Hive, 72-repository list that is about 40% fewer words on the first screen (516 to 296) and a page less than half as tall (8,080 px to 3,519 px).
- Contributor-lane auto-promotion now counts an author's clean merged PRs across every repository the hive manages (`auto_merge.contributor_lane.auto_promotion_scope: hive`, the default; `repo` restores the per-repository count), so a contributor trusted in the main repo is admitted on their first PR to a satellite repo; the audit marker and admission log carry the scope and a per-repo breakdown (#14517).
- chore(crux): extract backend resume-handle logic into agent/resumehandle (hivecommons/crux#89)
- chore(crux): extract the copilot token store into agent/copilottoken (hivecommons/crux#90)

- crux: `BreakerTrigger`, `PauseCausation` and `PauseTransitionEvent` are defined in the `crux` root (aliased by `crux/agent`) and `cmd/hive` names `ProjectContext` and `DefaultAgentMode` as `crux.<Name>`; the inbound boundary ratchet's `cmd/hive` row drops 22 → 12, and what remains is the in-process manager and its host wiring (refs #14138).
- `docs/design/crux.md`: Stage 2 prerequisite 1 (the `pkg/crux/config` leaf) recorded as done with the final outbound edge table, and prerequisite 2 (the `effects` / `gitidentity` / `outputschema` / `jev` / `fleetreport` / `pushbroker` edges out of `pkg/agent`) scoped with per-edge symbol counts and the shape of each cut. Docs only.
- Added the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/config` leaf holding the agent runtime's configuration types (`AgentConfig`, `AgentRuntimeConfig`, gateway/LiteLLM/sandbox/watchdog types and their defaults); `pkg/config` now aliases them, so `hive.yaml` loading and every key position are unchanged ([#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536)).
- `pkg/agent`, `pkg/crux` and `pkg/crux/cli` now import the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/config` leaf instead of `pkg/config`; the gateway resolution helpers moved onto `AgentRuntimeGovernorConfig` (still reachable through `GovernorConfig`), the `crux` CLI reads `hive.yaml` and definition files through an injected `cli.DefinitionLoader` that `cmd/crux` supplies, and the Crux outbound ratchet no longer lists `config` for those three packages.
- `pkg/inference`, `pkg/proxy`, `pkg/toolapprove` and `pkg/watchdog` now import the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/config` leaf instead of `pkg/config`, so no Crux ring package depends on Hive's loader. The inference route and gateway resolvers take `*config.AgentRuntimeGovernorConfig`; `toolapprove.DeskFromConfig` takes the `ToolApprovalConfig` block and reaches the ACMM-pack plan gates through `Desk.SetPlanPolicy`, which `cmd/hive` wires to `config.PlanAutoApproveForLevel` and `PlanningConfig.PlanFromLabelEnabled`; the origin-label vocabulary moved into the leaf (`pkg/config` aliases it). No behaviour change.
- crux: `CanonicalizeCopilotModel` and `BackendRequiresInteractiveAuth` are defined in the `crux` root (aliased by `crux/agent`), so `pkg/dashboard` no longer imports `crux/agent`; the inbound boundary ratchet drops its `pkg/dashboard` row (3 → 0), leaving `cmd/hive` as the only consumer naming `agent.<Symbol>` (refs #13536).
- `src/docs/design/crux.md`: Stage 2 prerequisite 2 recorded as done with the per-edge move/alias/invert table, the outbound baseline after it, the ring package list including `pkg/pushbroker` and `pkg/watsonx`, and prerequisite 3 (proxy and `cmd/crux` edges) scoped with symbol counts (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- `pkg/agent` no longer re-exports the governor-side audit vocabulary (`AuditLeaseStage*`, `AuditArtifactLinkMissing`, `Trailer*`, `ParseTrailers`, `MissingTrailers`, `ResolveCommit`, `ArtifactLinks`, `ArtifactResolver`, `LocalGit`, `CommitMessageReader`, `AuditRecord`, `AuditReader`, `Fields`, `FormatAuditDetail`); it lives in `pkg/agentaudit` and the dashboard references it there directly (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- `crux/lanes` configuration validation now names the failing field and its allowed range, and duration fields accept strings such as `"30s"` or `"5m"` in addition to integer nanoseconds (#16387).
- The Crux agent runtime (`pkg/agent`, `pkg/crux`, `pkg/inference`, `pkg/proxy`, `pkg/sandbox`, `pkg/toolapprove`, `pkg/watchdog`, `pkg/trajectory`, `pkg/pushbroker`, `pkg/watsonx` and the rest of the ring) now lives in the nested Go module `github.com/hivecommons/hive/crux` at `src/crux/`, joined to the root module by `src/go.work`; import paths moved from `github.com/hivecommons/hive/pkg/<name>` to `github.com/hivecommons/hive/crux/<name>` (`pkg/crux` → module root `crux`), the thin hive-side alias packages keep working, and CI, the Dockerfiles and the coverage floors address both modules (`./... ./crux/...` from `src/`). No runtime behaviour change (#13536).
- The Crux runtime surface (`pkg/crux`) now defines its value types — `ProcessState`/`State*`, `KickDispatch`/`KickPhase*`, `KickOutcome`/`KickOutcome*`, `KickLogInfo`, `KickRecord`, `RestartEvent`, `SubAgentModel`, `StartFailureClass`, `TurnLoss`, `TurnInterruption` — in `pkg/crux/types`, with `pkg/agent` aliasing them; `cmd/hive`, the spoke and `loginscan` reference the `crux.` names (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- Crux module API: `crux.Process` is now its own struct (a snapshot `crux/agent` copies out of its internal agent record) instead of an alias of `agent.AgentProcess`, and the `crux` root package no longer imports `crux/agent`. `ProjectContext`, `RingBuffer`, the Copilot-token constants, `GitHubTokenLogin`, `DefaultAgentMode` and `AgentAvailableAtACMMLevel` are defined in `crux`; `crux.FromManager` is now `agent.AsRuntime`, and `SanitizePaneText`, `ClassifyAuthPane`, `AuthPaneState` and `PaneShowsBlockingPrompt` moved to the new `crux/paneclass` leaf. This is the prerequisite for folding `crux/types` into the module root ([#13963](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13963), [#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536)).
- refactor: route Copilot-token and pane-classification helpers through crux ([#13962](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13962))
- Provider-status and backend-auth value types (`ProviderStatus`, `ProviderAgentEvidence`, `RollUpProviderStatus`, `BackendAuthState` and the `BackendAuth*`/`ProviderAuth*`/`Provider*` constants) are now defined on the Crux runtime surface (`pkg/crux`, backed by the leaf package `pkg/crux/types`) and aliased from `pkg/agent`; the hub, spoke and dashboard reference the `crux.` names (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- Crux: the ring's tests use their own `pkg/crux/testutil` helpers instead of `internal/testutil`, so the Crux outbound ratchet baseline is empty in test code too (#13536).
- The dashboard now programs against `crux.Runtime`, the exported agent-runtime surface in `pkg/crux`, instead of `*agent.Manager`; no behaviour changes, and the Crux boundary ratchet for `pkg/dashboard` drops from 68 to 51 distinct `agent.*` references.
- The agent runtime's self-reported error conditions (restart storms, repeated kick failures, stalls, data-disk pressure, GitHub App token-mint failures, CI-poll nudges, watchdog crash loops) now reach the fleet-report tracker through a `ConditionReporter` seam the host wires (`Manager.SetConditionReporter`, `watchdog.WithConditionReporter`); `pushbroker` takes its GitHub App credential as a `TokenScoper` interface and joins the Crux ring with `watsonx`. No behaviour change for hive; part of Crux Stage 2 prerequisite 2 (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- The agent watchdog's credential probe now reads a two-method `UsageProber` slice of the rotation probers (cmd/hive adapts them), and the tool-approval desk scans payload text through a `toolapprove.TextScanner` that `pkg/ioscan` implements and the host installs at init (`SetDefaultTextScanner`); a desk with no text scanner installed fails closed instead of skipping the scan. No behaviour change for hive; part of Crux Stage 2 prerequisite 2 (hivecommons/hive#13536).
- Crux docs: the design page records stage 3 of the sidecar plan (endpoint families, the sidecar client and parity test, callback wiring, `crux agy-turn`) and what stage 4 must do; `crux-serve.md` gains the per-family route table, the Host observer event types and `--hive-callback`; the module README lists `crux/api/client`, `crux/api/callback` and `crux/hivecap`.
- crux: the follow-stream overlap rule shared by the CLI and the serve layer now lives in one `internal/streamtail` package instead of two copies.
- tmux is now invoked outside `pkg/agent` only through the new `pkg/agent/tmux` funnel (`LookPath`, `Command`, `Attach`, `HasSession`); the TUI attach path uses it and the Crux boundary ratchet holds the tmux call-site count at zero elsewhere (RFC #13536).
- Crux Stage 2 prerequisite 2, value-type edges: `pkg/effects` moved whole into the stdlib-only `pkg/crux/effects` (aliased), `pkg/gitidentity` to `pkg/crux/gitidentity`, the Jev environment contract and jev-decide skill to `pkg/crux/jev` (aliased), the agent-report schema and validator to `pkg/crux/outputschema` with the receipt provenance handle as `pkg/crux/types.ProofProvenance` (aliased by `pkg/outputschema` and `pkg/convergence/proof`), and `pkg/jsonextract` to `pkg/crux/jsonextract` (aliased). `pkg/agent` no longer imports `effects`, `gitidentity`, `jev` or `outputschema`, and `pkg/trajectory` imports nothing outside the ring ([#13536](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13536)).
- Dashboard: the Agent Logs pane poll (one `/api/pane/<agent>` request per agent every 5 s, ~180 requests and ~6.5 MB a minute on a 16-agent hive) now runs only while the Logs section is visible and the tab is in the foreground, asks the server for just the lines the "all agents" view shows, and refetches once when the section is expanded or the tab returns. Activity monitor `stage-tracker` SSE nudges (one per status publish and per webhook delivery, ~36 a minute on a busy hive) are coalesced to at most one refetch per 2 s and deferred while the tab is hidden.
- The spoke dashboard's `static/index.html` is now generated from per-area sources in `src/pkg/dashboard/static-src/` (CSS, JS and HTML split by dashboard area, concatenated byte-for-byte per `manifest.txt` by `make dashboard-gen`). Served bytes are unchanged; `TestIndexHTMLIsGenerated` fails when the artifact and its sources drift, so PRs touch the area they change instead of one 60k-line file and stop conflicting with each other.
- Moved the DCO provider-unavailable runbook to `src/docs/operator-reference/` and named its policy-message literals; admission behavior is unchanged ([#16404](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16404)).
- Destination-merge guard now shares one claims/dependency-evidence helper in the automerge readiness checks and creates its state directory and lock files owner-only (#16054, #16055).
- Fleet self-reporting no longer files standalone `Fleet report: … hive-code defect` issues ([#13470](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13470)). Those were synthesised from bare dashboard counters (`StallNudges`, `Restarts`, `CIPollNudges`) with no identity, owners, spoke link or diagnostics, and nobody could act on them (hivecommons/hive#13465; 12 of 18 in two weeks were closed by the bot itself). The conditions are now `runtime-error` self-report classes — `agent_stall` (≥3 consecutive unrecovered "continue" nudges, with last-kick time and frozen-pane hash), `agent_crash_loop` (the watchdog's crash-loop latch, acting mode only) and `ci_poll_nudge` (one per 24h window) — observed by the agent manager and watchdog at the moment they happen, with a scrubbed pane tail as diagnostics. Every remaining report (`acmm-shortfall` included) now carries the hive name, spoke link, owners, repos and `Affected hives` block and uses the self-report label set; an ACMM shortfall about a component this hive already has an open self-report for posts a short roll-up comment on that issue instead of filing its own. The hub relay's label-rejection retry falls back to the core self-report labels, never to none.
- The advisory issue lookup reads the ForgeState cache when a store is bound (`forgestate.enabled`): a memoized advisory issue costs zero GitHub calls on a healthy cycle, a cache miss one targeted GET, and the search/list path runs only when the cache cannot answer. The review-request watcher is event-driven: request-dir notifications and `issue_comment`/`pull_request_review`/`pull_request_review_comment`/`issues` label deliveries wake it, the unprompted scan is a 5-minute reconcile while webhooks are healthy, and the 10 s poll returns only when webhooks are degraded. A `--revise` request for a repo outside `review.revise_repos` is denied once instead of retried every tick (#13252).
- The automerge sweep lanes (self-authored, trusted-author, contributor lane) share one cached open-PR set from the ForgeState cache and run event-driven when `forgestate.enabled` is on ([#13377](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13377), part of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)): no `/pulls` list per 10 s tick, a `check_suite`/`check_run`/`status`/`pull_request_review`/`pull_request` webhook triggers a pass for the affected PR only, a 5-minute floor pass covers the no-events case, and every merge first re-reads the PR through the cache with a 60 s freshness bound; a stale snapshot never merges. Review gate, required checks and hold labels are unchanged, and the legacy listing ticker remains the default.
- Overview open issue / PR totals are read from the ForgeState cache (`pkg/forgestate`) when it is ready, and the merged-PR / closed-issue counts behind cost-per-PR and cost-per-issue are incremented from `pull_request closed` (merged) and `issues closed` webhook events and reconciled against GitHub search once an hour (`forgestate.CountsReconcileInterval`) instead of on every 5-minute collection ([#13376](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13376), Phase 2b of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)). A rate-limited or failed reconcile keeps the last good counts: `/api/status` carries `staleSince` and per-repo `countsStale` / `countsStaleSince`, `/api/cost` carries `count_stale_since` / `count_source`, and the Overview tiles and cost labels show "stale since <t>" rather than zeros.
- With `forgestate.enabled: true` the governor work source reads each repo's open issues and PRs from the per-repo ForgeState cache instead of listing GitHub every cycle ([#13375](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13375), Phase 2a of [#13373](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13373)): the cache's reconcile is the only full list, webhook wakes decide from the cached snapshot without a list call, the first decision pass waits for the first successful reconcile of every repo, a repo whose reconcile failed is served last-good and marked stale, every kick ref is held to the same 60 s freshness bound as close/merge (one targeted `GET` when older, withheld when stale), and the hive's own label, close and merge writes plus webhook/confirmation single-item reads are fed straight into the cache.
- The sentinel now evaluates a PR as soon as a `pull_request` opened/synchronize/reopened webhook names it (reading only that PR and its files), and its full sweep is a 15-minute reconcile cadence that enumerates open PRs from the ForgeState cache instead of listing each repo. The GitHub Projects v2 work source lists its board on the same reconcile cadence rather than every eval cycle and applies `projects_v2_item` webhook deliveries as targeted patches; the spoke webhook receiver accepts and routes that event (#13379).
- hive-hosted-matrix stream overlay opens the dashboard with `view=reader` instead of the deprecated `view=matrix` alias (#16612).
- Activity Monitor: the muted pill a PR wears while the hive's GitHub App is missing a permission now reads "hive bot lacks permission" instead of "unauthorized", and its tooltip, the row hover line, the Needs-attention chip title, the needs-human tip, the human-merge gate word and the decision popover say the same — nobody did anything illegitimate, the App installation lacks one permission (hivecommons/hive#16639). The `hive:unauthorized` label, comment marker and API fields are unchanged.
- Hive-authored superseding PRs (`Supersedes #N`, opened by the hive App) now auto-merge with no operator decision: a reviewer `requires_human` — security-sensitive included — is routed to the fixer instead of parking at `stage/085`, and only an unacknowledged sentinel finding, a hold, exhausted fix attempts, red CI after fixes or an unresolvable base conflict park it, each named in the 085 caption. New knob `auto_merge.hive_superseding.auto_merge` (default `true`).
- The hub's GitHub webhook relay now fans out to every enrolled hive that tracks the delivery's repository (and has a dashboard URL) instead of only the first match, so additional hives on the same repo no longer fall back to polling. One log line is emitted per relay target; hives without a dashboard URL are skipped and counted. (#13202)
- Hive activity monitor: every `090 Ready for human merge` row and its tooltip now say why a person must merge (`· workflow files`, `· untrusted author`, `· branch protection`, `· auto-merge off`, `· unauthorized`, … falling back to `· policy`), derived from the stage record's lane reason; nested PR sub-rows and the needs-attention headline carry the same (#14658)
- Refreshed the CA trust bundle in the spoke, contributor, hub, CI-runner and OSS-scanner images: two Mozilla roots withdrawn by the root programs (emSign ECC Root CA - G3, Comodo AAA Services root) are now distrusted at build time, and Node-based CLIs in the spoke and contributor images verify against the system store via `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca`. The image build now asserts the test chains are rejected.
- Issue-side comment churn is cut by editing in place instead of re-posting ([#16433](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16433)): `hive:claim` / `hive:release` transitions now maintain one per-issue claim-ledger comment (`<!-- hive:issue-claim-ledger -->`, current state plus the last 8 transitions; `github.notifications.claim_ledger`, default on, `false` restores one comment per transition) that every existing claim reader still parses; a PR re-entering a needs-decision stage has its entry comment rewritten with an `Updated <ts>` line; a new push rewrites the hive's existing `hive-sentinel` comment for the new head; and in quiet mode a reviewer-lane review that narrates "no findings" with an approving, finding-free verdict is recorded and folded into the `hive:status` comment instead of being submitted as a review.
- ACMM L6 is now labelled **Autonomous** rather than "Fully Autonomous" everywhere operators see it — the dashboard header pill (`L6 · Autonomous`), the maturity-level dialog, the hub's level picker and ACMM pages, the `level-6` pack name, advisor criteria text, the tool-approval desk rationale, and the docs. L6 still parks items for human decisions, honours `hold`, cannot grant secrets, org membership, or workflow pushes, and keeps an owner in the loop, so "fully" overstated what the level does. The ladder is otherwise unchanged (L1 Inception → L5 Semi-Autonomous → L6 Autonomous); the numeric `acmm_level: 6` config value and the pack filename `level-6.yaml` are untouched, so no configuration changes are needed.
- `src/docs/landscape.md` is refreshed against the compared projects' current public docs (dated 2026-10-23), gains **New since August 2026**, **Agent isolation** and **Work sources** sections, and joins the fixed file list of `src/scripts/check-security-docs-readability.sh`, so the positioning page must also stay at Flesch-Kincaid grade 11 or below.
- Lane policies now check for an existing gate or written policy before filing a finding class, and propose the missing gate instead of filing a third same-class finding ([#13427](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13427), [#13428](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13428)).
- Tracker 090 *Ready for human merge*: the lead action is now **Approve and let hive merge** (`queue-merge`) — hive merges on its next tick once CI is green, soak and self-merge ban apply; **Merge now as maintainer** (`merge-now`, and its *Rebase, then merge as maintainer* variant) is secondary. The automerge sweep now honours an operator's recorded queue-merge approval on an untrusted-author PR and attributes the merge to that operator.
