- On a PR the hive did not author, the security review's `requires_human` now stays a hold for a person (`stage/085-needs-decision`, with the finding named) when another perspective also asks for changes. Before, the sibling `changes_requested` folded the security hold into the fix cycle and the PR went back to its author at `stage/072-returned-to-contributor`, although a security finding is the contributor rule's one early exit to a person ([#15640](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15640)). projectbluefin/utah-packages#890 was sent to its author for a PR-body edit while the security review's question about a new App credential waited on a maintainer.
- Activity Monitor bulk “Let hive decide” now works when a multi-PR parent issue is selected, confirming and deciding each open PR once even when its sub-rows are also selected ([#15061](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15061)).
- A spoke whose self-upgrade `PATCH` on its own Deployment is rejected or timed out by a cluster admission webhook (a failing Kyverno webhook on vllm-d blocked every patch) no longer reports the upgrade as **failed** when a plain restart will land it anyway. The patch deadline is raised from 10s to 45s (above the 10s webhook default, so the apiserver can return the real webhook error) and retried once; when the patch still fails and the Deployment tracks a floating tag that the kubelet re-pulls (`imagePullPolicy: Always` or unknown), the spoke exits immediately with a distinct exit code and reports **pending-restart**, so the hub keeps the in-flight latch instead of counting a failed attempt. The hub's stuck-upgrade alert and the orphan-sweep give-up message now carry the spoke's classified cause ("cluster admission webhook (e.g. Kyverno) is rejecting or timing out Deployment patches — a cluster admin must fix or exempt the webhook") instead of the misleading "Deployment tracks a floating tag" guess ([#14385](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14385)).
- The hub no longer re-requests a channel commit date from GitHub on every render after a failed lookup (e.g. HTTP 403 rate limit); it backs off for 10 minutes per commit, so rate-limited hubs stop repeating the "channel commit date: fetch failed" warning.
- The `ci_poll_nudge` self-report now lists the repeated CI-status commands (with counts) in its diagnostics, so the fleet issue is triageable instead of showing only an idle pane summary (#14289).
- Classify the login-required, ioscan classifier fail-closed and startup-kick-dropped WARNs as named fleet-report classes instead of `unclassified_error_repeated` (#14262, #14263, #14266)
- Classify transient GitHub-fetch, label-provisioning and agent-CLI restart-loop WARNs as named fleet-report classes (`github_fetch_transient`, `label_provisioning_failed`, `agent_cli_restart_loop`), report `ioscan_classifier_unavailable` on first observation, and tighten the `agent_pane_timeout` keywords (#14258, #14259, #14260, #14277, #14278, #14286)
- Recurring agent-runtime log lines no longer land in the self-report feed as "unclassified". Self-healing noise (cached GitHub 404s, rate-limited Copilot token validation, permissions repairs) is ignored, while tmux, proxy TLS handshake, per-agent directory setup and review-evidence write failures and feedback issue-refresh failures now report under their own named classes.
- The watchdog's `agent credential failure` log line is now reported under the existing `agent_login_required` selfreport class instead of `unclassified_error_repeated`, so owners are pointed at re-authenticating the agent backend rather than a generic defect report ([#16861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16861)).
- Repeated lane-gate and trusted-author sweep warnings caused by a transient GitHub 500 on the status read are no longer filed as selfreport issues (#15785, #15786); a hub heartbeat rejected with a restarting-hub 502/503/504 is likewise classified as transient (#15789)
- Fleet selfreports no longer file an unclassified-runtime-error issue when the request pacer refuses a request because its slot would miss the caller's deadline; the WARN stays in local logs (#15109).
- Fleet selfreports no longer file an unclassified-runtime-error issue per caller when GitHub rate limiting or the hive's own request pacing makes many callers log the same transient failure; the WARNs stay in local logs (#15106).
- Self-reports no longer loop between a spoke and whoever closes them: a runtime-error fingerprint names the defect (class + normalised message) instead of the build, a fingerprint closed upstream is not re-filed by the same hive while it keeps observing the condition (the 7-day cooldown now runs from the last observation, on the direct path and through the hub relay), "Cleared on" comments are paced to once per hive per 24h and withheld under a closed issue, and the catch-all `unclassified_error_repeated` class joins only issues whose title matches the message rather than any open issue of that class.
- The fleet self-report no longer files an unclassified-error issue when the review-request watcher suppresses a duplicate review comment under the per-head cap (#15906).
- Avoid filing repeated-error fleet reports for sentinel skips caused by GitHub pacing, while retaining the local warnings and reporting other failures.
- Sentinel: a dashboard Approve on a flagged PR is now remembered as the release of that head — the sweep reads the hive's own `hive:pr-approval head=<sha>` comment instead of treating the hive-account `unlabeled` event as nobody's clearance, so it no longer re-posts the alert and re-applies `sentinel-alert` to the head the owner just approved (dibs#510, hivecommons/hive#15214); a new push still re-arms. On a Prow repo where the bot is not an approver, a later Approve records the decision without re-posting `/lgtm` + `/approve` and reports `commands_skipped`.
- Surface shared-CI recovery permission refusals as an actionable operator handoff, retry after the permission cooldown even on unchanged PRs, and align bot-PR squash attribution with the existing required check.
- Sidebar count pills (Overview `40/18`, Governor `4/12`, Projects, Hive activity monitor, Knowledge, Contributors) now share one right edge. The hover-revealed hide toggle (⊘) is appended after the pill on every hideable row and held an invisible 20px slot there, so those pills sat ~26px left of Overview's (the one row that cannot be hidden). The pill is now always the last flex child; the toggle fades in between label and pill on hover, so nothing shifts.
- Dashboard sidebar: the Overview counter (`33/13`, open issues / open PRs) and the Hive activity monitor counter (`37`, rows) count the same open set two ways — every open issue is a row, a PR is its own row only when not drawn under a listed issue. Both tooltips and the activity-monitor header now say so (`37 rows (33 issues + 4 PRs on their own row) · 9 PRs shown on their issue's row`), so the numbers read as one population, not a disagreement.
- Spoke dashboard: clicking a left-sidebar item now keeps the chosen section pinned at the top of the viewport while late renders (status poll/SSE repaints, lazy panels, collapsing sections) shift the layout above it, instead of scrolling away and needing a second click. The hold re-anchors on layout drift for 2.5 s and releases on any wheel/touch/key input; render-time scroll anchoring pins the navigated section rather than the neighbour peeking under the sticky navbar.
- A signed-commit reconciler compare that hits a 404 (missing head branch or invisible repository) is now classified as a persistent GitHub refusal, so it is counted, bounded and noted once instead of being retried uncounted every pass ([#16202](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16202)).
- Activity Monitor: a row parked on a policy sign-off ask (e.g. a fork's workflow change) now says "Review 5/5 · needs your sign-off" / "needs owner sign-off" instead of "awaiting human decision", leads with an inline "Approve ▸" when CI is green (then "Let hive decide ▸"), and no longer captions "Recommendation recorded" when hive kept the park without recording a recommendation.
- Hive no longer supersedes its own PRs for a missing sign-off: the automerge DCO stage treats commits on a PR by hive's `ai_author` or App login as self-squash (so an App-signed commit no longer counts as squash-unsafe), `signoff-rehome` keeps hive-authored and operator-approved heads in place instead of re-authoring them as a new PR, the App's signed re-author commit always carries a `Signed-off-by` trailer, and the push relay refuses a hive-identity commit that lacks one.
- Activity Monitor: a tracker row (issue row or PR sub-row) now renders at most one hive note line. The needs-human / decision ask outranks the blocker, next-move and stage-transition notes; a lower note's facts ride the winning line as a trailing clause only when they say something the row does not already (a "moved to Needs human decision" note under a strip already lit at Needs human decision is dropped). The single line keeps its ⬡ icon, View link and one relative age ([#16627](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16627)).
- `skillreg.SpecServesRepo` no longer treats differently-owned org-qualified repo references as the same repo ([#16168](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16168)): a spec scoped to `laredo/cuga-agent` now correctly refuses to serve `acme/cuga-agent`, while bare↔qualified matching remains (bare `cuga-agent` still matches qualified `laredo/cuga-agent`).
- The scanner, issue-request watcher and `/contribute` relay lane no longer dispatch an issue an open pull request already fixes: a live open-PR check (`scanner.skip_issues_with_open_pr`, default on) skips the claim, labels the issue `has-open-pr` and logs `claim skipped: open PR already linked`; and a duplicate-fix sweep resolves two open PRs fixing one issue without an owner decision — the earlier green/pending PR stays, the later hive PR is closed as `duplicate-of:<keeper>` with one comment, a person's later PR is commented on and left open, and only an earlier red/stale PR facing a later green one is escalated to `stage/085` ([#14799](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14799)).
- List all 61 SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria in the compliance profile, with explicit not-covered rationales and mappings for monitoring, protected credential movement, and encrypted backups. The A1.2 backup mapping reports the effective key source (governor key_file, default Secret/PVC mounts, or the HIVE_BACKUP_KEY fallback) rather than the raw key_file path.
- `GET /api/hub/release/stable-promotion` no longer mixes a fresh stable SHA with the digest and commit date of the previous stable build, and reports the stable commit time as `built_at` (it was published as `promoted_at`, which misread a commit time as the tag's promotion time).
- `stage/030-pr-in-progress` now requires PR evidence. A hive-agent issue claim used to derive 030 on its own (claimswire `claimFactFor`, the `claim` issue request, and the live `hive:claim` marker on enumeration), so an issue the scanner claimed while triaging wore "PR in progress" with no PR or branch to show (hivecommons/hive#13069). Claims — agent, human, contributor, external — now derive `stage/020-claimed`; 030 is written only when the claim carries `PRStarted` (a `hive-open-pr --issues` request or a `<!-- hive:start branch=… -->` / `pr=…` marker), recorded on the ledger and the claim marker as `pr_started=true` so the sweep re-derives the same stage. Legacy `IssueStageFor` and the stage-engine adapter changed together (shadow mismatch gate stays 0); goldens regenerated with `pr_started` variants and three #13069 regression cases.
- The expected-transition table and pipeline diagram now draw `020-claimed → 010-actionable` and `030-pr-in-progress → 010-actionable` (claim released or expired) plus `020 → 040`, so claim expiry is no longer a `stage_transition_anomaly`.
- Stage engine (shadow): the PR deriver now reproduces the stage the automerge pass writes, not only `resolveStage`'s opinion — the pass hands it its post-step inputs (`PRPassFacts`: detected author kind, prior record, human-route evidence, DCO walk, adoption state) and `DerivePR` applies the same 07x split, normalized-fixing guard, `RouteHuman`, DCO override and 074 yield. Human hand-offs the route refined to 071/072 (red checks, conflicts) or 050 (no verdict for the head yet) were counted as `085` mismatches on every pass and kept the 48 h shadow gate from ever reading zero; a goldens parity test now derives all 8 231 fixtures through the engine.
- The stage pipeline diagram and the engine's expected-transition table now draw `071-needs-author ↔ 050-review-pending` (the human twin of the 072 edges), so a human author pushing a fresh head no longer counts as a `stage_transition_anomaly`.
- The stage-label reconciler now warns once per PR head and refusal reason when the write-back gate refuses reopening a hive-closed superseded PR, instead of on every tick.
- Make review-verdict normalization independent of the previous PR stage and suppress same-head stage reversals for 15 minutes at the reconciler write boundary, preventing idle PRs from repeatedly restarting label-triggered CI ([#16880](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16880)).
- An issue with both a live agent claim and an open hive PR that fixes it now stays at stage/040-covered-by-pr: the eval sweep runs the duplicate-PR guard before the live-claim filter, so the claim no longer re-buckets the issue "claimed" (020) every cycle after its PR opens and the dashboard stage tracker no longer shows a spurious `regressed` chip on nearly every claimed issue.
- The stage tracker now surfaces an Actionable issue the scheduler withholds for an open GitHub "blocked by" dependency: the row wears the `blocked` modifier, the chip and tooltip name the blocker(s), the payload carries `blocked_on`, and the caption reads "waiting on #N" instead of plain "waiting for the scanner" — sequenced RFC sub-issues no longer look like intake starvation (hivecommons/hive#14765).
- Stage tracker *Let hive decide* now opens its preview at once as a skeleton (Cancel enabled, the action disabled until the plan lands, errors inline with Retry, no double-fire), prefetches the plan when a row's decision options are revealed and serves it from a 45 s bounded server cache with a `Server-Timing` header; covered issue rows read "Covered by PR #N — waiting for a decision on the PR" with a chip that scrolls to the PR's row, and every 👤 next move carries a short `human_reason` after its chevron word ([#15773](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15773)).
- Stage tracker: Let hive decide now shows the hive is working at once, covered issues no longer repeat their PR's button, and a person's move says why (#15773)
- Activity tracker: the "updated … ago" chip now reports when its 30s poll is failing (`poll failing (HTTP 504)` / `(unreachable)`), goes amber at once and demotes `fresh` to `cache`, instead of counting up "updated 8m ago · fresh" from the last good payload while the server is unreachable (#14416).
- Dashboard: the Hive activity monitor's ▶ Play / ▶ Play both sound previews were silent in Safari and Chrome because the play checked `AudioContext.state` synchronously right after an un-awaited `resume()`; previews now create and resume the context inside the click, wait for it to come up (handling Safari's `interrupted` state), show "Playing…" on the button and toast when the browser blocks audio, while automatic merge/open plays resume briefly without bursting and re-arm gesture priming until a resume actually succeeds.
- Activity Monitor: the row event line no longer says "fell back to" for forward moves whose stage number happens to decrease — triage accepted (015 → 010), a decision made (085 → 080), the author resuming (072 → 070). The stage table now carries `falls_to` from the stage engine's regression rule, and only those hops read as a fall.
- Stage writer no longer removes Prow's `dco-signoff: yes|no` labels; it only reconciles its own `dco` / `no-dco` pair, ending the remove/re-add label war with Prow on every open PR (#13125).
- Issue stage sweep writes `stage/040-covered-by-pr` again for issues an open PR covers: the second in-cycle `annotateIssueWithClaim` pass no longer re-grades the hive's synthesised covered label as GitHub's, which had left issues with an open `Fixes #N` PR stuck at 010 (#14397).
- stagelabels: Owned and Plan now match existing stage labels case-insensitively, consistent with Current (#13909)
- Issue claims held by a hive agent are released the moment that agent's CLI is relaunched (hive boot, restart), with a `hive:release` marker comment that claim readers now honour, so an issue no longer sits at `stage/020-claimed` for the full agent TTL after a rollout. Rate-limit relaunches of Copilot agents are also spaced across the fleet (one per 30s) instead of all agents re-validating the same exhausted token budget together.
- Parked issues no longer show "Needs human decision" after a maintainer has acted: the un-park sweep honours a maintainer's `/fixed` (alias `/close`) on a parked issue — closing it as completed, clearing `needs-human` and the stage labels, and posting one acknowledgement ([dibs#459](https://github.com/hivecommons/dibs/issues/459)); `/hive approve` and `/hive decision` lift `needs-human` whoever applied it, with the reply naming who had, while `hold` stays untouched ([docs#419](https://github.com/hivecommons/docs/issues/419)); a new closed-issue sweep strips `stage/*` and a Hive-added `needs-human` from issues that closed wearing them ([homebrew-hive#127](https://github.com/hivecommons/homebrew-hive/issues/127)); and the dashboard tracker drops closed issues and reads the needs-decision state from the issue's current labels rather than a stale store record.
- Demote the stale status snapshot drop to Info; warn only after repeated consecutive drops (#14117)
- Classify repeated startup kicks dropped during an agent restart or stop as `startup_kick_interrupted` instead of an unclassified runtime error.
- Agent status, triage, verification and gate-check comments and every relay `label` request no longer count as a start signal, so they no longer record an agent claim or stage the issue `stage/030-pr-in-progress`; a comment starts work only with `<!-- hive:start -->`, a "starting now"-style phrase or an opening "Starting …"/"Implementing …". Claim admission (every producer) now also refuses issues parked on a person (`stage/045-needs-decision`, `needs-spec`, …) and umbrella issues labelled `epic` (new `governor.claims.never_claim_labels`, default `[epic]`), and the stage engine never derives `stage/020`/`stage/030` from a claim on an epic. The Settings dialog (Features → Issue claims) gains a “Never-claim labels” control for `governor.claims.never_claim_labels`.
- The dashboard status snapshot is now published before the governor's serial kick dispatch as well as after it, so `/api/status` (and the stage tracker, agent states and `governor.nextKickAt` derived from it) reflects an evaluation within seconds instead of after every due kick has been delivered — a phase that took 10–15 minutes on hosted hives and, when a rolling upgrade landed mid-dispatch, meant the evaluation never reached the dashboard at all. Snapshots the stale-build guard refuses are now logged at Warn and counted in a new `statusStaleDrops` field on `/api/status`.
- The Twitch matrix streamer no longer drops frames on every encoder hiccup: `VIDEO_QUEUE_FRAMES` defaults to 256, the audio queue is configurable (`AUDIO_QUEUE`), x11grab uses wallclock timestamps with `aresample=async=1` so audio/video PTS cannot drift, and a stall watchdog restarts ffmpeg when frames stop for 30 s or `speed` stays below 0.90x for 60 s, publishing its samples to `/run/stream/health.json`; the README gains a "Why does the player buffer?" diagnosis recipe.
- Twitch streamer (`src/deploy/stream`): no longer OOMKilled in a loop when the x264 encoder falls behind — the x11grab input queue is bounded (`VIDEO_QUEUE_FRAMES`, 16 raw frames instead of 1024, which could pin 8.5 GiB of MIT-SHM frames shared with Xvfb), x264 threads follow the cgroup CPU quota instead of `nproc`, Chromium runs with `--disable-dev-shm-usage --renderer-process-limit=1 --disable-extensions --js-flags=--max-old-space-size=1024`, the supervisor reloads the tab when Chromium's RSS passes `CHROMIUM_RSS_RELOAD_MIB`, and the Deployment requests 1 CPU / 3 Gi and limits 3 CPU / 6 Gi
- Twitch streamer self-heals: a watchdog asks Twitch whether the channel is live and restarts ffmpeg (then the pod) when ingest drops silently; probes now follow the watchdog heartbeat and tolerate Twitch's post-drop key lock.
- "Let hive decide" now tells the owner when a recorded decision never took effect and what to do about it: past `decisions.delegate.effect_timeout` (default 30m) a repeat click answers "Hive decided <plain action> at <time>, but it hasn't taken effect: <plain why>" with Merge as maintainer / Re-run decision / Close as superseded / Send back for a new commit as buttons, and the hive posts one plain-words follow-up on the item; every rule, verdict and reason is rendered from one glossary (Go + dashboard mirror) so slugs like `contributor-offline` or "supersede" are never shown bare; the delegate's `/hive decision` comment carries "Hive decided / Why / What happens next / If it doesn't happen"; and a decision comment the hive itself posted is never parsed as a reviewer's change request — the self-blocking seen on [#14822](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/14822).
- Delegated "supersede now" adoption decisions on trusted-bot PRs (`github-actions` and friends, observed on the self-authored lane) are executed instead of silently skipped every sweep with the `adoption/supersede` label left in place (hivecommons/docs#500 waited 15h); the supersede replays a conflicting head onto a fresh base first and, when that replay conflicts, posts one note naming the failure, consumes the request and keeps the PR on its fixing stage with reason `supersede-conflict`, and a request on the hive's own PR is refused once with a note rather than looping.
- Review aggregation no longer routes a hive-superseding PR to the fixer when every perspective's `requires_human` is a pure approver question with nothing above an informational finding. That route dispatched no-op fix kicks until the cycle was exhausted, then re-authored the same change (#16398 → #16456 → #16607) while the approver the reviewer asked never saw a decision. Such a head keeps its decision question, parks at `stage/085-needs-decision` with approve / request-changes actions, and the tracker's review chevron reads "waiting on a human approver · reviewer verified, needs sign-off".
- The dashboard's `/terminal` proxy now presents ttyd's basic-auth credential (`HIVE_TTYD_CREDENTIAL`, else `hive:<HIVE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN>` — the entrypoint's precedence) on every forwarded request, including the websocket upgrade, and drops any browser-supplied `Authorization` instead of relaying it. On token-protected spokes the already-authenticated browser was re-challenged by ttyd with a native user/password dialog after the dashboard had admitted it; the Node proxy's `/terminal` route is fixed the same way (#14693).
- Deflaked `test-issue-confirm-fixed.sh`: the DRY_RUN assertion piped `printf` into `grep -q`, which raced SIGPIPE under `pipefail` and intermittently failed `build-and-test`. (#16151)
- Fixed the tool-approval scan lane skipping its guardrail-path check for write tools it did not recognise by name ([#16976](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16976)): `create`, `apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor`, `multi_edit`, `write_file` and any agent-specific editor tool writing `.github/workflows/**`, `OWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `hive.yaml`, `policies/**`, `proxy/rules*` or `gh-wrapper*` auto-approved at L5/L6 where `write`/`edit` were denied. The check now holds every tool not classified read-only that names a file — an unrecognised tool name fails closed on those paths, so a read tool `IsReadOnly` does not spell is denied there until it is added (Copilot CLI's `view` is now spelled). `IsLocalWrite` spells the Copilot CLI and Codex editor tools too.
- Dashboard topbar: the ≡ drawer toggle is no longer clipped off the left edge on phones, and on ≤360px-wide screens the 🐛/⚙ chips collapse into the account menu (which gains a Settings entry) instead of overflowing the row.
- The dashboard topbar no longer shows an empty outlined pill between Settings and the health badge when every AI provider is usable: the hidden providers chip (`#oc-providers`) was still painted because the shared `.nav-chip` display rule outranked the `hidden` attribute. The chip now also carries a title/aria-label describing its state.
- The Hive activity monitor now lists every open issue and pull request from its `opened` webhook (with replay and poll fallback) instead of waiting for the governor's next publish, and renders a not-yet-staged item as a `000-new` row in the Open column that says who moves it next — a maintainer's triage label or the hive's stage-label pass — and when the next pass is due (#15094).
- Activity Monitor: while a row action is in flight the lit chevron shows one readable progress caption ("Queuing for merge…") on an opaque plate instead of a faint label over the stripes next to the old stage word (hivecommons/hive#15412).
- Hive Activity Monitor: every lit stage pill now draws its actor icon from a server-derived `stage_actor` (hive ⬡, contributor clanker, human, bot cog, or none with a "no one is working on this right now — why" tooltip) instead of guessing from the author; a bot-authored or unowned red PR reads "Conflicting · bot PR" / "Red · nobody on it" instead of an active "Fixing"; a PR closing several open issues is drawn once (`drawn_under`) with a "↳ #N · under #M" chip on the other issues; and the "Merged today" counter sits directly above the Merge gate / ✓ column header so the merge token's flight ends above the gate.
- Activity monitor row actions now show progress and never fail silently (hivecommons/hive#15436). **Close (read)** on an advisory row did nothing — an advisory is not a decision park, so the `decide:*` target mapping came up empty and the click returned without a request, a dialog or a toast. It now acts on the advisory row itself and really closes the issue (acknowledgement comment, closed as completed); an empty target list toasts a warning instead of returning silently. Every mutating row action (close-read, close-superseded, won't-fix, hold, approve, merge, decide) puts the chevron into the striped busy state with the verb as caption from the first byte sent, shows *Closed · leaving list* / *Merged · leaving list* once the server answers, and the server drops an operator-closed item from the tracker for `HIVE_OPERATOR_CLOSED_GRACE` (default 15m) so the row cannot come back before GitHub's list catches up. A close on an operator-paused repo is refused with the reason and writes nothing; refused, failed and network-errored actions restore the chevron, toast the reason and put it on the row's history badge (red, hover's first line), and the ledger records refused answers as `failed` with the one-line why.
- Describe failing author-owned PRs with unknown work activity instead of inferring that nobody is working from an absent Hive stage actor, including inline and nested PRs while preserving known Hive and bot routing.
- Activity Monitor: no status symbol rotates on a chevron or pill any more — the working glyph, the merge gate's ⟳ sweep glyph and the acting caption's spinner are static icons; their tooltips still say what the hive is doing (#15187).
- Every open issue in the Activity Monitor now offers a permission-checked Close issue action with an in-app confirmation; only the selected issue closes, leaving linked pull requests and other issues unchanged.
- Activity tracker: a follow-up or duplicate PR opened against an issue an earlier merge already delivered now reads `closed by #N` (the merged PR GitHub records as the closer, never an open PR with `Fixes #N`), or `closed · this PR unmerged` when no merged closer is known, instead of a bare `closed` chip that read as if the issue had been closed before its fix merged; docs state the rule that the hive closes an issue only after its PR merges
- A PR or issue closed on GitHub no longer reappears on the Hive activity monitor for minutes after the webhook re-read had already removed it. The eval cycle in flight at the time of the close published its status snapshot from the enumeration it started with (listing the item open), overwriting the webhook patch until the next full enumeration re-listed the repo (pluk#313 came back 4 s after closing and left again ~5 min later; up to `governor.eval_interval_webhook_s` plus a cycle in the worst case). Webhook re-reads are now remembered for `dashboard.stage_tracker.webhook_refresh_replay_window_s` (default `1800`) and re-applied to every status snapshot published meanwhile, monotonic on GitHub's `updated_at` so a later reopen still wins; repo issue / PR totals follow the patched lists, and a closed PR also takes its issues-feed copy with it. Closed items now leave within one dashboard poll.
- A closed issue or PR no longer stays on the Hive activity monitor when the confirming re-read a webhook delivery queues is refused (critical API budget, rate-limit caution window) or fails: the tracker now applies the payload's own `state` on every `issues`, `issue_comment` and `pull_request*` delivery, so a closed or merged item leaves on whichever action arrives (`labeled`, `unlabeled`, a comment — not only `closed`), its eviction is handed to the governor and remembered for replay like a re-read, and an open re-read older than the listed copy can neither rewrite the row nor un-remember a close (hivecommons/hive#14159 and #14064 sat at "Triage needed" / "Needs human decision" twenty minutes after closing, through the close, a bot comment and the stage-label sweep's unlabel). As a backstop for deliveries that never arrived, on each status publish it lists each repo's items closed since its last look every `dashboard.stage_tracker.closed_sweep_interval_s` (default `300`, one list call per repo, negative disables) and evicts any still shown.
- Activity Monitor: a PR the hive closed when it opened its replacement (close-first supersession) no longer renders under its issue as a bare sub-row with an empty ladder; the live replacement PR carries a small "supersedes #N" chip (hover: when it was closed, link) as the only trace, and the issue's ladder follows the live PR alone.
- Tracker Copy link now copies the selected issue or PR's canonical URL, including PRs linked or nested under issues, instead of copying the parent issue link.
- Show verified external merges at Activity Monitor's existing terminal step on root, inline and nested PR rows, using retained models and the actual recorded merger without inventing queue membership, Hive ownership or a second merge event.
- Hive activity monitor: the per-row select checkbox and ⋯ actions gutter is now present on every issue and PR row after every render path and always visible — dimmed at rest, full emphasis on hover/focus, on selected rows, and on all rows while a selection or the context menu is open — instead of a hover-only reveal that left an unpredictable, shifting subset of rows with a visible gutter as the live refresh swapped nodes under a still pointer (follow-up to [#13535](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/13535)).
- Activity Monitor: the right-most tracker column no longer shows a ✓ — the column header, the unmerged cap chevron and the "did I act on this?" badge now wear a history mark (clock with a counter-clockwise arrow); the badge is a neutral pill, carries the count of recorded actions and an aria-label, and keeps its hover history. The green ✓ remains only once a PR has merged.
- Explain exact-head human requirements separately from optional delegation and neutral ownership without inferring human presence, preserve covering-PR reasons and genuine current actions, reconcile old-head push requests and observed same-head CI retries, and keep pending head validation and requested review changes in CI/Review rather than implying approval or preparation admits a ready merge-queue seat.
- Keep informational trusted-author security notices separate from actual sentinel gates in Activity Monitor, quoting the real reviewer question without assigning exclusive decision authority to either the PR author or a person the reviewer mentions.
- Activity Monitor issue messages now follow covering PR progress instead of stale New/scanner captions, including links discovered from the PR side.
- Activity Monitor merge zap fires again: `recently_merged` entries recorded by the PR poller under a repo's short name (`repo=hive`) are now qualified to the `owner/name` the tracker rows carry, so human and observed merges match; a PR that drops off the open list a poll before its `pr_merged` audit entry lands is remembered as open until the entry arrives instead of being missed; a context the autoplay policy still holds suspended re-arms the gesture priming rather than queueing stale voices. New: a short bee-like buzz when an issue or PR first appears on the list (same opt-in chip, once per item, capped per refresh, silent on hidden tabs); turning the chip on plays one zap then one buzz.
- Keep Activity tracker chevrons compact on mobile while preserving their caption and icon alignment.
- Hive activity monitor: stage moves now animate on the live refresh. The hosted hive refreshes the tracker about once a second and the panel was rebuilt wholesale each time, cutting every move off after its opening flash; rows are now reconciled by item key so an in-flight move keeps its node, and rows leaving the list collapse out (`--ham-move-exit-ms`) while new rows fade in (`--ham-move-enter-ms`), both off under None or reduced motion.
- Hive Activity settings: the Movement animation preview no longer stacks a second, mis-sized chevron strip under the sample row; each Preview rebuilds the one sample row in place so it matches live tracker rows.
- Activity Monitor tracker: a human-authored PR waiting on its own author no longer leads with the red "Close as superseded" inline button (a close leads only when the server marks it `lead`, i.e. the reviewer named the superseding PR) and its pill reads "waiting on @author to push"; an issue and its asking nested PR render "Let hive decide" once, on the PR sub-row, instead of twice.
- Hive activity monitor: the `since` age now sits in line with the chevron strip and the status pill (`hold`, `stalled`, `unauthorized`, …) hugs the last title line directly over its own strip, with a hairline between entries and a whole-row hover tint, so a tall row (wrapped title, `↳ #PR` line) no longer floats its pill and age into the gap between two rows (#14640).
- Hive activity monitor: every row that involves a PR now draws the issue on the left and the PR on the right. A PR with no open linked issue shows a muted "no linked issue" (or "linked issue #N closed") placeholder in the issue slot and names itself in the PR column instead of standing in the issue slot with the PR column blank; `/api/stage-tracker` PR items carry `linked_issues` (GitHub's closing references for the PR body's Fixes/Closes/Resolves keywords) and a PR whose open issue is listed is paired with it from the PR side too ([#13421](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13421)).
- Activity tracker ([#15589](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15589)): a merge-queue chevron reads "Merge queued · 1st of 2" (the place with the queue length) and, when more than one train is on the page, names its train — "· train main.go" (the first overlapping file's basename, else the head `#N`) with a hover leading "Train of 2 PRs overlapping main.go; merges after #15567." — so two trains no longer show two unexplained "1st"s; the provisional suffix reads "queued 1st of 2 once ready" the same way, and each train's header and member rows share one left-rail accent colour so trains tell apart at a glance.
- Activity monitor: a PR whose body says `Refs #N` (or `Related to`, `Part of`, `Towards`, `See` …), whose title ends in `(#N, part 1)`, or whose first paragraph mentions an open issue, now sits on that issue's row under a muted `refs` chip instead of showing "no linked issue"; closing links still win and are drawn unchanged.
- Activity Monitor: a PR or issue by a registered contributor-hub clanker owner now reads as a clanker (author_kind_source `registry`) instead of an inferred person, so the row icon, its tooltip and the stage pill's holder ("@login's clanker") agree with the stage engine that adopts such PRs.
- An issue an open PR already covers (040) no longer falls to 020/010 — and books a spurious **regressed** badge on the activity monitor — when a contributor claims it, the claim is released, or a start mark lands between sweeps: the out-of-cycle stage-fact path now re-reads the remembered covering PR and keeps 040 while it is open. The `regressed` pill also explains itself: its tooltip, the row tooltip and the current-stage caption read "regressed: <from> → <to> at <time> because <reason>".
- Dashboard activity tracker: a pull request whose `Fixes #N` issue has already closed while the PR is still open is now anchored on the PR — the PR's number, title, stage and age lead the row and the closed issue becomes a muted `closes #N · closed` chip (plus `issue closed (not planned)` when GitHub says so) — instead of drawing the dead issue struck through as the headline (hivecommons/hive#14655).
- Activity Monitor: a PR whose linked issue is already closed keeps that issue as the row head (struck through, `closed` chip) instead of promoting the PR into the issue slot; when another merged PR closed the issue the chip reads `closed by #N` and links to it (#15232).
- Activity monitor hovers, the merge-gate chip popover, the ⋯ menu hints and the server captions say each thing once in plain words: the 090 "Ready for human merge" popover is now one sentence of state, one primary action ("Merge it") plus "More ⋯", who asked and when, and a collapsed Details holding how to trust the author and the rails; the untrusted-author reason, caption, next-move line and menu consequences lost their config keys, stage numbers and internal nouns and no longer repeat each other ([#15394](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15394)).
- **Hive activity monitor: open-since age and one row count.** A plain *Open* chevron (no stage label yet, not on hold) now reads "Open · since 3d" ("since 14h" under two days), taken from the same instant the row's `since` column draws, with the ISO time in the chevron tooltip and a subtle red tint past two days (`STAGE_TRACKER_OPEN_STALE_DAYS`); *Open · hold* is unchanged, and an Open item carrying the `blocked` label gets its own "Open · blocked" word (⛔, hold's tint) that keeps the age — "Open · blocked · since 7h" — with the blocker (or the label) named in the chevron tooltip; hold wins when both are present. The sidebar badge and the list header no longer disagree: both are the **row count** of the default view from one shared function (the badge used to count open issues + PRs while the "of N" line counted rows, so a PR drawn on its issue's row made the badge read higher). That gap is now a footnote on the "showing" line's tooltip and the badge — "2 PRs shown on their issue's row" — and each such PR is led by a ↳ glyph whose link tooltip explains the shared row (and names the other issue when two list the same PR). A PR whose issue a filter hides still renders as its own row.
- Activity Monitor sounds work for every repo the hive governs: the client-side short-name resolution for `recently_merged` now learns `owner/name` from every item of every repo (issues included), so a repo whose last open PR just merged still zaps; the multi-repo path (server-side qualification over all configured repos, merge/new-item detection over the union of all repos' items) is now pinned by tests.
- Activity Monitor: a PR under repair — being fixed, waiting on its author or contributor, parked on a human decision, or with a red required check — is no longer a merge-train member. The planner skips it, the tracker drops it from the train with a muted hover note ("left the merge train while being fixed; rejoins when green"), the remaining members close ranks (count, ordinals, front), and a train left with one PR renders no header and no ordinal. Hive's own #15405 led a header as "1st: #15405" while its chevron read "Fixing" ([#15615](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15615)).
- The shared tracker row asset now exports `trackerrow.RequiredGlobals`, the `STAGE_TRACKER_*` constants it reads from its host page pinned to the spoke's values, and tests fail if that list drifts from the asset or if the spoke declares a different value, so the hub cannot silently light different columns than the spoke. `dashboard-source-layout.md` also lists `tracker-human-attention` in manifest order (#16067, #16068).
- Activity Monitor: a PR queued in the base preparation train whose current head is already approved now reads "Approved N/M · queued for base refresh behind PR #<front>" instead of "waiting for a verdict on the current head" (hivecommons/hive#16756).
- Fix inference-gateway requests failing with `tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks` when a Claude Code user turn carries text alongside a tool result: the translator now emits the `tool` messages directly after the assistant `tool_calls`, before the text.
- Activity Monitor: an issue the reporter-trust gate holds for a maintainer now reads **Triage needed** in the Open column (chevron, hover and row headline) from the moment the gate holds it, with the `needs-triage` modifier and the inline **Accept triage** lead — instead of **New** with the ask only in the caption, as hivecommons/hive#15437–#15440 did before the awaiting label landed; the caption of every held row (000-new or 015) is now exactly *Triage needed — accept or close* instead of repeating *triage* three times.
- Stage engine: `stage/015-triage-needed` is now derived only for issues the reporter-trust gate is holding (`needs-triage` label or the `reporter_triage` bucket); issues filed by hive agents or trusted humans are triaged by construction and stay `010-actionable` instead of being demoted to 015.
- Refresh persisted triage acceptance into the work queue and activity monitor on first acceptance and idempotent retries, reporting handoff failures instead of showing an unconfirmed success.
- Trust-promotion announcement records in the stage-label store are no longer exempt from `Prune` forever: they are now dropped once unseen for 180 days (or the prune age if longer), so the store stops accumulating one record per contributor while an author is still not re-announced within that window (#15463).
- Contributor-lane auto-promotion is announced once per author per hive instead of on every open PR by the author at once: the first PR that earns it gets one shorter, author-wide comment ("@login is now trusted for contributor-lane merging in this hive …"), the author's other open and later PRs post nothing, the announced fact survives restarts in the stage store, and a demotion followed by re-promotion announces once more ([#15443](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15443)).
- Activity Monitor: a row never lights more than two chevrons, and a filled chevron now always means "this is where the item is / what is in motion". CI and Review are filled (amber) only while a check-run or a review perspective is actually running on the current head; passed / approved, findings, pending and decided verdicts are words in their colour on the muted field. Unreported checks and rows waiting on a person render as pending words, never amber. When both tracks run, the stage chevron is settled-current. A queued review swarm reads "Review 0/5 · swarm requested" instead of 5/5 (#16540).
- Refresh an issue's cached tracker snapshot after an accepted maintainer decision so its Actionable ribbon no longer retains stale needs-human badges and decision questions while waiting for a GitHub webhook.
- Show temporary upgrade holds as Delayed instead of missed windows, and clear resolved delay warnings after a successful upgrade on both dashboards, including older history entries.
- `hive validate` now lists base-config `launch_cmd` entries dropped for contradicting their backend and exits non-zero instead of printing "config OK" (#15769)
- Activity Monitor CI chevron counts (`CI 7/11`) are now driven by `check_run`/`workflow_job`/`status` webhook deliveries applied straight into a per-head check set — no PR re-read per check fan-out — with one coalesced check-run listing only when the head has none yet, so rows no longer sit at `CI ?/?` after a push or for sidelined PRs until the next eval cycle; `/api/status.webhooks` gains `last_ci_event_at`, `ci_events_1h`, `ci_events_applied_1h`, `ci_refetches_1h` and the hub relays `workflow_run`/`workflow_job` (hivecommons/hive#16521)
- review: a not-hive-authored head whose fix is withheld is now reported in `FixExclusions` only on the cycle that first withholds it, matching `auditWithheldReviewFixes`' doc instead of repeating every eval cycle (#14882, #14883).
- The contributor lane now binds an unmarked owner approval (a typed `/hive decision approve`, or a dashboard `/approve` posted without a head marker) to the time GitHub first showed the PR's current head, never to the head commit's committer date. That date is written by the pusher's git, so a later push carrying a backdated commit could inherit an approval given on the head before it and release the workflow-path fence for a diff the approver never saw. An approval older than the observed head now leaves the fence armed, exactly like an APPROVED review on a stale commit; the approver re-approves the new head to release it. This is deliberately fail-closed and slightly narrower than before: the observed time is pinned on the hive's first sweep of the head, and any comment or label that lands between the push and that sweep moves it later, so an approval typed in that gap is also treated as stale and has to be typed again. A head with no pinned time yet binds nothing.
- Preserve durable write counter totals and retry pending counts after transient file read errors ([#14531](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14531)).
- Write-back containment: every unsolicited GitHub comment, label and review from platform sweeps (sentinel, hold-gate notices, stage labels, supersession, duplicate-fix, reporter-trust) now passes one central per-kind gate (`writeback.*`) that requires both an ACMM floor and the review opt-in label on foreign PRs, never back-fills onto PRs that predate hive's write access, and surfaces suppressed writes in the dashboard instead of on GitHub
- Restore the writeback direct-write ratchet on `v5`: the lapsed claimed-by label removal added in #16849 is annotated as gated, so `TestDirectWriteRatchet` passes again for every PR based on `v5`

### Security

- Stage-074 adoption now applies the contributor lane's diff fences before taking over a contributor PR: a PR that touches CI workflow/action definitions, deletes or guts tests, or whose file list cannot be read is no longer adopted in place or superseded by an App PR (including the `dco-rehome` takeover); it stays at stage 072 with a logged `contributor-lane:*` reason ([#12850](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12850)).
- `hivectl hives web` now rejects requests whose `Host` is not a loopback host on the listening port (DNS-rebinding protection) and cross-origin browser requests (`Origin` / `Sec-Fetch-Site`), sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response, and the page removes the launch token from the URL and browser history once loaded. Token auth is unchanged. ([#13178](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13178), part of [#13153](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13153))
- The local `hivectl hives web` API now accepts its access token only through the `X-Hive-Commons-Token` header, preventing API credentials from leaking through query strings ([#13245](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13245)).
- Image builds compile with Go 1.27.3: the `golang:1.27-alpine` builder digest in `src/Dockerfile`, `src/Dockerfile.hub`, `src/Dockerfile.contributor` and the base-registry probe now resolves to `1.27.3-alpine` instead of `1.27.2-alpine`, and the contributor image's standalone toolchain moves from Go 1.24.4 to 1.27.3, so the shipped `hive`, `hivectl`, `bd` and hub binaries carry the `crypto/x509` fix for GO-2026-6809 ([#13329](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13329)).
- Dashboard review-evidence downloads, listings, aggregates, tracker annotations, heartbeats, and evidence-derived metrics now verify bundle signatures against the configured Ed25519 key before using on-disk data; unsigned mode still verifies content hashes, while an unavailable configured key or tampered bundle fails closed ([#13900](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13900)).
- Keep the hive PR open and parked when a clean competing contributor PR references the same issue; delegated decisions now recommend a human adequacy comparison instead of automatically closing the hive's work ([#13998](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13998)).
- Refuse to publish contributor workflow/action edits into upstream adoption branches, and revalidate head evidence before every supersession. The refusal is recorded once per head: the PR gets one note and moves to needs-decision instead of being re-checked every sweep.
- The proxy's plain-HTTP forward path now identifies its caller and refuses destinations that are not globally routable — loopback, link-local (cloud instance metadata), RFC 1918, CGNAT and multicast — checked at dial time so a hostname resolving inward is refused too; set `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD=true` to allow them (#14082)
- The proxy write-gate rule table mirrors GitHub posture for GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo: direct MR/PR creation and merge are hard-denied for every agent level (forcing the hive-open-pr and hive-merge request-file paths as the bot identity), reads and issues/comments/labels follow the ACMM ladder, and unknown routes fail closed ([#14114](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14114), part of [#14096](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14096)).
- "Let hive decide" (`POST …/items/{number}/decide-delegated`) no longer reads a pull request head as CI-green from `mergeable_state` alone. GitHub reports `blocked` both for a missing required review and for red required checks, and `unknown`/`behind` say nothing about the head, so the delegate could approve a PR whose required checks were failing or had never run and record it as a "green head" decision. The gatherer now settles those states from the head's combined status and check runs — no red, nothing pending, at least one green — the same way it already judged a competing PR, and such heads get the `fix-then-merge` direction instead of an approval ([#14167](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14167)).
- Limit GitHub claim-effect processing to one worker per active issue so claim/release churn no longer accumulates waiting goroutines; queued effects still run in order without dropping release cleanup.
- The hive capability endpoint (`callback.Listen`, bound from `$CRUX_HIVE_LISTEN`) now refuses a TCP address off loopback, the same fail-closed rule `crux serve --listen` has applied since #13967. The listener is plain http gated by `$CRUX_HIVE_TOKEN`, and it serves `POST /v1/tokens`, which mints GitHub App installation tokens — a routable bind would have carried both the bearer token and every minted token across the network in cleartext. The k8s sidecar-container option is unaffected: the containers share the pod's network namespace, so `127.0.0.1` reaches the sidecar. Remote access goes through a TLS-terminating proxy. (#14348)
- The inference translator on `127.0.0.1:18444` now names its caller from the socket owner's UID, the way the GitHub proxy path and the decision endpoint already do, instead of from the `x-api-key` header the caller chose. That header is `sk-hive-<agent name>` and the name is public inside the pod, so any local process could previously borrow a different agent's inference route — backend, model, upstream credential and usage attribution. A mapped agent UID is authoritative (a header naming someone else is logged and overridden), the hive's own control plane keeps the header name, and an unidentifiable caller is refused with 401 unless `HIVE_PROXY_ADVISORY_OK=true`. The translator server also gained a `ReadHeaderTimeout` ([#14439](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14439)).
- Refuse proxy-owned inference translator requests unless advisory identity is explicitly enabled, preventing forged agent identities through private plain-HTTP forwarding when `HIVE_PROXY_ALLOW_PRIVATE_FORWARD=true` (#14448).
- Keep raw IOScan classifier errors, including private endpoint URLs and DNS details, in local logs rather than public selfreport diagnostics.
- Prevent comment-only PR cross-references from moving issues to Reviewing or Closed in the dashboard; timeline PR links now require a closing keyword in the PR title or body ([#14985](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14985)).
- A rebase-then-merge follow-through no longer treats an unsigned head as the hive's own just because its author email is the App bot's noreply address: an author GitHub resolves to the App bot now counts only on a commit GitHub reports as verified, as GitHub's update-branch commits are ([#15421](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15421)).
- The hold guard no longer treats an approval carried from an adopted PR as proof that a trusted merger reviewed the copy's current head ([#15698](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15698)).
- Agent NO_PROXY only appends the OMP_AUTH_BROKER_URL host when it is a concrete hostname or IP, so a wildcard or leading-dot host can no longer widen the proxy bypass (#15726)
- Fix tool approval's built-in destructive-command detection for root/home removal and fork bombs without relying on host text-scanner findings, and avoid matching removal of ordinary subpaths ([#15727](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15727)).
- Redact credentials from logged errors, Stringer, TextAppender and TextMarshaler values (including marshal errors), and resolved LogValuer attributes, including nested groups and bound logger attributes ([#15729](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15729)). Text-rendered attributes are now emitted as strings, including in JSON logs where a value implementing `json.Marshaler` may previously have emitted a number or object.
- The built-in destructive-command check now also matches equivalent root and home removal spellings such as `rm -rf //`, `rm -rf /.`, `rm -rf "/"`, `rm -r -f /` and `rm -rf ${HOME}`, instead of relying solely on the host text scanner ([#15740](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15740)).
- The built-in destructive-`rm` check in `crux/toolapprove` now reads a command the way bash would hand it to `rm`, without running anything, and judges what each target means rather than how it is spelled ([#16094](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16094)). Quoting and escapes, `$'…'` strings, brace expansion (`/{,}`, `{rm,-rf,/}`), `.`/`..` components (`/tmp/..`, `$PWD/../../..`), `$IFS` splitting, subshells, command substitutions and re-quoted commands (`bash -c '…'`, `eval`) now resolve to the same verdict as plain `rm -rf /`. A recursive `rm` of the root, the home directory, the working directory or any ancestor of one is flagged. That set now includes `rm -rf .`, `./*`, `..` and `"$PWD"`, matching the existing treatment of `rm -rf *`. A new spelling-equivalence test derives about 70,000 bash-equivalent commands from destructive and safe seeds and gates every detector change on them. The analysis has explicit limits: 1024 brace words per word, nesting 32 brace groups and 8 re-read levels deep, and a work budget proportional to the command. A command past them is reported as a separate `shell command exceeds destructive-command analysis bounds` violation instead of passing clean. The `rm` branch of the old regex is retired, so its false positives no longer fire: non-recursive `rm -f /`, literal `'$HOME'` and `"~"`, and `a=rm -rf /`. An `rm` that is the subcommand of a version-control tool (`git rm -r --cached .`, `hg rm`, `svn rm`) is not the binary and is not flagged.
- The contributor lane's workflow-path approval no longer accepts an edited comment as an approval: a `/hive decision approve` (or dashboard `/approve`) whose comment was modified after it was posted is ignored, the same rule the un-park sweep already applies, so rewriting a merger's earlier comment cannot be read as that merger's approval (#16127).
- The push broker's trailing-newline normaliser now resolves each changed file's parent directory and skips any path that escapes the workspace through a symlinked directory, as it already did for a committed symlink at the leaf. Since the normaliser began committing HEAD's blob rather than the working-tree bytes, an agent that committed `dir/file` and then swapped `dir/` for a symlink out of the sandbox workspace could have had that blob written briefly into a hive-owned file by the host-side broker before the restore put it back ([#16211](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16211)).
- Require human policy sign-off for reviewer questions on workflow and action edits, including same-repository PRs.
- Harden Activity Monitor source-work verification with credential-free, bounded, read-only Git inspection that cannot execute workspace hooks, filters or helpers; unsupported normalization and unstable repository evidence stay unknown.
- Base-preparation state files and directory are no longer created group-writable (0o644/0o755, matching the stage store). (#15844)
- A recorded decision, and the base-preparation proof, now follow a PR onto a new head only when the merge commit is one GitHub created and verified (signed, committed by `web-flow` or the App) rather than any commit whose author email resolves to the App bot, and a base...head compare that reaches GitHub's 300-file listing cap fails closed instead of being compared on a truncated file list ([#16860](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16860)).
- Contributor registration tokens expire after 90 days by default, support an optional inactivity cutoff, and can be inspected or revoked individually or in bulk from Management and `hivectl contribute tokens`; GitHub-authenticated `hivectl contribute login` rotates expired tokens, while legacy credentials receive persisted migration-time issuance dates (#13804).
- Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0 in src/crux to clear GO-2026-6617/6612/6611/6603 (govulncheck red on hivecommons/crux main).
- Dashboard directions for contributor PRs now require the sweep's classification label, honoring `governor.labels.author` names, instead of falling back directly to PR-body markers; the sweep's body-marker classification remains unchanged ([#15268](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15268)).
- Deleting a registry-only hive now requires being its owner or a hub admin; entries whose spoke never reported an owner are admin-only (#16134)
- Discord notifications and RFC notices no longer ping @everyone or roles from untrusted text such as issue titles
- Bumped the Go toolchain to 1.26.10 so the `govulncheck` gate stops flagging GO-2026-6809 (`crypto/x509` certificate verification), reachable from the dashboard's HTTP server. The gate was red on the default branch itself, blocking every open PR.
- Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0 to clear GO-2026-6860 (govulncheck).
- The hold guard only advances a held PR's reviewed baseline after a merge-from-base when the new head is a two-parent merge of a base-branch commit into the head the hive asked to update, so a contributor push racing the update is no longer adopted as reviewed hygiene; the base parent is matched against the live base branch, so a base that moved before the update does not turn the hive's own merge into drift ([#14534](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/14534)).
- Scrub `[]byte`, `[]string`, map, struct and other composite log attributes (and `TextMarshaler` values) so credential-shaped tokens no longer bypass the log scrubber ([#15735](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15735), [#15736](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15736)).
- A hive authenticated with a personal access token and no configured identity now learns its own login from `GET /user`, so a once-only marker (unpark reply, label-approval, sentinel) pasted by another commenter is no longer trusted; hives that cannot reach `/user` keep the previous behavior ([#13520](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/13520)).
- Bumped transitive `body-parser` to 2.4.0 and `qs` to 6.17.1 in `src/proxy/package-lock.json` (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw), matching what `dashboard/` already pins, and `undici` to 6.29.1 in `discord/package-lock.json` (GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx TLS option drop and four DoS advisories). `/discord` now has its own Dependabot npm entry so the directory gets the same weekly coverage as `/src/proxy` and `/dashboard`.
- The `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception now verifies the commits behind the head, not only the PR author login: every commit must be authored by a `trusted_authors` login, committed by GitHub itself (`web-flow`) or a `trusted_authors` login, and carry a GitHub-verified signature (which binds to the committer, not the author), and the list must end at the current head. Before, anyone with write access could push a pin-shaped commit onto a trusted author's branch (a `dependabot/...` branch keeps `dependabot[bot]` as PR author) and have the sweep or `/approve` waive the human-merge-path hold on it. Unsigned or foreign commits, an unreadable or empty commit list, or a list that does not end at the head now hold the PR as before; the commit list is read only once the diff already qualifies, so refused PRs cost no extra API call.
- The opt-in `auto_merge.human_merge_pin_only` exception now admits an `action-sha` pin only when the new SHA is anchored in its upstream action repository: with a `# vX[.Y[.Z]]` comment the upstream `tags/vX…` ref (annotated tags dereferenced) must point at exactly that SHA, otherwise the SHA must be an ancestor of the upstream default branch ([#16399](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16399)). GitHub resolves a `uses:` SHA across the whole fork network, so a pin-shaped line could otherwise point at a commit pushed to any fork. Any 404, mismatch, rate limit or API error keeps the human-merge-path hold; repos without the key are unaffected. The pin-only commit check now uses the shared PR commit lister ([#16401](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16401)).
- Pushbroker now checks both source and destination paths of renamed files, preventing protected workflows, policies, and other guarded files from being moved out of protected paths to bypass the push gate ([#15728](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15728)).
- RFC lifecycle notices no longer post RFCs from private repositories (titles and links) to `notifications.discord.rfc_channel_id` unless `notifications.discord.rfc_include_private: true` authorizes it. The gate applies in every mode, line mode included. Repo visibility is resolved once per repo and cached for an hour. A repo whose visibility cannot be resolved, or that is `internal`, counts as private (fail closed). Withheld RFCs still advance the detector state, so they never replay later (#15926, part of #15869).
- The sentinel no longer releases an alert on a dashboard-approval comment, nor writes its clearance record into an existing marker comment, unless one of the hive's own known accounts wrote it: a hive that cannot name its own accounts no longer falls back to trusting any author there, so a PR author cannot forge the release for their own head ([#15262](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15262)). Skipping the dashboard `/lgtm` + `/approve` commands after a Prow rejection now believes only the Prow bot (`kubestellar-prow[bot]`), not any installed bot quoting the rejection phrase ([#15263](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/15263)).
- The Activity Monitor streamer's loopback `authproxy` (`src/deploy/stream`) now forwards only `GET`/`HEAD` to the dashboard and answers every other method `405` locally, before the bearer is attached. The token it injects is the spoke's shared dashboard token, which the dashboard treats as an unscoped owner; the kiosk only ever reads, so a compromised or misbehaving page in the `--no-sandbox` Chromium can no longer reach agent-control, config or settings mutations with that authority.
- Fixed the tool-approval guardrail-path check never seeing the target of a Copilot CLI `apply_patch` call ([#16979](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/16979)). The tool carries its paths in the patch text (`*** Update File:`, `*** Add File:`, `*** Delete File:`, `*** Move to:`) instead of a path argument, so `ToolRequest.GetFilePath` returned an empty string and a patch touching `.github/workflows/**`, `OWNERS`, `hive.yaml` or `policies/**` auto-approved at L5/L6. `GetFilePath` now falls back to the first path in the patch body, and the guardrail check now iterates the new `GetFilePaths` over every path the request names, so a patch that lists a harmless file first and a guardrail path later is still caught.

## 2026-10-18 (v5.186.4)

### Fixed

- Restart an agent whose live CLI pane stays off its input prompt (neither Working nor any prompt) after repeated undeliverable kicks, instead of leaving it wedged with every kick failing as "CLI did not reach input prompt" and, since the self-report now waits for that restart, never reported (#12916).

## 2026-10-18 (v5.186.3)

### Fixed

- Review aggregation: a partial (incomplete) re-review no longer displaces a prior `changes_requested` or `reject` aggregate for the same repo/number/head/body-digest, extending the `requires_human` retention from #12909. PRs mid fix-cycle stay on the fix path instead of being sent back to re-ask missing perspectives, and the original `RecordedAt` is preserved. Fixes #12911.

## 2026-10-18 (v5.186.2)

### Fixed

- Hub-side plumbing for a spoke-reported lane-scoped queue depth: the hub's agents-inactive idle rule now prefers `laneQueuedWork` over the hive-wide backlog when a spoke reports it, preventing an intentionally idle lane from being flagged when other lanes have work. Spokes do not yet report it (follow-up [#12876](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12876)), so the alert only narrows once the producer lands ([#12866](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12866)).
- Preserve a settled `requires_human` verdict while a replacement review of the same head and PR body is incomplete, preventing partial report refreshes from reopening the decision as review-pending ([#12878](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12878)).
- Completes the #12899 follow-through for contributor PRs ([#12897](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12897)): the `review_fix_withheld` audit entry now records the actual `review.fix_human_prs` value instead of a hard-coded `false`, and the review-thread kick no longer tells the agent to check out, commit to, or push a human-opened PR's branch with that setting on — it replies with a suggestion instead. The propose-only review prompt, operator docs, dashboard help text and config comments are reworded to match.

## 2026-10-18 (v5.186.1)

### Fixed

- Route Hive-authored non-risk reviewer findings with concrete remediation through the normalized changes-requested fixer path across aggregation, stage labels, and fixer dispatch.

## 2026-10-18 (v5.186.0)

### Added

- Add single-click global cadence setting templates (New Level testing, Weekly sprint, Biweekly sprint, and Daily cadence) in the dashboard Governor matrix and via `POST /api/config/governor/cadence-templates` to allow operators to quickly configure governor cadences across all agents without excessive manual clicks (#12300).
- Add `hivectl hives preset adopt` and `hivectl hives preset refresh` to review a contribution preset against your saved repository selection, record the accepted membership with preset provenance, keep personal exclusions and saved repositories unless removal is confirmed, preserve state on discovery outages, and opt in per Hive to following new repositories with `--follow-new-repos` ([#12570](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12570)).
- Contributor relays enforce per-Hive repository selections before accepting assignments, negotiate versioned scopes, visibly skip unsupported Hives, and idle on empty selections.
- Auto-promote contributor-lane trust after a clean merged-PR history so reviewed green contributor PRs can merge at L6.
- Show held open issues and PRs as held directly in the dashboard pipeline Open segment.
- `hivectl` can now parse and validate a **contribution preset**: a versioned, credential-free YAML document a project publishes at an HTTPS URL or ships as a file to recommend Hives and repository selections (`all-current` or an explicit `owner/name` list per Hive, plus optional hubs). Loading is strict and read-only: unknown `version` majors, unknown fields, and any field carrying tokens, credentials, shell commands, local execution settings or permission changes are refused with the field named; only `https://` (and loopback `http://`) or local paths are accepted, redirects may not leave HTTPS, and documents are capped at 256 KiB. See "Contribution presets" in `src/docs/hivectl.md` ([#12803](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12803), part of [#12570](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12570)).
- Wire the background-only Hive-self experiment scheduler into `hive` behind a new default-off `self_experiments.scheduler` block (`enabled`, `mode: background`, `interval_s`). When enabled in background mode, each tick judges every unresolved experiment in the local Hive-self ledger and hands the decision to the executor, which latches fast-fails and reverts treatments durably; reverts are restored at startup before the first heartbeat. Experiments are registered by the hub/relay, which is not yet wired, so the ledger (`/data/nous/self-experiments.json`) stays empty until then. With the default config nothing is loaded and no goroutine starts, and governor configuration is never touched ([#12397](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12397), [#12768](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12768)).

### Changed

- docs: document HIVE_REPO_SCOPE in the env-var references (#12867)
- Let Hive-authored issues resolve non-risk engineering decision questions without self-parking at stage/085.
- Issues parked on a person now wear the new issue-side stage `stage/045-needs-decision`; `stage/085-needs-decision` is PR-only. `needs-human` on an issue implies 045, `/hive approve` / `/hive decision` still un-park to `approved-direction` and keep `needs-human`, the good-first-issue scorer and the dashboard "Needs human" bucket recognise 045, and open issues still carrying 085 are re-staged to 045 by the issue stage reconciler and a one-shot startup sweep (`/data/issue-needs-decision-stage-v1.done`).
- Document `HIVE_REPO_SCOPE` and `HIVE_REPO_SCOPE_VERSION` in the env-var reference and the contributor-relay variable table (relay/hivectl, #12804).
- Let Hive-authored review decisions resolve low-risk sequencing, naming and config-shape questions by default while preserving risk escalations.

### Fixed

- Document the supported in-place adoption and offline/unregistered wait settings in `hive.yaml.example` (#12777).
- Correct the offline contributor grace example to match its 15-minute default (#12821).
- contributor-relay: strip the matching shell quotes `hivectl` writes around values in `contributor.env`, so `HIVE_REPO_SCOPE` reads back as written (#12826)
- hub: the zero-spend `token-burn` fleet alert now fires only when token spend is expected (queued work or unpaused expected-active agents) and nothing stronger already explains it — all-paused or quiet-by-design hives, fresh advisory output, stale heartbeat stats, a pending App install, a precondition-red health verdict (App broken, login stuck, budget, agents down), or an inference-auth, GitHub-App-required or agents-inactive alert no longer also raise it ([#12844](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12844))
- hub: unclaimed `available` pool slots no longer raise `health-check-failing` for `project_org`, which fails by design on their seeded placeholder org/repo until the slot is claimed ([#12843](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12843))
- hub: the `advisory-stale` fleet alert is no longer raised from a heartbeat carrying cached or minimal stats (`statsStale`), whose `advisoryLastPostedAt` is the last-good value rather than proof the digest stopped posting ([#12842](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12842))
- Contributor-PR adoption now falls back to a superseding App PR when the base branch has moved past a `.github/workflows/` change since the PR's merge-base: the App token cannot push such a base-sync to the contributor branch (no `workflows` permission), so the in-place mode promised by the adoption comment was a dead end that left the PR dirty forever (#12865, #6985).
- The spoke heartbeat now reports each reviewer-lane agent's own actionable queue depth (`laneQueuedWork`), computed with the same lane routing and gates the governor uses to skip an idle lane, so the hub's idle-with-work alert can narrow from the hive-wide backlog to the agent's lane; agents outside the reviewer lane omit the field and keep the hive-wide fallback ([#12876](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12876), follow-up to [#12875](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/12875)).
- Stage-label 085/090 entry comments are now posted once per (stage, head), so a same-head flap through `050-review-pending` no longer reposts a byte-identical comment ([#12878](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12878)). A new head or a different human stage still explains itself once.
- review: a partly answered revisit now re-asks only the perspectives that timed out instead of re-kicking the full set (#12883)
- Make the automerge review gate's human-approval read-failure log lane-neutral (#12891).
- List PR reviews once per self-authored sweep instead of twice for requires-human heads (#12892).
- Re-home adopted contributor PRs when unsigned commits cannot be DCO-repaired in place, with fixer instructions for DCO-clean superseding branches.
- Treat conflicting contributor PRs like red CI so offline clanker authors are nudged and adopted after grace.
- Keep conflicting contributor PRs in the author-rework stage instead of ready-for-human-merge while mergeability is known to be conflicting.
- **DCO post-merge monitor: waive `a9200f3d` per maintainer disposition.** The #12707 squash on `v5` kept the scanner `Signed-off-by` instead of the author's, so the monitor kept failing. A SHA-scoped `DCO_WAIVED_COMMITS` entry records the maintainer-accepted disposition without rewriting history or widening any identity allowlist ([#12727](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12727)).
- The issue stage sweep now closes a decomposed parent issue as completed once every tracked child (GitHub sub-issue linked by the relay) is closed, with one comment listing each child and its closing PR, and never marks a parent with open children `stage/stalled` (an existing marker comes off). The relay also writes a `<!-- hive:parent N -->` marker into each child it links (#12857).
- Require signed hive-authored fix-pr commits before push (merge commits exempt, as DCO checkers skip them) and choose in-place DCO repair versus re-home for adopted PRs on whether the unsigned commits are GitHub-linked to the hive App bot — never on forgeable git emails — and whether the branch is still pushable; the ownership split is cached with the commit check and a re-home is attempted once per head.
- Prevented reviewer/fixer follow-up commits from being pushed to non-App-authored PR branches, and keep hive-caused squash sign-off failures in the hive-owned fixing lane instead of returning them to contributors.
- `hivectl` Hive lookup by origin no longer fails for every onboarding target when a legacy profile uses a hub host the canonical identity form rejects (such as compose or Kubernetes service names with `_`); such profiles are skipped. The `HIVE_REPO_SCOPE` documentation now shows the format `hivectl` actually writes (`,` between hubs, `;` between repositories). (#12804)
- Treat trusted human APPROVED reviews on the current head as resolving `requires_human` reviewer verdicts across automerge lanes.
- Route Hive-authored non-risk incomplete-fix reviewer findings to the fixer lane instead of parking them for human decisions.
- `kick_failed_repeatedly` self-reports are now filed only after the busy-no-activity stall restart has been attempted and the session is still undeliverable (or the restart itself errored). Previously the fleet issue was filed at 1× `busy_no_activity_threshold` (30m), before the 2× restart bar, so it reported stalls that then self-recovered. The 30m condition stays visible as the dashboard busy condition and a warning log line; the report message now states when the restart ran and how many times (#12787).
- Apply normalized review verdicts consistently to stage labels and fixer dispatch.
- Shared CI failures now require an independent human-authored control and no green counterexample, so related agent PRs cannot hide the same PR-local defect from the escalation circuit breaker.
- Fix review dispatch so held review-pending pull requests stay in the reviewer queue and are served in review-rank order.
- List held review-pending satellite pull requests in reviewer kicks so the prompt matches the dispatched review queue.
- Derive stage role labels from author identity so non-owning lanes cannot flip trusted App-authored PRs to untrusted.
- Add regression coverage that resolved Hive-authored design questions leave the needs-decision stage label.
- Derive review-driven stage labels from one normalized verdict source to prevent 070/085 flapping.

### Security

- The contributor-lane auto-promotion ratchet no longer re-trusts a contributor whose registry tier is `revoked`, and counts a merged PR that a later merged revert undid as revert evidence ([#12874](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12874)).

## 2026-10-17 (v5.185.0)

### Added

- **Contributor repository scope** ([#12805](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/12805)). A hive now advertises its contribution-eligible repositories at the public `GET /api/contribute/repositories` (monitored repos minus `hub.disabled_repos`, as `{forge}/{host}/{owner}/{name}` ids) and, behind the new `repo_scope_v1` capability, accepts a versioned `repo_scope` from a relay and answers `repo_scope_ack`.
