## 2026-09-23 (v5.16.0)

### Added

- OMP workbench as the second external host behind the engine-neutral `pkg/extwork` adapter, answering the #6899 handoff question: an already-running OMP session takes a lease over the contributor relay channel it already holds (new `ext_*` frames, no new API), advertising `ext-exec/omp`; it receives the assignment summary only, must send an explicit accept or decline before the bounded context bundle is delivered, emits progress events (accepted, running, waiting, terminal, unknown) that land on the lease audit, and ends with a `stage-receipt/v1` receipt that Hive verifies by digest and binds to the lease and generation. Report-only: no repository credential, no dashboard token, publication stays Hive-side; because OMP is tier T3 (unconfined) the adapter refuses write-capable stages in code. Default off behind `runs.external.omp` with its own Features panel toggle beside the Flue one, linked into the binary only under the `extwork_omp` build tag, and proven by a conformance suite against a second-process workbench fixture (accept before context, decline audited, progress recorded, receipt bound, disconnect mid-stage stays unknown, dedup and conflict, cancel facts, shadow and off perform nothing, peer without the capability refused) ([#8361](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8361))
- The agent CLI pins in `src/Dockerfile` and `src/Dockerfile.contributor` now keep themselves current ([#8419](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8419)). A daily workflow (`.github/workflows/cli-pin-bump.yml`, also dispatchable per CLI) runs `src/scripts/cli-pin-bump.sh` for each of claude, codex, copilot, pi, goose, agy, omp, muse, bob and gh: it resolves the latest release from the CLI's own source of truth (npm registry, GitHub releases, or the vendor's manifest), recomputes every per-architecture SHA-256/SHA-512 from the downloaded artifact and cross-checks it against the vendor-published digest where one exists, rewrites the `ARG` lines in both Dockerfiles, builds the hub image and runs `<cli> --version` (plus `claude --help`) inside it, and only then opens one PR per CLI labelled `security`, `dependencies` and `no-changelog`, with `needs-human` added for a major version change. The pins themselves stay (#2903): nothing floats to `@latest` and no hash check is removed. Operators get fresher CLIs through their normal image upgrade instead of waiting for someone to notice a stale pin, which is how #8417 sat for six weeks. See `src/docs/cli-pins.md`.

### Changed

- Aligned the Spektacular stage runner with the status contract as shipped by jumppad-labs/spektacular#45 and the maintainer answers of 2026-09-23: leases join artifacts by the bare artifact name (`000057_git-commit`, any `.md` or `/plan.md` spelling is reduced to it) instead of the rarely populated `spec:`/`plan:` cross-references; `updated_at` is no longer read for any progress, receipt or staleness decision (it is a file mtime whenever no workflow state matches, and may be absent); the `{"error":true,"code":"artifact_not_found","message":...}` envelope is parsed into the typed missing-document error and `closed_at: ""` on open documents no longer breaks the parse; the `--json` flag the CLI does not have is no longer passed; and `src/docs/spektacular.md` records which assumptions were confirmed, which changed, and that `plan export` is still an open ask (#8303)

### Security

- security: issue-claim markers are only honoured from the hub bot and their expiry is clamped to governor.claims.ttl_s (#8434)

## 2026-09-23 (v5.15.1)

### Fixed

- The agent CLIs baked into the hub image (`src/Dockerfile`) and the contributor image (`src/Dockerfile.contributor`) are current again ([#8417](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8417)). Claude Code 2.1.226 refused `claude-opus-5-5` ("version 2.1.280 or newer is required"), so every claude agent or contributor set to Opus 5.5 failed on each run; it is now 2.1.280. Codex moves 0.153.4 -> 0.156.1, whose bundled catalog adds GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (the dashboard's static codex fallback list and `static/index.html` mirror are refreshed to the 0.156.1 catalog, which also retired `gpt-5.2` and `gpt-5.4-mini`). The other pins move with them: Copilot 1.0.78 (1.0.59 in the contributor image) -> 1.0.88, pi 0.84.1 -> 0.87.1, Goose 1.45.0 -> 1.51.0, Antigravity 1.1.19 / 1.1.22 -> 1.2.9, Oh My Pi 18.2.6 -> 18.2.11, Muse Code 1.0.3-R2198.1 -> 1.3.0-R3401.1, and bobshell 1.0.6 -> 2.0.4; gh 2.101.0 was already current. Every download-verified layer keeps its per-architecture SHA-256/SHA-512 check, with the digests recomputed from the published release artifacts.

### Security

- `review.all_authors` no longer lets the review-fix kick push commits onto PRs that Hive's own agents did not open: the fixer now runs an authorship check before every fix kick and, for a contributor's or maintainer's PR, the reviewer publishes its findings with the proposed fix as a suggestion or patch block instead, recording the withheld push on the audit log as `review_fix_withheld` with the PR, author, and setting. Pushing to other people's PR branches is a separate, owner-only, off-by-default opt-in, `review.fix_human_prs` ("Push fix commits to PRs Hive did not open" under Features -> Review Gate -> Reviewers); a hive that already ran with `all_authors: true` is migrated to `fix_human_prs: true` on load, logged once and shown as on, so an upgrade changes nothing it was doing ([#8421](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8421)).

## 2026-09-23 (v5.15.0)

### Added

- Report-only external-execution binding pilot: a new engine-neutral `pkg/extwork` contract (keyed start, accepted/running/waiting/terminal/unknown observation, cancel facts kept separate, digest-verified receipt fetch with size and path limits, accept-or-decline before any context is delivered, progress events on the lease audit) and a Flue adapter proven against a deterministic three-stage fixture that runs as a second local process with no network, model, or GitHub token. Admission intent and authority are the task lease; the binding is default off behind `runs.external.flue` with a Features panel toggle, shadow mode never starts external work, and the adapter is linked into the binary only under the `extwork_flue` build tag ([#8361](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8361)).

## 2026-09-23 (v5.14.0)

### Added

- Retro can now automatically promote or demote ACMM levels from repo-scoped autonomy signals when the new default-off autonomy policy is enabled, recording every decision with evidence for the dashboard and audit log ([#8364](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8364)).

## 2026-09-23 (v5.13.0)

### Added

- Added the opt-in Spektacular stage runner (`runs.spektacular.enabled`, default off, Features toggle): it polls `spektacular {spec,plan} status --json` for every active stage lease, writes a stage receipt and advances the lease on `document_status: final`, retries an expired stage within `runs.max_stage_retries` (default 2) and then raises a decision escalation, admits a final plan as a draft Hive plan without LLM redecomposition, and refuses to advance a plan that went back to draft or a document that was replaced (#8303)
- Retro now records progressive autonomy signal facts for first-pass plans, no-rework merged PRs, and rolled-back runs so the ACMM dashboard can show advisory scope signals without changing levels automatically ([#8313](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8313)).
- Runs can now fan out implementation waves across multiple repositories, refusing constellation repo-claim overlaps, holding later waves behind final/skipped barriers, and documenting forward-fix as the default for partial failures ([#8314](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8314)).
- Review gains an opt-in `plan_match` perspective (`review.plan_match.enabled`, Features panel toggle) that scores a PR against the approved plan wave its `Hive-Run` / `Hive-Plan` trailers name, reporting scope creep and missing planned items; trailer-less PRs get a not-applicable report that leaves their confidence score unchanged, and a high-severity scope finding holds the PR for a human ([#8317](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8317)).
- Isolate run-stage work in per-stage git worktrees and block stale implementation plans whose spec input_revision no longer matches the current spec revision.
- Add the owner-only `POST /api/runs/{key}/reset` route and `resetLeaseStage`, which move a run back to an earlier stage with a new generation and a recorded reason (#8350)
- Added the audit campaign's authorized issue publisher: one trusted publication effect that files each validated finding exactly once through the mutation journal (replay returns the recorded issue), routes security-sensitive findings to a configured private channel and never to a public issue, refuses with a typed error and audit entry below ACMM L3 or without a private channel, performs zero GitHub writes when disabled or in shadow mode, and wires `convergence/outcome` as the campaign's predicted-versus-actual repository outcome ledger; default off behind `publication.enabled` with a Features panel toggle ([#8353](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8353), [#7281](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7281))
- Added the `wavefront` additive work source (`governor.work_source.wavefront`, default disabled) that lists the ready nodes of an imported, versioned Crustify/Wavefront migration graph as run-stage work items with dependency edges, withholds blocked nodes, refuses items minted at a stale graph revision, admits the graph as a plan through `DecomposeFromOutput` with no LLM call, and records a receipt per completed node with zero GitHub calls (#8362)
- Per-agent reasoning effort for the claude backend: the dashboard effort dropdown now appears on claude agents and a stored `reasoning_effort` (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) is passed to Claude Code as `--effort <v>`; unset leaves the CLI at its own default, and the scripted and contributor-relay launches honor `AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT` for claude the same way (#8377)
- Add Oh My Pi (`omp`) as a dashboard agent method with pinned hub-image install, model discovery, and per-model reasoning effort.
- Issue claims: an issue someone has claimed on the issue itself (a `hive-claim` marker comment or an assignee) is withheld from the contribute queue and kick prompts until the claim expires (default 4h TTL); relay agents post a claim comment when they take a lease at a tier that may write issue comments and record it on the lease otherwise, exposed as `claimed_by`/`claim_expires_at` on the withheld listing and the runs API; default off behind `governor.claims.enabled` and the Features toggle ([#8380](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8380)).
- Add run artifact commit trailers and a trace reader that links commits to plan, spec, approval, and audit rationale.
- The `/contribute` onboarding picker now offers Oh My Pi (`omp`) with setup guidance and copy-paste contributor commands for omp users ([#8399](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8399)).

### Changed

- Add deterministic offline finding identity dedupe for retro advisories and duplicate sweep reporting.

### Fixed

- Fixed the mutation boundary dedup replay so a second execution of an already-applied logical operation returns the recorded typed result (status, provenance, and the PR number/URL in CreatePR) instead of an empty result with a nil error; an Unknown first attempt still replays as needs-reconciliation, never as an empty success ([#8347](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8347)).
- Pin with tests that hub-launched agents never receive the dashboard token in their environment, launch MCP flags, or project context; the v5 line has no task-MCP URL, so the reported leak does not reproduce there (#8348)
- Fix live contributor profile sync for trust-tier changes and multi-relay task accounting.

When the fetch does fail, `contributor-agent.sh` now says why on one line - the URL, the HTTP status (or curl exit code) and the reason, including an explicit "HIVE_HUB points at the hub, not a hosted spoke" hint when the response is the hub's HTML landing page - and the 10-minute refresh loop logs every failure and the recovery instead of swallowing both. (#8294)

## 2026-09-22 (v5.8.0)

### Added

- Run stages can now be appended to `governor.work_source` with `run_stages: true`, letting `spec`, `plan`, and `implement` work items enter the contributor queue without fabricating GitHub issues ([#8296](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8296)).
- Add the stage receipt agent report schema and validation contract for runs handoffs.

### Fixed

- A task lease that fails to persist is no longer handed out as if it were durable ([#8287](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8287)). Previously `saveLeasesLocked` logged every write failure and returned nothing, so a contributor could be assigned work whose lease lived only in hub memory; on the next hub restart the grant was gone and the relay resumed against a hub with no record of it. The save now returns its error: an assignment whose lease cannot be written is refused with an explicit `task_unavailable` reason of `lease_persist_failed`, the claim is rolled back so the item is offerable again at once, and the refusal is recorded in the hub decision log. A failed renew persist keeps the in-memory lease (a live task is never revoked over disk state), and revocation still succeeds when the registry is unwritable, so the live registry and the on-disk file always agree about which grants exist (#8287).
- The mutation operation journal now takes the same exclusive cross-process file lock as the claim ledger before every `Begin`, `RecordResult`, and `Reconcile`, reloading the on-disk snapshot under a `.lock` sibling before applying and persisting, so two processes sharing one journal can no longer overwrite each other's recorded external effects; a lock that cannot be taken within the bounded wait surfaces as `ErrJournalLocked` rather than a silent skip or a false success (#8288)

## 2026-09-22 (v5.7.1)

### Changed

- Reviewer independence now keeps one mixed PR queue kick and tells reviewers to delegate each PR to an in-session sub-agent with the annotated review model, instead of restarting the reviewer per model bucket.

## 2026-09-22 (v5.7.0)

### Added

- Add reviewer `review_models` pools so scheduled PR review can choose an independent model from the PR author, record review model pairings, and export Prometheus counters.

### Changed

- The hub Reading List (home, Learn, and /reading pages plus `GET /api/reading-list`) now sources articles from the Hive Commons Substack RSS feed instead of scraping the KubeStellar Medium list page; cards carry a Hive Commons byline, the "View all" link points at https://substack.com/@hivecommons, and the fallback seed lists the articles currently on Substack (#8281).
- Hub pages now identify Hive as a Hive Commons project: the footer, the home page project card, the docs links, and the CNCF reference-architecture page point at hivecommons.dev and docs.hivecommons.dev instead of KubeStellar (#8281).

## 2026-09-22 (v5.6.1)

### Fixed

- The docs index now names v5 as the current line and uses branch-agnostic relative links for its local references, so v5 readers are no longer routed back to v4 content ([#8275](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8275)).

## 2026-09-22 (v5.6.0)

### Added

- Add a Governor PRs-by-model tile, cached attribution aggregation API, and Prometheus PR outcome series.
- Settings → Features can now configure `governor.rotation`, including provider/backends mappings, agent tiers, thresholds, and live provider headroom readings, so operators can manage provider rotation without editing `hive.yaml` ([#8257](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8257)).

### Fixed

- ACMM pack apply now reconciles `on_demand` for existing pack agents (like `kick_template` and `mode`), starting or stopping the process on a flip. A reviewer created by the older on-demand pack definition stayed on-demand after the pack moved to the cadenced queue design — the new template landed, nothing ever kicked it. An `on_demand` set from the agent settings dialog is operator-owned (`on_demand_owner`) and is not touched.

## 2026-09-22 (v5.5.0)

### Added

- Settings -> Features now exposes the formal-verification quality-lane opt-in, including ACMM L5+ gating and durable `quality.formal` persistence ([#8256](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8256)).

### Fixed

- Add the missing v4→v5 operator migration guide linked from ROADMAP.md, covering the v4 EOL window, channel re-base, additive config deltas, deployment upgrade steps, verification, and digest rollback guidance (#8255).

### Security

- Bump the bundled GitHub CLI from 2.74.0 to 2.101.0. The 2.74.0 binary was built with Go 1.23.5, golang.org/x/crypto v0.38.0 and google.golang.org/grpc v1.72.0, which cluster image scanners (Red Hat ACS) report as 8 Critical CVEs including CVE-2026-33186 and CVE-2026-46595. The CVEs live in the gh binary, not in hive's own module graph (hive has no x/crypto dependency and already builds against grpc v1.83.2). gh 2.101.0 is built with Go 1.27.1, x/crypto v0.57.0 and grpc v1.83.2, clearing every finding. Checksums pinned from the upstream `gh_2.101.0_checksums.txt`.

- Improve TUI readability with pane zoom, responsive grid layouts, leaner chrome, wider hives overlay columns, and expanded theme palette.

### Fixed

- Fix Esc in the hives-only contributor TUI so it quits instead of closing to a blank screen.
- Review relay suppresses the comment (verdict still recorded) of a further top-level review on a PR head that already carries its quota of hive reviews (1 in combined mode, one per perspective otherwise, or `review.max_reviews_per_head`), exempting `--revise`, `--thread` and APPROVE; `review-links.json` now records the head each review was posted at, and `${PR_LIST}` marks `[hive-reviewed: …]` from that ledger too, so a review whose verdict could not bind to a dispatch no longer triggers a re-review every kick.

## 2026-09-22 (v5.4.1)

### Fixed

- Review relay refuses a request whose `--verdict-file` fails validation **before** posting the comment, and reports the exact error plus a full example object in `.result.json`; `hive-review` runs the same key check client-side. `reviewer-queue.md` now carries the verdict schema it used to only refer to, and `${PR_LIST}` marks PRs already judged at their current head as `[hive-reviewed: <verdict>@<sha>]` so the cadence reviewer stops re-commenting the same PR every kick (one PR collected six duplicate notices in two hours).

## 2026-09-22 (v5.4.0)

### Added

- Add `docs/repositories.md`, the authoritative list of hivecommons subproject repositories with intent, status and whether each ships in a Hive release, linked from the README, closing OpenSSF Baseline OSPS-QA-04.01 (#8212).
- Add an OpenSSF Security Insights `security-insights.yml` (schema 2.1.0) at the repo root declaring the project's repositories, administrators, vulnerability reporting, license and distribution points, so LFX Insights can read the subproject list for OSPS-QA-04.01 and the distribution channel for OSPS-BR-03.02 (#8217).

- Hosted-spoke Deployments now set `revisionHistoryLimit: 2` instead of inheriting the Kubernetes default of ten. Each `:stable` roll left another scaled-to-zero ReplicaSet behind, and a pod stuck Pending under an old one kept a retired image reference (including the pre-transfer `ghcr.io/kubestellar/hive` tag) visible to cluster security scanners long after the live pod had moved on. Existing spokes pick the limit up on their next provision apply; operators can patch it in place with `kubectl patch deploy hive -n hive-hosted-<id> -p '{"spec":{"revisionHistoryLimit":2}}'`.

### Security

## 2026-09-22 (v5.2.2)

### Fixed

- Harden hub SHA poller test isolation so leaked background pollers cannot mask first-tick cache changes.

## 2026-09-22 (v5.2.1)

### Fixed

- Fixed review submissions stalling in retry with "operation effect is already applied": a second review whose text matched an earlier one on the same PR (the common "no findings" pass on a newer head) was refused as a replay. Each request file is now its own logical operation, the mutation boundary treats a genuine replay as idempotent success, and it releases the claim on every exit so one stuck mutation no longer exhausts the repo's writer slot.

### Security

- The legacy dashboard no longer serves each contributor's plaintext registration token to anonymous callers ([#8165](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8165)). `GET /api/contributors` and `GET /api/contributors/:id` spread the raw stored profile — including `registration_token_plain` — into the response, so any local process (or any remote caller with `HIVE_DASHBOARD_BIND=0.0.0.0`) could enumerate every contributor's live credential in one request, defeating the earlier `/api/contribute/register` fix (#8102). Both endpoints now serve a sanitized view that strips the plaintext token, matching the Go dashboard's `TokenPlain` handling, and the unauthenticated `PUT /api/contributors/:id/trust` / `POST /api/contributors/:id/revoke` mutations are now gated by the same `requireLegacyOwnerRole` check the Nous endpoints gained in #8103 — anonymous callers can no longer promote themselves to a higher trust tier or revoke legitimate contributors.

### Added

- `hivectl hives export`, `import`, and `session` now move a named hive profile as a passphrase-encrypted bundle and create separate named session profiles for running two relays against one hive (#8127).
- Add unit tests for the spoke `ProjectConfigCallback` (project-claim reconciliation over heartbeat) covering vanity-URL-only pushes, misconfigured repo-target refusal, idempotent echo, author/filter preservation, and wrong-forge `api_url` refusal (#8153).

## 2026-09-21 (v5.1.0)

### Added

- `hivectl hives use` now switches a running contributor relay to the newly active hive without a restart by signaling the relay to reload its generated `contributor.env`; the relay records non-secret hub last-seen timestamps for `hives list` and lets any in-flight task finish on its original hive before soliciting from the new one (#8126).

## 2026-09-21 (v5.0.0)

### Added

- Added contributor capability-aware routing for explicit task requirement labels, while preserving assignments for undeclared clients and documenting the self-reported nature of the data.
- Added the accepted RFC #4002 re-entrant conversation-as-state design and restored its phased roadmap, closing the v5 spike while deferring production rollout to v6 follow-ups.
- Added hive-wide and per-repo `self_authorization_hold` switches for the #5117 self-authorization hold, defaulting on while allowing opted-out repos to skip new holds and safely release existing #5117-marked holds without touching human holds.
- Operators now have a public HiveCommons migration tracker covering org/package phases, dual-publish promises, communications checkpoints, and remaining gaps before any kubestellar namespace deprecation ([#5686](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5686)).
- Added RFC #5691 documenting constellation hub/spoke coordination, including the repo-overlap phase delivered by #5705 and follow-on charter, headroom, App-budget, credential, and routing contracts.
- Added RFC #5698 documenting backend capacity readings, model inventory, pacing, operator policy, and opt-in placement for backend/model selection.
- Capture MITM Copilot completion usage as timestamped live sessions so `/api/repo-cost` can attribute active Copilot spend without double-counting shutdown totals.
- Made the hub public URL, provisioned spoke domain, and optional legacy SSO cookie domain configurable while preserving the existing hive.kubestellar.io defaults.
- The MITM proxy can now inject GitHub authorization itself, so agents never hold a usable token ([#1861](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/1861), ported from [#4032](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/4032)). Opt-in via `HIVE_PROXY_INJECT_GH_AUTH=true`, default OFF: with the flag unset, token delivery and proxy behavior are unchanged. When enabled, the hub diverts each agent's real scoped token to an in-memory registry and writes only a placeholder (`hive-proxy-injected-<agent>`) to the agent's cache file; the proxy strips whatever Authorization an agent sends and injects the UID-identified agent's real token (`token <t>` for REST, `Basic x-access-token:<t>` for git). An unknown agent gets no credential at all — failing loud rather than borrowing another agent's identity — internal hub callers pass through untouched, `/login/...` paths are strip-only, and injection widens MITM interception to all GitHub-family hosts so no tokened request can tunnel past uninspected.
- The hub now watches the fleet wildcard certificate on every cluster that serves its spokes from one ([#5977](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5977)). Opting a cluster in with `wildcard_tls_secret` means provisioned spoke Ingresses carry no `tls:` block of their own, so a single certificate stands behind every hosted dashboard there — roughly 263 hostnames across the two clusters in the issue — and a renewal that silently fails takes all of them down at once instead of one. Each cluster-health build now reads the ingress-nginx default SSL flag and asserted secret (read-only, and only on opted-in clusters) and reports it as `wildcard_tls` in `/api/cluster-health`, rendered on the fleet-health cluster row: `expiring` under 21 days, which means renewal is overdue rather than merely upcoming, since cert-manager begins renewing a 90-day certificate at 30 days out; plus `expired`, `missing`, `domain_mismatch`, `not_served` and `unreadable`. This is also the first check anywhere on the opt-in itself: `wildcard_tls_secret` is an operator assertion the provisioner cannot verify — it has to decide without a cluster round-trip — so "the flag is set and the secret is not there", "ingress-nginx is not serving it as the default certificate", and "the certificate does not actually carry `*.<cluster domain>`", were all silent until someone opened a dashboard and got ingress-nginx's self-signed default. A healthy certificate renders nothing, and a cluster the hub cannot reach reports nothing rather than a reassuring `ok`.
- Fleet health now carries output-freshness telemetry so L3-L6 no-write verdicts explain whether kicks are broken, intentionally idle, advisory-only, budget-suppressed, or queued work is not writable ([#6036](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6036)).
- A repository can now be paused on its own, quieting one repo without stopping the hive ([#6203](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6203)). Until now an operator could stop one *agent* (everywhere) or stop *everything* (the fleet breaker); a release freeze, an incident, or one repo whose CI was red for an unrelated reason therefore cost the whole fleet — or cost the repo its place in `project.repos`, which loses its dashboard card and its ACMM eval, records nothing about who removed it or why, and reads as permanent. Pause is a run-state instead: the repo stays configured, scored and visible, and only agent activity stops. Set it from the new ⏸ button on each REPOSITORIES card, from `POST /api/repos/pause`, or as `project.paused_repos` in config; each pause records who, when and why (#4055's provenance, now for repos) and survives restarts. Enforcement is deterministic rather than a prompt instruction — the MITM proxy answers every agent write to a paused repo with a 403 whatever ACMM mode the agent holds, the `hive-open-pr`, `hive-merge`, `hive-open-issue` and `hive-review` relays refuse agent requests (including issue/PR comments, claim labels and every review event, because the hive's own fulfilment never traverses the proxy), work enumeration yields nothing for the repo so no kick can hand an agent work on it, and the auto-merge sweeps skip it. Reads stay open on purpose, as do the hive's own control-plane calls and anything a human does. Additive: a hive with no paused repos behaves exactly as before.
- An agent can now be scoped to the repositories it serves, so which agents exist is a per-repo answer instead of a hive-wide one ([#6204](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6204)). Hive could already vary what an agent KNOWS per repo — `AGENTS.md` injection, repo-local skills — but not which agents there are, so in a hive holding a Go service next to a Rust CLI next to a Terraform module a specialist added for one of them woke on cadence and hunted for its concern in all the others: inference spend and issue noise on repos that never wanted it. Set `repos:` on an agent (in `hive.yaml`, in the dashboard's agent config dialog, or via `PUT /api/config/agent/{name}/general`) and it is handed work only on those repos, its kick lists only those repos, and its `$HIVE_REPO`/`$HIVE_REPOS` follow. Omit it — the default, and every agent in every existing config — and nothing changes. Enforcement is deterministic rather than a prompt instruction: the MITM proxy answers an out-of-scope agent write with a 403 whatever ACMM mode it holds, and the `hive-open-pr`, `hive-merge` and `hive-open-issue` relays refuse to fulfil one (they must: the proxy hard-denies direct PR creation and merge for every mode, and the hive's own fulfilment never traverses the proxy). Reads stay open on purpose, as does the hive's control plane. The bring-your-own-agent contract gained the same `repos:` key as an OPTIONAL interface rather than a sixth `AgentSpec` method, so no existing third-party spec stops compiling. The field carries the `repos_owner` marker the model/backend/pause fields already have, so a future ACMM pack cannot silently widen a specialist back to the whole hive.
- Hosted-spoke rollback is now a first-class hub operation. `POST /api/saas/hives/{id}/pin-digest` (owner-only) holds a spoke at one immutable image digest, given either as `sha256:...` or as the short git SHA the My Hives page shows (the hub resolves it to the manifest digest), and applies it through the same `kubectl set image deployment/hive "*=..."` path the upgrade code uses. The pin is a run-state on the hive record with who/when/digest/reason, so it survives hub restarts, shows on the dashboard as a PINNED pill with its provenance, and is recorded on the hive timeline. While it holds, the tracked-channel re-arm, auto-upgrade, and every armed heartbeat directive leave the hive alone, and the upgrade / branch-switch endpoints refuse with 409 naming the pin; `POST /api/saas/hives/{id}/unpin-digest` lifts it and returns the hive to its channel or branch tag. Previously the only rollback path was a raw `kubectl` bypass with no provenance ([#6268](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6268)), and even that was undone on the next heartbeat because the channel re-arm honoured only the admin upgrade pause ([#6267](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6267)); together they left rollback effectively unsupported ([#6290](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6290)).
- Sandboxed agent kicks can now run as a Kubernetes `Job` instead of a rootless Podman container on the hive pod's own node ([#6311](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6311)). Set `sandbox.runtime: job` on an agent (or `agent_sandbox.runtime: job` globally) and describe the workload under `job:`: the image, a `node_selector`, `resources` limits such as a device count, `tolerations`, `env_from_secrets`, extra PVC `volumes`, and a `ttl_seconds` for the finished Job. This is how an agent's kicks reach a different runtime than the hive image and a node with accelerator hardware, the roadmap's "Kubernetes-native agent sandboxes" direction. The executor is unchanged: hive clones and branches the workspace on its own data PVC as it does for Podman, the Job mounts that same claim (`job.workspace_claim`, which must be ReadWriteMany when the Job lands on another node), and after the Job exits hive reads the commits back and the existing push broker and PR path take over. The credential boundary is stated rather than implied: the Job receives only the Secrets named in `env_from_secrets`; hive's brokered GitHub token never enters it, so a Job cannot push or open a PR itself. Logs, exit code, timeout, and the PR link land on the agent card like any sandboxed kick, and the finished Job is left in place until its TTL on failure so an operator can inspect it. The spoke ServiceAccount needs a Role for `batch/jobs` and `pods`/`pods/log`; the standalone kustomize base and the hub provisioner now grant it. `pkg/kubejob` is the launcher, `config.AgentSandboxGateWarnings` names a job-runtime agent with no claim or an unknown runtime at boot and on reload.
- Advisory dashboard rows show creation and last-seen times, existing evidence freshness warnings, and server-resolved OPEN/CLOSED/MERGED state for explicitly referenced GitHub work. Unlinked findings say "No linked remediation"; unavailable lookups remain unknown. Advisory retirement and cached-replay aging are unchanged ([#6318](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6318)).
- Repository cards now preserve raw GitHub issue and pull-request totals while showing the actionable, hold, advisory, dependency-dashboard, draft, filtered, and fallback work that comprises them ([#6320](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6320)).
- Contributor relays now have a contributor-owned quota-headroom guard that evaluates normalized capacity windows before accepting work, with documented reserve environment variables and a launch-time `off` opt-out ([#6833](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6833)).
- Contributor quota guard: add scoped override controls and a cross-process quota-pool store (kubestellar/hive#6953). `ask` mode now presents four scoped controls when it holds — continue-once, continue-until-reset, disable-session, and pause-until-reset — reachable on a detached relay through the new `just contribute-quota …` command path, and each expires mechanically (one assignment, the window's reset epoch, or session exit) so no override silently becomes a standing authorization to spend. An optional pool store, enabled with `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_POOL_DIR`, keys guard state to the local quota pool via atomically-written files so two relays sharing one provider account reserve against each other instead of independently oversubscribing the configured reserve; the pool key is a hash that exposes no raw account identifier. Overrides never bypass an unknown/unreadable reading and never enable paid credits.
- Added a dashboard release-line drift alarm (#6960): the status payload now reports how far the hosted edge line (`v5`) is behind the stable default branch (`v4`), flagging drift above a configurable `HIVE_RELEASE_LINE_LAG_MAX` threshold (default 5) and rendering `unknown` — never a healthy zero — when the compare cannot be measured, so a stalled v4→v5 sync can never go unnoticed again.
- Codex contributor-quota readings now fold in every scoped limit from the provider's `rateLimitsByLimitId` alongside the `primary`/`secondary` windows, deduping any entry that repeats a positional window's `limitId`, so an exhausted scoped limit binds the reading instead of hiding behind roomier windows; each window carries its `limitName`, and a recorded-shape fixture (codex-cli 0.154.0 `RateLimitSnapshot`) exercises the full documented schema. (#6964)
- Contributor quota readings from Claude Code are now decided and hardened (kubestellar/hive#6965): the adapter documents that it reads the HTTP `/api/oauth/usage` source rather than the status-line JSON #6833's table named, and #6833's adapter table is amended to match with the reason. A usage payload the build does not recognize — an empty or percent-less `limits` array — is now reported as an explicit error that enters the configured unknown-data behaviour instead of a confident, permissive full-headroom reading. Each window carries its documented duration so a reading matches #6833's shape and the shared window banding applies, the most-used window binds, and windows keep their reset timing. A schema-derived usage fixture ships for the parse path, to be replaced once a real recorded payload is available. Obtaining a reading sends no model prompt. (#6965)
- Contributor quota readings from Agy (Google) are now normalized from the CLI's documented structured status-line `quota` map (`remaining_fraction`, reset fields, plan tier) instead of scraping the decorative `/usage` text with a regex (kubestellar/hive#6966). Emitted windows now carry their reset time so the guard's terminal message can show it, each window's kind is derived from its duration via the shared banding, the most-used window binds, and the plan tier is surfaced. Structured output is capability-detected: a CLI too old to emit it, or any payload that does not carry the documented `quota` map, is reported as an explicit error that enters the configured unknown-data behaviour — replacing the scraper's confident-wrong-number failure mode with an honest unknown. A schema-derived fixture ships for the parse path, to be replaced once a real recorded payload is available. (#6966)
- ✨ Publish normalized rotation quota readings to where the contributor quota guard reads them (kubestellar/hive#6967): the Go probers atomically write a per-pool reading, a probe error publishes `unknown` (never a fabricated healthy reading), and a supported subscription backend with a configured pool directory now holds on a missing/torn reading instead of running inert.
- The rotation manager gains a Copilot contributor-quota adapter ([#6980](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6980)): `CopilotProber` reads the documented enhanced-billing endpoint `GET /users/{username}/settings/billing/premium_request/usage` through `gh api` and normalizes the calendar-month premium-request window (duration, reset on the first of the next month UTC). Copilot was the one first-class backend with no prober, so once the guard flips from `unprovisioned` to enforcing ([#6967](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6967)), Copilot contributors would have been left at "guard unavailable" — on the backend where a misread is a bill, not a wait. The endpoint reports **consumption only**, so a remaining percentage exists only when the operator states the plan's included allowance in the new `rotation.providers.<name>.monthly_allowance` config field; without it the probe reports an explicit unknown carrying the consumed count, never a guessed percentage. `netQuantity > 0` (billed overage) sets the paid-usage signal from a read-only source — `TestNoCopilotBudgetMutation` pins that no code path touches any budget-mutating endpoint. A logged-out `gh`, a token missing the Plan read scope, or an unrecognized response schema each report explicitly and hold as unknown; the emitted `monthly` kind is deliberately governed by the guard's base reserve via the unrecognized-kind path (decision recorded in `src/docs/contributor-relay.md`).
- Hardened the Copilot contributor-quota adapter's safety coverage ([#6980](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6980) follow-up, building on the landed adapter from [#6997](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6997)): added `TestCopilotProbeUsesOnlyGetVerb`, a runtime verb-level pin asserting every gh call a probe issues is a plain `gh api` read — it complements the existing static `TestNoCopilotBudgetMutation` scan and additionally rejects request-body field flags (`-f`/`-F`/`--field`/`--raw-field`) that silently turn `gh api` into a POST, so no code path can spend a premium request or mutate spend. Also added `TestCodexWindowKindBanding`, direct per-band coverage of the shared `codexWindowKind` window discriminator (previously exercised only incidentally), raising it to 100% and pinning every boundary and the deliberate unrecognized-kind tail. Test-only; no behaviour change.
- The contributor quota reading publisher now runs even when provider rotation is disabled (the default): a publish-only manager probes the guard-supported providers and publishes normalized readings, without enabling any rotation decision path. A probe that fails because the CLI is not installed publishes nothing, so hosts without a backend keep the unprovisioned admit ([#6987](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6987)).
- `v5` now cuts its own `v5.x.y` semver tags and GitHub Releases: `tagged-release.yml` is pinned to `v5`, and `derive-release-version.sh` bases the number on the line's own tags only (first tag on a line is `vN.0.0`) so `v4.*` tags never seed a `v5` number (#7721, #6016).
- Add a Spin/Promela model for the contributor lease/reconnect protocol.
- Teach Podman Quadlet spokes to report their own image and tracking mode so release status resolves without a Kubernetes Deployment. (#8066)
- Added per-hive contribute skip labels via `HIVE_CONTRIBUTE_SKIP_LABELS` / `hub.contribute_skip_labels`, with glob matching and a blocked-label floor so decision briefs are never offered as agent work (#8070)
- `hivectl hives` saves the hives you lend a CLI to as **named profiles**, so switching between them no longer means hand-editing `~/.config/hive/contributor.env` or re-running `contribute-setup` ([#8097](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8097)). `hivectl hives list` shows every hive with its contributor id and an active marker (`--check` also probes each hub); `add`, `use`, `rename` and `remove` manage the set. Profiles live in `~/.config/hive/profiles.yml` (mode 0600) and `contributor.env` becomes a generated projection of them, with the active hive first in the `HIVE_HUB` / `HIVE_REGISTRATION_TOKEN` / `CONTRIBUTOR_ID` lists — the hub the relay solicits from at startup. The relay, Compose and `contribute-k8s` read exactly the variables they always have. The first `hives` command on a machine with the old positional file migrates it, naming entries after their hub host and keeping the first hub active so a running relay is unaffected; a file whose three lists disagree in length is refused rather than guessed at, because pairing a token with the wrong hub points a live credential at the wrong hive. Registration tokens are never printed in any output format, and `remove` requires you to type the hive name because the hub cannot reprint the token it discards. Switching a *running* relay without a restart, `export`/`import`, and the TUI pane are the later phases of the same issue.
- `project.writing_guide` now reaches the contributor relay's task prompt, so an owner who sets a guide gets it on the PRs contributors open for their repos and not only on the PRs their own agents file ([#8124](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8124), extending [#7667](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7667)). The relay's prompt is built in Go rather than from a policy file, so it never expanded `${WRITING_GUIDE}`; it now takes the rendered guide from the assigning hub and places it immediately before the instruction to open the PR — the same position that made the setting work on the template path, next to the step that writes the body it governs. The guide belongs to the hive that owns the task, so a relay subscribed to two hives gets each hive's guide on that hive's tasks. A hive that sets no guide ships a byte-identical prompt.
- The terminal dashboard grew a **Hives pane** ([#8128](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8128), phase 4 of [#8097](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8097)). `hivectl tui`, then `H`, lists the hives this machine lends a CLI to — the named profiles from [#8115](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8115), active one marked, with the same reachability probe `hivectl hives list --check` runs. `enter` switches the active hive, `a` adds one (name and hub, then the registration POST), `d` removes one after you type its name, and `r` renames. It is the same list in the same order as the CLI's because it calls the same `pkg/hivectl` functions: switching from the pane leaves `profiles.yml` and the generated `contributor.env` in exactly the state `hivectl hives use` would. As with the CLI, a relay that is already running keeps its current hub until it restarts, and the pane says so.
- The five profile mutations (`use`, `add`, `rename`, `remove`, and the "profiles.yml before its projection" commit) and the two contributor-hub calls (register, reachability probe) moved out of `hivectl`'s cobra command bodies into `pkg/hivectl`, so the CLI and the TUI share one implementation of the rules that are easy to get subtly wrong in a copy — re-electing an active profile on removal, carrying the active marker through a rename, and never leaving a `contributor.env` describing hives no file records.
- A repository can now declare in `.acmm.yml` that an ACMM criterion is satisfied somewhere other than the file the criterion looks for, and the dashboard counts it while marking where the capability actually lives. The ACMM evaluation detects capability by file existence, which cannot distinguish a repo that never built something from a repo that deliberately moved it off-repo — so a maintainer who removes a workflow for a good reason is scored as having lost the capability, and the cheapest way to restore the score is to put the file back. That happened concretely: `Danathar/sensi` deleted `.github/workflows/ai-fix.yml` — an in-repo agent job holding `contents`/`issues`/`pull-requests`/`id-token` write plus an API key, whose `ai-fix-requested` label gate turned out to admit whatever the issue-filing bot labelled rather than expressing a human decision — and handed that work to hive, which was already doing it at L4 across one trust boundary instead of two. Two L4 criteria (`acmm:ai-fix-workflow`, `acmm:copilot-review-apply`) name that one filename, so the security fix alone took L4 from 9/9 to 7/9. A waiver names the criterion, what satisfies it instead, and why; all three are required, and one that cannot say where the capability went is refused. Crucially a waiver **cannot advance a level**: level pass/fail is computed on detected criteria alone, so a repo that waives an entire level shows a full ratio, still does not pass it, and does not move its codebase level — waivers close the distance between *passing* and *full green*, and nothing else. Waived criteria stay visible: a chip on the row, the justification above the pattern list, and a red asterisk on the level line naming what was waived. Repos without an `.acmm.yml` pay no additional GitHub calls, since the root listing the evaluation already fetches settles it. See `src/docs/acmm-waivers.md`.
- BYO-agent specs are now wired into v5: agents can set `agent_spec` to load an ADR-0012 spec at launch, and `hivectl agent specs list|search` exposes the skill registry discovery surface ([#5910](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5910)).
- New `github.app_signed_commits: true` makes every agent-opened PR carry a commit GitHub itself signed. Agents commit with plain git and cannot sign — a GitHub App has no account to hold a key — so a base branch with a `required_signatures` ruleset blocked every agent PR from merging no matter who approved it (observed: eight open, approved, green PRs all at mergeable_state "blocked"). With the flag on, the PR-request watcher re-authors the head branch through the `createCommitOnBranch` GraphQL mutation with the App installation token before opening the PR: one commit, GPG-signed by GitHub and shown as Verified, authored by `<app_slug>[bot]`, same tree, the agents' original messages and DCO trailers as its message. Changes the mutation cannot express (file modes, symlinks, submodules), oversized changes, and a head that moved under the rewrite fall back to the agent's own push with the reason in the request's `.result.json` (`signed_skipped`) and the hive log; the PR is never blocked by the step. Off by default. The DCO trailers copied into the signed commit are re-addressed to the bracket-free `<slug>@hive.kubestellar.io` form the pane identity uses since [#6276](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6276), so a pane still signing off as `<slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` cannot reintroduce [#6251](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6251) through the re-author; the commit's GitHub-stamped App-bot author is exempt from DCO as a Bot-type account. See github-app-setup.md.
- Hosted spokes at ACMM L5+ now get a larger CPU tier (1 CPU request / 4 CPU limit, up from 250m / 2). The high-level packs run 7+ agents with four CLIs active at once, which pinned the pod at the 2-core limit (71% of cgroup periods throttled on console-4vkt) and slowed the dashboard to a crawl. New provisions render the tier from the requested level; existing spokes grow themselves in place on the next level apply (startup, hub delivery, or operator set-level), which rolls the pod once. L4 and below are unchanged.
- Surface agent restart storms as hosted-fleet problems and add per-agent restart-counter resets from `/fleet`.
- Wire convergence mutation fencing and journaling around external PR, issue, comment, merge, label, review, and sandbox branch-push effects.
- Hive now prunes CLI session-state directories older than a retention window (7 days by default, `data.session_retention_days`; set it to `0` to disable). Every Copilot CLI invocation creates a session directory under `/data/home/.copilot/session-state`, every agent on a spoke shares that directory because they all run with `HOME=/data/home`, and nothing ever deleted them — one long-lived spoke had accumulated ~9,400 directories spanning three months, at a steady 150-200/day. That is an unbounded leak of the shared `/data` PVC, and because the directory is read on session start it made every agent slower as it grew. The janitor runs at startup and every 6 hours, and decides age from the newest write anywhere inside a session rather than the directory's own mtime — on NFS a directory's mtime does not change when a file inside it is appended, so trusting it would delete sessions that are still live. Note that `data.session_retention_days` shorter than the token scanners' 30-day window necessarily truncates dashboard token history, since a deleted session cannot be counted.

### Changed

- Routed the remaining merge-queue and plan-from-label ACMM gates through the tool-approval desk when enabled, preserving legacy decisions while adding the explicit RFC #4000 operation surface.
- Split the embedded SaaS dashboard document into focused same-package HTML constants so dashboard work no longer concentrates in one oversized file.
- Added a SaaS package ratchet test to keep future hub SaaS files split instead of regrowing into a single conflict-heavy surface.
- Reduced `pkg/dashboard` coupling by hiding scheduler access behind a dashboard-owned interface and ratcheting the package's internal import count.
- Operation idempotency keys now use `pkg/convergence/mutation` as the canonical derivation point, leaving `pkg/turn`'s duplicate journal as a deprecated compatibility wrapper while the unwired turn prototype migrates.
- Extracted the agent manager terminal/tmux seams behind a nil-safe TerminalSession boundary while preserving the existing tmux behavior.
- Split `pkg/config/config.go` into topical load, env, defaults, validation, persistence, Kubernetes, and core type files without changing behavior.
- Removed the remaining unwired delegation token lifecycle and mint HTTP authenticator/server code while preserving live delegation key publication and agent token minting paths.
- Removed the unused hub wrap-key prototype code; no runtime path read or wrote the sealed-master records.
- Documented `PUT /api/config/agent/{name}/models` as the path to use when changing an agent's backend **and** model together, and why doing it as two calls is a live footgun ([#5698](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5698)). `POST /api/switch/{agent}/{backend}` followed by `POST /api/model/{agent}/{model}` has no transaction across the two requests: if the second fails, times out, or is never made, the agent is left holding the new backend and the previous backend's model. The docs now spell out that the atomic route applies the pair in one request, does not restart the agent, and still has the phase-2 model-validation gap called out by the RFC.
- The release-channel docs now publish a v4 stable soak proposal that separates fast candidate retags from deliberate stable promotion, giving operators clear guardrails for burst release days and emergency exceptions ([#5744](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5744)).
- Port the accepted constellation and backend-capacity roadmap anchors and tunaos.org production-adopter entry to v5.
- The v4 Go module and repository references now use `github.com/hivecommons/hive`, removing the stable branch's dependency on GitHub redirects from the former `kubestellar/hive` location ([#5778](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5778)).
- The v5 Go module and repository references now use `github.com/hivecommons/hive`, completing the module-path migration away from GitHub redirects from the former `kubestellar/hive` location ([#5778](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5778)).
- Removed the unused knowledge maturity detector and its self-contained tests so the package no longer exposes a dead repository-maturity analysis surface.
- Removed the unwired merged-PR curator extraction pipeline and its advertised scheduling/source-list config surface while retaining the live auto-promotion threshold.
- Removed the unreachable legacy tmux-driving launch helpers and their coverage-only tests so pkg/agent keeps only the live per-agent terminal path.
- Removed the unused skill registry query and agent-spec loader surfaces, leaving the live load/resolve-requested/injection path intact.
- Recorded tool approvals as first-class ACMM-gated operations inside re-entrant turn envelopes.
- Added opt-in contributor assignment persistence through the re-entrant pkg/turn envelope.
- Fixed the re-entrant turn rollout's durable ownership primitive and added the explicit default-off turn envelope opt-in gate.
- Documented the v5 re-entrant turn opt-in rollout, soak plan, default-flip migration, and rollback guidance.
- The HiveCommons migration tracker is available on v5 with the completed repository transfer, Go module rename, GHCR package transfer, and sequenced closeout checklist for the remaining migration breakages ([#5811](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5811), [#5817](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5817)).
- Removed the dead spoke-push heartbeat client duplicate from pkg/hub (StartHeartbeat, SendUpgradingHeartbeat, ReportUpgradeFailure, StartTaskStatusPush and helpers); the live client is pkg/hub/spoke since the spoke/hub split.
- Release docs now state the v5 semver policy (semver tags are cut from `v4` only; a `v5` line is deferred until the v5 GA bar closes) and add a digest-verifiable rollback runbook (`src/docs/release-rollback.md`) covering `hive`, `hive-contributor`, and `hive-hub`, with the hub automation to pause first and the digest checks that prove a rollback landed ([#6113](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6113)).
- `NewServer` in `src/pkg/dashboard/server.go` now delegates to `NewServerWithAuth(port, "", logger)` instead of duplicating the 13-field `Server` literal and `registerCoreRoutes()` call, so new `Server` fields only need to be added in one constructor and the test-only path can no longer drift from the production one. No behavior change ([#6132](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6132)).
- Deleted dead legacy scanner variants from `src/pkg/tokens` (`ScanClaudeSessions`, `EnhancedAgentDetector`, `ScanBobSessions`) and the write-only `SetAgentNames`/`ConfiguredAgentNames` state that only the dead detector ever read; the live paths (`ScanClaudeSessionsWithPathDetection`, `ScanBobSessionsWithLogger`, `HiveAgentDetector`) are unchanged and their tests were ported. No behavior change ([#6142](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6142), refs [#6141](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6141)).
- Deleted the dead legacy leaderboard custom-style wrappers `sanitizeCSSURLToken`, `validateLeaderboardCustomStyleSource`, `getLeaderboardCustomStyle` and `sanitizeLeaderboardCustomStyle` from `src/pkg/dashboard/api_leaderboard_style.go`; their only callers were tests, which now exercise the policy-taking variants directly. No behavior change ([#6156](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6156)).
- Delete the dead `LoadStatsConfigWithCfg` and `buildBeads` helpers from `pkg/dashboard/status_builder.go` and their test-only pins; the live status path uses `loadStatsConfig` and `BuildBeadsFromConfig`. (#6157)
- Deleted the dead legacy kick-cadence pipeline (`computeNextKick`, `lookupCadence`, `lookupCadenceForMode`) from `src/pkg/dashboard/status_builder.go` along with the tests that only pinned it; the live status path no longer used any of them. No behavior change ([#6185](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6185)).
- Deleted the dead policy-less scheduler wrappers `enforceIssueText`, `enforceLabels`, `formatIssueList`, `formatPRList` and `substituteTemplate` from `src/pkg/scheduler`; production code already called the `...WithPolicy` variants and the tests now do the same. No behavior change ([#6195](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6195)).
- Removed the unused skill-version constraint lookup from `pkg/skillreg`: `Registry.Resolve(name, constraint)` and its private helpers `satisfies` and `sameMajor` (the `^X.Y.Z` / `>=X.Y.Z` / exact grammar) had no production caller on v5; `ResolveRequested` resolves through `Get` (highest version) and never honoured a constraint, so the grammar advertised version-pinning semantics the system did not implement ([#6200](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6200)). The live surface (`NewRegistry`, `Add`, `Load`, `Get`, `List`, `Search`, `LoadAgentSpec`, `ResolveRequested`, `InjectionText`) is unchanged; `docs/skills.md` drops the `Resolve` row and `docs/design/knowledge-system.md` no longer lists the `curator.go` pipeline removed in #5786 ([#6225](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6225)).
- Deleted the dead `pkg/review` prompt wrappers `BuildPerspectivePrompts` and `BuildSequentialPrompt` (src/pkg/review/prompts.go). Production dispatch builds each perspective prompt directly via `BuildPerspectivePrompt` (dispatch.go), and the sequential wrapper was the self-described "phase-1 sequential fallback" that the parallel fan-out superseded — the only remaining callers were test-only assertions, which are removed with it. (#6209)
- Deleted the dead server-side leaderboard render helpers `trustTierColor`, `trustTierBadgeCSS`, and `rankDisplay` from `src/pkg/dashboard/api_contribute.go`. All three were unreachable from every binary — leftovers from before leaderboard badges rendered client-side — and their tier→colour tables and medal-emoji HTML could silently drift from the real client-side styling. Their only callers were test-only assertions, removed with them. (#6210)
- Removed the dead Anthropic-to-OpenAI forwarder from pkg/proxy (forwardToInference, openAIChatCompletionsURL, flushResponseWriter); the live inference path already handles translation and streaming.
- Removed dead pkg/dashboard/api.go wrappers (refreshAndPersistSync, fetchInferenceModelsForBackend, fetchModelsFromEndpoints, maskToken); live code already calls the Detailed variants directly.
- Delete the production-dead `pkg/hub` spoke alias layer and the byte-identical duplicate hub test copies; hub tests now call `pkg/hub/spoke` directly (#6326).
- The hub SaaS dashboard SPA now lives in `src/pkg/hub/assets/dashboard.html` (served via `go:embed`) instead of four Go raw-string constants, so editors, JS linters, and CI can see the frontend; the served bytes are unchanged ([#6456](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6456)).
- The security self-assessment no longer contradicts itself about the [OpenSSF Best Practices Badge](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14261) ([#6684](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6684)). Correcting the "Open SSF best practices" section left three other passages still asserting the badge was unheld — including the TAG-Security response table at the very top of the document, the most reviewer-visible text in the file, which read "Agreed; being pursued." A document that answers the same question two ways is worse than one that answers it wrongly once, because a reviewer cannot tell which answer was checked. All four passages now state the same verified fact: project 14261, **passing**, 100% of criteria, awarded 2026-08-27, never lapsed, with silver (15%) and gold (22%) explicitly not claimed. The single remaining "not yet held" wording is deliberate and scoped to the paragraph that records the document's own error history.
- The security self-assessment now states correctly that Hive **holds** the [OpenSSF Best Practices Badge](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14261) at the **passing** level — project 14261, 100% of passing criteria, awarded 2026-08-27 and never lapsed ([#6684](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6684)). Two successive revisions of that section had it wrong in opposite directions: the first said it was "not yet assessed whether this is planned", and the correction for TAG-Security review overshot to "not yet held, and now being pursued" — but the badge had already been awarded four days before that review, and `README.md` had been displaying it the whole time. The document's audience is CNCF TAG-Security, so a reviewer working from it would have drawn the opposite of the truth about the project's posture. The root cause in both cases was writing the document from itself instead of re-deriving it from observable state, the same defect that previously left the maintainer count stale; the section now cites the programme's public API and records both errors rather than quietly overwriting them. The badge entry itself was corrected in the same pass: 67 of its criteria justifications — 70 URLs — still pointed at `github.com/kubestellar/hive` and `hive.kubestellar.io`, dead since the move to the vendor-neutral `hivecommons` org, which matters because the per-criterion justifications are the entire evidentiary value of a self-certified badge. All 70 now resolve to the current home and the entry re-verifies at `passing`.
- Contributor quota preflight is now capability-negotiated end to end (kubestellar/hive#6954). The relay advertises `quota_preflight_v1` back to the hub in `capabilities.relay_capabilities` on `auth_response`, and the hub gates the auto-accept credential hold on that advertised token instead of proxying on the relay's declared protocol version — which previously withheld the credential from every relay that declared any version (#6931 never bumped `RELAY_PROTOCOL_VERSION`). Mixed-version behaviour is backward compatible: a relay that does not advertise the token gets pre-#6833 immediate credential delivery, and an old hub that does not advertise the capability leaves an older relay unchanged. The new field is optional, so no protocol-version bump is required and `RELAY_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays in step with the hub.
- Made the contributor quota reading publisher default-on for supported subscription backends (kubestellar/hive#6987, #6967 criterion 1): the Go rotation probers and the JS relay now derive a per-install pool directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/user-config-dir → `hive/contributor-quota`) when `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_POOL_DIR` is unset, so a default install of a supported backend gets a real reading with no hand-configured env var. An explicit `HIVE_CONTRIBUTOR_QUOTA_POOL_DIR` still overrides the location. A missing default reading stays `unprovisioned`/admit (non-stranding) and only a present-but-unhealthy reading holds; the `unprovisioned`→hold flip is deliberately not shipped here so default installs cannot hold forever, and unsupported backends are unchanged.
- Flipped the contributor quota guard's `unprovisioned` admit to a hold wherever a publisher is positively expected (kubestellar/hive#6987, condition (b)): the Go reading publisher now writes a per-pool presence marker (`<poolKey>.publisher.json`) when its probe loop starts and refreshes it with every published reading, and the JS relay holds on a missing reading in the derived default pool dir whenever that marker is fresh (mtime within the reading TTL). Hosts with genuinely no route keep the non-stranding admit: a relay-only machine has no marker, a dead publisher's marker goes stale, and a `not_installed` probe removes the marker in publish-only mode. Unsupported backends are unchanged.
- Agent policy templates now tell agents to scope each issue so a single PR can close it. A finding that enumerated several independent deliverables — N untested files, N directories, a ranked list of gaps — was previously filed as one issue, and since a PR can only land one of those deliverables it had to write `Refs #N`. The issue stayed open after the work merged, so the backlog grew regardless of how much actually shipped: measured across six repos, 187 of 293 open issues were older than a week, and of 23 issues sitting behind a merged `Refs #N` claim, not one was closeable. The `## Opening Issues` section of all 18 templates that have one now asks for one issue per deliverable, or — where the work genuinely cannot be split — a `- [ ]` task list giving the issue a completion criterion a later reader can check, instead of a judgement buried in prose (#7066).
- Release channels moved to the v5 line (#7721 Phase 1): every green `v5` build now retags `candidate` and `:latest`, `stable` is promoted from the v5 candidate by `promote-stable.yml` after soak, and `edge` now follows `v6`. `v4` is a maintenance line publishing only `v4-latest` and short-SHA tags.
- Trusted Go test shards now join the self-hosted runner pool for same-repository CI while fork pull requests remain on hosted runners.
- Trusted CI lanes now target the repository self-hosted runner pool while fork pull requests and privileged release/runtime lanes remain on GitHub-hosted runners.
- The dashboard's coverage percentage now describes the hive's own repo: `HIVE_COVERAGE_BADGE_URL` accepts `repo://<ref>/<path>` to read a badge file from the primary repo through the GitHub App client (works for private repos), SVG badges are parsed as well as shields JSON, and the built-in hivecommons/hive gist is the default only for the flagship project instead of every hive — non-flagship hives used to show the flagship's number, and all dropped to 0 together when that gist broke.
- The v2 CI workflow now runs on the project's self-hosted runner fleet for trusted events, with fork pull requests still routed to hosted ubuntu-latest runners via a same-repo guard.
- Repository references now point at hivecommons/hive and the transferred GHCR image namespace so operators copy current clone, badge, deployment, and update commands.
- Republished the ioscan red-team results after #6714 closed the U05 (fullwidth capital) and U08 (soft hyphen) gaps: the Unicode family is now 8/8 blocked and the overall miss rate drops from 19/43 (44%) to 17/43 (40%). The stability ratchet (`TestRedTeamCorpusOutcomesAreStable`) caught the improvement, as designed.
- Revised the security self-assessment in response to CNCF TAG-Security review: added a deployer-facing threat section, stated that `ioscan` has not been red-teamed and has no measured detection rate, re-scoped log scrubbing as log hygiene rather than an exfiltration control, corrected the SBOM and adopter claims, and replaced the open-questions list with answers.

### Fixed

- Added contributor WebSocket close-correlation telemetry so relay logs carry hub connection ids, close codes/reasons, keepalive ages, and reconnect backoff state for production flap diagnosis.
- Hold-gated PR coordination now explicitly requires fresh `origin/<base>` branches and is covered by regression tests for docs/planning PRs that gain foreign commits while held, so branch drift is surfaced for re-review instead of quietly re-entering merge lanes ([#5589](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5589)).
- The `cmd/hive` heartbeat, duplicate-PR claim ledger, and Nous dashboard state loaders now expose narrow path seams with production defaults preserved, allowing hermetic tests for token-cache freshness, corrupt claim ledgers, and governor artifacts without touching host `/var/run` or `/data` paths ([#5696](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5696)).
- Pinned the live-fleet health detector seams so provider quota, provider spend limits, and missed-cadence agent stalls keep surfacing actionable fleet verdicts instead of falling back to generic blocked/no-output states.
- `GET /api/contribute/activity` now honours its `limit` parameter, and says how much history it actually has ([#5704](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5704)). The parameter was accepted and silently ignored: `limit=5` and `limit=300` both returned the same fixed 50 events. The response now returns the requested number of most-recent events, preserves oldest-first order within that window, and adds `retained` plus `capacity` so callers can distinguish a truncated response from a full ring with older entries evicted or a genuinely short history. Omitted, invalid, or non-positive limits still return everything retained, and requests above the ring size clamp visibly rather than pretending to serve history the hub never kept.
- Dashboard low-coverage seams now let tests exercise GHCR tag checks plus sidebar and audit disk persistence against injected clients and file paths, improving confidence in registry and operator-configuration code without live GHCR or `/data` access ([#5708](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5708)).
- A WebSocket flap no longer aborts the contributor relay's PR review cycle ([#5715](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5715)). After every fifth completion the relay builds a review task for *itself* — a `pr-review-…` id, `number: 0`, no `task_assign` and no server-issued lease — but the reconnect path re-asserted whatever was in `currentTask`, so it claimed a task the hub had never heard of. The hub correctly refused under the server-issued-lease rule and answered `task_revoke: no active lease for this task`; the relay treated that as terminal, stopped the agent, relaunched the CLI and asked for fresh work. The give-away was the log line naming an issue that does not exist: `Reconnected while working on kubestellar/hive#0 — resuming`. On a hive where `1006` closes are routine — 29 in under four hours in the report — a review taking a couple of minutes almost never ran to completion, so PR review coverage silently did not happen. Reproduced twice four months apart, on `claude` and on `agy`. Locally-created tasks are now marked as such: the relay withholds hub ownership frames (`task_accepted`/`task_progress`) for them, because no lease exists for the hub to confirm, and ignores a revoke that names one, because a task no hub ever owned cannot have been handed to another contributor. The review keeps running and still reports `task_complete` and `ready` when it ends. Resume behaviour for real, hub-assigned tasks is unchanged.
- NOTICE regeneration now retries the pinned `go-licenses` install before failing, so transient checksum database stream errors no longer fail the attribution gate without a code or module change ([#5716](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5716)).
- Knowledge PR enrichment now strips the `gh-` namespace from repo-qualified external references before fetching metadata, so multi-repo beads such as `gh-owner/repo#123` enrich from the intended repository instead of caching a silent miss ([#5741](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5741)).
- The design index no longer points operators at removed wrapkey source files or implies wrapped master delivery is partly shipped; it now records the feature as design-only after the unwired primitives were removed ([#5755](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5755)).
- Operators can now discover the major-version upgrade guide from both the repository README and the docs index, so v4 deployments have a visible path to the backup, manifest, and UID guidance needed before crossing release-line boundaries ([#5756](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5756)).
- The Podman CI lanes no longer go red fleet-wide when a runner-image Podman bump changes the `podman info` schema ([#5757](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5757)). The arm64 and rootless lanes read the environment field-by-field with Go templates, and a Go template hard-fails the whole call (exit 125) the moment any field it names leaves the schema — so when the runner rolled a Podman without `.Host.RootlessNetworkCmd`, a report-only field failed the "arm64 image pull and service startup" check on every PR. The environment steps in all three lanes (arm64, rootless, rootful) now make one `podman info --format json` read and extract fields with `jq` fallbacks, so a renamed or removed field degrades to `unknown` in the report instead of killing the lane, while every load-bearing assertion still fails loudly: the rootless network provider is now asserted as the capability the lanes actually need (a `pasta` or `slirp4netns` provider present for rootless containers, derived from the tool entries when the summary field is absent), the rootful lane refuses to run if `store.graphRoot` cannot be read (its post-run isolation check depends on that path), and an unreadable Podman version fails the 4.x floor check explicitly instead of as a bash integer-comparison error. The rootless probe script's environment report line was hardened the same way, field-by-field with per-field fallback, so it keeps its diagnostics on any Podman.
- The GitHub App credential surface now describes the **write path**, and names an org transfer as an org transfer ([#5774](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5774)). When the repository moved from `kubestellar` to `hivecommons`, every agent branch push started failing while issue creation kept working — and nothing said so: `DiagnoseAppAuth` classified solely on the Issues permission, so a hive that could file issues and could not push a single branch reported exactly what a healthy one reported. The diagnosis now also records the grants a pull-request flow actually runs on — Contents (push the branch), Pull requests (open the PR), and Workflows (needed when the diff touches `.github/workflows/**`) — exposes them as `GrantsAgentPushFlow()`/`PushFlowGrants()`, and logs them on **every** credential verdict including the healthy one, since the installation that looks fine is the one worth counting. They are recorded, never enforced: requiring them would flip the read-only advisory tier, which holds Contents: read by design and never pushes, into a fault state for working as intended. Separately, a coverage miss whose shape is a transfer gets a new `repo-moved` state instead of `repo-not-covered`. That mattered because the two need opposite instructions — "tick the repository in the org's App installation" cannot be followed once the repository has left that account, and sending an operator to a settings page for an org the repo no longer belongs to costs them exactly the debugging time the deterministic coverage check was built to give back. The new verdict names where each repository lives now, states plainly that the App, key and installation are all healthy, and fires only when the shape is unambiguous: complete listing, the configured owner entirely absent from coverage, and exactly one covered repository carrying the configured name. Anything less falls back to the previous verdict rather than guessing.
- Dashboard startup coverage on v5 now waits longer for `/api/health` and reports early listener failures, matching the v4 hardening for noisy race-enabled shuffled CI runs ([#5775](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5775)).
- Dashboard startup coverage now waits longer for `/api/health` and reports early listener failures, reducing noisy v4 CI flakes under race-enabled shuffled test runs ([#5775](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5775)).
- The dashboard Repos tab now accepts same-forge `org/repo` entries and GitHub URLs from a new organization as an explicit hosted-hive org migration, while cross-org validation errors explain how to migrate instead of reporting a misleading repo-name shape problem ([#5779](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5779)).
- Fixed the ACMM dashboard panel so repo selection drives the headline readiness, overall, and criteria totals while the aggregate view calls out union semantics and lagging repos.
- Spoke health now treats on-demand/off-schedule stopped agents as idle instead of down, and zero-token checks explain the cause while skipping all-paused or no-due hives ([#6030](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6030), [#6032](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6032)).
- Fleet health now counts only the agents actually named by provider-quota telemetry, surfaces pre-threshold start-failure causes in agent verdicts, and renders structured GitHub App auth failures with App/installation/host details ([#6031](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6031), [#6035](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6035), [#6037](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6037)).
- Fixed a v4 issue request watcher test race by joining watcher goroutines before restoring test globals and pinning PR/issue watcher directories per loop.
- Fixed the contributor WebSocket hub startup path so persisted contributor state is loaded from the configured data directory and nil loggers no longer panic during restore.
- `TestProxyHTTPUpstreamReadError` and `TestProxyHTTPResponseWriteError` now join the `proxyHTTP` goroutine before returning instead of sleeping ([#6110](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6110)). A leaked handler read `responseBodyStallTimeout` while the next test's `shortenBodyStall` wrote it — the data race that failed v4 CI run 33979236903. The v4 fix was dropped from the v4→v5 sync (#6309) to clear a merge conflict with #6233's dead-test deletion; this restores exactly that test-side join on v5.
- The App self-merge sweep now enforces the intent tier gate before squashing its own PRs: it classifies the PR, builds linked-issue and approved-plan evidence, and asks `intent.EvaluateForAppSelfMerge` with the same `BlocksMerge` refusal predicate the human merge-queue lane applies, so a green App-authored PR can no longer merge at a tier the normal path would refuse (for example Tier1 without a linked issue) when `intent.enforce` is on; a missing changed-file list now fails closed ([#6258](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6258)).
- The `review_rejected` hook now fires ([#6259](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6259)). The transition, its typed payload, the model-knob deep link, and the notification rendering all shipped with RFC #4001, but no production code path ever emitted it, so an operator who configured `on: review_rejected` got a validated, registered hook that could never run.
