The emitter is now wired at the approval desk: when an owner denies a queued agent action (`POST /api/approvals/resolve` or `/api/approvals/bulk` with `approved: false`), hive emits one `review_rejected` per denied item after the denial is journaled, carrying the requesting agent, the target repo and PR, the resolving operator as `actor`, the stated rationale as `reason`, the agent's effective backend/model/pin, the ACMM level, and the `model_knob_url` deep link built from `dashboard.public_url` (falling back to `hub.dashboard_url`, then the request host). A replayed resolve (409) and an ID another operator already resolved emit nothing. `hooks.EmitReviewRejected` now takes a `hooks.FireFunc` rather than a `*Dispatcher`, so a surface that reaches the dispatcher through a fire callback can use the typed emitter directly.
- Agent push brokering now rejects empty outgoing commits so CI retriggers cannot reset reviewed PR branches ([#6300](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6300)).
- `TestLeaseRestart_ResumeSurvivesHubRestart` no longer races `t.TempDir` cleanup on v5 ([#6306](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6306)). The websocket disconnect defer writes `ws-state/failed-tasks.json` after the test body returns, and `t.TempDir`'s `RemoveAll` raced that write with `directory not empty`. The v4 fix from #6158 (`waitContribDisconnect`, which blocks on the defer's last observable act before the restarted hub boots) was never carried to v5; this syncs exactly that test-side change, nothing else from #6158.
- The v5 `coverage` gate is green again for `pkg/github/automerge` ([#6308](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6308)). The self-merge intent gate from #6275 landed the package at 87.9% against its 88% floor, turning every v5 PR red regardless of what it touched. Rather than lowering the floor, the previously unexercised gate contracts are now pinned by tests: advisory mode (intent.enforce off) warns and still merges exactly once when the changed-file evidence is unavailable, matching the human merge lane; a gate with no Enforce callback is advisory; removing the gate restores the pre-#6258 sweep without ever consulting the files API; and `ListChangedFiles` refuses nil inputs and pages through the files API so large PRs return a complete list instead of failing closed.
- The spoke dashboard version badge now shows image tracking (`floating`, `pinned`, or `tracking unknown`) beside its linked commit and release channel/build branch ([#6321](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6321)). The tooltip includes the validated Deployment image reference. Channel and tracking use one cached server-side lookup and shared upgrade/drift classification, so malformed or unavailable image references cannot invent a pin; failed discovery can recover on later polls. This change targets v5.
- Restored the v5 `hive validate` pre-flight command and dashboard repository Rescan wiring so both shipped features are reachable again ([#6352](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6352)).
- Dispatch Docker image publishing for the exact commit produced by automated release merges, so release SHAs and moving release-line tags no longer remain unpublished.
- A contributor relay whose provider has refused it on quota now stops asking the hub for work until the quota resets, instead of failing one task per assignment for the whole window ([#6541](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6541)). Detection landed earlier; the remaining defect was what happened next. Every cycle was correctly classified as a fatal provider refusal, and the relay then advertised `ready` and took another task, which hit the same wall seconds later — two rejections 45 seconds apart carrying distinct provider error IDs, so each one genuinely spent a provider round-trip, a hub assignment slot, and a hive issue marked failed, for a window agy itself stated as `Resets in 4h42m28s`. Quota is a property of the provider *account*, not of the task: it applies to every task the contributor could be given, and it expires. The relay now parks the loop — `ready` is withheld at the single point every frame passes through, a pushed assignment is declined immediately so another contributor can take it, and the hold runs to the reset time parsed off the provider's own banner (with a bounded fallback when none is stated, and a cap so a malformed countdown cannot wedge a contributor out of the fleet). The operator gets one clear message naming the provider, the wait, and the remedy, where previously the banner was visible only inside the agent's pane while the log said `[environment]`; and the task failure now reports a provider quota refusal rather than reading like a broken contributor host. Authorization refusals are unchanged: a 403 is not time-bounded, so it still fails fast and the relay stays available.
- Repaired apt egress on the self-hosted CI runners, which had been failing every job that installed `gcc`, `libc6-dev`, or `tmux`. The cluster has no IPv6 egress, but DNS handed apt AAAA-only records for `archive.ubuntu.com`, so it exhausted its timeout budget on unroutable addresses. apt now uses the reachable `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` mirror and forces IPv4. The manifests are recorded under `src/deploy/ci-runners/`.
- `hiddenAgents` now reports agents dropped by the config-only pass of the
  dashboard status builder. Previously an agent present in the config but absent
  from the runtime status map was skipped silently, so a hive with no visible
  cards also reported an empty diagnostic list, making #6581-class reports
  impossible to triage.
- Codex in contributor **container** mode no longer asks for a bubblewrap sandbox the container cannot provide ([#6653](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/6653)). `--sandbox workspace-write` is implemented with bubblewrap, and bubblewrap's first act is to create an unprivileged user namespace — which the contributor container denies under the runtime's default seccomp profile. The result was not a weaker sandbox but no working command at all: every model-generated command died with `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace`, including *both* of Codex's patch-application paths, so the agent had to rediscover a working file-edit mechanism by trial and error on each task (one observed session burned five minutes and seven points of context on failed edits before landing anything). The error text also names a *host* sysctl, sending operators to reconfigure a machine that was never the problem. Hive now resolves the `--sandbox` value at launch instead of hard-coding it: it falls back to `danger-full-access` only when a root-owned marker proves an outer container boundary exists **and** an `unshare` probe proves user namespaces are blocked, and it prints one line saying which posture is in effect. **Local mode is never downgraded** — with no outer boundary there, a blocked probe leaves `workspace-write` in place rather than widening access to the operator's host (#4918). Relaxing the runtime with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` restores `workspace-write` automatically with no variable to set, and the contributor image now ships a real `bubblewrap` so that path uses a distro-maintained binary rather than Codex's bundled fallback. `HIVE_CODEX_SANDBOX_MODE` pins a value and skips the probe.
- Contributor assignment prompts now use valid `gh repo fork` clone syntax with an explicit destination and remote layout, and contributors who own or can push to a repository are sent through a direct-clone workflow instead of an impossible self-fork ([#6654](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6654)).
- Interactive contributors no longer advertise themselves to the hub before their tmux CLI has actually reached a prompt ([#6655](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6655)). The race could let a task arrive during startup, start the progress watchdog against an undelivered prompt, and report an environment failure before the agent ever saw the work; the backend smoke OMP stub now keeps its stdin handle open so the deterministic fixture exercises the same ready-before-work contract.
- A contributor agent can again open a PR whose body mentions authentication ([#6659](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6659)). `bin/gh-wrapper.sh`'s contributor-mode `gh auth` gate matched the substring `auth ` anywhere in the flattened argument string rather than the subcommand, so any `gh` call whose arguments merely *mentioned* authentication was refused — PR bodies, issue titles, commit messages. The trailing space was load-bearing in the worst way: `authfile` passed, `auth file` did not. The reported failure is the shape that matters: a codex contributor finished a `[sec-check]` task about keeping a registry token out of skopeo's argv — the fix replaces `--creds` with an auth *file* — and could not open the PR, because the body said "auth file". Security fixes are exactly the PRs whose bodies discuss authentication, so this systematically killed the last step of the tasks it could least afford to lose: work done, tested, committed and pushed, the slot held, nothing landed. The gate now keys on the parsed `$subcmd` (the same flag-aware parser the merge and mode gates use), so it is exactly as strict as intended and not one argument wider; every `gh auth` form stays blocked, including behind a value-taking flag. `bin/test_gh_wrapper_gates.sh` also now runs against a marker-redirected copy of the wrapper, so it no longer mis-reports eight unrelated cases when run inside a contributor container, where `/etc/hive/contributor-mode` exists and silently turned every "staff agent" case into a contributor one.
- The contributor relay no longer credits a contributor with a PR they did not open, or discards a correct `no_work_needed` verdict because one was visible on screen ([#6662](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6662)). `detectPRURL()` is a regex over the agent's pane and cannot tell a PR the agent **opened** from one it merely **read about** — and `gh pr list` / `gh issue view --comments` both render full URLs, so an agent researching prior art prints plenty of the latter. When it matched one, the relay reported it as this task's `pr_url` *and* the `prURL ? null : verdict` precedence threw away the agent's explicit verdict. That precedence read "a visible PR contradicts 'nothing shippable'", which is true of a PR this task opened and exactly inverted for a PR a maintainer merged a month ago — where the PR is the evidence that makes the verdict correct. It therefore defeated [#3987](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/3987) in precisely #3987's target population, where a merged reference PR is present by construction and the agent must cite it to justify the verdict at all; the issue was then booked as shipped and re-entered the offer pool when no merge materialised. Measured over one 45-minute session, 3 of 10 completions misattributed a third party's already-merged PR and lost a correct verdict, with the split falling cleanly on whether the agent happened to print a bare `#1103` or a full URL. A scraped URL is now a candidate rather than a conclusion: it is checked against GitHub for authorship and recency, a PR that merged or was created before the task started is dropped and the verdict stands, a confirmed PR suppresses the verdict exactly as before, and a PR that cannot be verified (no `gh`, offline, rate-limited) is still reported as an audit trail but no longer silently outranks the agent's own sentinel. The cross-repo fallback — the first PR URL in any repository when none matched the task's — is removed: for a value the hub books cooldowns on, an approximate audit trail is a wrong one.
- The contributor relay's PR review cycle now reviews the contributor's actual open PRs, and only runs when there are new ones to review ([#6664](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6664)). It scoped the review to the repo of the single task that had just finished, and it fired on completions rather than on PRs shipped — so a contributor working across eleven repos had PRs in ten of them permanently unreachable (the cadence is per-five-completions, not per-repo, so coverage never catches up), and a task that correctly concluded `no_work_needed` still advanced the counter while guaranteeing that repo had no new PR. Observed: a cycle whose five triggering completions were *all* `no_work_needed` ran `gh pr list --repo projectbluefin/utah --author @me --state open` against a repo with zero PRs, while twenty open PRs across eleven repos went unreviewed. The cycle is now account-scoped (`gh search prs --author @me --state open`, which spans every repository including PRs from earlier sessions), names the repos work landed in as an ordering hint rather than a filter, and runs only when at least one PR has shipped since the last review — which also skips it entirely when there is nothing to follow up on, without a second API call. A skipped cycle defers rather than starves, and a review cycle's own completion never counts as shipping, so a cycle cannot re-arm the next one off the PRs it was merely reading. The prompt now also asks for `HIVE_VERDICT: complete`: the review cycle was the one task type that never got #5376's completion sentinel, purely because its prompt is assembled in the relay rather than by the hub, so it could previously only finish through the terminal-chrome inference #5353 documents as having produced thirteen separate issues.
- The contributor relay now scans deep pane scrollback for the PR URL an agent
  opened, instead of only the 15-line window it sends upstream as `tmux_output`.
  About ten of those fifteen terminal rows are TUI chrome, so a genuine PR link
  scrolled out of view within seconds and a task that shipped a PR was reported
  as shipping nothing — costing it the correct issue cooldown ([#6667]).
- The contributor relay now debounces startup `needs-login` pane classifications before printing the authentication banner, preventing routine CLI relaunch redraws from paging operators while preserving the banner for persistent login failures ([#6668](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6668)).
- Claude contributor relaunches now keep the host-state deny list as a shell-safe `--disallowed-tools` argument instead of typing the raw `Bash(...)` patterns into the pane shell during fallback restarts ([#6673](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6673)). A queued task delivered immediately after a relaunch can no longer inherit deny-list text as prompt contamination or lose the intended `sudo`/`pkexec`/boot-tool blocks because the launch line was parsed incorrectly.
- The re-file gate added in [#6463](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6463) now keys on the files a finding actually names, so a scanner can no longer slip a rejected finding past it by rewording the prose around them ([#6674](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6674)). The gate identified a finding by every dotted token in its text, which swept in the verification command the run happened to use (`ast.parse` one day, `py_compile.compile` the next), version strings like `3.x`, and a bare `client.py` mentioned in one extra sentence — and since the sets had to match exactly, any one of those was enough to miss. A false positive a maintainer had closed four times had been filed a sixth time with the gate live. Identity is now the set of real paths: dotted attribute and module chains are excluded, a slashless token must carry a known source extension, and a basename folds into the fuller path for the same file when the finding quotes both.
- Hold-gated agents are now told, before they choose work, that they cannot push a change to `.github/workflows/**` ([#6681](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6681)). An `ISSUES_AND_PRS` agent mints its token at the `contributor` tier, which does not carry the Workflows permission, so GitHub rejects such a push server-side — and when the agent is sandboxed the push broker rejects it first. Nothing said so: an agent that found a security fix belonging in a workflow file wrote the exact replacement into an issue and opened no PR, which is the only outcome available to it but is indistinguishable, to the operator, from an agent that chose not to fix it. The kick now states the ceiling and what to do instead, and the `ci-maintainer` and `sec-check` hold-gated policies no longer advertise workflow edits that mode cannot land — `ci-maintainer-holdgated.md` listed `.github/workflows/*.yml` changes as its first capability.
- `just contribute-hive <backend> local` now passes `HIVE_WORKSPACE_DIR` to the agent CLI on the launch line, so the task prompt's `$HIVE_WORKSPACE_DIR/<owner>/<repo>` resolves ([#6707](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6707)). The recipe exported the variable, but that export reached the agent's tmux pane only when `tmux new-session` had to *start* a server. Running the recipe from inside tmux — a normal way to run a long-lived contributor — made `new-session` join the already-running server instead, and the pane inherited that server's environment, which predates the export. The prompt's path then expanded to `/<owner>/<repo>` at filesystem root and `gh repo fork --clone` failed with `could not create leading directories … Read-only file system`, *after* the fork had already been created on GitHub, leaving the agent to recover by hand. `-c "$HIVE_WORKSPACE_DIR"` on the same line sets the pane's working directory and not its environment, which is why it did not cover this. The variable now travels as a `VAR=value` prefix beside the build-cache variables — the technique the comment there already recommends for exactly this reason — and relaunches pick it up too, since the relay reuses the same `AGENT_LAUNCH_CMD`. Container mode was never affected: `contributor-agent.sh` exports the variable and starts that container's own tmux server in the same process.
- The published red-team figures now agree with the corpus in every passage that quotes them. [#6728](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6728) republished the per-family results table after [#6714](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/6714) closed the U+FF29 fullwidth and U+00AD soft-hyphen gaps, but left the prose that summarises those results untouched — so the document's own headline answer still said **37% withheld / 63% reached** and "Unicode steganography is the strongest family (6/8 blocked)" three lines above a table reporting 42% / 58% and 8/8. The stale numbers had also been copied into the docs index and into two places in the CNCF TAG-Security self-assessment, which is the document reviewers actually read. All of them now carry the measured values (42% withheld, 58% reached — 40% no rule fired, 19% fired below the block threshold; Unicode 8/8), and the "where it works" section points at the rule-gap entry rather than implying the family was always perfect. This is the third instance of the same failure mode in this document set — a fact corrected in one passage and left contradicted in its siblings — so the fix was applied as a repository-wide sweep for the figures rather than an edit to the file that happened to be noticed ([#6708](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6708)).
- Closed two gaps that defeated `ioscan`'s unicode steganography detection entirely: fullwidth Latin characters (for example `Ｉ`, U+FF29) were not folded back to ASCII, and the soft hyphen (U+00AD) was not treated as invisible. Either one hid a directive so well that the scanner produced no finding at all. Both families are now handled — the whole fullwidth alphanumeric block folds arithmetically rather than character by character.
- The contributor relay no longer reports chrome-idle as a completed task unless it has seen the agent actually produce task output; an idle pane with an unsubmitted prompt is failed so the hub can re-offer the issue instead of parking it as done.
- The contributor relay no longer reports a task as **completed** when its prompt was never submitted to the agent CLI ([#6717](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6717)). A ~2 KB task prompt is typed into the pane as one `tmux send-keys -l` burst, and a TUI with bracketed-paste handling classifies a burst that fast as *pasted content*: codex collapsed it to `[Pasted Content 1024 chars]` in its input widget and took all three Enters as newlines inside the paste rather than as submit. The agent never ran, the pane therefore never changed, and the `chrome_idle` fallback read that stillness as a finished turn — booking the issue **done** with no commit, no branch, no PR and the checkout untouched, and removing it from the offer queue for good. A false completion is strictly worse than a false failure here, because a failure is re-offered and a completion is never looked at again. Three changes, in the order they now apply: the send path waits for the widget to finish ingesting the burst before submitting, so the Enter is a keypress and not pasted text; it then re-reads the pane and re-sends Enter while the prompt is still sitting collapsed in the widget; and `chrome_idle` may no longer complete a task at all when the prompt is *still* visibly unsubmitted **and** the pane has not changed by a single byte since delivery — that task is reported `task_failed` (`failure_kind: environment`) so the hub re-offers the issue. Both signals are required together, so a CLI that echoes a submitted paste back into its transcript cannot have working tasks failed, and an agent that finished without printing `HIVE_VERDICT` still completes on the fallback exactly as before. A `chrome_idle` completion carrying neither a verdict nor a PR is now also logged as a warning to audit, since that combination is the shape of this bug.
- Fixed the hub's terminal-key constants silently re-declaring the spoke's domain-separation label and env var name as string literals. The hub provisions the terminal signing key and the spoke self-derives it; both feed the same label into the same HMAC, so any drift between the two copies would have made every terminal assertion fail to verify on a live hive. They now alias `spoke.InfoTerminalKey` and `spoke.EnvTerminalKey`, and a guard test rejects re-introducing a literal.
- The post-merge DCO checker now accepts GitHub noreply sign-offs only when GitHub identifies the commit author as that same account, matching the pre-merge DCO app while preserving mismatch failures.
- Evidence-gated task completion: a `task_complete` carrying no PR, no verdict and an explicit `chrome_idle` signal no longer escalates the issue's no-PR cooldown or clears its failure history. Such a completion is not evidence the work was attempted (#6717), and treating it as one walked the cooldown up to the full with-PR window and parked live work. Relays that do not report a completion signal are unaffected.
- The post-merge DCO monitor no longer reports `missing-signoff` for commits
  whose `Signed-off-by:` sits in an earlier paragraph than a trailing
  `Co-authored-by:` block. `check-dco-trailers.sh` parsed only the final
  trailer block (`git interpret-trailers --parse`), so a body shaped
  `Signed-off-by: …\n\nCo-authored-by: …` — which the pre-merge DCO app
  accepts — paged the monitor anyway (#6605 waived one instance; #6755 is the
  recurrence on `v5`). The checker now scans every line of the commit body,
  matching the pre-merge rule; the 8fe6bb34 entry in `DCO_WAIVED_COMMITS`
  becomes a reported `STALE-WAIVER` for maintainer removal (#6755).
- Race-test CI can now install the cgo toolchain from an actions/cache-restored `.deb` archive when Ubuntu mirrors are unreachable, so transient self-hosted runner egress outages no longer fail every shard before tests start ([#6935](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6935)).
- Contributor quota guard: the enforcing (relay) implementation no longer skips quota windows whose kind this build does not recognize, so an exhausted window of a newly-introduced kind holds work instead of admitting it. A guarded relay now re-reads the quota and asks for work again once every reserve is clear, an unreadable or partially-written reading file can no longer terminate the relay, and the idle `ready` hold is evaluated against the base window reserve rather than the simple-complexity reserve. The unwired duplicate `src/pkg/contributorquota` has been removed so there is a single authoritative guard. (#6951)
- Contributor quota guard: a hold caused by a quota window whose kind this build does not recognize now reports `guarded_unknown_window` rather than plain `guarded`, and the operator banner names the kind. The refusal is unchanged — the distinction separates "your quota is low" from "your provider reported a window kind we have not been taught", which is also the signal that any short/weekly reserve override did not apply to that window. Contributor documentation now covers the reading-file contract, the resume timer, the `unprovisioned` state, and why an unrecognized window kind is measured against the base reserve. (#6951)
- Contributor quota readings from Codex are now normalized from the provider's real schema: both the `primary` and `secondary` rate-limit windows are parsed instead of only the first, each window's kind is derived from the provider-stated `windowDurationMins` rather than hard-coded to `weekly`, and windows carry their duration so a reading matches the documented shape. Plan type and whether paid credits are available are surfaced without enabling them, `ordinaryUsageAllowed` is carried as a tri-state that can never be read as recovery, and a payload the build does not recognize is reported as an explicit error instead of a permissive reading. A test pins that no code path invokes a spend or billing mutation. (#6952)
- Contributor tasks now honour a `[vN]` release-line tag that follows a leading lane prefix (`[Tracker] [v5] …`) or template emoji (`🐛 [v5] …`), instead of silently discarding it and basing the work on the hive's own build branch ([#6969](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6969)). `releaseLineFromTitle` now skips a bounded run of leading bracketed lane tokens and decorative emoji/symbol runes and reads the first bracketed release line it finds, while still rejecting a `[vN]` loose in prose (`reviewer lane [v5] follow-ups`), so trackers and RFCs filed from a template route to the branch their title names.
- The pre-merge sign-off attribution gate now rejects a commit signed off by *anyone who is not the pull request author*, not only by a bot ([#6971](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6971)). `check-squash-signoff-attribution.sh` used to flag only bot `Signed-off-by` trailers, so a commit authored by one person but signed off as *another human's* GitHub noreply passed the gate and then squashed into a permanent mismatched-signoff on protected history — exactly what happened to `01bd2469` on `v5` (`author=Andy Anderson <andy@clubanderson.com>` / `signed-off-by=danathar@users.noreply.github.com`), which the post-merge monitor would have caught but the pre-merge gate did not. The gate now resolves the commit author's GitHub login (via the commits API, or `DCO_AUTHOR_LOGIN_MAP` offline) and fails unless at least one sign-off names the person the squash will be attributed to, while still accepting the author's own GitHub noreply and never misreading a `Co-authored-by:` trailer as a sign-off. The noreply-matching and author-login logic the two DCO checkers had each copied is now shared in `src/scripts/lib-dco-identity.sh` so they cannot drift apart again — the drift was how this gap survived. The already-landed `01bd2469` is dispositioned with a post-merge waiver because `v5` is protected and cannot be repaired.
- Contributor quota guard (Agy): a silently-broken Agy adapter is now distinguishable from an unconfigured or absent CLI (kubestellar/hive#6986). Before, a schema drift that stopped the adapter mapping a real, authenticated `/usage` payload reported `unknown` forever — indistinguishable, from the outside, from a host with no agy credentials, so the adapter was dead code that looked alive. Probe failures now carry a cause: `unrecognized_schema` (a `SUCCESS` envelope the adapter cannot map — a dead adapter on a credentialed host), `no_credentials` (a non-`SUCCESS` envelope: the CLI ran but is not serving usage), and `not_installed` (no `agy` on `PATH`). The cause is surfaced in the Headroom's `probe_error_cause` diagnostics and in the published contributor reading's `cause` field. Every cause remains an `unknown`/hold — the categorization never turns a hold into an admit, so the fail-safe direction is intact and `TestAgyHeadroomRejectsUnrecognizedSchema` is unchanged. Gap 2 is closed by recording the CLI-vs-status-line SOURCE DECISION in `src/docs/contributor-relay.md` and marking #6966's status-line-preservation criterion N/A for the CLI path.
- The Agy (Google) contributor quota adapter now parses agy's real `/usage` output and produces a reading again (kubestellar/hive#6986). #6966 modelled the response on field names described in prose rather than a captured payload — a root `quota` key holding a flat `windows` map with `reset_at`/`duration_mins` — and a live capture on agy 1.2.1 shows none of those exist: `--output-format json` is a print-mode response formatter, so the quota data sits under `command.data.groups[].buckets[]` with `window` ("weekly"/"5h"), `remaining_fraction` and `reset_time`, and carries no plan tier. The adapter therefore rejected every real payload and reported `unknown` on a correctly configured host — safe, but indistinguishable from having no agy credentials installed. The capture now ships as the test fixture, replacing the schema-derived guess. The adapter also learns that agy meters **two independent quota pools** (Gemini models vs third-party Claude/GPT models), each with its own weekly and 5h bucket: `AgyProber.Model` selects the applicable pool, and with no model known the worst bucket across every pool binds, so the guard can hold too often but never admit against an exhausted pool. Capability is detected from the response envelope (`command.name == "usage"` with populated `command.data`) rather than from `--output-format json` being accepted, which says nothing about whether `/usage` exists. (#6986)
- The contributor quota relay now timestamps published readings and holds on genuinely stale files while preserving the unprovisioned admit path for hosts with no reading route ([#7002](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7002)).
- The dashboard upgrade button is now deployment-runtime aware for standalone Podman/Quadlet and Docker Compose hives ([#7008](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7008), [#7011](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7011)). Unknown or incompletely configured runtimes no longer relay `Upgrade now` through the Hub/Kubernetes path; they show an honest manual-update state until an explicit runtime and host upgrade helper are configured.
- The release panel no longer claims "Last upgrade: never attempted" on hives that have been upgraded many times. The upgrade marker only records upgrades driven *through the hub*, so any hive moved by other means — a direct image bump, a redeploy, a spoke roll — reported "never attempted" no matter how many times it had actually been rolled, and the accompanying "No upgrade has been attempted on this hive yet" detail line stated it outright. Both lines are now omitted for that state; "succeeded", "failed" and "in progress" still render as distinct states, and the channel selector is unchanged.
- Fixed streaming LLM responses being severed mid-generation after 60s. The MITM proxy armed a single absolute write deadline around the whole response relay, which is correct for a small buffered body but wrong for a stream: `/v1/messages` (Anthropic-shaped) completions do not match the OpenAI-style completions path, so every Claude turn took the plain relay branch and was cut at exactly `httpWriteTimeout` even while tokens were still flowing. Agents saw "Response was interrupted due to a server error", retried the same long turn, and were cut again at the same mark — livelocking them on their longest turns. Response relays now use a rolling per-write deadline (`stallBoundedWriter`, the write-side mirror of the existing `stallBoundedBody`), so the bound is "no progress for 60s" instead of "must finish within 60s"; a client that genuinely stops draining is still released within one stall window.
- Advisory digest posting policy (primary-repo selection, pinned-issue resolution, build/post decisions and the update-interval gate) moved from `package main` into `pkg/advisory`, so it is testable and reusable outside the `hive` binary. No behavior change. (#7238)
- GitHub App credential verdicts moved from `package main` into a new `pkg/apphealth`, so they are testable and reusable outside the `hive` binary. No behavior change. (#7238)
- Inference gateway routing (litellm route resolution, watsonx gateway lookup and auth, endpoint list parsing, local litellm proxy supervision) moved from `package main` into a new `pkg/inference`, so it is testable and reusable outside the `hive` binary. No behavior change. (#7238)
- The login-required detector (pane matching, the credential and consecutive-sighting gates, and the pause/notify loop) moved from `package main` into a new `pkg/loginscan`, so it is testable and reusable outside the `hive` binary. No behavior change. (#7238)
- `derive-release-version.sh` now takes the release line from `RELEASE_LINE` (set by `tagged-release.yml`) and refuses to run on a detached checkout without it, instead of falling through to the global latest tag — which had minted a stray `v4.73.3` from the `v5` branch (release and tag deleted, release commit reverted).
- v5 boot registered the dashboard API twice (injected `registerAPI` plus a direct `RegisterAPI` call), so `http.ServeMux` panicked at startup before the dashboard was ready; the duplicate call is removed (#7802).
- CI: `docker.yml` on this branch no longer pushes `hive-contributor:latest` and `hive-hub:latest` — `INCLUDE_LATEST` is now `false` on all three image rows, matching the `hive` row and the #7721 premise that `:latest` follows v4 until Phase 1 hands it over. Previously the last branch to merge won the tag, so `:latest` served a mixed-version image triplet. ([#7893](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7893))
- Fixed v5 spokes heartbeating with an empty `Reporter` and zero `StartedAt` (the boot split left `boot.reporterName`/`boot.processStartedAt` unassigned), which also left the restart min-uptime guard inert. Identity is now set alongside `startTime` in `bootConfigWith`.
- The hub no longer lists the retired `v2` line under Latest available images, and no longer measures "N behind" against a hard-coded `v4` (#8061, #7721 Phase 1). The stable and edge release lines are now resolved from the `stable`/`edge` channels at runtime, so the next rollover needs no hub code change; the `""` branch fallbacks (heartbeat, bulk upgrade, hub self-identification) follow the hub's own branch, then the stable line.
- Reviewer agents no longer report a secret scrubber's placeholder as a code defect. A review whose evidence quotes masked text — `[REDACTED]`, `<redacted>`, or a bare `******` — is refused by the review relay instead of published, and the reviewer prompts and policies now say that a mask is a hive artifact to re-read from the repository, never a defect in the change under review ([#8067](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/8067)).
- Show typed `<redacted:kind>` markers on sandbox tool output while leaving logs unchanged, and stop scrubbing Bearer format placeholders as secrets (#8067)
- `just check-version` (and every recipe behind it — `contribute-setup`, `contribute-hive`) now compares HEAD against the checked-out branch's own `origin/<branch>` instead of a hard-coded `origin/v4`, so a v5 or v6 checkout at its tip is no longer told to pull v4; the hint names the right branch. `HIVE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK` still skips it. (#8071)
- Make dashboard ApplyPack tests use hermetic UID-map and UID-isolation marker paths so live host state cannot stall them. (#8119)
- The self-authored automerge sweep now skips held, exempt, draft, closed, non-App-authored, and headless PRs from the list response before spending a pull-request GET, aggregates skip logging per tick, and adapts its interval to unusually large post-filter candidate backlogs.
- Classify Bob API-key 401/expired failures as login/credential problems instead of restart-needed agents.
- My Hives `Release channels:` rows now carry each build's commit timestamp and, for a channel that is a plain ancestor of its upstream, how much older its build is than the upstream's (e.g. `↓12 3d 5h vs candidate`); the hub's `api.github.com` reads (branch polling, compares, commit lookups) now send `HIVE_HUB_GITHUB_TOKEN` when set, so the distance column no longer blanks out once the anonymous 60/h budget is exhausted.
- Fixed copilot-backend agents hanging idle after an intermittent model/transport failure. When the Copilot CLI exhausts its own retry budget it prints `Failed to get response from the AI model` and drops back to an empty prompt, but the transient-API-error watchdog could never nudge it: detection required Claude Code's `API Error:` chrome, which copilot never emits, and the idle-prompt check required the prompt marker to be the pane's last non-empty line, which copilot's hint footer makes impossible. Either bug alone stranded the agent until its next cadence kick — on an hourly cadence that is up to an hour of lost work per blip. Both predicates now understand copilot's pane shape, with the copilot error branch still requiring a transport-level cause so non-retryable auth and quota failures are not nudged.
- The coverage percentage read from an SVG badge is now taken from the badge's text, not its markup: a shields-style badge opens with a gradient whose `y2="100%"` attribute was matched first, so a repo at 98.5% showed 100 on the dashboard (follow-up to [#7038](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/7038)).
- Fail closed on retryable GitHub dedupe and label-ensure failures before creating agent-filed issues.
- Store the reviewer's per-perspective verdict reports under the durable data dir (`/data/review-reports`) instead of the container-local `/var/run/hive-metrics`, and retire them on the same 30-day horizon as the verdict artifact. A pod replacement between the relay writing a verdict and the next collect used to lose it, so the reviewer posted the same review on the same head SHA a second time.
- docs(v5-ga): correct two GA-bar rows whose recorded justifications did not survive re-measurement. The soak-window row claimed 8.7 consecutive green days from 2026-09-01T18:41Z, which contradicts its own restart rule — a red run on 2026-09-03T10:02:31Z restarts the window, so the correct start is 2026-09-03T11:25:39Z (the streak is longer than claimed, ~11 days with zero failures since, so the row stays evidence-ready). The formal-model row cited "latest Formal Verify runs on v5", but that workflow is `pull_request`/`workflow_dispatch`-only and has never run on `v5`; the row is now justified by byte-identity of every modeled trigger path between the last green verified SHA and `v5` HEAD.
- Governor kicks that arrive during the startup stagger are deferred and delivered when the agent finishes launching, so queue-draining agents no longer sit idle until the next cadence cycle after a pod restart.
- Keep hub heartbeats from overwriting live agent state and health with stale cached collector data after boot-time collection timeouts.
- Fixed the review human-decision label being re-applied to every held PR on every governor cycle: the already-labeled skip compared the hold's `owner/repo` against the enumeration's bare repo name and never matched. Both sides now resolve through `project.org`.
- Agents whose copilot hang diagnostic timed out were parked in `failed` with their tmux session already destroyed, refusing every kick ("failed to start: copilot hung with no output") until an operator restarted them. An inconclusive diagnostic now relaunches the agent instead.
- **Duplicate finding suppression now survives a reworded title.** `hive-open-issue` deduped against open issues by *exact* title, but agents routinely append a model-authored qualifier to a stable subject — `[scanner] Split web/e2e/compliance/card-cache-compliance.spec.ts (1237 lines)`, then the same line with `— extract cache helpers module`, `— extract snapshot/report helpers`, and so on. The qualifier is reworded on every scan, so the exact-title check never matched and the same finding was re-filed every cycle: one 1237-line file had accumulated **six** simultaneously-open issues in `kubestellar/console`, and roughly a quarter of that hive's scanner backlog was the same handful of files filed over and over. Dedupe now compares a canonical subject (qualifier stripped, case- and whitespace-normalised) and reuses the **oldest** open match, so repeats consolidate onto the original issue instead of growing the queue without bound. Distinct findings stay distinct — a different path, a different line count, or a stem too short to be a safe key all still file a new issue.
- **The eval-cycle log no longer reports agents it is about to skip.** `governor eval complete` logged `agents_due` *before* the on-demand and operator-paused gates ran, then dropped the gated agents with no log line at all. Operators reading the logs saw paused agents listed as due on every single cycle while those agents sat at a bare shell, which made a half-paused roster read like a healthy one. `agents_due` now names only the agents actually being kicked, and anything gated out is reported alongside it in `agents_skipped` with its reason (`operator-paused`, `on-demand`, `on-demand-in-pack`).
- Rank human-filed and priority-labelled actionable issues ahead of hive-filed backlog items in agent kicks.
- Fixed the watchdog paging an operator for re-authentication about agents that were logged in and working. Interactive CLIs paint login chrome while completing their own startup auth handshake, so rolling a spoke fired one `PaneShowsLogin` credential failure per agent seconds after launch — the pane poller already documents this flash and guards its restart path with a multi-poll streak, but the liveness classifier evaluated `auth-required` above the boot-grace guard that every other verdict honours. The reconciler's "healable" downgrade could not rescue those agents either, because it requires a proven credential and the fleet only proves credentials for the claude backend, so every copilot agent took the paging branch. Login chrome seen inside boot grace is now reported as unknown; an agent that genuinely needs a human still shows the same chrome once grace elapses and pages on the next tick.
- Fix remaining hub OIDC identity display stragglers, including pending access-request rows and provision decision attribution.
- Fixed two more OMP readiness false positives found by continued live monitoring: `#6639`'s "Tip:" paragraph stripping never terminated (no blank line reliably follows a tip's wrapped continuation), silently swallowing the rest of the pane and masking real state instead of just the tip; and a completed turn whose own reply happened to discuss authentication ("Authentication required: please sign in...") tripped the same needs-login gate on a fully idle, ready pane. Both are fixed by scoping OMP's onboarding/login checks to the last 3 non-blank lines, where its real prompt chrome actually renders, rather than the full 15-line tail or an attempted paragraph strip.
- Keep fleet pending access-request panels open across periodic refreshes.
- The entrypoint's 5-minute permission sweep is now bounded by modification time, so it can no longer be starved by an unbounded CLI session directory. `hive_fix_slow_cycle` walked `/data/home/.copilot` in full every 5 minutes; measured on a live spoke that sweep took 75s at 970 session directories, and the same spoke had reached 9,449 — where it runs roughly 12 minutes against a 5-minute cycle. A repair pass that cannot finish within its own period stops repairing: files newly created by an agent stayed group-unwritable for as long as the backlog took, and because agent UIDs differ (`hive-scanner`, `hive-sec-check`, ...) while the CLI creates files under a `022` umask, agents hit `Permission denied` on each other's session files. The 5-minute path now repairs only entries modified in the last 10 minutes (6s on the same spoke), and the full sweep still runs hourly as a backstop.
- Fix hive-owned conflicted PRs being deferred forever by annotating kick lists and updating self-authored behind branches during automerge sweeps.
- Fixed abandoned tmux clients permanently disabling every keyboard-based self-heal for an agent. `SessionAttached` exists so hive never types into a session an operator is using, but it asked tmux only how many clients were attached — and a client that dies without detaching (an SSH drop, a closed `kubectl exec`, a browser tab shut on a terminal view) stays attached forever. On a hosted spoke two such clients sat on the scanner session with `client_activity` frozen at `client_created` and no process owning either pty; scanner then hit a transient model error, dropped to an idle prompt, and sat there for 13.5 hours because the retry nudge kept vetoing itself on a terminal nobody was looking at. Attachment is now judged by client activity, so clients silent past a 30-minute grace no longer block healing. Every uncertainty still fails open, an active client still blocks, and a single active client among abandoned ones still blocks.
- Wait for delayed agent tmux sockets before attaching dashboard terminals, preventing ttyd reconnect storms during boot.
- Documented that `v5-latest`/`edge` are published by the `v5` line and `v4-latest`/`candidate` by `v4`, corrected `operator-reference.md`'s claim that a `v4` build publishes all three channels, and flagged that `:latest` is moved by both lines ([#6711](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6711)).
- Do not default vLLM to a cluster-specific in-cluster Service; report DNS gateway faults with the unresolved host.

### Security

- Contributor agents now authenticate knowledge-export downloads with their registration token before receiving `agent.md` ([#2438](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/2438)), closing the unauthenticated export path so hosted spokes can deliver live Hive instructions without exposing them to anonymous callers.
- The GitHub user-auth logout endpoint now requires a live user session before deleting persisted owner credentials, preventing anonymous POSTs from logging the hive owner out on non-allowlist spokes ([#5743](https://github.com/kubestellar/hive/issues/5743)).
- Public dashboard endpoints now strip forged `X-Hive-User`/`X-Hive-Role` identity headers unless the hub's `X-Hive-Proxy-Auth` proof is valid, closing an anonymous contributor-control and impersonation bypass ([#5771](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5771)).
- Removed the legacy hub session-cookie mint and verification helpers from the production binary while keeping the rejection regression tests.
- Legacy `dashboard/server.js` now binds to `127.0.0.1` by default via `HIVE_DASHBOARD_BIND`, so its unauthenticated control endpoints are not exposed to the network unless an operator explicitly opts into `0.0.0.0` behind an authenticated proxy ([#5905](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5905)).
- `hive-deploy.service` no longer trusts an unverified `/tmp/hive` checkout as the source of its `sudo` sync into `/usr/local/bin` ([#5936](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5936), same class as [#5435](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5435)/[#5483](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/5483)). `bin/hive-deploy.sh` `cd`s into `/tmp/hive` checking only that `.git` exists, runs git inside it (executing the checkout's own hooks), and `sudo cp`s every changed `bin/*.sh` over its `/usr/local/bin` counterpart — including `bin/hive.sh` → `/usr/local/bin/hive` and `bin/gh-wrapper.sh` → `/usr/local/bin/gh`, which fronts `/usr/bin/gh` in PATH for every user. `/tmp` is cleared on reboot and its sticky bit does not stop a local user *creating* `/tmp/hive` before the checkout is restored; with `hive-deploy.timer` firing at `OnBootSec=60`, the winner of that race had their scripts root-installed host-wide within a minute of boot — a strictly larger payoff than the `dev`-execution races already fixed in the discord and snapshot units, yet this was the one unit in the class left unguarded. The unit now runs `ExecStartPre=hive-checkout-guard.sh /tmp/hive/bin hive.sh gh-wrapper.sh hive-deploy.sh hive-checkout-guard.sh` (the #5481 guard generalizes without modification), refusing to start when any path component or pinned file is attacker-owned, writable by others, or a symlink; a missing checkout is a refusal, matching the script's own "not a git repo" bail-out. The #5481 hardening directives are deliberately *not* applied — `NoNewPrivileges` would break the script's `sudo` sync and any `ProtectSystem` level mounts `/usr` read-only, the very place this unit installs to — and `src/deploy/test_hive_deploy_unit_contract.sh` pins the guard wiring, those exclusions, and the guard's refusal of each attack shape by executing it against real trees. It now also verifies that the checkout remote is hivecommons/hive and that HEAD is on the expected branch/tag before git hooks run, then copies root-installed files from a git-archive snapshot of the verified HEAD instead of the mutable worktree to close the check/copy race.
- The merge-request watcher no longer merges a PR without independently verifying CI, and absent check runs are no longer treated as passing ([#6173](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6173)). `handleOneMergeRequest` used to call `MergePR` unconditionally and relied on GitHub's branch protection to refuse a red PR; on a base branch with no protection rules nothing refused it, and a fork PR whose four workflows had all died at startup with zero jobs (so zero check runs and an empty status rollup) was merged 13 minutes after opening. The watcher now requires positive confirmation on the pinned head SHA before any merge: at least one commit status or check run exists, every gating one concluded success (`neutral`/`skipped` accepted, the existing non-required ignore list and `auto_merge.required_checks` set still apply), every config-declared required check has actually reported, and no workflow run on the SHA failed without producing a job. Zero evidence is refused as unverified; queued/in-progress CI parks the request (`ci_waits` in the result file, no retry consumed) for up to one hour; a red verdict is a failed attempt that re-engages the fix loop exactly like a branch-protection refusal; an API error while gathering evidence is a failed attempt, never a pass. The self-merge sweep's `commitGreen` is unchanged in behavior and now shares its evaluation core with the gate.
- The merge-request watcher now refuses unprotected base branches by default and requires an explicit per-repo no-CI opt-in before absent CI can pass ([#6281](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6281)).
- The token-access audit log behind `GET /api/token-access` is no longer writable by the agents it audits ([#6287](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6287)). The log records every gh CLI command and git credential lookup an agent makes and is gated at owner role for exactly that reason, yet it was fed by the audited parties: `bin/gh-wrapper.sh` and `bin/git-credential-hive.sh` run as the agent UID and appended straight into `/var/run/hive-metrics/token-access.jsonl`, which only works when the file is writable by every agent (dev:node 0664, and every agent's primary group is node). Append is indistinguishable from write at the permission level, so a compromised or prompt-injected agent could truncate the trail of its own token use, rewrite lines to blame a peer, or forge entries outright. The wrappers now drop one JSON event per call into `/var/run/hive-metrics/token-access-events`, a drop-box the agents can create files in but cannot list (0730, sticky, setgid), and the hive process ingests those events into the log, which is now hive-owned 0600 with no group or other bit at all. On ingest the hive replaces each event's self-reported `uid` with the uid that owns the event file, the same trust anchor the PR-request watcher uses, and keeps a disagreeing claim beside it as `claimed_uid`, so an entry forged in a peer's name lands attributed to the forger. Malformed or oversized events are rejected rather than appended. A 0664 log left by an older image is tightened on every boot and on every ingest pass instead of trusted. What remains open is narrower than before: an agent can still delete its own event during the two-second window before ingest, and can still flood the log with real calls; it can no longer alter anything already recorded.
- Agent push brokering now rejects non-fast-forward branch updates and lane sign-offs on commits authored by someone else ([#6329](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6329)).
- Refuse a `workflow_dispatch` `release_sha` for `docker.yml` that is not an ancestor of the dispatched branch, closing a path where any `actions: write` principal could publish an unreviewed commit under a release line's moving tags ([#6419](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6419))
- Require owner role on the agent-control mutation endpoints (kick, switch, model set, restart, reset-restarts, pin, unpin), closing a gap where any authenticated read-write contributor could restart or reconfigure an agent, or inject an arbitrary prompt into its CLI session ([#6557](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6557))
- `ioscan` canary egress detection now covers the encodings the first pass at [#6686](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6686) left open: line-wrapped and nested base64, the URL-safe base64 alphabet, hex written with per-byte separators or `\x`/`0x` escapes, splitting on punctuation rather than whitespace, homoglyph and zero-width substitution, and partial leaks carrying an intact 16-hex-character window of a token. Candidate blobs are no longer capped per body, so padding an outbound write with decoy blobs can no longer push the real payload out of the scan, and the rewritten scan is roughly four times faster than the substring version it replaces on a full-size (2 MiB) body. `security-self-assessment.md` and `ioscan.md` now state what the egress canary check does and does not cover, replacing the stated encoding limitation.
- `ioscan` canary egress checks now detect canary tokens hidden with base64, hex, URL encoding, reversal, case changes, or whitespace splitting, closing an encoded-exfiltration bypass ([#6686](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/6686)).
- Require owner/operator authorization for legacy Node dashboard Nous mutation endpoints (#8103).
- Pin `bin/nous-install.sh` to a reviewed Nous upstream commit and verify the checkout before pip installation. (#8104)
- Stop accepting the shared dashboard owner token from `?token=` URLs; browser terminal links now use authenticated, short-lived single-use handoff codes and query `token`/`code` values are redacted in dashboard request logs.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.73.1)

### Changed

- ⚠ planning labels now default to `hive-plan`/`hive-design` with `design-approved` approval, add the design gate before breakdown for labeled epics, and keep the L5 plan-review gate on (`plan_auto_approve: false`). (#7993)

### Fixed

- Carry `converse` through the ACMM pack loader and `ApplyPack`. The L5/L6 packs declare `converse: true` on `reviewer` (#8023) but `PackAgent` had no such field, so the value was silently dropped and a pack-created reviewer could not post reviews. Packs now seed `converse` only where the agent has no value yet; an explicit operator `converse: false` is never re-granted.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.73.0)

### Added

- ACMM level-5 and level-6 packs now include the `reviewer` agent by default — the repo-grounded PR reviewer (ADVISORY, `reviewer-queue.md`, 30m cadence in every governor mode; never merges). Below L5 it stays opt-in, and hand-created reviewers keep their operator-owned model/backend/pause. (#8023)

## 2026-09-21 (v4.72.1)

### Changed

- REPOSITORIES cards now lay out at most four across (three/two/one on narrower viewports) instead of packing six at 240px, and the pill title budget scales from the card's actual layout width — so issue/PR pill rows are readable instead of squashed to a few characters each.

### Fixed

- Apply the configured `review.human_decision_label` when the reviewer's aggregate verdict is `requires_human`. Previously only fixer-side exhaustion created a human hold, so reviewer-flagged PRs carried the marker in the review body but never got the triage label.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.72.0)

### Added

- Dashboard shows epic↔issue linkage for plans (#8011): an issue pill that already has a plan shows a state chip (queued / stuck / N to review / d of N done / complete) that opens the plan review instead of a bare Plan button; the review lists each task's claimant and PR; the PLANNING tile tooltip and Plans modal name which plans are waiting on a human; and an opt-in `planning.mirror_to_issue` posts the approved plan as a checklist comment on the source issue with a `#plan=<epic>` deep link back.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.71.1)

### Fixed

- Plan mode now finishes: "Plan this issue" and the `plan`/`epic` label minted an epic and kicked the architect, but nothing ever turned its reply into child tasks — every plan sat "queued for architect" forever and the label trigger re-kicked the architect every eval cycle. The architect's prompt now names the epic and issue URL and tells it to hand the task list back with `bd decompose <epic> --plan <file>`; the label trigger kicks at most once per 30 minutes and, after 3 kicks with no plan, marks the epic **⚠ stuck** on the PLANNING tile and in the plan list instead of kicking again. Clicking Plan on the issue resets the budget and retries (#8010).

## 2026-09-21 (v4.71.0)

### Added

- Repository cards on the dashboard can now be resized one at a time (#8000). Every card used to be exactly as wide as every other one, so on a hive watching several busy repos a pill column read `#192 Pa…`, `FIX #1109 fix…` and the only way to learn what any of them was was to hover them one by one. Each card now has a `col-resize` handle on its right edge: drag it to widen the repo you are triaging and narrow the quiet ones to make room, double-click it to reset that card, or focus it and nudge with ← / → (Shift for a bigger step, Esc to reset). A widened card also stops cutting pill titles at 50 characters — the character budget grows with the card, so past a certain width the titles are complete and the hover is unnecessary. Widths are stored per repo in the browser, keyed by hive, so the layout survives a reload and the governor's repaint; a "Reset layout" button beside Rescan clears them all.

### Fixed

- Fixed a merged fix's claim expiring after 72h on a clock, which re-offered the still-open issue every three days for another "already fixed, please close" cycle (#8003). Settled claims — a strong claim from a merged PR, or a verified `no_work_needed` verdict — are now carried across scans for 30 days from the merge, and after 7 days the contribute queue withholds the issue under a new `merged_claim_stale` reason that asks a maintainer to close it or say what remains.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.70.4)

### Fixed

- A closing keyword written as prose is now a closing claim. The claim parser required GitHub's own trailer shape (`Fixes #12`, `Fixes: #12`), so a merged pull request whose body read "Resolves architect issue #1232 (first incremental step)" produced no claim at all — and the issue went back into the offer pool after every merge. The closing tier now accepts the same bounded 40-character prose gap the non-closing `Refs #N` tier already did, so such a PR makes a strong claim and suppresses its issue instead of releasing it for re-verification every cycle. The gap must start with whitespace, which keeps a Conventional Commits `fix:` / `fix(scope):` title prefix from claiming the first issue number it sees; the closing tier stays single-issue, matching GitHub ([#7995](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7995)).
- Issues that keep consuming pull requests are withheld for maintainer triage instead of being offered again. The claim ledger now keeps a cumulative churn history — which pull requests have been observed against each issue and how each one ended — built from the two PR listings the claim scan already pages through, so closed-without-merge PRs (previously invisible everywhere) are counted. At 2 merged or 2 closed-unmerged pull requests on one issue, the contribute queue stops offering it and records reason `issue_churn` on the operator-visible Withheld surface with the counts and PR numbers. The guard never closes, comments on, or relabels anything; records age out 14 days after a PR was last seen, and a maintainer can clear it immediately with the `hive: churn-triaged` label ([#7995](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7995)).
- Tracker detection now recognises the `epic` / `tracker` / `tracking` labels (including prefixed spellings such as `kind/epic`) and a case-insensitive `[Epic]` / `[Tracker]` title prefix, matching what the PR-request gate already honoured. A tracking issue is incremental by construction — its children carry the work — so it re-offered after every child merged until a human closed it ([#7995](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7995)).
- Fixed a contributor whose CLI login had expired reporting ready all night and failing every task on the 30-minute watchdog (#7996). The relay now treats an unattended "Please run /login" pane as a login hold: it hands the task back at once as an `environment` failure naming the login, withholds `ready`, declines pushed assignments, leaves the pane untouched for whoever attaches, and re-advertises once the pane shows a signed-in CLI. The hub's contributor failure-streak gate gains a stall streak — three consecutive watchdog-length failures pause the identity's claims with a message pointing at `/login`.

## 2026-09-21 (v4.70.3)

### Changed

- `upgradeMarkerPath` in cmd/hive is now a var (test-only seam, production unchanged) so the hub UpgradeCallback's give-up, backoff, stale-marker and uptime-floor branches are pinned by hermetic tests (#7990).

## 2026-09-21 (v4.70.2)

### Security

- v5/v6 Top-up workflows verify the pinned SHA-256 of the `gh` CLI tarball before installing it, matching the `just` download convention in v2-ci.yml; the job's checkout can hold a workflows-write credential, so an unverified binary there was an unsafe supply-chain pattern (#7976).

## 2026-09-21 (v4.70.1)

### Fixed

- v5/v6 Top-up workflows push with the `TOPUP_PUSH_TOKEN` repo secret (fine-grained PAT with Contents + Workflows write) when it is set, so forward-merges that touch `.github/workflows/**` (dependabot action-pin bumps) no longer fail at the push; without the secret the job now stops before pushing with an actionable error naming the files and the manual sync recipe (#7959).

## 2026-09-21 (v4.70.0)

### Added

- The contributor image now carries a small repository-check baseline, so a container-mode agent can run the checked-out repository's own checks instead of a substitute for them ([#7925](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7925)). The image could run the relay and the agent CLIs but shipped no `pip`, `pytest`, `pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `requests`, `make`, `just`, `shellcheck` or `yq` — so an agent could edit a Python-, Make- or `just`-driven repository and then not run its test suite, its `just check`, or its `make ci`. That is a correctness problem rather than a convenience one, because an agent that cannot run the real check reaches for a proxy that looks green: on one task, pytest-style tests run under `python3 -m unittest` reported `Ran 0 tests ... OK` and were about to be cited as a passing run. `just` and `yq` are not packaged in Debian 12 and are installed the way the image already installs Go, muse and omp — a pinned release verified with `sha256sum` before install, never a curl-pipe-to-shell installer; `JUST_VERSION` matches the pin CI already uses. Because Debian marks its system Python externally-managed and the container runs as the unprivileged `dev` user, Python packages install into `/opt/hive/pyenv`, a `--system-site-packages` virtualenv owned by `dev` and first on `PATH`, so `pip install` works inside a task with no privilege and no flags. Container tooling (`podman`, `skopeo`, `buildah`, `crane`) is deliberately still absent: it needs privileges the contributor container should not hold.
- Container mode installs a task repository's declared toolchain before the prompt is typed: `bin/repo-toolchain.sh` reads `<checkout>/.hive/tools` and pip-installs its `pip` lines (bare PEP 508 requirements only, capped, time-boxed, never fails the task) into the image's venv; `apt` lines are recorded not installed since the container has no root ([#7925](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7925))

### Fixed

- omp container mode's credential sync-back skips a row the container's own omp disabled (its refresh lost the race to the host's), so a dead token with a newer stamp can no longer overwrite a working host sign-in on the 300 s timer or at exit ([#7922](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7922))
- Contribute: an agent that finds an issue blocked on something outside its repository — another repo's release or build, a dependency that has not published — can now say so with `HIVE_VERDICT: blocked — <what it is waiting on>` (or `no_work_needed — blocked: …`), and the hub stops throwing that finding away ([#7924](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7924)). Before, such a verdict was booked as an ordinary `no_work_needed`, the issue came back on the 4h no-PR backoff, and every retry re-ran the same research to re-discover the same external dependency (projectbluefin/utah#100: ten minutes of research to find "no factory image carries the new packages yet", then the same ten minutes again on the next rung). A `blocked` completion is now held for the full with-PR cooldown from the first time, its ledger row carries the marker and the reason so an operator can see what it is waiting on, and its reason is not mistaken for a settlement. When the task credential can write issues, the relay also applies the repository's `blocked` label — the existing admission gate then withholds the issue until a human clears the label, which the relay never does itself. The assignment prompt asks the agent to leave one signed comment on the issue naming what covers or blocks it before printing either verdict, so the finding survives on GitHub and an open PR gets cross-referenced to the issue it covers; it also tells the agent never to edit someone else's PR body to add `Fixes #N`. On the wire the relay sends the marker alongside the `no_work_needed` an older hub already books, so mixed relay/hub versions behave as before.
- `TestHiveNameVanityHostUniquenessAcrossCalls` no longer fails on a single birthday-bound collision among 20 random 4-char suffixes (~1.1e-4 per run); it still fails immediately on a constant or low-entropy suffix ([#7929](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7929))
- The v5/v6 top-up workflows now release their own PR's held CI: `pull_request` runs on a PR opened or refreshed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` are either held for approval or die at startup with 0 jobs ("workflow file issue"), so forward-merge PRs showed no test evidence; the top-up job now approves the held runs and re-runs the 0-job startup failures ([#7930](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7930))
- `just contribute-hive omp` (container mode) now writes a refreshed omp OAuth credential back to the host every `HIVE_OMP_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_SECONDS` (default 300; `0` for exit-only) while the container runs, not only at exit, so the host's own omp and a second launch are not left on a revoked refresh token for the length of a run; the relay no longer advertises `ready` or a model for an omp whose configured provider's credential is disabled, says whether a detected model came from a session transcript or from `config.yml`, and classifies omp's `No API key found for <provider>. Use /login` as blocked on a human rather than a completed turn ([#7922](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7922), [#7931](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/pull/7931))
- The relay's frame clamp now shrinks the largest payload field first, so a small `tmux_output` tail or `summary` that already fit is no longer emptied to make room for an oversized later field such as `reason` ([#7932](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7932))
- The contributor relay no longer loses a `task_complete` to the hub's 64 KiB WebSocket read limit, which put headless contributors in a reconnect loop that re-ran tasks they had already finished ([#7932](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7932)). The captured-output tail was sent as fifteen *lines* with no byte bound, and a JSON-streaming backend such as pi puts a whole tool event — embedded diff and all — on one line, so a successful task reported its completion in a frame the hub refused with `1009 message too big`; the hub's lease outlived the close, the same task came back, and the agent redid work it had already shipped (four times over on a live spoke, one run having opened a real PR). Frames are now clamped where every frame passes through: the audit tail is held to 8 KiB and the whole frame to the hub's limit, shrinking only payload fields — `task_id`, `result`, `pr_url` and `verdict` always survive intact, and a trimmed tail carries a visible marker. The hub now states that limit on `auth_ok` as `max_message_bytes`, so a hub that raises its ceiling carries its relays up with it instead of the two numbers drifting apart, and it logs a frame that trips the limit rather than disconnecting a contributor with nothing in the hub log.
- The contributor relay's post-verdict review follow-up now quotes the advisor notes it is asking about instead of naming only the event ([#7935](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7935)). *"Advisor notes were posted after your verdict"* is unambiguous only when the pane holds exactly those notes, and with an advisor that reviews every turn it usually does not — the turn has already carried one to three mid-turn notes the agent read and acted on, so the sentence reads just as well as "the ones you already handled". On projectbluefin/utah#24 the agent made that reading: it matched the nudge to two mid-turn `⟦blocker⟧`s it had resolved, searched the hub and the PR for anything newer, found nothing and re-printed the verdict, so the wrong file citation the advisor had flagged shipped in utah#225 and the one follow-up turn was spent on the wrong places. The relay already had the note text in hand — it logs it — and now types it: the `⟦concern⟧`/`⟦blocker⟧` blocks that earned the turn, continuation lines joined, quoted inline on the one line `tmux send-keys` can carry without submitting early. `POST_VERDICT_REVIEW_ANCHOR` remains a verbatim prefix so the echo matching that detects the second verdict is unchanged, quoted text has any `HIVE_VERDICT:` sentinel defused so a wrapped echo cannot answer the follow-up itself, and a pane with nothing quotable falls back to the previous wording. The second, blocker-only round quotes its blockers the same way.
- The gh wrapper's identity-footer injection now understands every spelling of a body that `gh` accepts — `--body`/`-b` and `--body-file`/`-F`, separated, attached or `=`-joined, including `-F -` for stdin ([#7937](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7937)). It previously recognised only `--body` and `--body=`, and added a second `--body <footer>` when it saw neither: `gh pr comment -F notes.md` was refused outright by `gh` ("specify only one of --body or --body-file") so the comment was never posted, and `gh pr comment -b 'text'` posted the footer *alone* because `gh` keeps the last of two `--body` flags — silently dropping the agent's text. A file or stdin body is now read by the wrapper and re-emitted as a single `--body` carrying the caller's text plus the footer.

## 2026-09-20 (v4.69.1)

### Fixed

- Dashboard: the REPOSITORIES card now shows held PRs and held issues as pills, so a PR that is waiting on a human is no longer the one thing the card hides ([#7896](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7896)). The card's PRs number is the repo's total open PR count, but its pills were drawn from the actionable set only — and a `hold` label (the ACMM level gate's "held for human review", a Renovate bump the escalation ledger gave up on with `needs-human`, a maintainer's own `on-hold`) moves an item out of that set. So a repo whose every open PR was held read "3 PRs" with three *issue* pills under it and no PR listed, and an operator's first read was "the dashboard is missing my PRs". The pills are now laid out in two columns under the two numbers — issue pills under **issues** (blue), PR pills under **PRs** (purple) — so position says what a pill is, and colour within a column says what state it is in: held items sit in their column in a dashed neutral tint with a ⏸ chip (⚠ when `needs-human` is also on it, since that hold only a person can clear), and the tooltip names the label that holds it, says agents will not act on it until the label is removed, and on a hive-authored PR says a `hold` there is usually the level gate the hive lifts itself. The count and its column now agree. A held PR pill never offers **Queue auto-merge**, and a held issue pill never offers **Plan** — both are out of the automated lane by definition. The held items ride on the status snapshot beside the actionable ones (`heldPrs` / `heldIssues` on each repo, with the hold list's items now carrying their GitHub URL and labels); they are kept apart from `openPrs` on purpose, so the hold gate and every automated consumer of the snapshot — the contribute queue, the merge sweep counts, `/api/prs` — are untouched. The section header's "N need human review" counter now includes held `needs-human` PRs, and the hive's own review pill is stamped onto held PRs too.
- Container mode no longer strands the host's omp sign-in: the OAuth credential the container refreshed is written back to `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` on exit (`omp-backend.js --sync-back`, only the selected provider's existing row, only when newer), and `--stage`/`--describe` refuse to launch on a sign-in omp has marked `disabled_cause` instead of letting omp fall back silently to another provider while the relay reports the selected model ([#7922](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7922))

## 2026-09-20 (v4.69.0)

### Added

- The Operations page's "Your contribution" card now shows how many of your pull requests landed in the last 24 hours, next to the all-time count it already had ([#7894](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7894)). Issues worked already came as a 24h figure and an all-time figure, but PRs produced — the number auto-promotion actually reads — only had the all-time one, so you could see that you worked 41 issues today without knowing how many of them turned into a pull request. The new tile keeps the same honesty rules as the issues tile: an em dash and "no hourly history yet" until the spoke has rolled up your PR series, and "Nh of history so far" while fewer than 24 hours back it. Under the hood `/api/contribute/me` gains `prs_produced_24h`, `pr_window_hours_covered` and `pr_history_available`, summed from a second per-contributor hourly ring (`per_user_pr` in the persisted metrics file) rolled up from each profile's verified-PR counter exactly like the completion ring, so it survives restarts the same way. On a spoke upgraded mid-day the PR tile reports the hours measured since the upgrade rather than a full day of zeros nobody measured.

### Fixed

- A contributor whose connection drops for between ten and thirty minutes no longer has its in-flight issue handed to a second contributor while it can still resume: the hub now treats an unexpired task lease as a hold on its issue for exactly as long as the lease is re-adoptable, closing the gap between the ten-minute release cooldown and the thirty-minute lease that let both contributors end up on one issue with duplicate PRs. A relay that never returns parks its issue for the lease's length rather than the cooldown's ([#7773](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7773)).
- A task that was revoked or aborted mid-edit no longer leaves its half-done changes for every later task on that repo to start from ([#7790](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7790)). The contributor relay works every task on a repo out of one persistent checkout under `$HIVE_WORKSPACE_DIR`, and stopping an interrupted agent never touched the tree: on projectbluefin/utah one revoked task left three modified files on its branch and the next four tasks all began from them, one `git add -A` away from shipping another task's work under this contributor's name. The relay now sweeps the task's checkout on every exit — completion, failure, revoke, shutdown — after the agent is stopped, setting aside anything uncommitted (untracked files included) with `git stash push --include-untracked -m "hive leftover <task_id> …"`, never resetting or cleaning, so an operator can recover the work from `git stash list`; it only ever touches a directory it can prove is the task's checkout, and never the relay's own cwd. The assignment prompt now also tells the agent to run `git status` before branching, stash rather than discard or commit anything it did not write, confirm the tree is clean, and prefer `git worktree add` — the half that covers a contributor whose relay never sees the checkout.
- Contributor relay: a `HIVE_VERDICT` line is judged on a capture taken at least `VERDICT_SETTLE_MS` (2 s) after the tick that first saw it, not on the capture that discovered it. omp renders its end-of-turn advisor notes under the verdict about a second after the line appears, and the #7841 fast path was finalizing inside that second — so whether #7879 recorded the notes depended on timer phase. The first sighting defers and keeps the concern snapshot; the glance re-fires after the settle. One extra glance at most, no new turns (#7907).
- Contributor relay: the task prompt now reaches the agent with the literal workspace path in place of `$HIVE_WORKSPACE_DIR` (both dispatch paths). The agent handed the variable to its CLI's non-shell file tools, which do not expand it — a failed `Path not found` call and an advisor note at the start of 3 of 5 omp sessions. The relay knows the path; the hub's wording is unchanged (#7908).
- The PR claim ledger now sees every issue a pull request references, not just the one it closes ([#7911](https://github.com/hivecommons/hive/issues/7911)). Two gaps compounded: the non-closing reference tier (`Refs #N`, `Part of #N`, #3980) only ran when a PR had no closing keyword at all, so a maintainer's consolidation PR reading "Closes #159. Refs #72, #74, … #197" claimed #159 alone; and neither parser read a comma list, so even a bare `Refs #72, #74, #87` yielded #72.
